process.title: Tell us the paper split, not just the grade
process.description: The useful first message says which paper is weaker, what the last mock marks were on each, and which programming language the school teaches. With that we can match a specialist rather than a generalist, and tell you honestly whether one is free at your times.

process.title: A scored topic diagnostic
process.description: Before any plan, the student scores themselves against the ten syllabus topics and attempts one trace table and one short algorithm. That takes twenty minutes and replaces guesswork with a ranked list of what to fix first.

process.title: Free first lesson, one-to-one and live
process.description: Sixty minutes over video with the matched tutor, working on the weakest topic from the diagnostic rather than on introductions. No card details are taken and there is no obligation to continue afterwards.

process.title: A written plan naming the paper to attack first
process.description: You get a plan that commits to one paper, states how many sessions before a review, and says what will be measurable in six weeks. Where the honest answer is that the student needs programming fluency before anything else, the plan says that instead.

process.title: Six-week review against marked work
process.description: We compare the first diagnostic with current scripts and decide whether to continue, switch paper or change tutor. Switching tutor at a review costs nothing; continuing without evidence of movement is the thing worth avoiding.

whyPoints.title: Both papers, one specialist
whyPoints.description: Tutors matched to 0478 teach computer systems and the algorithms paper, including the database and Boolean logic topics schools often reach late. A tutor who can only help with Python homework covers roughly half of what the qualification examines.

whyPoints.title: Handwritten practice, because the exam is handwritten
whyPoints.description: Pseudocode and trace tables are set on paper every week, not typed. It is the least popular part of the work with students and the part that most reliably moves Paper 2 marks within a term.

whyPoints.title: The student's own code on screen
whyPoints.description: Lessons run over live video with the student sharing their editor, so a tutor can run their program, break it deliberately, and convert it into exam-ready pseudocode alongside. Everything annotated is saved and sent afterwards.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the school's language
whyPoints.description: Dubai schools teach different text-based languages for this syllabus. The match is made against the one your child's school uses, because switching language mid-course costs weeks that a Year 11 student does not have.

whyPoints.title: Clear about what we are not

whyPoints.title: Scarcity stated, not hidden
whyPoints.description: Computing specialists are a smaller pool than maths or English. If nobody suitable is free at your preferred slot, you hear that with the alternatives before a trial is booked rather than afterwards.

faqs.question: What does Cambridge IGCSE Computer Science 0478 actually involve?
faqs.answer: Two written papers of equal weight. One covers computer systems: data representation, data transmission, hardware, software, the internet and its uses, and automated and emerging technologies. The other covers algorithm design and problem-solving, programming, databases and Boolean logic. Candidates write algorithms by hand, in pseudocode or a high-level language, and no part of the qualification is assessed at a computer. Confirm the current paper structure, durations and mark totals against the Cambridge 0478 syllabus for your child's exam series, since component detail changes between syllabus cycles.

faqs.question: Is there any coursework or controlled assessment in 0478?
faqs.answer: The current syllabus has no coursework component. Both papers are written and externally marked, which surprises parents who remember computing qualifications built around a project. It has a practical consequence worth planning for: a student cannot bank marks through good classwork, so everything depends on performance in two written papers. It also means the academic-honesty risks attached to coursework-heavy subjects do not arise here, though a tutor still never produces work a school has set a student to do independently.

faqs.question: Which programming language should my child use for the algorithms paper?
faqs.answer: The one their school teaches, and the decision should not be revisited in Year 11. Candidates may answer in pseudocode or in a high-level language, and Cambridge publishes its own pseudocode conventions. What costs marks is not the choice of language but ambiguity: undeclared variables, loops that are not clearly closed, and conditions written loosely. We match tutors to the language in use at the school, because a student switching language mid-course loses weeks for no gain in marks.

faqs.question: My child writes good code but scores poorly on the algorithms paper. Why?
faqs.answer: Because the exam removes the interpreter. A student who debugs by running a program and watching the result has the machine doing their verification. In the paper there is no run button, so they must trace the logic themselves and record intermediate states, which is precisely what a trace table is for and what carries marks. The fix is specific and quick: convert their own working programs into handwritten pseudocode, then drill three timed trace tables a week until completeness is automatic.

faqs.question: What is a trace table and why does it carry marks?
faqs.answer: It is a grid recording the value of each variable after every step of an algorithm, including every iteration of a loop. It is examined directly, and it is also the method by which a candidate checks their own logic when no computer is available. Marks are awarded for the intermediate values, which is why stopping a row early or writing only the final result loses most of them. Students find them clerical and slow; that is the point, and accuracy improves markedly within about four weeks of weekly practice.

faqs.question: How much does a computer science tutor cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market figures for Dubai put qualified online one-to-one tuition at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors listing IGCSE tuition from AED 150, and named-syllabus specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 rate table giving 200 to 450 plus. In-home one-to-one runs higher, roughly AED 180 to 500, because travel is priced into the hour. Those are other providers' published rates as of October 2026; IB Gram quotes after a free first lesson.

faqs.question: Should my child take Computer Science 0478 or ICT 0417?
faqs.answer: They are different subjects with different assessment styles, and in many Dubai schools they sit in the same option column, so the choice is real. 0478 is two written papers covering systems theory, algorithms, programming, databases and logic. 0417 is largely practical, assessed at a computer across document production, databases, presentations, spreadsheets and website authoring. A student who enjoys building and problem-solving in code usually belongs in 0478; a student who works accurately and methodically with software tools often does better in 0417.

faqs.question: Does my child use a computer during the 0478 examination?
faqs.answer: No. Both papers are written, and algorithms are produced by hand in pseudocode or a high-level language. This is the single most under-prepared fact about the subject, because almost all of a student's practice during the course happens at a keyboard. Handwriting an algorithm is slower, less forgiving and harder to revise mid-answer, so it needs its own practice. We set handwritten algorithm work every week for exactly this reason, and the improvement is usually visible within a month.

faqs.question: How many topics does the 0478 syllabus contain?
faqs.answer: Ten, divided between the two papers. Six sit on the computer systems paper: data representation, data transmission, hardware, software, the internet and its uses, and automated and emerging technologies. Four sit on the algorithms paper: algorithm design and problem-solving, programming, databases, and Boolean logic. Scoring a student honestly against all ten in a first session produces a ranked revision list, which is far more useful than a general plan to revise the subject. Check the current syllabus for your child's series, as topic numbering can change between cycles.

faqs.question: Where do students lose marks in data representation?
faqs.answer: Almost entirely in arithmetic rather than in understanding. Converting between denary, binary and hexadecimal is examined every series and is mechanical, so the loss comes from slips made under time pressure by students who never learned to verify a conversion by converting it back. The second common loss is file size and sound or image representation calculations, where the method is right and the units are dropped. Both are fixable with short, frequent, timed practice rather than with more teaching of the concept.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a programming task the school has set without doing it?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is the only version of this work we offer. A tutor can explain the construct the task needs, demonstrate it on an unrelated problem, review the student's attempt and explain why it fails, and teach the student to trace their own logic. A tutor does not produce the code that is handed in. Work submitted to a school or to a board must be the student's own, and anything else puts the student at risk rather than the provider. Feedback given as instruction is slower once and faster thereafter.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in Dubai need a permit to teach my child computing?
faqs.answer: Individuals giving private lessons in the UAE need the private tuition work permit introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued by MoHRE. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published. MoHRE's private tutor licensing service is the official application route.

faqs.question: Is 0478 good preparation for A Level Computer Science 9618?
faqs.answer: It is the intended foundation, but the step up is real. The A Level assumes fluency in one text-based language and goes considerably deeper on data structures, logic, system software and a programming project. Students who reached a strong 0478 grade by memorising answer patterns rather than understanding mechanisms tend to find the first term of Year 12 difficult. The useful preparation is the summer between the two years: build genuine fluency in one language, without a deadline, before the course assumes it.

faqs.question: How early before the June series should 0478 revision start properly?
faqs.answer: The habit work should start in the autumn of Year 11, because trace tables, handwritten pseudocode and answer-length discipline are habits rather than content and they take weeks to settle. Content revision has a different timetable: all six systems topics covered and scored by the end of term one, databases and Boolean logic secure by February, and full papers under timing from February onwards. A student starting in April can still gain real marks from the short topics, which is why the diagnostic comes before any plan.

faqs.question: What if our child's school has no specialist computer science teacher?
faqs.answer: It is more common than parents expect, particularly in schools where one teacher covers computing, ICT and design technology. The practical signs are a syllabus covered out of order, Boolean logic and databases arriving in the final term, and no handwritten algorithm practice at all. One-to-one work can cover those gaps, but the sequencing has to be deliberate: topics first, then habits, then timed papers. Tell us what the school has actually taught so far rather than what the syllabus says, because the two often differ.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-coordinated-scienc.programmesIntro: 0654 sits inside a British-curriculum pathway that most Dubai schools run from Year 7 through to Year 13. programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: Three years of integrated science taught as biology, chemistry and physics strands with shared practical skills. Checkpoint tests in science sit in the March, May and October windows Cambridge publishes for Primary and Lower Secondary. Weak Year 9 practical-skills marks are the clearest early signal that Paper 5 or Paper 6 will be a problem two years later.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools use Year 9 Checkpoint data to set the Core or Extended tier for Year 10, and that decision is usually made in the spring term. A family that wants Extended science but has a Year 9 report pointing at Core has roughly one term to change the picture, which is why February and March bookings for Year 9 science are heavier here than anywhere else in the calendar.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, including Coordinated Sciences 0654
programmes.description: Two years, typically eight to ten subject entries. 0654 occupies two of them because it is a double award. Candidates sit a multiple-choice paper, a structured theory paper and either a practical test or its written alternative, entered at Core or Extended tier across the whole award rather than paper by paper.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's British-curriculum schools dominate by enrolment, and 0654 is the pragmatic choice where a timetable cannot fit three separate sciences alongside Arabic, Islamic Education and UAE Social Studies, which KHDA requires in every Dubai private school regardless of the licensed curriculum. That timetable pressure is why double-award science is more common in this city than the Cambridge global average would suggest.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: Three or four subjects over two years. Science A Levels assume an Extended-tier IGCSE foundation: the quantitative chemistry, mole calculations and electricity content in the first term of AS is pitched at students who met it at Extended, not Core. A double award covers the ground but at less depth than a separate-science entry.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai sixth forms running Cambridge A Level science will usually ask for a grade 6 or above in 0654 before admitting a student to AS Chemistry or Physics, and some ask for separate sciences outright. If A Level science is the plan, that entry requirement is worth reading in Year 10, not Year 11, because the tier decision is harder to reverse later.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects plus the core. International Baccalaureate accounts for 7% of Dubai private-school pupils, so a sizeable minority of 0654 candidates move into DP rather than A Level. DP Biology, Chemistry and Physics at Standard Level are reachable from a double award; Higher Level assumes more quantitative fluency than Core-tier 0654 builds.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, three of them International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. For a Year 11 student on 0654 that widens the post-16 options locally, and it makes the SL-versus-HL science decision a live one in the same term as the IGCSE exams.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-coordinated-scienc.subjectsIntro: A 0654 tutor is covering three mark schemes at once. These are the content blocks the award is built from, plus the neighbouring Cambridge codes families most often confuse it with when they read the statement of entry.

subjects.name: Biology content within 0654
subjects.description: Characteristics of living organisms, cells, enzymes, nutrition, transport in humans and plants, respiration, coordination, reproduction, inheritance and organisms in their environment. Marks go missing on enzyme graph interpretation and on genetics crosses where the student knows the biology but writes the ratio without the gametes.

subjects.name: Chemistry content within 0654
subjects.description: Particles, atomic structure, bonding, stoichiometry, electrochemistry, energetics, rates, acids and bases, the periodic table, metals, chemistry of the environment and organic chemistry. The mole is the single heaviest loss point, and it is an Extended-tier problem far more than a Core one.

subjects.name: Physics content within 0654
subjects.description: Motion, forces, energy, work and power, thermal physics, waves, light, sound, magnetism, electricity, electromagnetism and radioactivity. Electricity circuits cost more marks than any other physics block in a double award, usually because series and parallel reasoning was never practised on a drawn circuit.

subjects.name: Practical skills across all three sciences
subjects.description: Measuring, recording, plotting, drawing conclusions and evaluating a method. This is assessed either as a timed practical test or as a written alternative, and it is the component where a tutor can move marks fastest because the skills are generic and examinable in a predictable format.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Combined Science 0653
subjects.description: The single-award sibling of 0654. Same three sciences, less content, one IGCSE grade rather than two. Dubai schools sometimes move a student from 0654 to 0653 in Year 11 if the workload is unmanageable, and the switch changes which papers are entered.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physical Science 0652
subjects.description: Chemistry and physics only, no biology. Chosen where a student wants the two quantitative sciences without the biology load. The chemistry and physics content overlaps heavily with 0654, so a tutor who teaches one usually teaches the other.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: The separate-science biology entry. Deeper than the biology inside a double award, with its own practical paper. Students who want Biology at A Level or DP Higher Level are usually better served here, and some Dubai sixth forms say so in their entry requirements.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Separate-science chemistry, with substantially more organic chemistry and more quantitative work than the 0654 chemistry strand. The commonest reason a Dubai family adds tutoring in Year 11 is a plan to sit 0620 alongside or instead of the double award.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Separate-science physics. More mechanics, more electricity, and a practical paper that rewards graph-drawing precision. A 0654 student considering Physics A Level should look at the 0625 content list to see what the double award leaves out.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: The quiet dependency. Rearranging formulae, standard form, ratio and gradient work all show up in 0654 chemistry and physics answers. A student losing marks on calculation questions in science frequently has a maths problem wearing a science costume.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel Science Double Award 4SD0

sections.heading: The six things that move your quote in this emirate
paragraphs: Parents often assume the variable is tutor quality. In Dubai it is more often logistics. Six inputs explain most of the spread between an AED 150 quote and an AED 450 one, and four of them are things you can change before you ask for a price.

Travel is the biggest. A tutor driving from Deira to Dubai Sports City at 5.30pm is committing two hours to deliver one, and no sustainable rate hides that. The second is coverage: a double-award tutor is being asked to hold three syllabuses, and generalists who teach one science will either decline or quietly cover only the part they know. The third is session length, where a 90-minute slot almost always has a lower effective hourly rate than a 60-minute one because the setup cost is amortised. The fourth is timing in the exam cycle. The fifth is whether siblings share the slot, which this market prices at a discount per student rather than per session. The sixth is tier, because Extended-tier preparation involves quantitative chemistry and electromagnetism work that takes longer to teach than the Core equivalents.

The permit position is worth knowing because it sits behind some of the cheapest quotes you will see. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so nobody should be quoting you an amount. Ask any tutor you are considering whether they hold the permit; it costs them nothing to obtain, which makes not having one a choice rather than a hardship.

A separate rule applies in Abu Dhabi and is worth knowing if you move emirates: ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. It is press-reported rather than quoted from the policy document here, so verify it against the current ADEK text before relying on it, but the principle behind it — your child's own class teacher should not be their paid tutor — is sound practice in Dubai too.

sections.heading: Coordinated Sciences 0654 is one grade covering three sciences
paragraphs: 0654 is Cambridge's double-award coordinated science. A candidate sits one set of papers and the result is reported as a double award, which is why it occupies two slots on a results sheet. The content is coordinated rather than combined: the biology, chemistry and physics strands are sequenced so that ideas like energy transfer or particle behaviour are met in a consistent form across all three, instead of three departments teaching the same idea three different ways.

The assessment has three components. A multiple-choice paper, a structured theory paper, and a practical component that is either a timed practical test or a written alternative to it. The tier your school enters decides which versions of the first two your child sits: Core candidates take the Core multiple-choice and Core theory papers, Extended candidates take the Extended versions. The practical component does not change with tier, which is one reason it is the fairest place to chase marks. Component weightings and durations are printed in the Cambridge syllabus document for 0654; the version that matters is the one for your child's exam series, and it is worth downloading from cambridgeinternational.org rather than trusting a summary, including this one.

The practical choice is made by the school, not the family. Paper 5 is a hands-on test sat in a laboratory with a supervisor; Paper 6 is a written alternative that asks the same skills in the abstract, with described apparatus and supplied readings. Schools without the laboratory capacity to run a timed practical for a large cohort choose Paper 6. Some Dubai schools with strong facilities still choose Paper 6 because it is easier to invigilate across multiple sessions. Ask which one is entered before paying for any practical preparation, because preparing for the wrong one is the most common way families waste money on this syllabus.

One more structural point that catches parents: entry is at the award level, not the paper level. You do not sit Extended chemistry and Core biology. The tier applies to the whole double award, so a student strong in biology and weak in quantitative chemistry has a genuine decision to make, and it is a decision about where the grade ceiling sits rather than about effort.

sections.heading: A tutor in the room versus a tutor on screen, costed for a Dubai school run
paragraphs: This is the comparison the search term implies, so here it is without the sales gloss. A tutor who travels to you is buying back a logistical problem: nobody drives to a centre, the student is in a familiar room, and younger children settle faster. Those are real advantages and parents who want them are not wrong. What they cost, in this city, is a rate at the upper end of the AED 180 to 500 band, a tutor chosen from whoever is within reasonable driving distance of your community, and a session time dictated by traffic rather than by when your child concentrates best.

Home visits in Dubai are not something IB Gram sells, so this page cannot pretend to be neutral. What it can do is show the trade honestly. The case for live video on this particular syllabus is unusually strong, and it is about supply rather than technology. Double-award science needs a tutor who holds biology, chemistry and physics at IGCSE depth. In a drive-time radius around Al Furjan or Dubai Silicon Oasis on a weekday evening, that is a handful of people. Without the radius, it is everyone who teaches the syllabus. The practical component makes the same point from the other direction: Paper 6 is a written paper about described apparatus, and teaching it on a shared screen with the diagram annotated live is at least as effective as teaching it across a dining table.

The honest limitation is Paper 5. If your child's school entered the hands-on practical test, some of that preparation genuinely belongs in a laboratory, and the right answer is to use the school's practical sessions properly rather than to buy a tutor who claims to replace them. What a tutor can do for Paper 5 is everything around the apparatus: planning the table before the readings start, choosing scales, spotting anomalous results, and writing the conclusion and evaluation that carry the marks. That part transfers to a screen without loss.

The third option families consider is a tuition centre group class, usually sold as a monthly package. It is the cheapest per hour and the weakest fit for 0654, because a group moving at one pace cannot serve a student whose biology is fine and whose chemistry is not. For a double award specifically, the whole point of one-to-one is that the three strands are almost never equally weak.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the decision that changes how many hours you buy
paragraphs: Tiering is where 0654 differs most sharply from a single-science entry, and where a tutoring budget is most often misallocated. The tier is set by the school, usually on the strength of Year 9 data and early Year 10 assessments, and it applies to the entire double award. A Core entry caps the grade a candidate can be awarded; an Extended entry opens the top grades but puts harder content and harder papers in front of a student who may not be ready for them.

The practical consequence for a parent buying hours: a Core student and an Extended student need different tutoring. A Core candidate is working on completeness and command-term precision — making sure every question gets a scoring answer rather than a half-answer, and that describe, explain, state and suggest are each answered in their own register. An Extended candidate is working on the quantitative spine: moles, concentrations, rearranged equations, circuit reasoning and multi-step calculations where the marks sit in the working rather than the answer.

If your child is borderline, the most useful thing a tutor can do in the first month is diagnose which content, specifically, is keeping them in Core. It is almost never all three sciences. In the double-award cohorts we see in Dubai, the blocker is most often quantitative chemistry, followed by electricity in physics. Both are teachable in a defined number of weeks, and both show up as a visible change in school assessment marks, which is the evidence a school needs before it moves a student up a tier. That conversation has a deadline: once the entry is submitted it is a school administrative matter to change it, not a teaching one.

One caution. A tier change is a school decision made on school evidence, and no tutor can promise one. What a tutor can do is make the evidence exist by a particular date. If a provider tells you they can get your child moved to Extended, ask them what they are actually proposing to do, and treat the promise itself as a warning sign.

sections.heading: Paper 5 or Paper 6: the cheapest marks on this syllabus
paragraphs: The practical component carries roughly a fifth of the double award and is the only part that does not change with tier. It is also the part most families ignore until the mock results come back, which is why it is the best value block of tutoring available on 0654. The skills involved are generic, the question formats repeat across series, and almost all of the marks are awarded for things that can be taught rather than things that have to be remembered.

Start by finding out which paper the school entered. Paper 5 is a timed practical test under supervision; Paper 6 is a written alternative that assesses the same skills from described apparatus and supplied readings. The two demand different preparation. A student entered for Paper 6 does not need laboratory time; they need practice reading a described method, spotting the controlled variable, and writing an evaluation that identifies a weakness in the procedure rather than in their own performance. A student entered for Paper 5 needs both the bench skills and the paperwork around them.

What repeatedly costs marks in both versions: tables drawn after the readings are taken rather than before, so columns are missing headings or units; graph axes chosen so the points occupy a third of the grid; best-fit lines drawn through the first and last point instead of through the trend; conclusions that restate the readings instead of answering the question asked; and evaluations that say the student should have been more careful. Each of those is a rule a tutor can teach in one session and a student can practise in ten minutes a week.

A reasonable plan for a Year 11 student in Dubai is four to six focused sessions on the practical component, taken in the autumn term rather than in the spring. Autumn is when tutors have availability and rates sit lower across this market, and the skills, once learned, keep paying through mocks and into the final series. Do not buy this block without first confirming the paper number on the statement of entry.

sections.heading: Where 0654 marks actually go missing, science by science
paragraphs: Double-award students rarely lose marks evenly. The pattern across Dubai cohorts is consistent enough to plan around, and it matters for budgeting because it tells you which strand to buy hours for rather than paying for a general science tutor to cover everything slowly.

In chemistry, the mole dominates. Moles, concentration, reacting masses and anything requiring a balanced equation to be used rather than merely written. The underlying problem is usually arithmetic fluency rather than chemical understanding: a student who cannot rearrange a formula confidently will not produce a multi-step calculation under time pressure, however well they understand the reaction. The second chemistry loss point is electrochemistry, where products at each electrode are learned as a list instead of a rule and then misapplied.

In physics, electricity is the single biggest loss. Series and parallel reasoning, potential difference across components, and resistance combinations. Students who can recite the equations still lose marks because they do not sketch the circuit before calculating. Second is moments and equilibrium, where the geometry gets dropped. Third is radioactivity, which is normally a vocabulary problem rather than a physics one.

In biology, the content is better retained and the marks go on technique. Graph and data interpretation questions where the answer is in the figures and the student writes from memory instead. Genetics crosses written without the gametes, so the ratio appears with no working to support it. Transport and exchange questions where the answer needs a structure named and a function given, and only one of the two arrives. Across all three sciences, the quiet thief is the command term: describe answered as explain costs marks even when the science is right, and it is the fastest single thing to fix in a first month of tutoring.
bullets: Chemistry: moles, reacting masses, electrode products
Physics: series and parallel circuits, moments, radioactive vocabulary
Biology: data interpretation and genetics working
All three: command terms and unshown calculation steps

sections.heading: Budgeting two years of 0654 support in a Dubai context
paragraphs: Tutoring is bought alongside school fees, and in Dubai that context has changed. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a family planning two years of IGCSE support, a flat fee year is the first piece of good news in a while, and it makes a weekly tutoring line easier to commit to.

The scale of the market explains why the rate spread is so wide. Dubai had 387,441 private-school pupils across 227 schools in 2024-25, offering 17 curricula, with UK curriculum at 37% of enrolment, Indian at 26%, US at 14% and International Baccalaureate at 7%. A UK-curriculum share that size means tens of thousands of IGCSE candidates in any given series, and a tutoring market deep enough to contain both a AED 45 university student and a AED 650 specialist. The 2026-27 intake adds seven more private schools and 16,846 places, so demand for Year 10 and 11 support is not about to soften.

A realistic two-year plan, costed at market rates rather than ours: a weekly 60-minute session through Year 10 at the qualified-tutor band, stepping up to 90 minutes in Year 11, with a four-to-six-session practical block in the autumn of Year 11 and a short intensive before the series. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Those are the brackets to plan against.

Where families overspend: buying three sciences' worth of tutoring when one strand is the problem, booking the practical block in April instead of October, paying for a tutor who travels when the same money buys a better-matched tutor on screen, and continuing a weekly session through a term where the student needed marked written work instead. Where families underspend: skipping the practical component entirely, and leaving the tier conversation until the entry is already in.

sections.heading: What a 0654 tutor may and may not do, and how to verify one
paragraphs: There is a line in this market that matters more in science than parents expect, because 0654 has no coursework. There is no internal assessment to mishandle, which removes the worst temptation. What remains is more mundane and still worth stating: a tutor teaches, explains, sets practice and marks it. A tutor does not sit a paper, does not supply the school's internal assessment answers, and does not distribute copyrighted Cambridge material. Past papers and mark schemes belong to Cambridge; the right thing for a tutor to do is point you at cambridgeinternational.org and at your school, not host a download library.

On verification, three checks cover most of the risk. Ask whether the tutor holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is granted free of charge for two years under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system; MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Ask which syllabus code and which practical paper they have taught most recently, and listen for whether they ask you the same question back. Ask for a marked piece of work from the first session, because a tutor who marks to the published mark scheme will show you where the marks were and were not awarded.

What nobody in this market should be telling you: that they hold KHDA approval, ADEK approval or Cambridge accreditation as a tutoring provider. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific instrument issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai, with initial approval, a maximum six-month window to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram does not hold one and does not operate premises in the UAE, which is why this page describes an online service and not a centre. Any provider implying board accreditation for private tutoring is describing something that does not exist in that form.

Finally, grades. No tutor can promise a grade on 0654 or anything else, and a provider that offers one is either misunderstanding the assessment or hoping you will not notice. What can be promised is specific and checkable: that the right papers are being prepared for, that written work comes back marked, and that you will be told plainly when a plan is not working.

faqs.question: How much does a Cambridge IGCSE Coordinated Sciences 0654 tutor cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market rates in Dubai for a qualified science tutor working online run roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, and AED 200 to 450 and above where the tutor is an IGCSE and A Level specialist. A tutor who travels to your community sits in the AED 180 to 500 band once the drive is priced in. Those figures come from published UAE rate cards and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table, read in October 2026, and they are market rates rather than IB Gram prices. Double award pushes a quote upward because the tutor must cover biology, chemistry and physics.

faqs.question: Why does a 0654 home tutor in Dubai quote more than an online one?
faqs.answer: Because you are paying for the drive. A tutor travelling to Mirdif or Dubai Sports City for a 5.30pm session commits around two hours to deliver one, and that shows up in the rate rather than disappearing. The published in-home band of AED 180 to 500 an hour reflects it. The second cost is invisible: you choose from tutors within driving distance of your community rather than from everyone who teaches the syllabus, which on a three-science award is a much smaller group. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses; lessons run one-to-one over live video.

faqs.question: Is Coordinated Sciences 0654 worth two IGCSEs on a Dubai school report?
faqs.answer: Yes. 0654 is a double award, so one entry and one set of papers produce a result reported as two IGCSE grades. That is why it appears twice on a results sheet and why it counts twice towards a sixth-form entry requirement expressed as a number of subjects. It is not the same as sitting Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625 separately: three separate entries give three grades and cover more content per science. Which route suits your child depends on what they want to study after 16, and Dubai sixth forms differ in what they ask for.

faqs.question: Which practical paper will my child sit for 0654, Paper 5 or Paper 6?
faqs.answer: That is the school's choice, not yours, and it is printed on the statement of entry. Paper 5 is a timed practical test in a laboratory with a supervisor. Paper 6 is a written alternative assessing the same skills from described apparatus and supplied readings. Schools with limited laboratory capacity for a large cohort usually enter Paper 6. Find the paper number before paying for any practical preparation, because the two require genuinely different work and preparing for the wrong one is the most common way money gets wasted on this syllabus.

faqs.question: Can my child be entered for Extended in chemistry and Core in biology?
faqs.answer: No. On 0654 the tier applies to the whole double award, so a candidate is either a Core candidate or an Extended candidate across all three sciences. That is why a student who is strong in biology and weak in quantitative chemistry faces a real decision rather than a subject-by-subject one. Core caps the grade that can be awarded; Extended opens the top grades but puts harder papers in front of the student. The school sets the tier from its own assessment data, and changing it after entry is an administrative process with its own deadline.

faqs.question: My child is in Core and we want Extended. Can a tutor move them up?
faqs.answer: A tutor cannot move a tier; a school does, on its own evidence. What a tutor can do is make that evidence exist before the entry deadline. In Dubai double-award cohorts the blocker is usually one thing rather than three: most often quantitative chemistry, sometimes electricity in physics. Both are teachable in a defined number of weeks, and improvement shows up in school assessments, which is what a head of science will look at. Any provider who promises a tier change rather than describing the work should be treated with real scepticism.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a Year 11 student on 0654 usually need?
faqs.answer: A common pattern in Dubai is one 90-minute session a week through Year 11, plus a block of four to six sessions aimed only at the practical component, taken in the autumn term rather than the spring. If the content is broadly secure and the problem is timing or technique, two or three sessions a week in the last six to eight weeks works. If whole topics are missing, an intensive is the wrong purchase and a longer weekly plan is cheaper overall. The diagnostic session exists to tell you which situation you are in.

faqs.question: Do Dubai tutoring rates really rise closer to the exam series?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the effect is noticeable. A tutor with open slots in September is in a different commercial position from the same tutor in March, six weeks before the June series, when every Year 11 family in the emirate is looking for the same hours. The practical skills block is the clearest example: the content does not change between October and April, but availability and price do. Families who plan the practical component into the autumn term consistently pay less for it and get more use out of it, because the skills carry through the mocks as well.

faqs.question: Does a 0654 tutor need a permit to teach privately in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so nobody should quote you an amount. The permit costs nothing to obtain, which makes it a fair question to ask any tutor.

faqs.question: Can online lessons really prepare a student for a laboratory practical test?
faqs.answer: Partly, and the honest split matters. If the school entered Paper 6, the written alternative, there is no laboratory requirement at all and a shared screen with an annotated diagram works well. If the school entered Paper 5, the bench skills belong in the school laboratory and the right move is to use those sessions properly. What transfers fully to video is everything around the apparatus: designing the results table before taking readings, choosing graph scales, drawing a best-fit line through a trend, identifying anomalies, and writing conclusions and method evaluations that actually score.

faqs.question: Which 0654 topics cost Dubai students the most marks?
faqs.answer: Three stand out. In chemistry it is the mole: reacting masses, concentrations and anything that needs a balanced equation used rather than written, usually because formula rearrangement is shaky rather than the chemistry. In physics it is electricity, particularly series and parallel reasoning where students calculate without sketching the circuit. In biology the content is better retained and marks go on technique: data questions answered from memory, and genetics crosses written without the gametes. Across all three, command terms quietly cost marks when describe is answered as explain.

faqs.question: Should we switch from 0654 to Combined Science 0653 if Year 11 is too heavy?
faqs.answer: It is a real option and schools in Dubai do it, usually at the start of Year 11. 0653 is the single-award version: same three sciences, less content, one IGCSE grade instead of two. The gain is workload; the cost is a slot on the results sheet and, potentially, a sixth-form entry requirement expressed in subject counts. It also changes which papers are entered, so any tutoring plan has to be rebuilt around the new structure. Discuss it with the head of science before paying for more hours on the double award.

faqs.question: Does my child still need Arabic and Islamic Education alongside 0654?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students with specified languages of instruction. Those subjects sit on the same timetable as science, which is part of why double-award science is more common in Dubai than a separate-science entry: the timetable has to fit them. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met.

faqs.question: What should I ask a 0654 tutor before paying for the first month?
faqs.answer: Four questions. Which practical paper has my child been entered for, and how does that change your plan? Which tier are we working towards, and what evidence would a school need to change it? What written work will come back marked, and against which mark scheme? Do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit? A tutor who asks for the statement of entry before quoting is telling you something useful. So is one who quotes a single hourly figure without asking anything at all.

faqs.question: Are IGCSE science grades enough for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: For the British track, the Ministry requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at E or above or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Because 0654 is a double award it contributes two of the five. Equivalency is handled by the Ministry, not by any tutoring provider, and the requirements should be verified on moe.gov.ae before you rely on them.

Send them over with a note on which of the three sciences is the problem, and the trial lesson will tell you whether tutoring is the right purchase at all. intro.heading: What 0654 is really testing, and why that changes the tutoring
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE Coordinated Sciences 0654 is a double award: one entry, one set of papers, two grades. Inside it, biology, chemistry and physics run as coordinated strands rather than as three separate courses, which has a specific consequence for how it is examined. Ideas that recur across the sciences — energy transfer, particle behaviour, the structure-and-function pairing — are tested in a consistent register, and a question in the physics section can draw on language a student last met in chemistry. Students who revise the three strands as three separate silos are the ones who find the paper unfamiliar even when they know the content.

The assessment has three components. A multiple-choice paper, a structured theory paper, and a practical component sat either as a laboratory test or as a written alternative. The tier decides which versions of the first two are sat: Core candidates take the Core multiple-choice and Core theory papers; Extended candidates take the Extended versions. The practical component is common to both tiers. Durations, mark totals and exact weightings are printed in the Cambridge syllabus document for 0654, and the version that matters is the one published for your child's exam series — download it from cambridgeinternational.org rather than relying on a summary.

Where marks are lost on this syllabus is unusually predictable, and that predictability is the whole argument for structured one-to-one teaching rather than general revision. Roughly speaking: the multiple-choice paper punishes speed, the theory paper punishes vague command-term reading, the chemistry punishes weak formula rearrangement, the physics punishes calculating before sketching, and the biology punishes answering from memory when the data is on the page. Each of those is a habit rather than a knowledge gap, and habits respond to being named, practised and marked.

A Dubai student sits this syllabus alongside Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies, which KHDA requires in every private school in the emirate regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. The practical effect is a crowded Year 10 and 11 timetable, which is exactly why so many schools here enter the double award instead of three separate sciences. It also means science revision competes for evening hours with subjects that have their own assessment calendar.

This page does not price anything. It sets out what the papers ask, in order, with the loss points named and the fix described for each. If your child is sitting 0654 in a Dubai school this year, read the theory-paper section and the command-term table first: between them they explain most of the marks that go missing on a paper the student felt went well. Lessons from IB Gram are delivered one-to-one over live video; home visits are not a service we offer in the UAE.
bullets: Three coordinated strands examined in one consistent register
Multiple choice, structured theory, and a practical component
Tier changes the first two papers, never the practical one
Most lost marks are habits, not missing knowledge
Command-term precision is the fastest available gain

dubai/cambridge-igcse-coordinated-scienc.programmesIntro: 0654 is assessed at one point in a longer British-curriculum sequence. What a tutor should be doing depends far more on where the student sits in that sequence than on the calendar year, so these are the four stages that matter.

programmes.name: Lower secondary science, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: Integrated science with shared practical skills. The assessable habits that later decide 0654 marks are formed here: drawing a results table before taking readings, choosing a graph scale, writing a conclusion that answers the question asked. Cambridge runs Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October windows.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the Year 9 science report is effectively the tier decision for 0654, because schools set Core and Extended sets in the spring term. A student whose written work is strong but whose practical-skills marks are weak will often be placed by the practical marks, which surprises families who have only been watching topic tests.

programmes.name: 0654 Year 10: content delivery
programmes.description: Most of the content is taught in Year 10, usually by three teachers working to a coordinated scheme. The failure mode is quiet: a student keeps up with each teacher individually and never links the strands, so the first full mock paper reads as three unfamiliar subjects rather than one.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools with multi-form entries often rotate science teachers each term, which is efficient for staffing and hard on continuity. A Year 10 tutor's most useful job here is keeping one running record of what has actually been covered, because the student frequently cannot say and the school's scheme of work is not always what was taught.

programmes.name: 0654 Year 11: assessment technique
programmes.description: Content consolidation plus the papers themselves. This is the year command terms, timing, working-out discipline and the practical component decide the grade. A student who knows the syllabus and has never been marked against the published scheme will underperform their own understanding.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai mocks usually fall in November and again in February or March, and they are the evidence a school uses for predicted grades and for any tier change. That makes the autumn term, not the spring, the point at which tutoring changes outcomes rather than confirming them.

programmes.name: What comes after the double award
programmes.description: A Level sciences or IB Diploma sciences. Both assume the Extended-tier quantitative foundation: moles and concentration for chemistry, circuit reasoning and kinematics for physics. A double award covers the ground with less depth per science than a separate-science entry, which matters at Higher Level.
programmes.countryNote: International Baccalaureate accounts for 7% of Dubai private-school pupils and the emirate's 2026-27 intake adds three new IB schools among seven new private schools, creating 16,846 places. For a 0654 candidate that widens the post-16 choice locally, and it makes the Standard-versus-Higher Level science decision live in the same term as the IGCSE papers.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-coordinated-scienc.subjectsIntro: A session has to name a topic, not a science. These are the content blocks the 0654 outline is built from, with the examinable weakness each one tends to produce in a double-award cohort.

subjects.name: Cells and movement in and out of cells
subjects.description: Cell structure, specialised cells, diffusion, osmosis and active transport. Osmosis questions involving potato or visking tubing data are a reliable loss point because students describe the water movement without naming the concentration gradient the mark scheme wants.

subjects.name: Biological molecules and enzymes
subjects.description: Carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, food tests and enzyme action. Enzyme graph questions ask for an explanation at each region of the curve; answers that say the enzyme dies rather than denatures lose the mark even where the understanding is sound.

subjects.name: Plant and human nutrition
subjects.description: Photosynthesis, limiting factors, leaf structure, the alimentary canal and digestion. Limiting-factor questions reward reading the plateau on the graph and naming what has become limiting; most dropped marks are answers written from memory instead of from the figure.

subjects.name: Transport, respiration and gas exchange
subjects.description: Circulatory system, blood vessels, the heart, breathing and aerobic and anaerobic respiration. Structure-and-function pairs are examined together, so an answer naming only the structure or only the function collects half the available credit.

subjects.name: Coordination, homeostasis and reproduction
subjects.description: Nervous and hormonal coordination, the eye, temperature and glucose regulation, and reproduction in plants and humans. Negative-feedback questions need the stimulus, the receptor, the response and the return to normal, in that order, and partial sequences score partially.

subjects.name: Inheritance, variation and ecology
subjects.description: Chromosomes, mitosis and meiosis, monohybrid inheritance, variation, selection, food chains and nutrient cycles. Genetics crosses written without the gametes set out are the single most common avoidable loss in the biology strand.

subjects.name: Atoms, bonding and stoichiometry
subjects.description: Atomic structure, ionic and covalent bonding, formulae, equations and the mole. The quantitative spine of the whole award. Extended candidates who cannot rearrange a formula under time pressure lose multi-mark questions they could otherwise answer.

subjects.name: Electrochemistry, energetics and rates
subjects.description: Electrolysis, exothermic and endothermic change, reaction rate and the factors affecting it. Electrode products learned as a memorised list rather than as a rule misapply as soon as the electrolyte changes, which is exactly what the question does.

subjects.name: Acids, bases, salts and the periodic table
subjects.description: Acid reactions, neutralisation, salt preparation, periodic trends and group properties. Salt-preparation method questions are practical questions in disguise, and they reward the filtration, evaporation and crystallisation sequence stated in the right order.

subjects.name: Metals, the environment and organic chemistry
subjects.description: Reactivity series, extraction, corrosion, air quality, water treatment, fuels, alkanes, alkenes, alcohols and polymers. Organic naming and functional-group recognition are quick wins; the environmental chemistry questions reward precise named substances rather than general descriptions.

subjects.name: Motion, forces and energy
subjects.description: Speed, acceleration, distance-time and speed-time graphs, forces, moments, energy stores and transfers, work and power. Graph-gradient and area-under-graph questions are where the physics strand quietly separates grades.

subjects.name: Thermal physics, waves, light and sound
subjects.description: Particle model, expansion, heat transfer, wave properties, reflection, refraction and sound. Refraction questions need the ray drawn and the angle labelled relative to the normal; answers without the normal drawn cost marks regardless of the explanation.

subjects.name: Electricity, circuits and electromagnetism
subjects.description: Current, potential difference, resistance, series and parallel circuits, electrical safety, magnetism and the motor effect. The highest-value block in the physics strand for a tutor, because the reasoning is systematic and students almost never sketch the circuit first.

subjects.name: Atomic physics and radioactivity
subjects.description: Atomic model, isotopes, radiation types, half-life and safety. Mostly a precision-of-language problem: alpha, beta and gamma properties confused in a comparison question, and half-life calculations done by guesswork instead of by halving systematically.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-coordinated-scienc.regionsIntro: Science provision varies more across Dubai than parents expect, and the variation matters because it decides whether a student has had genuine practical exposure and how early the tier was fixed. Each note below is about school science capacity rather than driving distance.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Long-established schools with mature science departments and the capacity to run separate sciences alongside the double award. Students here are usually in a set, and the set they are in has already shaped the tier.

regions.name: Al Safa and Al Wasl
regions.note: Mid-sized British-curriculum schools where science sets are smaller and a student's weak strand can go unnoticed for a term. Enquiries from this cluster often follow a mock where one of the three sciences dragged the whole paper down.

regions.name: Dubai Festival City and Al Garhoud
regions.note: Large cohorts with well-equipped laboratories, so the hands-on practical test is more likely to be the entered component. Practical preparation here needs to complement school laboratory time rather than substitute for it.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba and Meydan
regions.note: Newer communities feeding newer schools with growing science departments. Schemes of work are still settling, so a running record of what has actually been taught is more useful here than a generic revision plan.

regions.name: Al Quoz and Dubai Investment Park
regions.note: Schools serving a broad fee range with large double-award entries. The written alternative to practical is common where laboratory capacity has to serve several hundred candidates in one series.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and The Springs
regions.note: Villa communities with established schools and strong parental visibility of grades. Students here typically arrive with a clear picture of which strand is weak, which shortens the diagnostic stage considerably.

regions.name: Dubai Creek Harbour and Sobha Hartland
regions.note: Recently opened schools with small Year 11 cohorts. Small cohorts mean fewer sets and more mixed-ability teaching, which raises the value of one-to-one work on the specific topics a student missed.

regions.name: Discovery Gardens and Al Furjan
regions.note: Apartment-dense communities with a wide mix of school choices and frequent mid-year transfers. Transfer students often arrive having covered the strands in a different order, which needs mapping before any revision plan is written.

schoolClusters.city: Jumeirah, Al Safa and Umm Suqeim
schoolClusters.note: Schools in this cluster usually run both separate sciences and the double award, so the question for a 0654 student is often whether the set placement still matches their current attainment. Students we support here commonly need one strand lifted rather than a general science programme.

schoolClusters.city: Al Garhoud, Festival City and Mirdif
schoolClusters.note: Large, well-established science departments with multi-form entries and substantial double-award cohorts. Mocks in this cluster are marked tightly, which makes them a reliable baseline for a tutoring plan and for any conversation about tier.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai Hills, Al Quoz and Nad Al Sheba
schoolClusters.note: A mix of recently opened and expanding schools where the Year 11 cohort may be the school's first or second. Scheme-of-work gaps are more likely here, and the first useful piece of tutoring is a content audit rather than paper practice.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-coordinated-scienc.modesIntro: All sessions run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, with the paper on a shared screen. These are the three shapes that actually suit a double award, and what each one is for.

modes.title: Diagnostic session on a marked paper
modes.description: A single session built around a paper the student has already sat, with the mark scheme open. The point is not to reteach the paper; it is to classify every lost mark as missing content, misread command term, unshown working or careless practical technique. That classification is what decides whether the next purchase is one strand or three.
bullets: Bring a marked mock, not a tidy revision guide
Every lost mark classified by cause, not by topic
Output is a written list of what to work on in order
Often the only session a well-taught student needs

modes.title: Single-strand teaching block
modes.description: Four to eight sessions aimed at one of the three sciences, usually chemistry or physics, because those are the strands where a double-award student most often loses systematically rather than occasionally. Each session ends with a timed question set, which comes back marked against the published scheme before the next one.
bullets: One strand at a time, taught in syllabus order
Timed question set after every session
Working-out discipline taught explicitly, not assumed
Progress measured on marks, not on confidence

modes.title: Paper-technique sessions before the series
modes.description: Short sessions in the final weeks that practise the papers as papers: reading time, question order, how long to spend on a six-mark question, when to leave one. Suitable only once the content is broadly secure, and the diagnostic session is what establishes whether it is.
bullets: Timing rehearsed on full papers, not single questions
Command-term drills on past questions
Practical-component question types practised separately
Sessions can move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan

sections.heading: The command terms decide more marks than the content does
paragraphs: A double-award student who knows the science and still scores below expectation is almost always answering a different question from the one asked. Cambridge papers use command terms precisely: state, describe, explain, suggest, compare, calculate and determine each have a required answer shape, and the mark scheme is written against that shape. An explanation offered where a description was asked for scores; a description offered where an explanation was asked for usually does not, because the because-clause carrying the mark never arrives.

This is the fastest available gain on 0654 and it is almost never taught directly. In a first month of tutoring, naming the command term at the start of every answer and checking the answer against it is worth more marks per hour of effort than any amount of content revision. It also transfers across all three strands at once, which matters on a double award where tutoring time is divided.

The second half of the same problem is mark allocation. A four-mark question wants four distinct scoring points, and students routinely write one point expressed four ways. Counting the marks before writing is a mechanical habit that can be installed in a single session and then reinforced on every marked piece of work afterwards. Where a question asks for two named examples and a reason, the answer needs exactly those three things in a form the examiner can tick.

The table below sets out the terms that appear most across the 0654 strands and what the mark scheme is looking for in each case. It is worth reading next to a past paper rather than on its own, because the pattern becomes obvious once applied to real questions.

sections.heading: The multiple-choice paper punishes speed, not ignorance
paragraphs: The multiple-choice component is where confident students lose the most unnecessary marks on 0654. It is the shortest paper, it feels easy in the room, and students finish it early. Nobody re-checks a paper they found easy, which means the two or three items misread rather than misunderstood stay wrong. On a paper of this length, two careless items is a visible difference in the final grade.

The items themselves are written to catch specific errors. Distractors in the chemistry section usually correspond to a predictable mistake: a formula not balanced, a mole calculation done with mass instead of moles, an electrode product taken from the wrong half of the cell. In physics, distractors catch unit confusion and reciprocal errors in resistance combinations. In biology, they catch definitions that are nearly right, which is why the strand that students find easiest still produces dropped items.

Extended-tier candidates face a further issue: the Extended multiple-choice paper includes multi-step reasoning, and multi-step reasoning in a timed multiple-choice format rewards doing the arithmetic on paper rather than in the head. Students who have never been told to use the question paper as working space will attempt a two-stage mole calculation mentally and then pick the plausible wrong answer that the examiner anticipated.

What a session does about it, concretely: a set of items done under time, then every wrong answer traced back to the distractor it matched and the error that distractor was built to catch. After two sessions of that, most students can name their own error pattern, which is the point at which re-checking becomes targeted instead of vague. The rule that follows is simple and worth stating to a Year 11 student: finish early, then re-check only the question types in your own pattern.

sections.heading: The structured theory paper, question type by question type
paragraphs: The theory paper carries the largest share of the award and it is where a tutoring plan either works or does not show. It is not a recall paper. Across both tiers it moves between short-answer recall, data interpretation from a table or graph, applied reasoning in an unfamiliar context, and calculation. Each of those four behaves differently under the mark scheme, and a student can be fluent in one and lost in another while feeling generally prepared.

Data-interpretation questions are the clearest example of a question type that rewards method over knowledge. The answer is on the page: a trend, a plateau, an anomalous point, a value to read off. Students who have revised hard are the most likely to answer from memory instead of from the figure, and memory answers do not match the data-specific mark scheme. Teaching a student to annotate the figure before writing anything is a single-session intervention with a measurable effect on the next mock.

Applied reasoning is the question type Extended candidates find hardest, because the context is unfamiliar by design. The syllabus content is all there; what is being tested is whether the student can carry it into a new setting. The teachable move is to identify which syllabus idea the question is about before attempting an answer, which sounds obvious and is almost never done under pressure. Calculation questions, meanwhile, lose marks for unshown working more often than for arithmetic: method marks exist and a bare answer forfeits them.

The table below maps the four question types to what a session actually changes. It is deliberately specific about evidence, because a parent paying for sessions is entitled to know what should look different in six weeks and on which paper.
