sections.heading: Quantitative chemistry: the block that sets the grade ceiling
paragraphs: If a double-award student has one systematic weakness, the odds favour quantitative chemistry. Moles, relative formula mass, reacting masses, concentration, percentage yield where it appears, and anything that requires a balanced equation to be used rather than simply written. On Extended-tier papers this content recurs in both the multiple-choice and the theory paper, so a weakness here is charged twice.

The underlying cause is usually not chemical. A student who cannot confidently rearrange a formula, convert units, or handle standard form will not complete a two-stage calculation under time pressure, however well they understand the reaction. This is why a competent 0654 tutor will check basic algebraic fluency early: a term spent on chemistry content when the problem is formula rearrangement produces no mark movement and a frustrated student.

The teachable structure is a fixed sequence. Write the balanced equation. Convert what you are given into moles. Use the ratio from the equation. Convert back into the quantity asked for. State the unit. Students who learn this as four steps with a written line for each collect method marks even when the final figure is wrong, and on a multi-mark question that is a substantial difference. Students who do mental arithmetic and write a single number get one mark or none.

Electrochemistry sits next to this and fails differently. Electrode products are frequently memorised as a list from one example, then misapplied the moment the electrolyte changes, which is exactly the variation the examiner introduces. Taught as a rule — what is present, what is preferentially discharged, what that means at each electrode — it becomes reliable. Taught as a list, it collapses. The same applies to the reactivity series, which is useful as a pattern and useless as a recitation.
bullets: Check algebraic fluency before teaching more chemistry content
Four written lines for every mole calculation, unit last
Electrode products as a rule, never as a memorised list
Reactivity series used to predict, not recited

sections.heading: Electricity and electromagnetism: the physics block worth the most
paragraphs: Electricity is the highest-value block in the physics strand of 0654 for a tutor to work on, because the reasoning is systematic, the question formats repeat across series, and the commonest error is procedural rather than conceptual. Students calculate before they sketch. Given a circuit described in words or shown partially, they reach for an equation instead of drawing the circuit, labelling the current direction and marking the potential differences they know.

Series and parallel reasoning accounts for most of the loss. Current the same throughout a series circuit, potential difference shared; current shared in parallel branches, potential difference the same across them. Stated like that it sounds trivial, and under exam conditions students apply the series rule to a parallel branch roughly as often as not. The fix is a sketch-first rule enforced on every question until it is automatic, plus practice on the question style where a component is added or removed and the student must say what happens to the readings.

Resistance combinations are the second loss point, with reciprocal errors in parallel resistance being the predictable mistake the multiple-choice distractors are built around. The third is electrical safety and power, where the content is easy and the questions reward naming the specific component or hazard rather than describing it in general terms. Electromagnetism, including the motor effect and simple transformers at Extended tier, is more often a diagram problem than a physics problem: a field direction drawn wrong propagates through the whole answer.

What this looks like in a session: a circuit diagram on the shared screen, annotated live, with the student making the predictions and the tutor only writing what the student says. That is deliberately slower than explaining, and it is the only version that produces an exam habit rather than a nod of agreement.

sections.heading: The biology strand: technique, not recall
paragraphs: Across the double-award cohorts seen in Dubai schools, biology is the strand students retain best and the one where the marks lost are most clearly technique rather than knowledge. That is encouraging, because technique is quicker to fix than content, and it is also easy to misdiagnose: a parent looking at a weak biology score reasonably assumes the biology was not learned.

Three failures account for most of it. First, data and graph questions answered from memory rather than from the figure provided, which is the same error as in chemistry and physics and shows up most in photosynthesis limiting-factor and enzyme-curve questions. Second, genetics crosses written without the gametes set out, so a correct ratio appears with no working to support it and the method marks are forfeited. Third, structure-and-function questions answered with only one half, when the mark scheme requires both and the question asked for both.

A fourth, quieter one: definitions in biology are marked tightly. Osmosis, diffusion, active transport, respiration and photosynthesis all have required elements, and nearly-right definitions score nothing. Rehearsing those in mark-scheme language is unglamorous work and it is reliably worth marks on both the multiple-choice and the theory paper.

In practice a biology block for a 0654 student is short. Four sessions covering data technique, genetics working, definition precision and the structure-function pairing will usually move more marks than a term of general biology revision, because the content is mostly already there. That is also why a proper diagnostic session matters: without one, a family can easily buy a long biology programme when what was needed was a short one and a chemistry block.
bullets: Annotate every figure before writing an answer
Gametes written out on every genetics cross
Structure and function both named when both are asked
Core definitions rehearsed in mark-scheme wording

sections.heading: The practical component as a set of rules
paragraphs: The practical component is common to both tiers and carries roughly a fifth of the double award. Whether your child sits the laboratory test or the written alternative is a school decision printed on the statement of entry, and the two need different preparation. The skills behind both, however, are the same, and they are rules rather than talents, which is why this is the most teachable component on the syllabus.

The rules that recover the most marks: draw the results table before taking or reading any measurements, with column headings and units in place. Choose graph scales so the plotted points fill at least half the grid in both directions. Plot accurately, then draw a single best-fit line through the trend rather than connecting the first and last points. Identify anomalous results explicitly rather than quietly ignoring them. Write a conclusion that answers the question asked rather than restating the readings. Evaluate the method, not the experimenter.

That last one is worth labouring. Asked to evaluate, students write that they should have been more careful or should have repeated the experiment more times. Neither scores reliably. What scores is identifying a specific weakness in the procedure — a variable that was not controlled, a measurement whose resolution was too coarse for the change being observed, a reading taken at a point where the quantity was still changing — and saying what would improve it. Taught as a template with three slots, this becomes a dependable source of marks.

A student entered for the written alternative does not need laboratory access, and teaching this component over a shared screen with the described apparatus annotated live works well. A student entered for the laboratory test should use school practical sessions for the bench skills and use tutoring for everything around the apparatus: the table, the scales, the anomalies, the conclusion and the evaluation. That split is honest and it is also where the marks actually are.

sections.heading: What one session can fix, and what takes a term
paragraphs: Parents are rarely told this plainly, so here it is. Some 0654 problems are single-session fixes, some are four-to-six-session blocks, and some are a term's work. Knowing which you are buying is the difference between tutoring that shows up in a mock and tutoring that quietly continues.

Single-session fixes are procedural: counting marks before writing, annotating a figure, laying out a mole calculation in lines, sketching a circuit before calculating, using the results-table-first rule. These are habits. They are installed in one session and then reinforced through marked work, and the reinforcement matters more than the explanation. A student can nod at all five in an hour and apply none of them under exam pressure without several weeks of marked practice.

Block-sized problems are topic-shaped: quantitative chemistry, electricity, genetics and data technique, the practical component. Four to eight sessions each, taught in syllabus order with timed questions in between. Term-sized problems are different in kind: a student who missed a long stretch of Year 10 through a school transfer, a student whose tier was set too high and who is now meeting Extended content without the Core foundation, or a student whose maths is not yet strong enough to support the quantitative work. Those need a plan measured in months, and a tutor who describes them as a quick fix is not being straight with you.

The honest version of availability, too. If no specialist covering all three sciences at the level and time you need is free, you will be told that rather than matched with whoever is available. Where a UAE-based tutor is not available for a niche combination, the alternative offered is an experienced IGCSE science tutor working from India to Gulf Standard Time, stated openly before you book, not discovered afterwards.

sections.heading: How an online 0654 session actually runs
paragraphs: The mechanics matter because they decide whether a session produces evidence. Lessons run one-to-one over live video with a shared whiteboard and the paper or question set on screen. The student writes; the tutor annotates. Work is photographed or scanned, submitted between sessions, and returned marked against the published Cambridge mark scheme with the marks attributed to specific points rather than given as a total. Where a mark was not awarded, the reason is written next to it.

That last detail is the whole point. A marked total tells a parent nothing. A script showing that four of the six lost marks were method marks on calculation questions tells you exactly what the next three sessions should do, and it gives a head of science something concrete if a tier conversation is coming. It also makes the tutoring falsifiable: if the same category of loss is still appearing after six weeks, the plan is wrong and should change.

Scheduling is built around Dubai school hours. Sessions sit after the school run and after activities, in Gulf Standard Time, and they move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan without renegotiation. There is no travel on either side, so a 90-minute booking is 90 minutes of teaching. Lessons can also follow a family that travels between terms, which in this city is a more common requirement than it sounds.

On what a tutor will not do: no tutor will supply Cambridge past papers, mark schemes or syllabus documents as downloads, because those belong to Cambridge; the right route is cambridgeinternational.org and your child's school. No tutor will take an assessment on a student's behalf. And no provider should be telling you they hold board or regulator accreditation for private tutoring — IB Gram operates no premises in the UAE and holds no KHDA permit, which is why this is an online service and the page says so plainly.

process.title: Share a marked paper
process.description: A mock or a school assessment that has already been marked is worth more than any description of the problem. With the statement of entry alongside it, a tutor can see the tier, the practical paper number and the actual pattern of lost marks before the first session rather than spending that session finding out.

process.title: Diagnostic lesson at no charge
process.description: One trial lesson per student, with no card details taken. The session works through questions from each strand and classifies every lost mark by cause: missing content, misread command term, unshown working, or practical technique. You get that classification in writing, including the case where school support is already enough.

process.title: Pick the block, not the subject
process.description: The plan names one strand or one skill and a number of sessions, rather than open-ended science tutoring. Session length and the weekly slot are set in Gulf Standard Time around school and activities, and the plan says what should look different and on which paper.

process.title: Teach, set, mark, repeat
process.description: Each session ends with a timed question set. It comes back marked against the published mark scheme with marks attributed point by point, so both you and the student can see whether the category of loss is shrinking. That record is also what a school looks at in a tier discussion.

process.title: Reassess at the mocks
process.description: The November and spring mocks are the checkpoints. If the same loss category is still appearing, the plan changes rather than continuing. If the content is secure, sessions switch to paper technique and timing for the final weeks, and sometimes the right answer is to stop.

whyPoints.title: A diagnosis before a plan
whyPoints.description: The first session classifies lost marks by cause rather than by topic, because the fix for a misread command term and the fix for missing content are not the same purchase. You get that classification written down, including when it says you do not need many sessions.

whyPoints.title: One tutor across three strands
whyPoints.description: 0654 is coordinated, so the tutor holds biology, chemistry and physics at IGCSE depth and can follow the school's sequence across all three. Online delivery is what makes that pool large enough to match on subject rather than on postcode.

whyPoints.title: Marks attributed, not totalled
whyPoints.description: Written work returns marked against the published Cambridge scheme with each mark attributed to a specific point and each missed mark explained. That is the only form of evidence that tells you whether anything is actually changing.

whyPoints.title: Problems sized honestly
whyPoints.description: Some issues are one session, some are six, some are a term. You are told which before you buy, and told plainly if a plan has stopped working. A provider who sizes everything the same way is selling a subscription, not a fix.

whyPoints.title: Availability stated up front
whyPoints.description: If no suitable specialist is free at the time you need, you hear that rather than being matched with whoever is available. Where a tutor outside the UAE is the right answer for a niche combination, it is disclosed before you book.

whyPoints.title: No claims we cannot evidence
whyPoints.description: No regulator or board accreditation, no grade promises, no copyrighted Cambridge material hosted as downloads, and no statistics without a source. IB Gram has no UAE premises, which is stated rather than implied.

faqs.question: How is Coordinated Sciences 0654 assessed compared with three separate sciences?
faqs.answer: 0654 is assessed as one double award: a multiple-choice paper, a structured theory paper and a practical component, with the result reported as two IGCSE grades. Separate sciences mean three entries, three sets of papers and three grades, with more content per science and its own practical paper for each. The double award covers all three sciences but at less depth per science, which is why some sixth forms specify separate sciences for A Level science entry. Check the Cambridge syllabus for 0654 on cambridgeinternational.org for the exact components in your child's series.

faqs.question: Which command terms cost 0654 students the most marks?
faqs.answer: Explain and suggest, by a clear margin. Explain requires a because-clause, and students who describe instead collect the description marks and lose the reasoning mark even when they understand the science. Suggest asks for a syllabus idea applied to an unfamiliar context, and students either skip it or write a remembered textbook answer that does not fit. Compare is a third: two separate descriptions with nothing linking them does not score as a comparison. Naming the command term before writing is a single-session habit with a measurable effect.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks on the 0654 multiple-choice paper they found easy?
faqs.answer: Because it is short, it feels comfortable, and nobody re-checks a paper they enjoyed. The items are written so that each wrong option corresponds to a specific predictable error: an unbalanced formula, a mole calculation using mass, a reciprocal slip in parallel resistance, a nearly-right biology definition. Two careless items on a short paper is a visible difference in the final grade. The fix is to trace every wrong answer back to the error its distractor was built to catch, until the student can name their own pattern and re-check selectively.

faqs.question: What is the fastest way to raise a 0654 theory paper mark?
faqs.answer: Count the marks and annotate the figure. A four-mark question needs four distinct scoring points, and students routinely give one point expressed four ways. Data questions have the answer on the page, yet well-revised students answer from memory, which does not match a data-specific mark scheme. Both are procedural habits, installable in one session and then reinforced through marked work for several weeks. Together they usually move more marks per hour of effort than any amount of additional content revision on a double award.

faqs.question: My child understands chemistry but cannot do mole calculations. What is going on?
faqs.answer: Nine times out of ten the problem is algebra, not chemistry. A student who is not fluent at rearranging a formula, converting units or handling standard form cannot complete a two-stage calculation under time pressure however well they understand the reaction. The fix is a fixed four-line method: balanced equation, convert to moles, apply the ratio from the equation, convert back and state the unit. Writing a line for each step also collects method marks when the final figure is wrong, which on multi-mark questions is a substantial difference.

faqs.question: Which physics topic in 0654 is worth the most tutoring time?
faqs.answer: Electricity, including series and parallel circuits, resistance combinations and electrical power. The reasoning is systematic, the question formats repeat across series, and the commonest error is procedural: students calculate before sketching the circuit. Enforcing a sketch-first rule on every question, then practising the style where a component is added or removed and the readings must be predicted, produces reliable gains. Electromagnetism is the second priority at Extended tier, where a field direction drawn wrongly propagates through an entire answer.

faqs.question: How do I know whether my child needs content teaching or exam technique?
faqs.answer: Look at a marked paper and classify the lost marks. If marks are going on questions where the topic is clearly known but the answer is the wrong shape — describing instead of explaining, answers without working, figures not read — that is technique, and it is a short intervention. If whole questions are blank or answered with unrelated content, that is missing content, and it needs a teaching block in syllabus order. A diagnostic session exists to do exactly this classification, and it is worth doing before buying a term of sessions.

faqs.question: Is the 0654 practical component worth preparing for separately?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the most teachable part of the syllabus. It carries roughly a fifth of the award, is common to both tiers, and the marks go to rules rather than talent: results table drawn before readings, graph scales filling the grid, a best-fit line through the trend, anomalies identified explicitly, a conclusion answering the question asked, and an evaluation that criticises the method rather than the student. Four to six focused sessions normally covers it. Confirm from the statement of entry whether the laboratory test or the written alternative was entered.

faqs.question: Can a tutor teach the laboratory practical paper over video?
faqs.answer: Partly, and the split should be stated honestly. Bench skills for the laboratory test belong in school practical sessions, and a tutor claiming to replace them is overselling. What transfers fully to a shared screen is everything around the apparatus: planning the table before readings, selecting scales, plotting, spotting anomalous results, writing conclusions and evaluating a method. For the written alternative there is no laboratory requirement at all, and annotating described apparatus live on screen works at least as well as doing it across a table.

faqs.question: How many 0654 sessions a week should a Year 11 student in Dubai have?
faqs.answer: One 90-minute session a week suits most Year 11 students, with a short block aimed at whichever strand is failing systematically and a separate block on the practical component. Two or three sessions a week makes sense only in the final six to eight weeks and only if the content is broadly secure. More than that, earlier, usually means a student with too little time to do the marked practice between sessions, which is where the actual learning happens on this syllabus.

faqs.question: When are the Dubai mocks, and why do they matter for 0654?
faqs.answer: Most Dubai schools run mocks in November and again in February or March. They matter for two reasons. They are the evidence a school uses for predicted grades and for any decision about moving a candidate between Core and Extended, and they are the first time most students sit the three components under timed conditions together. That makes the autumn term the point at which tutoring changes an outcome rather than confirming one, and it is why practical-skills work is better bought in October than in April.

faqs.question: Does the biology strand need as much tutoring as chemistry and physics?
faqs.answer: Usually less. In double-award cohorts the biology content is retained better and the lost marks are mostly technique: data questions answered from memory, genetics crosses without the gametes written out, structure-and-function questions answered with only one half, and definitions that are nearly right. Four sessions covering those four things normally moves more marks than a term of general biology revision. That is also why a diagnostic session is worth doing first, so a family does not buy a long biology programme when a short one plus a chemistry block was the answer.

faqs.question: What should come back to me as a parent between sessions?
faqs.answer: A marked script, not a progress report. Written work should return marked against the published Cambridge mark scheme with each mark attributed to a specific point and each missed mark explained next to it. A total tells you nothing; a script showing that four of six lost marks were method marks on calculations tells you what the next sessions should do. It also makes the tutoring testable: if the same loss category persists after six weeks, the plan is wrong and should change rather than continue.

faqs.question: What happens if no 0654 specialist is available at our preferred time?
faqs.answer: You get told. A double award needs a tutor holding biology, chemistry and physics at IGCSE depth, which is a narrower pool than general science tuition, and evening slots in Gulf Standard Time are the most contested. Where no UAE-based specialist is free, the alternative offered is an experienced IGCSE science tutor working from India to Gulf Standard Time, disclosed before booking rather than after. No provider should be quietly routing a UAE family elsewhere without saying so.

faqs.question: Can we use Cambridge past papers and mark schemes in sessions?
faqs.answer: Sessions work from past questions, but no tutor should be hosting or distributing Cambridge papers, mark schemes or syllabus documents, because those are Cambridge's copyright. The correct route is cambridgeinternational.org and your child's school, which can supply what it is licensed to supply. A tutor can reference a question, teach from it, and mark your child's answer against the published scheme. A provider offering a download library of papers is doing something it is not entitled to do.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-coordinated-scienc.closingHeading: Bring a marked paper, not a worry
dubai/cambridge-igcse-coordinated-scienc.closingBody: The most useful first message about Cambridge IGCSE Coordinated Sciences 0654 contains three things: the statement of entry, a marked mock, and one sentence about which of the three sciences feels worst. From those, a diagnostic session can tell you whether the problem is content, command terms, calculation method or practical technique, and roughly how many sessions each would take. Sometimes the answer is that school support and better marked practice is enough, and you will be told that. Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, around Dubai school hours and activities.

intro.heading: What families are not told at the options evening
paragraphs: Most parents meet the phrase Coordinated Sciences on a Year 9 options form and never receive a proper explanation of it. The form offers three science routes with similar-sounding names, the evening runs short, and the decision gets made on a teacher's recommendation about workload. Two years later a family discovers at a sixth-form open day that the route taken has consequences, and by then the entry has been made and the papers have been sat.

So this page starts with the definition. Cambridge IGCSE Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 is a double award. The student studies one coordinated course drawing on biology, chemistry and physics, and receives two grades for it. That is the central fact and it distinguishes 0654 from the single award, which gives one grade, and from three separate sciences, which give three. The content depth sits between the two: more than the single award, less than studying each science as its own subject.

The assessment follows the familiar Cambridge science pattern. There is a multiple-choice component worth 30 per cent, a theory component worth 50 per cent, and a practical component worth 20 per cent, with Core and Extended candidates sitting different multiple-choice and theory papers. Confirm the exact paper numbers and the practical choice on your child's statement of entry and against the current syllabus on the Cambridge International website, because centres make the practical decision at their own level and syllabuses are revised.

What makes 0654 distinctive to teach is the breadth at depth. A single-award course can be covered by a competent generalist. Three separate sciences are taught by three specialists. The double award asks one person to work at close to separate-subject depth in all three, moving from gas exchange to mole calculations to electrical circuits and back, and to know which science each lost mark came from. That is a less common skill than it sounds, and it is the thing worth testing before any plan is agreed. The practical test of it takes four minutes in a trial lesson: ask for a worked example from each of the three sciences, back to back, and listen for where the fluency thins out. A tutor who is strong in one science and approximate in another will steer every hour towards their own strength without intending to, and a fifteen-year-old will let them, because the alternative is harder work.

IB Gram is an independent matching platform. Tutoring for families in Dubai and across the Emirates is delivered one-to-one over live video; we do not make home visits in Dubai, as that is a service we run only in India. Nothing on this page claims an approval or affiliation from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge International or any school named here, and no grade is promised. What follows is the content detail and the mark-loss patterns, which is the information the options evening did not have time for.

sections.heading: What the 0654 double award assesses, component by component
paragraphs: The first thing worth having is a clear picture of where the marks are. Coordinated Sciences 0654 is assessed through three components: a multiple-choice paper worth 30 per cent, a theory paper worth 50 per cent, and a practical component worth 20 per cent. Core and Extended candidates sit different multiple-choice and theory papers. The practical component is either a supervised practical test or a written alternative, and the centre chooses which. Confirm the exact paper numbers against your child's statement of entry and the current syllabus on the Cambridge International website.

Half the grade arriving in one theory paper is the structural fact that should shape a revision plan. It means theory technique is the highest-yield thing to fix, ahead of content breadth, and it means a student who writes well but knows less can outscore a student who knows more and writes imprecisely. It also means a bad morning in one paper carries a lot of weight, which is an argument for full-length timed practice rather than topic-by-topic revision in the final weeks.

The multiple-choice component punishes a specific weakness that students rarely identify in themselves. Close distractors are designed to be chosen by somebody who recognises the topic without securely knowing it, which is exactly the state produced by rereading notes. A student scoring lower on multiple choice than on the theory paper is telling you their recall is recognition-level, and the remedy is retrieval practice rather than more reading.

The practical component is a fifth of the grade and the part Dubai households almost never revise. Across all three sciences it tests the same closed list of skills: identifying variables and controls, building a results table with units in the headings, choosing graph axes so a trend can be read, spotting an anomalous result and saying what to do about it, and suggesting a method improvement that genuinely reduces error. Every one of those is a rule, and rules respond quickly to teaching.

sections.heading: The biology inside 0654: what is kept and what is lighter
paragraphs: Families moving between the double award and the separate biology syllabus want to know what is different, and the honest answer is depth rather than coverage. The big ideas are all present. Cells and the organisation of the organism, movement of substances across membranes, enzymes, nutrition in plants and humans, transport, gas exchange and respiration, coordination and response, reproduction and inheritance, and ecology including human effects on the environment. A 0654 student meets that landscape.

What is lighter is the level of detail expected within each. The separate syllabus asks for more named structures, more biochemical specificity and more quantitative treatment of data. For tutoring this is good news and a trap at the same time. It is good news because a student can secure the biology marks in 0654 without the memory load of the separate course. It is a trap because the questions still reward precision in the terms used, and a student who has learnt a topic approximately will write approximately and score nothing.

The mark-loss pattern in the biology questions is consistent and it is almost never a knowledge problem. It is register. Describe answers are given to explain questions, which means the student says what happens when the mark scheme wanted a mechanism connecting cause to effect. Comparison questions get two separate paragraphs that never compare anything. Questions asking for a suggestion get left blank because the content was not in the notes, which guarantees zero where a reasoned attempt might have scored.

What a session fixes here is quick and measurable. Count the marks, plan that many separate credited points, force a because or a therefore into every explain answer, and use whereas as a structural device in comparisons. Students usually find biology is the first science where the technique work shows up in a marked paper, which makes it a useful place to start when confidence is low.

sections.heading: The chemistry inside 0654: where the calculation marks live
paragraphs: Chemistry is where the double award is hardest and where tutoring time concentrates. The qualitative content is approachable: states of matter, atoms and bonding, the periodic table, acids and bases, rates of reaction, energy changes, electrolysis, and an introduction to organic chemistry. Students generally cope with all of it. The marks go elsewhere.

They go to the quantitative work. Relative formula mass, moles, reacting masses, concentration and percentage yield are not chemistry problems in the way students expect. They are proportional reasoning with units attached, and they require a student to set up a relationship, rearrange it, substitute correctly and carry the units through. A candidate who cannot do that reliably loses the same marks in every paper no matter how much chemistry they revise, which is the single most common reason a 0654 grade sits below what a family expected.

This has a consequence for how a tutoring plan looks and it needs saying in advance. The first three or four sessions on a weak chemistry strand go to the arithmetic underneath it, during which the chemistry marks do not move at all. Families routinely read that flat period as the tutoring failing. It is the only order the work can be done in: there is no way to fix reacting-mass questions without first fixing the proportional reasoning they are built on.

The second recurring loss is multi-step working abandoned part way. A student computes a relative formula mass correctly, then stops, because the next step is unclear and the clock is running. Partial working often earns partial credit, so the habit worth building is to keep writing: state the relationship, substitute what is known, and show the step even when the final number does not arrive. That is a technique change rather than a knowledge change, and it is worth marks in every paper.

sections.heading: The physics inside 0654: formula work and graph marks
paragraphs: Physics in the double award is where marks are most volatile rather than most missing. The content is a recognisable core: motion, forces and pressure, energy and its transfers, waves including light and sound, thermal physics, electricity and magnetism, and an introduction to nuclear physics. Most students can explain the ideas. What decides the marks is whether the calculation routine runs automatically under time pressure.

Four steps have to happen in sequence and students lose marks at each of them. Selecting the right relationship from the handful that could apply. Rearranging it correctly. Converting units so that the quantities are compatible, which is where the majority of errors live. Then completing the arithmetic and attaching the correct unit to the answer. A student who can do all four calmly at home will still drop them in a timed paper until the sequence requires no thought, which is why physics scores swing between consecutive papers.

Graph questions carry marks that are entirely procedural and therefore entirely recoverable. Choosing axes with sensible scales, plotting accurately, drawing a line that answers the question rather than joining every point, reading a value off the line rather than off the nearest data point, and calculating a gradient with units attached. None of that is physics knowledge and all of it is credited. It is the quickest available improvement in the physics questions and it is almost never practised deliberately.

The table sets out the patterns we see most often in marked 0654 scripts, with the fix for each. The remedy across all of them is short, frequent and unpopular: the same calculation and graph types repeated until the method is reflexive. Twenty minutes twice a week beats an hour once a fortnight, which is why exam-term sessions get shorter and more frequent rather than longer.

sections.heading: Core or Extended for 0654, and what the ceiling means
paragraphs: The tier is the most consequential thing about a 0654 entry and the thing families least often know. Core and Extended candidates sit different multiple-choice and theory papers. Extended candidates carry supplement content across all three sciences on top of the core material and have access to the higher grades. Core candidates sit a narrower body of content with a lower ceiling. One lesson plan cannot serve both, because a meaningful share of an Extended candidate's material is content a Core candidate is simply never taught.

The entry is made by the centre, not by the parent and not by the tutor, and it is made on the evidence the school has: classroom performance and mock results. It is also made before the final entry deadline, which sits months ahead of the papers. The Cambridge March 2027 series makes the gap concrete, with final entries due on 27 November 2026 against an exam period starting 3 February 2027. The practical consequence is that the window for influencing a tier decision is Year 10 and the first term of Year 11.

If a sixth-form science place is the ambition and the current entry is Core, that conversation needs to happen early and with evidence. A marked past paper scored against the published points, with the loss attributed to each science, is a better basis for the discussion than an opinion about potential. Teachers respond to evidence about their own subject. Occasionally the answer will still be no, and then the honest planning question becomes what a strong Core grade leaves open and what a bridging term would need to cover.

What a tutor can do is make the Extended tier survivable. Supplement content is not conceptually harder so much as denser, and it concentrates in particular places: more quantitative chemistry, more detail in transport and gas exchange, more extended calculation in physics. A session plan for an Extended candidate has to name that material explicitly rather than hoping it is picked up in general coverage.

sections.heading: Two grades, and what they do for equivalency
paragraphs: Beyond university and sixth form there is a Ministry of Education process most competitor pages in this market ignore entirely. Equivalency is how a UAE authority recognises a school-leaving certificate, and on the British track the published requirement is specific: five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

One clause matters more than the rest for a science decision. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. That means a Dubai student carrying mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education streams cannot count them towards the five, and the remaining accredited subjects have to supply the number. A ranking competitor page in this market states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which is wrong; the published rule is five.

This is where the double award earns something concrete. Two science grades from one course contribute more to that count of five than the single award's one grade does, which is a narrow, practical argument for 0654 over 0653 that has nothing to do with how hard either course is. A family counting accredited subjects on an options form is doing a more useful piece of planning than most families manage at that stage.

Two cautions belong here. IB Gram does not perform or influence equivalency, and tutoring is not required for it; implying otherwise would be a false-urgency claim about a government process. And the figures above are the British-track rules as published in a secondary source. Verify the current requirements through the Ministry of Education's own channel before relying on them, and treat any published IB points threshold with suspicion unless it has been read on the Ministry's own pages.

sections.heading: Why 0654 students find the first A Level term hard
paragraphs: A double-award student who arrives in a Dubai sixth form with two solid science grades can still find the first term of an A Level science uncomfortable, and knowing why in advance turns it from a crisis into a plan. The gap is not general ability. It is specific content depth in a small number of places, and it is bridgeable in a few weeks of targeted work rather than a year of catching up.

In chemistry the gap is quantitative. A separate-subject IGCSE course drills moles, reacting masses, concentration and yield to a level the coordinated course introduces. An A Level Chemistry course assumes that fluency from the first week and builds on it immediately, so a student still thinking carefully about proportional reasoning is reasoning about the wrong layer of the problem. This is the most common place a 0654 student struggles and the most responsive to a short bridging block before term starts.

In physics the gap is mathematical rather than conceptual. Rearranging relationships with several variables, handling standard form, and working confidently with units are assumed rather than taught, and the coordinated course asks for less of all three. In biology the gap is memory load and precision of terminology: A Level biology rewards exact naming in a way the double award does not require, so a student used to approximate answers has a habit to change rather than a body of content to learn.

The useful conclusion is about sequencing rather than about ability. A student moving from 0654 to an A Level science benefits far more from four weeks of quantitative work in the summer than from reading ahead in the new textbook. If the destination is already known in Year 11, that bridging work can be built into the final term rather than squeezed into August, which is the kind of planning a documented record of which science is strongest makes possible.

sections.heading: The options evening questions, and the honesty boundary
paragraphs: If this page is read before a Year 9 options form rather than after it, five questions are worth taking into the evening. What attainment does the department look for before placing a student on three separate sciences? Does our own sixth form accept the double award for entry to each A Level science, and can we have that in writing? When is the Core and Extended decision made, and on what evidence? Which practical component does the centre enter candidates for? And how many accredited subjects will my child finish with, given the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education streams on the timetable?

Those are all questions the school holds the answers to, and a department will generally answer them straightforwardly because they are questions about their own subject rather than complaints. The one worth insisting on in writing is the sixth-form condition, because it is the answer that matters in two years and the one most likely to be remembered differently by both sides.

On what a tutor contributes, the boundary should be stated rather than implied. A tutor teaches, explains, demonstrates on examples that are not assessed work, marks past papers against the board's published points, and gives feedback on work the student has produced themselves. A tutor does not supply text for submission and does not hand over bundles of board material. Cambridge publishes syllabuses, past papers and mark schemes free on its own website; we reference and link them rather than redistributing them.

Two final disclosures. IB Gram is an independent matching platform with no premises in the UAE and no KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is a specific authorisation issued to training institutes with physical premises. It is not approved, accredited, licensed or endorsed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge International or Pearson, and has no relationship with any school named on this page. And anyone charging for private lessons in the UAE needs a MoHRE private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which is granted free of charge for two years and is a reasonable thing to ask a prospective tutor about.

process.title: Confirm it is the double award
process.description: A surprising number of families do not know whether their child is on the single award, the double award or separate sciences. The statement of entry settles it, along with the tier and the practical component. Those three facts decide what the first month of sessions contains, and all three are held by the school.

process.title: Mark a paper and split it three ways
process.description: A released past paper at the right tier, sat under exam timing and scored against the published points, with the marks totalled separately for biology, chemistry and physics. For a double award this split is the whole diagnosis, because the two grades hide which of the three sciences is carrying the loss.

process.title: Free trial lesson, tested across all three
process.description: One full-length one-to-one video session at no charge, with no card details taken. Ask the tutor for a reacting-mass calculation, an explain-style biology answer and a parallel-circuit problem. The double award needs someone who can work at depth in all three rather than a generalist who is comfortable in one.

process.title: Choose rotation or a depth block
process.description: If the difficulty is breadth, a fixed rotation keeps all three sciences live and no topic cold for more than three weeks. If one science is dramatically weaker, four to six consecutive sessions on that science alone works better, with the other two maintained by short question sets rather than teaching.

process.title: Review against a comparable paper
process.description: Six to eight weeks in, the same tier and paper format under the same timing, marked the same way, with the three-way split repeated. The comparison is the review. If nothing has moved, the plan changes or the tutor does, and that is a conversation we start rather than one you should have to chase.

whyPoints.title: The double award is taught as what it is
whyPoints.description: 0654 asks one tutor to work at close to separate-subject depth in three sciences and to move between them without losing the thread. That is a different job from teaching a single award, and it is testable in a trial lesson by asking for a worked example from each science rather than taking it on trust.

whyPoints.title: Marks are attributed to a science, then to a topic
whyPoints.description: Two grades still hide which of the three sciences is costing your child. Every paper is scored and split three ways, then tagged to topics inside the weakest science, so the hours go to measured loss rather than to whichever science the tutor teaches most comfortably.

whyPoints.title: The tier is established before any plan
whyPoints.description: Core and Extended candidates sit different papers and a meaningful part of the Extended body of content is never taught to Core candidates. Supplement material is named and timetabled explicitly, and past-paper practice uses the right tier, because the wrong one mistrains both pacing and expectations.

whyPoints.title: The practical component gets protected time
whyPoints.description: A fifth of the grade sits in a component households almost never revise, and across all three sciences it tests the same closed list of recording and evaluation rules. It is timetabled as its own strand so it is not displaced every time a content topic feels more urgent.

whyPoints.title: Claims stop where the evidence stops
whyPoints.description: No regulator or board approval is claimed, no school is presented as a partner, and no grade or improvement figure is published, because none could be shown with a sample size, a date and a method. Market rates carry their source, regulations cite the government page that states them.

faqs.question: What does the double award in Cambridge IGCSE Coordinated Sciences 0654 actually mean?
faqs.answer: It means one course produces two science grades. A student studies a coordinated programme drawing on biology, chemistry and physics and receives two grades for it, where the single award produces one grade and three separate sciences produce three. The content depth sits between those two options: more than the single award, less than studying each science as its own subject. Assessment follows the Cambridge science pattern of a multiple-choice component, a theory component and a practical component, with Core and Extended candidates sitting different papers.

faqs.question: How many grades will my child get from 0654, and how do they appear?
faqs.answer: Two science grades from the one course. Confirm how your child's school reports and records them, because families planning sixth-form applications sometimes assume a single averaged grade. The practical value of two grades is both in how a certificate reads and in the Ministry of Education equivalency count on the British track, where five accredited subjects at grade E or 3 or better are required and Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five.

faqs.question: Is 0654 harder than taking three separate sciences?
faqs.answer: Different rather than harder. Separate sciences ask for more depth in each subject and more total content, which is a larger memory and workload demand. The double award asks for breadth at a middling depth, and its particular difficulty is that papers move between the three sciences without warning, so a student has to hold three kinds of thinking at once. Students who dislike rapid switching sometimes find the coordinated course less comfortable than they expected, even though the content load is lighter.

faqs.question: Which papers does an Extended 0654 candidate sit?
faqs.answer: An Extended candidate sits the Extended multiple-choice paper, the Extended theory paper covering core plus supplement content across all three sciences, and one practical component, either the supervised practical test or the written alternative depending on what the centre has chosen. The multiple-choice component is worth 30 per cent, the theory paper 50 per cent and the practical component 20 per cent. Confirm the exact paper numbers on the statement of entry and against the current syllabus on the Cambridge International website.

faqs.question: Which biology topics are lighter in 0654 than in the separate biology syllabus?
faqs.answer: The coverage is broadly the same landscape and the depth is what differs. Cells, transport across membranes, enzymes, nutrition, transport in plants and animals, gas exchange, respiration, coordination, reproduction, inheritance and ecology all appear. The separate syllabus asks for more named structures, more biochemical specificity and more quantitative handling of data. The trap is that 0654 questions still reward precise terminology, so a student who has learnt a topic approximately writes approximately and scores nothing.

faqs.question: Does 0654 include mole calculations?
faqs.answer: Quantitative chemistry is part of the course and it is where most of the chemistry marks are lost. Relative formula mass, moles, reacting masses, concentration and yield are proportional reasoning with units attached rather than chemistry recall, so a student who cannot reliably set up and rearrange a relationship loses the same marks in every paper. Expect a plan that spends its first few sessions on the arithmetic underneath, during which the chemistry marks do not move. That lag is normal and it is the only workable order.

faqs.question: Where do 0654 candidates lose the most physics marks?
faqs.answer: In the four-step calculation routine, and mostly at step three. Selecting the right relationship, rearranging it, converting units so quantities are compatible, then completing the arithmetic with the correct unit attached. Unit conversion is where the majority of errors live, especially time given in minutes and used as seconds. Graph questions are the other recoverable area: points joined dot to dot instead of a line of best fit, values read off the nearest point rather than off the line, and gradients quoted with no unit.

faqs.question: Can my daughter go on to A Level Chemistry after the double award?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and the condition is set by your own school rather than nationally. Some Dubai sixth forms accept the double award for any A Level science and some ask for a separate-subject grade for a specific one, so get the answer in writing from the head of sixth form. Where the route is open, expect the first term to be demanding in the quantitative work, because A Level Chemistry assumes mole fluency from week one. Four weeks of targeted quantitative work before term starts closes most of that gap.

faqs.question: Do both 0654 grades count towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: On the British track the Ministry requires five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. Two science grades contribute more to that count than the single award's one grade. Confirm how the subjects are treated through the Ministry's own channel, because IB Gram neither performs nor influences equivalency and tutoring is not required for it.

faqs.question: Should my son take 0654 or the single award 0653 in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The honest answer depends on timetable capacity and on destination. The double award gives two grades and more content; the single award gives one grade and less. If post-16 science is a possibility, the double award keeps more doors open and contributes more accredited subjects to the equivalency count. If your child is already carrying a heavy timetable including mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education streams and is struggling, a strong single-award grade beats a weak double award. Ask the school what it recommends and why.

faqs.question: How is the practical component assessed in the coordinated course?
faqs.answer: It is worth 20 per cent and the centre chooses between a supervised practical test and a written alternative. Across all three sciences it tests the same closed list: identifying variables and controls, building a results table with units in the headings, choosing graph axes so a trend is readable, spotting an anomalous result and saying what to do about it, and suggesting a method improvement that genuinely reduces error. Those are rules rather than knowledge, which is why the component responds quickly to a protected strand of sessions.

faqs.question: How many tutoring hours does a 0654 student need across the two years?
faqs.answer: A student working weekly in step with the school from the start of Year 10 is looking at around thirty sessions a year, which is the cheapest effective pattern because it is teaching rather than repair. A Year 11 student starting after winter mocks typically needs eighteen to twenty-five sessions before a June series, with four to six of those protected for the practical component. A student six weeks out has about twelve hours, which can rebuild two topics and fix technique but cannot replace a year of content.

faqs.question: My child is in the Core 0654 set but wants the Extended entry - what can we do?
faqs.answer: Raise it with the head of science while the entry is still open, and bring evidence rather than an opinion. A marked past paper at the Extended tier, scored against the published points with the loss attributed to each science, is a far better basis than a conversation about potential. Entry deadlines sit months before the papers: for the Cambridge March 2027 series, final entries were due 27 November 2026 against an exam period starting 3 February. The window is Year 10 and the first term of Year 11.

faqs.question: Which kinds of Dubai schools put students on the coordinated course, and why?
faqs.answer: It is the common compromise route in British-curriculum schools across the emirate, which account for the largest share of private-school enrolment. Departments use it where they want students to keep post-16 science open without carrying three separate subject loads alongside the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies streams that all Dubai private schools must run regardless of their licensed curriculum. The recommendation is usually about timetable capacity rather than about a judgement on ability.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-coordinated-scienc.closingHeading: Get the tier and the three-way split before anything else
dubai/cambridge-igcse-coordinated-scienc.closingBody: Coordinated Sciences 0654 is a double award, and the two grades still hide which of the three sciences is costing your child marks. A useful first step with any Cambridge IGCSE Coordinated Sciences 0654 tutor in Dubai is narrow: confirm the tier from the statement of entry, then get a past paper at that tier marked against the published points with the losses attributed to biology, chemistry and physics separately. That document is what a plan is built from. The trial lesson is a full-length one-to-one video session at no charge, with no card details taken, and it is a good place to test whether a tutor can work at depth in all three.

intro.heading: Home tutoring for 0455 in Dubai: what the search leaves out
paragraphs: Three things decide whether a home tutor is the right purchase for Cambridge IGCSE Economics 0455, and the listings a parent finds rarely mention any of them. The first is legality. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit scheme introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and administered by MoHRE, and a tutor arriving at a Dubai villa for cash without one is operating outside that scheme. The second is the clock: a weekday session in this city is squeezed between a school bus and a bedtime, and a tutor's drive comes out of the same hour you are paying for. The third is fit, because about half of this syllabus is taught perfectly adequately in a decent Dubai classroom and the other half is where help earns its keep.

Our answer on the first point is straightforward. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For UAE families, 0455 is taught as one-to-one live video, scheduled around the Dubai school day, with written work set, marked and returned between sessions. That is a real constraint and we would rather you knew it on the first page than on the fourth call. If a physical presence in the room is your actual requirement, hire locally and ask the questions set out below before you pay anybody.

On the second point, the arithmetic is worth doing once. A tutor travelling from one side of Dubai to another between 17:00 and 19:00 is spending a substantial part of their working hour in a car, and that time is inside your rate whether the invoice says so or not. More importantly it limits what time the session can start, which in a household with two children and a 21:00 bedtime is often the binding constraint rather than money. An online session starts at the booked minute from anywhere.

On the third point, this page is unusually specific. Cambridge IGCSE Economics 0455 has six units, and Dubai schools are generally strong on the content-heavy ones and weaker on the assessment skills that carry the top marks. Knowing which is which stops you paying for a year of general support when ten weeks of targeted work on evaluation and data response would have done. The unit-by-unit table below is the version of that advice we would give a friend.

The rest of the page covers the permit categories and how a parent can verify them, the emirate-by-emirate regulator map that matters if you move house, how Ramadan and the UAE academic calendar reshape when revision actually happens, and what the first fortnight of a sensible arrangement should produce in writing. None of it requires you to take anything on trust, which is the point.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-economics-0455-hom.programmesIntro: Four economics qualifications appear in Dubai school prospectuses, and parents are frequently told their child is taking one when the entry says another. Check the specification code on the exam entry rather than the subject name on the report.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Economics
programmes.description: Two external papers, no coursework. A forty-five minute multiple-choice paper carries 30% of the qualification and a two-hour-fifteen-minute structured paper carries 70%, split between one data-response question and a choice of three structured questions from four. Six units run from scarcity through markets, decision makers, macroeconomic policy, development and international trade.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools usually start 0455 at the beginning of Year 10 and finish the content by the February of Year 11, which leaves a revision window that varies enormously between departments. Where a school finishes late, the squeeze lands on exactly the assessment skills that carry the highest marks, and that is where most of our Dubai enquiries originate.

programmes.name: Cambridge O Level Economics
programmes.description: A separate Cambridge qualification with overlapping content, run by some schools instead of the IGCSE. The syllabus territory is similar and the paper structure and question styles are not identical, so revision materials are not interchangeable. Cambridge runs O Level exams in the same June and November series as IGCSE.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools with large South Asian cohorts run O Level rather than IGCSE, and families moving between schools mid-phase can find the qualification changes under them. If your child transfers in Year 11, ask the new school's exams officer which code the entry will carry before buying any revision material.

programmes.name: IB MYP Individuals and Societies
programmes.description: The route students arrive from when they move out of Dubai's large IB sector into a Cambridge school. MYP assesses knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating and thinking critically against criteria A to D, with extended written tasks. It builds research and argument habits and does not build timed exam pacing.
programmes.countryNote: A student transferring from an MYP school into Year 10 or 11 of a Cambridge school in Dubai usually writes better prose than their classmates and runs out of time in exams. The first marked 0455 timed answer tends to show exactly that: a thoughtful, well-argued response to two of the four parts and nothing written for the others.

programmes.name: A Level and IB Diploma Economics in Dubai sixth forms
programmes.description: A Level extends the micro and macro models substantially and introduces aggregate analysis absent from IGCSE. IB Diploma Economics restructures the content around key concepts and adds an internally assessed portfolio of commentaries written on real news articles, which is the first time most students meet an assessed piece of extended economics writing.
programmes.countryNote: Because Dubai has both systems in strength, families can genuinely choose at 16, and the choice should be made on how the student writes rather than on which school has the better reputation. A student who thrives on timed argument suits A Level; a student who works well over weeks on a portfolio often does better in the Diploma.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-economics-0455-hom.subjectsIntro: These are the 0455 topics Dubai families ask about most, listed as topics rather than as skills. Against each is the thing that actually goes wrong, which is usually narrower than the topic heading suggests.

subjects.name: Scarcity, choice and opportunity cost
subjects.description: The opening unit, and the one where a sloppy definition costs marks for two years. Opportunity cost is the next best alternative forgone, not the money spent, and a student carrying the loose version into Year 11 loses two-mark openers across the whole paper.

subjects.name: Demand, supply and market equilibrium
subjects.description: The engine of the syllabus. Dubai classrooms teach this well; what goes missing is the discipline of finishing a diagram. A student who can explain a shift verbally and cannot label the new equilibrium is losing marks for presentation rather than understanding.

subjects.name: Price elasticity of demand and supply
subjects.description: The formula is rarely the problem. The problem is the sentence after the number: what an elasticity of 0.4 means for a firm's revenue if it raises price. Students calculate and then stop, and the mark scheme pays for the interpretation.

subjects.name: Market failure and government intervention
subjects.description: Maximum and minimum prices, indirect taxes and subsidies. The recurring error is treating a subsidy as a demand shift. It moves supply, and a one-minute recall drill fixes it permanently once someone notices it is happening.

subjects.name: Households: income, spending and saving
subjects.description: Decisions about spending, saving and borrowing, and the influences on them. Scripts here often attach correct reasoning to the wrong agent, explaining a firm's incentive where the question asked about a household's, which reads as carelessness and is usually hurried reading.

subjects.name: Wage determination and trade unions
subjects.description: Why wages differ between occupations, and the role of unions. A reliable source of mid-paper marks and one students under-revise because it feels less technical than the diagram units. It is also the easiest unit in which to give specific UAE examples.

subjects.name: Firms: costs, revenue and economies of scale
subjects.description: Fixed and variable costs, total and average figures, revenue, profit, and why size changes unit cost. The arithmetic is simple and the vocabulary is unforgiving: average and total are not interchangeable, and a question asking for one does not credit the other.

subjects.name: Inflation, deflation and the price index
subjects.description: Causes, consequences and measurement. Index interpretation is where numerically capable students stumble, usually by reading an index as a price rather than as a comparison with a base year. Once that is said out loud, it rarely recurs.

subjects.name: Unemployment: types, causes and consequences
subjects.description: Cyclical, structural and frictional unemployment, and the effects on individuals, firms and government. Answers improve sharply when a student can give one consequence for each of those three groups rather than three versions of the same consequence.

subjects.name: Fiscal, monetary and supply-side policy
subjects.description: Instruments, aims and conflicts between objectives. The commonest failure in marked work is naming a policy without tracing what it does: an answer that lists instruments where the question wanted a chain from instrument to outcome.

subjects.name: Development, living standards and indicators
subjects.description: Differences in development between countries, income distribution and population. Marks go to specific comparison, and generalities about rich and poor countries score low where a named indicator and a direction of travel would have scored.

subjects.name: Exchange rates and the balance of payments
subjects.description: Determination, changes and consequences for trade. The classic error is reversing the direction: a depreciating currency makes exports cheaper abroad, and roughly half the scripts we mark get this backwards under time pressure at least once.

subjects.name: Free trade, protection and globalisation
subjects.description: Specialisation, the arguments for and against protection, and the effects of globalisation. A strong unit for evaluation practice because both sides are genuinely arguable, which makes it the one we use most when drilling the eight-mark structure.

sections.heading: Can you get a 0455 home tutor in Dubai? The direct answer
paragraphs: Yes, the Dubai market has them, and no, we are not one of them. Independent tutors advertise home visits across the emirate, tuition centres run group classes on their own premises, and some school teachers tutor privately within the rules that apply to them. Published rates for in-home one-to-one tuition in Dubai run from roughly AED 180 to AED 350 in Bestimate's rate table, with independent home tutors advertising up to AED 500, and monthly in-home packages of four two-hour sessions appearing at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799. Those are market figures from those sources rather than our prices.

What a visit buys you is a physical presence: an adult in the room, a child who cannot wander off, and for some families a genuine behavioural benefit that no amount of video can replicate. What it costs you is travel time inside the hour, a tutor pool limited to people willing to drive to your community at the worst time of day, and a later start than you would choose. For a fifteen-year-old sitting 0455, the behavioural benefit is usually small and the constraints are not.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and the India business is the only part of the operation where a tutor travels to a student. We state that here because the alternative is a parent discovering it after three conversations, and because the honest version of the comparison is one we are content to lose sometimes. If supervision is the requirement, a local tutor is the right answer and the questions later on this page are the ones to ask them.

The table below sets the four realistic options side by side on the things that actually differ. It is deliberately not a comparison with named competitors; it compares models, which is the only fair way to do it.

sections.heading: What a home visit cannot leave behind
paragraphs: Set cost aside for a moment, because there is a difference between the two formats that matters more over a school year and almost nobody mentions it. A home visit produces an hour of teaching and a verbal report at the door. An online arrangement, run properly, produces a marked script every week that you can read, keep and compare. In an essay subject that is not a minor administrative difference; it is the only way to tell whether the money is working.

The reason is practical rather than ideological. A tutor who marks at a desk, away from the student, with the published criteria open, writes a different kind of comment from a tutor reading over a shoulder at the kitchen table. The first produces a band and a reason. The second produces encouragement and a suggestion. Both are useful in the moment and only one accumulates into evidence. We have had Dubai parents tell us they liked their previous home tutor a great deal and could not say, after two terms, what had changed in their child's writing.

The things we track for 0455 are all countable from marked scripts: whether two-mark definitions come back full or half, how many links each explanation carries, whether a diagram passed its five objective checks, how many times a Section A answer referred to the supplied source, and whether the eight-mark judgement named a basis or simply asserted one. None of that requires a tutor to be in the room. All of it requires someone to read the script carefully afterwards and write down what they found.

So the comparison a parent should make is not online against in-home. It is marked against unmarked. A home tutor who marks and reports in writing is a good purchase. An online tutor who chats pleasantly for an hour is not. The format only shifts the odds, because marking is easier to build into a process that already runs on shared files.

sections.heading: The Dubai school-run clock and what it does to a session
paragraphs: Every tutoring arrangement in this city is eventually decided by a bus timetable. A Dubai school day commonly ends between 14:30 and 15:30, after which a child may be on a bus for anything from fifteen minutes to an hour, and clubs and sport can push arrival home past 17:00. Then homework, dinner and a bedtime that a Year 11 student needs more than they admit. The window for a useful session is narrow, and a tutor's drive eats the front of it.

This is why the home-versus-online question is usually settled by logistics rather than by preference. A family in an outer community choosing a home tutor is choosing a 17:45 or 18:00 start, because that is when the tutor can get there. The same family online can start at 16:45 if the bus allows, which is an hour earlier in a child's day and a noticeably better hour for writing an argument. Where the commute is long in both directions, a weekend morning beats both.

The table gives the windows we actually schedule into. They are generalisations from arranging sessions into these districts and they vary by school and by bus route, so treat them as a starting point for your own calculation rather than as a timetable. The column that matters most is the last one: what can realistically be achieved in a session that starts then. A 19:00 session is not a worse hour because of any principle, but it is a worse hour for writing a timed eight-mark answer, and the work should be chosen to match.

One practical consequence for 0455 specifically. Because the subject improves through marked writing rather than through contact time, a household with a bad weekday window has an easy fix: write the answer at a sensible hour on a different day and use the session purely for the marked review. That reorders the week around the child's best writing hour instead of around the tutor's availability.

sections.heading: Who may legally tutor your child in the UAE, and how to check
paragraphs: This is the part of a home-tutor search that deserves more attention than it gets. Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated rather than informal. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE. The federal portal u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years, and that eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page describes the route as an application through its smart app, website and e-services system, listing no fee and a two-working-day completion time.

Two conclusions follow for a parent. A tutor who says the permit is expensive, slow or unnecessary is contradicting the official pages, and that is a useful signal about everything else they tell you. And a tutor operating without one is, in the portal's words, subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted at you by anybody, including by us.

There is an additional layer in Abu Dhabi that Dubai parents should know about if they move. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, with the permit's code of conduct reported to bar the same arrangement. That is press-reported rather than read from the policy document itself, so verify it against ADEK's current publication before relying on it. The underlying principle is sound wherever you live: your child's own classroom teacher tutoring them privately for money is an arrangement to approach with care rather than enthusiasm.

A business is a different matter from an individual. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA educational services permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no premises in the UAE, and claims no approval, accreditation or licence from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE or the Ministry of Education. Any tutoring page describing itself as regulator-approved is making a specific claim that can be checked, and it is worth checking.

sections.heading: Which 0455 units a tutor is actually needed for
paragraphs: Buying a year of general economics support when ten weeks of targeted work would do is the most common way money is wasted in this subject. Dubai schools are, in our experience of marking their students' work, reliably good at the content-dense units and reliably thin on the assessment skills that separate a middle grade from a strong one. The table maps that honestly, including the units where our answer is that you probably do not need us.

The pattern is consistent enough to be worth stating in advance. Units on markets, decision makers and the macroeconomy are taught thoroughly because they are examinable content with clear notes, and a well-staffed Dubai department covers them. The development unit is more variable, often taught late in Year 11 when time has run short. And the assessment skills, which are not a unit at all, are where almost all the demand sits: the eight-mark judgement, the data-response habit of using the source, diagram completion and multiple-choice pacing.

This has a direct implication for how long you should buy. A student whose problem is skills rather than content does not need weekly support from September to May. They need an intensive block of eight to twelve weeks, run on marked written answers, placed after the content is finished and before the final mocks. That is cheaper than a year, more effective than a panic block in April, and it is the recommendation we make most often to Dubai families who contact us in Year 11.

Where a genuine content gap exists, it is usually one unit and it is usually identifiable from a single marked paper. In that case the work is short and specific: four to six weeks on the unit, then back to skills. A tutor who proposes a comprehensive two-year programme before seeing any of your child's written work is proposing a subscription rather than a diagnosis.
