sections.heading: Why economics marks move on a different curve from maths marks
paragraphs: Parents who have bought maths tuition before often find economics tuition frustrating in the first month, and the reason is worth stating plainly rather than letting it become a complaint. In maths, a closed gap shows up immediately: the student could not factorise, now they can, and the next test proves it. Economics does not behave that way, because the marks are awarded for the quality of reasoning in prose and prose quality improves unevenly.

Three things follow. The first is that the earliest gains in economics are nearly always mechanical rather than intellectual: definitions, diagram labels, source references. They are real marks and they are not what parents imagine they are buying, so it is worth saying in advance that month one looks like admin. The second is that the middle phase genuinely plateaus. An explanation chain going from one link to two reads almost identically to an untrained eye and sits in the same band, so the record has to carry the evidence that something changed.

The third is that question choice adds variance nobody can coach away entirely. Section B offers four questions and the student picks three. A student who reads the four stems badly can write good economics on the wrong question and score below a weaker student who chose well. We train choice explicitly, with timed selection drills, because it is a skill and because it is otherwise a lottery sitting on top of all the preparation.

The practical consequence for a family deciding how long to commit is this: judge economics tuition at twelve weeks, not at four. Judge it on marked scripts rather than on school report comments, and ask specifically whether explanation links and judgement structure have changed. Those two things are what the paper pays for, and they are the two things a cheerful weekly message will never tell you about.
bullets: Month one gains are mechanical and look like admin

sections.heading: Model answers, memorisation and the honesty line in 0455
paragraphs: 0455 has no coursework, so the academic-honesty question here is not about who produced a submitted piece of work. It is about what a student carries into the exam room in their head, and whether a tutor has helped them think or handed them something to reproduce. The distinction matters for the grade as much as for the ethics.

Memorised answers fail in this paper for a mechanical reason. Section B questions are set in specific contexts, and a rehearsed paragraph answers the general topic rather than the particular question. Examiner reports across essay subjects describe the same pattern: a fluent, well-structured answer that does not address the stem, scoring below a rougher answer that does. A tutor who supplies model answers to memorise is selling something that reliably underperforms, quite apart from whether it is the student's own thinking.

What works instead is structure without content. The student learns the shape of a judgement sentence, the habit of adding a second link, the discipline of annotating a source. Those transfer to any question stem. Where we use an exemplar, it is marked and criticised rather than copied: the student levels it themselves, says why it sits where it does, and then writes their own on a different context. The exemplar is a marking exercise, not a template.

Two related boundaries. We do not reproduce or supply Cambridge syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; those are published by Cambridge and we link to the official source. And IB Gram holds no accreditation, approval, licence or partnership from Cambridge, KHDA, ADEK or any ministry, and nothing on this page should be read as suggesting otherwise. A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai would need a KHDA educational services permit for a training institute; we do not operate premises in the UAE and do not hold that permit.

process.title: Send one marked script, not a summary
process.description: A single Section B answer with the school's marking on it is worth more than any description of the difficulty. Ten minutes with a real script usually identifies which of the five failure patterns applies, and that determines the whole plan rather than only the first session.

process.title: A diagnostic session with a written answer
process.description: The student writes one short answer under time during the first session while the tutor watches the drafting, then the tutor levels it and explains the level. You receive the diagnosis in writing within a day, with the recommended plan and the session rate in AED attached.

process.title: Open the mechanical targets first
process.description: Definitions, diagram completion and source annotation go first because they close quickly and produce marks inside a month. That order is deliberate: early visible gains buy the patience needed for the slower work on explanation and judgement.

process.title: One marked answer every week
process.description: Each session sets one written answer, and that answer comes back levelled with the reason stated. The next session begins from the script. The accumulating pile of levelled scripts is the record, and it is shared with you rather than kept in a tutor's notebook.

process.title: A block review every four weeks
process.description: At the end of each four-week block we review the scripts together and make a decision: continue, change approach, or stop. The inputs are closed targets, explanation links per answer, source references per answer and component marks on matched papers.

process.title: Timed papers and choice drills before the series
process.description: In the final block, sessions move to full timed components, including deliberate practice at choosing three Section B questions from four. Choice is a trainable skill and leaving it untrained puts a lottery on top of everything else the student has done.

whyPoints.title: Scripts are levelled, not praised
whyPoints.description: Every written answer comes back with the band it sits in and the specific reason it sits there. Encouragement is not written in the margin, because it occupies the space where a criterion should be. You can read a term of scripts in ten minutes and see what changed.

whyPoints.title: Diagram marks are treated as countable
whyPoints.description: Five objective checks on every figure: axes in words, curves labelled, shift direction arrowed, both equilibria marked, the diagram used in the prose. It is the fastest-closing target in the subject and the one most commonly left open by general tuition.

whyPoints.title: Paper 1 is diagnosed by category
whyPoints.description: Wrong answers are sorted into definition, direction, data-reading and timing failures, and the distribution is what gets reported. Two students with the same multiple-choice score often need entirely different work, and a raw score cannot show that.

whyPoints.title: The evaluation plateau is addressed directly
whyPoints.description: Most students stuck in the middle of 0455 are stuck on the eight-mark part. We treat it as a structural problem with a specific drill rather than telling a student to add more detail, which lengthens the answer and leaves the band unchanged.

whyPoints.title: Stopping is a legitimate recommendation
whyPoints.description: Every four-week block ends with a decision that includes stopping. If twelve weeks of marked scripts show no movement in judgement structure, continuing is not automatically the right advice, and we would rather say so than keep invoicing.

whyPoints.title: We do not supply answers to memorise
whyPoints.description: Exemplars are levelled and criticised by the student, never copied. Structure transfers between question stems; memorised content does not and reliably underperforms in a paper where every Section B question carries its own context.

faqs.question: What does a marked Cambridge IGCSE Economics 0455 script actually show?
faqs.answer: More than a grade. A properly marked script shows which band each part sits in and why, whether the two-mark definition was full or half, how many links each explanation carried, whether the diagram passed its five objective checks, whether the eight-mark answer reached a reasoned judgement or an asserted one, and in Section A how many times the student used the supplied source. Those are all observable properties of a piece of writing rather than impressions. Ask any prospective 0455 tutor to show you one marked answer with the band and the reason written on it; the answer to that request is informative either way.

faqs.question: Why do so many Dubai students plateau on the 0455 eight-mark question?
faqs.answer: Because it rewards something nine years of schooling has not asked for. Most students arrive able to give a reason for and a reason against, each explained to one link, followed by a sentence asserting which matters more. That answer does four of the six things required and sits mid-band however often it is rewritten in the same shape. Adding detail makes it longer, not better. What moves it is developing one side to three links, the counter to two, and writing a judgement that names its basis: which effect is larger, sooner, conditional or reversible. Most students who drill that shape move within four to six weeks.

faqs.question: Is the 0455 multiple-choice paper worth revising separately?
faqs.answer: Yes, because it carries 30% of the qualification and because its failures have different causes from the written paper's. Thirty questions in forty-five minutes leaves little slack, and in our marking the largest single cause of a poor score is not content but timing collapse across the final six or seven questions. The efficient approach is timed sets of thirty with every wrong answer sorted into definition, direction, data-reading or timing categories. The category distribution tells you what to work on; the raw score does not. Two students on nineteen out of thirty can need a month of content work and two sessions of pacing respectively.

faqs.question: How can I tell whether my child's 0455 problem is knowledge or writing?
faqs.answer: Look at a marked script rather than a report. If the definitions are wrong and the diagrams show the wrong curve moving, it is knowledge, and content teaching is the right purchase. If the definitions are half-complete, the diagrams are accurate but unlabelled or unused, the explanations stop after one link and the judgements are asserted, it is writing, and content revision will not help. The two look identical on a grade and are entirely different problems. In practice most Dubai students we see arriving at a middle grade have adequate knowledge and untrained reasoning structure.

faqs.question: How long does it take to move a 0455 Section B answer up a band?
faqs.answer: It depends which part. Two-mark definitions close in about a fortnight because they are rote. Diagram marks close in two to four weeks, since the five checks are objective and quickly become habit. Source use in Section A closes in three or four weeks as an annotation habit. Explanation chains take six to eight weeks because the student has to understand the mechanism rather than recall it. Judgement structure on the eight-mark part is the slowest, typically four to eight weeks of focused work, and it is the one worth measuring the whole arrangement against at the twelve-week point.

faqs.question: Does Cambridge IGCSE Economics 0455 need diagrams, and how are they marked?
faqs.answer: Diagrams carry real marks and they are awarded for objective features rather than artistic quality: axes labelled in words, curves labelled, the shift drawn in the correct direction, the original and new equilibrium both identified, and the diagram actually referred to in the written answer. Most students know the diagram and fail to finish it, which is why this is the fastest target to close. One warning specific to this syllabus: aggregate demand and supply analysis belongs to A Level, and a student taught it early can end up writing A Level answers to IGCSE questions, which is not rewarded. Check the syllabus for your child's exam year.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Section A data-response question in 0455?
faqs.answer: That is often where the quickest marks are, and the help needed is technique rather than content. Section A is one extended question worth 30 marks built on supplied text and data, and the marks reward using the source. Strong students lose them precisely because they know enough economics to answer without looking at the extract. The drill is mechanical: annotate first by circling two figures, underlining one claim and noting one trend, then ensure every part of the answer carries at least one reference from those annotations. It feels artificial for three attempts and then becomes automatic, and the reference count is easy to track across scripts.

faqs.question: How much calculation is in Cambridge IGCSE Economics 0455?
faqs.answer: Enough to matter and not enough to be the main difficulty. Students meet percentage change, elasticity formulae, price-index interpretation, exchange rate conversion, and cost, revenue and profit arithmetic. In marked scripts the arithmetic itself is rarely the failure. What is marked down is the interpretation: a correctly calculated elasticity figure with no statement of what it means for the firm's revenue, or an exchange rate change with the effect on export prices reversed. The habit we drill is writing the meaning sentence immediately after the number, in the same breath, so the two never get separated under exam pressure.

faqs.question: Should my child take Economics 0455 or Business Studies 0450 in a Dubai school?
faqs.answer: 0455 is the more abstract and more diagram-dependent of the two and the better preparation for an economics degree. 0450 applies reasoning to a named business through a case study, with accounting-style arithmetic rather than elasticity. Students who think in models usually prefer 0455; students who prefer concrete scenarios usually do better in 0450. Several Dubai schools let a student take both, which works reasonably because the external-influences unit overlaps with the 0455 macroeconomy content. The cheapest way to decide is one diagnostic written answer in each style before options are locked, rather than choosing on reputation at an option evening.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge 0455 the same as Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Economics 4EC1?
faqs.answer: The content overlaps substantially; the papers do not. Question tariffs, mark-scheme wording, paper structure and the session pattern all differ, which makes past-paper practice board-specific. A Dubai student revising Cambridge papers for an Edexcel entry is practising the right economics in the wrong format, and the effect shows up in timing and answer shape rather than in knowledge. Ask the school's exams officer which board and specification code appears on the entry. Pearson runs International GCSE exams in May/June and November each year and publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so work from the live official timetable rather than a restated date.

faqs.question: Will UAE universities care that my child took Economics at IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Subject choice matters for course prerequisites rather than for admission in general, and the rules that apply to everyone are the Ministry of Education equivalency requirements. On the British track, students must show five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level, and Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. Economics can form part of that count. Requirements change and are administered by the Ministry, so verify the current position on moe.gov.ae or through your emirate's attestation channel rather than relying on any tutoring page.

faqs.question: What does a twelve-week 0455 plan look like for a Dubai Year 11 student?
faqs.answer: Three four-week blocks, each ending in a decision. Block one closes the mechanical targets: definitions, diagram completion and source annotation, which produce visible marks quickly. Block two works on explanation chains, raising the average number of links per explanation from one to three, and it plateaus visibly even while improving. Block three is judgement structure on the eight-mark parts plus Section A source use, and it is the point at which the family decides whether to commit to the exam term. After that, sessions run on timed full papers with component marks reported on matched papers only.

faqs.question: Is it a problem if my child memorises 0455 model answers?
faqs.answer: It costs marks, which is the practical argument against it before any ethical one. Section B questions are set in specific contexts, and a rehearsed paragraph answers the general topic rather than the particular stem. The marked result is a fluent, well-organised answer scoring below a rougher one that addressed the question. We use exemplars as marking exercises instead: the student levels the exemplar themselves, states why it sits where it does, then writes their own answer on a different context. Structure transfers between stems; memorised content does not. We do not supply answers for a student to reproduce.

faqs.question: How do you report 0455 progress between school mocks?
faqs.answer: By measures that can actually move in four weeks. The levelled scripts themselves, the target list showing what has closed, the average number of explanation links per answer, the count of source references in Section A attempts, the five diagram checks passed or failed, and component marks on matched papers once timed work starts. What we do not send is a weekly predicted grade. A grade derived from three answers in an essay subject where question choice can swing a script is a guess with a number attached, and reporting one every fortnight manufactures precision that nobody has.

faqs.question: Can 0455 sessions work around Ramadan and Dubai school holidays?
faqs.answer: Yes, and planning for it beats reacting to it. During Ramadan most of our UAE sessions move to post-Iftar timing, and the work shifts towards marked written answers completed earlier in the day with the session used for review, which suits shorter concentration windows. School holidays are usually the most productive weeks of the year for essay-subject work, because a student can write a full timed paper without a school day either side of it. We schedule around travel too; an online session follows a family to wherever they are, with the timing adjusted to the new zone.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-economics-0455-tut.closingHeading: Ask to see one levelled 0455 answer
dubai/cambridge-igcse-economics-0455-tut.closingBody: The quickest way to judge an economics tutor is to ask them to level a real answer in front of you and explain the band. If they can name the missing component, whether that is a second link, a counter-argument or a judgement with a stated basis, they will be able to move your child's script. If they describe the answer as needing more detail, they will produce a longer script in the same band. Start with a diagnostic, read the levelled answer, and review the pile of marked scripts at four weeks and again at twelve. The decision at twelve weeks is the one that matters, and it should be made on paper rather than on impression.

intro.heading: Start with the number, because that is what the search is really about
paragraphs: A Dubai parent typing "0500 home tutor" into Google at ten at night has usually just read a report card. The English grade has slipped from a 6 to a 5, the school has said something vague about "developing analytical depth", and the obvious move is to find somebody who will come round on a Tuesday and fix it. The first thing that should happen on a page like this is a straight answer about money, because every other decision follows from it.

Market rates for private tuition in Dubai are published, if you know where to look. EdFlik advertises from AED 45-65 an hour at the budget end. Tutopiya starts lower still, from AED 33-52. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150. TutorChase quotes AED 270. BartyED charges AED 650 for its premium tier. Bestimate's 2026 rate survey puts in-home one-to-one visits between AED 180 and AED 350, with independent home tutors reaching AED 500 once travel is priced in. Those are other companies' numbers, quoted here with their names attached, and they describe the market a Dubai family is shopping in.

The spread between AED 45 and AED 650 is not a mystery. It is mostly a measure of how much mark-scheme knowledge sits behind the hour, and how far somebody has to drive to deliver it. An undergraduate who speaks excellent English can help a Year 9 student read more carefully. A teacher who has marked hundreds of Paper 1 summary tasks can tell your child why the three points they wrote scored one mark between them. Those are different services at different prices, and 0500 punishes the gap more than most subjects, because the paper rewards precision about language rather than recall of content.

IB Gram sits in the online one-to-one part of that market. We do not sell home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to a Dubai address is a service we run only in India. For a family in Dubai that is a feature rather than a compromise, and the reason is geographic. If the tutor has to reach Mirdif or Arabian Ranches by half past four, the pool shrinks to whoever is free within a short drive. Online, the pool is every 0500 specialist who can take a slot in Gulf Standard Time, and the money you were paying for petrol and Sheikh Zayed Road goes into marking instead.

The rest of this page is built around that single idea: what the number is, what makes it move in this emirate specifically, and what you should get for it. There is a rate table with sources per row, a travel calculation you can check against your own commute, a term-by-term budget, and a plain statement of what a tutor may never touch in a coursework folder. If you finish reading and still want somebody at the dining table, you will at least know what the market charges for that and why.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-english-first-lang.programmesIntro: English as a First Language sits inside a Cambridge pathway that starts years before the IGCSE entry and continues after it. Where your child is on that pathway changes how many hours the 0500 grade needs, and changes the price accordingly.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary
programmes.description: The three years where reading stamina is either built or missed. Checkpoint tests run in March, May and October, and the writing strand is where a future 0500 candidate first meets the difference between describing an event and shaping a reader's response. Work here is cheap relative to its effect: an hour a week in Year 8 costs the budget band and removes the need for an exam-year scramble.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools vary widely in how seriously Checkpoint writing is used as a diagnostic. Some British-curriculum schools in Al Barsha and Dubai Hills set internal targets from it; others treat it as a formality. Ask your child's head of English which Checkpoint strand came out weakest, because that answer tells you whether you are buying reading hours or writing hours two years later.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE English as a First Language (0500)
programmes.description: Two written papers, each two hours long, each carrying half the grade. Paper 1 tests reading: close comprehension, a summary task, analysis of a writer's language choices, and an extended response that asks the candidate to write in role from the text. Paper 2 tests directed writing and composition. Schools may instead enter a coursework portfolio in place of the written composition paper, and speaking and listening is reported separately rather than inside the overall grade.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's British-curriculum cohort is large enough that 0500 entry patterns differ school by school. Some schools in Jumeirah and Emirates Hills enter almost everyone for 0500; others stream weaker writers into English as a Second Language. Check which syllabus number appears on your child's entry sheet before paying for tuition, because 0500 and 0510 ask for genuinely different skills.

programmes.name: Cambridge O Level English Language
programmes.description: A smaller number of schools still enter candidates for O Level English rather than IGCSE. The assessment shape is similar enough that a 0500 tutor can teach it, but the question wording and the weighting of the summary task differ. Hours are usually fewer because the paper is more predictable, and that shows up as a slightly lower total cost across an exam year.
programmes.countryNote: If your child's Dubai school is running O Level English, the exam centre will be using the same June and November Cambridge series and the same six administrative zones for timetabling. Ask the exams officer which zone the centre sits in, because a parent revising from the wrong zone timetable is a real and avoidable problem.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS & A Level English Language
programmes.description: The continuation route for a strong 0500 candidate. The skills carry over directly: close language analysis, controlled writing in a specified form, and the discipline of answering the question actually asked. Families who invest in 0500 writing in Year 10 typically need fewer hours at AS, which changes the two-year cost picture rather than just this term's.
programmes.countryNote: For MoE equivalency on the British track, students must show five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. English usually counts as one of the five, which is why a borderline 0500 grade carries weight beyond the school report.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-english-first-lang.subjectsIntro: Families rarely buy one subject. The list below shows where a 0500 student in Dubai most often needs a second set of hours, with the syllabus code so you can check it against the entry sheet rather than against a school's marketing.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (0500)
subjects.description: The page's subject. Two two-hour written papers, split evenly between reading and writing. Marks leak on the summary task, on writer's-effects answers that list devices without explaining effect, and on compositions that run out of structure in the final third.

subjects.name: English Literature (0475)
subjects.description: Frequently taken alongside 0500 in Dubai schools. The overlap is real but partial: both reward close reading, but literature demands memorised quotation and a sustained argument about a writer's method rather than a response written in role.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510)
subjects.description: The alternative entry for students whose English is strong but not first-language fluent. Assesses reading, writing, listening and speaking separately. A student moved from 0500 to 0510 in Year 11 needs different practice, not less of it.

subjects.name: History (0470)
subjects.description: The subject where weak 0500 writing shows up fastest. Source questions reward the same inference skill as Paper 1 comprehension, and extended answers collapse for the same reason compositions do: no plan, no paragraph control.

subjects.name: Geography (0460)
subjects.description: Case-study answers need precise, economical prose under time pressure. Students who fix their 0500 paragraphing usually gain marks here without extra geography teaching, which is worth knowing before buying two separate tutors.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Evaluation marks depend on written judgement, not on content recall. A Dubai student who can write a controlled two-sided paragraph for 0500 Paper 2 can usually be taught to transfer it here in three or four sessions.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: Listed because it is the most common second subject in a Dubai family's budget. Pairing maths and English in the same week spreads the monthly cost but doubles it; most families stagger them across Year 10 and Year 11 instead.

subjects.name: Combined Science (0653)
subjects.description: Six-mark extended responses in science are marked for clarity as well as content. Students who have learned to answer the question asked in 0500 tend to stop writing everything they know, which is where science marks are usually lost.

subjects.name: Arabic as a Second Language (0544)
subjects.description: Included because Arabic is mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum. For non-Arab students this often runs alongside 0500 and competes for the same homework evenings, which affects how many English sessions a week is realistic.

sections.heading: What "0500 home tutor in Dubai" usually means in practice
paragraphs: A Cambridge IGCSE English First Language 0500 home tutor in Dubai, as the phrase is used by families, means private one-to-one English tuition arranged outside school for a Year 10 or Year 11 candidate. The word "home" describes where parents imagine the lesson happening rather than anything about the teaching. In practice the question behind the search is whether somebody will give a single child undivided attention on the two papers that decide the grade.

IB Gram answers that question with one-to-one lessons delivered live on video to Dubai households. We do not send tutors to UAE addresses; in-home visits are a service we run only in India, and no page on this site should suggest otherwise. What a Dubai family gets instead is a specialist chosen for 0500 rather than for postcode. That distinction is worth stating plainly because it is the whole trade: you give up a physical presence in the room and you gain a much larger pool of people who know the paper.

The practical difference shows up in the first session. An in-home tutor with a general English background will usually start by reading through a text with the student. A 0500 specialist starts by asking for a marked script, finds the three question types where marks were lost, and spends the hour on those. Both feel like a lesson. Only one of them changes the mark. Everything below is written to help a parent in Dubai tell the difference before any money changes hands, starting with what the market charges and why the figures vary by a factor of ten.

sections.heading: The travel arithmetic hiding inside an in-home rate
paragraphs: An in-home quote in Dubai is a teaching fee plus a driving fee, and the driving fee is invisible. A tutor who accepts a 4:30pm slot in Arabian Ranches and a 6:30pm slot in Al Barsha has committed roughly ninety minutes of unpaid Dubai traffic to earn two paid hours. Rational pricing recovers that, which is why Bestimate's in-home band starts at AED 180 while its online observations start far lower. Nothing dishonest is happening; the number simply contains a cost that has nothing to do with English.

The second hidden cost is choice. Insisting on a tutor who can physically reach Mudon by half past four reduces the candidate pool to people who happen to live nearby and happen to be free. For maths that is survivable. For 0500 it is a real constraint, because the skill you are buying is familiarity with how examiners reward language analysis, and that is not evenly distributed across Dubai's residential communities. Online, the same family can work with a specialist who has marked the paper for years and who schedules in Gulf Standard Time.

The third is reliability. A driving tutor caught on Al Khail Road loses the first fifteen minutes of a paid hour, and a sandstorm or a school event cancels the session entirely. sections.heading: What the two 0500 papers actually ask a candidate to do
paragraphs: Paper 1 is reading, and it is two hours long. It moves from close comprehension of a text, through a summary task that rewards selection and concision, into analysis of how a writer's language choices work on a reader, and finally an extended response that asks the candidate to write in a given role using material from the passage. Each of those four demands is a separate skill. A student can be genuinely strong at comprehension and still lose a grade on the summary because nobody ever showed them that marks come from points selected, not from sentences produced.

Paper 2 is writing, also two hours, and splits into directed writing and composition. Directed writing supplies material and a form, and tests whether a candidate can shape somebody else's content for a stated audience and purpose. Composition is a free choice between descriptive and narrative writing, marked on content and structure alongside style and accuracy. Some Dubai schools enter a coursework portfolio instead of the written composition component, and speaking and listening is reported separately rather than folded into the grade. Confirm which route your child's school has entered, on the entry sheet, before buying hours.

Because the two papers carry equal weight, the cheapest grade movement usually sits wherever the gap is wider, not wherever the student is more anxious. Most Dubai candidates arriving for 0500 support are better readers than writers, and almost all of them have written fewer than ten full timed compositions in two years. The exact mark allocations and the component structure change between syllabus years, so check the syllabus for your child's exam year on cambridgeinternational.org rather than relying on a tutor's memory of an older version.

sections.heading: Where 0500 marks leak, in order of how much they cost
paragraphs: The summary task is the single most reliable source of lost marks. Candidates rewrite the passage in shorter sentences instead of selecting distinct points, then run out of words before the final third of the text. A tutor fixes this by marking a summary with the points numbered in the margin, so the student sees that nine lines of elegant prose contained four creditable points when the task offered many more. Two sessions on this alone will often move a borderline grade.

Writer's-effects answers are the second. A Dubai student who has been taught to spot devices will produce a confident paragraph naming metaphor, sibilance and personification without ever explaining what the reader experiences as a result. Marks follow the explanation, not the label. The repair is mechanical and teachable: quote short, name the effect on the reader, then explain why that particular word choice produces it rather than a synonym would.

Composition loses marks structurally rather than linguistically. Openings are strong because they have been practised; endings are weak because the clock runs out. Most candidates have never planned a composition in under four minutes, and most have never been forced to finish one in the time the exam actually allows. The fix is repetition under conditions, which is why a pre-series block is priced as two sessions a week rather than one. Accuracy matters too, but a well-structured piece with three comma errors outscores a flawless fragment of a story every time.

sections.heading: Permits, price and why the cheapest quote carries the most risk
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted through MoHRE free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page, "Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing", lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, with applications made through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Two consequences matter to a parent comparing quotes. The permit costs nothing, so no tutor can justify a higher rate by pointing at licensing expenses. And individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, which means the AED 45 an hour arrangement made through a community group chat carries a risk that the invoice does not mention. No fine schedule has been published, so any figure quoted to you as the penalty should be treated with scepticism.

A separate rule applies to anyone running tuition from premises with staff. That is a training institute and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit, with initial approval first and a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps. IB Gram is not a Dubai training institute and does not hold that permit, and holds no approval from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or the IB. Reporting from Abu Dhabi also indicates that ADEK's professional-ethics rules prevent school staff from tutoring students enrolled at their own school for payment, which is worth verifying against the current policy document before relying on it.

sections.heading: Costing a full Year 10 and Year 11 run in Dubai
paragraphs: Most Dubai families overspend on English in one term and underspend across two years. The pattern is familiar: nothing happens in Year 10, panic arrives with the Year 11 mocks, and three sessions a week get booked at specialist rates for the eight weeks before the June series. That is the most expensive way to buy the same number of hours, and it is also the least effective, because composition technique improves through spaced redrafting rather than through volume in March.

The table below puts tuition next to the other numbers in a Dubai education budget. The anchor at the top is useful context: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. School fees are, for one year, a fixed line. Tuition is the variable one, and it is the line a family can actually plan.

Entry costs are the item parents forget. If your child sits as a private candidate rather than through their school, the exam centre sets the entry charge and administration fee, not the tutor. Ask the centre in writing well before the final entry deadline, because Cambridge's deadlines sit months ahead of the exam window. For the March 2027 series, final entries were due on 27 November 2026 for an exam period running 3 February to 4 March 2027.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not touch in a 0500 coursework folder
paragraphs: Where a Dubai school has entered the coursework route instead of the written composition paper, the boundary between teaching and malpractice becomes something a parent should understand rather than assume. The pieces in that folder must be the candidate's own work, produced under the school's stated conditions and authenticated by the school. A tutor who improves the folder by supplying sentences has not helped; they have created a problem that lands on the student, not on the tutor.

What a tutor can legitimately do is substantial. They can teach the form, model a different piece on a different subject, explain the assessment descriptors in plain language, question a draft until the student finds the weakness themselves, and mark a practice piece that will never be submitted. They can also say, honestly, that a paragraph is not working and ask what the student was trying to achieve. None of that touches the submitted text. All of it changes the next draft.

One competitor in this market sells finished Internal Assessments outright. That is an academic-integrity breach with consequences for the candidate, and it is the clearest line in our own policy: tutors teach, review and give feedback on a student's own work, and nothing else. If a Dubai provider offers to produce assessed writing for your child, the correct response is to walk away and tell the school. The same rule covers artificial-intelligence drafting: a tutor may discuss how to critique machine-generated prose, never hand it over as the student's.

You see the quote before anything is booked, and we say plainly if a student needs fewer hours than the parent expected. Pausing for a school trip or Ramadan does not cost the slot.

process.description: One full piece written to time, marked against the published descriptors, returned with two targets rather than ten. The targets are written for a parent to read, not for a staffroom. Over a term those notes become the record of what changed and what did not.

faqs.question: How much does a Cambridge IGCSE English First Language 0500 home tutor cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market rates in Dubai run roughly AED 45-150 an hour at the budget end, AED 150-300 for a qualified online subject tutor, and AED 180-500 for an in-home visit once travel is priced in. Specialist IGCSE and A Level tutors sit at AED 200-450 and above, and one premium provider publishes AED 650. Those figures come from EdFlik, Tutopiya, Unitors, TutorChase, BartyED and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai survey, read in October 2026. They describe the market rather than an IB Gram price list; our own route is a free trial lesson followed by a quote for the sessions a particular student needs.

faqs.question: Will a 0500 tutor come to our villa in Dubai Hills Estate?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE, and in-home visits are a service we run only in India. Dubai lessons are delivered one-to-one on live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. The reason is not cost-cutting: it is that a Dubai Hills family restricted to tutors who can drive in by half past four chooses from a small pool, while a family online chooses a specialist who has marked 0500 scripts for years. If a physical presence in the room is essential to you, the market rate for that is AED 180-500 an hour and this page explains what sits inside that number.

faqs.question: Why is an in-home English rate in Dubai so much higher than an online one?
faqs.answer: Because an in-home fee is a teaching fee plus an unpaid driving fee. A tutor taking a 4:30pm slot in Arabian Ranches and a 6:30pm slot in Al Barsha spends about ninety minutes in traffic to earn two paid hours, and the quote has to recover that. Bestimate's in-home band starts at AED 180 for this reason while online observations start considerably lower. The second cost is choice: the pool shrinks to tutors who live nearby and are free at that hour, which matters more for a language paper than for arithmetic practice.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper undergraduate tutor good enough for 0500?
faqs.answer: For reading practice in Year 8 or 9, often yes. For a Year 11 candidate two grades below target, usually not. The budget band buys somebody who speaks excellent English; the mid and specialist bands buy somebody who can look at a summary answer and say that nine well-written lines contained four creditable points. That diagnosis is the service, and it is what moves a 0500 mark. A useful test before paying anybody: ask them to explain, in plain words, how the writer's-effects question is credited. The answer separates the bands quickly.

faqs.question: How many 0500 sessions a week should a Year 11 student in Dubai budget for?
faqs.answer: One session a week through the year, rising to two in the term before the written papers, covers most cases. At Bestimate's mid band that is roughly AED 600-1,200 a month for the single session and AED 1,000-2,000 or more during an intensive block. Three sessions a week is almost always a sign that work was left too late rather than a sign of ambition, and it buys the same hours at a worse price. The variable that actually matters is how many full compositions get marked and redrafted, not how many hours appear on the invoice.

faqs.question: Does the hourly rate normally include marking a whole Paper 1?
faqs.answer: Ask, because it varies and the answer changes the real price. Marking a full two-hour reading paper properly takes a tutor a substantial part of an hour, so some providers mark extracts, some charge separately, and some simply do not mark at all. With us, one full piece of written work is marked between sessions against the published descriptors and returned with two targets. If a quote looks unusually low, marking is the item most often missing from it, and it is the item that produces the grade change.

faqs.question: Does the MoHRE tutor permit change what we pay for 0500 lessons?
faqs.answer: It should not. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, with MoHRE listing a two-working-day completion time and no fee. So a tutor cannot justify a higher rate by citing licensing costs. The permit matters for a different reason: individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No official fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific amount quoted to you as unverified.

faqs.question: Can one tutor handle both 0500 and 0475 for the same student?
faqs.answer: Frequently, and in Dubai it is a common request because many schools enter both. The skills overlap in close reading and diverge sharply afterwards: 0500 Paper 1 asks a candidate to write in role from a text, while 0475 asks for a sustained argument about a writer's method, supported by memorised quotation. A tutor comfortable with both will usually split the week by paper rather than by subject. Doing so with one tutor saves scheduling friction and keeps the writing advice consistent, which matters more than it sounds.

faqs.question: What does the free trial cover before we pay for any 0500 sessions?
faqs.answer: A full sixty-minute one-to-one lesson with the proposed tutor, at no cost, with no card details taken and no obligation to continue. The trial works best when it covers one question type end to end, because that is when you can hear whether the tutor explains how marks are awarded or simply corrects mistakes. Send a recently marked script beforehand so the hour starts with real evidence. If the match is wrong, tell us and we propose a different tutor rather than asking you to make it work.

faqs.question: Do English tuition rates in Dubai rise closer to the June Cambridge series?
faqs.answer: Availability tightens rather than headline rates rising, and the effect on a family budget is the same. From February onwards the specialists with 0500 marking experience fill their Gulf Standard Time afternoon slots first, so late bookers choose between a less suitable tutor and an awkward hour. Booking a block in the autumn term costs less in total than an eight-week scramble in spring, because fewer sessions are needed when redrafting has had time to work. The cheapest intervention in this subject is always the early one.

faqs.question: Is English harder to move than maths, and does that change the hours we need?
faqs.answer: It moves differently rather than more slowly. A maths topic can be fixed in two sessions because the gap is usually a specific procedure. A 0500 grade moves when habits change: planning before writing, selecting points in a summary, explaining effect rather than naming devices. That takes repeated marked practice spread over weeks, which is why English support is better bought as a weekly habit than as a pre-exam block. Families who treat it like maths tend to buy more hours later and get less from them.

faqs.question: Who pays the Cambridge entry fee if my child sits 0500 as a private candidate?
faqs.answer: The family pays the exam centre directly, and the centre sets both the entry charge and its own administration fee. A tutor is not involved in that transaction and should not be quoting it. Timing matters more than the amount: Cambridge deadlines sit months ahead of the exam window, and for the March 2027 series final entries were due on 27 November 2026 for an exam period running 3 February to 4 March 2027. Ask your chosen centre in writing which series it offers and what its cut-off date is.

faqs.question: Does a 0500 grade count towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: On the British track, students must submit proof of five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. English normally counts as one of them, which is why a borderline grade has consequences beyond the school report. Verify the current requirements with the Ministry of Education or your emirate's attestation channel; IB Gram does not perform or guarantee equivalency.

faqs.question: Can we pause 0500 sessions during Ramadan without losing our tutor's slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, and many Dubai families instead move the session rather than pause it. School days shorten during Ramadan and concentration shifts, so an afternoon slot often works better in the late evening after Iftar. Because lessons run on video, that change costs nobody a journey and can be agreed week by week. If you would rather stop for the month, tell us and the slot is held. Nothing is charged for sessions that do not happen, and the marking cycle picks up where it left off afterwards.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-english-first-lang.closingHeading: Start with one marked script and a free trial lesson
dubai/cambridge-igcse-english-first-lang.closingBody: If you have read this far, you probably already know whether your child's problem is reading or writing. Send the most recent marked script and we will tell you which of the four Paper 1 demands is costing the most marks, and roughly how many sessions it takes to move. The trial lesson is free, takes sixty minutes, and needs no card details. Lessons after that run one-to-one on live video to your household in Dubai, in Gulf Standard Time, with one full piece of written work marked between each pair of sessions. If the honest answer is that your child needs fewer hours than you expected, we will say so.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-english-first-lang.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach Cambridge IGCSE English as a First Language online to students in Dubai schools. The common thread is marking: each has assessed timed 0500 scripts in volume and records per-question marks, so a parent can see which question type moved and which did not.

intro.heading: Judge an English tutor on the marked script, not the first conversation
paragraphs: English tuition is unusually easy to sell and unusually hard to verify. A session can feel productive, the student can come away saying the tutor was lovely, and nothing measurable changes for four months until a mock paper says so. That is why this page is built around evidence rather than around adjectives. Everything described below produces an artefact you can look at: a marked script, a numbered summary, a first draft beside a fourth, a table of marks by question type.

The reason evidence matters more in 0500 than in most subjects is the shape of the paper. Both written components are two hours long and each carries half the grade. Paper 1 tests reading through four separate demands, and Paper 2 tests directed writing and composition. A student can be strong at three of those demands and lose a grade on the fourth, and no amount of general reading practice will reveal which one is leaking. Only a marked script does, which means marking is the diagnostic rather than an afterthought.

Dubai makes the case sharper. The emirate has the densest private-school market in the country, with KHDA counting 227 private schools and 387,441 students in 2024-25 across 17 curricula, and British-curriculum provision taking the largest share of enrolment at 37 per cent. Classes are large by design, English departments mark to departmental deadlines, and individual redrafting of a full composition is rare. A student can reach the Year 11 mocks having never had a whole piece of writing marked line by line against the published descriptors.

Online delivery is what makes the marking affordable and the specialist reachable. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses, and in-home visits are a service we run only in India. For a Dubai family that removes the geographic constraint entirely: a student in Dubai Marina or Dubai Creek Harbour works with somebody chosen for their familiarity with the 0500 mark scheme, not for living nearby, and the hour that would have gone into driving down Sheikh Zayed Road goes into annotating a script instead.

What follows is the working method rather than a sales pitch. There is a week-by-week table of what gets produced and what reaches the parent, a breakdown of what each Paper 1 task actually credits, an honest account of what six weeks of composition redrafting does and does not achieve, the Cambridge entry clock counted backwards from the written papers, and the line a tutor must not cross with a coursework folder. Read the tables first if you are short of time; they carry the argument. Everything stated as a date or a figure on this page names the source it came from, and anything we could not verify is marked as unverified rather than smoothed over, which is a habit worth applying to every tutoring page you read this week.
bullets: Per-question marks recorded from week one, not a single overall grade
Summary answers marked by points credited, counted in the margin
Compositions kept in versions so movement is visible, not asserted
A written review at four sessions, including the option to stop
All sessions one-to-one on live video, in Gulf Standard Time

dubai/cambridge-igcse-english-first-lang.programmesIntro: Evidence looks different at each stage of an English pathway, because the assessment asks for different things. The programmes below are the ones Dubai students most often sit before, during and after 0500.

programmes.name: IB MYP Language and Literature
programmes.description: Marked against four criteria rather than against band descriptors, which changes what a student is used to seeing on returned work. MYP students moving into a Cambridge entry often write fluently and structure loosely, because criterion-based feedback rewards exploration more than it rewards the controlled forms a 0500 paper asks for.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai has a substantial IB cohort, around 7 per cent of private-school enrolment, so students transferring between an IB school in Nad Al Sheba and a British-curriculum school in Dubai Marina mid-secondary is common. The first marked piece of writing after a transfer is the single most useful diagnostic a tutor can have.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE English as a First Language (0500)
programmes.description: Two two-hour written papers of equal weight. Paper 1 moves from close comprehension through a summary task and language analysis to an extended response written in role. Paper 2 covers directed writing and composition. Some schools enter a coursework portfolio in place of the written composition component, and speaking and listening is reported separately.
programmes.countryNote: Component routes differ between Dubai schools, and the entry sheet is the only reliable source. Confirm the syllabus number and the component route with your child's exams officer before any tutoring plan is written, and check the syllabus for the exam year on cambridgeinternational.org rather than relying on an older version.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE English Language A
programmes.description: The main alternative entry in Dubai's British-curriculum schools. The reading demands are comparable but the anthology and the coursework option change what practice looks like, and the series calendar runs to Pearson's dates rather than Cambridge's. A tutor needs to know which board is on the entry sheet before setting a single past paper.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs International GCSE exams in May/June and November each year, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so check the live PDF rather than a tutor's calendar.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS Level English Language
programmes.description: Where 0500 habits either pay off or surface as problems. Close language analysis and writing in a controlled form carry over directly, so students who learned to plan and finish under time in Year 11 arrive with the mechanics already in place. Those who were taught content rather than technique tend to need the same work again at a higher rate.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools split after Year 11 between A Level and the IB Diploma, and the choice changes which English skills matter next. For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, students must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside the five GCSE or IGCSE subjects.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-english-first-lang.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are the ones where a marked 0500 script predicts a problem somewhere else. Each note says what the evidence usually shows rather than what the syllabus contains.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (0500)
subjects.description: The subject of this page. Marked scripts almost always show the same ranking of weakness: summary first, writer's effects second, composition endings third. Comprehension is rarely the problem, which is why generic reading practice feels pleasant and changes little.

subjects.name: English Language A (4EA1)
subjects.description: Often sat by siblings at different Dubai schools, which confuses parents comparing progress. Different anthology, different series dates, similar analytical demand. A tutor should be marking against the board actually on the entry sheet.

subjects.name: English Literature (0475)
subjects.description: The clearest evidence pair with 0500: students who cannot explain effect in a language paper usually narrate plot in a literature essay. Fixing the analytical sentence once tends to show up in both sets of marked work within a month.

subjects.name: History (0470)
subjects.description: Source inference and extended answers reward the same discipline as Paper 1. Marked history scripts from Dubai students frequently show knowledge without judgement, the exact failure pattern as a composition with no deliberate ending.

subjects.name: Global Perspectives (0457)
subjects.description: Research and written argument assessed through components the school supervises. Evidence of a student's own drafting matters here more than in most subjects, and a tutor's role stays firmly on the questioning side of the line.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Evaluation marks are written marks. Dubai students who have learned to hold two sides in one paragraph for Paper 2 directed writing transfer that in two or three sessions, which is visible in the next marked class test.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: Included as the comparison case. Maths evidence is unambiguous because a method is either right or wrong, which is why parents trust it more. English evidence needs the per-question record to become equally clear.

subjects.name: Physics (0625)
subjects.description: Six-mark extended answers are marked for clarity under time pressure. Students who stop writing everything they know after 0500 coaching typically pick up marks here without any additional physics teaching.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language (0508)
subjects.description: Arabic is mandatory in Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. For Arab students the written workload lands in the same evenings as 0500 redrafting, which is a scheduling fact rather than a teaching one.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-english-first-lang.regionsIntro: Online delivery means the question is not how far a tutor drives but when a student can realistically sit at a desk. The communities below show how differently that lands across Dubai.

regions.note: Parents working in the towers themselves often want a session they can watch the last ten minutes of. The written review at four sessions gets read closely in JLT, which is a good reason to make it specific rather than reassuring.

regions.name: Business Bay
regions.note: Long parental working hours and a lot of 8pm starts. A session timed late suits the household but rarely suits a Year 11 writing a timed composition, so the composition is set for a Saturday morning and marked before the evening slot.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai
regions.note: Short distances, slow traffic and a cohort split across several nearby British-curriculum schools. Students here frequently arrive with excellent vocabulary and no practice at finishing a composition inside the time allowed.

regions.name: Palm Jumeirah
regions.note: Households with the fewest scheduling constraints and the most frequent travel. Version history is the useful artefact here, because a family that misses three weeks for a trip needs to see where the writing was when they left.

regions.name: Dubai Creek Harbour and Al Jaddaf
regions.note: A newer, growing secondary cohort with several schools recently opened nearby. Dubai added seven private schools for 2026-27, creating 16,846 places, and new schools mean new marking cultures to read a script against.

sections.heading: What an online 0500 session leaves behind in writing
paragraphs: A Cambridge IGCSE English First Language 0500 online tutor in Dubai, working properly, produces four artefacts in the first fortnight: a marked timed response with per-question marks, a summary with the creditable points numbered in the margin, a composition in two versions, and a short written note naming the two tasks that are costing the most. If after two weeks none of those exists, the sessions are conversation rather than tuition, whatever the rate.

This matters because English feedback is easy to deliver in a form nobody can act on. "Needs more depth of analysis" is true of most Year 10 writing and tells a parent nothing. "Three quotations were named as metaphors and none explained what the reader feels" is the same observation turned into something a student can repair on Saturday. The second version only exists if somebody marked the whole piece rather than skimming it during the lesson.

Lessons run one-to-one on live video to Dubai households, with the screen shared so the student watches annotation happen rather than receiving it afterwards. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that service runs only in India. The practical gain is not convenience but choice of marker, because the person reading your child's script is picked for their 0500 marking experience rather than for living within a short drive of your community. A family in Jumeirah Lakes Towers and a family in Al Jaddaf get the same marker, on the same evidence loop, at the same hour of the Dubai evening.

sections.heading: The marking record, week by week
paragraphs: Progress in a written subject is a sequence, not a snapshot. The table below is the sequence we run for a Year 11 student starting in the autumn term, and it is deliberately boring: the same loop of produce, mark, record, redraft, with the emphasis moving across the Paper 1 tasks and into Paper 2 as the weaker demands get fixed. Nothing in it depends on where the student lives, which is why it works equally well for a family in Downtown Dubai and one on the Palm.

The third column is the part most providers skip. Marking a full two-hour reading paper against the descriptors takes a substantial part of an hour, so the economics push tutors towards marking extracts or towards discussing work in the lesson instead. That saves tutor time and destroys the evidence trail. Recording per-question marks costs a few extra minutes and turns six weeks of work into a comparison a parent can read without a teaching background.

The fourth column is what reaches you. Not a report with percentages, which would be invented, but the student's own work in versions, a count of creditable points found against points available, and a short note in plain words. At week six there is a written review that compares the first timed script with the latest one and says whether the session count should rise, fall or stop. Families are told to stop more often than the industry average would suggest, because a student who has fixed the summary task may not need a tutor for the rest of the year.

sections.heading: What each Paper 1 task actually credits
paragraphs: Most lost marks in 0500 come from a misread of the task rather than from weak English. A student who writes beautifully and summarises the first third of a passage will score less than a plainer writer who selects points across the whole text. Once a family sees that stated as a rule, the marked scripts start making sense, and the sessions stop feeling like generalised English improvement and start looking like repairs to specific habits.

The table sets each task against what the mark scheme rewards, the misread that costs most, and the drill that fixes it. The drills are short on purpose. A student does not need another hour of teaching about metaphor; they need to write three effects in three minutes with device names banned, twice a week, until explanation becomes the reflex. The same logic applies to the extended response, where the single most common failure in Dubai scripts is an essay that ignores the role it was told to adopt.

Exact mark allocations and the component structure change between syllabus years, so the table deliberately describes what is credited rather than quoting mark totals. Check the syllabus for your child's exam year on cambridgeinternational.org, and check the component route on the entry sheet. A tutor who quotes mark splits from memory is quoting a syllabus that may have been replaced. The behaviour the paper rewards has been stable for years; the arithmetic around it has not, and confusing the two is how revision time gets spent on the wrong component.

sections.heading: Six weeks of composition drafts: what movement actually looks like
paragraphs: Composition improves in a pattern that surprises parents. The first redraft usually looks worse. A student told to plan in four minutes and to write a deliberate ending will produce something stiffer and less fluent than their comfortable, unplanned narrative, and the marks often dip before they rise. Knowing that in advance is the difference between a family holding the line for three weeks and a family concluding after one that the tutor is not working.

By the third or fourth piece the structure stops costing fluency. The useful evidence here is not the mark but the version history: the same student's first composition and fourth composition in the same document, with the opening paragraph, the turn and the ending visible in both. Most Dubai students we see have written fewer than ten full timed compositions across two years, so four marked and redrafted pieces in six weeks is a meaningful change in volume as well as in technique.

What this cannot do is manufacture a grade. No tutor can promise a specific mark, and anybody who does is selling something other than teaching. What six weeks of redrafting reliably produces is a student who plans, finishes, and knows what the ending is for. Whether that converts into a grade boundary crossing depends on the paper, the session and the other three Paper 1 demands, which is precisely why the per-question record exists. A family that can read the record can also judge for itself whether another term of sessions is worth buying, which is a better position than trusting a tutor's summary of their own work.

sections.heading: Annotation on a shared screen, and why it beats a page on a table
paragraphs: In a physical lesson the tutor annotates a script while the student watches upside down, then the page goes into a bag. Online, the script sits on a shared screen, the annotation happens in a colour the student can toggle, and the file is still there on Saturday when the redraft happens. Nothing about this is magic; it is simply a better record, and in a subject where the evidence is the teaching, a better record is most of the benefit.

Three further things get easier. Two versions of the same composition can be shown side by side, which is almost impossible on paper. A short walkthrough can be recorded so the student hears the marking rationale again mid-redraft. And a parent can read the same annotated file without needing to ask how the session went, which removes the weekly interrogation that most teenagers dislike more than the homework.

IB Gram does not sell in-home sessions anywhere in the UAE, so there is no version of this service that arrives at a Dubai address. If a family strongly prefers somebody physically present, the market rate for that in this emirate is higher and the pool of 0500 specialists available within driving distance of any one community is small. Our judgement is that for a written subject the marker matters more than the room, and the artefacts above are the argument for it. Parents who have tried both usually describe the same difference: the online sessions produced files they could open, and the in-home sessions produced a feeling that the hour had gone well.

sections.heading: When Dubai students can actually sit down and write
paragraphs: A timed composition needs ninety undisturbed minutes, and the Dubai school week does not hand those out generously. Secondary students finish between 2pm and 3pm, many have activities until five, and homework for a full IGCSE set competes for the same evening. Add the mandatory UAE subjects, which every Dubai private school teaches regardless of its licensed curriculum, and the realistic slot for a timed piece is a weekend morning rather than a Tuesday night.

Our scheduling therefore separates writing from teaching. The timed piece is set for Saturday or Sunday morning when the student is fresh, marked during the week, and discussed in a live session that can sit as late as 8pm without damage. That split is only possible because nobody has to travel; a tutor driving to Mirdif for a 4:30pm slot has to put both halves of the work into the same visit, which is why in-home sessions so often become discussion rather than marking.

Ramadan changes the pattern again. School days shorten, concentration moves later, and many families prefer post-Iftar sessions for the month. Because lessons are on video, that shift costs nobody a journey and can be agreed week by week. Sessions can also pause entirely for travel without the slot being lost. The planning rule we use is simple: protect the weekend writing window first, then fit the live hour around whatever the household is doing. A student who never writes to time will not discover their pacing problem until the paper itself, which is the most expensive place in the process to find it.

sections.heading: The Cambridge clock, counted backwards from the written papers
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. That single fact is worth more to a Dubai parent than most revision advice.

Entry deadlines sit a long way ahead of the papers. For the March 2027 series, the exam period runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries were due on 27 November 2026, forecast grades on 27 February 2027, results reached Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June. Those dates are the worked example of why a tuition plan that starts after the mocks has already missed the decisions that matter, including whether to enter a candidate at all.

The table counts the clock backwards. Use it to work out which decisions belong to the school, which belong to Cambridge and which belong to you. Note that IB session dates are deliberately absent from this page: ibo.org blocks automated checking and no IB date here has been confirmed from the IB itself, so confirm any Diploma timing with your school's IB coordinator rather than with a tutor. Pearson candidates should read their own calendar from the live provisional timetable, since those dates can be revised after publication and a tutor's copy goes stale quietly.
