sections.heading: What in-home literature tuition costs in Dubai, and what travel adds to it
paragraphs: Dubai parents rarely get a straight price from tutoring websites. Of the competitor pages reviewed for this market in October 2026, three published no price at all and two quoted in US dollars, a currency no Dubai family pays a tutor in. The figures below are market rates in AED, each attributed to the provider or rate survey that published it. They are not IB Gram's price list, and nothing here is a quote.

The pattern across sources is consistent. Online one-to-one with a qualified subject teacher sits in the middle, in-home one-to-one carries a clear premium, and that premium is travel. A tutor driving from Al Barsha to Arabian Ranches for a 5pm lesson has given up ninety minutes of their working day for sixty minutes of paid work, and the rate reflects it. Nobody is overcharging; the economics are simply what they are.

For literature specifically there is a second cost that never appears on a rate card: the cost of a mismatch. A cheaper tutor who has not taught your child's set texts will spend paid hours reading them. At AED 200 an hour, three sessions of catch-up is AED 600 spent on the tutor's preparation. That is the real comparison to make, rather than the headline hourly figure.

IB Gram's own model is a free first lesson with the matched tutor, with no card details taken and no obligation to continue, followed by a quoted plan once the tutor has seen a piece of the student's writing. If the plan does not look worth it after the trial, nothing has been spent. We publish the market bands above so that the quote arrives in context rather than in a vacuum.

sections.heading: Online versus in-home for a text-based subject
paragraphs: The usual argument for in-home tuition is attention: a tutor in the room, no screen, no distractions. For some subjects and some students that case is strong. For closed-book literature essay work it is weaker than it looks, and the reason is that almost everything a literature tutor does is done to a document.

Annotation is the clearest example. A tutor marking a poem live on a shared screen produces a file the student keeps, and six months later that file is the revision material. The same lesson conducted over a paperback leaves pencil marks in a book that the student may or may not open again, and no record for the parent. Essay feedback behaves the same way: comments typed into a script are searchable, and the student can see whether the same fault appears in essay one and essay four.

Scheduling is the other decisive factor in Dubai specifically. Secondary students in Mirdif or Al Warqa attending schools on the Sheikh Zayed Road corridor are frequently not home before 4:30pm, and a tutor driving in across the same traffic is subject to the same delays. Online, a 7:15pm slot is a 7:15pm slot. When a family travels during Eid or the summer, the lesson follows them rather than stopping.

None of this makes in-home tuition a bad product. It makes it a different one, with a real premium attached and a smaller pool behind it. The table sets out the comparison honestly, including the places where a visiting tutor genuinely has the edge.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with your child's essay
paragraphs: This matters more in English than in any other subject, because the deliverable is writing and the line between coaching and authorship is easy to blur. The rule we work to is simple: the words that go to Cambridge must be the student's own. A tutor teaches, questions, models on a different text, marks, and explains why a paragraph underperforms. A tutor does not rewrite a student's paragraph into the version they would have written.

In practice that means feedback is given as instruction rather than as replacement text. Instead of supplying a better opening sentence, a tutor shows why the existing one delays the argument, demonstrates the move on an unrelated extract, and sends the student back to redraft their own. It is slower for one essay and considerably faster across a term, because the student can do it again without help.

Two related boundaries are worth stating. We do not supply Cambridge syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads; those belong to Cambridge, and a tutor's job is to point to the official source and work from it legitimately. And no tutor can promise a grade. Band descriptors are applied by examiners to a script written on one morning, and anyone offering certainty about that outcome is selling something they cannot deliver.

For families coming from an essay-writing service, the difference will feel stark at first. It is also the only version of this work that is safe for the student. Submitted work that is not a candidate's own is a malpractice matter with consequences that outlast any single grade.

sections.heading: Entries, series and the calendar read backwards
paragraphs: Cambridge runs IGCSE exams in a June series and a November series, and the entry deadlines sit months before the papers. Cambridge's own published key dates for the March 2027 series make the lead time visible: final entries close on 27 November 2026 for an exam period that begins on 3 February 2027, with forecast grades due on 27 February 2027. Different series carry different dates, but the shape is the same everywhere, and the deadline a Dubai family can actually miss is the school's internal one, which sits earlier still.

There is an administrative detail most parents never hear about and every exams officer worries about. Cambridge allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones, publishes a separate timetable version for each, and states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. If your child is revising from a timetable found online rather than the one the school issued, that is worth correcting today.

Read backwards from the exam window, a 0475 plan has a natural shape. Texts finished and annotated by the end of term one of Year 11. Full past papers under timing from February. The unseen component, where the school's route includes it, practised weekly from January rather than crammed in April, because it is a skill rather than a body of content. Mock results read in February as diagnostic information, not as a verdict.

November entries exist and are used, most often by students who missed a series through illness or who want one more attempt at a single subject. Pearson Edexcel runs an equivalent November series for its International GCSEs; its November 2026 timetable ran to 19 November 2026, with its November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026. Confirm every date against the board's live timetable page and your child's school, because provisional timetables are revised.

process.title: Tell us the texts, not just the subject

process.title: Send one marked piece of writing
process.description: A single marked essay tells a literature tutor more than any assessment call. We read what the school has already said, look at how quotations are handled, and arrive at the trial lesson with a view rather than a questionnaire.

process.description: Sixty minutes, one-to-one over live video, on a real piece of the student's current work. No card details are taken and there is no obligation to continue. Your child should finish it able to name one thing they will do differently.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge 0475 the same subject as First Language English 0500?
faqs.answer: No. 0475 is Literature in English and 0500 is First Language English, and they are separate syllabuses with separate papers and separate marking. First Language English rewards clear, controlled, accurate writing and reading comprehension. Literature rewards a close response to how a particular writer uses language, structure and form, supported by short quotations. This is why a child can hold a strong grade in 0500 and sit in the middle bands of 0475 at the same time. Most Dubai schools teach both to the same class, often with the same teacher, which hides the distinction until results arrive.

faqs.question: Which papers will my child sit for Cambridge IGCSE Literature in English 0475?
faqs.answer: Every candidate sits the poetry and prose paper, which carries half the grade and gives about forty-five minutes per essay. The remaining half depends on the route the school has entered: either a single closed-book drama paper, or a shorter open-text drama paper combined with an unseen paper on material the student has never studied. The school decides, so ask the head of English which components your child is entered for before booking tutoring. Confirm the current structure and timings against the Cambridge 0475 syllabus for your child's exam series, since component detail changes between syllabus cycles.

faqs.question: Does a 0475 tutor really need to know my child's set texts?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the question worth asking first. A tutor who has taught your child's play before recognises a two-line quotation instantly, knows which scenes passage questions tend to favour, and has marked real answers on that text. A tutor meeting the text for the first time spends the first few paid sessions reading it. At market rates that is several hundred dirhams spent on the tutor's preparation rather than your child's writing. We match on text first and tell you plainly when no specialist has taught that exact combination.

faqs.question: How much does in-home English Literature tuition cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market figures put in-home one-to-one tuition in Dubai at roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, with Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table giving AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500. Qualified online one-to-one sits lower, around AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE tuition from AED 150. The gap is travel time rather than teaching quality. These are other providers' published rates as of October 2026, not ours; IB Gram quotes after a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Can a tutor mark my child's literature essays against the assessment objectives?
faqs.answer: That is the core of the work. The four objectives in 0475 carry equal weight: knowledge of the text, understanding of meanings and contexts, response to language, structure and form, and a personal informed response. Marking against them shows a parent which objective is capping the grade, which is far more useful than a number. Scripts are returned annotated between sessions, and the next session is spent on the two or three recurring habits that cost the most marks rather than on a general discussion of the essay.

faqs.question: Should my child choose the passage-based question or the general essay question?
faqs.answer: For most students under time pressure the passage-based question is the safer choice, because the material is printed in front of them and the task is bounded. General essay questions tempt candidates into writing broadly about the whole text without selecting evidence, which is where relevance and analysis both slip. The decision should be made in practice over several papers, not in the exam hall, and it can differ by text: a student may be stronger on the passage for the novel and on the essay for the poetry selection.

faqs.question: How do you prepare for an unseen poetry or prose paper?
faqs.answer: By practising a method on unfamiliar material every week, not by reading more set texts. The method is deliberately mechanical at first: read twice, mark what is visibly unusual in the language and the shape, decide what the writer appears to be doing, then build three or four paragraphs around the clearest effects. Students fail this paper by hunting for a hidden meaning and writing nothing concrete. Weekly short practice from January, with a marked response every fortnight, turns an unpredictable paper into a predictable one.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a literature tutor to our home in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to a family's address is a service we run only in India. Every Dubai lesson is delivered one-to-one over live video on a fixed Gulf Standard Time slot. For closed-book literature work this suits the subject well, because annotation happens on a shared screen and the annotated text and marked scripts are saved and sent afterwards. It also widens the pool from tutors who can drive to your community to specialists who have taught your child's exact texts.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a Year 11 literature student usually need?
faqs.answer: One a week is the common pattern for a student who understands the texts but writes mid-band essays, with a timed essay written between sessions so the hour is spent on the writing rather than on reading aloud. Two a week is justified where a component route includes an unseen paper or where the student is behind on a set text. Short blocks of two or three sessions a week appear in the weeks before the exam window. More than that rarely helps, because essay writing improves on the marking cycle, not on contact hours.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with an essay my child has already drafted?
faqs.answer: A tutor can mark it, explain which objectives the draft is missing, model the move on a different extract, and send the student back to redraft in their own words. A tutor cannot rewrite the paragraph into their own version, and we do not. The words that go to Cambridge must be the candidate's own, and submitted work that is not is a malpractice matter with consequences well beyond one grade. Feedback given as instruction is slower for one essay and much faster across a term.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a permit from the authorities?
faqs.answer: Individuals giving private lessons in the UAE need a private tuition work permit, introduced through Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued by MoHRE. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published. The application route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service.

faqs.question: Will the tutor work from my child's school materials or from past papers?
faqs.answer: From the school's materials first. The sequence a tutor follows is the one the class is following, so nothing is taught twice and the student is never carrying two parallel versions of a text. Past questions come in once a component has been covered, and they come from the official Cambridge source rather than from a tutor's photocopies. We do not supply syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads, because those are Cambridge's to publish.

faqs.question: My child reads well but writes short, thin answers. Can that change before the June series?
faqs.answer: Usually, because thin answers are rarely a reading problem. The common cause is a student who does not know what a developed literature paragraph contains, so they state a point, offer a long quotation, and stop. Teaching the shape of a paragraph, then drilling it on four or five essays with marking in between, produces visible change within six to eight weeks. The timing question that matters is how many timed essays can still be written and marked before the window, not how many weeks remain on a calendar.

faqs.question: Do Dubai schools enter candidates for the November series as well as June?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs both a June and a November series for IGCSE, and Dubai schools use November mainly for students who missed a paper or who want one further attempt at a single subject. Pearson Edexcel runs an equivalent November series for its International GCSEs, with its November 2026 timetable running to 19 November 2026 and its November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026. Entry deadlines sit months ahead of the papers, so a November plan is made in the summer, not in October.

faqs.question: Does IGCSE Literature in English count towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: For the British track, the published requirement is five accredited subjects at IGCSE or GCSE with a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level, and Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. Literature in English is an accredited IGCSE subject, so it can form part of that count. Equivalency is assessed by the Ministry, not by any tutoring provider, so verify your child's specific combination through the Ministry's own channel before relying on it.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-english-literature.closingHeading: Start with one marked essay and a free lesson
dubai/cambridge-igcse-english-literature.closingBody: If your child is reading the texts and still writing mid-band answers, the quickest way to find out why is to let a literature specialist read one marked essay and then teach for an hour. Send the school, the year group and the set texts, and we will tell you whether we have a tutor who has taught that combination before. The first lesson is free, no card details are taken, and lessons run one-to-one over live video on a fixed Gulf Standard Time slot. If the plan afterwards does not look worth the money, nothing has been spent and you will at least know which assessment objective is costing the grade.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-english-literature.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach Cambridge Literature in English online to students in Dubai and across the Gulf. Each one works from the school's own text list and marks essays between sessions, which is where most of the measurable change happens.

intro.heading: An hour of live video, spent on one student's writing
paragraphs: The honest case for online literature tuition is not convenience. It is concentration. In a Year 11 class of twenty-four, a student who writes a weak second paragraph gets a margin comment. In sixty minutes of one-to-one video, that paragraph gets rebuilt in front of them, with the tutor asking what the chosen quotation is actually doing and the student having to answer. Nothing else in a school week works that way, and it is why one hour a week moves essay marks when four hours of rereading does not.

The second reason is the artefact. Everything a literature tutor does happens to a document: a poem being annotated, an essay being marked, a plan being built in five minutes against a question's exact wording. On a shared screen those documents are saved and sent after the lesson. By March a student has a folder of annotated texts and marked scripts in their own hands, and revision runs on those rather than on a tutor's notes they never see.

Dubai makes a third argument. Secondary students at schools along the Sheikh Zayed Road corridor are often not home before half past four, and a tutor driving the same roads is caught in the same traffic. A 7:15pm video slot is a 7:15pm slot. When a family travels during Eid or the summer, the lesson follows them. During Ramadan, sessions can move to after Iftar without anyone redrawing their evening around a commute.

What this page is not is a defence of online tuition in general. In-home one-to-one is a real product in this city, widely advertised at published rates between roughly AED 180 and AED 500 an hour, and for younger children it has advantages. IB Gram does not sell it anywhere in the UAE, because sending tutors to family addresses is a service we run only in India. For closed-book literature essay work at 15 and 16, the shared screen is the better tool anyway.

One more thing shapes how these lessons are run. Literature marks move on a writing cycle rather than on contact hours, so the live hour is deliberately not where the essays get written. The student writes to the clock between sessions, the tutor marks the script in the gap, and the next hour starts from a diagnosis instead of a discussion. Families who book two sessions a week and skip the writing spend twice as much for less movement, which is worth knowing before a plan is agreed rather than after a term of it.

The rest of this page is operational detail: how one session is structured, why poetry, prose and drama need three different approaches, how the marking cycle works, what the unseen paper requires, how 0475 interacts with First Language English on the same timetable, what a weekly slot has to survive in a Dubai school week, and what the whole arrangement comes to in a household budget across a term.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-english-literature.programmesIntro: Dubai families reach 0475 from several directions, and leave it for several more. These are the programme routes that matter for a literature student in this emirate, and what each transition actually demands.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Literature in English 0475
programmes.description: Two years of whole-text study assessed by closed-book essays. Poetry and prose are examined together in one paper carrying half the grade; drama is examined either in a single closed-book paper or split between an open-text paper and an unseen paper. The school chooses the route and the texts.
programmes.countryNote: Across Dubai's private sector the British curriculum is the largest single track by enrolment, at 37 per cent of the emirate's private intake in 2024-25, so 0475 cohorts here are large and school text choices vary widely. KHDA inspects these schools annually on a six-band scale. Two students in neighbouring villas can sit entirely different plays, which is why online matching is done on the text list rather than the neighbourhood.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme Language and Literature
programmes.description: The IB alternative to IGCSE in the same age band, assessed against four criteria by the school rather than by external closed-book papers. Students arriving into a British-curriculum school from MYP often write perceptive analysis and have never written to a ninety-minute clock.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai has a substantial IB sector, with International Baccalaureate schools taking 7 per cent of private enrolment in 2024-25 and three new IB schools among the seven opening for 2026-27. Transfers between the two systems mid-secondary are common here because of job moves, and a student switching into Year 10 or 11 of a British school needs the examination discipline taught explicitly rather than assumed.

programmes.name: IB Diploma English A: Literature
programmes.description: One of the post-16 routes out of 0475, assessed through a guided textual analysis, a comparative essay, an individual oral and a written assignment rather than through closed-book papers alone. Wider reading and independent judgement matter considerably more than at IGCSE.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai students choose between A Level and the IB Diploma in the spring of Year 11, before IGCSE results exist. A literature candidate heading for English A should be reading beyond the set list by then; the gap between the last 0475 paper in the summer and September is the natural window, and online sessions through the holidays are how most families use it.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS Level English Literature
programmes.description: The other post-16 route, where unseen criticism carries real weight and model answers stop working. Students who reached high IGCSE bands by memorising a tutor's paragraph structures tend to stall in the first term unless the habit is broken early.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools run AS Level as a standalone year before deciding on the full A Level, which gives a literature student an early external checkpoint. Tutors working with Year 12 students in this emirate spend much of term one on independent reading habits, because the step up from a set-text IGCSE to open critical response is the point where confident students are most often caught out.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-english-literature.subjectsIntro: The subjects below sit next to 0475 on Dubai timetables. Each note names the skill that transfers and the one that does not, because families choosing where to spend tutoring hours need that distinction more than a subject list.

subjects.name: Literature in English (0475)
subjects.description: Closed-book essays on poetry, prose and drama, with all four assessment objectives carrying equal weight. Knowing the text well earns a quarter of what is available, which is why thorough students still land mid-band.

subjects.name: World Literature (0408)
subjects.description: Cambridge's literature-in-translation option, taken at a minority of Dubai schools. The analytical demand overlaps heavily with 0475, though the handling of translated language needs its own treatment and a tutor who has taught it.

subjects.name: First Language English (0500)
subjects.description: Directed writing, composition and reading comprehension. Fluency transfers into literature essays; the habit of writing at length without textual evidence does not, and often actively costs marks in 0475.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: The alternative English entry at many Dubai schools. A student taking ESL alongside 0475 is doing something genuinely demanding, since literature essays assume a first-language range of expression under time pressure.

subjects.name: Drama (0411)
subjects.description: Performance and written work on play texts. The most useful companion subject for the drama component of 0475, because it trains students to read a scene as something staged rather than as dialogue on a page.

subjects.name: History (0470 / 0977)
subjects.description: Source evaluation under time pressure. The transferable habit is treating evidence as something to be interrogated rather than quoted, which is exactly the move that lifts a literature paragraph out of the middle bands.

subjects.name: Geography (0460)
subjects.description: Structured extended answers with specific case-study detail. Students who write in generalities tend to do so across subjects, and fixing it in one often shows up in the other within a term.

subjects.name: Global Perspectives (0457)
subjects.description: Research, argument and reflective writing. Builds the habit of holding a position while acknowledging a counter-view, which strengthens the personal-response objective in literature answers.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Data response and evaluative paragraphs. Included because option blocks collide: a student carrying both 0455 and 0475 has two essay-heavy subjects in the same exam fortnight and needs a revision plan that admits it.

subjects.name: Information and Communication Technology (0417)
subjects.description: Largely practical, which makes it the usual counterweight on a Dubai option block for a student who also takes literature. Different revision rhythm entirely, and the week has to be planned around that difference.

sections.heading: What actually happens in one live sixty-minute lesson
paragraphs: Parents paying for online tuition reasonably want to know what the hour contains. A good 0475 session is not a conversation about a book. It has a fixed shape, most of it spent with the student writing or speaking rather than listening, and it produces two things by the end: an annotated text and a specific instruction for the week.

The opening five minutes are administrative in the useful sense: what came back from school, what the class is on, what the student found hard in the essay they wrote. Then roughly fifteen minutes on the marked script, which is the heart of the lesson. The tutor does not read the comments aloud. They pick the two faults that cost the most marks and make the student fix one paragraph live, out loud, before writing it.

The middle twenty minutes move to new material: a passage from the current text, annotated together on screen. The student is asked what is unusual about the language before any interpretation is offered, because the habit being built is noticing first and concluding second. The last fifteen minutes are planning practice against a real question, timed to five minutes, followed by setting the week's timed essay.

Nothing about that shape is improvised, and nothing in it requires a tutor in the room. The table below sets out the standard structure, which tutors adjust by student but rarely abandon, because the parts that feel least comfortable for the student are usually the parts doing the work.

sections.heading: Poetry, prose and drama need three different approaches
paragraphs: Students and tutors both tend to treat literature as one skill applied to three kinds of book. The marking does not work that way. A strong poetry answer looks different from a strong prose answer, which looks different again from a strong drama answer, and a student who has one gear produces a flat paragraph in the other two.

Poetry rewards attention to shape: where a line breaks, where a stanza pattern is disrupted, where a rhyme that has been steady suddenly disappears. Those observations are visible on the page and do not require a judgement about meaning first. Prose rewards narrative technique: who is telling this, what are they not telling us, how does the writer control what the reader knows and when. Drama rewards stagecraft: entrances, silences, who is on stage listening, what an audience sees that a character does not.

The practical consequence for a weekly plan is that each genre needs its own run of sessions rather than a general rotation. Most students arrive strongest on prose, because that is what they read for pleasure, and weakest on drama, because they have read the play as a book. Diagnosing which gear is missing takes one marked essay per genre, which is roughly three weeks of work, and it is time well spent before any revision plan is drawn.

The table is the version of this we give students to keep. It is deliberately phrased as what the question rewards rather than as advice, because 'analyse more deeply' is the instruction every mid-band candidate has already heard and cannot act on.

sections.heading: The marking cycle is where the grade actually moves
paragraphs: If a family can only afford one structural change, it should be this one: a timed essay written every week or fortnight, marked by the same person, with the feedback keyed to the same four objectives each time. Marks move on that cycle. They do not move on contact hours, which is the mistake families make when they book two sessions a week and skip the writing.

The reason is that a literature essay is a performance under constraints, and performances improve by being repeated and reviewed. A student who writes one essay a month produces a dozen a year and has no basis for noticing a recurring fault. A student writing one a week produces thirty-odd, and by the fourth or fifth the tutor can say with evidence: you lose marks in the second half of every essay because you spend eleven minutes on your first paragraph.

Marking has to be specific to be useful. 'More analysis' and 'develop your points' are accurate and unusable. Useful marking names the mechanism: this quotation is four lines long and you comment on none of its words; this paragraph argues about the character rather than about the writing; this conclusion restates your introduction and earns nothing. A student can act on each of those by Tuesday.

The last part of the cycle is the one most often skipped: redrafting one paragraph, not the whole essay. Rewriting an entire script teaches endurance. Rewriting a single paragraph with a named fault removed teaches the fix, and takes fifteen minutes rather than ninety. Across a term, that single discipline is the most reliable change we see in Dubai students' scripts.

sections.heading: The unseen paper is a method, not a memory test
paragraphs: Where a school has entered the route that includes an unseen component, revision behaves differently. Nothing about rereading set texts prepares a student for a poem they have never met. Students who are excellent on prepared material frequently come out of the unseen paper having written half a page of guesses, because they have never been shown a procedure for the first ten minutes.

The procedure we teach is mechanical on purpose. Read it twice, once for sense and once with a pen. Mark the three or four things that are visibly unusual: a word that does not belong in its sentence, a shift in tense, a line that stops early, a sentence that runs far longer than its neighbours. Decide, from those marks alone, what the writer appears to be doing to the reader. Build the answer on that, with the most concrete observation first.

Students resist this because it feels like it skips interpretation, and good interpretation is exactly what it produces: an argument built from evidence rather than a theme asserted and then illustrated. Once the method is reliable, speed comes with practice. Fifteen or twenty short attempts across a spring term is usually enough to turn the paper from the one a student dreads into the one they prefer, because there is nothing to forget.

Practically, this is weekly work from January, with a full-length marked response every second or third week. It is also the single best use of a holiday block, since the material is endless and none of it depends on where the class has got to.

sections.heading: Literature and First Language English on the same timetable
paragraphs: Nearly every Dubai student sitting 0475 is also sitting an English language qualification, usually First Language English 0500 and sometimes English as a Second Language. The same teacher often takes both. That arrangement is efficient for the school and quietly confusing for the student, because the two subjects reward opposite instincts at the sentence level.

0500 rewards fluency, range and control. A strong composition sustains a voice and moves at pace. 0475 rewards restraint and evidence: a short quotation, a close comment on its words, a link to the question. A student who carries 0500 habits into a literature paper writes confidently and generally, and lands in the middle. A student who carries literature habits into 0500 writes carefully and runs out of time.

The useful thing a tutor can do is name the switch explicitly, so the student knows which mode they are in. We often ask a student to write the same 200 words twice, once as a 0500 descriptive paragraph and once as a 0475 analytical one, which makes the difference obvious in a way no amount of explanation does.

Where tutoring hours are limited, the choice between the two is usually decided by the marks: whichever subject sits further below the student's demonstrated ability is the one to fund first. Occasionally the answer is neither, and the real problem is timed writing speed, which both papers punish heavily and which can be fixed once for both subjects at the same time.

sections.heading: Fitting a weekly slot into a Dubai school week
paragraphs: Scheduling is the part of online tutoring that quietly decides whether it works. A slot that fights the family's week gets cancelled twice in February and never recovers. The practical constraints in Dubai are specific enough to plan around, and worth setting out before a first lesson rather than after three rescheduled ones.

School end times in the emirate cluster between half past two and half past three, but bus runs stretch that considerably for students travelling from communities like Al Furjan, International City or Town Square to schools elsewhere in the city. A student who finishes at 2:45pm may genuinely not be free until 5pm. Co-curricular commitments then occupy four to six most days, which is why 7pm and 7:30pm are the busiest slots we hold.

Two seasonal factors matter. During Ramadan, families frequently want sessions after Iftar, and the slot moves for the month rather than pausing. Over the summer and during Eid, many Dubai families travel; lessons continue across time zones, which is one of the clearer practical advantages over a visiting tutor. Exam fortnights are the other adjustment, when weekly sessions sometimes pause by agreement so the student can sleep.

There is one constraint we state rather than smooth over. Specialists for particular set texts are not infinite, and the best slots in term two go first. If the tutor who has taught your child's exact texts is not free at 7pm on a Tuesday, the honest options are a different time, a different week's start, or a different tutor with the trade-off explained. We say which, rather than filling the slot with whoever is available.

sections.heading: What a term of online 0475 support costs in a Dubai budget
paragraphs: Tutoring is a recurring household cost, so the useful question is not the hourly rate but what a term comes to and what it realistically changes. Published market estimates for Dubai put a weekly one-hour arrangement at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, according to Bestimate's 2026 tutoring cost tables. Monthly packages advertised locally include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Those numbers sit in a market where school fees are the dominant education cost and have been held flat: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. For families budgeting a tutoring year, that stability is the backdrop, and it is why a predictable monthly figure tends to matter more than the headline hourly rate.

What a term of weekly sessions buys, honestly stated, is about twelve marked essays, twelve annotated texts and a student who can plan an answer in five minutes. That is usually enough to move a script out of the middle bands if the writing habit was the problem. It is not enough to compensate for a set text the student has not read, and no amount of money solves that; reading does.

IB Gram's own arrangement is a free first lesson with the matched tutor, no card details taken, then a written plan and a quote in AED. The market figures above are other providers' published rates as of October 2026, included so that our quote lands in context. sections.heading: What an online tutor will not do, and who may legally teach
paragraphs: Two boundaries are worth stating in plain terms, because the English tutoring market in this region contains providers who cross both. The first is authorship. A tutor marks, questions, models on unrelated material and sends a student back to redraft in their own words. A tutor does not produce the paragraph that will be submitted. Work sent to Cambridge must be the candidate's own, and anything else puts the student at risk rather than the provider.

The second is what may be supplied. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade boundary tables belong to Cambridge. A tutor references them and points to the official source; redistributing them as downloads is not something we do. Where a student needs past material, the school and the board's own published resources are the route, and a tutor's job is to teach the student how to use them.

On legality, private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated rather than informal. The private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued by MoHRE free of charge for two years, with eligibility extending to registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted to you.

One further point from Abu Dhabi worth knowing even in Dubai: ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct along the same lines. Any offer of your child's own class teacher, privately, is one to decline. IB Gram holds no accreditation from KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or any school, has no UAE office, and does not claim otherwise.

faqs.question: How does an online Cambridge 0475 lesson actually work?
faqs.answer: It runs over live video, one tutor and one student, usually for sixty minutes on a fixed weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time. The text or essay sits on a shared screen that both can annotate. A typical hour spends five minutes reviewing the school week, fifteen on the last marked essay with one paragraph rebuilt live, twenty annotating new material, and the last stretch on timed planning before the next essay is set. The annotated file and the marked script are saved and sent afterwards, so the student keeps everything.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring effective for a reading subject like literature?
faqs.answer: For closed-book essay work at IGCSE, it suits the subject unusually well, because almost everything a literature tutor does is done to a document. Annotation on a shared screen produces a file the student keeps; the same lesson over a paperback leaves pencil marks and no record. Essay marking is typed, searchable and comparable across a term, so a recurring fault becomes visible rather than anecdotal. The limitation is attention span in younger children, which is why this format fits Year 10 and Year 11 better than primary.

faqs.question: What happens in the first twenty minutes of a trial lesson?
faqs.answer: The tutor works on something real rather than interviewing the student. Usually that means reading a short piece of the student's own writing or a passage from the current text, asking what they notice before offering any interpretation, and then making one concrete change to how a paragraph is built. By the end of twenty minutes a parent listening nearby can usually tell whether the tutor knows the text and whether the student is being asked to think rather than to agree.

faqs.question: How quickly can you match an online literature tutor for a Dubai student?
faqs.answer: Where a specialist has already taught your child's set texts and has a free slot, a trial usually happens within a few days. Where the combination of texts is unusual, or the only times you can use are the busiest evening slots in term two, it can take longer and we say so rather than filling the slot with a generalist. If no suitable specialist is available at all, we tell you that too; it is a better outcome than three paid sessions with the wrong tutor.

faqs.question: Does my child need a printed copy of the set text for online lessons?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they should keep using the school's edition. Page and line references differ between editions, which matters when a tutor says to look at the top of page 94. The student works from their own printed copy while the tutor displays the relevant extract on the shared screen for annotation. We do not supply texts, syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes as downloads, because those belong to their publishers and to Cambridge.

faqs.question: How often should a timed literature essay be written and marked?
faqs.answer: Weekly if the student is in Year 11, fortnightly in Year 10. The cycle matters more than the frequency of lessons: a student who writes one essay a month has no basis for spotting a recurring fault, while one writing weekly accumulates enough evidence for a tutor to name the mechanism precisely. Each essay should be written to the real clock, and only one paragraph should be redrafted afterwards. Rewriting whole scripts teaches endurance rather than the fix.

faqs.question: Does the weekly 0475 slot keep running through Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and a large share of our Dubai families ask for exactly that. The slot shifts for the month and then returns to its usual time, so the weekly rhythm survives rather than pausing for four or five weeks. Some families prefer to reduce to a fortnightly session during Ramadan and add a block in the spring break instead. Either arrangement is workable; what does not work is cancelling week by week, because the marking cycle breaks and the student loses the writing habit.

faqs.question: Can sessions continue over the summer when we travel?
faqs.answer: They can, and the summer is often when the most useful work happens. Lessons run across time zones with the slot adjusted, so a family in Europe or South Asia for six weeks keeps continuity. The natural summer projects are finishing or rereading a set text, starting unseen practice, and for students heading to Year 12, reading beyond the syllabus. None of that work depends on where the class has reached, which is why it fits a holiday better than term-time catch-up does.

faqs.question: What does a month of online literature support cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market estimates for Dubai put a weekly hour at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 for a mid-market qualified tutor, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, per Bestimate's 2026 cost tables. Packaged offers advertised locally include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Those are other providers' published figures as of October 2026. IB Gram gives a free first lesson and then quotes in AED against a written plan.

faqs.question: Is poetry harder than prose for most IGCSE candidates?
faqs.answer: Most students arrive stronger on prose, because prose is what they read for pleasure and narrative feels familiar. Poetry answers tend to be weaker not because poems are harder but because students paraphrase them line by line instead of commenting on shape: line breaks, stanza patterns, a rhyme scheme that falls away. That is a trainable observation habit rather than a matter of taste. Drama is usually the weakest of the three, since most candidates have read the play as a book and never as something staged.

faqs.question: What if no 0475 specialist is free at our preferred time?
faqs.answer: You hear that plainly, with the options. Those are usually a different slot with the specialist who knows your texts, a later start date when their diary frees up, or a different tutor with the trade-off explained in writing. Term two evenings between seven and half past eight are the tightest band in the Dubai calendar, so families booking in January should expect some negotiation. What we do not do is match a student to whoever is available and leave the text gap unmentioned.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both 0475 and First Language English 0500?
faqs.answer: Often, and it can be efficient, because the two subjects sit on the same timetable and share a teacher at school. The thing to watch is that they reward opposite instincts: 0500 rewards fluency and range, 0475 rewards restraint and close evidence. A tutor covering both should name the switch explicitly rather than teaching 'English'. Where hours are limited, fund the subject sitting further below the student's ability, which is frequently not the one the parent expected.

faqs.question: How do you measure progress in a subject marked by bands?
faqs.answer: By comparing marked scripts rather than by asking how the student feels. Three things are tracked: whether the recurring faults named in week one still appear, whether the second essay in a paper is now finished properly, and whether quotations have shortened and comment has lengthened. Those are visible in the writing and shown to parents at the six-week review. Band movement follows them, but no tutor can promise a specific grade, because examiners mark one script written on one morning.

faqs.question: Do you also teach Pearson Edexcel International GCSE English Literature?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the first question is always which board and which specification the school has entered, because the component structure and the set text lists differ. Pearson runs its International GCSE exams in May or June and in November, with its November 2026 timetable running to 19 November 2026 and November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026. Confirm your child's series and specification with the school, then the tutor match is made against that specification rather than against a generic literature brief.

faqs.question: What does my child need technically for an online lesson in Dubai?
faqs.answer: A laptop or tablet with a working camera and microphone, a stable home connection, headphones, and the school's own printed copy of the text. A phone is workable in an emergency but poor for annotation. A quiet corner matters more than a desk; in apartment communities like Jumeirah Lake Towers most students take lessons in a bedroom with headphones, which is entirely fine. No software purchase is required, and nothing needs installing beyond the video application we send a link for.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-english-literature.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach Cambridge IGCSE Literature in English to Dubai students and mark essays rather than discuss them. Each can show you the step most candidates miss: the sentence where a named device turns into an explained effect on a reader.

intro.heading: Literature marks move when essays get marked, not when texts get discussed
paragraphs: Literature is the subject where tutoring most easily becomes a book club. An hour spent talking about a play is enjoyable, defensible and almost impossible to audit, and a student can finish six of those hours writing exactly the same essay they wrote in September. The repair is unglamorous: plan, essay, marking, redraft, second essay on the same text to check the gain transferred. Everything on this page is built around that loop.

The reason it has to be essays is that 0475 marks depend on a single move that discussion rarely teaches. A candidate has to go from naming what a writer does to explaining what it does to a reader, inside a paragraph, supported by a short quotation they can use precisely. Students who can talk about a text intelligently very often cannot do that in writing under time, and the gap is invisible until somebody marks a whole script.

Dubai adds its own wrinkle: set texts differ between campuses, and sometimes between teaching groups in the same school. The Cambridge set-text list changes by exam year, so no tutoring page should tell you what your child is studying. Confirm the texts and the component route from the school, in writing, before any tutor sets a single essay. A session spent on a text the student is not sitting is the most complete waste of money available in this subject.

Delivery is one-to-one on live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home visits are a service we run only in India. For literature the online format carries a specific advantage beyond the choice of specialist: annotation happens on a shared screen, so a student watches their own paragraph being marked and the file is still there when the redraft happens on Saturday.

What follows is the working method. There is a table of the essay trail and what each stage shows, a table of the component routes a Dubai school may have chosen and what each rewards, a frank section on where literature marks are lost, the quotation drill that works for closed-text papers, and a calendar counted back from the series with text coverage treated as the first checkpoint rather than the last. The boundary on academic honesty is stated at the end, in full, because literature is the subject where that line gets crossed most casually and a parent is entitled to know where a tutor stops. Every date on this page is attributed to Cambridge's own published material, and no IB date appears anywhere, because the IB's site cannot be checked automatically and a tutoring page is the wrong source for a date your school holds.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-english-literature.programmesIntro: Literature in English runs from mid-secondary into sixth form, and the demand changes sharply at each step. These are the stages Dubai students most often pass through, and what the evidence looks like at each.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Literature in English (0475)
programmes.description: Study of poetry, prose and drama assessed through essay and passage-based questions, with schools choosing between component routes that may include a closed-text paper, an unseen option and a coursework option. Routes, weightings and durations differ by exam year, so confirm the exact components for your child's series on cambridgeinternational.org and against the entry sheet.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools choose their own texts within the syllabus, and two campuses of the same group often teach different ones. That makes group tuition in this subject unusually inefficient, and it makes confirming the text list the first job of any one-to-one plan.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE World Literature (0408)
programmes.description: A smaller, differently shaped literature qualification that some schools enter alongside or instead of 0475. It rewards comparison across texts from different cultures, which suits a multilingual cohort, and the essay discipline overlaps enough that a 0475 specialist can teach both once the text list is known.
programmes.countryNote: Where a Dubai school enters students for both, the risk is a student preparing one set of texts and sitting questions on another. Ask the department to write down which code goes with which texts and keep that note somewhere a tutor can see it.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS & A Level Literature in English
programmes.description: The progression route, and the reason 0475 technique is worth building properly. The analytical move from method to effect stays the same; the expectation of sustained argument and of independent critical reading rises steeply. Students who left IGCSE narrating plot usually spend their first AS term learning what they could have learned at sixteen.
programmes.countryNote: For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, students must show five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five.

programmes.name: IB Diploma English A: Literature
programmes.description: The alternative sixth-form route, taken by a sizeable share of Dubai students given the emirate's IB provision. Different assessment architecture, same underlying skill: close reading expressed as argument. A strong 0475 essay habit transfers directly, which is worth knowing when choosing between A Level and the Diploma.
programmes.countryNote: No IB exam or results dates appear on this page. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so every Diploma date in this project is unverified; confirm any session timing with your school's IB coordinator and cite that source rather than a tutoring page.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-english-literature.subjectsIntro: Literature sits in a cluster of subjects that all reward the same written discipline. The notes below say what a marked 0475 essay predicts about each.

subjects.name: Literature in English (0475)
subjects.description: The page's subject. Marked essays almost always show the same two failures first: a plan that retells the text instead of answering the question, and paragraphs that name a device without explaining its effect on a reader.

subjects.name: World Literature (0408)
subjects.description: Comparison across texts from different cultures. Students who write comparatively here often transfer the skill into 0475 drama answers, where comparing two moments in a play earns more than summarising either.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (0500)
subjects.description: Commonly sat alongside 0475 in Dubai. The overlap is close reading; the divergence is that 0500 asks a candidate to write in role from a text while literature asks for sustained argument about a writer's method.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510)
subjects.description: Where a student sits 0510 and 0475 together, literature is the harder purchase, because essay writing about method sits above the language level 0510 requires. Worth budgeting as a separate subject rather than as more English.

subjects.name: Drama (0411)
subjects.description: Reading a scene as performance is the shared skill. Students who take both tend to write the strongest drama answers in literature, because they instinctively ask what an audience sees rather than what a character says.

subjects.name: History (0470)
subjects.description: Source analysis and extended argument reward the same structure as a literature paragraph: claim, evidence, explanation of effect. A target that transfers from one marked essay to the other is the cheapest gain on a Dubai timetable.

subjects.name: Global Perspectives (0457)
subjects.description: School-supervised research and written argument. Evidence of the student's own drafting matters more here than almost anywhere, and a tutor's role stays entirely on the questioning side of the line.

subjects.name: Art and Design (0400)
subjects.description: Written annotation of intention and effect is assessed alongside the practical work. Students who learn to explain effect in literature usually stop describing their own pieces and start justifying them.

subjects.name: French (0520)
subjects.description: Listed for the workload rather than the overlap. A student carrying 0475, 0500 and a modern foreign language has three reading loads in three languages, and a literature plan that ignores that will not survive a term.

regions.name: The Springs

sections.heading: What a 0475 tutor in Dubai does in the first three sessions
paragraphs: A Cambridge IGCSE English Literature 0475 tutor in Dubai should spend the first session on evidence rather than teaching. That means reading a marked essay if one exists, confirming the set texts and component route from the school in writing, and auditing which texts the student has actually read and annotated as opposed to attended lessons about. Those three facts determine everything afterwards, and getting them wrong wastes a term. A tutor who opens a textbook in the first session has skipped all three and is guessing.

The second session sets a plan and one analytical paragraph, both timed. Eight minutes for the plan, then a single paragraph on a question the student has not seen. Those two artefacts expose nearly every common weakness: a plan that retells the story, an argument that names a theme rather than a method, a quotation long enough to fill a line and too long to analyse, and a paragraph that stops at the device without saying what a reader experiences.

The third session is a whole essay to time, marked in full. Only at that point is a target worth setting, because only then is it clear whether the problem is coverage, argument, quotation precision or pace. Lessons run one-to-one on live video to Dubai households; IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Annotation happens on a shared screen so the student watches their own essay being marked, and the file stays available for the redraft rather than going into a school bag.

sections.heading: The essay trail: what each stage shows
paragraphs: Literature progress is best read as a sequence of stages rather than as a series of grades. The table below is the sequence we run, and each row produces an artefact a parent can look at without a teaching background. Nothing in it involves a predicted grade or a percentage, both of which would be invented numbers attached to a subject where examiners mark against criteria rather than counting correct answers.

The first two rows carry most of the gain. A plan judged for argument rather than coverage is where a narrating student becomes an arguing one, and it takes eight minutes rather than an hour. Two openings on the same question, written a fortnight apart and kept side by side, show whether the student can now name a writer's method in the first two sentences. That single habit lifts more essays than any amount of additional reading.

The last row is the honest test. A second essay on the same text, set without reminders about the previous target, shows whether the teaching transferred or whether the tutor was carrying the student through each piece. Providers rarely run that check because it can reveal that four sessions produced nothing durable. It is exactly why it belongs in the record, and why the review at four sessions is allowed to recommend stopping. A parent reading both essays side by side can judge that for themselves, which is the point of keeping them in one place.

sections.heading: Set texts in Dubai schools, and why nobody should guess them
paragraphs: The Cambridge set-text list changes by exam year, and schools choose within it. Two campuses of the same group in Dubai routinely teach different poems and a different play, and in larger schools two teaching groups can diverge. This is the single most common source of wasted tuition in the subject: a tutor sets an essay on a text the student is not sitting, the hour feels productive, and nothing of it counts.

The fix costs one email. Ask the head of English to confirm, in writing, the syllabus code, the component route and the exact texts for your child's exam year, and keep that note where a tutor can see it. If the school is entering 0408 World Literature alongside or instead of 0475, ask which texts belong to which code, because candidates preparing one list and sitting questions on another is a real failure mode rather than a theoretical one.

Text choice also shapes what revision should look like. A route built on a closed-text paper demands memorised quotation, so the work is thematic recall and precision. A route with an unseen component demands transferable method, so the work is one timed unseen a fortnight. A drama text wants a student who can read a scene as performance. These are different programmes of work, and choosing between them from guesswork is how a term gets spent on the wrong drill. The email to the department is therefore the cheapest piece of preparation available to any family in this subject.

sections.heading: The component routes a Dubai school may have chosen
paragraphs: Cambridge allows schools to build their literature entry from different components, and the choice changes what a candidate should practise more than any teaching style does. The table sets out the routes we see in this market, what each involves, what it rewards and what the student should be doing weekly as a result. Treat it as a map for the conversation with the school rather than as a statement of what your child is sitting.

Two warnings belong beside it. First, weightings and durations differ by exam year and by route, so this page deliberately describes what is rewarded instead of quoting mark totals that may have changed; read the syllabus for your child's series. Second, where a coursework route is in use, the folder is school-supervised and school-authenticated, which places a hard limit on what any tutor may touch. That limit is set out in full in the last section.

A practical note on the unseen option, which Dubai students often fear most. It is the component that rewards method over memory, so it is also the one where a student with a reliable analytical paragraph structure gains quickest. One timed unseen a fortnight, marked for method rather than for insight, usually moves an unseen response further in six weeks than a term of discussion about studied texts. The same paragraph structure then improves the studied-text answers, so the practice pays twice and competes with nothing else in the revision week.

sections.heading: Where 0475 marks are lost: narration instead of analysis
paragraphs: The dominant failure in literature essays is retelling. A candidate writes what happens, in the order it happens, with the occasional judgement attached, and the examiner credits the paragraphs that explain how a writer creates an effect. The frustrating part for parents is that these essays often read well. Fluency is not the problem; the problem is that the essay describes the world of the text rather than the choices of the author.

The second failure is quotation. Long quotations feel impressive and cost marks, because a four-line extract leaves nothing to analyse and eats the clock. The repair is mechanical: three to five words, embedded in a sentence, followed by what the reader experiences and why that word rather than a synonym produces it. Students resist this for about two sessions and then find their paragraphs getting shorter and their marks getting better.

The third is the ending. Most candidates have a rehearsed opening and no planned conclusion, so the final paragraph is either a summary or an abandoned sentence. Because the plan is timed at eight minutes in our sessions, the ending gets decided before the prose starts. That one change removes the most common structural loss in the subject, and it is visible in the record: the first and fourth essay sit in the same document, with the last paragraph of each easy to compare. Parents who want one thing to look for in a marked essay should read the final paragraph first.

sections.heading: Quotation memory: the drill that actually works
paragraphs: For a closed-text route the student needs quotations they can produce under pressure, and the usual approach of rereading the text with a highlighter does not deliver that. What works is a thematic bank: ten to fifteen short quotations per text, grouped by the ideas the questions ask about rather than by where they appear in the book, each short enough to write in four seconds and rich enough to analyse for two sentences.

The drill itself takes five minutes of a session and is deliberately dull. The tutor names a theme, the student produces two quotations from memory aloud, and then writes one analytical sentence on the stronger of them. Doing this weekly for eight weeks produces a candidate who can enter a closed-text paper without the quiet panic that costs the first ten minutes of the exam. Recitation aloud matters: a quotation recognised on a page is not a quotation available in an exam hall.

Two Dubai-specific notes. Students carrying 0475 alongside 0500 and a modern foreign language have three memorisation loads at once, so the bank has to be small enough to maintain rather than comprehensive. And during Ramadan, when school days shorten and attention moves later, the five-minute drill survives far better than a ninety-minute essay, so the drill carries the month and the timed essays resume afterwards. Keeping one small habit alive through a disrupted month is worth more than attempting a full programme and abandoning it in week two.

sections.heading: The series clock for a literature candidate
paragraphs: Literature has one checkpoint that no other subject shares: every set text has to be read before revision can begin. A student who reaches February with a text unread cannot be rescued by analysis coaching, because there is nothing to analyse. That is why text coverage sits at the top of the table rather than at the bottom, and why the text-coverage audit exists as a two-session product in its own right.

The administrative dates are Cambridge's and the centre's, and they sit further ahead than families expect. Cambridge runs IGCSE exams in a June series and a November series. For the March 2027 series the exam period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries were due on 27 November 2026, forecast grades on 27 February 2027, with results on Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable.

The last row matters more in literature than elsewhere. In the final fortnight the temptation is to introduce criticism, a new secondary text or a fresh interpretation, and it almost always lowers the mark. What raises it is timed essays on texts already known, with the plan still timed at eight minutes. Nothing new goes in during the last two weeks; the work is converting what the student knows into paragraphs that explain effect.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, AI essays, and what a tutor may review
paragraphs: Literature is the subject where the line between help and malpractice is crossed most casually, because an essay is easy to improve by typing into it. Our position is fixed: a tutor reviews, questions and marks the student's own writing, and supplies none of it. Where a Dubai school uses a school-supervised route, the work must be the candidate's own, produced under the school's conditions and authenticated by the school, and a tutor adding sentences leaves that authentication unsupportable.

The legitimate space is large. A tutor may teach how an argument is built, write a model paragraph on a text the student is not studying, explain what examiners credit, question a draft until the student finds the weak claim themselves, mark practice essays that will never be submitted, and show why a long quotation is costing marks. All of that teaches. None of it puts the tutor's prose inside the student's work.

Artificial intelligence changes the route rather than the rule. Critiquing a generated paragraph is useful teaching: it shows why generic praise of a writer's technique scores nothing and where the register slips into something no sixteen-year-old would write. Handing that text over as the student's essay is the same breach as writing it yourself. One provider visible in this market sells completed assessed work at a published price; if that is offered for your child, decline it and tell the school, because the consequence falls on the candidate alone.

process.title: Get the texts and the route in writing
process.description: Ask the head of English to confirm the syllabus code, the component route and the exact set texts for your child's exam year. Keep the reply. Every hour spent on a text your child is not sitting is an hour wasted, and in this subject that is the most common way money disappears.

process.title: Audit coverage before teaching anything
process.description: Text by text, has it been read and annotated, or only taught? For transferring students and for anyone who changed groups mid-course this is the first and sometimes the only thing worth paying for. Gaps become a reading schedule with dates rather than a vague instruction to catch up.
