process.description: Sixty minutes at no cost, no card details, built around a timed plan and one analytical paragraph. By the end you should know whether the problem is coverage, argument, quotation or pace. If the match is wrong, we propose another tutor rather than defending the first.

process.title: Run the essay cycle
process.description: One essay between sessions, written to the paper's time, marked whole with the plan marked separately, rebuilt live on a shared screen, then a second essay on the same text with no reminders. Both essays stay in one document so transfer is visible rather than asserted.

process.title: Drill, then stop adding
process.description: In the final eight weeks the work narrows to thematic quotation drills and timed essays, as a package with an end date. Nothing new is introduced in the last fortnight. A written review before any extension says what has moved and whether more sessions are warranted.

whyPoints.title: Essays marked whole, plans marked separately
whyPoints.description: The plan is where a narrating essay becomes an arguing one, and it takes eight timed minutes to diagnose. Marking the plan separately from the prose is unusual in this market and it is the fastest route to a structural fix.

whyPoints.title: Transfer is tested, not assumed
whyPoints.description: A second essay on the same text, set without reminders, shows whether a target stuck or whether the tutor was carrying the student through each piece. That check can reveal that sessions produced nothing durable, which is precisely why it belongs in the record.

whyPoints.title: Texts confirmed, never guessed
whyPoints.description: Cambridge set texts change by exam year and Dubai campuses choose differently, sometimes within one school. We ask for the school's written confirmation before setting an essay, because a brilliant session on the wrong poem is worth nothing.

whyPoints.title: A hard line on whose writing it is
whyPoints.description: Tutors review, question and mark the student's own essays and supply none of the text, including anything machine-generated. The line is stated here because at least one provider in this market sells the opposite, and because the consequences land on the candidate.

whyPoints.title: Online, with the annotation kept
whyPoints.description: All UAE sessions run one-to-one on live video in Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE. Marking happens on a shared screen and the annotated file stays available for the weekend redraft, which a paper essay in a school bag does not.

faqs.question: How do I find out which 0475 set texts my child is actually studying?
faqs.answer: Ask the head of English to confirm it in writing, including the syllabus code, the component route and the exact texts for your child's exam year. Cambridge's set-text list changes by year and Dubai schools choose within it, with two campuses of the same group often teaching different poems and a different play. No tutoring page can tell you this, and a tutor who sets essays without that confirmation may be teaching a text your child will never be asked about.

faqs.question: Why does my child write fluently and still lose literature marks?
faqs.answer: Because fluency and analysis are different things. The dominant failure in 0475 essays is retelling: the candidate writes what happens, in order, with occasional judgements, while the examiner credits paragraphs explaining how a writer creates an effect. These essays often read pleasantly, which is why the problem survives for terms. The repair is visible in a marked script within one session: name the writer's method in the opening two sentences, then explain effect rather than describing event.

faqs.question: What does marking a plan separately from the essay achieve?
faqs.answer: It isolates the thing most essays get wrong before a word of prose is written. Eight timed minutes produce a plan that either answers the question or retells the text, and that is visible instantly. Fixing a plan takes minutes; fixing a finished essay takes an hour and teaches less. The plan also forces a decision about the conclusion, which removes the most common structural loss in the subject, where a candidate runs out of time and abandons the final paragraph.

faqs.question: How long should quotations be in a 0475 essay?
faqs.answer: Three to five words, embedded in the student's own sentence. Long quotations feel impressive, leave nothing to analyse and consume the clock: a four-line extract can swallow a minute of writing time and earn nothing. The drill is to follow each short quotation with what the reader experiences and why that particular word rather than a synonym produces it. Students resist for about two sessions, then notice their paragraphs getting shorter and their marks improving.

faqs.question: How many quotations per text does a closed-text paper need?
faqs.answer: Ten to fifteen short ones per text, grouped by theme rather than by where they appear in the book. Each should be writable in about four seconds and rich enough to support two sentences of analysis. Smaller banks are easier to maintain, which matters for Dubai students carrying literature alongside English Language and a modern foreign language. Recitation aloud is the test that counts; a quotation recognised on the page is not a quotation available in an exam hall.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the unseen component?
faqs.answer: It is the component that responds fastest to teaching, because it rewards method rather than memory. One timed unseen a fortnight, marked for method rather than for insight, usually moves a candidate further in six weeks than a term of discussion about studied texts. The structure being taught is the same analytical paragraph the rest of the paper needs, which is why unseen practice tends to lift the studied-text answers too rather than competing with them for revision time.

faqs.question: My child has not finished reading one of the set texts. What now?
faqs.answer: Deal with that before buying any analysis coaching. An unread text costs more marks than weak analysis on a read one, and no amount of essay technique rescues a question on a book nobody opened. The text-coverage audit exists for this: two sessions to confirm coverage text by text against the school's list, then a reading schedule with dates rather than an instruction to catch up. Families sometimes stop after those two sessions, which is a legitimate outcome.

faqs.question: Is group tuition sensible for 0475 in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Rarely, for a structural reason rather than a commercial one. Schools and campuses choose different texts, so two students in the same community are often sitting different poems and a different play, and a group session then teaches the wrong material to somebody. Group work can suit unseen practice, where the method is shared. For studied texts the efficient unit is one-to-one, and that is a fact about the syllabus rather than an argument for a higher rate.

faqs.question: How do drama answers differ from prose answers in 0475?
faqs.answer: A drama answer has to read a scene as performance. The strongest candidates ask what an audience sees and hears, how an entrance or a silence lands, what the staging does to the meaning of a line. Weaker answers treat the play as a story told in dialogue and describe what characters say to one another. Students who also take Drama usually write the best literature drama answers for this reason, and the habit can be taught to those who do not.

faqs.question: What does the review after four sessions tell us?
faqs.answer: Whether the target transferred. It compares the first and latest essays on the same text, shows both plans, names what has stopped going wrong, and recommends continuing, narrowing to drills, or stopping. It contains no predicted grade, because a prediction from four essays would be a guess with a decimal point on it, and your child's school already issues the predicted and forecast grades that carry weight with Cambridge.

faqs.question: Should we add literary criticism in the last few weeks?
faqs.answer: No. Introducing criticism, a new secondary text or a fresh interpretation in the final fortnight almost always lowers the mark, because the candidate tries to fit new material into an argument they have not practised. What raises marks in the last two weeks is timed essays on texts already known, with the plan still limited to eight minutes. Nothing new goes in; the work is converting what the student knows into paragraphs that explain effect under time pressure.

faqs.question: Can the tutor read my child's coursework draft?
faqs.answer: A tutor can question it and can teach from it, but supplies none of its text. Where a school uses a supervised route, the work must be the candidate's own, produced under the school's conditions and authenticated by the school. A tutor may explain what examiners credit, model a paragraph on a text the student is not studying, mark practice essays that will never be submitted, and keep asking why a claim is weak until the student rewrites it. Adding sentences to the submitted piece is not available at any price.

faqs.question: What if my child used an AI tool to produce an essay?
faqs.answer: Treat it as teaching material rather than a scandal. A generated paragraph is a good object lesson: it praises technique in general terms, scores nothing for effect on a reader, and slips into a register no sixteen-year-old uses. Working through why it would fail is useful. What a tutor must never do is hand such text over as the student's work, which is the same breach as writing it. Schools authenticate submitted work, and the consequence of a malpractice finding falls on the candidate.

faqs.question: Do literature sessions still work during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the shape changed. School days shorten and attention moves later, so a ninety-minute timed essay is the wrong thing to attempt, while the five-minute quotation drill survives easily. Many Dubai families move sessions to after Iftar for the month, which costs nobody a journey because lessons run on live video. Timed essays resume afterwards. Families who prefer to pause keep their slot, and nothing is charged for sessions that do not take place.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-english-literature.closingHeading: Confirm the texts, then send one marked essay
dubai/cambridge-igcse-english-literature.closingBody: Get the syllabus code, the component route and the set texts in writing from your child's school, and send them with the most recent marked essay. We will read the essay, time a plan and one paragraph in the trial lesson, and tell you whether the issue is coverage, argument, quotation or pace. The trial is free, lasts sixty minutes and needs no card details. Sessions run one-to-one on live video in Gulf Standard Time, with essays marked whole and the annotated file kept for the redraft.

intro.heading: In a four-skill subject, the only honest progress report is the work itself
paragraphs: Parents searching for a 0510 home tutor in Dubai are usually trying to solve a trust problem as much as an academic one. The school says the English grade is a 5 and could be a 6. A tutor says they can help. Nothing in between is checkable, and English is the subject where that gap is widest, because an hour of pleasant conversation about a reading passage looks identical, from the kitchen, to an hour of properly diagnostic teaching.

The answer this page proposes is artefacts. Every 0510 session should leave behind something a parent can open: a written task marked against what the task actually demanded, with task fulfilment, register and accuracy judged separately. The same listening recording attempted twice, a fortnight apart, so that the traps still catching the student are named rather than described. Two short recordings of speaking practice on unseen topics. A marked reading answer sheet where each loss has its question type written beside it.

That structure comes from the shape of the syllabus. 0510 assesses reading, writing, listening and speaking, and under that code the speaking test is reported separately from the overall grade. Four skills means four error patterns, and a single weak one can hold the whole grade down while the other three look healthy. A general impression of how English is going cannot locate the problem. Four separate records can, which is the entire argument for keeping them.

IB Gram delivers this as one-to-one lessons on live video to households across Dubai. We do not send tutors to UAE addresses, and in-home visits are a service we offer only in India. The honest trade is this: you give up somebody physically present, and you gain both a specialist chosen for the paper rather than for the postcode and a complete file of the work. For families in Town Square, Mudon or Damac Hills the second half of that trade is worth more than the first, because the specialist pool within driving distance of those communities is small.

The sections below set out the record skill by skill, then put the travel arithmetic in a table so the in-home comparison is explicit rather than implied. There is also a table of the mandatory UAE subjects every Dubai private school teaches alongside the licensed curriculum, because those lessons compete for the same evenings as 0510 practice and almost nobody writing about tutoring in this emirate mentions them. Read the tables first if you are short of time, then the section on what a tutor must never produce, because that is the boundary a parent is entitled to have in writing before any money moves. Everything factual here names its source, and anything we could not verify is left out rather than smoothed over.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-english-second-lan.programmesIntro: Language assessment changes shape between programmes, and so does the evidence a tutor can collect. These are the stages a Dubai 0510 candidate most often passes through.

programmes.name: IB MYP Language Acquisition
programmes.description: Assessed against criteria for comprehending spoken and written text and for communicating in response. Students arriving into a Cambridge entry from MYP language acquisition are usually confident speakers with loose written control, because criterion feedback rewards communication more than it rewards precision of form.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai has a substantial IB cohort within its private sector, so mid-secondary moves between an IB school and a British-curriculum school happen often. The most useful document after such a move is a piece of writing marked under the new school's expectations, not the last report from the old one.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE English as a Second Language (0510)
programmes.description: Reading, writing, listening and speaking are each assessed, with the speaking test reported separately from the overall grade under this code. Written tasks are set in defined forms for stated audiences, which is why task fulfilment has to be marked apart from accuracy. Component structures and timings have been revised in recent exam years, so confirm the current list for your child's exam year on cambridgeinternational.org.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the 0510 cohort includes many students taught in English since primary who speak another language at home. That profile produces strong listening and reading with weaker written register, and the evidence trail tends to show it within the first two marked tasks.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE English as a First Language (0500)
programmes.description: The entry a strong 0510 candidate sometimes moves to. Two written papers, no listening or speaking inside the grade, and a far heavier analytical demand: summary point selection and explanation of a writer's language choices. The evidence from a 0510 writing folder is the fairest basis for deciding whether that move is realistic.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai departments decide entry at subject level, often in Year 9. If a change is worth raising, raise it early: Cambridge final entry deadlines sit months ahead of the papers, with 27 November 2026 the deadline for a March 2027 exam period running 3 February to 4 March 2027.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS Level English General Paper
programmes.description: A progression option for students who want to keep writing as an academic skill without taking literature. Essays are judged on argument and control of written English, so the habits built during a 0510 writing block transfer directly. Students who leave 0510 without those habits usually have to buy them back at a higher rate later.
programmes.countryNote: For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, students must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among those five.

sections.heading: What a 0510 home tutor in Dubai means here, and how it is delivered
paragraphs: A Cambridge IGCSE English Second Language 0510 home tutor in Dubai, as families use the phrase, means private one-to-one English support arranged outside school for a Year 10 or Year 11 candidate. The word home describes where parents picture the lesson, not a feature of the teaching. What they are actually buying is undivided attention on four separately assessed skills, and a way of knowing whether that attention is working.

Our answer is lessons delivered one-to-one on live video to Dubai households, with a record kept of everything marked. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India, and no sentence on this site should imply otherwise. What a Dubai family gains in exchange is twofold: the tutor is chosen for familiarity with the 0510 components rather than for living nearby, and every marked task, recording and review stays in one place you can open.

The difference shows in the first fortnight. A visiting tutor with general English experience typically starts with a textbook unit and a conversation. A 0510 specialist starts with the school's marked work, identifies which of reading, writing, listening or speaking is costing the grade, and sets one task under controlled conditions to confirm it. Both approaches fill an hour. Only the second produces a finding, and a finding is the thing you can act on when deciding how many sessions to buy.
Ask any tutor you are considering what will exist on paper after two weeks. If the answer is a feeling about how the lessons are going, the price is irrelevant.

sections.heading: The evidence each 0510 skill produces
paragraphs: Because the four skills fail independently, the record has to be kept separately for each. The table below shows what a session produces, how movement is measured and when each strand is reviewed. None of it involves percentages, predicted grades or any figure we would have to invent. All of it is either the student's own work or a count of something observable, such as how many prompts a spoken answer needed before it developed.

The listening row is the one parents find most surprising. Attempting the same recording twice, a fortnight apart, is not a memory test; the questions are re-answered after the trap types have been taught, and the comparison shows whether the student now hears the self-correction or still takes the first number offered. It is the cheapest diagnostic in the subject and almost nobody runs it, because it requires keeping the first attempt rather than marking and discarding it.

The writing row carries the most weight. A 0510 written task is marked on what the task demanded as well as on accuracy, so a student can produce grammatically clean prose that answers a slightly different brief and lose marks they never knew existed. Keeping both versions of the same task in one document makes that visible to a parent in about thirty seconds, which is faster than any report could explain it. The reading row works the same way: a loss recorded with its question type beside it turns a disappointing score into a short list of habits to break.

sections.heading: The writing folder: email, report and article tasks in versions
paragraphs: 0510 written tasks come in defined forms for defined readers, which is what makes them teachable and what makes them easy to fail quietly. An article for a school magazine, an email to a head teacher and a report for a youth group want different registers, and a candidate who writes all three in the same comfortable voice will lose task marks while their sentences stay correct. Marking has to separate those judgements or it teaches the wrong lesson.

The folder we keep for a Dubai student therefore holds each task twice, with three notes attached: whether the brief was fulfilled, whether the register matched the reader, and what the accuracy pattern was. After four tasks the pattern is usually unmistakable. A student might consistently fulfil the brief and consistently drift in register, which is a thirty-minute fix repeated three times rather than a term of general English.

Modelling is handled carefully, and the rule is written down because it matters. A tutor may write a model answer on a different topic to show the form. A tutor may not write sentences for the task the student is submitting, and may not improve the student's own text by adding their own writing to it. Families sometimes expect the second thing and are surprised to be refused. The refusal is the point: a folder improved by somebody else is evidence of nothing and risk for the candidate. A model on an unrelated topic teaches the form just as well and leaves the student's own text untouched.

sections.heading: Speaking: recorded practice, and what development sounds like
paragraphs: Under 0510 the speaking test is reported separately from the overall grade, which leads some Dubai families to ignore it and some schools to treat it lightly. The skill being assessed is development: taking an unfamiliar prompt and building a real answer without rehearsed phrases. That is trainable, and it is the strand where recorded evidence persuades a student fastest, because hearing yourself stop after one sentence is more convincing than being told you do.

A speaking block runs as short sessions twice a week rather than a weekly hour. Each starts with an unseen topic, pushes the student past their first full stop, and ends with a note on how many prompts were needed. Two brief recordings are kept across the block, with consent asked for first, the purpose stated, and deletion available on request. Nothing is recorded for a student who would rather not be, and the block works without it.

Progress here sounds specific rather than general. In week one a student answers in a sentence and waits. By week three the same student offers a reason, an example and an opinion without being asked for them. That is the change the component rewards, and it is also what transfers into every other subject's oral work. Where a school has entered 0511, the count-in speaking code, this strand stops being optional and the recorded evidence becomes considerably more valuable, because the component is then carrying marks rather than sitting beside them.

sections.heading: Travel minutes against lesson minutes in Dubai
paragraphs: The in-home question deserves a straight answer rather than a dismissal. A visiting tutor in Dubai is selling an hour of teaching plus a journey that nobody enjoys and somebody pays for. Bestimate's 2026 survey puts in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180-350 an hour, with independent home tutors reaching AED 500, against AED 150-300 for a qualified online subject tutor, where Unitors publishes a floor of AED 150. The gap is mostly road.

The table below is the version of that argument a parent can test against their own week. The journeys are real pairings we are asked about, the drive times are ordinary term-time afternoons rather than worst cases, and the third column is the part that never appears in a quote: the paid minutes that disappear when a tutor arrives late, leaves early for the next booking, or cancels because of weather or a school event.

The last row is the honest counterpoint. Inside a single community such as Jumeirah Village Circle, travel is barely a factor, and an in-home arrangement is perfectly sensible on logistics. What you are choosing then is the tutor pool: whoever lives in JVC and is free at that hour, rather than whoever knows the 0510 components best. For a four-skill language paper that is a meaningful narrowing, and it is the reason we do not sell home visits in the UAE even where the drive would be short. Judge the choice on who marks the work, not on how far they live from your gate.

sections.heading: The four-session review a parent can audit
paragraphs: At four sessions a written review goes to the parent. It names the skill that was weakest at the start, shows the first and latest version of one written task, states which listening trap types have stopped catching the student, records how many prompts a spoken answer now needs, and makes a recommendation. The recommendation has three honest options: continue as planned, reduce to a narrower cycle, or stop because the specific failure has been repaired.

What the review deliberately does not contain is a predicted grade. A prediction built from four sessions would be a guess with a decimal point attached, and your child's school already issues predicted and forecast grades, which are the figures that carry weight with Cambridge. Nor does it contain satisfaction scores, star ratings or percentage improvements. Every number in it is either a count of something observable or a mark from a task you can read yourself.

Reviews that recommend stopping are a normal outcome, not a rare one. A 0510 candidate whose written register has been corrected and whose listening traps have gone may need nothing more this academic year, and saying so costs us a booking. It is also the only position consistent with a page built on auditable evidence: a record that can only ever justify more sessions is marketing with a spreadsheet attached. Parents who want the review earlier can ask for it at two sessions, and some do, usually the ones paying for two children at once.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside 0510
paragraphs: No tutoring plan for a Dubai student survives contact with the timetable unless it accounts for the mandatory UAE subjects. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. These are not optional enrichment lessons; they carry timetable allocation and homework.

The organisational rules are specific enough to matter to a parent. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided weekly totals are met, and it is advised that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes.

Two further points shape how this content may be taught. Schools are required to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate approval KHDA requires to teach those subjects. And for the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, which is why a tutoring plan should work around these lessons rather than attempt to supplement their material. The federal position behind all of this is that private schools must follow Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies requirements whatever curriculum they licence.

sections.heading: The evidence a language tutor must never create
paragraphs: Everything described on this page is evidence of a student's own work. There is one category we will not generate: any part of a text that gets submitted. Where a Dubai school uses a supervised component, the work must be the candidate's own, produced under the school's conditions, and authenticated by the school. A tutor who adds sentences has not raised the mark; they have put the entry at risk and handed the school an authentication it cannot stand behind.

The legitimate space is wide and worth stating positively. A tutor may teach the form, write a model on an unrelated topic, explain what the task demands in plain language, question a draft until the student finds the weakness themselves, and mark practice work that will never be handed in. All of that leaves a record. None of it touches the submitted text. Our tutors are instructed to refuse the second thing even when a parent asks for it directly.

Machine-generated prose belongs in the same category by a newer route. Discussing why a generated paragraph reads as generic against the assessment expectations is useful teaching. Supplying it as the student's work is the same breach as writing it yourself. At least one provider visible in this market sells completed assessed work outright, at a published price; if that is offered for your child, decline it and tell the school, because the consequences land on the candidate alone. A grade obtained that way is also worthless to the student who has to sit the next qualification without the skill.

process.title: Confirm the code, then send marked work
process.description: 0510 and 0511 handle speaking differently, and 0500 is a different subject. The code is on the entry sheet. Send it with one marked written task and, if there is one, the latest marked mock, because those two documents set the baseline that everything afterwards is measured against.

process.title: Free trial lesson with a task attached
process.description: Sixty minutes at no cost and no card details, built around one skill rather than a tour of the subject. You should be able to tell afterwards whether the tutor diagnosed something or simply taught a nice lesson. If the match is wrong, we propose somebody else instead of defending the choice.

process.title: Set the baseline under our own conditions
process.description: One task written to time under stated conditions, marked with task fulfilment, register and accuracy separated. For transferring students this matters doubly, because two schools' marking rarely agrees and a baseline nobody can dispute is the only fair starting point for targets.

process.title: Run the cycle and keep the versions
process.description: Task set, task marked, task rebuilt, both versions kept in one document. The listening cycle and the speaking block run alongside it as needed, each with their own record. Nothing is reported that cannot be shown, and anything recorded is recorded with consent.

process.title: Review at four sessions, and act on it
process.description: A written review comparing start and latest, naming what has stopped going wrong, with one of three recommendations: continue, narrow, or stop. If the answer is stop, that is what it says. Families who want to pause for travel or Ramadan keep their slot and are charged for nothing that does not happen.

whyPoints.title: The record is auditable by a parent
whyPoints.description: Two versions of each written task, both listening attempts, the speaking recordings and a plain-language review. You can check a claim about progress against the work itself rather than against a tutor's account of their own hour.

whyPoints.title: Four skills tracked separately
whyPoints.description: Reading, writing, listening and speaking fail independently in 0510, so a single impression of how English is going cannot find the leak. Keeping four records costs a little administration and locates the problem in a fortnight instead of a term.

whyPoints.title: Listening attempted twice, not marked and discarded
whyPoints.description: Re-answering the same recording after the trap types have been taught is the cheapest diagnostic in the subject, and it only works if the first attempt was kept. Almost nobody does this, which is why so many 0510 candidates lose listening marks without knowing why.

whyPoints.title: Consent handled properly for a minor's work
whyPoints.description: Speaking recordings happen only with consent, the purpose is stated, and deletion is available on request. Lead forms say what is collected and why, with a privacy link on every page, in line with the UAE's personal data protection law.

whyPoints.title: Online delivery, said plainly
whyPoints.description: Every UAE session is one-to-one on live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; that service runs only in India. The gain is the choice of specialist and the continuity of the record, and the trade is stated rather than hidden.

faqs.question: Will a 0510 tutor come to our house in Town Square or Mudon?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE; in-home visits are a service we run only in India. Dubai sessions are one-to-one on live video in Gulf Standard Time. For communities out along Al Qudra Road the trade is favourable: an ordinary term-time drive from central Dubai takes most of an hour, which is why published in-home rates there sit at the top of the AED 180-500 band, and why a visiting tutor is drawn from whoever happens to live nearby.

faqs.question: What should we have in writing after four 0510 sessions?
faqs.answer: A review naming the skill that was weakest at the start, one written task shown in its first and latest version, a note on which listening traps no longer catch your child, a count of how many prompts a spoken answer now needs, and a recommendation to continue, narrow or stop. It will not contain a predicted grade, a satisfaction score or a percentage improvement, because none of those could be produced honestly from four sessions. Everything in it is either observable or readable by you.

faqs.question: How do you prove listening has improved rather than just saying so?
faqs.answer: By keeping the first attempt. The student answers a recording, the trap types that caught them are taught, and a fortnight later the same recording is answered again. The comparison shows whether the self-correction is now heard, whether the second number is taken rather than the first, and whether distractors still pull the answer. It costs nothing except the discipline of not discarding the original paper, and it is the cheapest diagnostic available in this subject.

faqs.question: Why mark task fulfilment separately from grammar in 0510 writing?
faqs.answer: Because they fail independently and the repair is different. 0510 written tasks are set in defined forms for defined readers, so an article, an email to a head teacher and a report all want different registers. A candidate can produce grammatically clean prose that answers a slightly different brief and lose marks without any error being visible. Separating the judgements shows a parent in seconds whether the problem is accuracy, register or reading the task, and each of those takes a different number of sessions.

faqs.question: Do you record my child's speaking practice, and who keeps it?
faqs.answer: Only with consent, and only two short recordings across a speaking block. We state the purpose before anything is recorded, keep it for the block, and delete it on request. A student who would rather not be recorded can still do the block; the measure is how long an answer develops before a prompt, which a tutor can note without any audio. Our lead forms also state what is collected and why, with a privacy link on every page, under the UAE's personal data protection framework.

faqs.question: Can you work from the mock paper our school has already marked?
faqs.answer: That is the preferred starting point. A marked mock shows what the department credited and what it let pass, which is more useful than any conversation. The post-mock diagnostic pair exists for exactly this: one session to read the mock in detail and set a replacement task under our own conditions, one to mark it and report a finding. Some families take that finding and decide no further sessions are needed, which is a legitimate outcome and sometimes the right one.

faqs.question: My child just changed schools in Dubai. Which marking do we trust?
faqs.answer: Neither, at first. Transfers are common across Dubai's private sector and two schools' expectations rarely align, so a student can arrive looking stronger or weaker than they are. The fair move is to set one task to time under stated conditions and mark it against the syllabus demands, producing a baseline neither school's grading can explain away. Targets are then set from that baseline. It costs one session and prevents a term of work aimed at the wrong skill.

faqs.question: How does the mandatory Arabic workload affect a 0510 plan?
faqs.answer: It decides what is realistic on a weeknight. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with KHDA calculating instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit and requiring separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. That is real homework competing for the same evenings as English practice. We schedule timed written tasks for weekend mornings for this reason, and keep weeknight sessions for marking and rebuilding.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help write my child's supervised written work?
faqs.answer: No, and the refusal is deliberate even when a parent asks directly. Supervised work must be the candidate's own, produced under the school's conditions and authenticated by the school. A tutor may teach the form, write a model on an unrelated topic, explain what the task demands, question a draft until the student locates the weakness, and mark practice work that is never handed in. Adding sentences to a submitted text puts the entry at risk and leaves the school unable to stand behind its authentication.

faqs.question: What if my child uses an AI tool to draft a task?
faqs.answer: Then the useful lesson is critique rather than concealment. A tutor can show why a generated paragraph reads as generic against what the task demands, where the register slips, and which sentences no sixteen-year-old would write. What a tutor must not do is supply that text as the student's work, which is the same breach as writing it for them by a newer route. If a provider offers finished assessed work for your child, decline it and tell the school; the consequences fall on the candidate.

faqs.question: How many prompts should a 0510 speaking answer need by the end of a block?
faqs.answer: Fewer than at the start, and that is the honest version of the target. In week one a typical student answers in one sentence and waits. By week three the same student usually offers a reason, an example and an opinion without being asked for each. We record the count rather than a score, because the component rewards development and a count is something you can check. Anyone promising a specific speaking grade from a three-week block is selling certainty that does not exist.

faqs.question: Does the record transfer if we switch tutors inside IB Gram?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is one practical reason for keeping it. The written task folder, both listening attempts, the speaking notes and the four-session review go to the next tutor, so a new specialist starts from the baseline rather than from a blank page. Families who have moved between independent tutors in Dubai usually describe the opposite experience: a fresh diagnostic hour paid for twice. Continuity of the record is worth more than continuity of the person.

faqs.question: Is online as effective as a tutor in the room for a speaking component?
faqs.answer: For speaking it is arguably better, because the thing being trained is talk and the thing that limits progress is who you are talking to. Live video lets a Dubai family work with somebody who can hold an unscripted conversation pitched just above the student's comfort level, rather than with whoever is free locally. Recording a short extract is also easier, and hearing your own hesitation is the fastest route to removing it. We do not offer in-home sessions in the UAE at all.

faqs.question: What happens to the evidence trail if we stop for a term?
faqs.answer: It waits, intact. The folder, both listening attempts and the review stay available, the slot is held where we can, and nothing is charged for sessions that do not take place. When you come back, the first session re-tests the weakest skill rather than reviewing everything, which usually takes one session instead of three. Families pause for travel, for exam periods in other subjects and for Ramadan, and the record is what makes restarting cheap.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-english-second-lan.closingHeading: Ask to see the first week's evidence before committing to a term
dubai/cambridge-igcse-english-second-lan.closingBody: Send the syllabus code from the entry sheet and one marked written task. We will name which of the four 0510 skills is costing the grade, set one task under stated conditions to confirm it, and show you both versions once it is marked. The trial lesson is free, runs sixty minutes, and needs no card details. Sessions after that are one-to-one on live video to your household in Dubai, in Gulf Standard Time, with a written review at four sessions that is allowed to tell you to stop.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-english-second-lan.tutorsIntro: The tutors here teach Cambridge IGCSE English as a Second Language online to students in Dubai schools. Each works to a session plan with a stated end point, because open-ended weekly tuition is how English budgets quietly double between October and May.

intro.heading: The cheaper hour is only cheaper if you buy the right number of them
paragraphs: Online 0510 tuition costs less per hour than the in-home alternative in Dubai, and the published figures show the gap clearly. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai survey puts in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180-350 an hour, with independent home tutors reaching AED 500. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150, and TutorChase quotes AED 270 for specialist support. At the budget end EdFlik advertises from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. Each figure belongs to the company named beside it and was read in October 2026.

A lower hourly rate, though, is the least interesting part of the saving. The expensive mistake in this subject is not paying too much per hour; it is paying for the wrong number of hours in the wrong term. A family that books one hour a week from September to May buys roughly thirty-five sessions whether or not the problem needed them, and in 0510 the problem is frequently four written tasks and two listening reviews away from being fixed.

So this page is organised around pacing rather than around rates. It sets out what money buys in Year 10 against what it buys in Year 11, where a stated ceiling should sit on each block, and which costs are not the tutor's at all. The exam centre's entry and administration charges, a review of results, a November retake entry: all of those sit outside a tuition quote and all of them surprise somebody every year.

It also states two things most providers in this market leave vague. The first is what happens when no suitable specialist is free at the hour you want, which is a real constraint rather than a hypothetical one, and we publish the fallback instead of discovering it after you have paid. The second is what the free trial includes and what conditions attach to it, because the word free without its conditions on the same screen is not an offer, it is a hook.

All UAE sessions run one-to-one on live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home visits are a service we run only in India. For a Dubai family that means the comparison on this page is between what the local market sells and what we actually deliver, with the difference in both price and pool stated rather than implied. One further note on figures: everything quoted here is attributed to whoever published it and dated to the month it was read, and where a number could not be verified it has been left out. No IB exam or results date appears anywhere on this page for exactly that reason, because ibo.org cannot be checked automatically and a tutoring site is the wrong place to learn a date your school can confirm.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-english-second-lan.programmesIntro: Which qualification your child is entered for decides the calendar, the component list and the number of hours worth buying. These are the four we are asked about most by Dubai families looking at English as a second language.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE English as a Second Language (0510)
programmes.description: Reading, writing, listening and speaking are each assessed, with the speaking test reported separately from the overall grade under this code. Written tasks are set in defined forms for stated readers. Component structures have been revised in recent exam years, so confirm the current list and timings for your child's exam year on cambridgeinternational.org before buying hours against an old paper format.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs IGCSE exams in a June series and a November series, which gives a Dubai family a genuine second chance within one academic year. It also means two sets of entry deadlines, and the deadlines sit months ahead of the papers rather than weeks.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE English as a Second Language
programmes.description: The Edexcel route some Dubai schools prefer. Comparable demands, different paper formats and a different calendar, so past-paper practice is not interchangeable with Cambridge material. A tutor setting Cambridge papers for an Edexcel candidate is spending your money on question types the student will never sit.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs International GCSE exams in May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the next day, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

programmes.name: Cambridge O Level English Language
programmes.description: Still used by some schools in the emirate. The writing demands are close enough to IGCSE that a specialist can teach both, but the paper shape differs and the hours needed are usually fewer because the format is more predictable. That difference belongs in the quote rather than being absorbed silently.
programmes.countryNote: Ask the exams officer which series the centre enters and which of Cambridge's six administrative zones it sits in. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE English as a First Language (0500)
programmes.description: Where a strong 0510 candidate sometimes moves. Two written papers, no listening or speaking inside the grade, and a heavier analytical load built on summary point selection and explanation of language effects. Moving up usually costs a block of extra writing hours in Year 10, and saves them later.
programmes.countryNote: Any entry change has to clear a Cambridge deadline, not just a department's agreement. For the March 2027 series final entries were due on 27 November 2026 for an exam period running 3 February to 4 March 2027, which is why these conversations belong in the autumn term.

subjects.description: The page's subject. Four skills, of which writing absorbs most paid hours and listening the fewest. A plan costed by skill rather than by week is usually a third shorter than the standard one-hour-a-week offer.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (4ES1)
subjects.description: The Edexcel equivalent, on a different calendar. Worth confirming before the first session, because a term of Cambridge past papers bought for an Edexcel candidate is money spent on the wrong question formats.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (0500)
subjects.description: The upgrade route. Costs a concentrated block of writing hours in Year 10 and tends to reduce what a family spends in Year 12, because the analytical habits are already built before AS Level.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (4MA1)
subjects.description: The most common second subject in a Dubai family's tutoring budget. Word problems punish weak reading, so before paying for two tutors it is worth checking whether the maths loss is actually a language loss.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Written answers about algorithms reward precision over fluency. Students who have learned to answer the exact task in 0510 writing tend to stop narrating their code and start describing it, which is where the marks are.

subjects.name: Accounting (0452)
subjects.description: Short written explanations carry marks alongside the numbers. A 0510 candidate who can write a controlled two-sentence justification gains here without extra accounting teaching, which is a cheaper repair than a second tutor.

subjects.description: Evaluation marks are written marks. The report-writing work inside a 0510 plan transfers almost directly, so sequencing English before business usually costs a family less than running both at once.

subjects.name: Travel and Tourism (0471)
subjects.description: Popular in the emirate and heavily written. Case-study answers need economical prose under time pressure, which is the same discipline a 0510 report task teaches, so the two sit well in one plan.

subjects.name: Geography (0460)
subjects.description: Case-study recall is rarely the problem; structuring an answer inside the time is. Families often buy geography hours for what is really a writing-pace issue, and the cheaper fix sits in the English session.

sections.heading: What an online 0510 tutor in Dubai costs, answered first
paragraphs: A Cambridge IGCSE English Second Language 0510 online tutor in Dubai sits, in market terms, in the AED 150-300 an hour band for a qualified subject tutor. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and TutorChase quotes AED 270, both read in October 2026. Below that band, EdFlik advertises from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52, which buys supervision rather than diagnosis. Above it, BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium tier.

The in-home comparison is published too. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai survey puts visiting one-to-one tuition at AED 180-350 an hour, with independent home tutors reaching AED 500 once travel is included. Monthly packages circulate as well: AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. Those are other companies' numbers, quoted with their names and the month they were read. IB Gram quotes after a free trial lesson rather than publishing a rate card.

What none of those figures answer is how many hours your child needs, which is the number that decides the bill. A 0510 plan built around four to six marked written tasks, a short listening cycle and a speaking block is a fundamentally different purchase from a year of weekly hours, even at an identical rate. The rest of this page is about that distinction, because it is where the money actually goes. Ask any provider to break a quote into skills with a session count against each, and the comparison becomes possible; ask only for an hourly rate and it does not.

sections.heading: Why the online unit is cheaper, and what you give up
paragraphs: The gap between AED 150-300 and AED 180-500 is mostly road. A tutor driving between two Dubai appointments in the late afternoon spends unpaid time in traffic and prices it into the hour, which is rational rather than greedy. Remove the journey and the same teaching hour costs less, the session starts when the student sits down, and a cancellation becomes a twenty-minute reschedule rather than a lost evening for both parties.

Two further savings are structural. A video session can be thirty minutes, which makes frequent short speaking practice affordable; nobody drives across Dubai for half an hour. And the tutor pool stops being a function of geography, so a family is choosing from people who know the 0510 components rather than from people who live within range and are free at five. For a four-skill language paper that widening matters more than for most subjects.

What you give up is real and worth stating. There is no physical presence to enforce concentration, so a student who will not sit at a desk without an adult beside them is harder to help online. Younger students need a parent within earshot for the first few sessions. Equipment matters: a headset and a stable connection are the difference between a listening exercise and an argument about audio. IB Gram does not sell in-home sessions anywhere in the UAE, so these are the trade-offs on offer rather than a menu. A trial lesson is the cheapest way to find out which side of them your child falls on.

sections.heading: Pacing the spend across Year 10 and Year 11
paragraphs: The table below is the shape we recommend to Dubai families, and it is deliberately front-loaded. Work done in Year 10 is cheaper per unit of benefit because there is time for redrafting to do its job, and because a problem identified early is usually three or four marked tasks away from repair. The same problem found at the Year 11 mocks costs a compressed block at exam-term intensity, which is the most expensive way to buy the same hours.

Read the fourth column as a band rather than a quote. It applies Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions, AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, to the number of sessions each stage actually needs. A fortnightly plan halves the mid-band monthly figure, which is why the autumn of Year 10 appears so much cheaper than the spring of Year 11.

One line in the table has no tuition cost at all. The stage after results is where a family decides between accepting a grade, asking the centre about a review of results, and entering for the November series. That decision is worth more than several sessions and costs nothing but a conversation with the exams officer, provided it happens inside the centre's own deadlines rather than after them. Families who ask about those deadlines in April rather than in August give themselves a choice; the others inherit whichever option is left.

sections.heading: The costs that belong to the exam centre, not the tutor
paragraphs: Three charges catch Dubai families out every year, and none of them is a tuition fee. The first is entry. A candidate sitting through their school usually has entry inside school fees, and KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for 2026-27 under Dubai's second economic incentives package, valued at AED 1.5 billion. A private candidate pays the exam centre directly, and the centre sets both the entry charge and its administration fee.

The second is a review of results. The window is short and the decision is better taken before results arrive than during the week they land, which means asking the exams officer in advance what the centre's internal cut-off is and what it charges. The third is a retake entry. Cambridge runs June and November series, so a near miss in June can often be re-sat in November, but that series has its own deadline and the centre's cut-off sits earlier than Cambridge's.

A tutor has no part in any of these transactions and should not be quoting figures for them. If a provider offers to handle your entry or implies that tuition is required for a successful entry, treat both claims carefully: the first is the centre's job, and the second is false urgency about a process that has nothing to do with buying lessons. Ask the centre in writing, early, and keep the reply. A dated email from the exams officer is worth more at results time than any assurance from a tutor.

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, and why it changes the plan
paragraphs: Dubai families with children at schools in neighbouring emirates, or who are considering a move, often assume one authority covers everything. It does not. Five bodies oversee private schools across the seven emirates, and they govern different things. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi. SPEA regulates private education in Sharjah, and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same there.

The practical consequences are concrete. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum and fee decisions sit with the emirate regulator rather than only with the school. The Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Across all of them the federal baseline holds: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations.

For a tutoring plan this matters in two ways. It tells you whose published inspection or licensing information to read when judging a school, and it tells you where to ask about entry and equivalency questions. It is also the point at which to be plain about our own position: IB Gram holds no permit, approval, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB, and no page on this site should be read as implying otherwise.

sections.heading: What happens when no 0510 specialist is free
paragraphs: Every tutoring platform has coverage limits and almost none of them publish theirs. Ours are ordinary and worth stating. Afternoon and early-evening slots in Gulf Standard Time fill first, and they fill earliest between February and May when every exam-year family in the emirate wants the same hours. A request for a 0511 speaking specialist three weeks before an oral is harder to meet than a request for a writing block in October, and pretending otherwise would just waste your week.

The table sets out what we can usually do, how long matching takes, and what the fallback is when nobody suitable is free at your preferred hour. The fallbacks are honest rather than flattering: a different time slot, a different session shape, a tutor outside the UAE working to Gulf Standard Time, or a straight answer that we cannot help in the window you need. No part of this is a tutor count or a claim about availability we could not evidence.

The reason to publish it is that the alternative is worse. Several providers in this market conceal non-UAE delivery behind a local-looking contact number, and at least two route UAE parents to numbers in another country entirely. If a tutor is working from outside the UAE, you should be told before you book, not discover it from an accent and a time zone. Our position is that all UAE sessions are online, so where the tutor sits is a question of scheduling, and we answer it directly.

sections.heading: What the free trial includes, and the conditions attached
paragraphs: A trial lesson with us is one full sixty-minute one-to-one session with the proposed tutor, at no cost, with no card details taken and no obligation to continue afterwards. One trial per student, with the tutor we think fits best. If the match is wrong you say so and we propose somebody else rather than asking you to persevere. Those are the conditions in full, and they belong on the same screen as the word free rather than in terms nobody reads.

The trial is most useful when it has something to work on. Send the syllabus code from the entry sheet and one marked written task beforehand, and the hour can be spent diagnosing rather than introducing. A good trial ends with you knowing which of the four skills is costing the grade and roughly how many sessions that repair takes. A weak trial ends with everyone agreeing that your child is lovely and should read more.

What a trial cannot do is predict a grade, and nobody offering one should. It also cannot commit us to an hour we do not have: if the only slots left are at times that do not suit your household, we say that during the trial rather than after you have paid for a block. Any quote that follows states whether VAT is included in the figures given; we do not publish general claims about the VAT treatment of tuition in the UAE, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation we are not in a position to make.

sections.heading: Price signals that should make a Dubai parent pause
paragraphs: A quote carries information beyond its number. At the bottom of the market the thing missing is almost always marking: reading a 0510 written task properly against what it demanded takes a real share of an hour, and at AED 45 nobody can afford to do it, so the session becomes conversation. Ask directly what gets marked between sessions and ask to see anonymised written feedback. That one question separates the bands faster than any credential list.

At the top of the market, scrutinise claims rather than prices. Examiner status used as a selling point should be evidenced and should never be presented as access to marking, boundaries or paper content. Self-published star ratings are worth little: competitors in this SERP show different review totals on the same page, and one shows a rating from twenty reviews beside a claim about a student body in the thousands. A rate of AED 650 an hour may be perfectly fair; the claims attached to it still need checking.

Three further signals are worth noting. Any promise of a specific grade, or a refund tied to an outcome, is a claim nobody in this market can honour honestly. Any suggestion of approval or accreditation from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB should be checked against the body's own register, since the permit regime for individual tutors sits with MoHRE and the training-institute permit with KHDA. And a UAE page offering a contact number in another country is telling you where the service actually sits.

process.title: Send the code and one marked task
process.description: The syllabus code from the entry sheet decides the plan, and one marked written task shows whether marks went on register, on task fulfilment or on accuracy. Those two documents take you five minutes to find and save a session of diagnosis, which is a session you would otherwise pay for.

process.title: Free trial lesson, conditions stated
process.description: One full sixty-minute one-to-one lesson per student, no cost, no card details, no obligation. Built around one skill rather than a tour of the subject. If the slot you need does not exist, we say so during the trial rather than after a block has been bought.

process.title: Agree a block with a ceiling
process.description: A stated number of sessions, a stated end date, and the full price visible before the first lesson. Eight to ten sessions is typical for a writing block. Nothing rolls over silently, and pausing for travel or Ramadan does not consume sessions you have not had.

process.title: Review before extending
process.description: At the end of a block you get a written note on what has stopped going wrong and what has not, with a recommendation. Extending is a decision taken from that note, not a default. Families who only needed half the block are told so and billed for what happened.

process.title: Plan the exam admin separately
process.description: Entry, review of results and November retake questions go to the exam centre, in writing, well ahead of its internal deadlines. We will tell you which questions to ask and when, and we will not quote the centre's charges, because setting them is the centre's job and guessing them is nobody's.

whyPoints.title: Blocks with ceilings, not rolling months
whyPoints.description: Every plan has a session count and an end date agreed before payment. Open-ended weekly tuition is how an English budget doubles between October and May without anyone deciding that it should, and it is the default shape across most of this market.

whyPoints.title: Rates sourced, ours quoted after a trial
whyPoints.description: EdFlik, Tutopiya, Unitors, TutorChase, BartyED and Bestimate published the AED figures used here, read in October 2026. We quote after a free trial lesson instead of publishing a rate card, and we say plainly when a shorter plan would do.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits published
whyPoints.description: Afternoon slots between February and May are the hardest thing we sell, and a speaking specialist three weeks before an oral may not exist at your preferred hour. The fallback is on this page rather than in an email after payment.

whyPoints.title: The centre's charges stay the centre's
whyPoints.description: Entry fees, review of results and retake entries are set by the exam centre and we never quote them. Nor do we suggest that tuition is needed for a successful entry or for Ministry equivalency, which would be false urgency about a regulatory process.

whyPoints.title: Online delivery, stated without hedging
whyPoints.description: All UAE sessions run one-to-one on live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. Where a tutor sits is a scheduling question, and we answer it before you book rather than after.

faqs.question: Why does an online 0510 tutor charge less than one who drives to us?
faqs.answer: Because the journey is a cost somebody pays. Bestimate's 2026 survey puts visiting one-to-one tuition in Dubai at AED 180-350 an hour, with independent home tutors reaching AED 500, against AED 150-300 for a qualified online subject tutor where Unitors publishes a floor of AED 150. A tutor crossing the city in the late afternoon prices the unpaid traffic into the hour. Remove the travel and the teaching hour costs less, the session starts on time, and a clash becomes a reschedule rather than a lost evening.

faqs.question: Can we spread 0510 costs across Year 10 and Year 11?
faqs.answer: That is the cheaper plan, and the table on this page sets out the shape. Fortnightly marked writing through Year 10 at roughly half the mid-band monthly figure, a short listening cycle and a first speaking block before the summer, then the main weekly writing block in the Year 11 autumn at Bestimate's mid band of AED 600-1,200 a month. Spreading the work costs less in total than compressing it, because redrafting needs time to do its job and panic buys hours rather than progress.

faqs.question: Is starting in Year 10 genuinely cheaper than starting after the mocks?
faqs.answer: Yes, measurably, because the same repair takes fewer sessions when there is time between them. A written register problem found in October of Year 10 is usually three or four marked tasks away from fixed, at a fortnightly rate. The identical problem found at the Year 11 mocks needs a compressed block at exam-term intensity, where Bestimate's specialist band runs AED 1,000-2,000 or more a month. The hours are similar; the price per hour and the number needed are both worse.

faqs.question: What do we pay the exam centre rather than the tutor?
faqs.answer: Entry charges and the centre's administration fee if your child sits as a private candidate, any fee for a review of results, and a fresh entry charge for a November retake. A tutor has no role in those transactions and should not be quoting figures for them. Ask the centre in writing early, because its internal cut-off dates sit earlier than Cambridge's own deadlines, and keep the reply. If a provider offers to handle your entry, remember that entry administration is the centre's job.

faqs.question: Does a November resit cost more than entering in June?
faqs.answer: The charges are set by the exam centre, so ask it directly rather than taking a figure from a tutoring site. What is predictable is the timing: Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, so a near miss in June can usually be re-sat in November, but the November deadline arrives faster than families expect and the centre's cut-off is earlier still. Budget for the entry and for a short rehearsal package rather than for a second year of weekly tuition.

faqs.question: Do you charge for a session cancelled the night before?
faqs.answer: Our working rule is that nothing is billed for a session that does not happen, and that a slot can be moved rather than lost, because moving a video session costs nobody a journey. What we ask in return is as much notice as a household can realistically give, since a late cancellation in February removes an hour that another exam-year family would have taken. Any specific terms attached to a block are stated before payment rather than appearing afterwards.

faqs.question: What exactly is included in the free trial lesson?
faqs.answer: One full sixty-minute one-to-one session per student with the proposed tutor, at no cost, with no card details taken and no obligation to continue. If the match is wrong, we propose a different tutor instead of asking you to persevere. Send the syllabus code and one marked written task beforehand so the hour diagnoses rather than introduces. Those are the conditions in full; a trial described as free without its conditions on the same screen is not an offer worth acting on.

faqs.question: Is there a discount if both our children need 0510 support?
faqs.answer: Two children usually need two plans rather than one shared hour, because the skill that is leaking is rarely the same. What does save money is scheduling: consecutive slots with the same tutor where the syllabus and level genuinely overlap, which removes a second diagnostic and a second set of scheduling friction. Any price adjustment is stated in the quote before payment. We will say plainly if two different specialists would serve your children better than one compromise match.

faqs.question: Our school is in Sharjah but we live in Dubai. Which regulator applies?
faqs.answer: The school's emirate, not your address. Sharjah private schools are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which also approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Dubai schools sit with KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain with ADEK, Ras Al Khaimah with its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah with the Ministry of Education. For entry, equivalency and inspection questions, read the authority that licenses the school your child attends.

faqs.question: What if no 0510 tutor is free at the hour we need?
faqs.answer: We tell you, and offer the fallback rather than a vague promise. Afternoon slots in Gulf Standard Time fill first and fill earliest between February and May. The realistic alternatives are a 7pm or weekend-morning slot, a fortnightly shape instead of weekly, a marking-focused arrangement with brief live time, or a place in the queue with an honest estimate. Sometimes the right answer is that we cannot help inside your window, and saying so beats taking the booking.

faqs.question: Do rates go up in the six weeks before the exams?
faqs.answer: Availability tightens rather than the hourly figure rising, but the monthly cost goes up anyway because families buy two sessions a week instead of one. Bestimate's specialist exam-year band of AED 1,000-2,000 or more a month reflects that intensity rather than a price increase. The way to avoid it is to buy the writing block in the autumn, when slots are open and fewer sessions achieve more. Late bookers pay in choice of hour as much as in money.

faqs.question: Is a monthly package better value than paying per block?
faqs.answer: Packages published in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits, which look efficient and assume you need that volume every month. Our view is that a block with a stated session count and end date fits 0510 better, because the subject needs concentrated work on one or two skills and then less. A monthly debit through a term where nothing is being marked is the most common way families overspend here.

faqs.question: Are the figures on this page inclusive of VAT?
faqs.answer: The AED figures here are other companies' published rates, so how each treats VAT is a question for them. For our own work, any quote we give you states whether VAT is included in the number quoted. We deliberately do not publish general statements about the VAT treatment of tuition fees in the UAE, because that would require a Federal Tax Authority citation, and we do not display a tax registration number we do not hold. Ask any provider to put the VAT position in the quote.

faqs.question: How do we tell whether a cheap 0510 quote is hiding something?
faqs.answer: Ask three questions. What gets marked between sessions, and can we see anonymised written feedback? Who covers the sessions if the tutor leaves Dubai in June? And is the tutor working under the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is granted free of charge for two years under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023? A low rate is not dishonest, but at the bottom of the market the missing item is almost always the marking, and marking is the part that moves a grade.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-english-second-lan.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed here teach Cambridge IGCSE English as a Second Language to students in Dubai schools. All four skills matter to them equally, which is less common than it sounds: plenty of English tutors can teach writing and have never marked a detail-level listening answer.

intro.heading: 0510 costs what it costs because it asks for four different things
paragraphs: Parents pricing 0510 tuition in Dubai usually start from a number they heard for maths and find it does not fit. The reason is structural. English as a Second Language assesses reading, writing, listening and speaking, and a candidate can be comfortable in three of them while a single weak skill holds the grade down. Buying one hour a week of general English is therefore an inefficient way to spend money on this syllabus, because the hour tends to land on whichever skill the tutor enjoys teaching.

The published market gives a range to work within. EdFlik lists tuition from AED 45-65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33-52 at the budget end. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150. TutorChase quotes AED 270. BartyED charges AED 650 for its premium tier. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai survey puts in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180-350, with independent home tutors reaching AED 500 once the drive is priced in. Each of those figures belongs to the company named beside it, read in October 2026, and none of them is an IB Gram price.

What those bands do not tell you is how many hours a 0510 candidate needs, and that is the number that decides the bill. In our experience the writing component absorbs the largest block, speaking needs several short sessions rather than a few long ones, listening improves faster through unsupervised practice than through paid teaching, and reading sits somewhere in between. Costing a term by skill rather than by week is the one change that most often reduces what a Dubai family spends on this subject.

There is also a decision upstream of the budget. Some Dubai schools enter students for 0510 who would be better served by English as a First Language, and some do the reverse. Getting that wrong wastes a year of hours on the wrong skill set, so this page includes a comparison table of 0510 against 0500 that you can take to a parents' evening. The entry sheet, not a tutor's opinion, is the document that settles which syllabus number applies.

IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition as one-to-one lessons on live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home visits are a service we run only in India. For 0510 that matters more than for most subjects, because speaking practice needs a tutor who can hold an unscripted conversation at a controlled level, pitched just above where the student is comfortable, and the pool of people who can do that well is not distributed evenly across Al Nahda, Al Qusais and International City. The hour that an in-home arrangement would spend on Dubai traffic goes into marking a written task instead, and the marked task is the part that moves a 0510 grade.
