dubai/cambridge-igcse-english-second-lan.programmesIntro: Cambridge offers more than one route for a student learning in English without first-language fluency. The code on the entry sheet decides what gets assessed, how speaking is reported, and therefore what a term of tuition should cover.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary English as a Second Language
programmes.description: The stage where accuracy habits form. Checkpoint tests run in March, May and October and give a school an early signal about which of the four skills is lagging. Work at this stage is inexpensive relative to its effect, because a Year 8 student still has time to build listening stamina through habit rather than through paid hours.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools use Checkpoint inconsistently as a diagnostic. Ask which skill came out weakest rather than asking for the overall band, because the overall band hides exactly the information a parent is paying to discover two years later.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE English as a Second Language (0510)
programmes.description: Reading, writing, listening and speaking are all assessed. Under syllabus code 0510 the speaking test is reported separately from the overall grade rather than counted into it. Component structure and timings were revised for recent exam years, so confirm the current component list for your child's exam year on cambridgeinternational.org rather than relying on an older paper's format.
programmes.countryNote: 0510 is widely entered in Dubai's British-curriculum schools, including by students who have been educated in English for years but speak another language at home. The entry choice is made by the school department, so ask when it was reviewed; a decision taken in Year 9 is often left unchallenged into Year 11.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE English as a Second Language, Count-in Speaking (0511)
programmes.description: The same subject with speaking counted into the overall grade rather than reported separately. For a confident speaker that is an advantage worth having; for a student who freezes in an oral it is a risk. The tutoring plan changes accordingly, with far more short conversation sessions and recorded practice on unfamiliar topics.
programmes.countryNote: Not every Dubai school offers both codes, and some enter the whole cohort for one of them. If your child is articulate in conversation and loses marks in writing, it is worth asking the department which code they are entered for and why, well before the final entry deadline.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS & A Level English Language
programmes.description: The progression route for students who finish 0510 strongly and want to keep English as an academic subject. The jump is real: analysis of language use replaces task-based communication, and writing is judged on control rather than on accuracy alone. Students who left 0510 with weak writing usually need that gap closed before Year 12 rather than during it.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai sixth forms split between A Level and the IB Diploma. For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, students must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-english-second-lan.subjectsIntro: 0510 rarely arrives alone on a Dubai timetable. The subjects below are the ones whose cost and difficulty are most affected by a student's English, with the syllabus code so you can check the entry sheet.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510)
subjects.description: This page's subject. Four skills, assessed separately, with speaking reported apart from the grade. Writing absorbs most tuition hours because task fulfilment, register and precision are all marked, and most candidates have written few pieces to time.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language, Count-in Speaking (0511)
subjects.description: The variant where the oral counts towards the grade. Worth checking before buying speaking sessions, because the value of oral practice changes completely depending on which code the school entered.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (0500)
subjects.description: The alternative entry. Two written papers, no listening or speaking component in the grade, and a much heavier analytical demand. Some Dubai students sit it successfully after a strong 0510 performance in Year 10.

subjects.name: English Literature (0475)
subjects.description: Taken by a minority of 0510 candidates and demanding for them, because essay writing about a writer's method sits well above the language level 0510 requires. Budget for it as a separate subject, not as English practice.

subjects.name: French (0520)
subjects.description: Often a third language on a Dubai timetable. Students juggling 0510 alongside a modern foreign language and Arabic have three sets of vocabulary learning competing for the same evenings, which is a scheduling cost before it is a money one.

subjects.name: Arabic as a Second Language (0544)
subjects.description: Arabic is mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. For many 0510 candidates this is the single largest competing homework load.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: Word problems punish weak reading comprehension, so a 0510 candidate sometimes loses maths marks for language reasons. Worth diagnosing before paying for a second maths tutor, because the repair may belong in the English session.

subjects.name: Information and Communication Technology (0417)
subjects.description: Practical papers with dense written instructions. Candidates who misread a task lose marks they could do the work for, which is the clearest example of English cost showing up on somebody else's mark sheet.

subjects.name: Biology (0610)
subjects.description: Terminology-heavy and precise. Extended answers reward exact wording, so 0510 students benefit more from learning to define than from learning to elaborate. Two or three sessions of command-word work usually pays for itself here.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-english-second-lan.regionsIntro: 0510 entries cluster in parts of Dubai where English is the school language and another language is the family one. The communities below are where we take the most 0510 enquiries, with what tends to be different about each.

regions.name: Al Nahda
regions.note: A dense, multilingual residential belt with several large private schools within a short radius. Enquiries here frequently involve two or three children in the same household at different stages, which changes the budget conversation more than the teaching one.

regions.name: Al Qusais
regions.note: Long-established schools and a cohort where students have often been taught in English since primary. The weakness is rarely vocabulary; it is precision in writing tasks and detail-level listening, which are cheap to fix once identified.

regions.name: Deira and Al Rigga
regions.note: Older apartment stock, short commutes and a wide spread of school types. Families here are the most price-sensitive we deal with, and the skill-by-skill costing in this page was built largely from those conversations.

regions.name: International City
regions.note: A highly multilingual community where students often speak three languages daily and write confidently in none of them. Speaking marks tend to be strong, writing marks weaker, which is the opposite of the usual Dubai pattern.

regions.name: Al Warqa and Mirdif
regions.note: Villa communities feeding a cluster of British-curriculum schools. Afternoon traffic is bad enough here that in-home tuition quotes carry a visible premium, which is one reason online slots fill quickly.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis
regions.note: A newer secondary cohort with a mixture of boards. Mid-year transfers are common, and a transferring 0510 student often arrives entered for a different code than the one they were taught toward.

regions.name: Karama and Oud Metha
regions.note: Central, well served by schools and public transport, and the community where group classes at tuition centres are most widely used. Group pricing is genuinely lower per student; the trade is the group's pace.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha, The Villa and Jebel Ali
schoolClusters.note: Large British-curriculum campuses with substantial multilingual intakes and sizeable 0510 cohorts. Students from here usually read well and lose marks on written task fulfilment, which is a teachable repair rather than a language problem.

schoolClusters.city: Silicon Oasis, Academic City and Al Warqa
schoolClusters.note: A spread-out eastern belt where school choice is wide and mid-year movement frequent. The first job with students from this cluster is usually to confirm which syllabus code they are entered for before any teaching is planned.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-english-second-lan.modesIntro: Because 0510 splits across four skills, session length matters as much as session count. These three shapes cover almost every 0510 plan we write for a Dubai family.

modes.title: Weekly writing session with marked tasks
modes.description: The main block. One written task set between sessions in a specified form, marked against what the task asked for rather than on general fluency, then rebuilt in the live hour. Register, audience and task completion get scored separately from accuracy, because a candidate can write flawless sentences and still miss half the marks for answering a different question.

modes.title: Short speaking sessions
modes.description: Thirty minutes, twice a week during a speaking block. The format is deliberately uncomfortable: an unseen topic, a prompt, and a push to develop answers past one sentence. Shorter sessions cost less than full hours and work better, because oral stamina builds through frequency rather than duration. Recorded extracts let a student hear their own hesitation, which is usually more persuasive than being told about it.

sections.heading: What 0510 is, and what Dubai parents often think it is
paragraphs: A Cambridge IGCSE English Second Language 0510 tutor in Dubai is teaching a qualification for students who work in English without first-language fluency. 0510 assesses reading, writing, listening and speaking, with the speaking test reported separately from the overall grade under that code. It is not a remedial qualification and it is not an easier version of English for weaker students, which is the most common misunderstanding we hear on first calls.

The practical consequence is that 0510 marks are lost in places a general English tutor does not look. A candidate can speak fluently, read a newspaper comfortably, and still lose a grade because written tasks ignored the stated audience, or because listening answers missed the number in a distractor. Those are specific, teachable failures, and each one has a different cost in hours. That is why this page prices the subject by skill rather than quoting one hourly figure and leaving you to guess.

IB Gram delivers 0510 support to Dubai families as one-to-one lessons on live video. We do not send tutors to UAE addresses; home visits are available only through our India service. The reason this suits 0510 specifically is the speaking component: holding an unscripted conversation at a controlled level is a skill, and online delivery lets a Dubai family choose somebody who has it rather than somebody who lives nearby and is free at five. A student in Deira and a student in Dubai Silicon Oasis can work with the same specialist on the same evening, which is not possible with a car.

sections.heading: 0510 or 0500: the decision upstream of the budget
paragraphs: Before pricing anything, establish which syllabus your child is entered for and whether it is the right one. Dubai schools make this call at department level, often in Year 9, and it is rarely revisited. A student who has been taught in English since primary and reads widely may be under-placed in 0510, losing the analytical stretch that selective sixth forms look for. A student placed in 0500 who is still building written accuracy may be set up to lose a grade for reasons unrelated to intelligence.

The table below is written to be taken to a parents' evening. It compares the two syllabuses across what is assessed, how speaking is handled, who each suits, where marks leak, how each counts for equivalency and university entry, and what each implies for a tutoring plan. The honest headline is that these are different subjects, not two difficulty levels of the same one, and the tutoring hours look different as a result.

One practical warning. If an entry change is being considered, the deadline matters more than the argument. Cambridge entry deadlines sit months ahead of the exam window: for the March 2027 series final entries were due on 27 November 2026, for an exam period running 3 February to 4 March 2027. A conversation in February about moving syllabus is usually a conversation about next year, so raise it early with the head of English. Ask on what evidence the original placement was made, and whether any written work has been reviewed since.

sections.heading: What the Dubai market charges, by provider model
paragraphs: Comparing tutoring quotes in Dubai is hard because the models are not comparable. A freelance tutor found through a community group, an agency with a replacement policy, a marketplace pricing in dollars, a tuition centre with premises, and an online platform are five different purchases. The table compares them on the things that actually differ: the published rate, who published it, where the permit duty sits, and what happens when the arrangement fails.

Two columns deserve attention. The permit column matters because private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted through MoHRE free of charge for two years, and individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. A centre with premises and staff is a different animal again and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit as a training institute. IB Gram is not a Dubai training institute and holds no permit, approval or accreditation from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or the IB.

The replacement column matters because 0510 plans run for terms, not weeks. A freelance arrangement that ends in March leaves a family searching during the worst possible month, while an agency or platform should be able to propose somebody else within days. Ask for that in writing before paying, along with what happens to unused sessions. Rates below are quoted with their sources and the month they were read; they describe the market, not an IB Gram price list.

sections.heading: Where the hours go, skill by skill
paragraphs: This is the section that changes what a Dubai family spends. Most 0510 plans sold in this market are one hour a week for a year, which is a comfortable product to sell and a blunt instrument to buy. Costing by skill produces a different shape: a long writing block, a short intense speaking block, a brief listening cycle that gets dropped once the error pattern disappears, and a small amount of whole-paper rehearsal at the end.

The numbers in the table are session counts drawn from how 0510 plans actually run rather than from a price list, multiplied against the market mid band of AED 150-300 an hour that Unitors' published floor and Bestimate's survey both point to. They are indicative. A student with strong writing and a terror of speaking inverts the whole shape, which is exactly why a diagnostic conversation before booking is worth more than a discount.

Two savings are available to almost everybody. Listening practice does not need a paid hour to sit alongside it; it needs setting, marking and a short review. And speaking works better in thirty-minute sessions twice a week than in a weekly hour, which costs less in total. A provider who sells you four full hours a month of mixed-skill English is not wrong, but they are not optimising for your bill. Ask any quote to be broken into skills with a session count against each, and compare the shapes rather than the headline rates; the differences between providers show up there far more clearly than they do in an hourly figure.

sections.heading: Listening and speaking, the components Dubai families underestimate
paragraphs: Almost every 0510 enquiry we take from Dubai is about writing. Almost every 0510 marked paper we read shows listening losing marks quietly. The reason is that listening feels like a passive skill and therefore like something that cannot be practised, when in fact the losses are concentrated in a handful of predictable traps: a number said twice with the second one correct, a speaker who corrects themselves, a distractor that answers a question slightly different from the one asked.

Those traps are learnable in two or three sessions, which makes listening the cheapest grade movement available in the subject. The work is mostly unsupervised: structured practice set by the tutor, answers marked, and a short live review of the question types that went wrong. Paying a tutor to sit beside a student through a recording is not a good use of AED 200 an hour, and we say so rather than selling the hour.

Speaking is the opposite case, undervalued for a different reason. Under 0510 the oral is reported separately from the grade, so some families reasonably deprioritise it, while under 0511 it counts and deprioritising it is expensive. Either way the skill that gets assessed is development: taking an unfamiliar prompt and building past one sentence without rehearsed phrases. That improves with frequency, so short sessions twice a week beat a monthly hour, and recorded extracts let a student hear their own hesitations instead of being told about them.

sections.heading: How a 0510 grade counts for equivalency and university entry
paragraphs: A 0510 pass is an accredited IGCSE subject, and for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track students must submit proof of five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, together with one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, which is a detail at least one ranking tutoring site in this market gets wrong by claiming six subjects are needed.

That makes the English grade structurally important rather than just academically desirable, because it is almost always one of the five. It does not, however, make tutoring a requirement for equivalency, and any provider implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency about a regulatory process. IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency; the authority does that, and parents should verify current requirements through the Ministry of Education or their emirate's attestation channel before making decisions.

University entry is a separate question with separate answers. Some selective courses outside the UAE prefer or require first-language English rather than ESL, some accept 0510 without comment, and some ask for a separate language test regardless. The American-track equivalency rules give a sense of how test-based thresholds work: English proficiency there requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT. Ask the specific university, in writing, rather than accepting a tutor's general reassurance.

sections.heading: The costs that are not the tutor's: entry, re-marks and resits
paragraphs: Families budgeting for 0510 often forget that the tuition line is not the only line. If a candidate sits through their school, entry costs are usually inside school fees, and KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package. If a candidate sits as a private candidate, the exam centre sets both the entry charge and its administration fee, and a tutor has no part in that transaction and should not be quoting figures for it.

Re-marks and reviews of results are a second cost with a tight deadline, and the decision is better made before results arrive than during the week they do. The same is true of a retake entry: Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, so a candidate who narrowly misses in June can usually re-sit in November, but the entry deadline for that series arrives faster than most families expect. Ask the exams officer for the centre's internal cut-off dates, which sit earlier than Cambridge's own.

The third forgotten cost is timetable risk. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. A family revising from a timetable found online rather than from the centre's zone version is carrying a risk that no amount of tutoring offsets.

sections.heading: What cheap buys, and what it leaves out
paragraphs: The AED 45 an hour arrangement made through a community group chat is not automatically bad teaching, but the price tells you what is missing. Usually it is marking. Reading a 0510 written task properly against what the task demanded, then writing feedback a student can act on, takes a meaningful share of an hour, and at the budget rate nobody can afford to do it. The lesson becomes a conversation, and conversations improve confidence rather than grades.

The second omission is diagnosis. A tutor who starts with a textbook rather than with a marked paper is guessing which of the four skills is costing marks, and in this subject guessing wrong is the standard failure mode. The third is continuity: an informal arrangement has no cover when the tutor leaves Dubai in June, and 0510 plans that get interrupted in the final term rarely recover inside the same academic year.

There is also the permit question, which parents are entitled to ask about directly. The permit itself is free, so cost is no excuse for its absence, and reporting from Abu Dhabi indicates that ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff there from paid tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, a position worth verifying against the current policy document. None of this makes a low rate dishonest. It means the figure on the invoice is not the whole comparison, and a page that quotes rates without saying so is not helping you decide.

process.title: Tell us the syllabus code first
process.description: 0510 and 0511 need different plans, and 0500 needs a different tutor. The code is on the entry sheet, not on the report card. If the school has not confirmed it, ask the head of English before booking, because a term spent practising the wrong component is the most expensive mistake available here.

process.title: Send one marked written task
process.description: A returned email, report or article task with a teacher's comments shows whether marks were lost on register, on task fulfilment or on accuracy. Those three failures look identical to a parent and need different teaching. If nothing recent exists, we set one short task before the trial.

process.title: Free trial lesson, then a costed plan
process.description: Sixty minutes at no cost, with no card details taken. Afterwards you get a plan broken down by skill with a session count against each, so the quote shows what you are buying rather than a monthly figure. If the honest plan is four sessions rather than a term, that is what the plan says.

process.title: Run the writing block first
process.description: Writing takes the largest share of hours and moves most reliably, so it goes first unless a speaking test is imminent. One task marked in full between sessions, with task fulfilment scored separately from accuracy, and a model written on a different topic rather than on the student's own piece.

process.title: Drop skills as they stop losing marks
process.description: The listening cycle ends once the error pattern disappears. The speaking block ends when answers develop without prompting. Reducing the plan is the normal outcome of it working, and we propose the reduction rather than waiting to be asked, which is the opposite of how a subscription is designed to behave.

whyPoints.description: A plan that says six writing sessions, four short speaking sessions and two listening reviews can be checked against your child's marked paper. A plan that says one hour a week for a year cannot, and it is the shape almost every provider in this market sells.

whyPoints.description: Thirty minutes twice a week builds oral development faster than a weekly hour and bills lower. Selling the hour would be easier. The reason to do it the other way is that the component rewards frequency, and the arithmetic happens to favour the family.

whyPoints.description: No promised grades, no invented satisfaction percentages, no self-declared star ratings, and no suggestion that we hold any regulator's approval. faqs.question: How much does a 0510 tutor in Dubai cost per hour?
faqs.answer: Published market rates run from AED 33-65 an hour at the budget end, where Tutopiya and EdFlik advertise, to AED 150-300 for a qualified online subject tutor, with Unitors listing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and TutorChase publishing AED 270. In-home visits run AED 180-500 once travel is included, per Bestimate's 2026 survey, and one premium provider publishes AED 650. All figures were read in October 2026 and belong to the companies named. IB Gram quotes after a free trial lesson rather than publishing a rate card.

faqs.question: Why is 0510 priced differently from a single-skill subject?
faqs.answer: Because four skills are assessed and they do not need equal hours. Writing usually absorbs six to ten sessions in a term, speaking needs three to five short ones, reading two to four, and listening often needs only two or three live reviews on top of unsupervised practice. A flat hour a week spends the same money across all four regardless of where the marks are leaking. Costing by skill is the single change that most often reduces what a Dubai family pays for this subject.

faqs.question: Is my child in the right syllabus, 0510 or 0500?
faqs.answer: The entry sheet answers which one they are in; the comparison table on this page helps you judge whether it is right. Broadly, 0510 suits a student working confidently in English without first-language fluency, while 0500 suits a student schooled in English throughout who needs analytical stretch. Dubai departments often set this in Year 9 and rarely revisit it. If a change is worth discussing, raise it early: Cambridge entry deadlines sit months ahead of the papers, so a February conversation usually concerns next year.

faqs.question: What is the difference between 0510 and 0511?
faqs.answer: The speaking test. Under 0510 the oral is reported separately from the overall grade; under 0511, count-in speaking, it is included in the grade. That single difference changes the value of oral practice completely. For a confident speaker 0511 is an opportunity, and for a student who freezes in an oral it is a risk. Not every Dubai school offers both codes, so ask the department which one your child is entered for and why before buying any speaking sessions.

faqs.question: Which 0510 skill gives the cheapest grade improvement?
faqs.answer: Listening, almost always. The losses concentrate in a few predictable traps: a number said twice where the second is correct, a speaker correcting themselves, a distractor answering a slightly different question. Those are learnable in two or three sessions, and most of the practice can be set, marked and reviewed briefly rather than done inside a paid hour. Paying a tutor to sit through recordings alongside your child is poor value, and we would rather say that than sell the hour.

faqs.question: Are group 0510 classes at a Dubai centre better value than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: Per hour, yes. Group pricing at Dubai centres commonly runs AED 90-180 per student, against AED 150-300 for a qualified online one-to-one tutor. The trade is pace and diagnosis: a group moves at the group's speed and nobody marks your child's written tasks against the specific thing they get wrong. Groups work well for listening and reading drills and poorly for written task fulfilment. A centre with premises and staff also needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is reasonable to ask about.

faqs.question: Do we pay for a tutor's travel if sessions are online?
faqs.answer: No, and that is a real part of the price difference. Bestimate's in-home band starts at AED 180 an hour partly because a visiting tutor is absorbing unpaid Dubai traffic between appointments, and that cost has to be recovered somewhere. Our UAE sessions run one-to-one on live video, so the hour you pay for is teaching time. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses in the UAE at all; in-home visits are a service we run only in India.

faqs.question: How many months of 0510 tuition should we budget for?
faqs.answer: Think in blocks rather than months. A typical plan is a writing block of six to ten sessions, a speaking block of three to five short sessions, a listening cycle of two or three reviews, and two to four whole-paper rehearsals in the final six weeks. Spread across a Year 11 autumn and spring term, that is well under a year of weekly hours. Families who start in Year 10 usually spend less in total than families who start after the mocks, because fewer sessions do more.

faqs.question: Does a cheaper tutor mark written tasks properly?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and that is what the price is telling you. Reading a 0510 written task against what the task actually demanded, then writing feedback a student can act on, takes a serious share of an hour. At the budget band nobody can afford that time, so the session becomes a conversation about English. Conversations build confidence; marked tasks move grades. Before paying anybody, ask what gets marked between sessions and ask to see an example of their written feedback.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover 0510 and my other child's 0500?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, but check rather than assume. The two syllabuses reward different things: 0510 rewards task fulfilment, register and precision across four skills, while 0500 rewards point selection in a summary and explanation of language effects. A tutor strong in one is not automatically strong in the other. Where a tutor genuinely covers both, running the two children back to back in one evening slot saves scheduling friction, and we will say openly if two different specialists would serve you better.

faqs.question: Does 0510 count towards the five subjects for UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: Yes, as an accredited IGCSE subject. On the British track students must show five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One ranking site in this market states that six subjects are required, which is incorrect. Verify the current rules with the Ministry of Education or your emirate's attestation channel; tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency.

faqs.question: Who pays for a re-mark if the 0510 grade looks wrong?
faqs.answer: The family, through the exam centre, and the window is short. The practical advice is to decide in advance: before results week, agree with your child what grade would trigger a review of results and what would trigger a November retake entry instead. Cambridge runs June and November series, so a near miss in June is usually re-sittable, but centres set internal cut-off dates earlier than Cambridge's own deadlines. A tutor has no role in the transaction and should not be quoting fees for it.

faqs.question: Should we pay for sessions during the summer holidays?
faqs.answer: For 0510, a short summer block before Year 11 is often good value, because listening and speaking both decay over a long break spent in another language. Two or three short sessions a fortnight keeps the habit without costing a term's budget. What rarely pays is a full programme across July and August at exam-term intensity; students return in September tired and no further forward. The cheaper plan is a light summer and a properly resourced autumn writing block.

faqs.question: Can sessions move during Ramadan without extra charge?
faqs.answer: Yes. School days shorten during Ramadan and attention shifts later, so many Dubai families move an afternoon slot to after Iftar for the month. Because lessons run on live video, that change costs nobody a journey and can be agreed week by week at no additional charge. Families who prefer to pause entirely keep their slot, and nothing is billed for sessions that do not take place. Short speaking sessions tend to survive the month better than long writing ones.

Rates are agreed in AED before the first paid session, with the session length, the inclusions and the cancellation terms written down rather than left to be discovered on an invoice.

intro.heading: An in-home 0680 rate is a teaching rate plus a driving rate
paragraphs: Start with the arithmetic nobody puts in writing. A tutor who visits a villa in Arabian Ranches at 4.30pm on a Tuesday spends somewhere between fifty and ninety minutes in a car for one hour of teaching. That time is real, it is unpaid, and it is recovered inside the hourly figure the family is quoted. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350; independent home tutors in the emirate advertise up to AED 500. Online, the same table and the same providers put qualified subject tuition at AED 150 to 300 and specialist exam-year support at AED 200 to 450. The gap between those two columns is mostly fuel, traffic and risk.

That is not an argument that in-home tutoring is a swindle. For a nine-year-old who will not stay at a desk without an adult beside them, physical presence is the service and it is worth paying for. For a Year 11 student sitting two written papers on resource management, it is a premium attached to something the subject does not require. 0680 has no coursework, no practical and no apparatus. What it has is a resource booklet of graphs and tables that both people need to annotate at the same time, which a shared screen does better than a shared printout.

The honest position, stated before any rate table: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and that is true on this page as it is on the forty-eight other country pages we publish. What a Dubai family gets instead is one-to-one teaching over live video in Gulf Standard Time, a tutor chosen for having taught the whole 0680 syllabus rather than for living nearby, and an hour in which nothing is being recovered except teaching.

The second thing the in-home premium buys, unintentionally, is a smaller choice. Environmental Management is thin on the ground in this emirate. It is frequently taught as an additional subject by a geographer or a biologist, often to a group of eight, and the number of adults in Dubai who have taken a cohort through both papers is small. Draw a twenty-minute radius around a villa in Town Square or Al Khawaneej and the number inside it may be zero. Remove the radius and the constraint disappears, at a lower rate.

So this page does two things. It prices in-home 0680 support in Dubai using figures each provider published, with the month we read them, because three of the six best-ranking pages in this market publish no price at all. And it then budgets the work the way a parent actually needs it budgeted: by which third of the syllabus is broken and how many sessions that third takes, rather than by an hourly rate that tells you nothing about the total.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-environmental-mana.programmesIntro: What a family should spend changes with how much runway is left. These are the four points in a Dubai student's route where 0680 money gets committed, and what each one buys.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, first year
programmes.description: The cheapest intervention in the whole subject. A short block on data technique in Year 10 - reading values with units, describing a trend with figures, answering the command term printed - costs a few sessions and removes the fault that would otherwise cap Paper 2 eighteen months later. Almost nobody buys here, which is why the February market is so busy.
programmes.countryNote: Most Dubai British-curriculum schools begin IGCSE teaching in Year 10, and 0680 often sits in an option block with less class time than the core sciences. Asking the school how many periods a week the subject gets is a useful piece of free information: a thinner timetable allocation is a fair predictor of how much outside support the student will need.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, exam year
programmes.description: Where most 0680 spending happens and where each mark costs most. A family arriving after the January mocks is buying a compressed block in the weeks when every Year 11 cohort in Dubai wants the same scarce specialists. The teaching is the same; the choice of who delivers it is much narrower.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai mock windows cluster in January, and the emirate's Year 11 tutoring demand peaks immediately afterwards. For a thin subject that means availability, not the headline rate, is what moves. A family that books a specialist in October pays the same figure for a materially better match.

programmes.name: Resit and second-series entry
programmes.description: An underused route and one with real costs attached beyond tutoring. Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, so a student who misses a grade in June can re-enter later in the year. The tutoring block for a resit is usually short and surgical, because the diagnosis already exists in the original script.
programmes.countryNote: Entry for a resit may be through the student's own school or through an external centre, and the entry fee is set by the centre rather than by any tutoring provider. Ask the centre in writing, and ask specifically about 0680 rather than about IGCSEs in general, because availability by syllabus varies between Dubai centres.

programmes.name: Sixth form and Diploma routes
programmes.description: Where the return on 0680 spending shows. The subject feeds AS and A Level Geography, Environmental Management where a school offers it, and IB Environmental Systems and Societies or Geography. Dubai market rates for post-16 support sit above IGCSE rates, so technique bought at fifteen displaces dearer remediation at seventeen.
programmes.countryNote: Not every Dubai school that teaches 0680 continues it after Year 11, and provision varies considerably between sixth forms in the emirate. Confirm in writing with the specific school which post-16 options a 0680 grade actually feeds before locking option choices, rather than assuming continuity.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-environmental-mana.subjectsIntro: Supply depth differs enormously by subject in Dubai, and supply is what sets a rate. Here is who actually teaches each of these subjects in the emirate and how easy it is to find them.

subjects.name: Environmental Management (0680)
subjects.description: Thin supply. Usually taught by a geographer or biologist carrying it as an additional subject, so a tutor strong on one half of the syllabus and weak on the other is the common case. Finding someone who has taught all ten topic areas and both papers is the constraint that drives the rate, not the difficulty of the content.

subjects.name: Geography (0460)
subjects.description: Reasonable supply across Dubai, concentrated in the Al Barsha and Jumeirah school corridor. The nearest adjacent subject to 0680 and the most common fallback when no 0680 specialist is free, though a geographer needs support on the ecological topics to cover the syllabus properly.

subjects.name: Biology (0610)
subjects.description: Deep supply and competitive rates, because every school has a biology department and many teachers tutor. A biologist covers 0680's ecosystems, population and pollution material well and typically needs preparation on rocks, minerals, energy generation and the atmosphere.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620)
subjects.description: Deep supply, similar rates to Biology. Relevant to 0680 pricing only as a comparison point: if a provider quotes the same figure for Chemistry and for 0680, ask what their 0680 tutor has actually taught, because the two markets do not have the same depth.

subjects.name: Physics (0625)
subjects.description: Good supply and the highest demand of the three sciences in Dubai. Useful for the energy topic specifically - efficiency, energy transfer, the real limits of solar and nuclear output - which a physicist explains more precisely than most geographers.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: The deepest supply and the lowest rates in the emirate. Worth engaging separately if a 0680 diagnosis points at arithmetic: percentage change from the wrong baseline and misread graph scales are cheaper to fix with a maths tutor than with a specialist charging the 0680 band.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (0654)
subjects.description: Widely taught in Dubai, so supply is adequate. Students on this route take 0680 as a third science option and come with broad but shallow foundations, which means more topic-building hours and fewer technique hours than a single-science student needs.

subjects.name: Global Perspectives (0457)
subjects.description: Thin supply, the same band as 0680 and for the same reason. Genuinely worth combining: the source-evaluation skill the 0457 written paper tests is the same reliability thinking a 0680 resource booklet rewards, so one tutor can cover both and the reading is bought once.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Reasonable supply, mid-band rates. Sharpens the cost reasoning in 0680 evaluation answers, where a student who understands opportunity cost argues far better about whether to build desalination capacity or to manage demand.

subjects.name: Travel and Tourism (0471)
subjects.description: Very thin supply in Dubai and quoted accordingly. Shares 0680's sustainability and coastal-management territory, and a student taking both can reuse UAE tourism-pressure case studies in either paper, which is a rare efficiency in a thin pair of subjects.

subjects.name: Development Studies and Sociology (0453 / 0495)
subjects.description: Thin supply, specialist band. Both sit close to 0680's population and sustainability material, and the research-methods content in Sociology trains the same scepticism about a data source that a resource booklet demands.

subjects.name: Arabic as a Foreign Language (0544)
subjects.description: Deep supply across Dubai at a wide range of rates. Relevant to any 0680 budget simply because KHDA requires Arabic in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, so it is rarely a subject a family can choose not to fund.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-environmental-mana.regionsIntro: This is where an in-home rate comes from. The teaching is identical everywhere; what varies is how much car sits inside the hour and whether any 0680 specialist is within reach at all.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Arabian Ranches 2
regions.note: Twenty-five to forty minutes from the Al Barsha tutor corridor outside peak, considerably more at 4.30pm. Villa families here see the widest spread between in-home and online quotes for the same calibre of tutor, and the fewest 0680 specialists inside a sensible radius.

regions.name: Town Square and Dubai South
regions.note: The far edge of most tutors' travel range. Some decline the journey outright and others add a surcharge that never appears as a line on the invoice. For a thin subject the practical answer here is often that no local 0680 specialist exists at any rate.

regions.name: Al Khawaneej and Mushrif
regions.note: A long eastern run from the school corridor, and awkward in both directions. Families here commonly end up with a generalist who covers five subjects rather than a 0680 specialist, because the specialist will not make the drive for one hour.

regions.name: Mudon and Remraam
regions.note: Dubailand communities with growing secondary cohorts and limited local tutoring supply. Online removes the travel surcharge entirely, which matters more here than almost anywhere else in the emirate for a subject with this little local provision.

regions.name: Al Barsha South and Dubai Hills
regions.note: Close to the deepest tutor supply in Dubai, so in-home rates here sit at the lower end of the published band. Even so, the choice is between a nearby generalist and a specialist who has taught both 0680 papers, and proximity does not resolve that.

regions.name: Jumeirah Park and Jumeirah Village Triangle
regions.note: Mid-range distances with unpredictable evening traffic around Al Khail. Shorter, more frequent sessions make sense for data-technique work, and a 45-minute online slot is economically sensible in a way a 45-minute visit never is.

regions.name: International City and Warsan
regions.note: Highly price-sensitive communities where the budget online band of AED 33 to 65 is marketed hardest. For 0680 specifically that band rarely contains anyone who has taught the syllabus, which makes the question of what a cheap hour contains especially worth asking here.

regions.name: Dubai Festival City and Ras Al Khor
regions.note: Central and reachable, with the protected wetland next door as a genuine 0680 case study. In-home supply is reasonable; the constraint is still whether the available tutor knows the oceans, fisheries and ecosystems half of the syllabus or only the physical half.

schoolClusters.city: Dubailand, Arabian Ranches and Motor City
schoolClusters.note: Community schools with young secondary cohorts and small Year 11 groups, which thins both class time for 0680 and the pool of local teachers who have taught it fully. Families we support in this cluster are the most consistent users of online delivery, because the in-home alternative often does not exist.
schools: Jumeirah English Speaking School Arabian Ranches

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha, Al Sufouh and Jumeirah
schoolClusters.note: The emirate's deepest tutoring supply and therefore its most competitive in-home pricing. Students we support here usually have good content knowledge from a full science department and come to us for Paper 2 resource-booklet technique rather than for topic coverage.

schoolClusters.city: Mirdif, Al Warqa and Dubai Festival City
schoolClusters.note: Large sibling groups and tight budgets, where cost per household matters more than cost per hour. Two children on alternating weekly online slots with the same tutor is a common and considerably cheaper structure than two separate in-home visits.

sections.heading: What the Dubai market charges for in-home 0680 support
paragraphs: Here are the published numbers, each attributed to the provider or rate table that published it, read in October 2026. For in-home one-to-one across Dubai, Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table gives AED 180 to 350 an hour, and independent home tutors in the emirate advertise up to AED 500. Monthly in-home packages are marketed at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. Online, Unitors quotes IGCSE tuition from AED 150, TutorChase publishes AED 270 for specialist support, Bestimate puts specialist exam-year support at AED 200 to 450 or more, and at the budget end Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end.

Set against each other, those figures say something specific rather than something vague. The in-home premium over a comparable online rate is roughly AED 50 to 150 an hour depending on where you live and how far the tutor travels. For a weekly session across an academic year that is a meaningful sum, and it buys physical presence rather than better teaching. A family should decide deliberately whether presence is the thing they need, because for a subject assessed by two written papers with no practical, it usually is not.

The table below is organised by format rather than by price band, and it includes the column no provider in this market publishes: what is actually inside the hour. An in-home hour contains the drive, recovered through the rate. A group class at a centre contains the pace of the group. A recorded course contains no marking at all. An online one-to-one hour contains teaching and, where the provider includes it, written feedback on the student's own script between sessions.

One figure on this page is ours rather than the market's, and it is not a price: zero. That is the number of home visits IB Gram makes anywhere across the Emirates. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and we would rather say so in the first screen of a page targeting this search than let a parent discover it after a consultation call.

sections.heading: The travel maths, community by community
paragraphs: Dubai geography decides the in-home premium far more than qualifications do. The tutoring supply in this city is concentrated in a corridor running roughly from Al Sufouh through Al Barsha to Dubai Hills, where most of the long-established British-curriculum secondaries sit and where most of the people who tutor their subjects live. The further a family is from that corridor, the more car is inside their hour.

From that corridor to Arabian Ranches is twenty-five to forty minutes outside peak and considerably worse at 4.30pm, when the school run and the first wave of office traffic overlap. To Town Square or Dubai South is longer again, and some tutors simply decline. To Al Khawaneej or Mushrif is an awkward eastern run in both directions. To International City and Warsan the distance is moderate but the demand is price-sensitive, so what gets offered locally is usually a generalist covering five subjects rather than a 0680 specialist.

There is a second, less visible cost to the drive: it shapes the timetable. An in-home slot must sit in the window a tutor can physically reach, which in practice means 4pm to 6pm on weekdays. That is exactly the window a Year 11 student is least able to use well, arriving from school, often straight from a co-curricular, with an hour of homework already waiting. An online slot can sit at 7.30pm, at 9am on a Saturday for longer resource-booklet work, or after Iftar during Ramadan when a shorter later session actually lands.

For families who do want someone in the room, the sensible version of that choice is to buy presence for the subjects that benefit from it and buy specialism for the ones that do not. A younger sibling who needs an adult at the table is a good use of an in-home hour. A sixteen-year-old whose Paper 2 technique is the problem is not, and paying the travel premium to get the wrong half of a syllabus taught is the worst outcome available.

sections.heading: Budgeting a 0680 plan by weakness rather than by hours
paragraphs: An hourly rate cannot answer the question a parent is actually asking, which is what this will cost in total. That depends on which fault the student has, and the faults in this subject are distinguishable enough to cost separately. The table below sets out the ones we see most, the session counts each typically takes, and an indicative AED range built by multiplying those sessions against the published specialist band of AED 200 to 450 an hour. The arithmetic is simple and the assumption is stated, which is more than this market generally offers.

Two of these faults are cheap and are usually fixed last. Arithmetic errors - percentage change from the wrong baseline, values read between gridlines, totals compared when the question asked about rates - cost a meaningful number of marks and take one or two sessions to drill out, and can often be addressed by a maths tutor at a lower rate than a 0680 specialist. Command-term discipline is the other: four marked papers with the term circled in every question changes behaviour, and it transfers to Geography, Biology and Economics at no extra cost.

The expensive fault is genuine topic absence, particularly when a student has taken 0680 standalone without Geography or Biology behind it and the entire physical half of the syllabus has to be built. That is eight to sixteen sessions, it cannot be compressed into three weeks, and a family arriving in April should be told so rather than sold a package that cannot deliver. We would rather have that conversation than take the booking.

One more line that belongs in a budget and rarely appears in one: the cost of doing nothing until February. The same number of hours bought in the peak weeks after the January mocks buys a narrower choice of tutor, because the few people in Dubai who have taught both 0680 papers are committed by then. The rate does not move much. What you can buy with it does.

sections.heading: Why there are so few 0680 teachers in Dubai at any price
paragraphs: Parents often read a high quote for a niche subject as opportunism. In this case it is arithmetic about supply. Dubai had 227 private schools serving 387,441 students in 2024-25 across 17 different curricula, and the great majority of the UK-curriculum schools among them run the mainstream IGCSEs. Every one of them has a maths department and a science department. Environmental Management is an option subject, not every school offers it, and where it is offered it is often one class taught by one teacher.

That arithmetic produces a teaching population measured in dozens rather than hundreds for the whole emirate, and only a fraction of those people tutor privately. Of the ones who do, many are comfortable with half the syllabus. A geographer carries water, hazards, population and development confidently and needs preparation on nutrient cycling, biodiversity and marine systems. A biologist is the mirror image. A tutor who has genuinely taught all ten topic areas across both papers is the scarce item, and scarcity is what the specialist band is pricing.

The consequence for a family hiring in-home is sharper than the rate suggests. Restricting the search to a twenty-minute radius does not just raise the price; in some Dubai communities it reduces the candidate pool to zero, and the family ends up hiring a general science tutor and hoping. We see the result of that regularly: a student who has had eight sessions on ecosystems and has never been shown how to work a resource booklet.

Being honest about this cuts both ways, and we will say the uncomfortable half too. There are weeks in the Dubai academic year when we cannot place a 0680 specialist either, particularly in the squeeze between the January mocks and the end of Term 2. When that happens we give you a date, or we offer a tutor who covers the half of the syllabus your child needs and we name the half they do not. No competitor in this market discloses a coverage limit. It is the single piece of information a parent most needs and least often gets.

sections.heading: The costs around 0680 that nobody quotes you
paragraphs: Tutoring is rarely the only line item, and the others are worth knowing before a budget is set. The largest context figure is school fees, and for 2026-27 it is fixed: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there will be no increase in school fees for private schools in Dubai for the coming academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion of AED 2.5 billion in total. Against a term's fees, a four-session technique block is a small item and a term of weekly support is not.

Exam entry is the cost families most often discover late. If a student is entered through their own school, the fee usually sits inside the school's charges. If they are entering as a private candidate - for a resit, or because their school does not offer 0680 - the entry fee is set by the exam centre, varies between centres, and is not something a tutoring provider should be quoting. Ask the centre directly, in writing, and ask about 0680 by name rather than about IGCSEs in general.

There is a related expense with no invoice: the cost of a wrong series. Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the centre's zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. A family revising to a timetable downloaded from a search result rather than confirmed by their school is risking the entry fee and the year.

Finally, the costs that should not exist. No tutoring provider should be charging for a syllabus document, a past paper or a mark scheme; those are Cambridge's copyright material and the official route runs through the school's exams officer. Nobody should be charging for an equivalency or attestation service they do not perform - the Ministry of Education's processes are the Ministry's, and a tutoring company describing them is not conducting them. And nothing should be sold on the basis of a promised grade, which no tutor can deliver.

sections.heading: Two students, one session: when sharing a 0680 hour works
paragraphs: Splitting a session is the most effective way for a Dubai family to cut the cost per child, and it works for some 0680 work and fails for other parts of it. Worth setting out honestly, because the providers who sell shared sessions rarely explain where the value goes.

It works well for Paper 2 technique. Two students at a similar standard working the same resource booklet produce a better session than one student would, because describing a trend out loud and hearing another attempt at the same question is genuinely useful, and the marking review benefits from comparing two scripts against the same criterion. Cost per family roughly halves and the teaching does not degrade. Pairs of siblings in the same year group, or two classmates, are the natural case.

It works badly for topic repair, because the whole point of topic repair is that the gap is specific to the student. One child needs oceans and fisheries built from nothing; the other needs rocks and minerals. An hour split between those two requests gives each child half a session at full attention and the price saving is not real. We will say that rather than take the booking and let the family discover it in week three.

The structure that works best for larger Dubai households is not sharing at all but alternating. Two children on the same weekly online slot in alternate weeks, with the same tutor, costs the same as one child's weekly support, keeps both diagnoses separate, and halves the household's total compared with two in-home visits. It is less tidy than a group package and it is usually better value, and for families in Mirdif or Al Warqa with three children in secondary school it is the arrangement we recommend most often.

sections.heading: What changes about safeguarding when the tutor is not in your house
paragraphs: This is a cost in a different currency and it belongs in a page about hiring a home tutor. Inviting an adult into your home to work alone with a teenager is a decision with a safeguarding dimension that nobody in this market discusses, and so is the alternative. Both deserve stating plainly rather than being left as an unspoken preference.

For an in-home arrangement, the questions worth asking are concrete: who is this person, what checks exist on them, who else knows the session is happening, and is there an adult elsewhere in the home. The regulatory backdrop is relevant too. Individuals providing private tutoring in the UAE need a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, and the permit carries a code of conduct. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for school staff additionally bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students at their own school, which is worth knowing as a general direction even though it is an Abu Dhabi rule and should be verified against the current ADEK policy document.

For an online arrangement, the shape of the risk is different and the mitigations are more available. Sessions happen on a platform rather than in a private room, a parent can be in earshot without being in the room, the tutor and student are never alone in a physical space, and there is a record of when sessions happened. What a family should ask instead is about data: what personal information about their child is collected, why, how long it is kept, and how to have it deleted. UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection sits behind those questions, and a lead form that asks for a child's school, grades and photograph without stating a purpose is a reasonable thing to refuse to complete.

Our own position: we collect what is needed to match a tutor and run a session, we keep a privacy link on every page, and we do not ask for a child's photograph. Sessions are one-to-one over live video and we are explicit that no adult is dispatched to a UAE address. That is not presented as a safeguarding product; it is simply the honest description of a format whose risk profile differs from the one this search term implies.

sections.heading: What we will not do at any price
paragraphs: A page about cost should be clear about what is not for sale, because several things that are sold in this search result should not be. The first is a grade. No tutor can promise one, and any provider offering a certain 7, a promised grade improvement or money back linked to a result is making a claim they cannot stand behind. The softer version is a statistic with no sample, date or method behind it, and it deserves the same scepticism.

The second is borrowed authority. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. We hold no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or the IB, and we operate no centre or office in the UAE. A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a specific thing issued to institutes with physical premises, and any provider attaching a regulator's name to itself as an endorsement is making a claim worth checking.

The third is exam material. Cambridge past papers, mark schemes and syllabus documents are copyright, and we do not reproduce or distribute them at any price. The official route runs through your child's school and its exams officer. In sessions we teach against what the student legitimately holds and build equivalent data questions from published sources - UAE water, energy and population statistics are ideal for this - when fresh material is needed.

The fourth is the arrangement families sometimes ask for directly: your child's own classroom teacher, hired privately. It is the wrong arrangement on principle, the MoHRE permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for school staff prohibit it outright for teachers in that emirate. We will not broker it. What we will do is match a tutor who has taught the syllabus, show you the published market bands, quote in AED with the inclusions written down, and tell you when the specialist you need is not free this week.

process.title: Say where you are and what you were quoted
process.description: The community and any in-home figure you have been offered. We will tell you what the published bands say for that format and whether the premium you are being asked for is travel, scarcity or neither, before we talk about our own sessions at all.

process.title: Send a marked script, not a description

faqs.question: How much does a Cambridge IGCSE Environmental Management 0680 home tutor cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published in-home one-to-one rates in Dubai run from AED 180 to 350 an hour in Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table, with independent home tutors advertising up to AED 500, and monthly in-home packages marketed at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. For 0680 specifically expect the upper half of those bands, because the emirate's teaching population in this subject is small. IB Gram does not sell home visits in the UAE; our equivalent online one-to-one sits in the published AED 150 to 450 range depending on whether you need a generalist or a full-syllabus specialist.

faqs.question: Why is an in-home 0680 hour more expensive than an online one?
faqs.answer: Because the hour contains a drive. A tutor reaching a villa in Arabian Ranches or Town Square at 4.30pm spends fifty to ninety minutes in a car for sixty minutes of teaching, and that unpaid time is recovered through the rate. The premium over a comparable online figure runs roughly AED 50 to 150 an hour depending on distance. What it buys is physical presence, not better teaching. For a subject assessed by two written papers with no practical and no coursework, presence is rarely the thing that was missing.

faqs.question: Which Dubai communities have no 0680 specialist within reach?
faqs.answer: Tutoring supply in this city clusters between Al Sufouh, Al Barsha and Dubai Hills, where most of the long-established British-curriculum secondaries sit. Town Square, Dubai South, Al Khawaneej, Mushrif, Mudon and Remraam are all far enough from that corridor that many tutors decline the journey outright for a single hour. For a thin subject like Environmental Management that frequently means the candidate pool within a twenty-minute radius is zero, and the family ends up hiring a general science tutor rather than someone who has taught the syllabus.

faqs.question: Is a monthly in-home 0680 package at AED 1,599 good value?
faqs.answer: It depends on what else is in it. Advertised Dubai in-home packages at AED 1,599 to 1,799 typically cover four two-hour sessions a month, which is eight teaching hours and four round trips. Per hour that is competitive against the top of the in-home band. The things to check before committing are whether unused sessions expire, whether the package renews automatically, whether the two-hour block suits a Year 11 student arriving from school, and whether the tutor has taught both 0680 papers or only the half of the syllabus their own subject covers.

faqs.question: How many sessions will my child need for 0680, and what will that total cost?
faqs.answer: It depends on the fault, which is why we diagnose before quoting. Arithmetic on data questions is one or two sessions. Command-term discipline is three or four. Paper 2 procedure is four to six. One weak third of the syllabus is five to eight. The whole physical half missing is eight to sixteen across a term. Priced against the published specialist band of AED 200 to 450 an hour, that runs from roughly AED 400 for the narrowest fix to AED 7,200 for a full rebuild. Send a marked script and you get the session count in writing.

faqs.question: Can we split a 0680 session between two children to halve the cost?
faqs.answer: For Paper 2 technique, yes, and it often improves the session: two students working the same resource booklet learn from hearing each other describe a trend, and comparing two scripts against one criterion is genuinely useful. For topic repair it fails, because one child needs oceans and fisheries built from nothing and the other needs rocks and minerals, so each gets half a session and the saving is not real. For most Dubai households with two secondary children, alternating weekly slots with the same tutor is better value than sharing an hour.

faqs.question: Does a lower hourly rate mean the 0680 tutor has no MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: No, and this is widely misunderstood. The MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, so it adds nothing to a tutor's costs and cannot be inferred from a rate in either direction. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific figure circulating online as unverified. Ask the permit question separately from the price question, and ask it directly.

faqs.question: What should I ask before letting a tutor into our villa in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Concrete things: who the person is, what checks exist on them, whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, who else knows the session is happening, and whether another adult will be elsewhere in the home. Avoid the arrangement families sometimes seek deliberately - your child's own classroom teacher, hired privately - because the MoHRE permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules prohibit it for school staff in that emirate. IB Gram does not place tutors in UAE homes at all.

faqs.question: What personal data do you collect about my child for 0680 tutoring?
faqs.answer: What a match and a session need: the year group, the school, the syllabus, the specific difficulty, and a contact for the parent. We do not ask for a child's photograph, and we keep a privacy link on every page explaining what is held and how to have it removed. UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection is the backdrop here, and the practical advice we would give about any provider, including us, is to decline a lead form that asks for a child's grades, school and photograph without stating why it needs them.

faqs.question: Do 0680 rates in Dubai rise before the Cambridge exam series?
faqs.answer: The headline figure usually holds; availability is what changes, and in a thin subject that has the same practical effect. Dubai schools cluster mock examinations in January, and Year 11 demand across the emirate peaks immediately afterwards. By February the handful of people in this city who have taught both 0680 papers are committed, so the family buying then pays the specialist band for whoever remains. Booking in Term 1 costs the same per hour and gets a materially better match, which is the strongest financial argument for not waiting.

faqs.question: What does 0680 exam entry cost if my child sits it as a private candidate?
faqs.answer: The entry fee is set by the exam centre rather than by Cambridge or by any tutoring provider, and it varies between centres in Dubai, so we will not quote a figure. Contact centres directly, in writing, and ask specifically about 0680 rather than about IGCSEs generally, because what each centre accepts by syllabus differs. One related point worth confirming at the same time: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and the correct zone timetable is the one your child must revise to.

faqs.question: Is 0680 tutoring worth the money if my child is already predicted a grade 6?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and for a specific reason. The gap between a 6 and an 8 in this subject is usually Paper 2 procedure and evaluation structure rather than content, and those are the cheapest faults on the syllabus to fix - four to six sessions and two to three sessions respectively. A student predicted a 6 who knows the topics is the best-value case in 0680 tutoring. A student who is missing half the syllabus in April is the worst, and we will tell you that rather than sell a block that cannot deliver.

faqs.question: Will you sell us Cambridge 0680 past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No, at any price. Cambridge holds the copyright on past papers, mark schemes and syllabus documents, and distributing them is not ours to do. The official route is through your child's school and its exams officer, and the current syllabus lives on cambridgeinternational.org. In sessions we teach against the material the student legitimately holds, and where new material is needed we build equivalent data questions from published sources such as UAE water, energy and population statistics. A question the student has not seen before is the only honest test of the Paper 2 skill anyway.

faqs.question: How does 0680 tutoring spend compare with Dubai school fees?
faqs.answer: A four-session technique block at the published specialist band is a small fraction of a term's fees; a term of weekly support is not, and deserves a harder question about whether this is the subject that most needs the money. One fixed point helps the 2026-27 sum: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai will not increase for the academic year, under the emirate's AED 1.5 billion economic incentives package. Before spending, ask the school what 0680 intervention it already runs inside those fees.

intro.heading: The structure of a 0680 plan decides the bill more than the hourly rate does
paragraphs: Two Dubai families can pay the same hourly figure for 0680 support and spend wildly different totals, because the unit they bought was different. One takes a 45-minute slot weekly for three terms. One takes four 90-minute blocks in the month before the paper. One signs a monthly package of eight sessions and uses five. The rate is almost irrelevant to the outcome of those three decisions, and yet the rate is the only number most providers will discuss.

This page is about the other variables. What a 45-minute session is good for and what it cannot do. Why 90 minutes is better value for resource-booklet work and worse value for definition drilling. What a twelve-week paced plan actually costs laid out week by week. What a November resit costs against a June first attempt. And what should be on the invoice, because an agreement with no written scope is where the disputes in this market live.

The market figures used throughout are published ones, attributed, read in October 2026. Unitors quotes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. TutorChase publishes AED 270 for specialist support. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts specialist exam-year support at AED 200 to 450 or more, and its monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. Monthly online packages are advertised from around AED 799 for eight sessions. Tutopiya starts at AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik at AED 45 to 65; BartyED publishes AED 650.

A word on why this matters more for 0680 than for most subjects. The qualification is two written papers with no coursework and no practical, and the half that decides grades is a resource booklet of unseen data. That is skill work, and skill work responds to spaced repetition rather than to volume. Eight sessions spread across twelve weeks move a Paper 2 grade more than eight sessions crammed into three, at identical cost. Structure is not administrative detail here; it is most of the value.

Delivery, stated plainly before any figures: IB Gram teaches one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and home visits are a service we run only in India. For this syllabus that suits the work, because annotating a graph together on a shared screen is the core activity and a shared screen does it better than a shared printout. It also means the tutor is chosen for having taught both 0680 papers rather than for living within driving distance of your community, which in a subject this thinly staffed across the emirate is the difference between a specialist and a general science teacher reading the syllabus a week ahead of your child.

programmes.name: Paced plan across a term
programmes.description: Weekly sessions over ten to fourteen weeks, which is the structure that suits a skill-led syllabus. Spaced practice on data questions beats concentrated practice at the same cost, because the habit of reading a value with its unit has to survive a week of not doing it. This is the cheapest route to a Paper 2 improvement and the least popular.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai school terms and the January mock window make the autumn term the natural home for a paced plan. Booking then also sidesteps the February squeeze, when every Year 11 cohort in the emirate wants the same scarce 0680 specialists and availability rather than price becomes the binding constraint.

programmes.description: Four to six sessions in the final six weeks, usually 90 minutes each, aimed squarely at Paper 2 procedure and the high-tariff evaluation items. programmes.countryNote: Across the emirate this is what most 0680 spending looks like, concentrated between the January mocks and the series. A family in this position should ask any provider directly what can realistically be achieved in the time, and treat an answer that promises everything as a reason to look elsewhere.

programmes.description: The cheapest tutoring in this subject per mark gained, because the diagnosis already exists.
