intro.heading: Price first, because that is what you came for
paragraphs: A Cambridge IGCSE Geography 0460 home tutor in Dubai is quoted at somewhere between AED 45 and AED 650 an hour, and the spread is not noise. It is five different products wearing the same job title. At the bottom sit undergraduates who studied geography and are revising it alongside your child. In the middle sit qualified subject teachers charging AED 150 to AED 300 for an online hour, which is the band Unitors publishes for IGCSE work. Above that sit exam-year specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and beyond, where TutorChase lists AED 270. At the top, BartyED quotes AED 650 for a named premium tutor. None of those numbers is ours, and none of them should be read as a price list. They are what this market publishes, and a parent who knows the bands cannot be sold the wrong tier.

The single largest lever on that number is not the teacher's degree. It is travel. A visiting tutor who drives from Al Barsha to Dubai Hills for a 4pm session loses an hour to the road, and that hour is inside the quote whether the invoice itemises it or not. Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to AED 350 and home-tutor listings reach AED 500, against AED 150 to AED 300 for the same qualification delivered online. The gap is roughly the cost of a car in Dubai traffic between four and six in the evening.

That is why IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Geography 0460 lessons for Dubai families run one-to-one over live video, with the map extract on a shared screen and the student annotating it while the teacher watches. The practical consequence is that the pool of available teachers is no longer bounded by a twenty-minute drive from your villa. A family in Mudon can work with someone who has taught the hot desert and tropical rainforest case studies to five successive cohorts, rather than whoever happens to live on the same side of Al Qudra Road.

The second lever is which part of 0460 you are buying. The three components are priced very differently in practice, because they cost different amounts of a teacher's time. Paper 1 carries 45% of the grade across three 25-mark theme questions and needs sustained content teaching over months. Paper 2 is a 60-mark skills paper worth 27.5%, and it is the cheapest paper in the syllabus to repair because map skills are procedural: grid references, gradient, cross-sections and photograph interpretation can be drilled to competence in a handful of sessions. Coursework supervision under Paper 3 is the most expensive hour you will buy, because reading a 2,000-word draft properly takes longer than the lesson does.

The third lever is when you buy. Demand in Dubai spikes twice: in the weeks after the Year 11 mock results land, and again once the Cambridge entry deadline has passed and families realise the series is real. Booking in September for a June series costs the same per hour as booking in March, but it buys thirty sessions instead of eight, and the hourly rate stops being the interesting number. The sections below take each of these levers in turn, with the figures and the sources attached.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-geography-0460-hom.programmesIntro: Geography does not start at IGCSE and it does not stop there. These are the three stages Dubai families ask about around 0460, and what each one costs in teaching time rather than in marketing language.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary Geography, before 0460
programmes.description: The three years that decide whether 0460 feels like a new subject or a continuation. Lower Secondary geography builds map reading, graph construction and the habit of explaining a pattern rather than listing it. A student who arrives in Year 10 able to read a contour map and write a two-step explanation starts 0460 with a working advantage worth several months.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai complicates this because families move schools and curricula mid-stage. A child who did Years 7 and 8 on an American middle-school programme and then joins a Cambridge school in Year 9 has usually never met a 1:25,000 topographical map. That gap is cheap to close at thirteen and expensive to close in the February of Year 11, which is the main argument for buying hours early rather than many.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Geography 0460, first year
programmes.description: Most Dubai schools teach Theme 1 Population and settlement and part of Theme 2 The natural environment in Year 10, and this is where the case-study bank is built. The 7-mark part of every Paper 1 question is marked in levels of response and needs named, located, dated examples. A student who collects those examples as they go spends Year 11 practising answers rather than scrambling for content.
programmes.countryNote: Year 10 is also when the Paper 3 and Paper 4 decision becomes visible. Dubai schools split on this: some enter candidates for the coursework route and build fieldwork into a term, others enter for Paper 4 and teach fieldwork technique in a classroom. Ask the head of geography which route your child's cohort is entered for before you buy any tutoring hours, because the two routes need different work.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Geography 0460, exam year
programmes.description: Theme 3 Economic development, the whole of the skills paper, and the coursework or alternative paper all land in the same year as mocks. The hour rate matters least here and the sequence matters most: skills paper first because it moves fastest, then the weakest theme, then timed full papers. Most families who start in Year 11 buy between twenty and thirty-five sessions.
programmes.countryNote: The Dubai school calendar puts mocks in the winter window and the Cambridge June series in the summer term, with the entry deadline months before either. Cambridge's published key dates for its March series show the pattern clearly: final entries close on 27 November 2026 for an exam period that begins on 3 February 2027. UAE centres sit the June and November series, and their deadlines sit just as far ahead.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level Geography 9696, after 0460
programmes.description: The step up is in the writing, not the content. AS and A Level geography asks for extended evaluative essays, independent research and statistical treatment of data, and it assumes the physical geography from 0460 is secure. Students who scraped a 0460 grade on memorised case studies find the first AS term difficult in a way that nothing at IGCSE predicted.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools run 9696 alongside IB Diploma geography, and the choice between them is usually a timetable question rather than an academic one. A 0460 student aiming at geography, environmental science or urban planning at a UAE or UK university benefits from being told, in Year 11, which of the two routes their school actually staffs well.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-geography-0460-hom.subjectsIntro: 0460 is not one subject. It is three themes and a skills paper, each with its own failure mode. These are the syllabus units a Dubai family actually books hours against, with what each one assesses and where the marks go missing.

subjects.name: Population dynamics and migration
subjects.description: Birth and death rates, the demographic transition model, push and pull factors, and the difference between a refugee and an economic migrant. Marks go on candidates describing a graph when the command word asked them to explain it, and on case studies with no country attached.

subjects.name: Population structure and density
subjects.description: Reading and drawing population pyramids, dependency ratios, and explaining why people are distributed as they are. This unit appears on both papers: as a 25-mark theme question and as a graph-completion task on the skills paper, so it repays double attention.

subjects.name: Settlements, service provision and urbanisation
subjects.description: Settlement hierarchy, sphere of influence, land-use models, and the causes and consequences of rapid urban growth. Dubai students have the best possible local example and over-use it: an answer needs a named contrasting case from a lower-income country as well.

subjects.name: Earthquakes, volcanoes and plate margins
subjects.description: Plate boundary types, hazard impacts, prediction and management, and why people continue to live in hazardous places. The common loss is explaining a hazard's effects without distinguishing primary from secondary, or management before an event from response after it.

subjects.name: Rivers and coasts
subjects.description: Drainage basin processes, erosion and deposition landforms, flooding and coastal management. Landform diagrams are worth marks on their own and most candidates draw them badly: labelled process arrows and a named example recover marks that content revision alone will not.

subjects.name: Weather, climate and natural vegetation
subjects.description: Instruments and measurement, climate graphs, and the tropical rainforest and hot desert ecosystems. The hot desert is on the doorstep, which helps with adaptation and soil, and hurts when candidates describe Dubai's irrigated landscaping as natural vegetation.

subjects.name: Development and inequality
subjects.description: Indicators of development, the limitations of GNI per head, the informal sector, and inequality within countries. Examiners reward candidates who can say why a single indicator misleads; they do not reward lists of indicators with no evaluation attached.

subjects.name: Food production, industry and tourism
subjects.description: Farming systems and food shortages, industrial systems and location factors, and the growth and management of tourism. Each needs one developed case study, located and dated. Three vague examples score less than one that names a place and a figure.

subjects.name: Energy, water and environmental risk
subjects.description: Energy supply and demand, water sources and shortages, and the environmental risks of economic development. Desalination and water security are directly relevant to the UAE, which makes this one of the few units where a Dubai student has genuinely better evidence than a candidate in Surrey.

subjects.name: Geographical skills
subjects.description: Topographical map interpretation at 1:25,000, grid references, distance and bearing, gradient and cross-sections, photograph and sketch interpretation, and graph and table work. Entirely procedural, entirely teachable, and the fastest component in the syllabus to move upwards.

subjects.name: Fieldwork and the coursework route
subjects.description: A single piece of fieldwork written up to a 2,000-word limit and marked out of 60. The assignment must be the student's own work throughout; a tutor's role is to question the hypothesis, probe the method and give feedback on what the student has already produced.

subjects.name: Alternative to coursework technique
subjects.description: A written paper that tests fieldwork understanding without fieldwork: hypothesis design, sampling, data-collection methods, presentation choices and evaluation of reliability. Candidates who have never collected data in the field struggle most with the evaluation questions at the end.

sections.heading: Six things that move a 0460 quote in this emirate
paragraphs: Two Dubai families can be quoted AED 180 and AED 420 for the same subject in the same week without either tutor being dishonest. The variables are predictable, and knowing them is the difference between negotiating and guessing.

The first is the tier of teacher, which the table above already covers. The second is which component you are buying. A Paper 2 skills block is cheap per mark gained because the content is procedural. Coursework supervision under Paper 3 is the most expensive hour in the syllabus, because reading a 2,000-word draft, checking the data presentation and writing usable feedback takes longer than the session it feeds. Any tutor quoting the same rate for both is either underpricing the coursework or overpricing the skills work.

The third is how close you are to the series. The fourth is session length: a ninety-minute slot often costs less per minute than sixty, because the teacher's preparation and admin are fixed. The fifth is siblings. Two children in the same household studying 0460 in the same year can share a slot, which halves the cost per child, but only if they are genuinely at a similar point in the syllabus; a Year 10 and a Year 11 sharing a session wastes both hours. The sixth is continuity. Buying a block of ten and keeping the same teacher costs less in real terms than buying ten single hours from whoever is free, because nobody is paid to re-diagnose the same student three times.

Underneath all six sits one number nobody quotes: hours to the exam. A family starting in September has thirty sessions available at any rate they choose. A family starting in April has eight, and at that point the hourly rate is close to irrelevant compared with how precisely those eight hours are aimed.

sections.heading: Travel time is the line item nobody itemises
paragraphs: Dubai's geography is the reason in-home tutoring costs what it does here. The city is long, the school run and the evening commute overlap between four and six, and a 0460 session at 4.30pm sits precisely in the worst window. A tutor who accepts a one-hour booking across the city is committing closer to two and a half hours of their working day, and no sustainable business absorbs that for free.

The arithmetic is simple enough to do yourself. Take the in-home quote, work out the round-trip drive at the hour your child would actually be taught, and ask what the effective teaching rate is. A tutor charging AED 350 for a one-hour visit with a ninety-minute round trip is charging AED 140 per hour of their time, which is below the market rate for an online specialist. That is why the better in-home tutors in Dubai either charge near AED 500 or decline to cross the city at all, and why the cheaper ones tend to be the ones who live nearby rather than the ones who know the syllabus.

There is one honest advantage to a visit that online delivery does not replicate: a tutor in the room can confiscate the phone. For a thirteen-year-old with no study habits that matters. For a Year 11 candidate working on levels-of-response answers and map interpretation, a shared screen with both parties annotating the same extract is a closer substitute than most parents expect, and the saved hour goes back into the week.

sections.heading: Paper 1 carries 45%, so it carries most of the budget
paragraphs: Paper 1 is one hour forty-five minutes, 75 marks and 45% of the Cambridge IGCSE Geography 0460 grade. Candidates answer three questions, one from each of the three themes: Population and settlement, The natural environment, and Economic development. Each question is worth 25 marks and is built the same way, which is the single most useful structural fact a 0460 student can know.

The early parts of each question are resource-based and short. They hand the candidate a map, a graph or a photograph and ask them to identify, describe or give reasons. These marks are available to anyone who reads the resource carefully and uses the command word they were given. The later parts move away from the resource and into content, and the final part of each question is a levels-of-response answer worth seven marks that requires a named, located case study. That 7-mark part, three times over, is 21 of the 75 marks on the paper.

Where the money goes in Paper 1 teaching is the case-study bank. A student who has nine developed examples, one for each major unit, with a place name, a date and two or three figures attached, is in a different position from a student who has read three textbook chapters. Building that bank takes months of small increments, which is why a September start is worth more than an identical number of hours bought in April. The second cost centre is command words: describe, explain, suggest and give reasons ask for different things, and a candidate who explains when asked to describe has wasted a correct answer.

The practical teaching sequence that works for Dubai students is to diagnose which of the three themes is weakest from the mock script, repair that theme to a working case-study standard, then run timed 25-mark questions on all three in rotation. It is unglamorous and it is where the 45% actually moves.

sections.heading: Paper 2 is the cheapest 27.5% in the syllabus
paragraphs: Paper 2 is one hour thirty minutes, 60 marks and 27.5% of the grade, and every question is compulsory. It tests geographical skills: interpreting a 1:25,000 topographical map, four and six-figure grid references, measuring distance and bearing, calculating gradient, constructing and reading a cross-section, interpreting photographs and sketches, and completing graphs and tables.

That list is entirely procedural, and procedural skills respond to drilling in a way that case-study knowledge does not. A student who cannot read a six-figure grid reference on Monday can read one reliably by Friday. A student who has never drawn a cross-section can learn the method in a single session and then needs three or four repetitions to make it automatic. Measured in marks gained per AED spent, Paper 2 is the best-value component in 0460 and it is consistently the least practised, because it does not look like revision and there is no chapter to read.

The failure pattern is identifiable from a mock script in about five minutes. Candidates lose marks for giving grid references in the wrong order, for measuring distance along a straight line when the question asked for a road, for reading contour values from the wrong interval, and for describing a photograph instead of interpreting it. None of those is a knowledge gap. All of them are habits, and habits are what one-to-one teaching with a shared screen is best at correcting, because the teacher sees the error being made rather than reading the result.

For a family on a tight budget with a weak overall Geography grade, a block of six to eight sessions aimed only at Paper 2 is usually the most defensible purchase available. It will not fix a candidate who knows no content, but it reliably recovers marks that were being thrown away for no good reason.

sections.heading: Paper 3 coursework or Paper 4 alternative: the choice that changes your bill
paragraphs: The last 27.5% of 0460 comes one of two ways, and your child's school has already chosen which. Paper 3 is coursework: one piece of fieldwork written up to a limit of 2,000 words and marked out of 60. Paper 4 is the Alternative to Coursework, a one-hour-thirty-minute written paper also worth 60 marks, which tests fieldwork understanding without requiring fieldwork. Find out which route the cohort is entered for before you buy a single hour, because support for the two looks nothing alike.

If your child is on the coursework route, the expensive part is reading. A tutor supporting a 2,000-word fieldwork report spends more time outside the session than inside it: checking whether the hypothesis is testable, whether the sampling method matches the question, whether the data presentation earns its space, and whether the conclusion answers what was asked. The assignment must be the student's own work from first word to last. A tutor may ask why a graph was chosen, point out that a conclusion does not follow from the data, and explain what the mark criteria reward. A tutor who offers to produce assessed work is offering the student a malpractice finding, and no grade is worth that.

If your child is on Paper 4, the work is different and cheaper. The paper asks about hypothesis design, sampling strategy, data-collection instruments, presentation choices and the evaluation of reliability and limitations. Students who have never collected field data struggle hardest on the evaluation questions at the end, because they have no experience of a method going wrong. That is fixable in teaching: walk through a flawed method, ask what it would actually produce, and the evaluation answers start to write themselves.

Either way, this component is the one where families most often discover in March that nobody has done anything. Both routes have internal school deadlines that sit well before the Cambridge series, and the school sets them, not Cambridge.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in the context of a Dubai school-fee budget
paragraphs: Tutoring in Dubai is bought against a school fee that is already the largest line in most family budgets, and the useful question is not whether AED 250 an hour is a lot. It is what proportion of the year's education spend it represents and what it is displacing.

The context is unusually favourable at the moment. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the second of Dubai's economic incentives packages. The market itself is large and growing: Dubai's private school sector served 387,441 students across 227 schools offering 17 curricula in 2024-25, with UK-curriculum schools accounting for 37% of enrolment, and the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools and 16,846 places. A frozen fee and a growing supply of schools are the background against which a tutoring decision is made.

Against that, a single 0460 subject at one session a week for a year sits in the AED 600 to AED 1,200 a month band that Bestimate publishes for mid-tier weekly tutoring, rising to AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support at two sessions a week. Monthly packages advertised in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. The right comparison is not tutoring against nothing; it is tutoring against a resit entry, a dropped option subject, or a sixth-form application made with a grade that closes doors.

sections.heading: Permits, honesty and what you are actually paying for
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated, not grey. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories are wide: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. The MoHRE service is listed as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the ministry's smart app, website and e-services system, with a two-working-day completion time and no fee shown.

Two consequences for a parent. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; the ministry has not published a fine schedule, so any page quoting you a specific figure is inventing it. And because the permit is free and quick, a tutor who cannot tell you whether they hold one is telling you something about how they run their work. Ask. It is a reasonable question and it costs nothing to answer.

There is a second boundary worth knowing. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction. The practical reading across the UAE is that your child's own class teacher is the wrong person to hire privately, however convenient it looks. A separate, properly permitted teacher who does not mark your child's school work is a cleaner arrangement for everyone.

A third boundary is ours rather than a regulator's. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge International or Pearson, and any tutoring page that tells you otherwise should be read carefully. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific instrument issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai. We teach online and we are not one. What you are buying is a qualified teacher's hours, the student's own work marked honestly, and a clear statement of what we will not do.

At each point we re-rank the three themes and the skills paper by marks available, and move the hours to where they are worth most. faqs.question: How much does a Cambridge IGCSE Geography 0460 home tutor cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The Dubai market advertises roughly AED 45 to AED 650 an hour, and the band that matters for most families is AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject teacher online, or AED 180 to AED 500 for an in-home visit where travel sits inside the price. Unitors publishes IGCSE rates from AED 150, TutorChase lists AED 270, Bestimate's Dubai table puts in-home visits at AED 180 to AED 350, and BartyED quotes AED 650 at the premium end. Those are their published figures, read in October 2026, not ours. IB Gram teaches 0460 one-to-one online and starts with a free trial lesson rather than a quote.

faqs.question: Why is an online 0460 session cheaper than a home visit in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Because a visit buys the tutor's travel as well as their teaching. A cross-city trip in the 4pm to 6pm window costs between fifty and a hundred and twenty minutes of a tutor's day, and that time is inside the quote whether or not the invoice shows it. A tutor charging AED 350 for a one-hour visit with a ninety-minute round trip is earning about AED 140 per hour of their working time, which is below the online specialist rate. Remove the drive and the same qualification costs less, or the same money buys two sessions instead of one.

faqs.question: Does a 0460 tutor charge more for Paper 3 coursework supervision?
faqs.answer: Usually, and with good reason. Supporting a 2,000-word fieldwork report means reading it properly between sessions, checking the hypothesis is testable, the sampling matches the question and the data presentation earns its space, then writing feedback the student can act on. That work happens outside the billed hour. A tutor quoting the same rate for coursework support as for map-skills drilling is either underpricing one or overpricing the other. Ask how the draft-reading time is charged before the block starts, so the first invoice is not a surprise.

faqs.question: How many 0460 sessions does a Year 11 student in Dubai usually need?
faqs.answer: It depends far more on the starting point than on the subject. A candidate sitting around the middle of the grade range with a specific weakness, such as the skills paper or one weak theme, often moves on a block of six to ten sessions. A candidate who has fallen behind across all three themes and the skills paper is realistically looking at twenty to thirty-five sessions across the exam year. The variable that matters most is how many weeks remain. Thirty hours spread from September does more than thirty hours compressed into April, at exactly the same cost.

faqs.question: Is Paper 2 map skills cheaper to fix than Paper 1 case studies?
faqs.answer: Yes, and by a wide margin. Paper 2 is worth 27.5% of the grade and tests procedures: grid references, distance and bearing, gradient, cross-sections, photograph interpretation, graph completion. Procedures respond to drilling, so six to eight focused sessions can move the component substantially. Paper 1 carries 45% but rests on a bank of named, located case studies that takes months to build. For a family with a limited budget and a weak overall grade, a Paper 2 block is usually the most defensible purchase, and it is the component almost nobody practises at home.

faqs.question: Do 0460 tutoring rates in Dubai rise closer to the June series?
faqs.answer: The published hourly bands do not change much, but availability does, and availability is what you are really buying. Demand rises sharply after the Year 11 mock results and again once the Cambridge entry deadline passes. By the spring term the specialists with a free 4.30pm slot are the ones nobody booked, and families end up paying the exam-year band of AED 200 to AED 450 rather than the standard band simply because that is who is left. Booking in September costs the same per hour and buys roughly four times the hours.

faqs.question: Can two children in the same Dubai household share a 0460 session?
faqs.answer: If they are genuinely at the same point in the syllabus, yes, and it roughly halves the cost per child. Two Year 11 candidates in the same set, working on the same theme and the same question types, can be taught together productively. A Year 10 and a Year 11 cannot: one of them spends the hour watching. The honest test is whether the same marked past-paper question would be useful to both. If the answer is no, two shorter separate sessions beat one shared hour, even though the invoice looks worse.

faqs.question: What does the Cambridge IGCSE Geography 0460 syllabus actually cover?
faqs.answer: Three themes and a skills component. Theme 1, Population and settlement, covers population dynamics, migration, population structure and density, settlements, service provision and urbanisation. Theme 2, The natural environment, covers earthquakes and volcanoes, rivers, coasts, and weather, climate and natural vegetation including the tropical rainforest and hot desert. Theme 3, Economic development, covers development, food production, industry, tourism, energy, water and the environmental risks of economic development. Paper 2 tests geographical skills on a 1:25,000 map and other resources. The coursework or alternative paper tests fieldwork understanding.

faqs.question: Does Geography 0460 count towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: For the British track, the Ministry requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. Geography 0460 is an accredited IGCSE subject and can form part of that count. Equivalency is assessed by the Ministry, not by any tutoring service, and the rules are the Ministry's to change, so verify the current position on moe.gov.ae before relying on it.

faqs.question: Can a tutor supply Cambridge 0460 past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No, and you should be wary of anyone who offers to. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are Cambridge's copyright material, and reproducing or redistributing them is not something a legitimate tutor does. What a tutor can do is reference them, point you to cambridgeinternational.org and to your child's school, which holds proper access, and then teach against the published assessment criteria. Your child's geography department is the correct route to practice material, and most Dubai schools provide it readily when asked.

faqs.question: Does a private Geography tutor in Dubai need a MoHRE permit, and what does it cost?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The application runs through MoHRE's smart app, website or e-services, listed as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific figure with suspicion.

faqs.question: Can 0460 sessions move to post-Iftar slots during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most families ask for it. Dubai schools shorten the day during Ramadan, concentration shifts to the evening and a 4.30pm lesson stops working. Moving to a post-Iftar slot keeps the weekly rhythm intact at a point in the year when the Year 11 cohort cannot afford to pause, since the month often sits close to mocks or to the run-up to the series. Because lessons are online and the teacher is not driving anywhere, the slot can move week to week without renegotiating a travel window.

faqs.question: What happens if no 0460 Geography specialist is free at our hour?
faqs.answer: We tell you, rather than filling the slot with a general science or humanities tutor. Geography is a minority option subject and the pool of teachers who have taken a full cohort through 0460 is genuinely limited, particularly in the late-afternoon Gulf Standard Time window when every Dubai family wants to be taught. The usual options are a different time, a short wait for a named teacher to come free, or a different format such as a fortnightly longer session. What we will not do is pretend a generalist is a specialist and let you discover it in week three.

faqs.question: How should a Dubai family budget 0460 tutoring against school fees?
faqs.answer: Treat it as a proportion of the year's education spend rather than as an hourly rate. KHDA confirmed no increase in Dubai private school fees for 2026-27, so the fee line is predictable this year. Against it, one weekly session in the mid band sits at roughly AED 600 to AED 1,200 a month on Bestimate's estimates, and exam-year support at two sessions a week at AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above. The comparison worth making is not tutoring against nothing, but tutoring against a resit entry or a sixth-form application made with a grade that closes options.

faqs.question: Is there a free trial before we commit to weekly 0460 sessions?
faqs.answer: Yes, one lesson, with no card details taken and no obligation to continue. The condition is simply that it is a single lesson with a named teacher. We ask for the mock script and the school report beforehand so that the hour is spent teaching a real weakness rather than running a general assessment, and you receive a short written note afterwards setting out what the teacher found and what they would do next. If that note does not match what you see at home, that is useful information too.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-geography-0460-onl.tutorsIntro: These teachers work with Dubai students on Cambridge IGCSE Geography 0460 and mark their written work against the published assessment criteria. Each has taken a full cohort through the syllabus, so they know which of the three themes a particular school tends to leave thin.

intro.heading: How you can tell whether 0460 tutoring is working
paragraphs: Most tutoring arrangements fail quietly. The sessions happen, the student says they were fine, the tutor says progress is being made, and then the mock comes back at the same grade as the last one. Nobody lied. The problem is that nothing measurable was ever produced, so there was no point at which anyone could have noticed the plan was wrong. A Cambridge IGCSE Geography 0460 online tutor in Dubai working properly produces a short, specific paper trail, and a parent who knows what to ask for can read it in ten minutes a fortnight.

For 0460 the paper trail is unusually easy to define, because the syllabus is unusually concrete. Paper 1 is worth 45% of the grade and consists of three 25-mark theme questions, each ending in a 7-mark part marked in levels of response that needs a named, located case study. Paper 2 is a 60-mark skills paper worth 27.5% in which every question is compulsory and every skill is procedural. The remaining 27.5% comes either from a 2,000-word coursework assignment or from the Alternative to Coursework written paper. Four artefacts cover all of it: a marked theme question, an annotated map extract, a case-study inventory, and either a commented draft or a marked Paper 4 attempt.

The first of those is the most diagnostic and the most often skipped. A 25-mark question marked properly does not come back with a number on it. It comes back with the command word of each part circled, the marks that were available in the resource identified separately from the marks that required recall, and the 7-mark part annotated against the levels: whether the answer named a place, whether it gave a date or a figure, whether it developed two points or listed six. Two students can both score eleven out of twenty-five for entirely different reasons, and the plan for the next six weeks differs completely between them.

The second artefact is the case-study inventory, and it is the one that shows whether a plan exists at all. There are roughly nine content units across the three themes that can carry a 7-mark question. A student either has a developed example for each, or has gaps. Writing those nine lines down and marking each as secure, thin or absent takes one session, and it converts a vague feeling that revision is happening into a list that can be worked through. By week six you should be able to see which lines moved.

The third thing to look for is honesty about what has not moved. Geography grades do not climb smoothly, mock papers vary in difficulty, and the first marked question after a diagnosis is often worse than the one before it because the student is attempting something harder. A teacher who reports steady improvement every fortnight is reporting a feeling. A teacher who says the skills paper has moved, Theme 2 has moved, Theme 3 has not, and here is what we are changing, is reporting evidence. The sections below set out what each piece of that evidence looks like and when it should appear.
bullets: Artefact one: a 25-mark theme question marked against the levels, not scored
Artefact two: an annotated 1:25,000 map extract from a real Paper 2 task
Artefact three: a case-study inventory, nine units marked secure, thin or absent
Artefact four: a commented coursework draft or a marked Paper 4 attempt
Artefact five: a timing log showing where the hour and forty-five minutes went

dubai/cambridge-igcse-geography-0460-onl.programmesIntro: Dubai students arrive at 0460 from four quite different places, and the evidence you should expect in the first month differs for each. These are the four routes we see most, with what the first six weeks should produce in each case.

programmes.name: Joining 0460 from IB MYP or an American middle school
programmes.description: Students transferring in have usually done enquiry-led humanities with no topographical map work and no case-study discipline. The content gap is smaller than it looks; the assessment gap is larger. Week one should produce a map-skills baseline and an honest statement of which Paper 2 tasks the student has literally never seen before.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai generates more of these transfers than almost any comparable market, because families move schools and curricula mid-stage and because several large schools run both MYP and Cambridge pathways. A transferring student's first marked 0460 question is frequently strong on ideas and unscored on technique, which is good news: technique is the faster of the two to teach.

programmes.name: The standard two-year 0460 route
programmes.description: The route the syllabus is designed for, and the one where evidence is cheapest to collect. A fortnightly marked question from the start of Year 10 produces, by the end of the course, a folder showing exactly which units were secure at which point. The case-study inventory is filled in as each unit is taught rather than reconstructed in April.
programmes.countryNote: Most Cambridge-curriculum schools in Dubai teach Theme 1 and part of Theme 2 in Year 10, leaving Theme 3 Economic development and the skills paper to compete with mock season. Families who start evidence-gathering in Year 10 almost never need an emergency block in Year 11, which is the cheapest outcome available.

programmes.name: One-year, accelerated and resit candidates
programmes.ageRange: Ages 15-17 · Year 11 or a November series retake
programmes.description: Compressed routes need the diagnosis done in the first session, not the first month. The evidence here is a full marked past paper in week one, used to rank the three themes and the skills paper by marks available rather than by how uncomfortable each feels. The plan is then explicitly a triage plan, and it says out loud which unit is being abandoned.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, so a Dubai candidate who misses a grade in June can re-enter for November with a defined window rather than a full year's wait. Entry is made through the school or an exam centre, and the centre's internal deadline is the one that binds, not the published series dates.

programmes.name: After 0460: AS 9696 or IB Diploma Geography
programmes.description: Both post-16 routes assume the physical geography and the data-handling from 0460 are secure, and both move the weight towards extended evaluative writing and independent investigation. A student whose 0460 evidence folder shows marks earned from memorised case studies rather than from argument is the one who struggles in the first AS or DP term.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools offer both Cambridge AS Level Geography 9696 and IB Diploma Geography, and the choice is often decided by the option block rather than the subject. Asking in Year 11 which of the two the school staffs more deeply is a more useful question than asking which is harder.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-geography-0460-onl.subjectsIntro: Evidence in 0460 is organised by question type, because that is how the marks are organised. These are the ten things a marked script can show you, with what each one is actually testing and what a weak answer looks like.

subjects.name: Resource-based short answers
subjects.description: The opening parts of each theme question hand the candidate a map, graph, table or photograph and ask them to identify or describe what is there. The marks are in the resource. A script losing these is a script where the student is answering from memory instead of reading, which is the easiest fault in the syllabus to correct.

subjects.name: Describe questions
subjects.description: Describe asks what the pattern is: the trend, the distribution, the shape, with figures quoted from the resource. Candidates lose these marks by explaining instead. A marked script should show the command word circled and the explanation crossed through, so the student sees exactly what was thrown away.

subjects.name: Explain and give-reasons questions
subjects.description: These want a causal chain, not a label. Two developed reasons taken two steps each score better than five reasons stated once. The diagnostic marker is whether the answer contains the word because or an equivalent link; scripts without any causal connective rarely reach the upper marks here.

subjects.name: The 7-mark levels-of-response part
subjects.description: The final part of each theme question, marked in levels rather than by points. It needs a named and located case study with some figures or dates and a developed argument. Three of these sit on every Paper 1, so the part worth seven marks is worth twenty-one across the paper, and it is where the grade is decided.

subjects.name: Climate and population graph interpretation
subjects.description: Climate graphs, population pyramids, line and bar graphs, and the completion of partly drawn graphs. Precision is the whole mark: reading the correct axis, quoting the unit, and plotting to the gridline. These are the marks most often lost by a capable student working at speed.

subjects.name: Topographical map interpretation
subjects.description: Grid references in the correct order, distance along a road rather than a straight line, bearings from the right point, gradient as a ratio, and relief described from contour patterns. Teachable in a handful of sessions and visible immediately in a marked script, because the errors are specific rather than vague.

subjects.name: Cross-sections and sketch construction
subjects.description: Constructing a cross-section between two grid references and annotating it, or completing a sketch from a photograph. Method-driven work where a student either has the procedure or does not. One demonstration followed by three repetitions is usually enough to make it reliable.

subjects.name: Photograph and image interpretation
subjects.description: Interpreting a ground, aerial or satellite image: identifying land use, inferring process, and linking what is visible to syllabus content. Weak answers describe the photograph. Strong answers use it as evidence for a geographical statement, which is a habit rather than a knowledge gap.

subjects.name: Coursework data collection and presentation
subjects.description: Hypothesis design, sampling, instrument choice, and whether each graph or map in the report earns its place. The report must be the student's own work throughout; a tutor's contribution is to ask whether the presentation answers the question and to explain what the criteria reward.

subjects.name: Coursework and Paper 4 evaluation
subjects.description: The evaluation sections ask what went wrong with the method and how reliable the result is. Students who have never seen a method fail find this hardest. Walking through a deliberately flawed sampling plan and asking what it would really produce is the fastest route into the top band here.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-geography-0460-onl.regionsTitle: Where in Dubai our 0460 students study, and what their schools leave thin
dubai/cambridge-igcse-geography-0460-onl.regionsIntro: Geography is an option subject, so the shape of a 0460 cohort varies enormously from school to school and therefore from community to community. These are the Dubai areas our 0460 students write in from, with what the marked scripts from each tend to show.

regions.name: Al Barsha, Tecom and Al Sufouh
regions.note: Large, long-established Cambridge cohorts with strong departmental past-paper stocks. Scripts from here are usually technically competent and thin on Theme 3, which lands late in the course and competes with mock season.

regions.name: Dubai Marina, JBR and Bluewaters
regions.note: High-mobility apartment communities where students often arrive mid-course. The common pattern in a first marked script is confident content and unpractised map skills, because Paper 2 technique is the thing a transferring student has genuinely never been taught.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate and Dubai Hills
regions.note: Newer schools with growing geography sets, where the departmental stock of exemplar answers is still being built. Scripts tend to show students who know the content and have never seen a 7-mark answer in the top band, so they do not know what one looks like.

regions.name: Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Mizhar
regions.note: Mixed-curriculum cluster where Cambridge IGCSE sits alongside mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies. Timetable pressure shows up as units taught quickly, and the case-study inventory from here usually has the most absent lines.

regions.name: Jumeirah 1, 2 and 3
regions.note: Short school runs and established British-curriculum departments. Scripts are often strongest on Theme 1 Population and settlement and weakest on rivers and coasts, which several schools in this corridor teach in a compressed block.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches, Mudon and Town Square
regions.note: Villa communities where after-school sport competes hard with homework. The timing log matters most here: students are capable but routinely run out of time on Paper 1 because the three questions are not budgeted at thirty-five minutes each.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle, Al Furjan and Discovery Gardens
regions.note: High proportion of mid-year arrivals from Indian and American curricula. The first six weeks here are usually spent on assessment technique rather than content, and the evidence folder shows the fastest early movement of any group.

regions.name: Deira, Al Qusais and Bur Dubai
regions.note: Older districts with large cohorts and a wide spread of starting points inside one class. Scripts from here show the clearest benefit from a case-study inventory, because class teaching cannot differentiate nine units for thirty students.

schoolClusters.city: Established Cambridge departments across Al Barsha, Tecom and the Marina
schoolClusters.note: Schools in this corridor have run IGCSE geography for long enough to hold deep past-paper banks and consistent internal marking. A marked script from one of these cohorts is usually reliable, which makes the external second opinion a comparison rather than a correction.

schoolClusters.city: Schools serving Dubai Hills, Arabian Ranches and Mudon
schoolClusters.note: Newer villa-community schools whose geography sets are small and growing. Small sets mean a student who misses two weeks loses a whole unit, which is the single most common reason a Year 11 script here has an absent case study.
schools: Jumeirah English Speaking School Arabian Ranches

schoolClusters.city: Schools serving Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Qusais
schoolClusters.note: Large mixed-curriculum cohorts carrying the mandatory UAE subjects alongside Cambridge IGCSE. Marked work from these schools tends to be strong on recall and light on extended writing, because the timetable gives less room for essay feedback.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-geography-0460-onl.schoolDisclaimer: School names appear here only as context for Dubai's Cambridge IGCSE geography market; IB Gram has no affiliation with, partnership with or endorsement from any school, school group or examination board mentioned.
dubai/cambridge-igcse-geography-0460-onl.modesIntro: Three ways Dubai families run 0460 support, each defined by what it produces rather than by how long it lasts. All three are delivered one-to-one over live video; none involves a visit to a UAE address.

modes.title: The fortnightly marked-paper cycle
modes.description: A weekly session with a marked question handed back every second week. The cycle is deliberate: teach, attempt under timing, mark against the levels, re-teach the specific fault. It is the slowest-looking format and the one that produces a readable record, because by week twelve you have six marked questions in sequence rather than six impressions.
bullets: One 25-mark theme question under timing each fortnight
Marked against the published levels, with the command words annotated
Case-study inventory updated in the same session
A two-line note to the parent on what moved and what did not

modes.title: Coursework draft review block
modes.description: For candidates on the Paper 3 route. Three to five sessions spaced around the school's internal deadlines, each built on a draft the student has already written. The work between sessions is the reading, and the session itself is spent on questions about method, presentation and whether the conclusion follows from the data collected.
bullets: Hypothesis tested for whether it can actually be answered
Sampling and method questioned before data collection, not after
Feedback on the student's own draft, never text supplied for them
The 2,000-word limit treated as a design constraint, not a target

modes.title: Mock-to-series repair block
modes.description: Six to ten sessions that begin with the full mock script and end with a timed paper under exam conditions. The mock is read before the first session so the first hour teaches rather than tests. The plan explicitly names which unit is being left alone, because a triage plan that pretends to cover everything covers nothing.
bullets: Full mock script read and ranked before session one
Themes ordered by marks available, not by discomfort
Paper 2 skills drilled in parallel rather than afterwards
A final timed Paper 1 marked and returned inside forty-eight hours

sections.heading: What an online 0460 tutor should put in your hands by week six
paragraphs: Six weeks is long enough to produce evidence and short enough that a wrong plan has not yet cost the year. By the end of it a Cambridge IGCSE Geography 0460 online tutor in Dubai should have produced five specific things, and none of them is a progress report written in adjectives.

The first is a marked 25-mark theme question with the command words annotated and the 7-mark part assessed against the levels. The second is an annotated 1:25,000 map extract showing the student's own grid references, measured distance and constructed cross-section, with the errors marked rather than corrected. The third is the case-study inventory: nine content units, each marked secure, thin or absent, dated at week one and updated at week six so the movement is visible. The fourth is either a commented coursework draft or a marked Paper 4 attempt, depending on which route the school entered. The fifth is a timing log showing how the student actually allocated an hour and forty-five minutes across three questions.

That last one surprises parents more than any of the others. A substantial number of Dubai candidates lose marks not to ignorance but to budget: they write a generous answer to the first theme question, a reasonable answer to the second, and run out of time on the third 7-mark part, which is the most valuable single mark allocation on the paper. No amount of content teaching fixes that. A log that shows thirty-eight minutes, thirty-four minutes and twenty-eight minutes on three questions worth twenty-five marks each tells the student something a grade never will.

Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, which is how the evidence gets produced at all. The student annotates the resource on a shared screen while the teacher watches the annotation happen, so the error is visible at the moment it is made rather than inferred afterwards from a finished script. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India.

sections.heading: Inside a 25-mark theme question: where the marks sit
paragraphs: Paper 1 of Cambridge IGCSE Geography 0460 runs for one hour forty-five minutes, carries 75 marks and is worth 45% of the grade. Candidates answer three questions, one from each theme, and each is worth 25 marks. All three are built to the same pattern, and knowing the pattern changes how a student reads the paper.

The question opens with resource-based parts worth small numbers of marks each. These sit on a map, a graph, a table or a photograph printed in the insert, and the information needed is in front of the candidate. It then moves into parts that require content as well as the resource, typically asking for explanation across a middle band of marks. It closes with a part worth seven marks that is marked in levels of response and requires a named, located case study. Three questions, three 7-mark parts, so twenty-one of the paper's seventy-five marks are decided by whether the student has developed examples ready.

This distribution has a practical consequence that scripts show repeatedly. A candidate can be fluent on the resource parts, competent on the explanation parts and score two or three out of seven on each levels part, and land in the middle of the grade range despite knowing a great deal of geography. The reverse also happens: a student with excellent case studies who misreads command words on the early parts throws away a dozen marks that required no revision at all. The marked script distinguishes these two students in about five minutes. A grade does not distinguish them at all.

What a tutor does with that is sequence the teaching accordingly. Resource-reading habits are fixed in one or two sessions. Command-word discipline takes three or four. Case studies take months, which is why the inventory is built early and worked through steadily rather than crammed in the final weeks.

sections.heading: Three diagnostics the first session should actually run
paragraphs: A first session that explains what IGCSE Geography is has wasted an hour. The student knows. What nobody has established is which of the specific, identifiable faults is costing marks, and three diagnostics cover almost all of it.

The command-word audit comes first. Take a marked script, circle the command word in every part, and ask the student what each word requires. Candidates who cannot distinguish describe from explain, or explain from suggest, are losing marks across every theme simultaneously, which looks like weak geography and is actually weak reading. The fix is quick and the gain shows up on the next attempt, which is why it goes first: an early visible improvement buys the goodwill needed for the slower work.

The case-study inventory comes second. Nine content units across the three themes can each carry a levels-of-response question. For each one, the student states their example out loud with place, date and one figure. What emerges is rarely what either parent or student expected. Students usually have three strong examples they reach for constantly, four they half remember, and two units with nothing at all. The two with nothing are where the next month goes, because a 7-mark part on an absent unit scores close to zero regardless of general ability.

The timing audit comes third and is the easiest to skip. Give the student a past Paper 1 under real conditions and record, per question, the minutes spent and the marks earned. The ratio is often startling. A student scoring well on marks-per-minute in Theme 1 and badly in Theme 3 is not weak at economic development; they arrived at it with nineteen minutes left. Those three diagnostics take one long session or two short ones, and everything in the plan that follows is derived from them rather than guessed.

sections.heading: Teaching a 1:25,000 map extract over a shared screen
paragraphs: The reasonable worry about online geography teaching is the map. Paper 2 is worth 27.5% of 0460 and much of it sits on a topographical extract that students are used to handling on paper with a ruler. It is a fair question and the answer is specific rather than reassuring.

The extract is displayed on a shared screen and the student annotates it directly, with the teacher watching the cursor move. When a six-figure grid reference is read out in the wrong order, the teacher sees the eastings and northings being counted in real time and stops it at the point of error. When distance along a winding road is measured as a straight line, the measurement happens on screen and the fault is visible before the answer is written. A paper-based tutor sitting beside the student sees the same thing; a tutor who only marks the finished script sees neither.

Three procedures account for most of the lost marks and all three teach well this way. Gradient requires reading two contour values, converting the horizontal distance to the same unit and expressing the result as a ratio, and the step students drop is the unit conversion. Cross-section construction requires a scaled axis and plotted contour intersections, and it is a method that is either known or not known. Relief description requires reading contour spacing and pattern rather than listing heights, which is a vocabulary problem as much as a technical one.

Students should still work with a paper copy and a ruler for timed practice, and that is part of the homework rather than part of the lesson. The lesson is for watching the method being used and intervening at the moment it goes wrong. Each session ends with the annotated extract saved, which is why it becomes one of the five artefacts in the evidence folder rather than a conversation nobody can reconstruct.

sections.heading: The case-study inventory: nine units, named, located, dated
paragraphs: Case studies decide the levels-of-response marks, and levels marks decide the grade. Yet almost no Dubai student arrives with a written list of which examples they hold for which unit, because class teaching delivers examples unit by unit and nobody audits the set at the end.

A usable case study has four properties: a place name, a location that is more specific than a country, at least one date or figure, and a line of argument it can support. A candidate who writes about deforestation in Brazil has a topic. A candidate who writes about soy and cattle expansion in Mato Grosso with a rate of clearance and a named consequence has a case study. The gap between those two answers on a 7-mark levels part is usually three or four marks, repeated three times across the paper.

The inventory is built in one session and maintained in every session after it. Each line is marked secure, thin or absent, dated, and reviewed at week six. The point is not the document; the point is that it makes a revision plan falsifiable. A student who says they have revised Theme 3 can be asked which example they would use for industry and which for tourism, and the answer either exists or it does not. Dubai students have one genuine advantage here, which is that several units have excellent local evidence: water supply and desalination, tourism management, urbanisation, and the hot desert ecosystem. They also have one genuine trap, which is reaching for the UAE on every question, including the ones that explicitly want a lower-income country.

The table below is the inventory format, with one workable option per unit and the trap that goes with it. It is a starting template rather than a prescription, and a student who ends up with better examples of their own has done the exercise correctly.
