sections.heading: The coursework draft chain, and what a parent sees at each stage
paragraphs: If your child's cohort is entered for Paper 3, 27.5% of the grade arrives as a 2,000-word fieldwork assignment marked out of 60, and the deadlines that bind are the school's internal ones rather than anything Cambridge publishes. The draft chain is where this component is won or quietly lost, and it is the easiest part of 0460 for a parent to monitor because every stage leaves a document.

Stage one is the question. A hypothesis that cannot be answered with data the student can actually collect in Dubai is the most expensive mistake available, and it is made in week one and discovered in week eight. A tutor's job here is to ask the awkward questions: what will you measure, where, how many times, and what result would disprove this. Stage two is the method, and it must be questioned before collection rather than after, because a sampling plan cannot be repaired retrospectively. Stage three is presentation, where every graph and map has to justify its place. Stage four is analysis and conclusion, and stage five is evaluation, which the mark criteria reward and most candidates treat as an afterthought.

The boundary matters as much as the chain. The assignment must be the student's own work from start to finish. A tutor may question a hypothesis, point out that a conclusion does not follow from the data, explain what the published criteria reward, and say plainly that a graph is doing no work. A tutor may not produce assessed material on a candidate's behalf, and any service offering to do so is offering a Cambridge malpractice finding alongside it. There are sellers of finished coursework in this market; what they sell puts the whole entry at risk.

For candidates on the Paper 4 route there is no draft chain, and the evidence is a marked attempt at the Alternative to Coursework paper instead. That paper asks about hypothesis design, sampling, data-collection methods, presentation choices and the evaluation of reliability. Students who have never collected field data struggle most on the evaluation questions, which is fixable by walking through a flawed method and asking what it would really have produced.

sections.heading: Real grade movement, and mock-paper noise
paragraphs: Parents are asked to judge tutoring on grades, and grades are the noisiest signal available. Two mock papers set from different past series are not the same instrument. Internal marking varies between teachers and between terms. A student who scores a grade lower on a harder paper has not gone backwards, and a student who gains two grades on an easier one has not necessarily gained anything.

There are three cleaner signals. The first is marks on a repeated question type: the same 7-mark levels part, attempted in week one and week six on the same unit, marked against the same criteria. That comparison controls for difficulty because the task is identical. The second is the inventory, which is a count rather than a judgement: how many of the nine units moved from absent or thin to secure. The third is the timing log, where a student finishing all three questions is a measurable change from a student who did not.

There is also a predictable and misleading dip. The first marked attempt after a serious diagnosis is often worse than the one before it. A student who has been told to stop describing and start explaining will, for two or three attempts, do neither fluently. A student learning to budget thirty-five minutes a question writes less than they used to. This dip is normal, it lasts a few weeks, and a tutor who does not warn you about it in advance will have a difficult conversation in week four.

What a report should therefore contain is uncomfortable specificity: the skills paper has moved, Theme 2 has moved, Theme 3 has not, two inventory lines remain absent, and here is what changes next fortnight. That is less comforting than steady progress and considerably more useful, because it can be acted on.

sections.heading: What a KHDA inspection report tells you about a geography department
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, and which inspects schools on a six-band scale running from Outstanding down to Very Weak. Parents reasonably use the band as a proxy for teaching quality. It is a reasonable proxy for a school and a poor one for a single option subject.

An inspection report is a whole-school judgement built across phases and subjects. A school rated Outstanding may have a small geography set taught by a teacher covering two subjects, and a school rated Good may have a deep humanities department with a dozen years of past-paper practice. Neither fact appears in the band. What the published report can give you is more useful than the headline: comments on attainment and progress in specified subjects, on the quality of teaching and assessment, and on how well the school uses assessment data, all of which bear directly on whether a 0460 cohort is well served.

Two questions get you further than the report does. Ask how many students are in the Year 11 geography set and who teaches them, because a set of eight taught by a specialist is a different proposition from a set of thirty taught by someone whose main subject is history. And ask whether the department issues marked past-paper questions against the published criteria, and how often. A department that marks a full theme question every three weeks produces candidates who need far less external help than one that does not.

The regulator map beyond Dubai is worth knowing because families move within the UAE. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain schools answer to ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so a move across the emirate line is a change of regulator as well as of address.

process.title: Send the script, not a description of the problem
process.description: The most useful thing you can send is the marked mock paper, followed by the school report and which paper route the cohort sits: Paper 3 coursework or Paper 4. A script read before the first session means the free trial lesson teaches something instead of discovering what a teacher could have read in advance.

process.title: Run the three diagnostics in the first session
process.description: Command-word audit, case-study inventory, timing audit. By the end of the first hour there is a dated list of nine units marked secure, thin or absent, and a statement of whether marks are being lost to content, to reading or to the clock. The plan comes from that list, not from a template.

process.title: Fix the fast faults first, deliberately
process.description: Command words and resource-reading habits move within two sessions, and that early visible gain matters because the slower work on case studies takes months. The sequence is chosen for evidence as much as for pedagogy: something should have measurably changed before you are asked to commit to a term.

process.title: Mark a question every fortnight and hand it over
process.description: One 25-mark theme question under timing, marked against the published levels with the command words annotated, every second week. You receive the marked script, not a summary. Over a term that produces six scripts in sequence, which is a record rather than an impression.

process.title: Re-rank at each mock, and say what is being dropped
process.description: Mock results change the ranking of the three themes and the skills paper by marks available. A triage plan names the unit it is abandoning. If six weeks of evidence shows a theme has not moved, the honest options are to change the approach, change the teacher, or stop, and we will say which one we think it is.

whyPoints.title: Evidence you can read in ten minutes
whyPoints.description: Five artefacts per cycle: a marked theme question, an annotated map extract, a dated case-study inventory, a commented draft or Paper 4 attempt, and a timing log. None of them requires you to know geography to interpret, and all of them are specific enough to argue with.

whyPoints.title: Marked against the published criteria, not scored out of ten
whyPoints.description: A 7-mark levels part assessed against the levels tells you whether the answer named a place, gave a date, and developed an argument. A number out of seven tells you none of that. The annotation is where the teaching actually lives.

whyPoints.title: The dip is explained before it happens
whyPoints.description: A student told to stop describing and start explaining gets worse for two or three attempts before getting better. Any honest evidence-led approach produces that dip, so it is better flagged in week one than defended in week four when a mock comes back lower.

whyPoints.title: Live video is what makes the error visible
whyPoints.description: The student annotates the map extract on a shared screen while the teacher watches. A grid reference counted in the wrong order is caught as it happens rather than deduced from a finished script. Lessons are online; IB Gram runs no home visits in the UAE.

whyPoints.title: A specialist rather than whoever was free
whyPoints.description: Geography is a minority option subject with small Dubai cohorts. Teaching over video means the teacher is chosen for having taken a full cohort through 0460 and marked its levels answers, rather than for living within reach of your community at 4.30pm.

whyPoints.title: Clear limits on coursework support
whyPoints.description: A tutor questions a hypothesis, probes a method and comments on what the student has already written. Assessed material is never produced on a candidate's behalf. This market contains sellers of finished coursework; the grade they offer is not worth the malpractice risk attached to it.

faqs.question: What should an online Cambridge IGCSE Geography 0460 tutor send me after the first month?
faqs.answer: Five things, and none of them a progress report. A marked 25-mark theme question with the command words annotated and the 7-mark part assessed against the levels. An annotated 1:25,000 map extract showing your child's own grid references and measurements with the errors marked. A dated case-study inventory listing nine syllabus units as secure, thin or absent. A commented coursework draft or a marked Paper 4 attempt, depending on the entry route. And a timing log showing how an hour and forty-five minutes was actually divided across three questions. All five can be read in ten minutes.

faqs.question: How are the marks split inside a single 25-mark Paper 1 question?
faqs.answer: Each theme question opens with resource-based parts worth one to three marks each, sitting on a map, graph, table or photograph in the insert. It moves into describe and explain parts across a middle band of marks, which need content as well as the resource. It closes with a part worth seven marks, marked in levels of response, which requires a named and located case study with some figures or dates. Three questions means three of those 7-mark parts, so twenty-one of the paper's seventy-five marks turn on whether developed examples exist.

faqs.question: My son knows the case studies but scores four out of seven on the extended part. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the example is a topic rather than a case study. Levels-of-response marking rewards a place name, a location more specific than a country, a date or a figure, and a developed line of argument. A student who writes knowledgeably about deforestation without naming a region, a rate or a consequence sits in the middle band however much they know. The repair is mechanical: take each example in the inventory and attach a place, a number and a consequence. It usually moves three or four marks per paper.

faqs.question: Can map skills really be taught over a screen share?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for the diagnostic part of the work it is better than marking a finished script. The extract is on a shared screen and the student annotates it while the teacher watches, so a six-figure grid reference counted in the wrong order is stopped at the point of error rather than deduced afterwards. Gradient conversions, cross-section construction and relief description are all procedures you can watch being performed. Timed practice should still happen on paper with a ruler, and that is set as homework rather than used up in the lesson.

faqs.question: How do I tell a real grade improvement from mock-paper noise?
faqs.answer: Compare like with like. Two mocks built from different past series are different instruments, and internal marking varies between teachers and terms. The cleaner signals are a repeated question type attempted twice on the same unit and marked against the same criteria, the count of inventory lines that moved from absent or thin to secure, and whether your child now finishes all three questions. Those three comparisons control for paper difficulty. A grade on its own does not, which is why it is the noisiest number in the folder.

faqs.question: Which 0460 command words cost Dubai candidates the most marks?
faqs.answer: Describe and explain, in that order, and the loss is in both directions. Describe asks for the pattern with figures quoted from the resource, and candidates lose the marks by explaining instead. Explain asks for a causal chain developed over two steps, and candidates lose the marks by listing five labels once each. Suggest asks for a plausible reason the resource supports rather than a recalled fact. The audit is quick: circle every command word on a marked script and ask the student what each one requires. The gaps appear immediately.

faqs.question: How many case studies does a 0460 candidate actually need?
faqs.answer: Around nine, one for each content unit capable of carrying a levels-of-response question: migration, urbanisation, a hazard, rivers, coasts, an ecosystem, food production or industry, tourism, and energy or water. Depth beats breadth. One example with a place name, a date, a figure and a consequence outperforms three vague ones, because the levels criteria reward developed use rather than coverage. The honest test is whether your child can state each example out loud with its location and one number attached, without notes.

faqs.question: Can a tutor read my daughter's 0460 coursework draft before she submits it?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is the correct use of the hour. A tutor can question whether the hypothesis can be answered with data she can actually collect, whether the sampling matches the question, whether each graph earns its place, whether the conclusion follows from the evidence, and whether the evaluation section reaches what the criteria reward. What a tutor must not do is produce assessed material on her behalf. The assignment has to be her own work throughout, and anything else risks a Cambridge malpractice finding against her entry.

faqs.question: What is the word limit on the Cambridge IGCSE Geography 0460 coursework?
faqs.answer: The coursework assignment is written to a limit of 2,000 words and is marked out of 60, carrying 27.5% of the grade. Treat the limit as a design constraint rather than a target: a report that reaches 2,000 words with a weak method and three decorative graphs scores below a tighter one where every element does work. The deadlines that actually bind are your child's school's internal ones, which sit well before the Cambridge series, and they are set by the school rather than by Cambridge.

faqs.question: Does my child sit Paper 3 or Paper 4 for Geography 0460?
faqs.answer: The school decides, and you should confirm it before buying any tutoring. Paper 3 is the coursework route: one fieldwork assignment up to 2,000 words, marked out of 60. Paper 4 is the Alternative to Coursework, a written paper of one hour thirty minutes, also 60 marks, testing fieldwork understanding without fieldwork. Both carry the same 27.5% weighting and support for them looks nothing alike, so a tutor working on draft feedback when the cohort is entered for Paper 4 is wasting your money and your child's time.

faqs.question: What does a KHDA inspection rating tell me about my child's geography department?
faqs.answer: Less than parents assume. KHDA oversees the quality of private education in Dubai and inspects on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, but the band is a whole-school judgement across phases and subjects. An Outstanding school can have a small geography set taught by someone covering two subjects. Read the report's comments on attainment, teaching and use of assessment data instead, then ask the school two questions directly: how many students are in the Year 11 geography set, and how often the department marks a full theme question against the published criteria.

faqs.question: How often should a 0460 student be sitting a full past paper?
faqs.answer: Full papers under timing are expensive in a student's week, so they are worth rationing. A reasonable pattern is one full Paper 1 at diagnosis, one after the mock, and one in the final fortnight, with single 25-mark questions under timing every fortnight in between. Paper 2 is different: because it is procedural and compulsory throughout, it rewards frequent short practice rather than occasional full attempts. What matters more than frequency is that every timed attempt is marked against the criteria and returned, because an unmarked past paper teaches almost nothing.

faqs.question: Is there any difference between the June and November 0460 series?
faqs.answer: The qualification is the same and the standard is the same; what differs is the cohort and the timing. Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, so a candidate who misses a grade in June can re-enter in November rather than waiting a year. Entry is made through a school or exam centre, and the centre's internal deadline is the one that binds. Note also that every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones and must use the correct version of the timetable for its zone.

faqs.question: Do we get the same online tutor every week?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the evidence is the reason. The case-study inventory, the timing log and the sequence of marked questions only mean something if one person is maintaining them and can remember what week three looked like. Rotating teachers means re-diagnosing the same student repeatedly, which you pay for twice. If the match is wrong we will change the teacher deliberately and hand over the folder with it, but a different face each fortnight is not a service, it is an absence of one.

faqs.question: Can UAE examples be used in 0460 answers, or do examiners want British case studies?
faqs.answer: Examiners want appropriate examples, and nationality is irrelevant to that. A UAE example is strong for water supply and desalination, tourism management, urban growth and the hot desert ecosystem, because the evidence is real and local. It is wrong for any question that specifies a lower-income or middle-income country, and that is where Dubai candidates most often lose marks: reaching for the familiar example on a question that explicitly excluded it. The inventory should therefore pair the local examples with at least three from lower-income contexts.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-geography-0460-tut.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Cambridge IGCSE Geography 0460 to Dubai students over live video, marking skills questions and extended answers against the published criteria. Each profile shows the themes and papers they focus on and the year groups they currently teach.

intro.heading: Geography is the option subject where progress is visible quickest
paragraphs: Most tutoring is judged late. A Dubai family commits in October, hears that things are going well through the winter, and finds out in August whether that was true. Cambridge IGCSE Geography is an exception, and the reason is structural: one of its three papers is a skills paper, skills questions have objectively right answers, and a student either reads a gradient correctly or does not. Within four weeks of marked practice you can see whether anything has changed.

The subject divides into three assessments. Paper 1 is the geographical themes paper, an hour and forty-five minutes carrying 45% of the grade, with candidates answering three questions, one from each of population and settlement, the natural environment, and economic development. Paper 2 is the geographical skills paper, an hour and a half, built on map extracts, photographs, graphs and data. The third component is either Paper 3, a school-based coursework assignment, or Paper 4, the alternative to coursework, and which one your child sits was decided by the school.

That structure gives three different kinds of evidence and they move at three different speeds. Skills marks move in weeks because the sub-skills are discrete and practisable: measuring distance on a map, calculating a gradient, drawing a cross-section, describing a distribution, completing a graph, interpreting a photograph. Case-study knowledge builds over months and can be counted at any point. Extended-answer technique is the slowest of the three and usually the reason a student who knows a lot still writes six marks out of nine.

So the evidence file for 0460 has three sections, and the first one is the honest early indicator. A student whose skills-paper score on comparable question types has gone from eleven out of twenty to seventeen out of twenty across a month has improved, and no interpretation is needed to see it. A student whose skills score has not moved has either not practised or has a specific sub-skill problem nobody has named, and both of those are findings.

Case studies are the second section and the most commonly mismanaged. Students are told to learn case studies and never told how many, how specific or in what form, so they arrive in the exam with vague recollections of six places and no figures. A counted, dated bank with named locations and a handful of specific facts each is a document a parent can inspect. It is also the part of the subject where Dubai students have an advantage nobody uses, because they live in one of the most studied urban environments on earth.

On delivery, the plain statement: IB Gram does not run in-home visits anywhere in the UAE, and home visits are a service we offer only in India. Dubai students are taught one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. For geography this is close to ideal, because the map extract, the photograph and the mark scheme can all be on a shared screen with both people annotating the same image.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-geography-0460-tut.programmesIntro: Geography appears at several stages of a Dubai student's school career and produces different evidence at each. These notes say what to look at when.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Geography 0460 runs over two years across three themes, assessed by a themes paper, a skills paper and either a coursework assignment or the alternative to coursework. The skills paper is the component most students under-prepare for and the one where practice converts into marks fastest, because the question types repeat and the answers are objectively right or wrong.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai centres differ on the third component: some enter Paper 3 coursework, which requires the school to run fieldwork, and others enter Paper 4. That choice changes everything about how a student should prepare, so it is the first thing to confirm before planning any support. The exams officer or head of geography will know which the centre has entered.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary
programmes.description: Geography here establishes the skills that Paper 2 later examines: using a key and a scale, reading grid references, describing a pattern from a map, and reading figures off a graph without losing the units. A student weak on those in Year 9 will be weak on a quarter of the IGCSE grade two years later.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai students who join mid-key-stage from systems with little map work often reach Year 10 confident on content and shaky on skills, and because the content is the visible part the gap goes unnoticed. A single marked skills exercise in Year 9 identifies it for nothing, which is the cheapest diagnostic available in this subject.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: Geography 9696 continues the subject and raises the demand on extended writing and on data response. Students who reached their IGCSE grade on strong skills and thin extended answers find the first AS term difficult, because the proportion of the grade carried by sustained written argument rises sharply.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai sixth forms offering 9696 commonly set a grade condition at IGCSE. The evidence worth looking at before that transition is not the overall grade but the split within it: a candidate carried by Paper 2 has a writing problem that AS will expose, and Year 11 is the cheaper place to address it.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Diploma Geography is the other post-16 route in Dubai, assessed across several papers plus an internally assessed fieldwork report. The content overlaps substantially with 0460's themes; the assessment style does not, since the Diploma rewards sustained analysis and a structured investigation rather than short skills responses.
programmes.countryNote: International Baccalaureate students are around 7% of Dubai private-school enrolment, with three further IB schools joining the 2026-27 intake. A 0460 student considering the Diploma should know that the fieldwork report there is a long internally assessed piece, so the habits of recording data and writing methodology properly are worth forming at IGCSE.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-geography-0460-tut.subjectsIntro: 0460 shares specific skills with other subjects a Dubai student may be taking, and the overlap is practical rather than thematic. The notes below name what transfers.

subjects.name: Geography (0460)
subjects.description: Three themes, three papers. Skills marks are recoverable in weeks, case-study knowledge in months, extended-answer technique slowest of all. Most Dubai students who plateau are losing extended-answer marks while believing the problem is content.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: Supplies the skills paper's arithmetic: scale conversion, gradient as a ratio, percentage change, reading values between graph gridlines. A student losing skills marks to calculation rather than to method has a maths problem appearing in a geography paper.

subjects.name: First Language English (0500)
subjects.description: Feeds the extended answers on Paper 1. The transferable skill is structure: making a point, developing it, and supporting it with a specific example. Students who write under-developed English paragraphs write under-developed geography paragraphs.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 and 0511)
subjects.description: Many Dubai candidates sit ESL, and in 0460 the cost is in command words. Describe, explain and suggest ask for different things and carry different mark values, and an answer that describes when it should explain is competent and under-rewarded.

subjects.name: Biology (0610)
subjects.description: Overlaps on ecosystems, vegetation and human impact on the environment, and more usefully on data interpretation: both subjects ask students to read a graph, state a trend and account for it. The transferable habit is quoting figures from the source.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Shares the economic development theme at the edges, particularly industry, employment structure and the effects of globalisation. Both subjects reward answers anchored in a specific named example rather than in general statements.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Overlaps on development indicators, trade and employment sectors. A student taking both can build one case-study bank serving two subjects, which is one of the few genuine efficiencies available in an IGCSE option block.

subjects.name: Environmental Management (0680)
subjects.description: Offered by some Dubai centres alongside or instead of Geography. Substantial overlap on natural resources, water and sustainability, and the data-response skills transfer almost completely, which is worth knowing when planning practice time across both.

subjects.name: Global Perspectives (0457)
subjects.description: Shares the research and evaluation habits the coursework assignment needs, including handling sources and acknowledging them properly. Students who have done 0457 usually find the methodology section of a geography investigation less foreign.

subjects.name: Arabic as a Foreign Language (0544)
subjects.description: Taken by many non-Arab students in Dubai, where Arabic is a mandatory subject in private schools whatever the licensed curriculum. Listed because it occupies weekly study time that a geography practice schedule has to work around.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-geography-0460-tut.regionsIntro: Dubai is unusually useful to a geography student, because several of the processes the syllabus describes are visible within a short drive. These notes are about what each area offers as local evidence rather than about tutor availability.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and JBR
regions.note: High-density, high-rise residential development on reclaimed and planned land, which illustrates urban land use, population density and the pressures the syllabus describes under settlement. A student can describe the local land-use pattern from memory and from a map extract of the same area.

regions.name: Palm Jumeirah and the coast
regions.note: Coastal management and land reclamation in a form few students anywhere can observe directly: breakwaters, beach nourishment and the effects of altering a coastline. Useful under the natural environment theme, and specific enough to carry figures rather than impressions.

regions.name: Deira and Dubai Creek
regions.note: The original settlement site, which makes the standard syllabus questions about why settlements grow where they do answerable with a local example: a sheltered inlet, trade, water access and subsequent outward growth. Older and denser street patterns contrast usefully with planned communities.

regions.name: Jebel Ali and the industrial south-west
regions.note: Port, free zone and heavy industry, which supports the economic development theme on employment structure, industrial location factors and the shift between sectors. One of the clearest industrial-location case studies available to a Dubai student.

regions.name: Ras Al Khor and the wetland reserve
regions.note: A protected wetland inside a major city, which makes conservation against development pressure concrete rather than abstract. Fits the natural environment theme and the sustainability questions that recur in extended answers.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate and Arabian Ranches
regions.note: Planned low-density suburban growth with car dependence and long internal road networks, which supports questions on urban sprawl, the rural-urban fringe and the costs of low-density living. The contrast with Deira is the point.

regions.name: Al Qusais and Muhaisnah

sections.heading: The 0460 evidence file: three streams, three speeds
paragraphs: Geography produces three distinct kinds of evidence and confusing them is what makes tutoring in this subject feel unmeasurable. Skills marks are discrete and fast. Case-study knowledge is cumulative and countable at any moment. Extended-answer technique is slow and only visible on comparable questions. A file that mixes all three into one percentage tells a Dubai parent nothing, and a file that separates them tells you almost everything within a month.

The table sets out what each stream produces and how quickly. Note the first row: the skills paper is the honest early indicator in this subject, and it is also the component students most often neglect, because content revision feels like work and practising gradient calculations does not. A student who has never sat a full timed skills paper has an unknown quarter of their grade, and finding out costs ninety minutes.

The case-study stream is the one to insist on as a document. Ask to see the bank: how many examples, for which themes, with what facts attached. 'We have covered case studies' is not an answer. 'Eleven examples, four for population and settlement, four for the natural environment, three for economic development, each with a named place and at least three figures' is an answer, and it is checkable by anybody.

The extended-answer stream needs patience and comparable questions. A nine-mark question on one topic and a nine-mark question on another are not equivalent, so a single improved mark proves little. What works is the same question type, written timed, marked against the criteria, with the lost mark named each time. Three of those over six weeks is a trend; two improved papers on different topics is noise.

sections.heading: Paper 2: the quarter of the grade most students leave unexamined
paragraphs: The skills paper runs for an hour and a half and is built on sources: map extracts, photographs, graphs, tables and diagrams. Candidates are asked to do specific things with them, and the list of things is short enough to be worked through systematically. Measuring a distance using the scale. Giving a grid reference the right way round. Calculating a gradient. Drawing or completing a cross-section. Describing the distribution of a feature. Completing a graph accurately. Interpreting a photograph in relation to a map of the same area.

Because the list is short and each item is objectively marked, this is the component where tutoring produces visible movement fastest. A student who loses four marks a paper on grid references and gradient is losing them to two specific procedures, and both are teachable in a single session. The improvement then shows up on the very next paper, which is why the skills block is usually the first thing we do with a Dubai student who has never had their skills marks separated out.

Two patterns recur. The first is scale: students convert incorrectly or forget that a measured distance has to be converted into ground distance, and the error is mechanical rather than conceptual. The second is the describe-against-explain distinction on distribution questions. Asked to describe a distribution, a strong student often explains it instead, offering reasons where the mark scheme wanted the pattern, the exceptions and some figures from the source.

There is also a reading habit worth naming. The skills paper rewards quoting from the source: a figure, a grid reference, a named feature on the map. Answers written from general knowledge, without reference to the extract in front of the candidate, lose marks even when they are geographically sensible. That is a habit that transfers to Paper 1 as well, where specificity is the difference between the middle and the top of the mark range.
bullets: Sit one full timed skills paper before deciding anything else

sections.heading: Paper 1: three themes, three questions, and the nine-mark problem
paragraphs: Paper 1 runs for an hour and forty-five minutes and carries 45% of the grade. Candidates answer three questions, one from each theme: population and settlement, the natural environment, and economic development. Each question moves from short recall and data-response parts into an extended answer, and it is the extended answer that decides the grade band. This is where a knowledgeable Dubai student most often scores six out of nine and cannot see why.

The reason is almost always specificity rather than knowledge. An answer that describes how urban growth causes problems in general reads fluently and earns mid-range credit. An answer that names a place, gives figures and ties each consequence to that place reaches the top band. The mark scheme rewards the second, and the difference between the two is not more revision; it is a case-study bank and the habit of using it.

The second cause is command words. Describe, explain, suggest and evaluate ask for different work and carry different mark values, and Dubai cohorts with a high proportion of students sitting English as a second language lose a measurable number of marks to answering a different question competently. Counting command-word mismatches per paper is a fast diagnostic and the count usually falls quickly once named.

The third is structure. A nine-mark answer needs developed points rather than a list, and students who were taught to write in bullet-style paragraphs at Key Stage 3 often never convert. The repair is mechanical: make a point, develop it with a consequence, support it with a specific detail from a named example, then move on. Practised on three or four timed answers with the lost mark identified each time, it moves within a month.

sections.heading: Case studies: how many, how specific, and can a Dubai student use Dubai?
paragraphs: Students are told to learn case studies and rarely told the specification. A workable target is three or four per theme, each with a named place, a scale, a few figures and two or three consequences that can be deployed in an extended answer. Eleven well-known examples beat thirty vague ones, because an extended answer has room for one example used properly and no room for a tour of several.

Yes, a Dubai student can use Dubai, and examiners mark what is geographically valid rather than what is British. The syllabus asks about processes, and an example that illustrates the process accurately with specific detail earns credit regardless of where it is. What loses marks is an example used thinly, so a local case study has to be learned with the same rigour as a textbook one: figures, dates, named features, and the mechanism rather than the impression.

The city supplies unusually good material. Rapid population growth driven by migration, with a demographic structure shaped by it, sits directly under population and settlement. Dubai Creek as an original settlement site, and the outward growth from it to planned communities on the periphery, answers the standard questions about settlement location and urban form. Palm Jumeirah and the coastline illustrate coastal management and the consequences of altering a shoreline. Jebel Ali supports industrial location and employment structure. Ras Al Khor puts conservation against development pressure in one place.

Two cautions. First, a local example still needs checkable figures, and the place to get them is a published source rather than a tutor's recollection; the KHDA and Dubai government statistical publications are usable and so are the relevant authorities' own pages. Second, a student should not rely only on local examples, because some syllabus topics are not well illustrated by anything in the Emirates, and a bank of eleven examples that are all from one city is a fragile bank.

sections.heading: Paper 3 coursework or Paper 4 alternative: which did your school enter?
paragraphs: This is the first question to settle and families frequently do not know the answer. The third component of 0460 is either a school-based coursework assignment, which requires the centre to run fieldwork and to supervise and assess the work, or the alternative to coursework, which is a written paper testing the same investigative skills using data the paper supplies. Both carry the same share of the grade and they demand completely different preparation.

If the centre entered the coursework route, the student will be collecting primary data on a fieldwork visit and writing an investigation around it. The tutoring boundary here is strict and worth stating before anybody starts. A tutor may teach the underlying geography, explain what a good methodology looks like, discuss how data can be presented, and give feedback on what the student has written. A tutor will not produce any part of an assignment that must be the student's own work, and this holds regardless of what any provider offers.

If the centre entered the alternative to coursework, the preparation is different and in some ways easier to measure. The paper asks about hypotheses, sampling, data collection methods, presentation techniques and the limitations of findings, all applied to material it provides. Those are practisable without leaving the house, and because the question types recur, scores on comparable questions are trackable in the same way skills marks are.

Dubai adds two practical constraints to the fieldwork route. Heat is the obvious one: outdoor data collection is realistic in the cooler months and uncomfortable to the point of unsafe in the summer, which is why schools schedule fieldwork between roughly November and March. Ramadan shifts timings too, with shortened school days and sessions moving later in the evening, and families planning tutoring around a fieldwork deadline should ask the school for its dates early rather than assuming the usual term rhythm.

sections.heading: Where 0460 marks disappear, question type by question type
paragraphs: Marked papers from Dubai students show the same handful of losses repeatedly, and each has a different cost and a different repair time. The cheapest to fix are the mechanical skills: grid references given in the wrong order, scale conversions done without converting, gradients expressed without a ratio. Those are single-session repairs and they recur on every skills paper, so the return is immediate.

The middle group is command words and source use. An answer that explains when it was asked to describe, or one that answers from general knowledge without quoting the map or graph in front of it, loses marks the student does not know they lost. Both respond to being counted: a tally of mismatches and a tally of answers that cited nothing from the source, kept for three papers, usually halves within a month because the student starts noticing.

The expensive group is extended answers, and the loss is specificity. A six-out-of-nine answer is normally fluent, accurate and general. It earns credit for knowledge and stops short of the top band because it names no place and quotes no figure. Fixing it requires a case-study bank to exist first, which is why the sequence matters: build the bank, then work on the answers, rather than trying to teach technique to a student with nothing specific to deploy.

The last loss is timing, and it is the most wasteful. A candidate who does not reach the final extended answer loses a block of marks regardless of ability. Attempt rate, meaning questions attempted out of questions set, belongs in the evidence file alongside the score, because a rising score with a falling attempt rate is not progress. Two full timed papers with a per-question clock is usually enough to fix it.

sections.heading: A four-week skills block, written out
paragraphs: The block below exists because 'we will work on exam skills' is a phrase every provider uses and almost nobody specifies. It assumes a Dubai student who has never had their skills marks separated from their paper total, which is the commonest situation. Four weeks is enough for this component specifically, which is what makes it the right place to start when a family wants to know quickly whether tutoring is worth continuing.

Week one is a full timed skills paper, marked with the score broken out per sub-skill. That single document usually surprises everyone: students who believed geography was their weak subject often turn out to have a specific four-mark problem rather than a general one. Weeks two and three take the two or three weakest sub-skills and work them directly, with short practice sets between sessions.

Week four repeats a comparable skills paper. Because the sub-skills are objectively marked and the question types recur, the comparison is genuinely like for like in a way that two different themes papers never are. A rise from eleven out of twenty to seventeen out of twenty on the same sub-skills is real, and a parent can read it without interpretation.

What happens next depends on the result. If skills marks have moved and the student is still mid-range overall, the problem is in extended answers and the case-study bank, and the next block is longer and slower. If skills marks have not moved at all, either the practice did not happen or there is a numeracy problem underneath, and both are worth knowing before buying another month.

sections.heading: How sessions run in Dubai, and the limits we hold to
paragraphs: A family sends a marked geography paper, or says which of the three papers worries them. The trial lesson is free, collects no card details, and is spent on that paper. It ends with a written note saying which of the three evidence streams is weakest, what the first target is, and how many sessions it should take. For a skills problem that estimate is often three or four sessions, and the note says so.

Sessions then run one-to-one over live video at a fixed slot in Gulf Standard Time, with the map extract, photograph or graph on a shared screen so both people annotate the same image. That is a genuine advantage in this subject rather than a compromise: a cross-section drawn on a shared screen can be compared against the mark scheme line by line. Practice is written independently between sessions and marked before the next one.

IB Gram does not run in-home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. That is stated on every country page we publish. For 0460 it has a practical upside, because the subset of tutors who mark skills papers against the criteria and know what a credited distribution description looks like is small, and over video a family in Mirdif chooses from the same subset as a family in Al Barsha.

Two limits do not move. A tutor teaches, reviews and gives feedback on work the student has produced, and nobody here will produce any part of an investigation or assignment that must be the student's own work. And we reference Cambridge syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes and link the official pages rather than distributing them. IB Gram holds no accreditation from KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, operates no UAE premises, and makes no promise about a grade.

process.title: Say which paper, not which subject
process.description: A message naming the component works immediately: 'Year 11, Cambridge 0460, skills paper, scored 24 out of 60 in the mock, paper attached'. If you do not know whether the centre entered Paper 3 coursework or Paper 4, ask the head of geography first, because the answer changes the whole plan.

process.title: Free trial lesson on your child's own paper
process.description: One session at no cost and with no card details collected, spent on a marked script rather than on a sales conversation. It ends with a written note naming the weakest of the three evidence streams, the first target and a session estimate. For skills problems the estimate is usually small, and the note says so.

process.title: Start with the skills paper
process.description: Not because it matters most, but because it moves fastest and therefore tells you soonest whether the arrangement is working. A full timed skills paper broken out per sub-skill is the single most informative ninety minutes available in this subject, and it is often the first time a student's quarter-grade has been looked at properly.

process.title: Build the case-study bank as a document
process.description: A counted, dated list with named places and figures, three or four examples per theme, held by the family. Extended-answer technique cannot be taught to a student with nothing specific to deploy, so the bank comes before the writing work rather than alongside it.

process.title: Decide at four weeks
process.description: Four weeks is enough for a like-for-like skills comparison and a real decision. Continuing, changing target, changing tutor and stopping are all on the table, and the note recording the decision carries the comparison behind it. The file and the case-study bank stay with the family in every case.

whyPoints.title: The fastest honest signal in the subject
whyPoints.description: Skills-paper marks broken out per sub-skill move in two to four weeks and are objectively right or wrong. That makes 0460 one of the few option subjects where a Dubai family can know within a month whether the tutoring is doing anything.

whyPoints.title: Case studies as a countable document
whyPoints.description: A dated bank with named places and figures, three or four per theme, inspectable by anybody. 'We have covered case studies' is not evidence. A student who holds eleven properly learned examples writes specific extended answers; one who does not writes fluent generality that caps mid-range.

whyPoints.title: Local material used rigorously
whyPoints.description: Dubai supplies genuinely strong examples for settlement location, coastal management, industrial location and conservation against development. We use them with figures and named features from published sources, not as impressions, and we do not let a bank become entirely local.

whyPoints.title: The coursework boundary stated upfront
whyPoints.description: On the Paper 3 route a tutor teaches the geography, discusses methodology and gives feedback on what the student has written. Nobody here will produce part of an investigation that must be the student's own, and we say so to the student at the first session rather than waiting to be asked.

whyPoints.title: Dubai's calendar accounted for
whyPoints.description: Fieldwork is realistic roughly between November and March because of the heat, and Ramadan shifts school days and session timings. A plan built around a fieldwork deadline needs the school's dates in September, and we ask for them rather than assuming a standard term rhythm.

whyPoints.title: No claim beyond what is shown
whyPoints.description: Paper structure referenced to the Cambridge syllabus document for your child's series rather than restated as settled fact, no regulator approval claimed, no invented statistic, and no promise about a grade in any subject or series.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge 0460 paper shows progress soonest?
faqs.answer: The skills paper. Its question types recur and the answers are objectively right or wrong, so a score broken out per sub-skill is comparable from one paper to the next in a way that two different themes papers are not. A student losing four marks a paper to grid-reference order and scale conversion can usually recover them in one or two sessions, and the improvement appears on the very next paper. That is why we start there even when the family's worry is elsewhere.

faqs.question: My child writes long geography answers and still scores six out of nine. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost always specificity rather than knowledge. A fluent, accurate, general answer earns credit for understanding and stops below the top band because it names no place and quotes no figures. The mark scheme rewards a developed point tied to a specific named example. Fixing this needs a case-study bank to exist first, which is why the sequence matters: build the bank of named examples with figures, then work on the writing, rather than teaching technique to a student with nothing specific to use.

faqs.question: How many case studies does a Cambridge 0460 candidate actually need?
faqs.answer: Three or four per theme, so about eleven in total, each with a named place, a few figures, dates where relevant and two or three consequences that can be deployed in an extended answer. Eleven examples learned properly beat thirty vague ones, because an extended answer has room for one example used well. Ask to see the bank as a document with a count rather than accepting that case studies have been covered, since the difference is visible immediately.

faqs.question: Can my child use Dubai and the UAE as geography case studies?
faqs.answer: Yes. Examiners credit what is geographically valid and specific, not what is British. Dubai supplies strong material: rapid migration-driven population growth for the settlement theme, Dubai Creek as an original settlement site, Palm Jumeirah and the coastline for coastal management, Jebel Ali for industrial location, Ras Al Khor for conservation against development pressure. The condition is rigour, which means published figures and named features rather than impressions, and not relying on local examples for every topic.

faqs.question: Did my child's Dubai school enter Paper 3 coursework or Paper 4?
faqs.answer: Ask the head of geography, because it is the single most important thing to establish and families frequently do not know. Paper 3 is a school-based assignment built on fieldwork the centre runs and supervises. Paper 4 is the alternative to coursework, a written paper testing the same investigative skills on data it supplies. Both carry the same share of the grade and need entirely different preparation, so planning any support before confirming this is guesswork.

faqs.question: What can a tutor legitimately do on the 0460 coursework route?
faqs.answer: Teach the underlying geography, explain what a sound methodology looks like, discuss ways of presenting data, and give feedback on what your child has already written. What a tutor will not do is produce any part of work that must be the student's own, and that limit holds whatever a provider advertises. If somebody offers to supply a finished investigation, treat it as a warning about everything else they say, because for the student it is a malpractice risk.

faqs.question: When can fieldwork realistically be done in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Roughly between November and March. Outdoor data collection in the Dubai summer is uncomfortable to the point of being unsafe for a class, which is why centres running the coursework route schedule fieldwork in the cooler months. Ramadan also shortens school days and shifts session timings later in the evening. If your child is on the Paper 3 route, ask the department in September for its fieldwork window and internal deadlines, because tutoring has to be planned around them rather than the other way round.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks on describe questions in the skills paper?
faqs.answer: Because they explain instead. Asked to describe a distribution, students often give reasons, when the mark scheme wanted the overall pattern, the exceptions to it, and figures or grid references quoted from the source. It is a command-word problem rather than a knowledge problem, and it responds quickly to being counted: keep a tally of mismatches across three papers and the count typically halves, because the student starts reading the command word deliberately.

faqs.question: How do I know if the problem is geography or arithmetic?
faqs.answer: Look at which skills marks are lost. If the method is right and the number is wrong, it is arithmetic: scale conversion done without converting, a gradient expressed without a ratio, a value misread between graph gridlines. Those are maths skills appearing in a geography paper, and they are faster and cheaper to fix as maths. If the method itself is wrong, it is geography. A marked skills paper broken out per sub-skill answers this in about ten minutes.

faqs.question: Is a rising mock score always a sign of progress in 0460?
faqs.answer: Not on its own. Check the attempt rate alongside it, meaning how many questions were attempted out of those set. A candidate who improves their score while attempting fewer questions has got slower, and the final extended answer is worth more than the marks gained elsewhere. Mock papers also differ between Dubai centres and are marked internally against the school's own boundary estimate, so treat the grade as a rough position and the breakdown underneath it as the real information.

faqs.question: What should be in a 0460 tutor's written feedback?
faqs.answer: Three things. The score broken out by sub-skill or by question part rather than as a total, the specific lost mark named on any extended answer, and the next target stated as something countable. 'Needs to use more case studies' is not a target. 'Three named examples for the natural environment theme, each with figures, by the end of the month' is. Ask for feedback in that form at the start, because retrospective targets are chosen to match whatever happened.

faqs.question: How many sessions does the extended-answer problem usually take?
faqs.answer: Two to four before movement shows, and longer than the skills work because the repair depends on the case-study bank being in place. The mechanism is mechanical once a student has material: make a point, develop it with a consequence, support it with a specific detail from a named example. Practised on three or four timed answers with the lost mark identified each time, the mark on comparable questions usually rises within a month. A single improved answer on a different topic proves nothing.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a geography tutor to our home in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer in-home visits anywhere in the UAE, and home visits are a service we run only in India. Dubai students are taught one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. For geography that is a real advantage: the map extract, photograph or graph sits on a shared screen with both people annotating the same image, and a cross-section can be compared against the criteria line by line in a way a paper copy passed across a table does not allow.

faqs.question: Is Geography a sensible IGCSE option for a Dubai student aiming at sciences later?
faqs.answer: It can be, and the reason is the skills paper. Reading sources accurately, quoting figures, describing patterns and handling data are transferable, and students heading towards science or economics at sixth form often find the data-response habits useful. The honest caution is workload shape: 0460 has three components and a case-study memory load, so it is not the light option it is sometimes assumed to be. Ask the department for the component structure before the option form is signed.

faqs.question: How late is too late to start 0460 support before the exams?
faqs.answer: Six to eight weeks still buys real marks, and the plan narrows. At that point there is no time to build a full case-study bank, so the work goes to the skills paper, which is the fastest-moving component, plus command-word accuracy and timing. Two timed papers with a per-question clock and a sweep of the mechanical sub-skills will often recover more marks in that window than attempting to deepen content knowledge across three themes.

The written note names the weakest stream, the first target and the sessions it should take.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-global-perspective.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Cambridge IGCSE Global Perspectives 0457 and the humanities subjects Dubai students usually sit alongside it. Each has worked through a real Individual Report with a student: narrowing a research question, finding sources worth citing, and cutting a 2,400-word draft back inside the limit without losing the argument.

intro.heading: 0457 is a skills qualification, and that is why it goes wrong quietly
paragraphs: Global Perspectives is the one IGCSE on your child's timetable with no body of content to revise. There is no list of dates, no set text, no equations. What Cambridge assesses in syllabus 0457 is a set of transferable skills: framing a research question, finding evidence, judging whether a source can be trusted, holding several perspectives in view at once, working inside a team, and reflecting honestly on your own part in it. A student who is strong in English and History can still drift towards a grade 5 here, because none of the habits that earn marks in those subjects earn marks in this one.

The drift is quiet because the warning signs do not look like trouble. Your child has a topic. They have pages of notes. They have a draft. What they do not have, usually, is a question narrow enough to answer in 1,500 to 2,000 words, or sources that disagree with each other, or any sentence in the report that weighs one perspective against another rather than setting them side by side. Dubai teachers running 0457 across a class of twenty-four cannot sit with each student for the two hours that fixing a research question takes. That gap is the whole reason parents search for a Cambridge IGCSE Global Perspectives 0457 home tutor in Dubai in the first place.

The second thing that fails is the Team Project. It fails for social reasons, not academic ones. Four students agree on a topic in October, one changes school in January, two are in different mock timetables in February, and the outcome arrives half-built. The individual reflective writing attached to it is then produced in a rush, and it narrates what the group did instead of examining what the student themselves contributed, learned and would change. That is a mark-losing habit a tutor can correct in two sessions, and it is almost always still correctable late, because the reflection is written after the project rather than during it.

On delivery, we are blunt, because a search for a home tutor in Dubai deserves a straight answer. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India. Everything we do for a Dubai family is one-to-one online over live video, with a shared screen on the draft, the source booklet or the mark criteria. For 0457 specifically that is not a compromise. The subject is read, written, researched and discussed; there is no practical to set up and no apparatus to pass across a table. A screen-shared document with two people editing the same paragraph is a better teaching surface than two people leaning over one laptop.

It also widens the pool enormously. Global Perspectives is taught by a small number of teachers in each Dubai school, often by whoever has the timetable space, and the number of adults in this city who have taken a cohort through all three 0457 components is small. Hiring by postcode means hiring whoever is free within a twenty-minute drive of your villa. Hiring online means hiring for the component your child is actually stuck on. That trade is the single strongest argument for online delivery in this subject, and it costs nothing in teaching quality.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-global-perspective.programmesIntro: Dubai families reach 0457 from three different directions, and the gap to close is different in each case. These are the routes we see most, with what the transition into Global Perspectives actually demands.

programmes.name: Cambridge Upper Secondary (IGCSE)
programmes.description: The two-year course most British-curriculum schools in Dubai run before A Level or the IB Diploma. Global Perspectives 0457 sits in the Humanities and Social Sciences group and is commonly taken as a ninth or tenth subject. It is a single-tier syllabus, graded A* to G, with no Core and Extended split, so every candidate sits the same written paper and submits the same two pieces of coursework-style work to Cambridge.
programmes.countryNote: Across Dubai, UK-curriculum schools account for the largest share of private enrolment, and almost all of them certificate at 16 through Cambridge or Pearson. KHDA inspects these schools annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, and inspection reports comment on how well a school develops research and critical-thinking skills. 0457 is often the subject that evidence sits on, which is why some Dubai schools make it compulsory.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The programme Dubai's IB-continuum schools run instead of IGCSE. MYP students who move into a Cambridge school at Year 10 arrive with strong inquiry habits and a real advantage in 0457, because MYP Individuals and Societies already asks for multiple perspectives. What they usually lack is the discipline of a Cambridge word limit and a formal reference list, both of which carry marks.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools let MYP students certificate externally in one or two Cambridge subjects, and Global Perspectives is a popular choice because the skills overlap. If your child is moving from an MYP school in Nad Al Sheba or Al Barsha into a Cambridge cohort mid-course, the first job is mapping which 0457 assessment objectives their MYP work already evidences and which are genuinely new.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The destination for a large share of Dubai's IGCSE cohort. A student who has done 0457 properly walks into Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay with the two hardest habits already built: framing a researchable question and evaluating a source rather than quoting it. That transfer is worth saying out loud to a Year 11 student who thinks Global Perspectives is the subject they can afford to coast in.
programmes.countryNote: International Baccalaureate students make up a small but growing share of Dubai private-school enrolment, and the emirate's 2026-27 intake adds three new IB schools among seven openings. For a Dubai family choosing between A Level and the Diploma at 16, 0457 performance is a fair predictor of how a student will handle the Diploma's independent components.

programmes.name: Cambridge AS Level Global Perspectives and Research
programmes.description: The direct continuation of 0457 for students staying with Cambridge. It takes the same skills and raises the load: a longer research report, a written exam with harder source material, and a presentation. Students who finished 0457 without ever learning to write an evaluative paragraph find this step brutal, which is one practical reason to fix the habit at IGCSE rather than later.
programmes.countryNote: A number of Dubai sixth forms offer this alongside conventional A Levels, and admissions tutors treat it as evidence of independent research capability. It is not a required subject for any UAE university route we can verify, so treat it as a skills choice rather than a tick-box, and check the current entry requirements with the university directly.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-global-perspective.subjectsIntro: 0457 is rarely the only subject in the conversation. These are the Cambridge IGCSE subjects Dubai students most often sit alongside Global Perspectives, with what each one actually assesses and where marks go missing.

subjects.name: Global Perspectives (0457)
subjects.description: A written paper on unseen sources, an Individual Report of 1,500 to 2,000 words, and a Team Project with individual reflective writing. Marks are lost on research questions that cannot be answered, on perspectives that are listed rather than weighed, and on reflection that describes the project instead of the student's own contribution.

subjects.name: History (0470)
subjects.description: Source-based questions plus essay questions on a depth study. Dubai students often take it with 0457 and confuse the two skill sets: History rewards inference from a source in context, while 0457 rewards judging whether the source should be believed at all. Keeping those two habits separate is worth real marks in both.

subjects.name: Geography (0460)
subjects.description: Physical and human geography with a compulsory skills paper and a fieldwork-style alternative paper. Shares subject matter with 0457 topics such as water, migration and sustainable living, so a student taking both can reuse case-study knowledge, though never the same written work.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (0500)
subjects.description: Reading response and directed writing. The paraphrasing and summary skills assessed here are exactly what rescue an over-long 0457 Individual Report, which is why we often run the two together for a student who writes 2,500 words when the limit is 2,000.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: Reading, writing, listening and speaking for students working in English as an additional language. Many Dubai 0457 candidates sit this rather than First Language, and their reports lose marks on register and connectives rather than on thinking, which is a fixable and fast win.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Multiple choice and structured questions on markets, the macroeconomy and development. Pairs naturally with 0457 topics such as trade and aid or poverty and inequality, and teaches the data-handling habits the written paper rewards.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Short-answer and case-study questions across marketing, finance, operations and people. Students bring the evaluation structure from Business into 0457 well, but tend to import its formulaic conclusion paragraph, which reads thin against the 0457 criteria.

subjects.name: Sociology (0495)
subjects.description: Research methods plus topic sections including family, education, and crime and deviance. The research-methods half is close to 0457's evaluation of evidence, and students who study both usually make the strongest reliability judgements in the written paper.

subjects.name: Environmental Management (0680)
subjects.description: Two written papers on resources, water, ecosystems, hazards and sustainability, one of which is built on a resource booklet. Overlaps heavily with 0457's sustainable living and water, food and agriculture topics, and the resource-booklet skill transfers straight across.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: Two written papers with no coursework. Included here because 0457 Individual Reports frequently use statistics badly, and a student who can read a percentage change and spot a misleading axis makes far better use of the data they find.

subjects.description: Theory and algorithmic problem-solving across two papers. Shares 0457's digital world territory, and students taking both tend to write the sharpest reports on data privacy and artificial intelligence because they understand the mechanism, not just the headline.

Sits alongside the Arabic that KHDA requires in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, and a student who can read a local source in Arabic has access to perspectives their classmates cannot cite.

sections.heading: What a parent searching for a 0457 home tutor in Dubai is really asking
paragraphs: A Cambridge IGCSE Global Perspectives 0457 home tutor in Dubai is almost never wanted for general study support. The search follows a specific event: a teacher's comment that the research question will not work, a Team Project that has collapsed, or a mock written paper that came back several grades below the student's other subjects. What the family wants is someone who knows the three components and can fix the one that is broken. IB Gram delivers that one-to-one online, over live video, in Gulf Standard Time.

The in-home version of this exists in Dubai and it is worth understanding before you choose. Independent tutors advertise villa visits across the city, and for a Year 7 student who needs an adult sitting beside them, proximity has real value. For 0457 it has much less. The subject is a shared document, a source booklet and a conversation about whether an argument holds. A tutor and a student editing the same paragraph on a screen they can both see and both type into is a more precise teaching surface than two people sharing one laptop at a kitchen table.

The cost of proximity in this city is the pool it leaves you with. Global Perspectives is taught by one or two teachers in most Dubai schools, and the number of adults in the emirate who have taken a cohort through Component 1, Component 2 and Component 3 is genuinely small. Hiring within a twenty-minute drive of Arabian Ranches or Mirdif means hiring whoever that radius contains, which in practice is a humanities generalist who has read the syllabus rather than taught it. Hiring online means hiring for the component in trouble.

So the honest answer to the search is this. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. What a Dubai family gets instead is a 0457 specialist, a weekly slot that survives a 6pm traffic jam, and written feedback on the actual draft between sessions. The table further down this page sets the two formats against each other on rate, travel and tutor pool so you can judge the trade yourself rather than take our word for it.

sections.heading: The three components of 0457 and what each one is worth
paragraphs: Global Perspectives is assessed three ways, and the two that carry the most weight are not sat in an exam hall. That single fact changes how a family should plan the year. Roughly seventy per cent of the grade is submitted work with internal school deadlines months before the exam series, which means a student who treats 0457 as something to revise in April has already lost most of the available marks before revision starts.

Component 1 is the written paper. The student receives source material they have not seen and answers questions that ask them to analyse it, judge how far it can be relied on, and construct a reasoned position. There is nothing to memorise. What improves the mark is the habit of asking who produced a source, for whom, with what interest, and what is missing from it. That habit is trainable in a handful of sessions and it is the single highest-yield thing a tutor does for this component.

Component 2, the Individual Report, is the biggest single block of marks. The student chooses one of the global topics on the current syllabus list, frames a research question, and answers it in 1,500 to 2,000 words using evidence and distinct perspectives. Almost every lost mark here traces back to the question. A question like 'Is climate change bad?' cannot be answered evaluatively; a question like 'How far should the UAE prioritise desalination over demand reduction in managing its water supply?' forces perspectives, evidence and a judgement. Getting that sentence right is two hours of work that protects forty per cent of a grade.

Component 3 is the Team Project: a collaborative outcome plus the student's own reflective writing about their part in it. The reflection is marked on the student's individual thinking, not on how impressive the group's outcome was, and that is the distinction most candidates miss. A reflection that reads as a diary of what the team did will sit in the lower bands however good the project was. One that examines a decision the student made, why it was wrong, and what they would do differently, sits much higher.
