sections.heading: Where 0457 marks are actually lost, in order of cost
paragraphs: After enough Individual Reports, the failure modes repeat. The most expensive is the research question. A question that invites a yes or a no, or that asks whether something is good, gives the student nowhere to go but description. The report then becomes a well-written survey of a topic, which sits in the middle bands no matter how much reading went into it. Rewriting the question in week two is cheap; rewriting it in week ten means rewriting the report.

The second is perspective depth. Candidates learn early that 0457 wants multiple perspectives, and many deliver that literally: a paragraph on what one group thinks, a paragraph on another, a paragraph on a third. Nothing in that structure compares them. The criteria reward reasoning about why perspectives differ, what each is based on, and which holds up better against the evidence. One properly comparative paragraph does more for the mark than three descriptive ones, and it is shorter, which also helps with the limit.

Third is evidence quality. A report built on the first page of search results will cite a campaigning organisation and a news aggregator and treat both as neutral. The written paper tests exactly this skill, so the student is being assessed twice on the same weakness. Teaching a student to ask who funded a claim, when it was published, and whether anyone credible disputes it raises both the report and the paper at once, which makes it the best value hour on the whole syllabus.

Fourth, and infuriating because it has nothing to do with ability: the mechanical rules. A report over the word limit, a missing reference list, quoted material that is not attributed, a reflection written in the plural when it should be in the first person singular. These cost marks that the student has already earned elsewhere. Half an hour spent on the submission checklist in the last fortnight is usually worth more than another hour of content.
bullets: Rewrite the research question until it cannot be answered with yes or no
Build one comparative paragraph per perspective pair, not one descriptive paragraph each
Record the date, author and funder of every source as you read it
Check the word count against the current syllabus limit, not against last year's
Write the reflection in the first person about your own decisions

sections.heading: In-home 0457 support in Dubai versus one-to-one online
paragraphs: Here is the comparison set out plainly, with market rates attributed to the places that publish them. The figures below are what the Dubai market charges, not an IB Gram price list. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180 to 350 an hour, with independent home tutors advertising up to AED 500. Among online providers, EdFlik lists rates from AED 45 to 65, Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, and Unitors quotes IGCSE tuition from AED 150. TutorChase publishes AED 270 for specialist support. Those are their published numbers, read in October 2026.

What the table makes visible is that the in-home premium is mostly travel. A tutor crossing Dubai at 4.30pm to reach Arabian Ranches is spending an unpaid hour in the car, and that hour is priced into the rate whether the invoice names it or not. The same money spent online buys either more time with the same calibre of tutor or a more specialist tutor for the same time. For a subject with three distinct assessed components and a small teaching population, the specialist option is usually the better purchase.

The second thing it makes visible is scheduling. An in-home slot has to sit in the window a tutor can physically reach, which in practice means 4pm to 6pm on weekdays. An online slot can sit at 7.30pm after dinner, at 9am on a Saturday when a student can give the Individual Report two clear hours, or after Iftar during Ramadan. For Year 11 students in Dubai with mock timetables and co-curriculars, that flexibility decides whether the sessions actually happen.

None of this makes in-home tutoring a bad choice for every subject or every age. For a Year 6 student who will not sit still without an adult present, it is the right call. For a sixteen-year-old whose problem is that their research question does not work, it is paying a travel premium for a service the subject does not need. We would rather say that clearly than pretend the choice is obvious.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with an Individual Report
paragraphs: This matters more in 0457 than in almost any other IGCSE, because seventy per cent of the grade is work submitted under the student's own name and authenticated by the school. Cambridge requires that submitted work is the candidate's own. A tutor who crosses that line does not just behave badly; they expose the student to a malpractice finding that can cost the whole qualification. So the boundary needs stating, not hinting at.

A tutor may teach the skills: how to narrow a question, how to search beyond the first page, how to test a source, how to structure an evaluative paragraph, how to reference. A tutor may read a draft the student has written and say where the argument weakens, which paragraph is description masquerading as analysis, and which section is over the limit. A tutor may model the skill on a different topic entirely, which is often the clearest way to teach it. A tutor may show the student Cambridge's criteria and ask them to mark their own work against them.

A tutor may not supply sentences for the report, restructure it on the student's behalf, choose the research question for them, or hand over a plan so detailed that the thinking has been done elsewhere. A tutor may not edit a draft line by line into a finished piece. And no tutor, however experienced, should be producing text that will be submitted as a candidate's own work. We say no to those requests, and we would rather lose the booking than put a sixteen-year-old in front of an academic-honesty panel.

There is a practical version of this boundary that parents find useful. If the student could explain, unprompted, why every paragraph in their report is there and where every citation came from, the support was teaching. If they could not, something has gone wrong regardless of who typed it. That test is also roughly what a school will apply when it authenticates the submission, so it is worth applying it first at home.

sections.heading: Command terms and the unseen source booklet
paragraphs: Component 1 is the component students most often assume they cannot prepare for, and they are wrong. The sources change; the question types do not. A student who has worked through eight or ten past source booklets under time recognises the shape of what is being asked within the first minute, and spends the paper answering rather than deciding what the answer should look like. That recognition is the whole of exam technique in this subject.

The command terms do real work. 'Identify' wants the thing itself and no explanation; writing a paragraph there spends time that is needed later. 'Explain' wants a causal chain, which means at least two linked steps, not a restated fact. 'Compare' wants explicit connective language between the two things being compared, in the same sentence. 'Evaluate' and 'To what extent' want a judgement with reasons attached, and a mark scheme will not reward a judgement that arrives in the last line with nothing behind it. Students lose marks they have earned by answering the question they expected rather than the one printed.

Timing is the other half. With roughly 75 minutes and a booklet to read, a student who reads everything twice before writing runs out of paper time. The workable pattern is to read the question set first, then read the sources once with the questions in mind, annotating as they go. That order feels wrong to a careful reader and has to be practised until it feels normal, which is three or four timed attempts, not one.

The marking is where the session value sits. A student can produce ten timed papers alone and improve very little, because they cannot see what a marker would not credit. Going through one paper line by line with someone who knows the criteria, and keeping a running list of that student's own repeated errors, is what turns practice into a grade movement. By the fourth paper the list is usually three items long, and those three items are the tutoring plan.
bullets: Read the questions before the sources, then annotate on a single pass
Answer 'identify' in a phrase and save the prose for 'explain' and 'evaluate'
Use explicit comparative connectives rather than two separate statements
Keep a personal error list from every marked paper and re-check it before the next

sections.heading: The Cambridge calendar for 0457, counted backwards
paragraphs: Every deadline that matters in this subject sits before the exam, and most families discover that too late. Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, with a March series available in some regions. Entries close months ahead of the papers, internal deadlines for submitted work sit earlier still, and the school's exams officer is the person who controls all of it. A parent who asks for the school's internal 0457 submission dates in September has already removed the commonest cause of a lost grade.

The published March 2027 key dates make the gap concrete. Cambridge sets final entries for that series on 27 November 2026, forecast grades on 27 February 2027, the exam period from 3 February to 4 March 2027, results on Cambridge Direct on 13 May 2027 and certificates in late June. Read that sequence backwards and the implication is plain: the Individual Report has to be finished while the student is still sitting mocks, not after them.

One technical point costs candidates their papers every year. Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Dubai parents who download a timetable from a search result rather than from their own school are taking a risk that has nothing to do with how well their child knows the syllabus. Ask the school which zone it sits in, in writing.

For families on Pearson rather than Cambridge, the shape is the same with different dates: International GCSE series run in May and June and in November, with the November 2026 final timetable running to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so check the live PDF rather than a date quoted on a page like this one.

sections.heading: What 0457 counts for after Year 11 in the UAE
paragraphs: Parents reasonably ask whether a subject with no content is worth a place on the timetable. Two answers are useful here, and both are about what happens next rather than about the grade itself. The first is the UAE Ministry of Education equivalency route, which matters for any student intending to study at a UAE university or to have their school certificate attested locally.

For the British track, the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. That last detail is worth knowing, because at least one competing tutoring site tells UAE parents they need six IGCSE subjects, which is not what the published rule says. Global Perspectives can sit inside that count of five like any other accredited subject. Verify the current wording on the Ministry's own channels before you rely on it for a university application; we describe the process, we do not perform it.

The second answer is skills transfer, and it is the stronger one. A student who has fought through a 0457 research question and a 2,000-word evidence-based report arrives at Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay or an AS research report already knowing how to do the two hardest things those assessments ask for. Dubai sixth forms see that difference. It is also the reason some schools in the emirate make Global Perspectives compulsory rather than optional, and why a grade 4 in it is a poorer signal about Year 12 readiness than a grade 4 in a content subject.

What 0457 is not is a requirement for anything. No UAE university route we can verify demands it, and tutoring in it is certainly not required for equivalency, admission or progression. Anyone telling a Dubai parent otherwise is manufacturing urgency. Take it because the skills are the ones every later qualification assumes, and support it if the Individual Report has stalled, not because a page on the internet implied a door closes without it.

faqs.question: What does a Cambridge IGCSE Global Perspectives 0457 home tutor actually do in a session?
faqs.answer: Most sessions do one of four things. They test and narrow a research question until it cannot be answered with a yes or a no. They mark a timed Component 1 source paper line by line and build a list of that student's repeated errors. They read a section of the Individual Report and show where description is standing in for evaluation. Or they rebuild a Team Project reflection so it examines the student's own decisions rather than narrating what the group did. The work is diagnostic, not a second set of lessons, and it happens online over live video with the document shared on screen.

faqs.question: Can a 0457 tutor help with the Individual Report without breaking Cambridge's rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor may teach how to frame a question, find and test sources, structure an evaluative paragraph and reference properly, and may read a draft your child has written and say where the argument weakens. A tutor may not supply sentences, choose the question, restructure the report on your child's behalf or edit it into a finished piece. The school authenticates that submitted work is the candidate's own, so the test we apply is simple: your child should be able to explain, unprompted, why every paragraph is there and where every citation came from.

faqs.question: How long is the 0457 Individual Report supposed to be?
faqs.answer: The current syllabus sets the Individual Report at 1,500 to 2,000 words, and the limit is enforced, so a 2,600-word draft is a problem to solve rather than a sign of effort. Over-length reports are usually over-length for a diagnosable reason: three descriptive paragraphs where one comparative paragraph would do, or a long introduction explaining why the topic matters. Cutting those raises the mark as well as the word count. Always confirm the figure against the syllabus on cambridgeinternational.org for your child's exam series, because Cambridge revises specifications on a cycle and last year's limit may not be this year's.

faqs.question: My child's 0457 Team Project group has stopped replying. What happens now?
faqs.answer: This is more common than schools admit, and it is usually recoverable, because the reflective writing attached to the project is marked on your child's individual thinking rather than on how polished the group's outcome was. The first step is a written message to the subject teacher describing what has happened and what your child has contributed, with dates. The second is to build the reflection around a real decision your child made inside the collapse: what they tried, why it did not work, what they would do differently. That is exactly what the criteria reward.

faqs.question: Is Global Perspectives 0457 an easy IGCSE to add as a ninth or tenth subject?
faqs.answer: It is lighter on content and heavier on process, which is not the same as easy. There is nothing to memorise, so a student who revises well gets no advantage, and roughly seventy per cent of the grade is submitted work with school deadlines falling months before the exam. Students who treat it as the subject they can leave until April routinely underperform their other grades in it. Added deliberately, with the Individual Report started early, it is a reasonable ninth or tenth subject and it builds habits every later qualification assumes. Added casually, it becomes the grade that drags an otherwise strong set down.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a 0457 tutor to our villa in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Every session for a Dubai family is one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, with the draft, source booklet or mark criteria shared on screen. For this subject that is genuinely the better format rather than a fallback: the work is reading, writing and argument, both people can type into the same document, and you are choosing from tutors who have taught all three components instead of from whoever lives within a twenty-minute drive.

faqs.question: When in the Dubai school year should 0457 report work actually start?
faqs.answer: Term 1 of Year 11 at the latest, and Year 10 if the school sets the topic that early. The reason is sequencing rather than diligence: the research question has to be tested and rejected a few times before one survives, and that cannot be compressed into the fortnight before an internal deadline. Dubai schools typically set their submission dates in Term 2, immediately after the January mock window, so a family working backwards from that date has the autumn to use. Arriving three weeks out means the first hour goes on deciding what can realistically be saved.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a global, national, local and personal perspective in 0457?
faqs.answer: They are different scales of viewpoint, and the report is marked on how well a student distinguishes them. A global perspective is how an issue looks across countries or to international bodies. A national perspective is the position of a particular country, including its government and media. A local perspective is a specific community's experience, which for a Dubai student might be a neighbourhood, a school or an industry in the emirate. A personal perspective is the student's own reasoned view, arrived at from the evidence rather than asserted at the start. Collapsing two of these into one is a common and costly error.

faqs.question: Which 0457 global topic should my child choose for the Individual Report?
faqs.answer: Choose for evidence availability, not for interest. The best topic is one where credible sources genuinely disagree and where your child can reach a local perspective they can verify. A Dubai student writing on water, food and agriculture, on sustainable living or on the digital world has real local material available: desalination and demand management, construction and heat, or data regulation in the Gulf. A topic chosen because it sounds impressive but has only campaigning material behind it produces a report with nothing to evaluate. Check which topics appear on the current syllabus list before committing, as the list is revised periodically.

faqs.question: How is the 0457 written paper different from a History or Geography source question?
faqs.answer: History asks what a source tells you about its context and how far it is useful for a particular enquiry. Geography usually asks you to read data accurately and apply a concept. The 0457 written paper asks something narrower and harder: whether the source should be believed at all, who produced it and with what interest, what it leaves out, and what a reasoned position looks like once you have weighed several of them. Students who import a History structure write well and score in the middle bands. Separating the two habits deliberately is worth marks in both subjects.

faqs.question: Does Global Perspectives 0457 count towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: Equivalency for the British track is published as five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. An accredited subject such as Global Perspectives can sit inside that count. Confirm the current wording through the Ministry's own channels or your school's registrar before relying on it, and be wary of any tutoring site quoting a different subject count. IB Gram describes the process; we do not perform or guarantee it.

faqs.question: Can my child sit 0457 as a private candidate in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Private candidate entry depends entirely on whether a Dubai exam centre will accept an external entry for this syllabus, and 0457 is harder than most because two of the three components are submitted work that a centre has to authenticate and upload. Some centres decline it for exactly that reason. The practical route is to contact Cambridge exam centres in the emirate directly, ask specifically about 0457 rather than about IGCSEs in general, and confirm the submitted-work arrangements in writing before paying any entry fee. Your child's current school is the first place to ask.

faqs.question: Can 0457 sessions run in the evening or during Ramadan in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most do. With no travel attached to a session, the slot can sit wherever it genuinely works: after 6.30pm when the school run and traffic are done, at 9am on a Saturday when a student can give the Individual Report two uninterrupted hours, or after Iftar during Ramadan when a shorter, later session is more productive than an exhausted afternoon one. We also move the slot during mock weeks rather than pretending a student can absorb a new skill the night before a Maths paper. Tell us the constraints and we schedule around them.

faqs.question: What happens in the first 0457 session with a new tutor?
faqs.answer: The tutor will have read whatever you sent in advance, so the session starts with the work rather than with introductions. Typically your child talks through their research question while the tutor pushes on whether it can be answered, or they work through one marked source question to establish where the technique is breaking. By the end there should be a named problem and a first fix, plus a short written note to you on what the tutor thinks is actually wrong. The trial is free, there are no card details taken up front, and if the fit is poor we look for a different tutor.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-global-perspective.closingHeading: Start with the component that has stalled
dubai/cambridge-igcse-global-perspective.closingBody: If the Individual Report has no workable question, if the Team Project has fallen apart, or if a mock Component 1 paper came back below every other subject, that is the thing to fix first. Send us the school, the year group and the draft or marked script, and we will match a Cambridge IGCSE Global Perspectives 0457 specialist and run a free trial lesson online before anything is paid for. You will get a written note on what the tutor thinks is actually wrong, whether or not you carry on. Sessions are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time; home visits are an India-only service.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-global-perspective.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach Cambridge IGCSE Global Perspectives 0457 and the humanities subjects that compete with it for a family's tutoring budget. Rates are agreed before the first paid session, in AED, with what each session includes written down rather than implied.

intro.heading: The price of 0457 support is a scarcity question, not a difficulty question
paragraphs: Global Perspectives is not a hard subject in the way Further Maths is hard. It is a hard subject to buy support for, which is a different problem and the one that shows up in the price. Across Dubai's private schools, 0457 is usually taught by one or two members of a humanities department, sometimes by whoever had timetable space, and the pool of adults in this city who have taken a full cohort through the written paper, the Individual Report and the Team Project is small. A thin supply of people who can teach something, against steady demand from Year 11 parents in February, produces exactly the rate you would expect.

That is why the quoted figure for 0457 often sits above what the same family pays for Maths or Biology support, and why a parent comparing hourly rates across subjects without understanding supply reaches the wrong conclusion. The useful comparison is not AED per hour against another subject. It is total AED against the thing that actually needs fixing, because roughly seventy per cent of the grade is submitted work and the submitted work either has a workable research question or it does not.

Dubai also has an unusually wide published spread. At the budget end, Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. In the middle, Unitors quotes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and specialist exam-year support at AED 200 to 450 or more. TutorChase publishes AED 270. At the top, BartyED publishes AED 650. Those are each provider's own published numbers, read in October 2026, and the twenty-fold gap between the extremes tells you the word tutor is doing a lot of different jobs.

What you cannot find anywhere in that market is the figure most parents actually need: how many hours a 0457 problem takes to fix. Three of the six best-ranking pages in this cluster publish no price at all, and one of them asks the price in its own FAQ and then declines to answer it. The two that do quote use US dollars, a currency no Dubai family pays school fees in. So the sections below cost the work by component rather than by the hour, and name the assumptions.

On delivery, so there is no ambiguity before you read a rate table: IB Gram runs one-to-one online sessions over live video, in Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and home visits are a service we run only in India. That matters to the pricing conversation because an in-home rate in this city carries an unpaid hour of driving inside it, and an online rate does not.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-global-perspective.programmesIntro: Where a student sits in the Cambridge or IB sequence changes the sensible spend, because the cost of a missed 0457 deadline is not the same in Year 10 as it is six weeks before a series.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, first year
programmes.description: The cheapest point at which to buy 0457 support, because the only thing that needs fixing is technique. A handful of sessions on source evaluation and on what an evaluative paragraph looks like, spread across a term, costs a fraction of the emergency block a family buys in February and produces a better Individual Report. Few parents spend here, which is why so many spend more later.
programmes.countryNote: Most Dubai British-curriculum schools start IGCSE teaching in Year 10 and set the first 0457 skills tasks within the first term. Asking the school in September for its internal submission dates, and whether Global Perspectives is compulsory or optional at that school, is the single piece of free information that determines the whole budget.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, exam year
programmes.description: Where almost all 0457 spend happens, and where it is most expensive per mark. Two deadlines collide with mocks: the Individual Report and the Team Project reflection. A family arriving in Term 2 is typically buying four to six sessions on the report plus a short written-paper block, which at market specialist rates is a four-figure AED commitment rather than a few hundred.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai mock windows usually fall in January, immediately before the heaviest coursework period, so Year 11 tutoring demand across the emirate peaks in a narrow few weeks. Specialist availability in a thin subject tightens at exactly that point, which is the practical reason rates for scarce subjects firm up closer to a series.

programmes.name: Cambridge AS Global Perspectives and Research
programmes.description: The continuation for students staying with Cambridge after IGCSE. Rates for AS and A Level support sit above IGCSE across the Dubai market, and the research report is longer and harder, so a student who never learned to write evaluatively at 0457 pays twice: once for the IGCSE rescue and again at sixteen.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai sixth forms run this alongside conventional A Levels. It is not a verified entry requirement for any UAE university route, so treat the spend as a skills investment and confirm any admissions assumption directly with the university rather than with a tutoring provider.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The destination for a large share of Dubai's IGCSE cohort, and the reason 0457 spend has a return beyond the certificate. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay assess the same two habits 0457 trains: framing a researchable question and evaluating a source. Dubai market rates for IB support run above IGCSE, so skills bought cheaply at 15 displace dearer remediation at 17.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, three of them International Baccalaureate, alongside a 6 per cent rise in enrolment during 2025-26. More Diploma places in the emirate means more students arriving at TOK and the Extended Essay from a Cambridge IGCSE background.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-global-perspective.subjectsIntro: A tutoring budget is spent across subjects, not on one. These are the Cambridge IGCSE subjects Dubai families most often fund alongside 0457, with the hours each usually takes and why the figures differ so much.

subjects.name: Global Perspectives (0457)
subjects.description: Typically four to eight sessions, concentrated on the Individual Report and a written-paper block. Priced at the specialist end because the teaching population in the emirate is thin, not because the content is heavy. The hours are front-loaded: one session that fixes a research question protects the largest block of marks on the syllabus.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: The most heavily tutored IGCSE in Dubai and the cheapest per hour, because supply is deep. Families often run thirty or more sessions across two years. Useful as a price anchor: if a 0457 quote sits far above a Maths quote from the same provider, scarcity rather than opportunism is usually the reason.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (0500)
subjects.description: Six to twelve sessions is common, split between reading response and directed writing. Worth funding alongside 0457 for one specific reason: the summary and paraphrase skills assessed here are what bring a 2,500-word Individual Report back inside the limit without gutting the argument.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Usually eight to fifteen sessions, with demand peaking at data-response technique. Overlaps 0457's trade and aid and poverty and inequality topics, so a family funding both can ask one tutor to cover the shared evidence base rather than paying twice for the same reading.

subjects.name: History (0470)
subjects.description: Ten to twenty sessions is typical, most of it essay structure and source technique. Mid-band pricing in Dubai because supply is reasonable. Students taking it with 0457 need the two source habits kept separate, which is a teaching cost rather than an hours cost.

subjects.name: Biology (0610)
subjects.description: Fifteen to thirty sessions in an exam year, with a distinct cost spike around the alternative-to-practical paper. Included here because science tutoring usually consumes a Dubai family's budget first, and 0457 then gets whatever is left in February, which is the most expensive possible order.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620)
subjects.description: Similar hours to Biology and similar rates. The relevant point for budgeting is sequencing: science hours are spread over the year while 0457 hours are compressed into a six-week window, so the two compete badly unless the report work is started early.

subjects.name: Sociology (0495)
subjects.description: Six to twelve sessions, often concentrated on the extended evaluation questions. Priced close to 0457 because the teaching pool in Dubai is similarly thin, and genuinely complementary: the research-methods material is the same reliability thinking the 0457 written paper tests.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Eight to fifteen sessions, mostly case-study application and evaluation structure. Cheaper per hour than 0457 in this market. Students bring a serviceable evaluation habit across, though its formulaic conclusion paragraph reads thin against the 0457 criteria and has to be unlearned.

subjects.name: Geography (0460)
subjects.description: Ten to eighteen sessions, with the skills paper taking a disproportionate share. Shares case-study territory with 0457 topics such as water, migration and sustainable living, which is the clearest example of two funded subjects where the reading can be bought once.

subjects.name: Environmental Management (0680)
subjects.description: Eight to sixteen sessions, concentrated on the resource-booklet paper. Sits in the same thin-supply band as 0457 in Dubai, and the resource-interpretation skill transfers directly to 0457 source analysis, so a combined plan is more efficient than two separate ones.

subjects.name: Arabic as a Foreign Language (0544)
subjects.description: Hours vary more than any other subject here, from a handful of sessions to weekly support across two years, because starting points differ enormously. Relevant to a 0457 budget because KHDA requires Arabic in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, so it is rarely optional spending.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-global-perspective.regionsTitle: What the same 0457 hour costs across Dubai
dubai/cambridge-igcse-global-perspective.regionsIntro: The teaching is identical wherever a family lives. What changes across the emirate is the travel premium an in-home provider has to recover, and how late a session can realistically start.

regions.name: The Springs, The Meadows and Emirates Living
regions.note: A long way from the humanities-tutor supply around Al Barsha, so in-home quotes here sit at the upper end of the published 180 to 350 band. The online rate is the same figure a Jumeirah family pays, which is most of the argument in this community.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle
regions.note: Dense, affordable and badly served by school transport, so families here fund more tutoring per child than the emirate average. JVC parents are also the most likely to be offered a monthly package, and the most likely to be charged for sessions they could not attend.

regions.name: Al Furjan and Discovery Gardens
regions.note: Apartment living with limited quiet study space, which argues for shorter, more frequent sessions rather than two-hour blocks. No travel attached means a 45-minute slot is economically sensible here, where an in-home visit of that length never is.

regions.name: Palm Jumeirah
regions.note: Short distances but a single access road that adds unpredictable time at the end of the school day. In-home providers price the uncertainty, not the kilometres. An online slot at 7.30pm removes the variable entirely and costs the published online band.

regions.name: Town Square and Dubai South
regions.note: The furthest reach of most Dubai tutors' travel radius, where some will not visit at all and others add a surcharge they do not itemise. Families here see the widest gap between an in-home quote and an online one for the same calibre of tutor.

regions.name: Deira, Al Mamzar and Al Nahda
regions.note: Older, well-served by Indian and British curriculum schools, and highly price-sensitive. The budget online band of AED 33 to 65 is most actively marketed to these communities, which makes the question of what a cheap hour actually contains especially worth asking here.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: Large sibling groups and tight budgets, so cost per household matters more than cost per hour. Two children on alternating weekly slots with the same tutor is a common structure, and it is cheaper than two separate in-home visits by a wide margin.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai and Business Bay
regions.note: Parents working late, which pushes sessions past 7pm and makes written feedback between sessions part of what is being bought. Worth checking whether a quoted rate includes that feedback or treats it as a separate billable item.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha, Al Sufouh and Umm Suqeim
schoolClusters.note: The deepest tutor supply in Dubai and therefore the most competitive in-home pricing in the emirate. Students we support in this cluster usually sit 0457 as an additional subject, and their families are comparing a nearby generalist against an online specialist on cost as much as on quality.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai Hills, Meydan and Nad Al Sheba
schoolClusters.note: Newer secondary cohorts with small Year 11 groups, which thins the number of local teachers who have taken a cohort through all three 0457 components. Scarcity shows up directly in the quotes families receive here, and is the clearest case for paying for a specialist rather than for proximity.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai Silicon Oasis, Academic City and Mirdif
schoolClusters.note: A long commute in both directions, so in-home visits here consume an hour of a tutor's unpaid time and are priced accordingly. Families in this cluster are the most consistent users of Saturday morning sessions, which cost the same per hour but produce more report progress than a weekday evening.

sections.heading: What an online 0457 tutor costs in Dubai, with the sources
paragraphs: A Cambridge IGCSE Global Perspectives 0457 online tutor in Dubai costs between roughly AED 150 and AED 450 an hour at the qualified and specialist end of the market, with budget providers advertising from AED 33 and premium named tutors at AED 650. Those are published figures from the providers named in the table below, read in October 2026. IB Gram does not publish a fixed price list on this page, because the right number depends on the component and the hours, and we would rather quote you than have you read a figure that does not fit your child.

The spread is real rather than a presentation trick, and the bands correspond to different products. At AED 33 to 65 an hour you are typically buying a university student or an unqualified tutor working through content, often in a group or with recorded material. At AED 150 to 300 you are buying a qualified subject teacher online. At AED 200 to 450 you are buying someone who has taught the specific syllabus to a full cohort. At AED 500 and above you are usually paying for a named individual's reputation, which may or may not be the thing that fixes an Individual Report.

For a thin subject like 0457 the practical floor is higher than for Maths. There are very few people available at AED 60 an hour who have taught the written paper, the Individual Report and the Team Project, because that experience is rare in the emirate and the people who hold it do not compete at the budget end. A parent who insists on the lowest band for this subject usually gets a general humanities tutor reading the syllabus alongside the student, and that is not a bargain.

One further honesty point about rates on this page. Every figure named is a competitor's or a rate table's own published number with the month we read it, not an estimate we generated. No ranking page in this cluster cites a source for a single AED figure, and three publish no figures at all. If you compare quotes, ask each provider what the rate includes, whether it is per hour or per session, and whether written feedback between sessions is inside it or billed separately.

sections.heading: What moves the 0457 number in this emirate specifically
paragraphs: Four variables do most of the work in a Dubai quote, and none of them is the subject's difficulty. The first is how close the school's internal submission deadline is. Specialist availability in a thin subject tightens sharply in the weeks when every Year 11 cohort in the emirate hits the same coursework window, which in most Dubai schools falls between the January mocks and the end of Term 2. A family buying in October is shopping in a loose market; a family buying in February is not.

The second is session length. A 60-minute slot and a 90-minute slot are not priced proportionally by most providers, and for Individual Report work the longer session is usually better value because the first fifteen minutes are spent reloading where the draft got to. For written-paper technique the opposite holds: a timed paper plus a review fits an hour, and a longer session adds fatigue rather than marks.

The third is what the rate contains. Written feedback on a draft between sessions, a marked timed paper returned with annotations, a handover note for the subject teacher: some providers include these and some bill them. Two quotes that look twenty per cent apart can be forty per cent apart once you ask. This is the question parents most often skip and the one that changes the total most.

The fourth is the student's starting point, which sounds obvious and is routinely mispriced. A student whose research question works and whose problem is evaluative writing needs three or four sessions. A student six weeks from a deadline with a 2,600-word descriptive draft on an unanswerable question needs the question rebuilt first, and that is a different and larger job. An honest provider will tell you which of those you have after reading the draft, before quoting.
bullets: Buy before the January mock window, not after it
Ask whether the rate is per hour or per session, and what length a session is
Confirm in writing whether between-session feedback is included
Send the draft before asking for a quote, so the quote reflects the real job

sections.heading: Hours by component: what a 0457 plan actually costs end to end
paragraphs: Hourly rates are the wrong unit for a decision. What a family needs is the total, and the total is driven by hours per component. The table below sets out the session counts we see most often, with an indicative AED range built by multiplying those hours against the published specialist band of AED 200 to 450. The arithmetic is yours to check and the assumptions are stated, which is more than any page currently ranking for this query offers.

Two patterns are worth naming. The first is that the Individual Report dominates the spend, which is appropriate, because it carries the largest single block of marks on the syllabus. The second is that the written paper is the cheapest component to improve and the one most families fund last. Four timed papers, marked and reviewed with a running error list, moves a Component 1 grade more reliably than any amount of content work, and it costs four sessions.

The Team Project reflection is the sleeper. It is short work, usually two sessions, and it is the component where a late intervention still pays, because the reflection is written after the project and is marked on the student's own thinking rather than on the group's outcome. Families who have written off the Team Project because the group collapsed are often two sessions away from recovering most of those marks.

A whole-course plan from Term 1 of Year 10 looks expensive on paper and is usually cheaper in practice than the February emergency, because the emergency block buys the same number of hours at peak-demand availability and spends the first of them on triage. Spreading the same spend across eighteen months also lets a family stop early if the student no longer needs it, which a compressed block never allows.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context against Dubai school fees
paragraphs: A tutoring figure means nothing on its own. It means something against what a Dubai family is already spending on education, and that denominator has just been fixed. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there will be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion out of AED 2.5 billion in total. For families budgeting a Year 11 tutoring plan, that removes one variable from the sum.

The scale of the market is worth stating too, because it explains the depth of tutoring supply in some subjects and the thinness in others. Dubai had 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with UK-curriculum schools taking the largest share of enrolment at around 37 per cent, Indian curriculum next, then US, with the International Baccalaureate at a smaller share. A city that size produces plenty of Maths tutors. It produces very few people who have taught three assessed components of Global Perspectives.

Against those fees, the component plans in the previous table are a modest line item, and that is the honest framing rather than a sales one. A four-session written-paper block at market specialist rates is a small fraction of a term's fees. A full weekly plan across the exam year is not small, and a family should ask whether the subject in question is the one that most needs the money. Sometimes it is not, and we will say so.

One cost families forget: exam entry as a private candidate, if the student is not entered through their school. That is a centre-set fee, it varies, and it is not something a tutoring provider should be quoting. Ask the centre directly, in writing, and ask specifically about 0457, because two of its three components are submitted work the centre has to authenticate and some centres decline external entries for that reason alone.

sections.heading: Where the money gets wasted: buying hours instead of a diagnosis
paragraphs: The most common way a Dubai family overspends on 0457 is by booking a block of hours before anyone has read the student's work. The sessions then start with content: a tour of the global topics, a general discussion of perspectives, some advice about structure. Three hours in, the research question is still unanswerable, and the family has paid specialist rates for a seminar. This happens because booking hours is easy to sell and a diagnosis is not.

The fix is cheap and almost nobody asks for it. Send the draft, the teacher's comment or the mock script before you book anything. A tutor who has read the actual work can tell you in writing whether the problem is the question, the evaluation, the evidence or the word count, and how many sessions each of those takes. If a provider will not do that before taking payment, that is useful information about what you are buying.

The second waste is paying for presence. A student can sit through twelve hours of pleasant conversation about global issues and improve very little, because improvement in this subject comes from work being marked against criteria and the same error being named repeatedly until it stops. Ask what evidence each session produces. If the answer is a feeling that things are going well, the hours are not working, whatever the rate.

The third is duplicating school provision. Dubai schools run intervention sessions, and some run 0457 clinics in the run-up to internal deadlines. Those are included in fees that KHDA has frozen for 2026-27. Paying market specialist rates for coverage the school already gives is a straightforward loss, and five minutes of asking the subject teacher what is already available prevents it.

sections.heading: What a 0457 quote should contain before you pay
paragraphs: Dubai parents are given a number and almost never given a scope. A quote that names only an hourly rate is incomplete, and the gap is where the disagreements later live. Below is what we think a quote should state, and what we state ourselves. None of it is complicated; it is simply not standard in this market, where one ranking competitor asks about price in its own FAQ and then declines to answer.

It should say the currency and the unit: AED, per hour or per session, with the session length named. It should say what the figure includes: live teaching time, written feedback on a draft between sessions, marked timed papers, a handover note. It should say what it excludes. It should say how cancellation works, with notice periods in hours and whether a missed session is chargeable. It should say whether anything is conditional, including a free trial, and state the condition on the same page rather than in a footnote.

It should also be honest about availability. Global Perspectives is a thin subject, and there are weeks in a Dubai year when the right tutor is not free. The correct response to that is to say so and offer a date, not to substitute a general humanities tutor at the specialist rate. We would rather lose a booking than place a tutor who has not taught the component that is broken.

Finally, it should carry no outcome promise. No tutor can promise a grade or a point improvement, and any Dubai provider offering a certain 7, a promised grade jump or money back linked to a result is making a claim they cannot stand behind. Be sceptical of anything in that shape, including the softer versions that quote a percentage of students achieving something without stating the sample, the date or the method.

sections.heading: Permits, legality and why the cheapest hour can be the riskiest
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and price is tangled up with that fact. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's own service page is 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', which lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Because the permit costs nothing, a low hourly rate is not evidence that a tutor has skipped it, and a high rate is not evidence that they hold one. The two are independent, and parents are often sold the opposite impression. What is true is that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you, and a figure circulating online as a specific penalty has not been verified.

There is a related rule that affects who a family should be hiring at any price. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat that as press-reported and verify it against the current ADEK policy document before relying on it, but the direction is clear: your child's own classroom teacher, hired privately, is the arrangement to avoid rather than the one to seek.

For completeness about what IB Gram is and is not: we are an independent tutor-matching platform. We hold no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or the IB, and we do not operate a centre or office in the UAE. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a specific thing issued to institutes with physical premises. Any provider describing itself with a regulator's name attached as an endorsement is making a claim worth checking.

process.title: Send the work before asking for a number
process.description: A draft report, a teacher comment or a marked mock script. A quote built on the actual work reflects the actual job, and the written diagnosis you get back tells you whether the problem is one session or six. We do this before any payment.

process.title: Get the scope in writing
process.description: Rate in AED, per hour or per session, session length, what is included between sessions, cancellation notice, and whether a missed session is chargeable. If anything is conditional, including the trial, the condition is stated with it rather than later.

process.title: Use the free trial lesson
process.description: One session at no cost before any payment, with no card details taken to book it. Your child works on their own material and you receive a short written note on what the tutor believes is actually wrong, whether or not you continue afterwards.

process.title: Agree a session count, not a subscription
process.description: Most 0457 work is a block with an end: four to six sessions on the Individual Report, four on the written paper, two on the Team Project reflection. We prefer a stated finish to a rolling monthly charge that nobody remembers to cancel.

process.title: Pause rather than pay through dead weeks
process.description: Mock fortnights, exam weeks and family travel are not good teaching time. Sessions pause, and during Ramadan the slot moves to post-Iftar hours rather than being pushed into an afternoon when nothing lands.

process.title: Stop when the evidence says to
process.description: When the report is referenced and inside the limit and the error list on timed papers has cleared, the block ends. We write a handover note for the school's subject teacher and you stop spending. A plan with no finish condition is a subscription, not a plan.

whyPoints.description: Global Perspectives is a thin subject in this emirate. When nobody with three-component experience is available, we give you a date instead of substituting a general humanities tutor at the specialist rate and hoping you do not notice.

whyPoints.description: No grade promise, no point-improvement claim, no percentage of students achieving anything without a sample, a date and a method. Those claims are common in this search result and none of them can be stood behind.

faqs.question: How much does a Cambridge IGCSE Global Perspectives 0457 online tutor cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates for qualified online subject tutors run from about AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, and specialist exam-year support from AED 200 to AED 450 or more. Budget providers advertise from AED 33 to 65 and premium named tutors up to AED 650. Those are each provider's own published figures, read in October 2026. For 0457 specifically the practical floor sits higher than for Maths, because very few tutors available at the budget end have taught the written paper, the Individual Report and the Team Project. We quote after reading your child's work rather than publishing a flat rate.

faqs.question: Why is 0457 tutoring priced above IGCSE Maths tutoring in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Supply, not difficulty. Maths is taught by a large department in every school in the emirate and tutored by hundreds of people, so competition holds the rate down. Global Perspectives is usually taught by one or two members of a humanities department, and the number of adults in Dubai who have taken a full cohort through all three assessed components is small. A thin supply meeting concentrated Year 11 demand in a six-week window produces a higher figure. If a provider quotes the same rate for both subjects, it is worth asking what their 0457 tutor has actually taught.

faqs.question: Is a monthly 0457 package better value than paying by the hour?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the discount is rarely the reason. Monthly packages advertised in Dubai start around AED 799 for eight online sessions, which is cheaper per hour than most specialist rates. The risks are that unused sessions expire, that the package renews automatically, and that it commits you to a cadence the subject does not need. Most 0457 work is a block with a natural end: four to six sessions on the Individual Report, four on the written paper. If a package fits that shape, take it. If it rolls monthly with no finish condition, you are buying a subscription.

faqs.question: Do 0457 tutoring rates rise closer to the Cambridge exam series?
faqs.answer: The headline rate usually holds. What changes is availability, and in a thin subject that has the same effect on what you pay. Dubai schools cluster mocks in January and internal coursework deadlines in Term 2, so every Year 11 cohort in the emirate wants the same few specialists in the same weeks. Families buying then are choosing from whoever is left, which in practice means paying the specialist band for a generalist or accepting a later start. Buying in Term 1 costs the same per hour and gets you a different quality of tutor.

faqs.question: Does the quoted AED rate include feedback on an Individual Report draft between sessions?
faqs.answer: It should, and you should confirm it in writing, because this is where two quotes that look similar diverge most. Reading a 2,000-word draft properly against Cambridge criteria and writing useful comments on it takes real time, and some providers include that in the session rate while others bill it separately or do not offer it. For 0457 it is not an extra; most of the value in report work happens between sessions, when the student revises against named comments. Our rate includes written feedback on the student's own draft.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper 0457 tutor at AED 60 an hour worth trying?
faqs.answer: For general content coverage or essay-writing habits, a tutor in the budget band can be genuinely useful and Dubai families use them well. For 0457 the risk is specific: the person is likely to be reading the syllabus alongside your child rather than teaching it, and the failure mode of this subject is an unanswerable research question that a non-specialist will not recognise as the problem. If you do try the budget band, ask directly whether the tutor has taught the Individual Report and the Team Project to a cohort before, and ask for the answer in writing.

faqs.question: How much should a complete 0457 Individual Report plan cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Four to six sessions is typical, which at the published specialist band of AED 200 to 450 an hour works out at roughly AED 800 to 2,700 in total. That buys testing and narrowing the research question, building a source set that genuinely disagrees, structuring the report, writing the first evaluative paragraph, and two cycles of feedback and revision on the student's own draft. A rescue three weeks before a school deadline costs about the same but delivers less, because the first session goes on triage and the question may no longer be changeable.

faqs.question: Are 0457 sessions charged per hour or per 90-minute session?
faqs.answer: Both exist in the Dubai market and the distinction matters more than the headline rate. A 90-minute session is not usually priced at one and a half times the hourly figure, so for Individual Report work it is often better value: the first ten or fifteen minutes of any session go on reloading where the draft got to, and a longer block spends proportionally less time on that. For written-paper technique an hour is the better unit, because a timed paper plus a line-by-line review fits it and anything longer adds fatigue rather than marks. Ask which unit a quote uses.

faqs.question: Does the price of 0457 tutoring in Dubai include VAT, and what should the invoice show?
faqs.answer: Ask the provider directly and get the answer in writing, because the treatment of tuition fees depends on the provider's own registration status and we will not state a general VAT position for the sector without a Federal Tax Authority citation. What a parent should insist on is an invoice that shows the amount in AED, what the charge covers, the number and length of sessions, and the tax position clearly on its face, with a tax registration number if the provider holds one. A quote given verbally with no invoice behind it is the thing to avoid.

faqs.question: Can two students share one online 0457 session and split the cost?
faqs.answer: It can work and it often should not. Two students at a similar standard working on the written paper can share a session productively, because source analysis is discussable and the marking review benefits from a second view. Individual Report work does not share, because each student has a different research question and the hour collapses into two half-sessions. The honest version of the saving is that a shared written-paper block cuts the cost per family roughly in half, while shared report work halves the price and more than halves the value.

faqs.question: What does the free trial lesson include for 0457, and what is the condition?
faqs.answer: One full session at no cost, before any payment, with no card details required to book it. Your child works on their own material, usually their draft or a marked mock paper, and afterwards you receive a short written note from the tutor on what they believe is actually wrong and how many sessions each part would take. The condition is simply that it is one session per student, and the material has to be sent in advance for it to be useful. If the fit is poor you say so and we look for a different tutor.

faqs.question: Does a 0457 tutor in Dubai need a MoHRE permit, and does that change the price?
faqs.answer: Individuals providing private lessons in the UAE need a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and those operating without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, so it has no effect on what a tutor needs to charge. That is the useful point for a parent: a low rate is not evidence of an unpermitted tutor and a high rate is not evidence of a permitted one. Ask the question separately from the price.

faqs.question: What happens to our fees if we pause 0457 sessions during the January mocks?
faqs.answer: With us, sessions pause and nothing is charged for the gap, because a student absorbing new technique the night before a Maths mock is not learning anything and you should not be paying for the pretence. Across the Dubai market the answer varies, and it is worth asking before you commit: some monthly packages charge through pauses, some expire unused sessions, and some require notice measured in days rather than hours. Get the cancellation and pause terms in writing alongside the rate, because this is the clause families discover late.

faqs.question: How does the cost of 0457 support compare with Dubai private school fees?
faqs.answer: Against a term's fees, a four-session written-paper block at market specialist rates is a small line item, and a five-session Individual Report plan is a modest one. A full weekly plan across the exam year is not small and deserves a harder question about whether this is the subject that most needs the money. One helpful fixed point for 2026-27 budgeting: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai will not rise for the year, under the emirate's AED 1.5 billion economic incentives package, so the denominator in that calculation is known.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-global-perspective.tutorsIntro: The teachers listed below work with Dubai students on Cambridge IGCSE Global Perspectives 0457: testing research questions, marking source evaluation, commenting on report drafts and coaching the reflective paper. Each has taken a cohort through the course, which in a research subject matters more than subject expertise alone.

intro.heading: The subject where effort and marks come apart
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE Global Perspectives 0457 produces a particular kind of parental frustration. The student is working. There are tabs open, there is a document with headings, there is a folder of articles. Then the mark comes back in the middle of the range and nobody can explain what went wrong, because unlike maths there is no wrong answer to point at and unlike history there is no missing date. The explanation is almost always the same: the work was research-shaped rather than assessed-shaped, and nothing in the file was ever measured against what the criteria reward.

The course is assessed three ways. There is a written examination of one hour fifteen minutes, worth 30% of the grade, answered from source material rather than from memorised content. There is the Individual Report, a piece of personal research of 1,500 to 2,000 words on a global topic from the syllabus list, worth 35%. And there is the Team Project, worth the remaining 35%, which combines a collaborative outcome with a personal reflective paper of roughly 700 to 1,000 words. No part of that is content you can revise in the ordinary sense, which is exactly why it rewards evidence-led teaching and punishes vague effort.

What the syllabus actually assesses is a set of named capabilities: researching a question, analysing information, evaluating sources and arguments, reflecting on your own thinking and on the team's work, collaborating, and communicating the result. Each of those is observable. A student either has a research question that can be answered in two thousand words or has a topic. They either evaluate their sources or list them. They either reflect on what changed in their own view or summarise what the team did. The gap between those pairs is where the marks live, and each gap is visible in a document long before the deadline.

That is the whole argument for an evidence-led approach in this subject specifically. In the first six weeks a 0457 tutor should produce four things: a research question that has survived being argued with, a source-evaluation grid in which at least one of the student's own favourite sources has been downgraded, a commented draft that names where argument has been replaced by description, and a reflection written to the criteria rather than as a diary entry. A parent who holds those four documents can see the state of the project. A parent holding a progress message cannot.

Lessons run one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, with the draft or the source on a shared screen. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. For 0457 that is more than a logistics note. The report requires a genuine local or national perspective alongside a global one, and a Dubai student has excellent local evidence available, from government open data to the emirate's own published statistics. The work is in choosing a question those sources can actually answer.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-global-perspective.programmesIntro: Four situations in which Dubai students meet 0457, each needing a different first session. The situation matters more than the year group, because it determines what the first document should be.

programmes.name: 0457 as a timetabled option across Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: The standard route, where the school teaches the skills explicitly and runs the Team Project as a class activity. Support here is usually targeted: the research question, the source evaluation, and the reflective paper. The first document should be a question tested to destruction, because everything downstream depends on it being answerable.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools vary widely in how much curriculum time 0457 receives, and several run it in a reduced block alongside the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies periods. Where time is short, the Team Project tends to be compressed and the reflective paper written in a hurry, which is why reflection is the component most often underperforming in this market.

programmes.name: 0457 carried alongside nine or ten other IGCSEs
programmes.description: For many candidates 0457 is the eleventh subject and the first to be deprioritised when science and maths deadlines collide. The honest support here is scheduling and scope control: a research question narrow enough to be finished, and a plan that puts the report ahead of exam preparation because the deadline is fixed and earlier.
programmes.countryNote: The pressure is sharpest in the Dubai winter term, when mocks for other subjects land in the same weeks as the internal 0457 deadlines. Families who ask in September which school deadline comes first almost always find it is the Global Perspectives one, which is the opposite of what the subject's reputation suggests.

programmes.name: 0457 as preparation for the IB Diploma core
programmes.description: A student going on to the IB Diploma will meet the same demands again in larger form: a research question in the Extended Essay, evaluation of knowledge claims in Theory of Knowledge, and reflection throughout. A 0457 report done properly is genuine preparation; one assembled from summarised articles teaches a habit that costs marks later.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai has one of the denser concentrations of IB schools in the region, and many families move from a British-curriculum IGCSE programme into the Diploma at sixteen. Treating 0457 as practice for the Diploma core rather than as a soft option is the single most useful reframing available to that group of students.

programmes.name: After 0457: AS Global Perspectives and Research
programmes.description: The post-16 continuation raises the research demand substantially: a longer independent study, a formal literature base and a defended argument. Students who reached a strong 0457 grade by narrowing a question well and evaluating sources honestly are prepared. Those who reached it on fluent writing alone find the research component unfamiliar.
programmes.countryNote: A smaller number of Dubai schools offer the post-16 course than offer 0457 itself, so a student who wants to continue should check availability in Year 11 rather than assume it. Where it is not offered, the Extended Essay in the IB Diploma or an independent project qualification covers similar ground.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-global-perspective.subjectsIntro: 0457 is researched rather than taught, so the useful list is of topics from the syllabus and what local evidence a Dubai student can realistically reach for each. These are the areas our 0457 students most often work in.

subjects.name: Water, food and agriculture
subjects.description: Strong for a Dubai candidate because desalination, food import dependence and controlled-environment agriculture are all documented locally and nationally. The trap is writing a report about water in general; the mark comes from a question narrow enough that local and global evidence can both be brought to bear.

subjects.name: Sustainable living
subjects.description: Energy use, waste, building standards and consumption. Workable locally, with the risk that the student ends up describing initiatives rather than evaluating whether they work. A report that compares a stated target with a published outcome scores considerably better than one that lists schemes.

subjects.name: Urbanisation
subjects.description: Few students anywhere have a better case study on their doorstep, and few over-use it more. The successful reports narrow hard: a single aspect of urban growth, examined with a named local source and a contrasting case from a different income context.

subjects.name: Transport systems
subjects.description: Metro, road capacity, cycling infrastructure and freight. The local evidence base is unusually good, including published ridership and network data, which makes this one of the few topics where a 0457 candidate in Dubai can build an argument on primary statistics rather than commentary.

subjects.name: Migration
subjects.description: A topic where perspective is the whole assessment: the same movement of people reads differently from the origin country, the destination economy and the individual household. A report that presents three genuinely different perspectives, rather than three sources agreeing, is what the criteria reward here.

subjects.name: Fuel and energy
subjects.description: Supply, transition, cost and security. Rich in published national and international data, and vulnerable to the commonest 0457 failure: a report that is accurate, well written and makes no argument because the student never decided what the question was asking them to judge.

subjects.name: Employment
subjects.description: Automation, youth unemployment, labour mobility and the informal economy. Works well where the student can compare a national statistic with a global trend and explain the difference, which is a higher-order move than describing either one on its own.

subjects.name: Education for all
subjects.description: Access, quality and cost. Deliverable locally through published sector data, including the structure and scale of a private-school market that served 387,441 students across 227 schools in Dubai in 2024-25, offering 17 curricula. A strong topic for a student who can resist writing about their own school.

subjects.name: Disease and health
subjects.description: Prevention, access and the gap between health systems. Demands care with sources, since health claims circulate widely in unreliable form, which makes it a good topic for a candidate whose source evaluation is already a strength and a poor one for a candidate whose is not.

subjects.name: Human rights
subjects.description: A topic where candidates most often substitute conviction for evidence. The criteria reward perspectives supported by sources and a reflection on how the student's own view changed, not the strength of the view itself. Handled with discipline it produces some of the best reports in the subject.

subjects.name: Trade and aid
subjects.description: Flows, dependency, conditionality and effectiveness. Among the most evidence-rich topics on the list, and one where a Dubai student can draw on the emirate's position as a re-export hub as a genuinely local perspective rather than a decorative mention.

subjects.name: Digital world
subjects.description: Access, data, misinformation and the effects of online life. Attractive to students and the hardest to keep narrow, because every sub-question opens three more. A report here succeeds or fails on whether the question was cut down to something two thousand words can answer.

subjects.name: Changing communities
subjects.description: Demographic shift, identity and the effects of mobility. Well suited to a city where a large share of residents were born elsewhere, giving a candidate access to local perspective that is genuinely their own rather than borrowed from a published commentary.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-global-perspective.regionsTitle: Dubai communities, and the local evidence on each doorstep
dubai/cambridge-igcse-global-perspective.regionsIntro: The Individual Report needs a local or national perspective alongside the global one, and where a student lives shapes what local evidence is genuinely available to them. These are the communities our 0457 students write from, with the research angle each one opens.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Dubai Science Park
regions.note: Dense school and clinic corridor with heavy daytime traffic. A workable local angle for transport systems or education access, where the student can gather observational data rather than quoting a published commentary about somewhere else.

regions.name: Deira, Al Rigga and the Creek
regions.note: The historic trading district, with the souks, the abra crossings and the old port. The strongest local evidence base in the city for trade and aid or changing communities, and one that almost no competing candidate's report will use.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Coastal residential areas where beach management, water quality and tourism pressure are all observable. Suitable for a sustainable living question, provided the report moves past describing initiatives into evaluating published outcomes.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and Jumeirah Lakes Towers
regions.note: High-rise living at high density, with district cooling, waste management and vertical-community dynamics all on the doorstep. A good setting for urbanisation or sustainable living questions narrowed to a single building-scale issue.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: Established family suburbs with a wide mix of nationalities and school curricula. Useful for migration or changing communities, where the local perspective can be built from a student's own community rather than from secondary commentary.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: Technology and education cluster with concentrated student populations. Natural ground for digital world or education for all questions, and a reminder that a report needs a contrasting perspective from a very different income context.

regions.name: The Springs, Meadows and Emirates Living
regions.note: Low-rise villa communities with landscaped planting and high domestic water use. A concrete local angle for water, food and agriculture, where household consumption can be compared with published national figures.

regions.name: Dubai South and Expo City
regions.note: Planned development around aviation and logistics. Strong for transport systems, trade and aid, or employment questions, with the usual caution that a planning document states an intention rather than an outcome.

schoolClusters.city: Schools offering 0457 across Al Barsha, Tecom and the Marina
schoolClusters.note: Large British-curriculum cohorts where Global Perspectives is usually timetabled as a taught option with a class Team Project. Students from these schools generally need targeted help with the research question and the reflective paper rather than with the course as a whole.

schoolClusters.city: Schools serving Mirdif, Al Qusais and Al Warqa
schoolClusters.note: Mixed-curriculum cohorts carrying the mandatory UAE subjects alongside a full IGCSE programme. Where curriculum time for 0457 is compressed, the Team Project and the reflection are the parts most often rushed, and that is visible in the marks.

schoolClusters.city: Schools serving Dubai Hills, Dubailand and Academic City
schoolClusters.note: Newer secondary cohorts where 0457 is often recently introduced. Young departments hold fewer exemplar reports, so students have rarely seen what a top-band Individual Report reads like, which is the fastest gap for an external teacher to close.
