programmes.description: Arrives having studied a different depth study, a different core-content option, or a different exam board entirely. The first evidence needed is a content audit rather than a marked essay: a written list of what the new cohort has covered that this student has not, dated, so the gap is a finite list rather than a general anxiety.

A student who studied Russia arriving in a Germany cohort has a real content gap, and selling them essay technique first is the most common mistake in this market.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-history-0470-home-.subjectsIntro: Evidence in 0470 is organised by assessed skill, because that is how the marks are awarded. These are the ten things a marked script can show you, with what each is testing and what a weak answer looks like on the page.

subjects.name: The part (a) recall question
subjects.description: Describe or identify, answered in a few short factual points with no argument required. Candidates lose these marks by writing a paragraph where four bullet-level facts were wanted, which costs time rather than content, and the time is taken from part (c) at the end of the paper.

subjects.name: The part (b) explanation question
subjects.description: Asks why something happened and rewards a causal chain developed over two or three steps. The diagnostic is whether the answer links a cause to a consequence explicitly. Scripts that list four causes once each sit in the middle band however accurate the content is.

subjects.name: The part (c) judgement question
subjects.levels: 0470 Paper 1 · 10 marks, three times per paper
subjects.description: How far or to what extent, requiring both sides argued with precise evidence and a conclusion that weighs them. Thirty of Paper 1's sixty marks. The common ceiling is an answer that argues one side well, mentions the other in a sentence, and concludes by repeating the stronger side.

subjects.name: Source comprehension and inference
subjects.description: What a source says and what can be inferred beyond it. The marks are in the source, and the failure is importing remembered content instead of reading what is printed. Quick to diagnose from a script and quick to correct once the student sees it happening.

subjects.name: Cross-referencing two sources
subjects.description: Requires agreement and disagreement handled together, at the level of message rather than topic. Weak answers establish that both sources are about the same subject. Strong answers quote the specific claim in each that conflicts, then explain why two authors in those positions would differ.

subjects.name: Utility and reliability
subjects.description: The single largest source of lost marks in the paper. Writing that a source is biased scores nothing on its own. Utility depends on what you are trying to find out, and a partisan source is highly useful evidence of the attitude it expresses, which is the move most candidates never make.

subjects.name: Cartoon and visual sources
subjects.description: Needs the symbolism decoded, the figures identified and the message tied to the date and context rather than described. Candidates who narrate the picture score in the lowest band; candidates who explain what the cartoonist wanted the reader to think score in the highest.

subjects.name: The 12-mark source judgement
subjects.description: How far do the sources support a given statement. Answered by grouping the sources that support it, grouping those that do not, and reaching a verdict that refers to provenance. Working through the sources one at a time in printed order almost never reaches the top band.

subjects.name: Coursework argument and structure
subjects.description: One assignment on the depth study. What the criteria reward is a sustained argument supported by evidence with the counter-case genuinely engaged. The work must be the candidate's own throughout; a tutor marks where evidence is absent and explains what the criteria want.

subjects.name: Chronology, terminology and recall under pressure
subjects.description: Dates, names and sequence have to be automatic rather than retrievable, because two hours of writing leaves no capacity for recall effort. A written chronology test, repeated and timed, is the only honest evidence that this has happened, and it is the slowest thing in the course to build.

sections.heading: What a 0470 home tutor is hired to fix, and why marked work beats a visit
paragraphs: The search for a Cambridge IGCSE History 0470 home tutor in Dubai is usually a search for individual attention on written work. That instinct is right. Where it goes wrong is in assuming the attention has to arrive in a car. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or elsewhere in the UAE, because in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and the comparison below is why that is not the concession it sounds like.

In an essay subject the binding constraint is how much written work gets marked, and how fast it comes back. A tutor driving across Dubai for two sessions a week spends four or five hours in the car, and those hours come out of marking time. A student needs to attempt the same question type again while the annotation is still fresh in mind, which in practice means a two-day turnaround rather than a week. That is a scheduling fact, not a sales argument, and it is the reason the online file tends to be thicker than the in-home one at the same price.

The second real difference is the depth study. Every 0470 candidate studies one in detail, and Dubai schools do not all choose the same one. A visiting tutor must live within a feasible drive of your community and happen to have taught your child's option. Those two constraints multiply, and for a cohort entered for China or South Africa they multiply to very nearly nobody. Removing the drive leaves only the constraint that matters: whether the teacher has taken a cohort through that option and marked its essays.

There is one honest advantage to a visit that video does not reproduce. A tutor in the room controls the environment, which for a thirteen-year-old with no study habits is worth paying for. A Year 11 candidate writing timed essays and source answers is a different case; the work is the same work whether the marker is in the room or on a screen, and the annotation is legible either way.

sections.heading: The five documents a 0470 evidence file should hold
paragraphs: Six weeks of tutoring in an essay subject should leave five specific documents behind. None of them requires you to know history to read, and all five are specific enough to disagree with, which is the point.

The first is an annotated part (c) essay. Not a score: an essay with the levels written against it, the sentence marked where the argument stopped developing, and a note on whether the counter-case was argued or mentioned. The second is a marked source answer, ideally the 12-mark judgement, showing whether the sources were grouped or worked through in printed order. The third is a causal-link log: a running list of the connections the student keeps leaving implicit, which is the single most repeated fault in 0470 writing and the one that moves a part (b) from three marks to five.

The fourth is a dated chronology test with the misses recorded. This is the document families find least interesting and tutors find most predictive, because a candidate who cannot place the Munich Agreement or the Enabling Act in sequence without hesitating is going to spend exam capacity on retrieval that should be spent on argument. Repeating the same test at intervals makes recall measurable rather than assumed.

The fifth is a timed full paper with the minutes recorded per question alongside the marks earned. Two hours across three questions is forty minutes each, and the commonest pattern in Dubai scripts is a generous question one, a reasonable question two, and an unfinished part (c) on question three, which throws away the most valuable single mark allocation on the paper. That pattern is invisible in a grade and obvious in a log.

sections.heading: How a 10-mark 'how far' answer actually moves up the levels
paragraphs: Part (c) is worth ten marks and appears three times on Paper 1, so thirty of sixty marks and a fifth of the whole qualification rest on it. It is marked in levels rather than by points, which means marks are awarded for what kind of answer it is rather than for how many facts it contains. Understanding that distinction is usually worth two marks on its own.

The lowest band holds answers that describe. The student writes everything they know about the topic in the hope that the examiner will assemble an argument from it. The next band holds answers that argue one side, often well, with accurate and specific evidence, and either omit the other side or dispose of it in a clause. This is where the capable, well-revised Dubai candidate sits, and it is the most frustrating place to be because the student has done the work and cannot see what is missing.

The band above holds answers that argue both sides with evidence on each. Not a paragraph of argument and a sentence of concession: two developed cases, each supported by named, dated specifics. The top band adds a conclusion that weighs those two cases against one another and reaches a position because of the weighing. A conclusion that announces a view and then repeats the stronger paragraph is not a judgement; it is a summary wearing a judgement's clothes, and examiners are extremely practised at telling the difference.

What a marked script does is locate the answer in that sequence and name the move to the next level. For most candidates the move is mechanical: write the second case properly, then write a conclusion that uses the word because about the relationship between the two. Done twice on the same question type, four weeks apart, the improvement is visible in the annotation rather than inferred from a grade.

sections.heading: Part (a) and part (b): the marks everyone treats as warm-ups
paragraphs: Each Paper 1 question opens with a 4-mark part and a 6-mark part, which together carry ten of the question's twenty-five and thirty of the paper's sixty marks. Candidates treat them as a preamble to the real question, and the marked scripts show two distinct costs.

On part (a) the cost is time rather than content. The question asks for description or recall and wants a handful of short factual points. A student who writes a structured paragraph with an introduction has spent eight minutes earning four marks, and those eight minutes come directly out of the part (c) at the end of the paper. The correction is almost absurdly simple: four separate factual statements, no argument, no scene-setting, and move on. It is the cheapest intervention in the whole syllabus and it usually shows up in the next timed paper.

On part (b) the cost is content organisation. Six marks for explaining why something happened rewards a chain developed over two or three steps, so two reasons taken properly beat four reasons asserted. The repeated fault is listing: a student who writes that the Depression caused unemployment, which caused political instability, which caused support for extremism, has built a chain. A student who writes that there was unemployment, instability and extremism has written three nouns. The causal-link log exists precisely to make this visible, because it is the same fault every fortnight until someone names it.

These two corrections are worth doing first for a reason that is partly psychological. They move marks within two or three attempts, which buys the credibility needed for the slower work on judgement writing and chronology. A student who sees their own script improve believes the next instruction; a student told to be patient for a term does not.

sections.heading: Six source skills you can measure one at a time
paragraphs: Paper 2 is two hours, 50 marks and a third of the grade, and it is the component that responds fastest to teaching because it is a set of readable habits rather than a body of knowledge. The prescribed topic changes between series, which means the content cannot be the main work and the technique has to be.

The useful move is to stop treating it as one paper. There are six separable skills, each with its own failure mode, and each can be diagnosed and marked on its own. That matters for evidence, because a parent can then see that cross-referencing has moved while utility has not, instead of watching a single paper mark wobble for reasons nobody can name.

The largest single loss in the paper is the utility question, and the reason is a habit taught early and never corrected: writing that a source is biased and stopping. Every source is partial. A politician's speech is weak evidence of what happened and excellent evidence of what that politician wanted an audience to believe, and the mark is awarded for identifying what the source is useful for. Until a student makes that move they are capped, no matter how much content they know.

The table below sets out the six skills, the failure that shows up in scripts, and the drill that fixes it. Each is marked separately at the start of a block and again at the end, which is what converts six to ten sessions of source teaching into evidence rather than a feeling that it went well.

sections.heading: Draft feedback and the boundary a tutor holds
paragraphs: If your child's cohort sits Paper 3, 27% of the grade is a single assignment on the depth study, limited to 2,000 words and marked out of 40. It is the component where the question of what a tutor may legitimately do becomes sharpest, and where this market contains services that should be avoided entirely.

What a tutor can do with a draft is substantial. They can ask whether the question can be answered inside the word limit. They can mark every place where a claim is asserted without evidence. They can point out that the counter-case has not been engaged, that a paragraph is doing no work, or that a conclusion does not follow from what precedes it. They can explain what the published criteria reward and show, using an exemplar, what the difference between two bands reads like. All of that is teaching, and all of it is feedback on work the student has already produced.

What a tutor must never do is produce assessed material on a candidate's behalf, in whole or in part. The assignment has to be the student's own work from the first word to the last. Cambridge's regulations treat malpractice as the candidate's problem, which means the person who loses the entry is the child, not the service that sold the text. Competitor research in this market found a provider selling finished internal assessments outright; what they are really selling is a risk transferred entirely onto a sixteen-year-old.

There is a related boundary around materials. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are the board's copyright material, and a tutor who offers to supply them as downloads is telling you something about how else they operate. The correct route is to reference them, link to cambridgeinternational.org, and work through the school, which holds proper access. Most Dubai history departments release past material readily when a parent asks.

sections.heading: What progress looks like across one Dubai school term
paragraphs: A term is roughly twelve teaching weeks, which in a fortnightly marking rhythm is six marked scripts. That is enough to see a trend and short enough that a wrong plan can be abandoned without losing the year. What follows is the shape a term usually takes, written out so you can tell early whether yours is on it.

Weeks one and two are diagnosis. A timed part (c), a marked source answer, a chronology test, and a decision about which of the three is the binding constraint. Weeks three to six are the fast corrections: part (a) length, part (b) causal chains, provenance-first reading. These produce visible movement, and if they do not, the diagnosis was wrong and should be changed rather than repeated more loudly.

Weeks seven to ten are the slow work. Judgement writing at part (c) and the 12-mark source question are the two things that genuinely take a term, and they are also where the remaining marks are. Expect a dip here. A student who has been told to argue both sides will, for two or three attempts, do neither fluently, and a mock landing in this window can come back lower than the one before it. Being warned about that in week one is the difference between holding the plan and abandoning it at exactly the wrong moment.

Weeks eleven and twelve are consolidation: a timed full paper, marked inside two days, with the minutes recorded per question. By then the file holds six marked scripts in sequence, a causal-link log that should be shorter than it was, and two dated chronology tests. The table sets the same thing out as a checklist, and the honest use of it is to ask in week six whether what should exist does.

sections.heading: Reading your school's history data honestly
paragraphs: Parents in Dubai are given two kinds of information about how a child is doing in history, and both need interpreting rather than accepting. The first is internal: predicted grades, term assessments and mock results. The second is external: the school's published inspection outcome from KHDA, which oversees the quality of private education in Dubai and inspects on a six-band scale.

Internal history grades carry a specific distortion worth knowing about. Essay marking is a judgement, and judgements drift. A department marking generously in the autumn term so that students do not lose confidence will mark closer to the standard in the spring, and the student's apparent decline is the marking converging on reality rather than the student getting worse. The reverse happens too. The only way to see through it is to have a second marker apply the published levels to the same script, which is precisely what an external marked essay provides.

Predicted grades deserve similar care. A prediction is a professional estimate made for a purpose, often an application deadline, and it is not a measurement. A useful conversation with the head of history asks what the prediction is based on: which assessments, marked by whom, and against which criteria. A department that can answer that in detail is giving you reliable information. One that cannot is giving you an impression, which may still be correct but cannot be checked.

The inspection band is the least precise of the three for this purpose, because it is a whole-school judgement across phases and subjects rather than a statement about a single option set. Two questions get further. Ask how many students are in the Year 11 history set and who teaches them. And ask how often the department marks a full part (c) essay against the published levels, because a department doing that every three weeks produces candidates who need very little outside help, and one doing it twice a year produces the exact problem that brought you to this page.

faqs.question: How will I know a Cambridge IGCSE History 0470 tutor is working?
faqs.answer: By the documents, not the reports. Within six weeks you should hold an annotated part (c) essay with the levels written against it, a marked source answer showing whether the sources were grouped or answered in printed order, a causal-link log listing the connections your child keeps leaving implicit, a dated chronology test with the misses recorded, and a timed paper with minutes logged per question. All five can be read in ten minutes by someone who knows no history, and all five are specific enough to argue with.

faqs.question: Will a tutor visit our villa in Dubai Hills, or is the 0470 lesson online?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, and in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Lessons for Dubai families are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. In an essay subject that is an advantage rather than a compromise: a tutor who is not spending four hours a week in traffic marks more written work and returns it faster, and the choice of teacher is no longer limited to people who happen to live near your community and happen to know your depth study.

faqs.question: What does arguing both sides actually mean on a 10-mark 0470 question?
faqs.answer: Two developed cases, each supported by named and dated evidence, not one argument and a sentence of concession. A part (c) asking how far something was responsible wants a genuine case for and a genuine case against, roughly comparable in weight, followed by a conclusion that weighs them against one another. The commonest ceiling in Dubai scripts is an excellent single-sided answer with the other view mentioned in a clause. That answer is capped regardless of how much content the student knows, which is why it is so frustrating.

faqs.question: Why does my daughter get full marks on the first part and three out of ten on the last?
faqs.answer: Because the three parts want three different kinds of writing and only the first one rewards recall. Part (a) is four marks of short factual statements. Part (b) is six marks for a causal chain developed over two or three steps. Part (c) is ten marks for judgement: both sides argued, evidence specific, conclusion weighing the two. A student strong on recall will shine on part (a) and plateau on part (c) until someone marks a part (c) against the levels and shows them the specific structural move that is missing.

faqs.question: How many 0470 past-paper questions should be marked each week?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families imagine, marked better. One part (c) essay written under timing and properly annotated every fortnight, with a marked source answer in the alternate week, is a sustainable rhythm that produces six scripts a term. Volume without marking teaches almost nothing, because the student repeats the same fault with more confidence. The useful discipline is repeating a question type four weeks later to test whether the correction held, which is the only comparison that controls for the difficulty of the question.

faqs.question: What does a marked Paper 2 script actually show a parent?
faqs.answer: Which of six separable skills is costing marks. Comprehension errors mean your child is answering from memory instead of reading the printed source. A weak cross-reference means they established the topic rather than the conflicting claim. A utility answer that says the source is biased and stops is the single largest loss on the paper. A cartoon narrated rather than decoded is another. And the final 12-mark answer either groups the sources for and against or works through them in printed order, which is visible at a glance.

faqs.question: How does a tutor check my son has learned the right dates and names?
faqs.answer: With a written, timed chronology test, repeated at intervals, with the misses recorded each time. It is the least interesting document in the file and the most predictive. Two hours of exam writing leaves no spare capacity for effortful recall, so a candidate who hesitates over the sequence of events is spending on retrieval what should be spent on argument. Repeating the same test in week two and week eight turns recall from something everybody assumes into something you can see on paper.

faqs.question: Can a tutor comment on a 0470 coursework draft without breaking Cambridge rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is the correct use of the time. A tutor can mark every claim asserted without evidence, ask whether the question can be answered inside 2,000 words, point out that the counter-case has not been engaged, say that a conclusion does not follow, and explain what the published criteria reward. What a tutor must not do is produce assessed material on the candidate's behalf, in whole or in part. The assignment must be the student's own work throughout, because Cambridge's malpractice rules fall on the student rather than on anyone else.

faqs.question: How long before a 0470 grade actually moves?
faqs.answer: The short-part corrections usually show in two or three attempts: part (a) length and part (b) causal chains move quickly because they are mechanical. Judgement writing at part (c) and the 12-mark source question take most of a term, and there is a predictable dip in between, when a student instructed to argue both sides does neither fluently for a few weeks. A mock landing in that window can come back lower. Judge the work by the annotated scripts in sequence rather than by any single grade.

faqs.question: What should happen in the first 0470 session?
faqs.answer: Teaching, not an introduction to the syllabus. We read the marked script beforehand, so the hour goes on one real weakness identified in advance: the structure of a part (c), or provenance-first source reading, or the length of part (a) answers. By the end there should be a dated diagnosis naming whether the binding constraint is content, technique or timing, and a short written note to you saying what would be tackled first and what evidence would prove it worked.

faqs.question: Does my child need to memorise exact statistics for 0470?
faqs.answer: Precision matters more than volume. What earns marks is evidence specific enough to be unarguable: a named person, a dated event, a particular policy or treaty clause. A rough figure used confidently is worth more than a precise one recalled hesitantly, and a vague gesture at a decade is worth nothing. The practical standard is whether your child can support each major argument with two specifics they can state without pausing. That is a shorter list than most revision guides imply, and a harder one to fake.

faqs.question: How do history sessions fit around a Dubai school run and after-school sport?
faqs.answer: The slot is fixed in Gulf Standard Time and held weekly, which is possible precisely because nobody is driving to it. Families in Motor City, Sports City and the villa communities usually take a later slot after training, and those in apartment communities often prefer earlier. During Ramadan, when school days shorten and concentration moves to the evening, sessions commonly shift to a post-Iftar time for the month. None of that requires renegotiating a travel window, so the fortnightly marking rhythm survives the change.

faqs.question: What does a tutor do if the school has moved past a topic my child never understood?
faqs.answer: Decide honestly whether it is worth going back, and say which option is being dropped. A 0470 candidate carries two core-content periods, a depth study and a source topic at once, and there is not time to repair everything. The marked script ranks the gaps by marks available rather than by how uncomfortable each feels. Sometimes the answer is to leave a core-content topic thin and spend the hours on the source paper, which is a third of the grade and responds faster. A plan that pretends to cover everything covers nothing.

faqs.question: Can we see the tutor's marking against the official criteria?
faqs.answer: Yes, and you should ask for it from the first script. An annotated essay shows the level the answer sits in, the sentence where the argument stopped developing, and the specific move to the next band. What a tutor cannot do is hand you Cambridge's mark schemes or past papers as files, because those are the board's copyright material. The proper route is to reference them, link to cambridgeinternational.org, and work from the school's own stock, which most Dubai history departments release readily when a parent asks.

faqs.question: What if the first 0470 tutor is not the right match?
faqs.answer: We change the teacher and hand over the file with them, so the next person starts from the marked scripts and the causal-link log rather than re-diagnosing from scratch. Mismatch is usually about marking style rather than competence: a student near the top of the band needs a harsher marker, and one who has lost confidence needs the corrections sequenced to produce an early visible gain. Say so early. Six weeks of a wrong match costs more than the change does, in a year with a fixed number of fortnights in it.

intro.heading: What the 0470 syllabus actually contains
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE History 0470 is often described to parents as a general history course, and it is not. It is a specific, bounded syllabus with a core-content option, one depth study chosen by the school, and one prescribed source topic set for the series. A tutor who cannot name which of those your child is studying is not yet in a position to teach them, and a parent who knows all three can tell within one conversation whether the person on the other end of the call has done this before.

The assessment has three parts. Paper 1 runs two hours, carries 60 marks and is worth 40% of the grade; candidates answer three questions, two from the core content and one on the depth study, and every question splits into a 4-mark part, a 6-mark part and a 10-mark part. Paper 2 runs two hours, carries 50 marks and is worth 33%, and is answered entirely from a set of sources on the prescribed topic, closing with a 12-mark question on how far the sources support a given statement. The final 27% comes either from Paper 3 coursework, an assignment of up to 2,000 words marked out of 40, or from Paper 4 Alternative to Coursework, a one-hour written paper also worth 40 marks.

Behind those papers sit three distinct demands. The first is knowledge: recalling and selecting relevant material, which sounds trivial and is the thing most often underestimated, because two hours of continuous writing leaves no capacity for effortful retrieval. The second is explanation: constructing causation and reaching a supported judgement, which is what the 6-mark and 10-mark parts reward. The third is source handling: interpreting and evaluating historical evidence, which is the whole of Paper 2 and the skill Dubai candidates most consistently misunderstand, because they have been taught to label sources as biased rather than to ask what a source is useful for.

The core content comes in two options. Option B, International Relations since 1919, is taught by the overwhelming majority of Dubai schools and runs through seven key questions, from the fairness of the 1919 to 1923 peace settlements to events in the Gulf at the end of the century. Option A covers the nineteenth century from 1814 to 1914 and is taught by far fewer schools here, which has real consequences for how easy it is to find a teacher who has delivered it recently. The depth study is a separate choice again: Germany, Russia, the USA, China, South Africa, or the Israelis and Palestinians since 1945.

Lessons for Dubai families run one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, since in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. For a syllabus this specific, that matters: the teacher is chosen for having taught your child's exact option rather than for living within reach of your community, and in a market where Germany is taught far more often than China or South Africa, that distinction decides whether the first session is teaching or research.

The federal position is that private schools must follow Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies alongside their own curriculum.

programmes.name: After 0470: A Level History 9489 or IB Diploma History
programmes.description: Both routes assume the 0470 skills and then change their character. Source evaluation becomes historiographical rather than provenance-led, essays double in length, and independent reading replaces the textbook. A student who reached a strong 0470 grade through secure narrative and clean structure is well prepared; one who reached it by memorising model answers is not.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools run Cambridge AS and A Level History 9489 and IB Diploma History side by side, and the honest difference for most candidates is writing volume rather than difficulty. A question worth asking in Year 11 is which of the two the department has staffed consistently over the last three years, because continuity of teaching matters more than the label.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-history-0470-onlin.subjectsIntro: This is the content itself: the key questions of both core-content options, the depth studies, and the two skills the papers are built on. These are the units a 0470 session is actually spent inside.

subjects.name: The peace settlements, 1919-1923
subjects.description: Versailles and the other treaties, the aims of the leading powers at Paris, German reactions, and whether the settlement was fair. The commonest weakness is knowing the terms and not being able to argue the fairness question from more than one perspective, which is exactly what a part (c) demands.

subjects.name: The League of Nations, 1920-1939
subjects.description: Structure and membership, the 1920s successes and limits, the Manchurian and Abyssinian crises, and why the League failed. A rich source of causation questions, and one where candidates often confuse the League's organisational weaknesses with the specific decisions taken in each crisis.

subjects.name: The collapse of international peace by 1939
subjects.description: Nazi foreign policy, rearmament, the Rhineland, Anschluss, Munich in 1938, the Nazi-Soviet Pact and the invasion of Poland. The argument examiners return to is appeasement: whether it caused the war, delayed it, or was the only realistic policy available.

subjects.name: Who was to blame for the Cold War?
subjects.description: Yalta and Potsdam, the Soviet takeover of Eastern Europe, the Truman Doctrine and Marshall Plan in 1947, the Berlin Blockade of 1948 to 1949, and the founding of NATO. The question is a judgement question by design, so a one-sided answer cannot reach the upper levels however accurate it is.

subjects.name: American containment in practice
subjects.description: Korea from 1950 to 1953, the Cuban Missile Crisis of 1962, and American involvement in Vietnam. Three case studies with a shared question: how effective containment was. Students frequently narrate all three and compare none of them, which is where the marks sit.

subjects.name: Soviet control of Eastern Europe
subjects.description: Hungary in 1956, the Berlin Wall in 1961, Czechoslovakia in 1968, Solidarity in Poland, and the collapse of 1989. The analytical thread is how secure that control actually was, which requires treating each crisis as evidence rather than as a separate story.

subjects.name: Events in the Gulf, c.1970-2000
subjects.description: The Iranian revolution, the Iran-Iraq war, the invasion of Kuwait and the war of 1990 to 1991. The key question most relevant to students in this region and, in our experience, the one Dubai cohorts are most often taught last and fastest.

subjects.name: The nineteenth-century settlement, 1814-1871
subjects.description: The Congress of Vienna, the revolutions of 1830 and 1848, and the unifications of Italy and Germany. Taught by relatively few Dubai schools, so a cohort on Option A should establish early whether a prospective tutor has delivered it recently rather than merely studied it.

subjects.name: Empire, the Eastern Question and the road to 1914
subjects.description: The decline of Ottoman power, the Congress of Berlin, the partition of Africa, the alliance system, the Moroccan and Bosnian crises and the Balkan wars. Dense in treaties and alliances, which makes a dated spine more important here than anywhere else in the syllabus.

subjects.name: Depth Study: Germany, 1918-1945
subjects.levels: 0470 depth study · Paper 1 part (c) and Paper 4
subjects.description: Weimar's crises from 1919 to 1923, the Stresemann recovery, the Nazi rise, the Reichstag Fire and Enabling Act of 1933, the Night of the Long Knives, the Nuremberg Laws and life in the Third Reich. Taught in Dubai far more often than any other option.

subjects.name: Depth Study: Russia, 1905-1941
subjects.levels: 0470 depth study · Paper 1 part (c) and Paper 4
subjects.description: 1905, the February and October revolutions of 1917, the civil war, the New Economic Policy, Stalin's rise, collectivisation and the purges. Dense chronology with unfamiliar names, where the sequence has to be secure before judgement is attempted.

subjects.name: Depth Study: the USA, China, South Africa or the Israelis and Palestinians
subjects.levels: 0470 depth study · Paper 1 part (c) and Paper 4
subjects.description: The four less commonly taught options in this market: the USA from 1919 to 1941, China from around 1930 to 1990, South Africa from around 1940 to 1994, and the Israelis and Palestinians since 1945. Each is examined on evidence and argument against the published criteria.

subjects.name: Recall and selection of knowledge
subjects.description: The skill behind every mark on Paper 1. Not the volume of knowledge but the speed of access: a candidate who can place events in sequence without hesitation has capacity left for argument, and one who cannot spends it on retrieval instead.

subjects.name: Interpretation and evaluation of evidence
subjects.description: Reading provenance before content, judging what a source is useful for rather than whether it is true, decoding a cartoon's intended message, and grouping a set of sources for and against a statement. Habits rather than knowledge, which is why they move quickly when taught.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-history-0470-onlin.regionsTitle: Dubai communities where our 0470 students live
dubai/cambridge-igcse-history-0470-onlin.regionsIntro: Delivery over video means geography no longer limits who teaches your child. It still shapes which part of the syllabus is thin, because schools differ in what they teach quickly. These are the communities our 0470 students write in from.

regions.name: Jumeirah Lakes Towers and Al Sufouh
regions.note: Dense tower communities feeding several large British-curriculum schools. Cohorts here are usually on Option B with Germany as the depth study, and the content taught fastest tends to be the final key question on the Gulf.

regions.name: Dubai Festival City and Ras Al Khor
regions.note: Mixed-curriculum cluster with large year groups. History sets are often substantial, which means plenty of class discussion and comparatively little individual feedback on the 10-mark judgement questions.

regions.name: Al Garhoud and Oud Metha
regions.note: Older, established schools with long-standing humanities departments and deep past-paper stocks. Students here usually arrive with secure core content and need work on evidence evaluation rather than on narrative.

regions.name: Al Quoz and Al Khail Heights
regions.note: Smaller schools and a high proportion of families seeking additional academic support. Option sets are small, so a missed fortnight removes a whole key question, and those gaps show up as blank patches in the dated spine.

regions.name: Arjan, Barsha South and Dubai Science Park
regions.note: Rapidly growing communities with newer schools and young history departments. The common pattern is careful content teaching with few top-band exemplar essays in circulation for students to measure their own writing against.

regions.name: Remraam, Dubailand and Liwan
regions.note: Outlying residential communities with long school runs. Students here benefit most from a fixed evening slot, and their scripts most often show the timing fault: a generous first question and an unfinished third.

regions.name: Jumeirah Golf Estates and Emirates Hills
regions.note: Villa communities feeding schools with large option blocks. History frequently competes against economics or business studies, so sets can be small and the student who chose it is often genuinely interested, which changes what a session can attempt.

regions.name: Al Nahda and Muhaisnah
regions.note: Mixed-curriculum area with a wide spread of starting points inside a single set. The most useful early work here is almost always the chronology spine, because the content was delivered at a pace that assumed prior knowledge.

schoolClusters.city: Schools serving JLT, Al Sufouh and the Marina corridor
schoolClusters.note: Established British-curriculum cohorts, almost all on Option B with Germany as the depth study. Departments here hold deep resources, so external teaching is usually about evidence evaluation and judgement writing rather than about content delivery.

schoolClusters.city: Schools serving Al Garhoud, Festival City and Oud Metha
schoolClusters.note: Long-established schools with mixed curricula and large year groups. The constraint in this cluster is individual feedback volume rather than teaching quality, since a history set of thirty cannot receive fortnightly marked essays from one teacher.

schoolClusters.city: Schools serving Al Quoz, Arjan and Dubailand
schoolClusters.note: Newer and smaller secondary cohorts across a fast-growing part of the city. Small history sets mean fewer exemplar answers circulating and a higher chance that one key question was taught in half the time the others received.

modes.title: Weekly teaching through the key questions
modes.description: For a student whose content is thin rather than whose technique is weak. One key question at a time, taught in sequence with the dated spine built as you go, so that by the end there is a single document covering eight decades rather than seven sets of notes that do not connect to each other.
bullets: One key question per block of sessions, taught in chronological order

modes.title: Depth-study rebuild for a mid-course transfer
modes.description: For a student who arrives in a Dubai cohort entered for a depth study they have never studied. The work is content, not technique, and pretending otherwise wastes the budget. A written gap list comes first, then the option is taught from the start at a pace a transferring student can hold.

modes.title: Evidence-evaluation block for the source paper
modes.description: Six to ten sessions on Paper 2, which is a third of the grade and is examined on a prescribed topic that changes between series. The content therefore cannot be the work; reading provenance, judging utility and grouping sources for a 12-mark verdict is. The fastest measurable change available in this syllabus.
bullets: Provenance read before content on every source as a trained reflex
Utility answered as useful for what, never as true or biased

sections.heading: What Cambridge IGCSE History 0470 asks a student to do
paragraphs: The three components of Cambridge IGCSE History 0470 test three different things, and a student who does not know which is which tends to prepare for all of them in the same way. Paper 1 is two hours and 60 marks, 40% of the grade, answered as three questions each split into parts worth four, six and ten marks. Paper 2 is two hours and 50 marks, 33% of the grade, answered entirely from sources on a prescribed topic. The final 27% is either a 2,000-word coursework assignment marked out of 40, or Paper 4, a one-hour written paper also worth 40 marks.

Underneath that sits a cleaner distinction. Paper 1 rewards knowledge and causal argument. Paper 2 rewards the handling of evidence and barely rewards recall at all, because the sources are printed in front of the candidate and the topic rotates between series. The coursework or Paper 4 rewards sustained argument on the depth study. Three components, three skills, and a revision plan that treats them identically will leave one of them untouched.

The practical reading for a Dubai family is that the grade can be approached from more than one direction. A candidate with secure content and weak source technique is losing most of their marks on a third of the paper that responds to a short block of teaching. A candidate with excellent source instincts and a shaky chronology has the opposite problem and a slower road. The first question an online tutor should ask is not what grade the student is on; it is which of the three components the last mock shows them losing marks in.

Delivery is one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, with the source extract or the student's own writing on a shared screen. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we provide only in India. The table below sets the three components side by side so that the comparison is on one page rather than scattered across a syllabus document.

sections.heading: Option B: the seven key questions, 1919 to 2000
paragraphs: Almost every Cambridge school in Dubai teaches Option B, International Relations since 1919, and it is organised as seven key questions rather than as a continuous narrative. Knowing them as questions rather than as topics changes how a student revises, because each one has an argument built into it that the exam will ask them to take a position on.

The sequence runs from the peace settlements of 1919 to 1923 and whether they were fair, through the League of Nations and why it failed, to the collapse of international peace by 1939 and the long argument about appeasement. Then it crosses into the Cold War: who was to blame, how effectively the United States contained communism through Korea, Cuba and Vietnam, and how secure Soviet control of Eastern Europe really was from Hungary in 1956 to the collapse of 1989. The final key question covers events in the Gulf from around 1970 to 2000, including the Iranian revolution, the Iran-Iraq war and the invasion of Kuwait.

Two of those seven cause most of the trouble in Dubai cohorts, for opposite reasons. The League of Nations is taught early, when students are still learning how to write at this level, so the content is often secure and the argument underdeveloped: candidates can list the League's weaknesses and cannot distinguish them from the specific decisions taken over Manchuria and Abyssinia. The Gulf question is the one most often taught last and fastest, because it sits at the end of a crowded two-year scheme of work, and it is also the question students in this region are best placed to answer well if anyone gives them the time.

The teaching move that works is to convert each key question into a two-sided argument with three specifics on each side, built as the content is learned rather than assembled in revision. A student who can argue both that appeasement caused the war and that it was the only policy available, with named events and dates on each side, is prepared for any part (c) the examiner can set on that question. A student who has a chapter of notes is not.

sections.heading: Option A, 1814 to 1914, and why fewer Dubai schools teach it
paragraphs: The other core-content option covers the nineteenth century: international relations and developments from 1814 to 1914. It is a legitimate and in some ways more coherent course, and it is taught by a small minority of schools in this market. That minority status has practical consequences worth knowing before you hire anyone.

The content runs from the Congress of Vienna and the settlement after Napoleon, through the revolutions of 1830 and 1848, to the unifications of Italy and Germany in the 1860s and 1870. It then moves into the Eastern Question and the decline of Ottoman power, the partition of Africa, the hardening of the alliance system, and the crises that precede 1914: Morocco in 1905 and 1911, Bosnia in 1908, and the Balkan wars of 1912 and 1913. It is denser in treaties and congresses than Option B, and considerably less familiar to students from popular culture, which cuts both ways: nothing is half-known from films, and nothing is half-wrong either.

For a Dubai family the issue is supply. A tutor who has taught Option B to five cohorts may never have delivered Option A, and learning it alongside your child is not what you are paying for. This is the single most useful question to ask at the point of enquiry, and the honest answer narrows the field quickly. It is also a reason a cohort on Option A should not leave the search until the spring term: the pool is small and it does not expand under pressure.

The teaching approach differs slightly too. Because the period turns on diplomacy, a dated spine is not optional here. A student who cannot place the Congress of Berlin relative to the Dual Alliance, or the Moroccan crises relative to the Anglo-Russian entente, cannot build a causal argument about 1914 regardless of how well they write. The spine comes first, the argument second, and that order is not negotiable in this option.

sections.heading: The six depth studies, and what each actually requires
paragraphs: Every 0470 candidate studies one depth study in detail, examined through the part (c) question on Paper 1 and through either the coursework or Paper 4. The school chose it, and the six options differ substantially in what they demand of a student rather than merely in subject matter.

Germany from 1918 to 1945 is the most widely taught option in Dubai and probably the most heavily resourced in the world. Its difficulty is volume: Weimar's crises, the Stresemann recovery, the Nazi rise, the consolidation of power in 1933 and 1934, and life in the Third Reich, all with dense chronology. Russia from 1905 to 1941 has similar volume with the added burden of unfamiliar names and two revolutions in one year, which is where students lose their footing. The USA from 1919 to 1941 is comparatively compact, and its characteristic difficulty is economic mechanism: candidates describe the Crash accurately and cannot explain why it propagated into a decade-long depression.

The three less commonly taught options each present a specific challenge. China from around 1930 to 1990 covers an enormous span with almost no prior familiarity for most students, so the spine is the whole battle. South Africa from around 1940 to 1994 rewards exact terminology to an unusual degree, because the legislation and the organisations have precise names and an imprecise answer reads as a vague one. The Israelis and Palestinians since 1945 is assessed, like every other option, on evidence, causation and argument against the published criteria, and the responsibility of a tutor there is the accurate and careful use of contested terminology rather than the advancement of any position.

The table below sets out what examiners return to in each option and the misconception that most often costs marks. It is a guide to what to prepare rather than a ranking: the option your child studies is the one the school entered, and the useful question is how to teach it well.

sections.heading: Why 'the source is biased' scores nothing
paragraphs: Paper 2 is a third of the 0470 grade and it is where the largest single block of marks is thrown away in this market, by a habit learned early and never corrected. A student is asked how useful a source is, writes that it is biased and therefore unreliable, and stops. That answer is worth very little, and the reason is worth explaining properly because once a student understands it the marks appear immediately.

Every historical source is partial. A politician's speech, a cartoon, a memoir, a government statistic and a private diary are all produced by someone with a position, for an audience, at a moment. Partiality is not a defect to be noted; it is the property that makes a source evidence of something. A ministerial speech defending a policy is weak evidence of whether the policy worked and excellent evidence of how the government wished it to be seen. The examiner's question is never whether a source is true. It is what the source is useful for finding out.

The move a candidate has to make is therefore mechanical and teachable: read the provenance first, state who produced it, when, for whom and why, and then say what that provenance makes the source good evidence of. A student who writes that a 1936 German newspaper report is unreliable has said nothing. A student who writes that it is unreliable as a record of public opinion because the press was controlled, and valuable as evidence of what the regime wanted believed, has made two marks appear from the same observation.

The same logic governs the comparison and the final judgement questions. Two sources that disagree are not a problem to resolve; the disagreement is the finding, and the explanation lies in who produced each one. The 12-mark question asking how far a set of sources supports a statement is answered by grouping the sources that support it, grouping those that do not, and using provenance to say which group carries more weight. sections.heading: Paper 4 Alternative to Coursework in sixty minutes
paragraphs: If your child's school entered Paper 4 rather than Paper 3, the final 27% of the grade arrives as a one-hour written paper worth 40 marks on the depth study. It is a different kind of challenge from everything else in the syllabus, and the usual failure is treating it as a short Paper 1.

Sixty minutes for forty marks is a demanding rate, and the paper rewards a candidate who has decided in advance roughly how long each part of the answer gets. Students who begin with a scene-setting introduction of the kind a coursework assignment would carry run out of time before the argument is complete, and an unfinished argument on a depth study the candidate knows well is the most avoidable loss available in 0470. The correction is a plan written in two minutes on the paper itself: the two sides, three specifics each, and the line the conclusion will take.

The content is the depth study already studied, so there is no new material to learn. What is new is the compression. An argument that would occupy twelve hundred words in coursework has to be made in a fraction of that without becoming a list, which means the evidence has to be chosen rather than deployed exhaustively. Three precise specifics on each side will outscore eight general ones, and selecting those three is a skill that improves with marked practice rather than with reading.

Three to five sessions usually covers it, which makes Paper 4 the cheapest of the three components to prepare for. The sessions should be spent on timed attempts and marking rather than on content revision, because the content exists and the clock is the constraint. Any session on this paper that does not include a timed piece of writing has probably not addressed the actual problem.

sections.heading: The dated spine: solving the two-hour memory problem
paragraphs: Two hours of continuous writing under exam conditions leaves no spare capacity for effortful recall. A candidate who has to pause and reconstruct whether the Rhineland came before or after the Anschluss is spending on retrieval what the examiner is paying for in argument. This is the least discussed and most decisive part of 0470 preparation, and it cannot be bought in the final fortnight at any price.

The instrument is a dated spine: a single document, built over the course and rehearsed at intervals, that holds the sequence rather than the detail. For Option B it runs from Versailles in 1919 through the League's founding in 1920, the Ruhr occupation and Munich Putsch of 1923, the Manchurian crisis of 1931, Abyssinia in 1935 and 1936, the Rhineland in 1936, Anschluss and Munich in 1938, the Nazi-Soviet Pact and the invasion of Poland in 1939, then Yalta and Potsdam in 1945, the Truman Doctrine and Marshall Plan in 1947, the Berlin Blockade of 1948 to 1949, Korea from 1950, Hungary in 1956, the Berlin Wall in 1961, Cuba in 1962, Czechoslovakia in 1968, the Gulf from the late 1970s, and 1989.

For a Germany depth study it runs in parallel and in more detail: the abdication and armistice of 1918, the Weimar constitution and Spartacist rising of 1919, the Kapp Putsch of 1920, hyperinflation and the Munich Putsch in 1923, the Dawes Plan of 1924 and Locarno of 1925, the Young Plan of 1929, the elections of 1932, Hitler's appointment as Chancellor in January 1933, the Reichstag Fire in February and the Enabling Act in March, the Night of the Long Knives and Hindenburg's death in 1934, the Nuremberg Laws of 1935, and Kristallnacht in 1938.

What makes a spine work is rehearsal rather than possession. Written out once it is a document; tested at intervals with the misses recorded, it becomes automatic. Fifteen minutes at the start of a session, every session, costs very little and is the difference between a candidate who writes from knowledge and one who writes around it. sections.heading: Mandatory UAE subjects beside 0470, and the timetable collision
paragraphs: A Dubai history student's week is not the same as a British one, and the difference is not cosmetic. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. That time comes from the same timetable the option subjects are drawn from, and history is almost always an option.

The detail matters because it is specific. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and advises that no mandatory-subject lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language applies for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in moral, social and cultural studies. For these subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited.

The federal position behind all of this is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. Every emirate's mandatory-subject requirement rests on that baseline, which is why the pattern repeats across the UAE rather than being a Dubai peculiarity.

For a 0470 candidate the consequence is arithmetic. A fixed number of periods a week, several of them committed, means a history scheme of work covering seven key questions plus a depth study plus a source topic is usually delivered at a pace that assumes nothing goes wrong. When something does go wrong, a school trip, an absence, a term that runs short, the content taught fastest is the content taught last, which across Dubai cohorts is reliably the final key question. Knowing that in advance is how a family decides what outside help is actually for.

process.title: Establish the three syllabus facts
process.description: Which core-content option the cohort studies, which depth study the school entered, and whether the last 27% comes from coursework or Paper 4. One email to the head of history produces all three, and no sensible teaching plan exists without them. A tutor who does not ask has not understood the syllabus.

process.title: Find out which component is losing the marks
process.description: Send the mock script. Paper 1 and Paper 2 fail for completely different reasons, and the remedies have different timescales: source technique moves in weeks, chronology takes a term. The script shows which of the three components the grade is actually resting on, which a grade on its own never does.

process.title: Build the dated spine before the argument
process.description: If the sequence is not automatic, the judgement writing cannot work, because exam capacity is finite. The spine is written once and rehearsed at the start of every session with the misses recorded. It is the least interesting part of the plan and the one that makes the rest of it possible.

process.title: Convert each key question into a two-sided argument
process.description: Three specifics for and three against, written down as the content is learned. A student who can argue both sides of appeasement or of Cold War blame, with named events and dates, is prepared for any part (c) on that question. A chapter of notes is not the same thing and never has been.

process.title: Drill the source paper separately
process.description: Paper 2 is a third of the grade and its prescribed topic rotates, so technique rather than content is the work. Provenance first, utility as useful for what, cartoons decoded, sources grouped for the 12-mark verdict. Six to ten sessions produces the fastest measurable change available in this syllabus.

whyPoints.title: Taught to your child's actual option
whyPoints.description: Option A or Option B, and one of six depth studies. We confirm which a teacher has taken a cohort through before matching, and say plainly when the answer does not include yours. In a market where Germany dominates, a China or South Africa cohort needs that question asked early.

whyPoints.title: Evidence evaluation taught as a method
whyPoints.description: Provenance before content, utility as what a source is good evidence of, cartoons decoded for intended message, the 12-mark answer built by grouping. The habit of writing that a source is biased and stopping is the largest avoidable loss in the paper, and it is a teachable fault.

whyPoints.title: The chronology is treated as a precondition
whyPoints.description: A dated spine, written once and rehearsed with misses recorded, because two hours of writing leaves no capacity for effortful recall. This is the part of 0470 preparation that cannot be compressed into the final fortnight, so it is started first rather than promised later.

whyPoints.title: Content gaps named rather than papered over
whyPoints.description: A student who transferred into a cohort entered for a different depth study has a content problem, and selling them essay technique first wastes the budget. The first document in that case is a dated list of what the cohort covered and the student did not.

whyPoints.title: The student's own work stays their own
whyPoints.description: A tutor marks where evidence is missing, asks whether the counter-case has been engaged and explains what the criteria reward. Assessed material is never produced on a candidate's behalf, and syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes are referenced and linked rather than redistributed.

whyPoints.description: We hold no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson approval and operate no UAE office. The regulators are named on this page because their rules shape a Dubai student's week, not because any of them has any relationship with us.

faqs.question: What are the three components of Cambridge IGCSE History 0470?
faqs.answer: Paper 1 is a two-hour written paper of 60 marks worth 40% of the grade, answered as three questions each split into parts of four, six and ten marks: two on the core content and one on the depth study. Paper 2 is a two-hour source paper of 50 marks worth 33%, set on one prescribed topic and ending with a 12-mark question on how far the sources support a statement. The last 27% is either Paper 3 coursework, up to 2,000 words and marked out of 40, or Paper 4, a one-hour paper also worth 40 marks.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Option A and Option B core content in 0470?
faqs.answer: Option B covers International Relations since 1919 through seven key questions: the peace settlements, the League of Nations, the collapse of peace by 1939, blame for the Cold War, American containment, Soviet control of Eastern Europe, and events in the Gulf. Option A covers 1814 to 1914, from the Congress of Vienna through the unifications of Italy and Germany to the alliance system and the crises before the First World War. Nearly every Cambridge school in Dubai teaches Option B, which makes finding a teacher for Option A noticeably harder.

faqs.question: How much of the 0470 grade comes from source work?
faqs.answer: A third. Paper 2 carries 50 marks and 33% of the qualification, and it is answered entirely from a printed set of sources on one prescribed topic, so recall plays almost no part in it. Because the topic rotates between series, content revision has limited value here and technique has nearly all of it. That combination makes Paper 2 the best-value component in the syllabus to teach, and in practice the one most often left until the final weeks when there is no longer time to change a habit.

faqs.question: Why does writing that a source is biased score nothing?
faqs.answer: Because every source is partial, so noting it tells the examiner nothing. The question is never whether a source is true; it is what the source is useful for finding out. A government speech defending a policy is weak evidence of whether the policy worked and excellent evidence of how the government wanted it seen. A candidate who states the provenance, then says what that provenance makes the source good evidence of, earns the marks from exactly the same observation that a one-line bias answer wastes.

faqs.question: What does the 6-mark part of a 0470 question want that the 4-mark part does not?
faqs.answer: A causal chain rather than a set of facts. The 4-mark part asks for description or recall and wants a handful of short factual statements with no argument attached. The 6-mark part asks why something happened and rewards two or three reasons developed over successive steps, with the link between cause and consequence stated rather than implied. Four causes asserted once each sits in the middle band; two causes taken properly from trigger through to outcome reaches the top. The marker is looking for the connective, not the quantity.

faqs.question: Which 0470 depth study has the least content to memorise?
faqs.answer: The USA from 1919 to 1941 is the most compact of the six and the best resourced for its size, covering the boom of the 1920s, the Crash, the Depression and the New Deal. Its characteristic difficulty is not volume but mechanism: students describe the Crash accurately and cannot explain why it propagated. Germany and Russia carry substantially more dated detail, and China spans sixty years with little prior familiarity. In any case the choice is the school's, so the practical question is how to teach the option entered rather than which is lightest.

faqs.question: How long is Paper 4 Alternative to Coursework for 0470?
faqs.answer: One hour, for 40 marks, worth the same 27% of the grade as the coursework route. The content is the depth study already studied, so nothing new has to be learned; the constraint is the clock. The usual failure is writing a Paper 1 style answer at coursework length, beginning with a scene-setting introduction and running out of time mid-argument. A two-minute written plan naming the two sides and three specifics each is the single highest-value habit for this paper.

faqs.question: Does 0470 Option B require knowledge of events after 1991?
faqs.answer: The final key question covers events in the Gulf from roughly 1970 to 2000, which takes the course past 1991, and the collapse of Soviet control in Eastern Europe runs to 1989 and beyond. In practice Dubai cohorts most often meet this material last and fastest, because it sits at the end of a crowded scheme of work. Confirm with the school how far the cohort was actually taught, because an exam question on a key question delivered in three lessons is a predictable and avoidable loss.

faqs.question: How many dates does a 0470 candidate really need?
faqs.answer: Fewer than a revision guide implies, held more securely than most students hold them. The working standard is a spine of perhaps twenty to thirty dated events for the core content and a similar number for the depth study, known well enough that the sequence never requires a pause. Precision matters where the syllabus turns on it, such as January to March 1933 in Germany, and a decade is sufficient elsewhere. What ruins a paper is not a missing date but a candidate spending exam capacity reconstructing an order.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge IGCSE History 0470 harder than Geography 0460?
faqs.answer: They are difficult in different places, which is more useful than a ranking. History asks for sustained argument under time pressure: thirty of Paper 1's sixty marks are judgement writing, and a third of the qualification is source evaluation. Geography 0460 asks for a bank of named case studies plus a procedural skills paper on a 1:25,000 map. A student who writes fluently and dislikes diagrams usually finds history easier; one who prefers defined procedures to open argument usually finds geography easier.

faqs.question: Does Dubai's mandatory Social Studies requirement overlap with 0470 content?
faqs.answer: Hardly at all, and parents frequently expect otherwise. Social Studies is a KHDA-required subject in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with its own content, its own language-of-instruction rules and separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs. Cambridge IGCSE History 0470 is an examined international qualification on the core-content option and depth study the school entered. They share a timetable rather than a syllabus, and the real interaction is competition for weekly periods, which falls on option subjects first.

faqs.question: Can my child take 0470 while a sibling studies a different history board?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it happens often in Dubai because schools make different board choices. Cambridge 0470 and the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE in history are separate qualifications with different papers, different content options and different assessment structures, so the two students need separate preparation and ideally separate sessions. What does not transfer is material: a past paper from one board is of limited use for the other. What does transfer is the underlying method of evidence evaluation and causal argument.

faqs.question: How is a cartoon source marked in 0470?
faqs.answer: On the message, not the description. A candidate who narrates what is visible in the drawing sits in the lowest band. The marks go to identifying the figures and symbols, placing the cartoon in the context of its date and publication, and stating what the cartoonist wanted the reader to think. A cartoon is strong evidence of an attitude and weak evidence of factual detail, which is why provenance has to be read first. Practised deliberately, it is one of the fastest-improving question types on the paper.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring work for an essay subject like history?
faqs.answer: It works well, because the product in an essay subject is marked writing rather than physical presence. The source extract or the student's own paragraph sits on a shared screen, the annotation happens where both parties can see it, and the marked script comes back within a day or two rather than at the next visit. A teacher who is not driving across the city marks more work. For a syllabus this specific it also means the teacher can be chosen for having taught your child's exact option.

faqs.question: When should a Year 10 student start proper 0470 revision?
faqs.answer: Revision in the usual sense can wait; the dated spine cannot. From the first term of Year 10 a student should be extending a single sequence document as each key question is taught, and rehearsing it briefly rather than re-reading notes. That habit costs a few minutes a week and removes the retrieval problem that otherwise surfaces in a two-hour paper eighteen months later. Essay technique has a shorter runway and can reasonably begin once the first two key questions are complete.

intro.heading: Why a history quote is harder to read than a maths quote
paragraphs: A Cambridge IGCSE History 0470 tutor in Dubai will quote you an hourly rate, and that number is less informative than it looks. The published market bands are known: budget online tutoring from AED 45 to AED 150, a qualified subject teacher online at AED 150 to AED 300, an in-home visit from AED 180 to AED 500 with travel inside the price, an exam-year specialist at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, and premium named tutors above AED 500. Unitors publishes IGCSE rates from AED 150, TutorChase lists AED 270, Bestimate's Dubai table gives the in-home band, and BartyED quotes AED 650. Those are their figures, read in October 2026. None is ours.

The reason the hourly rate misleads in history specifically is that the work does not fit inside the hour. A maths tutor can set twenty questions, mark them in six minutes and hand them back. A history tutor who sets a 10-mark part (c) essay and a full source-paper response is taking forty minutes to mark a single student's work properly, with annotation against the mark criteria rather than a number at the bottom. Any tutor charging a maths rate for history is either not marking the written work or not pricing their own time, and both of those become visible in about a month.

The second reason is that history is not one subject at this level. Cambridge IGCSE History 0470 has three assessed parts: Paper 1, two hours and 60 marks, worth 40% of the grade; Paper 2, the source paper, two hours and 50 marks, worth 33%; and then either Paper 3 coursework or Paper 4 Alternative to Coursework, 40 marks and 27%. The tutoring these need is not interchangeable. Source technique is a short, teachable block. Core content is a long haul. Coursework supervision is expensive per hour because the reading happens outside the session. Quoting one rate for all three hides which one you are buying.

The third variable is the depth study, and it is the one most families do not know to ask about. Every 0470 candidate studies one depth study in detail, and the school chose which: Germany 1918 to 1945, Russia 1905 to 1941, the USA 1919 to 1941, China, South Africa, or the Israelis and Palestinians since 1945. Germany is taught in Dubai more than all the others combined, so the pool of teachers who know it well is deep and the rate is competitive. A cohort entered for China or South Africa has a much thinner pool, and that scarcity shows up in both price and availability at 4.30pm.

The last variable is when you buy. History demand in Dubai is concentrated into two short windows, and the hourly rate barely moves between them while availability collapses. The sections below price each component separately, set out which depth studies are widely taught here, and give the weeks of the Dubai school year in which hours are genuinely cheaper in real terms. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video; IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, since in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India.
