dubai/cambridge-igcse-history-0470-tutor.programmesIntro: Four routes through 0470 that Dubai families actually buy, with what each costs in hours. The route matters more than the hourly rate, because it determines how many hours there are.

programmes.name: 0470 across a full two-year Cambridge cohort
programmes.description: The cheapest route per mark. One weekly session from the start of Year 10 spreads the core content across sixty-odd weeks, which means the part (c) essay is practised a dozen times rather than three times. At the mid market band of AED 150 to AED 300 an hour this is also the largest absolute spend, which is why most families do not do it.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools generally teach the core content in Year 10 and the depth study plus the source topic in Year 11, so a Year 10 start buys content teaching and a Year 11 start buys technique. Families who plan to use a tutor at all are better off booking a fortnightly slot from Year 10 than a weekly one from February of Year 11, for the same total outlay.

programmes.name: 0470 exam-year support only
programmes.description: The most common purchase in this market: twenty to thirty-five sessions across Year 11, usually starting after the mocks. The constraint is that the core content is already taught, well or badly, and the hours have to be split between repairing it and building essay technique. Expect to pay the exam-year band rather than the standard one.
programmes.countryNote: Mock results in Dubai schools typically land in the winter term, and the Cambridge entry deadline sits months before the exam window. Cambridge's published key dates for its March series illustrate the structure: final entries closed 27 November 2026 for exams starting 3 February 2027. UAE centres sit the June and November series, with comparably early internal deadlines.

programmes.name: 0470 resit and November series candidates
programmes.description: Cambridge runs IGCSE in both a June and a November series, so a missed grade does not cost a year. A resit block is short, dense and cheap relative to a full programme, because the content exists and the work is almost entirely technique: part (c) structure, source provenance, and timing. Eight to fifteen sessions is typical.
programmes.countryNote: Re-entry is made through a school or an exam centre in the UAE, and the centre's own deadline binds rather than the published series window. Several Dubai centres accept private candidates, and each sets its own entry fee, so the cost of the retake itself needs checking with the centre before the tutoring budget is set.

programmes.name: After 0470: AS and A Level History 9489 or IB Diploma History
programmes.description: Both post-16 routes assume the essay discipline from 0470 is in place and then raise the stakes: longer arguments, independent reading, and source work judged against historiography rather than against provenance alone. Students who reached a good 0470 grade by memorising narrative find the first post-16 term harder than their IGCSE result predicted.
programmes.countryNote: A number of Dubai schools offer Cambridge AS and A Level History 9489 and IB Diploma History side by side, and the real difference for most students is the writing volume rather than the content. Asking in Year 11 which of the two the department staffs more deeply is more useful than asking which carries more prestige.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-history-0470-tutor.subjectsIntro: Pricing 0470 properly means knowing which unit is being bought. These are the content blocks and assessed skills a Dubai family books hours against, with what each one demands of a teacher's time.

subjects.name: Core content Option B: International Relations since 1919
subjects.levels: 0470 Paper 1 · the route most Dubai schools take
subjects.description: The peace treaties of 1919 to 1923, the League of Nations, the collapse of peace by 1939, the origins of the Cold War, American containment, Soviet control of Eastern Europe and events in the Gulf. Broad, chronological and heavy on causation, so it needs sustained weekly teaching rather than a short block.

subjects.name: Core content Option A: the 19th century, 1814-1914
subjects.description: International relations and developments from the Congress of Vienna to the eve of the First World War. Taught by far fewer Dubai schools, which means fewer teachers have delivered it recently and the available pool for a cohort on this option is noticeably thinner.

subjects.name: Depth Study: Germany, 1918-1945
subjects.description: Weimar's crises, the rise of the Nazi party, the consolidation of power, life in the Third Reich and the war years. The most widely taught depth study in Dubai by a wide margin, so this is the cohort with the deepest choice of teacher and the most competitive rate.

subjects.name: Depth Study: Russia, 1905-1941
subjects.description: The 1905 and 1917 revolutions, the civil war, the New Economic Policy, Stalin's rise, collectivisation and the purges. Dense chronology with a high proportion of unfamiliar names, which is where the hours go: securing the sequence before attempting judgement.

subjects.name: Depth Study: the USA, 1919-1941
subjects.description: The boom of the 1920s, the Crash, the Depression and the New Deal. Comparatively compact and well resourced, with the common difficulty being economic mechanism rather than narrative: students describe the Crash accurately and cannot explain why it propagated.

subjects.name: Depth Study: China, c.1930-c.1990
subjects.description: The Communist victory, the early People's Republic, the Great Leap Forward, the Cultural Revolution and the reform era. Unfamiliar to most students and taught by few Dubai schools, so a cohort on this option should check depth-study coverage before booking anything.

subjects.name: Depth Study: South Africa, c.1940-c.1994
subjects.description: Apartheid legislation, resistance movements, international pressure and the transition to democracy. A thin pool of teachers in this market relative to Germany or Russia, and a depth study where precise terminology carries a disproportionate number of marks.

subjects.name: Depth Study: Israelis and Palestinians since 1945
subjects.description: A syllabus option assessed, like every other, on evidence, causation and argument against the published mark criteria. A tutor's responsibility here is the assessment requirement and the accurate use of contested terminology, not the advancement of a position.

subjects.name: The Paper 2 prescribed source topic
subjects.description: One prescribed topic set by Cambridge for the series, examined entirely through sources. The topic changes between series, so the content is less important than the technique, and this is the component that responds fastest to a short, well-aimed block of teaching.

subjects.name: The coursework assignment
subjects.description: One assignment on the depth study, written to a 2,000-word limit and marked out of 40. The most expensive component to support per hour, because the draft reading happens between sessions. The work must be the candidate's own throughout.

subjects.name: Paper 4 Alternative to Coursework
subjects.description: A one-hour written paper on the depth study, worth the same 27% as the coursework route. Cheap to prepare for relative to coursework, because it is a timed technique problem rather than a project, and three to five sessions usually covers it.

subjects.name: Chronology, terminology and recall
subjects.description: The underlying requirement nobody times correctly. Two hours of writing under exam conditions demands that dates, names and sequence are automatic, not retrievable with effort. Building that is slow, repetitive work that cannot be bought in the final fortnight at any rate.

sections.heading: What Cambridge IGCSE History 0470 tuition costs in Dubai, component by component
paragraphs: The honest answer to what a Cambridge IGCSE History 0470 tutor in Dubai costs is that the hourly rate sits in a published band of roughly AED 45 to AED 650, and that the figure you should actually care about is the total for the component you need. A source-paper block and a full exam-year programme are both bought at the same hourly rate and differ by a factor of four in total cost.

Work it the other way round. Take the market midpoint for a qualified subject teacher online, which the published bands put around AED 200 an hour, and multiply it by the hours a component realistically needs. The source paper needs six to ten sessions and carries 33% of the grade. Paper 1 core content needs ten to sixteen if the school has taught it reasonably and more if it has not, and carries 40%. The coursework or alternative paper needs three to six and carries 27%. A full exam-year programme covering all three lands between twenty-five and thirty-five sessions.

That arithmetic does something a quoted rate cannot: it tells you which component is worth buying first on a limited budget. Paper 2 is the best ratio in the syllabus, because a third of the grade turns on technique that can be taught in weeks rather than content that takes months. Core content is the opposite. If you have the budget for one block only, the source paper is usually the defensible choice, and any tutor who tells you otherwise without having seen a marked script is guessing.

sections.heading: Why history is priced differently from maths and science
paragraphs: Parents comparing quotes across subjects notice that history and English tutors in Dubai sit at or above the rate for maths and the sciences at the same level, and the usual explanation offered is that essay subjects are harder to teach. That is not the reason. The reason is marking time.

A maths tutor can set twenty exercises, mark them in a few minutes by looking at the answers, and spend the lesson on the three that went wrong. A history tutor who sets a 10-mark part (c) essay and a full source-paper response has to read every word, decide which level the answer sits in against the published criteria, annotate the specific sentences where the argument stopped developing, and write something the student can act on. Done properly for one student that is thirty to forty-five minutes of unbilled work per fortnight, and a tutor who does not price it either stops doing it or stops working.

The practical test for a parent is therefore not the rate. It is a question: how often will written work be marked against the criteria, and will I see the annotated script. A tutor charging AED 150 an hour who marks an essay every fortnight is better value than one charging AED 300 who discusses essays and never marks one, and the difference is invisible until you ask. The marked script is the product in an essay subject. The conversation is the delivery mechanism.

There is a second cost driver peculiar to history, which is breadth. A 0470 candidate must hold two core-content periods, one depth study and one source topic simultaneously. A tutor who has taught the core content but not your child's depth study will be learning it at your expense in week three. That is a fair question to ask before booking, and the answer changes the quote more honestly than any negotiation over the hourly rate.

sections.heading: Which depth study your school chose, and what it does to the quote
paragraphs: Every 0470 candidate studies one depth study in detail, examined through the part (c) question on Paper 1 and through the coursework or Paper 4. The school chose it, probably before your child joined, and most parents have never been told which. It is the first thing to establish, because it changes both who can teach your child and what that costs.

Germany 1918 to 1945 is taught in Dubai more than every other option combined. That has a direct price effect: almost every experienced IGCSE history teacher has delivered it, resources are abundant, and the pool of available tutors at a Gulf Standard Time evening slot is deep. A cohort entered for China or South Africa faces the opposite position. Fewer schools in this market run those options, fewer teachers have taken a cohort through them, and scarcity in a thin pool shows up first as unavailability at the hour you want and second as a higher rate for the people who are genuinely expert.

This is also the situation where a mid-year school move becomes expensive. A student who studied Russia at their previous school and joins a Dubai cohort entered for Germany has a content gap that no technique teaching closes, and the honest quote is for content hours rather than essay practice. Families in this position are the ones most often sold a short technique block that cannot work. Ask the new school which depth study the cohort is entered for on the first day, not in February.

sections.heading: Paper 1: two hours, 60 marks, and the part (c) that decides the grade
paragraphs: Paper 1 runs for two hours, carries 60 marks and is worth 40% of the Cambridge IGCSE History 0470 grade. Candidates answer three questions, two drawn from the core content and one on their depth study. Each question comes in three parts, and the mark allocation is the same every time: four marks, six marks and ten marks.

That structure is the most useful thing a 0470 candidate can internalise, because the three parts want three different pieces of writing. Part (a) is worth four marks and asks for description or recall: short, factual, no argument required, and complete in a few minutes. Part (b) is worth six and asks why something happened: explanation developed over two or three steps rather than a list of causes. Part (c) is worth ten and asks for judgement, usually phrased as how far or to what extent, and it requires both sides argued and a conclusion that actually answers the question rather than summarising the paragraphs above it.

Ten marks, three times over, is thirty of the paper's sixty marks. Half of Paper 1 is judgement writing, and judgement writing is the thing Dubai candidates are least often drilled on, because a class of twenty-eight cannot be given individual essay feedback every fortnight. This is precisely why the marked essay rather than the lesson is the product you are buying in history, and why the cost of that marking is what you are really paying for.

The timing problem compounds it. Two hours across three questions is forty minutes each, and a candidate who writes generously on part (a) of question one has already damaged part (c) of question three. A timed full-paper attempt reveals that in a single afternoon, and it is worth doing early enough that the habit can be changed rather than merely diagnosed.

sections.heading: Paper 2: one prescribed topic and a 12-mark judgement
paragraphs: Paper 2 is two hours, 50 marks and 33% of the grade, and it is examined entirely through sources on a single prescribed topic that Cambridge sets for the series. The topic rotates, so content revision has a limited role here and technique has almost all of it. That makes Paper 2 the best-value component in 0470 to buy tutoring for, and the one most often left until last.

The questions move through a predictable sequence of skills. Early questions test comprehension and inference from one or two sources. There is a comparison question requiring both agreement and disagreement between two sources, where candidates lose marks by writing about only one of them or by comparing topic rather than message. There is a utility or reliability question, where the single biggest failure in the whole paper occurs: the student writes that a source is biased and stops. Bias is not an answer. Every source has a provenance, a purpose and an audience, and utility depends on what you are trying to find out.

A cartoon or visual source usually appears, and it needs the symbolism decoded and tied to the context of the date rather than described. The paper closes with a 12-mark question asking how far the sources support a given statement, which is answered by grouping sources that support it, grouping those that do not, and reaching a verdict with reference to provenance. A candidate who works through the sources one by one in order almost never reaches the top band.

All of this is teachable in six to ten sessions because it is a set of readable habits rather than a body of knowledge. It is also the part of the course where the marked script matters most, since the difference between a mid-band and a top-band source answer is often two sentences that the student does not know are missing.

sections.heading: The last 27%: coursework or Paper 4, and what each costs
paragraphs: The final 27% of 0470 arrives either as Paper 3 coursework, one assignment on the depth study written to a limit of 2,000 words and marked out of 40, or as Paper 4 Alternative to Coursework, a one-hour written paper also worth 40 marks. Your child's school has already chosen, and the two cost very different amounts to support.

Paper 4 is the cheaper of the two. It is a timed technique problem on material the student has already studied, and three to five sessions usually covers the question types, the time allocation and the depth of argument a one-hour paper can carry. Candidates mostly lose marks here by writing a Paper 1 style answer at Paper 1 length and running out of time.

Coursework is the more expensive, and the expense is not in the lesson. Supporting a 2,000-word assignment means reading each draft properly: whether the question can be answered in the word limit, whether the argument is supported by evidence rather than asserted, whether the counter-argument is present, and whether the conclusion follows. That reading sits outside the billed hour, and a tutor pricing coursework support at their standard rate is absorbing it. Ask how the draft-reading time is handled before the block begins.

One boundary applies regardless of route. The assignment must be the candidate's own work from beginning to end. A tutor may question the argument, mark where evidence is missing, explain what the published criteria reward and say plainly that a paragraph is not doing any work. A tutor may not produce assessed material on a student's behalf, and a service offering to do so is selling a malpractice risk alongside it. There are such services in this market, and Cambridge's rules treat the student rather than the seller as the person who loses the entry.

sections.heading: When to buy: the Dubai history-tutoring year
paragraphs: Hourly rates in this market are stable across the year. Availability is not, and availability is what you are actually buying, so the effective price of a history tutor in Dubai changes considerably depending on the week you make the call.

Two windows absorb most of the demand. The first is the fortnight after mock results land in the winter term, when every Year 11 family in the city makes the same decision simultaneously. The second is the short period after the school confirms the entry and the series stops being abstract. In both windows the published rate holds and the specialists with free 4.30pm and 6pm slots are the ones nobody booked, which means families pay the exam-year band of AED 200 to AED 450 for whoever remains rather than the standard band for the teacher they wanted.

The quiet windows are September and October, the weeks immediately after a mid-year break, and the period right after the June series when the November cohort has not yet organised itself. Booking in a quiet window costs the same per hour and buys a choice of teacher, a choice of slot, and roughly four times as many sessions before the exam. For a subject where the product is marked essays delivered at a fortnightly rhythm, the number of fortnights left is the whole argument.

There is also a Ramadan consideration that sits outside the demand cycle. School days shorten, concentration shifts to the evening, and a 4.30pm history session stops being useful. Because lessons run over live video with no travel to schedule, moving to a post-Iftar slot for the month is an administrative change rather than a renegotiation, and families who plan for it keep the fortnightly essay rhythm intact through a period when the cohort can least afford to pause.

sections.heading: Equivalency, permits and two checks worth ten minutes
paragraphs: Two pieces of administration sit around a 0470 entry, and both are frequently misdescribed by tutoring websites in this market. Neither is complicated if you read the primary source.

The first is Ministry of Education equivalency, which matters for UAE university admission. On the British track the Ministry requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, together with one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. History 0470 is an accredited IGCSE subject and can form part of that count. One competing site in this market publishes a six-subject requirement, which is wrong, and the correct figure is five. Equivalency is assessed by the Ministry, not by any tutoring service, and the rules are the Ministry's to change, so confirm the current position on moe.gov.ae before you plan around it.

The second is the tutor's permit. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. The service is listed by MoHRE as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing and runs through the ministry's app, website and e-services with a two-working-day completion time. Working without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so any page quoting you an amount has invented it.

Two checks, then. Ask the tutor directly whether they hold the permit, because it is free and quick and the answer tells you how they run their work. And do not hire your child's own class teacher privately: ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi school staff from paid tutoring of students at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a comparable restriction. For completeness, IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge International or Pearson, and operates no UAE office. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific instrument issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai, and we are not one.

faqs.question: How much does a Cambridge IGCSE History 0470 tutor cost per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The published market runs from about AED 45 an hour for budget online tutoring to AED 650 for premium named tutors. The band most families work in is AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject teacher online, and AED 200 to AED 450 and above for exam-year specialists. Unitors lists IGCSE from AED 150, TutorChase AED 270, and Bestimate's Dubai table puts in-home visits at AED 180 to AED 350. Those are their figures as read in October 2026. The more useful number is the total for the component you need, which this page works out separately.

faqs.question: Why do history tutors charge more than maths tutors for the same hour?
faqs.answer: Because the marking does not fit inside the hour. Twenty maths exercises can be checked in a few minutes. A 10-mark part (c) essay and a full source-paper response have to be read in full, placed against the published levels, annotated at the sentence where the argument stopped developing, and returned with something actionable. That is thirty to forty-five minutes of unbilled work per fortnight for one student. A rate that ignores it produces a tutor who discusses essays rather than one who marks them, and you will not notice for a month.

faqs.question: Which depth study has my child's Dubai school entered for 0470?
faqs.answer: Ask the head of history; it is one email and it changes everything about the quote. The options are Germany 1918-45, Russia 1905-41, the USA 1919-41, China from around 1930 to 1990, South Africa from around 1940 to 1994, and the Israelis and Palestinians since 1945. Germany is taught in Dubai more than all the others combined, which means a deeper pool of teachers and a more competitive rate. A cohort on China or South Africa should confirm a tutor has actually taught that option to a cohort before booking a block.

faqs.question: What is the prescribed topic on Paper 2, and does it change each year?
faqs.answer: Paper 2 is examined entirely through sources on one prescribed topic that Cambridge sets for the series, and it rotates between series rather than staying fixed. The practical effect is that content revision has a limited role on this paper and technique has almost all of it, which is why a source block is the best-value tutoring purchase in the syllabus. Your child's school will know which topic the cohort is prepared for, and the official syllabus document on cambridgeinternational.org states the topic for each series.

faqs.question: How much of the 0470 grade rests on the 10-mark question?
faqs.answer: More than most families realise. Paper 1 carries 60 marks and 40% of the grade, and each of its three questions ends with a part (c) worth ten marks. That is thirty of sixty marks on Paper 1, so half of the paper and a fifth of the whole qualification turns on judgement writing: both sides argued, evidence deployed, and a conclusion that answers the question rather than restating it. It is also the skill a class of twenty-eight cannot be given fortnightly individual feedback on, which is why it is the usual reason a tutor is hired.

faqs.question: Is Paper 4 cheaper to prepare for than the 0470 coursework option?
faqs.answer: Yes, noticeably. Paper 4 Alternative to Coursework is a one-hour written paper worth 40 marks on the depth study, and three to five sessions usually covers the question types, the timing and the depth of argument an hour can carry. Coursework is a 2,000-word assignment marked out of 40, and supporting it means reading each draft properly between sessions, which is unbilled work. Both routes carry the same 27% of the grade. Confirm which one the school entered before buying anything, because the two kinds of support look nothing alike.

faqs.question: How many hours of 0470 tutoring does a Year 11 student usually need?
faqs.answer: A candidate with the core content reasonably secure who needs source technique and essay practice typically buys twelve to twenty sessions. A candidate who has fallen behind on content as well is realistically at twenty-five to thirty-five across the exam year. At the market midpoint of around AED 200 an hour that is roughly AED 2,400 to AED 7,000 in total. The number of weeks remaining matters more than the number of hours: thirty sessions from September deliver more than thirty compressed into the spring term, at identical cost.

faqs.question: Do 0470 rates go up during the Dubai mock season?
faqs.answer: The published hourly bands barely move. Availability collapses, which has the same effect on what you pay. In the fortnight after mock results every Year 11 family in the city makes the same decision at once, and the specialists left with a free 4.30pm slot are the ones nobody booked. Families then pay the exam-year band of AED 200 to AED 450 for whoever remains rather than the standard band for the teacher they wanted. Booking in September or October costs the same per hour and buys roughly four times the sessions.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both History 0470 and Geography 0460?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking because it simplifies scheduling and occasionally the price. Many humanities teachers have taught both, but the two syllabuses need different things: 0460 rests on case studies and a 1:25,000 map skills paper, while 0470 rests on source technique and judgement essays. The honest test is whether the teacher can mark a 7-mark geography levels answer and a 10-mark history part (c) against the right criteria. If they are strong in one and passable in the other, two specialists usually serve the student better.

faqs.question: Does History 0470 count towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: It can. On the British track the Ministry requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. Arabic and Islamic education are not included in the five. History 0470 is an accredited IGCSE subject and may count. One ranking site in this market states a six-subject requirement, which is incorrect. Equivalency is assessed by the Ministry rather than by any tutoring service, so verify the current rule on moe.gov.ae.

faqs.question: Does a history tutor working with Dubai students need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE operates under the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The application route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, completed in two working days. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts has been published, so treat any quoted figure sceptically.

faqs.question: Can my child's own school history teacher tutor them privately?
faqs.answer: It is the wrong arrangement even where it is technically possible. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct with a comparable restriction. Beyond the rules there is a practical problem: the person marking your child's school work should not also be paid to prepare it. A separate properly permitted teacher who has no stake in the internal marks gives you a genuine second opinion on where the grade actually sits.

faqs.question: What happens if no 0470 specialist is free in our evening slot?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than placing a general humanities tutor and letting you discover the gap in week three. History is an option subject and the depth studies narrow the pool further: a family needing China or South Africa in a 5pm Gulf Standard Time slot is drawing on a genuinely small group. The usual options are a different hour, a short wait for a named teacher, or a fortnightly ninety-minute session instead of a weekly hour. Which of those is best depends on how many fortnights remain before the series.

faqs.question: Can we pay for a short block before the June series rather than a full year?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for many candidates it is the right purchase. The question is which block. On a limited budget the source paper usually wins: 33% of the grade resting on technique that six to ten sessions can genuinely move. A part (c) essay block is the next best, because thirty of Paper 1's sixty marks are judgement writing. What a short block cannot do is rebuild core content that was never learned, and a tutor who promises that in six weeks before the exam is selling you something they cannot deliver.

faqs.question: Is there a free trial 0470 lesson, and what does it involve?
faqs.answer: One lesson, free, with no card details taken and no obligation afterwards. The condition is that it is a single lesson with a named teacher. We ask first for the marked mock script and the three facts that set the plan: the depth study, the core-content option, and whether the cohort sits Paper 3 or Paper 4. The hour is then spent teaching one real weakness rather than running an assessment, and you get a short written note of what the teacher found and what they would buy first.

intro.heading: Why two quotes for the same subject differ by AED 300
paragraphs: A family in Dubai ringing round for a Cambridge IGCSE home tutor will be quoted somewhere between AED 45 and AED 650 an hour, and every quote will sound reasonable to the person giving it. The spread is not mostly about quality. It is about what the hour contains, who is paying for travel, how scarce the subject specialism is, and whether anybody is marking the student's work against the published mark scheme, which takes a tutor roughly forty minutes per paper and cannot be done inside a sub-hundred-dirham hour.

This page therefore prices the components rather than publishing a single number. Market bands come from published 2026 Dubai rate guides and from providers' own public pricing pages, and they are presented as market rates rather than ours. What IB Gram charges depends on the subject, the level and the number of sessions, and we quote after a conversation in which those are actually known, which is why no single figure appears on this page as our price.

Three structural facts sit behind every number below. Travel is paid for by somebody, so an in-home hour has to recover two journeys. Marking is the most valuable thing a tutor produces and the inclusion most often left out of a quote. And scarcity, not difficulty, sets the top of the range.

Context helps more than families expect. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for Dubai private schools in the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For most Dubai families, tuition fees are the dominant education cost and they have just been held flat, which makes a tutoring decision easier to size: it is an increment on a known number rather than an unknown added to a rising one.

The second piece of context is supply. Dubai's private education sector is growing quickly, with seven new private schools opening for 2026-27, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places after six openings in 2025-26 and a 6 per cent rise in enrolment. More schools means more Cambridge cohorts and more demand for subject specialists, and the scarce specialisms are where rates move fastest. Additional Mathematics 0606 and Arabic as a First Language 0508 are not expensive because they are hard; they are expensive because few people teach them well.

One structural point about delivery, because it changes the arithmetic on this page. IB Gram teaches Dubai families one to one over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai, since sending a tutor to an address is a service we run only in India. In-home figures are quoted below as market information, because a family asking what a home tutor costs deserves the real answer, and because the gap between those columns is largely the price of an evening drive across this city.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Cost behaves differently at each Cambridge stage, because the number of sessions a brief needs varies more than the hourly rate does. These are the four stages Dubai families budget for, with what drives the total at each.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Core tier
programmes.description: Core briefs are usually shorter and cheaper in total, because the content is a defined subset and the papers are more structured. Cambridge builds the tier to award grades C to G. Where a family is paying for Core support to lift a student towards the top of that range, the honest budget is eight to twelve sessions rather than an open-ended weekly arrangement.
programmes.countryNote: The decision worth spending money on at Core is the tier itself. Two marked papers, one from each tier, cost two sessions and can change the ceiling on the final grade. Dubai schools set tiers from cohort data, so a family bringing marked evidence to the conversation is spending a small amount to influence a large outcome.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Extended tier
programmes.description: Extended is where most Dubai spending happens and where the per-subject totals run highest, because the papers carry multi-step problems and extended response. A typical brief is one session a week across a term, rising to two in the final months, which is twenty to thirty sessions across Years 10 and 11 for a single subject.
programmes.countryNote: The cost-control lever at Extended is subject count rather than hourly rate. Two subjects supported properly produce movement; four supported thinly produce a larger bill and a student slightly better at everything. Families who cap it at two and extend the duration spend less in total and see more.

programmes.name: Additional Mathematics and scarce-specialism subjects
programmes.description: Additional Mathematics 0606, Arabic as a First Language 0508 and the less common languages sit at the top of the rate range for a straightforward reason: few tutors teach them to examination standard. Quotes here are typically a third higher than for mainstream mathematics, and availability rather than price is often the binding constraint.
programmes.countryNote: For these subjects we give a realistic matching date rather than a fast yes, because putting a generalist into a scarce-specialism slot wastes a family's money more efficiently than anything else in this market. If no specialist is free at the hour you need, that is what we will say.

programmes.name: Retakes and private candidate entries
programmes.description: A retake budget has two halves: teaching and entry. Teaching for a single subject retake is usually eight to fifteen sessions focused on the components that failed rather than the whole syllabus. Entry is a separate cost paid to an examination centre that accepts external candidates, and it varies by centre and by how late the entry is made.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai centres set their own closing dates ahead of Cambridge's final entry deadline, and late entry fees are a real and avoidable cost. For the March 2027 series, Cambridge's final entry date is 27 November 2026 against an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027, so a decision made in December is already a decision about a later series.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Below is each popular Cambridge IGCSE subject with the thing that drives its cost: how many sessions a typical brief takes, and why. The hourly rate is the smaller half of the equation for most families.

subjects.name: Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: The most competitively supplied subject in Dubai, so rates sit mid-band. Briefs are long rather than expensive: twenty to thirty sessions across two years is common, because fluency accumulates. A short brief works only where the problem is unshown method rather than number work.

subjects.name: International Mathematics 0607
subjects.description: Fewer tutors teach the graphic-display-calculator route and the investigation paper, which lifts the rate above 0580. A family switching schools mid-IGCSE between 0580 and 0607 should budget four to six sessions purely for the calculator and investigation technique.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics 0606
subjects.description: Top of the rate range on scarcity. Briefs are usually short and intense, eight to twelve sessions in Year 11, focused on calculus applications and trigonometric identities rather than on the whole syllabus. Availability is the real constraint, not price.

subjects.name: Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Mid to upper band, with the practical-skills component the part families forget to budget for. A brief that covers the written papers and ignores the alternative-to-practical paper leaves a predictable chunk of marks untouched, and adding it costs three or four sessions.

subjects.name: Physics 0625
subjects.description: Comparable to chemistry in rate. Cost is driven by how much of electricity and waves needs rebuilding, which a marked paper reveals in twenty minutes. Where those two topics are sound, the brief is short; where they are not, budget a session per topic plus practice.

subjects.name: Biology 0610
subjects.description: Often the cheapest of the three sciences to support, because the content is learnable and the marks are lost on precision and command words. Eight to ten sessions of marked short-answer practice is a common and effective brief.

subjects.name: Coordinated Sciences 0654
subjects.description: Three disciplines in one award, so a single tutor rarely covers all of it to the same standard. The honest budget is one tutor for the two sciences they are strongest in, and either a second tutor or classroom reliance for the third.

subjects.name: English as a First Language 0500
subjects.description: Mid-band rate, and the subject where total cost is most sensitive to how much writing the student will actually produce between sessions. A student who writes weekly needs ten sessions; one who does not will need thirty and still plateau.

subjects.name: Economics 0455
subjects.description: Short briefs work well here. Diagram accuracy and command words account for most lost marks, and six to eight sessions of marked practice moves a grade more reliably than a term of content teaching.

subjects.name: Business Studies 0450
subjects.description: Similar economics of supply and similar brief length. The cost driver is whether the student is applying case-study data or writing generic theory, which is a habit and therefore fast to change once marked work exposes it.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language 0508
subjects.description: Scarce specialism, so rates sit high and matching takes longer. Briefs concentrate on formal register and extended written argument in Standard Arabic rather than on language acquisition, which keeps the session count lower than families expect.

subjects.name: Computer Science 0478
subjects.description: Mid-band, with cost driven by whether the student needs pseudocode conventions and trace tables drilled. Both are habits, so briefs are short: five or six sessions typically covers the gap between writing working code and scoring marks.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and JBR
regions.note: Dense apartment living with constrained parking and a long approach at peak hour. Tutors quoting in-home rates here price the access as well as the drive, and a 17:00 arrival usually means leaving at 16:00 from anywhere inland.

sections.heading: What a Cambridge IGCSE home tutor costs in Dubai, by level and format
paragraphs: The table below is the thing almost nobody in this market publishes: AED rates split by level, by format and by session count. The figures are market rates drawn from published 2026 Dubai rate guides and from tutoring providers' own public pricing pages, reviewed in October 2026. They are not a price list for IB Gram, and the in-home column is included because a family asking about a home tutor is entitled to the real number rather than a redirection.

Read the monthly column rather than the hourly one if you are budgeting. An hourly rate is a unit price and families do not buy units; they buy a term. A specialist at AED 300 an hour taught weekly is roughly AED 1,200 a month, and a budget tutor at AED 100 taught twice weekly is roughly AED 800, which is a far narrower gap than the headline rates suggest, and the specialist is marking the work.

Two of the rows are deliberately unglamorous. Tier-decision support is two sessions, not a term, and it is probably the highest-return spend available to a Year 10 family because it affects the grade ceiling. Retake and private-candidate briefs are short and focused on the components that failed, which is why a retake can cost considerably less than a family fears, with the entry fee a separate matter paid to a centre.

The group column needs a caveat. Cost per student falls with group size and so does diagnostic value. Four students in a shared hour lose marks in four different places, and no tutor can chase all four. Group teaching works well for covering content and poorly for the marked, individual work that actually moves a grade, so treat it as a different product rather than a discount on the same one.

sections.heading: The seven things that move a Dubai quote
paragraphs: Families comparing quotes usually assume the variation is about tutor quality. Some of it is. Most of it is one of seven identifiable factors, and knowing which one is in play turns a confusing spread of numbers into a comparison you can actually make.

Scarcity is the biggest. Mathematics 0580 is supplied by hundreds of competent tutors in this city and prices accordingly. Additional Mathematics 0606, Arabic as a First Language 0508 and the smaller languages are supplied by a few dozen, and the rate reflects that rather than the difficulty of the content. Proximity to a series is the second: the same tutor is scarcer in March than in September, and families booking late in an exam year pay for the timing.

Then come the inclusions, which is where most of the apparent disagreement between quotes actually lives. Marking a paper against the published mark scheme costs a tutor around forty minutes; written parent feedback costs another ten; planning against a school's scheme of work costs more. A quote that includes all three is not expensive relative to one that includes none, it is a different thing being bought, and the only way to compare them is to ask.

The table lists all seven with the direction and rough magnitude of the effect. One of them, travel, disappears entirely under online delivery, which is the single clearest reason the two columns in the previous table differ. Two of them, group size and session frequency, are levers a family controls directly, and the remaining four are market conditions to plan around rather than negotiate.

sections.heading: Travel priced as the line item it is
paragraphs: In-home tutoring in Dubai costs more than online tutoring by roughly the value of a tutor's evening drive, and the published bands bear that out: approximately AED 180 to 500 an hour in-home against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online. The gap is not a premium for presence. It is two unpaid journeys that have to be recovered somewhere.

The consequences for a family are practical rather than financial. A tutor who spends ninety minutes travelling for a sixty-minute lesson can teach two or three students an evening, which is why in-home slots are few, fixed and hard to move. A school fixture, a mock exam or a late bus does not shift an in-home session; it cancels it, because a round trip cannot be refitted at short notice.

There is also the quiet cost of arriving late. Dubai's arterial roads between four and seven do not reward optimistic planning, and a tutor who arrives at 17:15 for a 17:00 session will usually still leave at 18:00 because the next family is waiting. A family paying for sixty minutes can receive forty-five several times a term without anyone raising it, which is a larger effective price increase than any of the factors in the previous table.

None of which makes in-home tutoring a bad choice for every family. A younger child who needs an adult physically present, or a household without a quiet room, may genuinely be better served that way. The point is that the decision should price the drive explicitly, because the provider already has.

sections.heading: Provider models compared, without the straw man
paragraphs: Most tutoring pages compare themselves favourably with an unnamed alternative. A more useful comparison is between models, because the model determines what a family can expect on price, replacement, verification and marking regardless of which brand sits inside it.

The six models in the table are the ones genuinely available to a Dubai family. An independent freelance tutor found through a community group is usually the cheapest and carries the most variance, because there is no replacement if the match is wrong and no verification beyond what the tutor says. A tuition centre with premises offers structure and group economics, and operates under a different regulatory regime: a centre with premises and staff requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a specific permit with initial approval, a six-month completion window and an annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry.

An international marketplace offers the largest pool and the least curation, with the recurring problem that prices are quoted in dollars or pounds that a UAE family does not transact in. A specialist agency curates and charges for it. A platform model such as ours sits between the two, with matching and replacement handled centrally and the teaching delivered by the named tutor.

The permit column is the one worth dwelling on. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Because it costs the tutor nothing, there is no reasonable excuse for not holding one, and asking is a fair question with a verifiable answer whichever model a family chooses.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context: fees, entry and the alternatives
paragraphs: A tutoring figure means little in isolation. Set beside the other education costs a Dubai family already carries, it becomes a decision about proportion rather than an unknown expense, and that is usually the conversation parents are actually trying to have.

The anchor is school fees, which KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 would not rise for Dubai private schools in 2026-27, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a family whose largest education line is flat this year, an incremental tutoring decision is easier to size. The sector itself is expanding: seven new private schools open for 2026-27, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, adding 16,846 places.

Exam entry is the cost families most often forget, and it only applies to private candidates; students entered through their own school have entry handled within the school's fees. A private candidate pays the examination centre, the amount varies by centre and by subject, and late entry costs more. Cambridge's published final entry date for the March 2027 series is 27 November 2026, so the saving from deciding early is real money rather than tidiness.

The table puts the items side by side. The intention is not to argue that tutoring is cheap; it is to make the trade-off visible. A family can see at a glance that one weekly specialist session for an academic year is a different order of commitment from two sessions a week across two subjects, and can choose accordingly rather than discovering the total in April.

sections.heading: Four ways Dubai families waste tutoring money
paragraphs: These are the spending patterns we see most often, and each one is expensive without being obviously wasteful at the time. Naming them is more useful than another argument about hourly rates, because the total a family spends is driven far more by these choices than by the unit price.

The first is breadth. Four subjects at one session a week each, in Year 11, produces a bill of several thousand dirhams a month and a student marginally better at everything. The marks move when two subjects get the full attention, because that is enough time to find the recurring losses and attack them. Families who cut from four subjects to two and extend the arrangement by a term almost always spend less and see more.

The second is the open-ended subscription. A weekly session that has run for eighteen months without a stated stopping condition has stopped being a plan. If there is no marked evidence every fortnight, there is nothing to review, and the default becomes continuation. The third is late starting: the same tutor costs more and is harder to book in March, and a Year 11 family starting in February is buying the most expensive version of the least effective plan.

The fourth is paying for contact time without marking. This is the most consequential because it is invisible. An hour of pleasant, well-explained teaching feels identical to an hour that produced an annotated script, and only one of them leaves evidence. Ask what arrives after each session before agreeing a rate, and the question itself will usually shift the conversation onto better ground.

sections.heading: VAT, payment and the questions to ask before you pay
paragraphs: Families reasonably ask whether a quoted rate includes VAT. The accurate answer from any provider is about their own prices rather than about the tax treatment of education generally, which is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority and not something a tutoring page should assert. The right question to a provider is simply whether the number quoted is what will be charged, and whether anything is added at invoice. Ours is quoted inclusive of anything we charge, with no booking or administration fee.

Payment structure matters more than most families realise. Paying per session keeps the arrangement reviewable and keeps the provider accountable for each one. Paying for a term up front usually attracts a discount and transfers risk to the family, which is fine where the tutor is already known and poor where they are not. The sensible compromise is to pay per session for the first month, then consider a block once the evidence from the marked work supports it.

Four questions are worth asking of any provider before money changes hands. What happens to a session cancelled with a day's notice. Whether unused sessions in a block expire. Who marks the work, since on some platforms the teacher and the feedback writer are different people. And what happens if the tutor becomes unavailable mid-term, because an answer involving a replacement with your consent is very different from one involving a credit note.

We do not offer any outcome-linked refund and would be wary of anyone who does, because honouring it requires grading the examiner's decision against a marketing promise. What we do offer is a free thirty-minute trial lesson, one per family, with no card details taken, which is the cheapest possible way for a family to test everything on this page before committing anything at all.

sections.heading: Is the tutor you are paying legally permitted to teach?
paragraphs: This question costs nothing to ask and is skipped by almost every family. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

MoHRE's own service page for the permit lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, with applications made through its smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No schedule of fine amounts is published, so treat any page quoting a figure with scepticism; the ministry has not specified them.

There is a separate point about school teachers, and it affects the common idea of hiring your child's own teacher privately. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from providing paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct is reported to bar serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Verify the current wording with the relevant authority, and in the meantime treat such an offer as a question rather than an opportunity.

An operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal from an individual tutor. A training institute in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram does not hold that permit and does not operate premises in the UAE, which is a fact rather than a selling point, and it is why our teaching is delivered online.

sections.heading: Budgeting Years 10 and 11 against the Cambridge calendar
paragraphs: The cheapest version of a two-year plan is the one that spends early. Work done in Year 10 costs the same per hour as work done in Year 11 and does considerably more, because the tier decision is still open, there is time for habits to change, and the tutor you want is not yet booked out by other families' exam panic.

Cambridge's published dates make the shape obvious. For the March 2027 series, final entries are due 27 November 2026, the exam period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, forecast grades are due 27 February 2027, results reach centres on Cambridge Direct on 13 May 2027 and certificates follow in late June. Cambridge runs June and November series as well, and allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones, stating that the correct zone timetable must be used because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam otherwise.

Read backwards from those dates and the budget allocates itself. Tier-decision support belongs a term before the entry deadline, which for a March series means the spring or early autumn beforehand, not December. Content repair belongs in the long middle stretch where rates are lowest and availability best. Whole-paper practice belongs in the final ten weeks, and that is the only period where two sessions a week is usually worth paying for.

The summer between Years 10 and 11 is the underpriced window. Nothing competes for the evening, specialists have availability, and four or five sessions in August addressing the gaps found in July's marked papers is worth more than ten sessions in May. Families who use it typically spend less across the two years than those who do not, which is the only kind of saving in this market that does not cost something else.

process.title: Tell us the subject, the tier and the term you are budgeting
process.description: Cambridge 0620 Extended, Year 10, one session a week until the summer is a brief we can price honestly. A request for your cheapest rate cannot be answered usefully, because the total depends on how many sessions the brief needs, and that depends on what a marked paper shows.

process.title: Get the diagnostic done before you commit money
process.description: We set a full past paper, mark it against the published scheme and sort the losses into habit, misconception and gap. That determines the session count, which is the larger half of your total cost. It also occasionally shows that a short block will do where a family had budgeted a year.

process.title: Settle the tier question if it is still open
process.description: Two sessions, one marked paper from each tier, and a written comparison for the school conversation. It is the highest-return spend available to a Year 10 family because the tier caps the grade, and it has to happen before the board's final entry deadline closes the question.

process.title: Use the free trial, then pay per session for a month
process.description: Thirty minutes with the proposed tutor, no card details taken, one trial per family. After that, pay session by session until the marked work gives you a reason to commit to a block. Paying a term up front before you know the tutor transfers all the risk to you.

process.title: Review at six weeks against two comparable marks
process.description: A baseline paper and a same-style paper six weeks later, both marked, is a measurement rather than an impression. At that point continue with a new target, switch subject, or stop. Reviewing on a schedule is what prevents an arrangement running for eighteen months by default.

whyPoints.title: Rates published and attributed
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page comes from published 2026 Dubai rate guides or providers' own public pricing, is labelled as market rather than ours, and carries the month it was reviewed. Three of the six competitor pages researched for this market publish no price at all, and two quote in currencies UAE families do not transact in.

whyPoints.title: No travel in the price
whyPoints.description: Because lessons are delivered over live video, nobody is paying for an evening drive across Dubai. That accounts for most of the difference between the in-home and online columns in the rate table, and it also means a session can move when a mock week lands rather than being cancelled.

whyPoints.title: Session count quoted, not just an hourly rate
whyPoints.description: We tell a family roughly how many sessions a brief needs before they commit, because that number drives the total far more than the unit price. A short expensive brief frequently costs less than a long cheap one, and families cannot see that from an hourly figure.

whyPoints.title: Marking included and stated
whyPoints.description: Marking a paper against the published mark scheme takes about forty minutes and is the single most valuable thing a tutor produces. It is inside what we quote, and we say so, because the commonest reason two quotes look different is that one of them excludes it silently.

whyPoints.title: Permit questions answered, not dodged
whyPoints.description: The MoHRE private tuition permit is free and valid for two years, so there is no reason for a tutor not to hold one. We treat the question as routine, and we are equally clear that IB Gram holds no KHDA institute permit and operates no UAE premises, because claiming otherwise would be a serious misstatement.

whyPoints.title: No outcome-linked refunds, and no grade promises
whyPoints.description: We do not sell a money-back arrangement tied to a result, because honouring one would mean arguing with an examiner's decision. What is offered instead is a free thirty-minute trial lesson and payment per session for the first month, which puts the risk in the right place while the evidence accumulates.

faqs.question: How much does a Cambridge IGCSE home tutor cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published 2026 market rates put in-home one-to-one tuition at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, with the upper part of that range covering specialist subjects and exam-year briefs. Online one-to-one with a qualified subject tutor runs about AED 150 to 300, and the gap between the two is largely the tutor's evening drive. Monthly in-home packages around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions appear in the market. These are market figures, not IB Gram's price list, and the decisive question for any of them is whether marked written feedback on your child's own work is included.

faqs.question: What makes one Cambridge IGCSE tutor cost double another?
faqs.answer: Usually one of three things rather than raw quality. Scarcity: Additional Mathematics 0606 and Arabic as a First Language 0508 are taught to examination standard by a few dozen people in this city, and Mathematics 0580 by hundreds. Inclusions: marking a paper against the published scheme costs a tutor about forty minutes, and a rate that excludes it is a different product. Career stage: a university student and a career teacher are genuinely different purchases. Proximity to a series adds another ten to twenty-five per cent from February, because specialist diaries fill before the June and March sittings.

faqs.question: How much does a tutor's drive across Dubai add to the hourly rate?
faqs.answer: Somewhere between AED 30 and 150 of an in-home hour, judging by the gap between published in-home and online bands. The more significant cost is not financial. A tutor spending eighty minutes travelling for a sixty-minute lesson can teach two students an evening instead of four, which is why in-home slots are scarce and fixed. A session cannot be moved when a school fixture lands, because a round trip cannot be refitted at a day's notice, and a tutor arriving late will still leave on time because the next family is waiting.

faqs.question: Are monthly tutoring packages better value than paying per lesson?
faqs.answer: They are usually cheaper per hour and they transfer risk from the provider to you. That trade is sensible once you know the tutor and the marked work shows the sessions are working. It is a poor trade in month one, when the match is unproven. Our suggestion is to pay per session for the first four weeks, then consider a block. Before agreeing to any package, ask two questions: do unused sessions expire, and what happens if the tutor becomes unavailable mid-term. A credit note is a very different answer from a replacement tutor with your consent.

faqs.question: Do tutoring fees in Dubai include VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask each provider specifically about their own prices, and treat any page that states the general tax treatment of education as fact with caution, because that is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority rather than for a tutoring website. The useful question is narrow: is the number quoted the number that will be invoiced, and is anything added afterwards. Our quoted figure is what we charge, with no booking or administration fee on top. If a provider cannot answer that question in one sentence, it is worth asking what else is unclear in the quote.

faqs.question: What does it cost to enter Cambridge IGCSE exams as a private candidate?
faqs.answer: The fee is set by the examination centre rather than by us or by Cambridge directly, and it varies by centre, by subject and by how late the entry is made. Students entered through their own school pay nothing separately, as entry sits inside school fees. For private candidates the practical cost control is timing: centres set internal closing dates ahead of the board's final entry deadline, which for the March 2027 series is 27 November 2026. Also check that the centre offers any coursework or practical component your subject requires before committing to the subject.

faqs.question: Did Dubai school fees change for the 2026-27 academic year?
faqs.answer: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. This matters for tutoring decisions because the largest line in most families' education budget is flat this year, which makes an incremental decision easier to size. The sector is also expanding, with seven new private schools opening for 2026-27 and 16,846 new places created.

faqs.question: How far ahead of the papers does a Cambridge entry have to be paid for?
faqs.answer: Months before the exams, which is what catches families out. For the March 2027 series Cambridge's final entry date is 27 November 2026, against an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027, with forecast grades due 27 February 2027 and results on Cambridge Direct on 13 May 2027. Cambridge also runs June and November series with their own published key dates. The practical implication is that a tier or subject conversation started after the entry deadline is a conversation about the following series, so any decision you want to influence has to be raised a term earlier.

faqs.question: Why does Cambridge give my child's school a zone timetable?
faqs.answer: Because exams are sat in many time zones and Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version of the timetable. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong version was used. For a school candidate the exams officer handles this. For a private candidate the family carries the risk, so the question to ask the centre is which zone it sits in, and then to work only from that timetable.

faqs.question: Is group tuition a sensible way to cut the cost per subject?
faqs.answer: For content coverage, yes. Cost per student falls substantially at a group of three or four, and where two children are genuinely at the same point in the same syllabus code and tier, a shared hour can work well. For diagnosis, no. Four students lose marks in four different places and one hour cannot chase all four, so the marked, individual work that moves a grade does not happen. Treat group tuition as a different product rather than a discounted version of one-to-one, and ask specifically whether individual scripts are still marked.

faqs.question: Which spending on tutoring tends not to move a Cambridge IGCSE grade?
faqs.answer: Four patterns. Supporting four subjects at one session a week each, which produces a large bill and a student marginally better at everything. An open-ended weekly slot with no stated stopping condition and no marked evidence to review. Starting in February for a June series, when the same tutor costs more and the plan has to be repair rather than construction. And paying for contact time that produces nothing marked, which is the most expensive of the four because an hour of well-explained teaching feels identical to an hour that produced an annotated script.

faqs.question: Is the private tutor permit in Dubai something the family pays for?
faqs.answer: No. The MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's service page lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time through its smart app, website and e-services. The permit is the tutor's responsibility, not the family's, and because it costs nothing there is no reasonable excuse for not holding one. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts has been published.

faqs.question: How many terms of tutoring should we budget for Years 10 and 11?
faqs.answer: For one subject, plan three to five terms spread across the two years rather than six consecutive ones. The most effective and cheapest allocation puts tier-decision support early in Year 10, content repair through the long middle stretch when rates and availability are best, and whole-paper practice in the final ten weeks, which is the only period where two sessions a week usually justifies itself. The summer between Years 10 and 11 is the underpriced window: four or five sessions in August addressing gaps found in July is worth more than ten in May.

faqs.question: Can we pause and restart tutoring without losing our tutor?
faqs.answer: Usually, and it is worth agreeing the terms before you need them. Because lessons are delivered over video and nobody is holding a travel slot, a pause for a holiday, a mock period or a family trip is a calendar matter rather than a commercial one. What to establish in advance is how long a slot is held, whether a block's unused sessions survive a pause, and whether the same tutor is guaranteed on return. During exam term a popular specialist's slot may not be held indefinitely, and we will say so rather than discover it with you later.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-home-tutor.closingHeading: Get a number that means something
dubai/cambridge-igcse-home-tutor.closingBody: Tell us the Cambridge syllabus code, the tier, the year group and the term you are budgeting for, and send a recent marked paper if one exists. We will tell you roughly how many sessions the brief needs, which is the part of the cost nobody else quotes, and where your money has the highest return, which is often the tier decision rather than another term of lessons. The trial lesson is thirty minutes, free, one per family, with no card details taken, and every AED band on this page is market information you can take to any provider you like.

intro.heading: What a 0417 tutor costs in Dubai, and what the money actually buys
paragraphs: Start with the number, because every other decision follows from it. A qualified subject tutor teaching Cambridge IGCSE ICT 0417 online to a Dubai family sits in a market band of roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts specialist IGCSE and A Level tuition at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. At the budget end, EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52, which buys general homework support rather than marked practical papers. Those are market figures published by those providers, not IB Gram prices.

A home visit costs more, and the reason is arithmetic rather than quality. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one tuition in Dubai at AED 180 to AED 350, and independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to AED 500. Monthly packages seen in this market run to AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour home sessions, against roughly AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. The gap is travel. A tutor crossing from Mirdif to Dubai Marina at five in the afternoon spends longer in the car than in the lesson, and that time is inside your hourly rate whether the invoice itemises it or not.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Dubai. Home visits are a service we run only in India. For UAE families, every lesson is one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, which is also why the subject in your URL suits the format unusually well. Cambridge IGCSE ICT 0417 is assessed mostly through software. Papers 2 and 3 ask the student to produce documents, databases, presentations, spreadsheets and web pages under timed conditions. A tutor watching the student's own screen, cursor and keystrokes sees more diagnostic detail than a tutor sitting beside them, because the file history is visible and reviewable.

The second half of the money question is how many hours you are buying. Most Dubai families who contact us about 0417 start with one 60-minute session a week and raise it to two in the term before the exam series. A Year 10 student building practical fluency needs steady weekly contact more than long sittings. A Year 11 student eight weeks out from the papers needs volume, and the honest version of that conversation includes the fact that volume costs money and that there is a point past which extra hours stop paying for themselves.

What follows is the detail nobody in this search result publishes: the rate bands with their sources, the six variables that move the figure in Dubai specifically, the assessment structure that explains why practical tuition is priced differently from theory tuition, the equipment line most parents forget, a two-year spend plan, and the permit question you should ask anyone you are about to pay in cash. Where a figure comes from a published page, that page is named. Where a figure is not verifiable, it is left out.
