sections.heading: Spreadsheets and website authoring: the two highest-value drills
paragraphs: The spreadsheet and website components reward a narrow set of mechanical skills, which is good news for anyone with limited time. Two or three skills account for most of the lost marks, and each of them responds to repetition rather than to explanation. A student who understands absolute references perfectly and has typed them fifty times behaves differently in an exam from one who understands them and has typed them twice.

On spreadsheets, the recurring losses are replication and references. A formula is typed correctly into one cell and then retyped rather than replicated, so a slip appears three rows down. Or it is replicated without absolute references, so the lookup drifts. Both are visible in the printed evidence of formulae, which the task usually requires, so the examiner sees exactly what happened. Nested functions and conditional logic are the next tier, and the error there is almost always a missing bracket or an argument in the wrong position rather than a misunderstanding.

On website authoring, the single most common disaster is a stylesheet that was written correctly and never attached, which strips every styling mark from a page that would otherwise have scored well. After that come table structures that do not match the specified layout, images referenced with paths that do not resolve when the files are collected, and inline styling used where the task required the stylesheet. Each is a five-minute check that students do not perform under pressure unless they have been trained to.

The drills below are deliberately small. We set them as short set work two or three times a week rather than as long sessions, because the goal is automatic behaviour. A student who checks the stylesheet link before writing any markup has removed a whole category of risk from the paper.

sections.heading: The software environment problem, and why a shared screen solves it
paragraphs: ICT is the only IGCSE where the version of a piece of software can cost marks. Menu locations move between releases, default behaviours differ, and a student taught one route to a dialogue box can be stranded when the ribbon looks different in the school lab. Dubai makes this sharper than most markets because families move between schools and between countries mid-course, and the application suite in use is rarely the first thing anyone checks.

The practical consequence is that a tutor has to work in the student's environment rather than their own. That is awkward to arrange in a room, where the tutor either brings their own machine or peers at the student's from the side, and straightforward over a shared screen, where the tutor sees the actual ribbon, the actual file dialogue and the actual folder structure. When a student cannot find an option, the tutor is looking at the same screen rather than imagining it.

There is a second advantage that matters more as the exam approaches. Watching live means the intervention happens at the error. A student about to save with the wrong filename is stopped before they do it, which is how a habit forms; reviewing the file list afterwards teaches far less. Over several sessions the tutor builds a list of that student's specific recurring slips, and the final weeks are spent on that list rather than on a generic revision plan.

Before the first session we ask two questions: which applications and versions does the school lab use, and what can the student match at home. Where there is a mismatch, it is better to know in October than to discover it in a mock. Occasionally the right advice is to practise in the school's lab at lunchtime and use sessions for review, and we will say so.

sections.heading: The written paper: thirty per cent that students neglect
paragraphs: Because 0417 is a practical subject, the theory paper gets treated as an afterthought, and it costs grades. The content is broad rather than deep: computer systems and devices, storage, networks and their effects, ICT applications, the systems life cycle, safety and security, audience, and communication methods. None of it is conceptually hard. All of it is examined with the precision of a mark scheme.

The characteristic loss is answer grain. Asked to describe two effects of a technology for four marks, students write a paragraph containing three ideas loosely blended, and score two. The fix is procedural: count the marks, make that many distinct points, separate them visibly, and name the thing rather than gesturing at it. Students who do this consistently gain several marks a paper without learning any new content, which is the cheapest improvement available in the subject.

The second loss is the applied question. The paper regularly asks about a scenario, a workplace, a school or a service, and the answer must be about that scenario rather than about the technology in general. Students who have revised definitions answer the definition question they expected. Reading the scenario twice and underlining who it concerns takes fifteen seconds and changes the mark.

Safety, security and the effects of using IT are also the topics where students write from opinion rather than from the syllabus. There are specific, listed effects and specific, listed precautions, and the paper rewards those. A tutor's job here is narrow and useful: teach the list, then drill the grain of the answer against past questions provided through the school or the board's official source.

sections.heading: ICT 0417 or Computer Science 0478? A straight comparison
paragraphs: In many Dubai schools these two subjects sit in the same option column, so this is a real choice rather than a question of ambition. Parents frequently assume computer science is the more serious subject and ICT the easier one. Neither is reliably true, and the student who is placed in the wrong one usually works hard for a mediocre grade in a subject they do not enjoy.

The genuine difference is the mode of work. Computer science is examined entirely on paper: algorithms written by hand, trace tables, Boolean logic, systems theory. It rewards abstraction, patience with symbolic detail and tolerance for being wrong in silence until you find the error. ICT is examined mostly at a keyboard. It rewards accuracy, following a specification exactly, methodical file handling and the discipline to evidence every step.

A student who builds things in code and enjoys debugging belongs in computer science. A student who works accurately, likes a clear specification and takes satisfaction in a correct and tidy result frequently does better in ICT and finds it more interesting. A student who dislikes both but wants a technology subject should look hard at the practical papers before choosing, because seventy per cent of 0417 is produced under timing at a machine.

One further point for Dubai families planning ahead: check what the school offers after Year 11. A Level Computer Science is available at more schools in the emirate than A Level Information Technology, so the Year 9 choice can quietly constrain the sixth-form options. Ask before choosing rather than afterwards.

paragraphs: Practical papers change the economics of tutoring, because a sixty-minute session cannot contain a realistic task plus a review of it. Families planning for 0417 should budget for longer sessions closer to the exam window and shorter ones earlier, which is a different shape from a theory subject. The figures below are published market rates in AED, each attributed to the provider or rate survey that published them in 2026. They are not our price list.

Published Dubai rates put qualified online one-to-one at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors listing IGCSE tuition from AED 150, and in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table giving AED 180 to 350 and independent tutors advertising up to AED 500. Named-syllabus specialists sit at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. Monthly packages advertised locally include AED 799 for eight online sessions.

For this subject there is a format question as well as a price question. A ninety-minute practical session costs more than an hour and is worth more than two hours split in half, because the task has to be produced end to end. Conversely, drilling a single skill such as absolute references needs twenty focused minutes, not ninety. Families who get good value here tend to mix the two rather than buying one rhythm for the whole year.

IB Gram's model is a free first lesson with the matched tutor, no card details taken, then a written plan and a quote in AED. We publish the market bands so that quote arrives with context, and we will say when the sensible plan is a short pre-series block rather than a year of weekly sessions.

sections.heading: Entries, zone timetables and the practical papers' logistics
paragraphs: Practical papers have an administrative layer that written papers do not, and it is the school that manages it: lab availability, software configuration, the collection and submission of candidate files. A parent cannot influence most of it, but knowing it exists explains why ICT mock arrangements are sometimes awkward and why practising in the school's own environment matters.

On entries, Cambridge runs IGCSE examinations in a June series and a November series, and the deadlines sit months before the papers. Cambridge's published key dates for the March 2027 series show the pattern plainly: final entries close on 27 November 2026 for an exam period beginning on 3 February 2027, with forecast grades due on 27 February 2027 and results released on Direct on 13 May. Dates differ by series; the lead time does not.

The detail most worth acting on is the timetable version. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable for each, stating that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam through using the wrong one. Practical papers are often scheduled in sessions rather than as a single sitting, which makes using the school's issued timetable rather than a downloaded one more important here than elsewhere.

Read backwards, a 0417 year has a clear shape: software environment confirmed and matched at home by the autumn; all practical task types attempted once by the end of term one of Year 11; the theory paper drilled for answer grain from January; and full timed tasks, printed and checked, from February onwards. Students who leave the first full timed task until April almost always discover an evidence habit they do not have.

faqs.question: What does Cambridge IGCSE ICT 0417 actually assess?
faqs.answer: Three components: a written theory paper covering computer systems, storage, networks, the effects of using IT, ICT applications, the systems life cycle, safety and security, audience and communication, plus two practical papers produced at a computer. The practical work covers document production, databases, presentations, spreadsheets and website authoring, and candidates submit files and printed evidence. Confirm the current structure, durations and weightings against the Cambridge 0417 syllabus for your child's exam series, since component detail changes between syllabus cycles.

faqs.question: How much of the qualification is practical rather than written?
faqs.answer: The clear majority. One paper is written and two are produced at a computer, and between them the practical components carry considerably more weight than the theory. This matters because families instinctively buy theory revision, since that is what revision looks like, while the marks sit in the practical papers. A plan for this subject should start with a full timed practical task and work outwards, not with a textbook. Check the exact weightings for your child's series with the school.

faqs.question: Which software does my child need at home for the practical papers?
faqs.answer: Whatever the school's lab uses, as closely as possible. Menu locations, default behaviours and printing options differ between application suites and between versions, and a student taught one route can be stranded when the ribbon looks different. Ask the ICT department which applications and which versions they teach in, then check what the student can match at home. Where there is a mismatch, practising at school during lunchtime and using sessions for review is sometimes the better arrangement.

faqs.question: Does the version of the software really affect marks?
faqs.answer: Not directly, but it affects whether a student can find what they need under timing, and that costs marks. The paper asks for an outcome; the candidate has to produce it in the environment in front of them. A student who has only ever used one release may not know where a printing option or a stylesheet setting lives in another. This is the one IGCSE where a family moving between schools or countries mid-course should check the lab software before the first lesson.

faqs.question: What is an evidence document and why do students lose marks on it?
faqs.answer: Several practical tasks require proof that a step was carried out, typically a screenshot or a printed output collected into one document. The proof is the mark, not the doing. Confident students are the most likely to skip it, because to them the work is self-evidently complete, and they lose marks on tasks they performed correctly. The habit we drill is treating the evidence document as the deliverable from the first session rather than as an afterthought at the end of a task.

faqs.question: Where do students lose marks on the spreadsheet work?
faqs.answer: Overwhelmingly in replication and references. A formula typed correctly into one cell and then retyped down a column introduces a slip; a formula replicated without fixing the reference makes the lookup drift. Both are visible in the printed evidence of formulae, which the task usually requires, so the examiner sees exactly what happened. After that come nested functions with an argument in the wrong position and charts built from a range that includes a header row or an extra column.

faqs.question: Does my child need to learn HTML and CSS for 0417?
faqs.answer: The website authoring component requires page structure, stylesheets, tables, links and images, so yes, at the level the syllabus specifies rather than at a developer's level. The most common and most expensive error is a stylesheet written correctly and never attached, which strips every styling mark from a page that would otherwise have scored well. The second is image or link paths that work locally and break when the files are collected. Both are five-minute checks that need to be trained until automatic.

faqs.question: Should my child choose ICT 0417 or Computer Science 0478?
faqs.answer: They often sit in the same option column in Dubai schools, so it is a real choice. Computer science is examined entirely on paper through algorithms, trace tables, logic and systems theory, and rewards abstraction and patient debugging. ICT is mostly produced at a keyboard and rewards accuracy, following a specification exactly and methodical file handling. Also check the sixth form: A Level Computer Science is offered by more Dubai schools than A Level Information Technology, so the Year 9 choice can constrain later options.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor really help with a practical subject?
faqs.answer: For this subject the shared screen is the strongest format available. The tutor sees the student's actual ribbon, file dialogue and folder structure, and can stop them at the moment an error occurs rather than reviewing the result afterwards. A tutor in the room watches one keyboard from an angle. The practical constraint is session length: a realistic task plus a review needs about ninety minutes, so the format changes rather than the delivery method being a compromise.

faqs.question: How much does an ICT tutor cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published figures put qualified online one-to-one at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors listing IGCSE tuition from AED 150, and named-syllabus specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. In-home one-to-one runs roughly AED 180 to 500 per Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table and local advertising. Those are other providers' published rates as of October 2026. Budget for longer sessions nearer the exam window, since practical tasks need ninety minutes rather than sixty.

faqs.question: Is IGCSE ICT recognised for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: ICT 0417 is an accredited IGCSE subject, so it can form part of the published British-track requirement of five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one A Level at grade E or two AS Levels. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. Equivalency is assessed by the Ministry of Education, not by any tutoring provider, and nobody should present it as something they can perform or accelerate, so verify your child's combination through the Ministry's own channel.

faqs.question: How many weeks of practical practice does a student realistically need?
faqs.answer: Six to eight weeks of regular timed tasks is the pattern we see work, which means starting in January rather than April for a June series. The reason is that the gains are procedural: filenames, evidence, printing options, replication discipline. Those habits need repetition under mild pressure, and they decay if practised once. A student doing one full timed task a fortnight from January arrives with a personal error checklist; a student starting in April arrives with a list and no habits.

faqs.question: Can a tutor work through past practical tasks with my child?
faqs.answer: Yes, using material obtained legitimately through the school or from the board's own published resources. We do not supply or redistribute Cambridge papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents or grade boundary tables, because those belong to Cambridge; a tutor references the official source and teaches the student to work from it. In practice the school's ICT department can usually provide appropriate practice tasks, and a tutor adds the timing, the inspection and the review rather than the material.

faqs.question: Does 0417 lead anywhere after Year 11?
faqs.answer: The direct continuation is AS and A Level Information Technology, which has heavier practical components and considerably stricter documentation than the IGCSE. Fewer Dubai schools offer it than offer A Level Computer Science, so check the sixth-form provision before assuming the pathway exists in-house. Students moving to the IB Diploma can continue with Digital Society, which rewards the analytical side of the subject rather than application fluency. Either way, the written-answer discipline built in 0417 theory transfers.

faqs.question: My child uses computers constantly but scores badly on the practical papers. Why?
faqs.answer: Because fluent computer use and examinable file production are different skills, and the second one is clerical. A student can edit video, build sites for fun and fix the home router, and still lose marks because a file was saved with a name that was close but not identical, or a required screenshot was never taken. The marks sit in the margins around the work and those margins are examined. Rehearsal with inspection fixes it quickly, usually inside five or six sessions.

intro.heading: The decision you are actually making
paragraphs: Most families searching for a 0607 home tutor in Dubai are not comparing tutors. They are reacting to something: a mock result, a parents' evening, a child who has stopped doing maths homework. The search happens in an evening, two or three providers get a message, and the one that answers first with a plausible rate gets the booking. That is how a tutoring decision usually gets made, and it is why so many of them are abandoned by week five.

A better approach costs almost nothing and takes about a week. Establish what the syllabus actually is, which this page sets out. Establish who can teach it, which is a smaller group than the market suggests. Ask a short list of screening questions, which are printed below so you can use them on anyone. Run a trial as a test rather than a sales call. Then decide, with a written plan in front of you, whether to buy six sessions or a term.

The home-tutoring question deserves a straight answer rather than a sales argument. In-home one-to-one visits in Dubai are widely available and published market rates run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is accounted for, against about AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. The difference is not a quality discount; it is the road. A tutor who crosses the emirate for a single hour has to price the journey somewhere, usually as a higher rate or a two-hour minimum.

For International Mathematics there is a second constraint that matters more than price. The number of people in Dubai who teach 0607 specifically, with the graphics display calculator and the investigation paper included, is small. Filtering that group by driving distance from your community leaves very few names, and the shortlist is then made of whoever is near rather than whoever knows the syllabus. That is the trade this page asks you to look at honestly.

It is worth being clear about what this page is not. It is not an argument that in-home tutoring is a poor product, because for some children and some households it is clearly the right one, and there are capable independent tutors in Dubai doing it well. It is an argument that for one narrow syllabus, sat by a small cohort, the location filter costs you more than it buys. Reasonable families will read the same comparison and reach a different answer, and the point of printing the numbers is that the decision stays yours.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; in-home tuition is a service we run only in India. In the UAE every lesson is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The rest of the page is written so that the comparison is checkable rather than asserted: supply, cost, household logistics, screening questions, what a trial should produce, and the point at which you should walk away from an arrangement that is not working.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-international-math.programmesIntro: Before comparing tutors it helps to be sure what your child is being examined on, because a surprising number of Dubai families discover at the first session that the syllabus they described is not the one on the statement of entry. These four are the ones most often confused with each other in this emirate.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics
programmes.description: Three components in either Core or Extended tier, a graphics display calculator assumed throughout, and an investigation component that no other Cambridge maths syllabus carries. Written for international schools and aligned to the IB Diploma maths courses. If this is the code on the entry, a tutor needs to be fluent with the device and to have read investigation scripts before.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai this is the signature of an IB-continuum or international school rather than a British-curriculum one. Families moving between the two sectors inside the emirate sometimes change maths syllabus without being told it is a change, which is why the statement of entry rather than the school's prospectus is the document to work from when hiring help.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics
programmes.description: The mainstream Cambridge maths syllabus, Core and Extended, with no investigation component and a scientific calculator rather than a graphics one. Far more candidates sit it worldwide, so the tutor pool is much larger and quotes are correspondingly lower. The content overlaps heavily with 0607 without the technology or the open-ended reasoning.
programmes.countryNote: This is the default in most Dubai British-curriculum schools and it is the reason a general maths tutor in the emirate is usually a 0580 tutor. Hiring one for a 0607 candidate is not a disaster, since most of the content transfers, but it means two parts of the examined course are being left alone and you should know that before paying rather than after.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS & A Level Mathematics
programmes.description: The two-year sixth-form route in most Dubai British-curriculum schools, built from Pure Mathematics plus Mechanics or Statistics components. It assumes Extended IGCSE content and then moves quickly into calculus and radians. A student arriving from 0607 Extended brings strong graph reasoning and will need to build algebraic stamina.
programmes.countryNote: Worth knowing even if your child is in Year 10, because the sixth form a family is aiming at changes which tier is the right 0607 entry. Dubai sixth forms set their own entry requirements for maths and publish them, so the honest way to settle the question is to read the requirement for the school you have in mind rather than to ask a tutor.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Mathematics, both routes
programmes.description: Analysis and Approaches for the algebra-and-proof route, Applications and Interpretation for the modelling-and-technology route, each at Standard or Higher Level, both with an internal exploration written by the student. The 0607 syllabus was designed with these courses in view, which is why the calculator and investigation work transfer so directly.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's IB sector is expanding: the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, three of them International Baccalaureate, among 16,846 new places in total. Many of those schools examine IGCSE at sixteen before the Diploma, so a Year 10 maths tier decision made this term is in practice a decision about which Diploma course is comfortable in two years.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-international-math.subjectsIntro: Households rarely need one subject in isolation, and a Dubai family hiring for 0607 often has a second request within a term. The codes below are the ones most commonly paired with International Mathematics in this emirate, with a note on what each assessment actually rewards.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics 0606
subjects.description: Taken alongside a main maths entry by strong candidates, adding differentiation, integration, logarithms, series, radians and vectors. Two written papers, no coursework. It is the usual stretch option in British-curriculum Dubai schools, and it is a different hire from a 0607 tutor despite both being maths.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Multiple choice, theory and either a practical test or the written alternative. Marks concentrate in equation recall, in precise experimental description, and in the gap between describe, explain and calculate. It is the commonest second request from families already booking maths support.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Theory papers with a practical or written alternative. Mole calculations and ionic equations are where marks move, and definitions are marked for precision rather than for gist, so a nearly-correct wording scores nothing at all.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: Content-heavy and assessed largely through command terms, with a practical component. Students lose marks by describing a trend when asked to explain it, and by omitting the control when asked to design an investigation.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Arabic as a Foreign Language 0544
subjects.description: Listening, reading and writing components for non-native learners. The writing task is assessed on accuracy and on range, so a student who writes safely in short sentences caps their own mark. Dubai students often take this alongside the mandatory school Arabic provision rather than instead of it.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE French 0520
subjects.description: Listening, reading, writing and a speaking component assessed by the school. The speaking element is where preparation pays most, because it rewards extended, prepared answers to predictable prompts rather than spontaneous fluency.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Spanish 0530
subjects.description: The same shape as French, with a widely used Dubai cohort. Marks are lost on tense accuracy in the writing paper more than on vocabulary, which makes targeted grammar correction on the student's own written work the highest-yield support.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Geography 0460
subjects.description: Physical and human geography with case-study requirements and a skills paper. The skills paper, including map and graph interpretation, is the component where a mathematically confident student can gain quickly, and it is often the least revised.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE History 0470
subjects.description: Source-based and essay papers in which the mark depends on using evidence to support an argument rather than on recalling more of it. Students who write everything they know and reach no judgement consistently stall in the middle bands.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Information and Communication Technology 0417
subjects.description: A theory paper plus practical components assessed on documents, databases and spreadsheets produced to a brief. Marks go on following the brief exactly, so students who produce something better than what was asked for still lose the mark.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-international-math.regionsIntro: The communities below are ones where the in-home question comes up most, usually because they are villa areas where hosting a tutor is physically easy and the drive to reach them is not. The notes cover what each setting actually implies for a weekday session.

regions.name: Jumeirah Golf Estates
regions.note: Large villas with space for a tutor to work undisturbed and a long drive from almost every school cluster. Hosting is easy here and supply is the constraint: the number of 0607 specialists willing to make that journey for one hour is close to none.

regions.name: The Springs and The Meadows
regions.note: Established villa communities with mature year groups and a short run to several international schools. Families here often already have a tutor for one subject, which makes the screening questions on this page the useful part rather than the cost comparison.

regions.name: Remraam and Dubai Investment Park
regions.note: Affordable communities a long way from the central school cluster, with a high proportion of single-income households. Cost sensitivity is real, and the honest recommendation here is often a defined six-session block rather than an open-ended term.

regions.name: Al Warqa'a and Al Khawaneej
regions.note: Eastern villa areas with large families and several children at school at once. The sibling question comes up constantly, and it has a real answer, which is that a shared session works for content review and does not work for an investigation task.

regions.name: Jumeirah Islands and The Lakes
regions.note: Low-density communities where a visiting tutor needs parking, a route in and a guest space, all of which exist. What does not exist is a short drive, so in practice the local market quotes at the upper end of the published in-home band here.

regions.name: Mudon and Arabian Ranches 3
regions.note: Newer family communities with young Year 10 cohorts and a bus run that frequently arrives after 4.45pm. A 5pm in-home booking is therefore theoretical, and the realistic weekday window opens at about seven in the evening.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: Denser housing with strong connectivity and a cluster of schools inside the same ring road. Short commutes mean an earlier slot is genuinely possible here, which is unusual in Dubai and worth using if your child concentrates better before dinner.

schoolClusters.city: Schools in the southern and western corridor
schoolClusters.note: A spread of British and international schools serving the newer communities along the Al Khail and Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed corridors. Maths entries here vary between schools and sometimes between year groups in the same school, which is exactly why the statement of entry matters more than the school's name.

schoolClusters.city: Schools on the eastern side of the emirate
schoolClusters.note: Long-established schools serving Mirdif, Al Warqa'a, Al Khawaneej and the Creek-side communities. Year groups here are often larger, which means a wider ability range in one maths class and more students for whom the tier decision is genuinely open.

sections.heading: Who can actually teach 0607 in Dubai
paragraphs: The supply question is the one that decides everything else, and no provider in this market publishes an honest answer to it. Dubai has a large population of maths teachers and tutors, and the great majority of them teach Cambridge 0580, Edexcel Mathematics A, or a national curriculum. International Mathematics is sat by a smaller cohort in a particular kind of school, so the group with real experience of it is correspondingly smaller, and the group with real experience of the investigation component is smaller again.

That has a specific consequence for a parent. When you ask a Dubai agency for a 0607 tutor, the reply is frequently a maths tutor who is confident with the content and has never used a graphics display calculator in a lesson. Nothing dishonest need be happening: the content genuinely does overlap, and the tutor will teach it capably. What will not happen is any work on the two things that make the syllabus distinct, and you will not find that out until a results day.

The table below sets out the realistic sources of a 0607 tutor in this emirate, what each is likely to be strong at, and the one thing to verify in each case. It is written to be used on any provider, including this one. The single most useful question in it is the simplest: ask which calculator model they teach on, because a tutor who has taught 0607 has an immediate answer and a tutor who has not does not.

sections.heading: What an in-home visit costs in money and in minutes
paragraphs: Published Dubai rates group into bands. Budget online tutors advertise from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, qualified online subject tutors AED 150 to 300, in-home one-to-one visits AED 180 to 500 with travel included, IGCSE and IB specialists AED 200 to 450, and premium named tutors have been quoted as high as AED 650. Monthly packages seen in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those figures come from providers' own published pages and from Bestimate's 2026 Dubai cost survey, not from us.

The minutes matter as much as the dirhams and almost nobody prices them. A visiting tutor crossing from one side of Dubai to the other in the early evening is committing something like ninety minutes of road time for a sixty-minute lesson. They can therefore sell fewer slots in a week, and each slot has to carry part of the journey. That is most of the gap between the in-home and online bands, and it is why a two-hour minimum is so often attached: it halves the dead time per paid hour.

A two-hour block is not automatically good value for a Year 11 either. Concentration on written mathematics degrades, and the second hour frequently becomes supervised homework at a specialist's hourly rate. Two separate sessions in the same week, with marked work in between, does more for the same money. That preference is easier to arrange without travel, which is one of the quieter advantages of the online format rather than a sales point about it.

sections.heading: The household logistics nobody puts on a pricing page
paragraphs: Beyond cost there is a set of practical questions that decide whether an arrangement survives. Who is at home during the session. Whether there is a room with a door. What happens when a younger sibling comes home. Whether a visiting adult in the house suits your family, and whether anyone has to be present for it. These are not awkward questions and they are rarely discussed, with the result that many arrangements fail for reasons that have nothing to do with teaching.

Some of them favour a visit. A child who will not sit down without an adult in the room is better served by one. A household with poor connectivity, or with no space a student can occupy alone for an hour, is better served by one. So is a family that genuinely wants the tutor to be a known face rather than a video window. Those are real preferences and a provider that dismisses them is selling rather than advising.

Others favour video strongly. Sibling logistics are easier, because two children can have sessions at different times without anyone travelling twice. Travel plans are easier, because a family in Europe in July keeps the same tutor. A supervising parent can be in the kitchen rather than in the room, which a sixteen-year-old usually prefers. And the household does not need to be presentable at seven in the evening, which over a full academic year is worth more than families expect. The table sets out the factors side by side.

sections.heading: Seven questions to ask before the first invoice
paragraphs: The questions below are the ones that separate a competent arrangement from an expensive one, and they work on any provider in this market. None of them is about price. All of them are answerable in a two-minute conversation, and the pattern in the answers tells you more than any rate card: a tutor who has taught this syllabus answers specifically and quickly, while one who has not answers in general terms about experience and results.

Two of the seven matter most for 0607 in particular. The calculator question is a direct test of whether the syllabus has been taught, because the answer is either a model name or a pause. The investigation question is the other, since it is the component most often skipped entirely. A provider who says the investigation paper does not need separate preparation is describing a plan that leaves a whole examined component to chance.

The marking question is the one families most often forget. An hour of teaching with nothing marked between sessions is a different product from an hour that follows marked homework, and the two are frequently sold at the same rate. Ask whether marking is included, who does it, and against what. The honest answer involves the published mark scheme.

There is an eighth question that is really a test of the other seven: ask what would make them tell you to stop. A provider who can describe the circumstances in which they would recommend ending the arrangement, or changing the tutor, has thought about how it is judged. A provider who cannot imagine such a circumstance is selling a subscription. The table gives each of the seven with what a good answer sounds like and the warning sign to watch for, and it is as usable on this platform as on any other.

sections.heading: Running the trial lesson as a test, not a sales call
paragraphs: A free trial is worth having and is easy to waste. Used well it is a diagnostic: the tutor should spend most of it finding out what your child can and cannot do, and you should receive something in writing afterwards. Used badly it becomes a friendly conversation in which the tutor establishes rapport, promises a plan and asks for a booking, and you learn nothing you could not have guessed.

Ask for three things from a 0607 trial specifically. A spread of content questions, so the strand map is real. One short investigation task, because a content-only diagnostic misses the component most at risk. And something on the calculator, so you find out whether your child can set a window and find an intersection or has been pressing buttons hopefully for two years. Forty-five minutes is enough for all three if the session is run as an assessment.

Afterwards you should hold a document: a strand-by-strand note of what was secure and what was not, an error log sorted by cause rather than by topic, and a recommended starting point. You should keep it whether or not you book anything, and it should be specific enough to be useful to a different tutor. Our trial is a free 45-minute session, no card required and nothing to cancel, and the notes are yours either way. If a provider will not put the trial's findings in writing, that is itself the finding.
bullets: Content questions across the strands, not one topic in depth
One short investigation task attempted cold
A calculator check: viewing window, intersection, a statistical summary

sections.heading: Two children, two syllabuses, one evening
paragraphs: Dubai households are often large and the tutoring question is rarely about one child. A common shape is a Year 11 on 0607 and a Year 9 who needs general maths support, or two Year 10s in different schools on different syllabuses. The instinct is to put them together, and sometimes that is right. More often it produces a session that suits neither, because the two children are not at the same point in the same course.

A shared session works for content review when both children are on the same syllabus and the same tier, and when both are reasonably willing. It works for recall drills, for going through a marked paper where the errors overlap, and for calculator work. It does not work for an investigation task, which requires one reader for one student's written reasoning, and it does not work across different syllabuses, where the tutor ends up alternating and each child gets half an hour at full price.

The practical answer is usually two shorter separate sessions rather than one shared longer one, which is cheap to arrange when nobody travels and awkward when someone does. That is a genuine logistical advantage of the online format rather than an argument about teaching quality. Where a shared slot is right, we will say so, and where it is not, we will say that instead rather than take a booking that quietly fails in week three.

One further household pattern is worth naming because it is so common here. An older sibling who sat 0607 two years ago is frequently used as the family's maths support, and that can work well for content review. What an older sibling cannot usually do is mark to a published scheme, read an investigation script as a stranger would, or say honestly that the tier is wrong. Using them for homework help and buying a specialist for the examined components is often the cheapest sensible arrangement in a large Dubai household.

sections.heading: The first month, and the moment to stop
paragraphs: Families are good at starting tutoring and poor at ending it. An arrangement that is not working usually continues for a term because nobody has defined what working would look like, and because stopping feels like a judgement on the child. Defining the evidence at the start removes both problems, which is why this page is insistent about documents rather than about rates.

The first month should produce four things: a strand map from the diagnostic, marked homework from each session with method and accuracy marks separated, an error log grouped by cause, and one re-test showing whether the first topic worked on has stuck. That is enough to make a judgement. It is deliberately not a predicted grade, because a tutor predicting a grade is guessing and your child's school is the only party with the evidence to do it properly.

The moment to stop is when the error log shows the same named causes after two re-tests on material that has been taught twice. At that point more hours of the same will not help, and the honest options are a different approach, a different tutor or a conversation with the school about coverage. We will raise that rather than wait for you to notice, and a provider who will not define in advance what would cause them to raise it is asking you to buy something unmeasurable.

Stopping is also sometimes the right answer for a reason nobody likes to say aloud, which is that the child has had enough. A Year 11 in Dubai may be carrying nine or ten subjects, a long bus run and two or three activities, and adding a weekly session to a schedule that is already full can cost more in exhaustion than it returns in marks. Where that is what the evidence suggests, a pause with a restart date is a better recommendation than a reduced rate, and it is the one we would make.

sections.heading: Permits, premises and the claims we will not make
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is lawful and regulated, and a parent is entitled to ask about it. The instrument is the private tuition work permit introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, applied for through MoHRE's smart app, website and e-services system under the service name Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a stated two-working-day completion time. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since no schedule of amounts is published, no figure should be quoted to you by anybody.

Two related points come up in Dubai conversations. A tutoring business with premises and staff in the emirate is a different legal thing from an individual tutor and requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, renewed annually with the request made at least thirty days before expiry. And in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, which the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also reflects. A provider offering to arrange your child's own teacher privately is offering something that should not be on sale.

Our own limits, in plain words. IB Gram is a tutor-matching platform with no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or IB endorsement, no licence as a school or training institute in the UAE, and no premises in the country. We publish no star ratings, no student counts and no success percentages, because a figure without its sample size, date and method is not information. We make no promise about a grade. We do not perform or guarantee Ministry of Education equivalency, which is the Ministry's process and should be checked on moe.gov.ae. And we do not state the VAT treatment of tuition as a general fact, since that is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority; what we will tell you is whether a specific quote includes it.

faqs.question: Do 0607 tutors in Dubai come to the villa?
faqs.answer: Some do. In-home one-to-one tutoring is widely sold in this emirate and published rates run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is included, often with a two-hour minimum, with monthly in-home packages advertised around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. IB Gram does not sell that in the UAE; in-home tuition is something we run only in India. The harder constraint for International Mathematics is not the money but the shortlist: filtering a small pool of 0607 specialists by who will drive to your community usually leaves nobody who teaches the syllabus.

faqs.question: What is a fair quote for a 0607 tutor in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Judge a quote by what it includes rather than by the number. Published bands put budget online tutors at roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, qualified online subject tutors at AED 150 to 300, in-home visits at AED 180 to 500, specialists at AED 200 to 450 and premium named tutors as high as AED 650, from providers' own pages and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai survey. Then ask whether marking is included, whether the rate is per hour or per session, whether VAT is stated, and whether the person has ever taught the investigation component. Two quotes at the same number can be very different products.

faqs.question: Can a Year 11 and a Year 9 share the same 0607 slot?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it should be assessed rather than assumed. A shared session works when both children are on the same syllabus and the same tier and both are reasonably willing: content review, recall drills, calculator work and going through a marked paper with overlapping errors all survive sharing. It does not work for an investigation task, which needs one reader for one student's written reasoning, and it does not work across different syllabuses, where each child effectively gets half a session at the full rate. Two shorter separate slots are usually better, and cost nothing extra in travel.

faqs.question: How do I check a tutor actually knows 0607 before paying?
faqs.answer: Ask two questions and listen to how quickly they are answered. Which calculator model do you teach on, and have you taught the investigation component. Someone who has taught this syllabus answers both immediately and specifically. Someone who has not talks about experience, results and general IGCSE maths. Then ask for a trial that includes one short investigation task, because that is the part a content-only trial will not reveal. None of this requires you to know the mathematics yourself.

faqs.question: What should actually happen in a trial lesson?
faqs.answer: It should be an assessment, not a conversation. For 0607 that means a spread of content questions so the strand map is real, one short investigation task attempted cold, and a calculator check covering a viewing window, an intersection and a statistical summary. Afterwards you should hold a written note of what was secure, an error log sorted by cause rather than topic, and a recommended starting point, specific enough to be useful to a different tutor. Ours is 45 minutes, free, with no card required, and the notes are yours whether or not you continue.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre class a better value option than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: Per student it is cheaper, and for content taught from the front it can be perfectly sound. Two things limit it for this syllabus. The investigation component needs one reader for one student's written reasoning, which a group format cannot really provide. And in Dubai the practical obstacle is assembling the group at all: 0607 candidates in any one area are fewer than 0580 candidates and are spread across schools at different points in the course, so a group of four at the same stage is hard to find rather than merely rare.

faqs.question: My son does not want a tutor at all. Does online make that easier?
faqs.answer: Usually, slightly, for a reason that has nothing to do with teaching. A sixteen-year-old who resents the idea often objects most to a stranger arriving in the house and to the family watching the lesson happen. A video session in his own room, with a parent nearby rather than present, removes a good deal of that friction. What it does not remove is the underlying objection, and the thing that generally shifts that is a first session in which somebody competent explains why four specific marks were lost, rather than a session about effort and attitude.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be in the room during an online session?
faqs.answer: No, and for most sixteen-year-olds it is better not to be. Being nearby, with the door open and the session visible if you glance in, is the arrangement most families settle on. What is worth doing instead is reading what arrives afterwards: the marked work, the error log and the fortnightly note tell you more about the session than sitting through it would. For younger children the answer changes, and if your child genuinely needs an adult alongside them to work, we would say that this format is not the right one.

faqs.question: Should we book a whole term in advance to secure a slot?
faqs.answer: Book the slot, not the term. Holding a fixed weekly time for a term is genuinely useful, because a schedule renegotiated every week is how fourteen planned sessions become nine. Paying for a term in advance is a different thing and it removes your ability to act on what the evidence shows at week four. A six-session block with a stated target and a written closing review gives you the continuity without the commitment, and it should renew deliberately rather than roll on by itself.

faqs.question: What happens if my daughter and the tutor do not get on?
faqs.answer: It is a common outcome rather than a failure, and it should be cheap to fix. Ask any provider before you pay what their replacement process is and whether it costs anything, because the answer varies enormously in this market and some arrangements are effectively locked for a term. Our position is that a match that is not working gets changed, and that the strand map and error log transfer to the new tutor so the work does not restart from zero. A bad match found in week two costs far less than one tolerated until April.

faqs.question: Is marking between sessions included in the rate?
faqs.answer: Ask, because it frequently is not, and it is most of the value. An hour of teaching with nothing marked in between is a conversation; an hour that follows marked homework and precedes a written note is a course. When you ask, the useful follow-up is what the marking is against: the honest answer is the published mark scheme, with method marks and accuracy marks shown separately, so you can see which marks were lost to understanding and which to carelessness. A number with no script attached tells you nothing you can act on.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying more for someone who has taught the investigation paper?
faqs.answer: Yes, more than for almost any other single qualification in this syllabus. The investigation component is examined, is a meaningful share of the marks, and is the part a crowded Year 11 scheme of work most often leaves until April. It is also the part a tutor cannot fake, because teaching it means setting unfamiliar tasks and reading written reasoning rather than working through examples. If a provider tells you it needs no separate preparation, they are describing a plan that leaves a whole component to chance.

faqs.question: Can we pause tutoring over the Dubai summer?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most families should at least partly. Dubai empties in July and August and a slot left vacant for eight weeks is hard to recover, so the sensible options are an agreed pause with a restart date in the diary, or a short holiday block of three or four sessions aimed at one specific thing. For a student entering Year 11 the second is often worth it: the non-calculator paper and the calculator skills both respond well to summer work, and neither needs the school to have taught anything first.

faqs.question: How much notice is needed to move or cancel a session?
faqs.answer: Ask for the rule in writing before you pay, because this is the single commonest source of disputes in private tutoring anywhere. A reasonable arrangement has a stated notice period, treats a genuine illness differently from a forgotten appointment, and does not charge for a session the tutor cancels. What to be wary of is a term paid in advance with no stated policy at all, since that combination gives you no remedy and gives the tutor no reason to protect the slot.

faqs.question: Does VAT apply to the quote, and who can tell us the rules?
faqs.answer: The authority on UAE VAT is the Federal Tax Authority, and the treatment of tuition fees depends on the provider and the circumstances rather than on a general rule a tutoring page can state. What any provider should tell you plainly is whether the figure they have quoted you includes VAT or not, and whether they hold a tax registration number. Ask for that in writing on the quote itself. A rate quoted without saying whether it is inclusive, and without saying whether it is per hour or per session, is not yet a quote.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-international-math.closingHeading: Buy the trial, not the term
dubai/cambridge-igcse-international-math.closingBody: The cheapest useful step is a diagnostic, and the second cheapest is asking seven questions. Send the statement of entry so the code and the tier are facts rather than assumptions, then book the free 45-minute trial and ask for an investigation task and a calculator check inside it. You will come out holding a strand map, an error log sorted by cause and a recommended starting point, which is yours whether or not you book anything, and which is specific enough to use with any tutor in Dubai. If a six-session block with a stated endpoint is the right purchase, that is what we will suggest; if the right answer is a conversation with the school about the tier, we will say that instead.

intro.heading: Why the calendar decides more than the syllabus does
paragraphs: Two families can buy the same number of tutoring hours for the same syllabus and get very different results, and the usual difference is when the hours were bought. The 0607 year has a shape. There is a period in which content can still be learned properly, a period in which only technique can be fixed, and a period in which nothing can be changed except pacing and nerve. Hours spent in the wrong one of those are not wasted exactly, but they buy far less than the same hours spent earlier.

The dates that create that shape are set by Cambridge and administered by your child's school, and almost none of them are published where a parent would look. Cambridge runs its International GCSE examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The final entry deadline for a series sits months before the papers: the published key dates for the March 2027 series show final entries due on 27 November 2026 against an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027.

Read that gap and the planning becomes concrete. The decision about which subjects and tiers a child is entered for is taken by an administrator working to a deadline roughly ten to twelve weeks before the first paper. Mock results that land in late January are therefore evidence for a decision that has already been made. A family that wants a say has to be looking at marked work in the autumn term, which is exactly when nobody is worried yet.

There is one further Cambridge detail that catches UAE families out every year. Every exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the centre's zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Two Dubai schools can therefore sit the same paper at different times. Your child's dates come from their own school's timetable and from no other source.

None of this is an argument for starting earlier out of anxiety. It is an argument for knowing which period you are in, because the right purchase differs completely between them. A family with thirty weeks left should buy content teaching with marked homework. A family with eight weeks left should buy timed papers and error-log work and should refuse a provider who offers to cover the syllabus. Being sold the wrong one of those two is the commonest way tutoring money is wasted in this emirate.

This page is written around that calendar. Everything in it is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai, since in-home tuition is a service we run only in India. Dates from Cambridge and Pearson are quoted with their source and are the kind that get revised, so treat every one of them as something to confirm with your school's exams officer and against the board's own published timetable rather than as settled fact.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-international-math.programmesIntro: The four stages below are the points at which a Dubai student's mathematics is formally assessed, and each one has its own calendar. Seeing them in sequence is what makes it obvious why the autumn of Year 10 is a better time to intervene than the spring of Year 11.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary Mathematics and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The pre-IGCSE stage, with Checkpoint tests available in March, May and October. The tests are diagnostic rather than qualifying, and their value to a family is as the last cheap warning before the two-year examined course begins. A weak Checkpoint result in algebra is the single most useful predictor of trouble in Year 10.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools use Checkpoint unevenly: some enter whole year groups, others use internal assessment instead. Where your child's school does enter it, ask for the breakdown by strand rather than the overall score, because the strand profile is what a Year 10 plan should be built on and it is the part that rarely reaches parents.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics
programmes.description: Three components in Core or Extended tier, sat in a single series, with a graphics display calculator assumed and an investigation component unique to this syllabus among Cambridge maths courses. Nothing is banked across series, so a difficult day on one component cannot be compensated for by work done earlier in the year.
programmes.countryNote: The practical Dubai consequence is that the whole qualification rests on one sitting, usually in June of Year 11. That is an argument for treating the November series as a real option in some cases and for front-loading content work into Year 10, because the final term of Year 11 cannot carry teaching as well as revision.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS & A Level Mathematics
programmes.description: Modular in structure, with AS Level available as a qualification in its own right and A Level completed over two years. Pure Mathematics starts immediately in Year 12 and assumes Extended IGCSE content, so the summer between the two courses is the most valuable unsupervised period in a mathematician's school career.
programmes.countryNote: This matters for equivalency as well as for admission. For the British track the Ministry of Education requires one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside the five GCSE or IGCSE subjects. A student taking AS Levels and stopping is in a different position from one taking full A Levels, and the rule is worth reading before Year 12 choices are made.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
programmes.description: Two years, Standard or Higher Level, with an internal exploration written over several months and examinations at the end. The exploration has internal deadlines set by the school rather than by the board, which means the pressure points in a Diploma year are different from those in an IGCSE year and arrive earlier than families expect.
programmes.countryNote: IB session and results dates are not confirmed anywhere in this project, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking, so this page publishes none. If your child is heading for the Diploma, get the session window and the internal deadlines from the school's IB coordinator and from ibo.org directly. Any tutoring page that states IB exam dates without naming its source is guessing.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-international-math.subjectsIntro: A 0607 candidate in Dubai is typically entered for eight to ten subjects in the same series, and the calendar pressure comes from the combination rather than from maths alone. The codes below are ones commonly taken alongside International Mathematics, with a note on where each one eats revision time.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Occasionally entered alongside 0607 by schools hedging a tier decision, which doubles the maths revision load for no clear gain. If both appear on your child's statement of entry, that is worth a conversation with the head of maths before the final entry deadline rather than after it.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Co-ordinated Sciences 0654
subjects.description: Biology, chemistry and physics in one double-award qualification with a practical component. It compresses three subjects into two grades, which saves timetable space and concentrates revision into a narrower window. Students underestimate the volume until the Easter before the papers.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Combined Science 0653
subjects.description: A single-award science covering all three disciplines at lighter depth, common where a student is carrying a heavy language or arts load. The risk is a late discovery that a sixth-form science course expects the double award, which is an entry-deadline problem rather than a revision one.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE English as a Second Language 0510
subjects.levels: Single tier, with a count-in speaking variant
subjects.description: Listening, reading and writing with a speaking component. Marks move on task fulfilment rather than vocabulary range, and the writing paper rewards answering the brief precisely. It is often the subject a 0607 candidate can safely revise least, which makes it useful as a release valve in a crowded April.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Global Perspectives 0457
subjects.description: Assessed through a written exam and team and individual project work, with deadlines set internally by the school. Those deadlines routinely land in the same fortnight as the maths mock, which is a scheduling collision worth mapping in September rather than discovering in January.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Accounting 0452
subjects.description: Two written papers built on formats that must be reproduced accurately. It pairs naturally with mathematics and it rewards drill, so it is one of the few subjects where late revision genuinely works, which makes it a sensible thing to postpone when the calendar gets tight.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Enterprise 0454
subjects.description: Coursework-led alongside a written component, with internal deadlines months before the series. Coursework subjects are where a Year 11 timetable actually breaks, because the deadlines are immovable and sit well before the exam revision period opens.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Design and Technology 0445
subjects.description: A substantial coursework component plus written papers, with the practical work consuming large blocks of the spring term. Families planning maths tutoring for April should check this deadline first, because it will win any conflict and should be planned around rather than through.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Art and Design 0400
subjects.description: Assessed by coursework and a timed practical examination, both of which demand sustained studio time. In a Dubai Year 11 this is often the single largest unscheduled time commitment of the spring, and it is invisible on any revision timetable built from exam dates alone.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physical Education 0413
subjects.description: A written paper plus assessed practical performance, with moderation visits scheduled by the school. The practical assessment windows are fixed externally, so they cannot be moved for a maths mock, and knowing when they fall makes an eight-week plan realistic rather than aspirational.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-international-math.regionsIntro: In exam season the geography that matters is the journey to the hall and the state of the household in the weeks around it. The notes below cover what each community means in practice during mocks and the June series rather than in an ordinary term.

regions.name: Dubai Creek Harbour
regions.note: A newer community with a limited set of access routes and schools mostly a drive away. In exam weeks the morning run is the pressure point, which argues for evening sessions that end early rather than late during the series itself.

schoolClusters.note: Long-established international and British schools serving the older coastal communities. Mock examinations in this group tend to run in January under full exam conditions, which makes a January script a genuinely useful diagnostic rather than a classroom test.

schoolClusters.note: Newer schools with young Year 11 cohorts, where internal assessment calendars are still settling and parents often have no older sibling's experience to draw on. Asking for the published assessment calendar in September is particularly worth doing in this group.

sections.heading: The 0607 year counted backwards from the paper
paragraphs: Planning forwards from September produces a revision timetable that nobody follows. Planning backwards from the paper produces a sequence of decisions with owners and dates, which is a different and more useful document. The table below is that sequence, with the party who actually sets each milestone named, because a parent who knows whether a date belongs to Cambridge, to the school or to the family knows who to ask.

The dates themselves have to be taken from the board and from the school. Cambridge publishes key dates per series, and the March 2027 series is a clean worked example of the shape: final entries due 27 November 2026, an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027, forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results on Direct 13 May and certificates in late June. The same structure applies to June and November series, with different dates, which is why the table below describes milestones rather than restating a timetable that will be revised.

Pearson works similarly for families on Edexcel syllabuses: International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year, the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is precisely why the live official timetable rather than a page like this one is where dates should be read.

sections.heading: Zones, timetables and why two Dubai schools differ
paragraphs: Parents compare notes, and in exam season they discover that a friend's child at another Dubai school is sitting the same paper on a different day. This is not an error. Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a timetable version for each, and it states plainly that it is essential to use the correct version for the centre's zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

The practical rule that follows is simple and worth repeating to a teenager. The only timetable that applies is the one issued by their own school. A date circulated in a parents' group, a date found on a revision website, and a date a cousin in another country is working to are all capable of being wrong for your child. Ask the exams officer for the written timetable, put it on the kitchen wall, and plan the final fortnight from that document alone.

Zones matter for revision planning as well as for turning up. Two components sat four days apart need a different final week from two sat on consecutive mornings, and in 0607 the gap between the non-calculator paper and the investigation paper decides what the last few sessions should be spent on. Once the school's timetable exists, the eight-week plan should be rewritten against it rather than built from a generic template.

The same caution applies to any date printed on a page like this one. Pearson, for families on Edexcel syllabuses, publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and then confirms them, which means a date copied from a third-party site in September can be wrong by November. Reading the board's live timetable, and the school's issued version of it, takes a few minutes once a term and removes an entire category of avoidable panic.

sections.heading: What a January mock script actually tells you
paragraphs: In most Dubai schools the January mock is the only full-length paper a student sits under proper conditions before the real series. It is a genuinely valuable document and it is usually wasted, because it comes back with a grade and a brief comment. The grade is the least informative thing on it. What matters is where in the paper the marks were lost, in what pattern, and whether the loss was understanding, technique, convention or time.

Read properly, a 0607 mock script answers four questions. Did the student run out of time, and if so at which question. Were the accuracy conventions followed after calculator work, or were answers copied from the screen. In the geometry and transformation questions, were reasons given or only answers. And on the investigation component, were cases generated and tested, or was a general rule asserted. Each of those four has a different response, and only one of them involves re-teaching content.

The timing of the mock is also the problem with it. January is after the entry deadline, so a mock cannot inform the tier decision it looks like it should inform. That is the single strongest argument in this page for an autumn diagnostic: it produces the same information while it can still change something. Where the mock arrives as a shock, the debrief block in the modes above is the salvage operation, and it is a better purchase than a general increase in hours.

sections.heading: Resits, the November series, and the options that are not worth taking
paragraphs: A disappointing IGCSE maths result is not the end of a route, and the choices available are more varied than families assume. Cambridge runs a November series as well as a June one, so a resit inside the same calendar year is possible in principle. Whether it is sensible depends on what the grade is needed for, how much time a Year 12 student has, and whether the problem was the mathematics or the day.

The honest framing is a cost in attention rather than in money. A student beginning A Level Mathematics or Diploma maths in September has a demanding new course, and preparing for a November resit at the same time borrows from it. Where the IGCSE grade is a formal requirement that is already met, a resit for improvement is usually a poor trade. Where the grade blocks a sixth-form place or an equivalency requirement, the arithmetic changes completely.

There is also the case of a near miss, where a review of results is worth discussing before anything else. Reviews are requested by the centre, not by a family, and they run to deadlines set by the board, so the conversation to have in the first week after results is with the school's exams officer.

One option that deserves more consideration than it gets is doing nothing. A grade that already satisfies every requirement the next step actually sets does not need improving, and the energy spent improving it is energy taken from a course that will matter more. Families under stress in August routinely book a resit before anyone has read the receiving course's published entry requirements. Reading those requirements, in writing, is the first action rather than the last. The table sets out the realistic options with what each costs a student and the one thing to check before committing.

sections.heading: Where an IGCSE maths grade goes next in the UAE
paragraphs: Families in Dubai are planning for two different systems at once, and the rules are published in different places. For admission to a UAE university or for the attestation of a school certificate, the Ministry of Education's equivalency requirements are the relevant document, and they are specific. For the British track, a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

Two details inside that rule are worth knowing because one ranking competitor in this market publishes them incorrectly. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE or IGCSE count. And the requirement is five subjects, not six. A mathematics IGCSE, whether 0580 or 0607, ordinarily counts as one of the five, which is one reason a pass in maths matters beyond the subject itself.

For the American track the same source sets out English proficiency through a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. No IB points threshold appears in that source, so none is published here: an IB figure needs to be read on moe.gov.ae or the emirate's attestation authority. IB Gram does not perform equivalency, does not act in the process, and does not guarantee any outcome in it. The table summarises what each track must show and where to verify it.
