sections.heading: Running a graphics calculator lesson over video
paragraphs: This is the part of 0607 teaching that is genuinely easier remotely, and it is worth explaining because it sounds as though it should be the opposite. In a room, a tutor watching a student use a calculator sees a hand and a small screen at an angle. Over video, the student can hold the device to the camera or mirror its display, and the tutor sees the actual screen, the actual menu and the actual keystroke sequence. Diagnosing a calculator problem is a matter of seeing what the student sees.

The skills that earn marks are a short, finite list: setting a viewing window deliberately, graphing a function and reading intercepts and turning points, finding an intersection, building a table of values, solving numerically, and producing one and two-variable statistics. Each is a keystroke sequence that should be written down rather than demonstrated and forgotten, and the written list becomes a one-page reference the student keeps beside them for a year.

Alongside the sequences sits the habit that protects the marks: keep full precision through intermediate steps and round only at the end, to the accuracy the question asks for. Students lose a steady trickle of marks across both calculator-permitted components by copying a long decimal verbatim or rounding too early in a multi-step calculation. Seeing that loss on a marked script, with the mark scheme beside it, is what breaks the habit; being told about it does not.

sections.heading: The last eight weeks, week by week
paragraphs: The final block has a shape that is well understood and widely ignored. New content stops early, because a topic met for the first time in May will not be reliable in June and the hours are better spent making secure material fast and accurate. Timed work rises steadily. Session length comes down rather than up in the last fortnight, because a tired student practising badly is reinforcing the errors the plan exists to remove.

A workable pattern looks like this. Weeks one and two close the last genuine content gaps and sit a full timed paper to establish a pacing baseline. Weeks three to five run one timed paper a week, each marked and worked through, with sessions spent only on the recurring causes in the error log. Weeks six and seven narrow to the two or three causes that are still costing marks, plus the calculator conventions. The final week is question reading, the written timetable, and sleep.

Two Dubai-specific adjustments belong in that plan. Coursework and practical deadlines in other subjects frequently land in the same weeks, so the plan should be built around the school's published assessment calendar rather than around maths alone. And where the exam period overlaps Ramadan, sessions can move to after Iftar and should be shorter, with the content weighted towards recall and notation rather than towards new technique.

A third adjustment is about the student rather than the schedule. Eight weeks is long enough for a Year 11 to exhaust themselves if every evening is booked, and an exhausted candidate makes exactly the careless errors this block exists to remove. The plan should therefore contain scheduled nothing: one evening a week with no revision in it, protected as deliberately as the timed paper. Parents find this the hardest instruction on the page and it is one of the few that reliably shows up in the final scripts.

Weeks 3-5: a timed paper a week, sessions on recurring causes only
Weeks 6-7: two or three causes plus accuracy conventions

Built around the school's other deadlines, not around maths alone

sections.heading: What this page will not claim about dates, grades or approvals
paragraphs: Every date on this page is attributed and provisional. Cambridge and Pearson publish and revise their timetables, Pearson explicitly issues provisional timetables ahead of each series, and Cambridge allocates centres to zones with different timetable versions. That means a tutoring page is the wrong place to rely on for a date. Confirm each one with your child's exams officer and against the board's own published timetable, and treat anything quoted here as the shape of the year rather than as the year itself.

IB session and results dates are a specific gap and it is worth being explicit about why. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no IB date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and none is published here. Secondary sources circulate windows that look authoritative and may be wrong. If you need an IB date, get it from the school's IB coordinator or from ibo.org, and be suspicious of any site that states one without naming its source.

The rest of our limits are short. IB Gram is a tutor-matching platform with no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or IB endorsement, no licence as a school or training institute in the UAE, and no premises in the country. Private tutors here require a MoHRE private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. We publish no ratings, no student counts and no statistics without a method, and we promise no grade. Lessons are one-to-one over live video; IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai, because in-home tuition is a service we run only in India.

process.title: Map the school's other deadlines first
process.description: Ask the school for its published assessment calendar, including coursework and practical deadlines in every subject. Those dates win any conflict with a maths plan, and building around them in September is the difference between a plan that holds and one that collapses in March.

process.description: A 45-minute session at no charge, no card required, which produces a strand map, an error log sorted by cause and a recommendation keyed to how many weeks remain. If there are eight weeks left, the recommendation will not be a content course, because that would be the wrong purchase.

process.title: Weekly sessions, then a block structure for the run-in
process.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Autumn is weekly and content-led; January is a mock debrief; the last eight weeks switch to timed papers with no new content after the first fortnight and shorter sessions in the final week.

process.description: Once the school issues the zone-specific timetable, the final weeks are replanned against it, because the gap between components changes what the last sessions should cover. That document, not a generic revision template, is what the run-in should be built from.

whyPoints.description: Thirty weeks and eight weeks are different products, and selling the same course for both is the most common waste in private tutoring. A late start gets technique, pacing and accuracy work rather than a content syllabus, and we will say so at the diagnostic rather than after a month.

whyPoints.description: A January script read question by question against the published scheme yields a pacing profile and an error log, which is a plan. The same script read as a grade yields a mood. The debrief block exists because most schools return the paper with the latter.

faqs.question: When are Cambridge IGCSE maths papers actually sat in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs International GCSE examinations in a June series and a November series, and UAE centres sit those, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests available in March, May and October. The precise dates for your child depend on the centre's administrative zone, because Cambridge publishes a timetable version for each of six zones. That is why two Dubai schools can sit the same paper on different days. Get the written timetable from your school's exams officer and treat it as the only one that applies, rather than any date circulated between parents.

faqs.question: How far before the exams does the entry deadline fall?
faqs.answer: Months, which is the fact that surprises families most. The published key dates for the Cambridge March 2027 series show final entries due on 27 November 2026 against an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027, with forecast grades due 27 February 2027 and results on Direct on 13 May. June and November series follow the same shape with different dates. The practical consequence is that subject and tier decisions are settled by an administrator long before the January mock, so a family wanting a say has to be looking at marked work in the autumn.

faqs.question: Why is my child's timetable different from a friend's at another school?
faqs.answer: Because Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and issues a different timetable version for each. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for the centre's zone and warns that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. The rule that follows is worth repeating to a teenager: the only timetable that applies is the one their own school has issued. Put that document on the wall and plan the final fortnight from it alone.

faqs.question: Can a 0607 candidate resit in the November series?
faqs.answer: In principle yes, since Cambridge runs a November series as well as a June one, and the entry would be made through a centre. Whether it is sensible is a separate question. A student starting A Level Mathematics or Diploma maths in September is carrying a demanding new course, and preparing for a November resit borrows attention from it. Where the grade already meets every requirement that matters, that is usually a poor trade. Where it blocks a place or an equivalency requirement, the arithmetic changes. Check what the receiving course actually requires, in writing, first.

faqs.question: When do Cambridge and Pearson results reach students here?
faqs.answer: Results go to centres before candidates, and the gap is a few days. For Pearson, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. For Cambridge, the March 2027 series shows results on Direct on 13 May with certificates in late June. Those are the published figures for those series and later series will differ, so the school's exams officer is the person to ask for your child's series.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start tutoring in March for a June series?
faqs.answer: No, but it changes what you should buy. With roughly eight weeks left the useful work is technique, pacing, accuracy conventions and the recurring causes in an error log, not a content course. New topics introduced in May are rarely reliable in June. The honest version of a late start is a diagnostic in week one, timed papers weekly, no new content after the second week, and shorter sessions in the final fortnight. If a provider offers to cover the whole syllabus in eight weeks, that is a sales answer rather than a plan.

faqs.question: How many subjects does UAE equivalency need, and does maths count?
faqs.answer: For the British track the Ministry of Education requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. A mathematics IGCSE, 0580 or 0607, ordinarily counts as one of them. One ranking competitor page states six subjects, which does not match the published rule. Verify your own case on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority.

faqs.question: Does an IGCSE certificate need attestation in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Certificate attestation and equivalency are processes run by the Ministry of Education and the emirate's own authority, with requirements that depend on where the certificate was issued and what it is being used for. They are not something a tutoring company performs, arranges or guarantees, and we do not present them as such. The practical advice is to start early, because the paperwork takes longer than families expect, and to take the requirements from the official channel rather than from any third-party summary, including this one.

faqs.question: What should a Year 10 be doing in the autumn term for 0607?
faqs.answer: Three things, none of them dramatic. Install the graphics calculator properly, so that windows, intersections, tables and statistics are habits by Christmas rather than discoveries in April. Start investigation tasks early, roughly one every three weeks, because the component rewards a habit of reasoning that takes months to build. And keep the non-calculator skills alive, since internationally educated students lose fluency by hand over time. Autumn is the cheapest and least popular time to buy support, and it is when the same hours buy the most.

faqs.question: Does the January mock predict the real result?
faqs.answer: Not reliably, and that is not its value. Its value is that it is usually the only full-length paper sat under proper conditions before the series, which makes it the best available diagnostic. Read question by question it answers four things: where the time ran out, whether accuracy conventions survived the calculator work, whether reasons were given in geometry and transformation questions, and whether the investigation was built from tested cases or an asserted rule. Those four have different responses, and only one of them is about re-teaching content.

faqs.question: Can my daughter sit 0607 as a private candidate in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Some centres in the emirate accept private candidates and some do not, and acceptance varies by syllabus and by series, so the route is to identify a centre that will take the entry for that specific syllabus. Cambridge publishes guidance on finding a centre and the centre itself sets its own arrangements, fees and deadlines. This matters most for a student who has left the school where they studied, or who needs a resit after moving. Start the search early, because entry deadlines fall months before the papers.

faqs.question: How do we plan revision around Ramadan and the exam window?
faqs.answer: By shortening sessions and changing what they contain rather than by trying to keep the usual timetable. School days are shorter during Ramadan and household routine shifts substantially, so sessions moved to after Iftar and cut to forty or fifty minutes tend to survive when a 6.30pm hour does not. The content should lean towards recall, notation and calculator conventions rather than new technique. Because lessons run over live video, the change costs nothing to make and does not depend on anyone's travel plans.

faqs.question: What can be done if a mark looks wrong after results?
faqs.answer: A review of results is requested by the examination centre rather than by a family, and it runs to deadlines set by the board, so the conversation to have in the first week after results is with the school's exams officer. They can advise whether the mark sits close enough to a boundary for a review to be worth requesting and what the process and timing are. No tutoring company can initiate or influence that, and any claim to be able to should be treated as a reason to look elsewhere.

faqs.question: Does an IGCSE maths grade matter for a UAE university application?
faqs.answer: It matters in two separate ways and they are easy to confuse. As part of the Ministry of Education's equivalency requirements for the British track, a mathematics IGCSE ordinarily counts as one of the five accredited subjects needed at grade E or 3 or better. Separately, individual universities set their own admission requirements, which may ask for specific subjects or levels, and those are published by the institution. Read both, from their own sources, and do not treat a tutoring page as the authority on either. Tutoring is not required for any part of that process.

faqs.question: How far ahead should we book an online 0607 tutor for the exam run?
faqs.answer: Earlier than feels necessary. Demand for this syllabus concentrates sharply from January as mock results arrive, and the specialist pool for International Mathematics is smaller than for mainstream IGCSE maths, so the eight weeks before the June series are the hardest to staff. Booking a slot in the autumn costs less and secures the time; asking in April means taking what is free. If nothing is available at your preferred hour we will say so and set out the alternatives rather than matching a general maths tutor to a 0607 request.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-international-math.closingHeading: Get the timetable, then build the plan
dubai/cambridge-igcse-international-math.closingBody: Two documents decide almost everything on this page, and neither of them comes from us. The first is the statement of entry, which tells you the syllabus code, the tier and the series. The second is the school's own zone-specific examination timetable, which tells you when the components fall and therefore what the last fortnight should contain. Ask the exams officer for both, map the coursework deadlines in your child's other subjects alongside them, and then book the free 45-minute diagnostic so the plan is keyed to the weeks that actually remain. You keep the strand map and error log either way, and if the right advice is to buy less than you expected, that is what we will give you.

intro.heading: Why 0607 behaves differently from every other IGCSE maths course
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics 0607 was written for international schools, and the design intention shows in three places. It assumes a graphics display calculator as standard equipment rather than as an aid. It includes an investigation component in which the student is given an unfamiliar situation and asked to explore it. And its content and vocabulary line up deliberately with what the IB Diploma maths courses expect, which is why Dubai schools running an IB continuum so often enter it instead of Mathematics 0580.

For a parent this matters most at the point of hiring help. A tutor who teaches 0580 well is teaching a syllabus where the calculator is a convenience and every question has a known method. In 0607 the calculator is part of the mathematics: a student is expected to sketch a function on it, find an intersection, read a numerical solution, and then write the answer with appropriate accuracy. A tutor unfamiliar with that workflow will teach around it, and the marks for it will still be on the paper.

Candidates sit three components in whichever tier they are entered for, and the tiers are not interchangeable. Core candidates work through a reduced content list and are reported on a narrower grade scale; Extended candidates cover the full syllabus, including functions, and can reach the top grades. Both tiers sit a non-calculator paper, a calculator paper and an investigation-based paper, so the structure is consistent while the demand is not.

The investigation paper is where Dubai students are most exposed, because it is the hardest thing to teach from a textbook. It rewards a student who notices a pattern, states it generally, tests it and explains why it holds. Those are habits rather than facts, and they are built by doing a dozen investigations with feedback, which is almost never what a crowded Year 11 scheme of work has room for. It is the most useful thing a 0607 tutor can spend time on.

One more thing is worth knowing before any of that: 0607 is not a harder 0580 and it is not an easier one. It is a different qualification with a different purpose, sat by a smaller international cohort, and a sixth form reading the grade knows that. Families who arrive assuming a straight ranking between the two syllabuses tend to make the tier decision on the wrong grounds, and the tier decision is the one with consequences that last into Year 13.

Everything here is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; in-home tuition is a service we run only in India. For this particular syllabus the online format has a specific advantage, since a graphics calculator screen can be shared directly or mirrored, and the tutor can watch the keystrokes rather than the student's hand. Working through a calculator procedure is one of the few teaching tasks that is genuinely easier remotely than across a kitchen table.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-international-math.programmesIntro: 0607 sits in the middle of a route that usually begins in the Middle Years Programme and ends in one of the two IB Diploma maths courses. Understanding that route is what makes the Core and Extended decision answerable, because the right tier depends on where the student is going rather than on how Year 10 felt.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme Mathematics
programmes.description: Criterion-assessed rather than examined, with four criteria covering knowledge, pattern investigation, communication and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Students are graded 1 to 8 against descriptors, and investigation tasks are a standing part of the course. The pattern-investigating criterion is close relative of the 0607 investigation paper, which is not a coincidence.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools run MYP to Year 11 and then enter IGCSE alongside it, or run MYP mathematics with a 0607 entry bolted on. Students arriving from a pure MYP background are usually comfortable with investigation and uncomfortable with timed written papers, which is the exact inverse of a student arriving from a British-curriculum school. The tutoring plan follows from which of those two your child is.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics, Core tier
programmes.description: A reduced content list, three components, and a grade ceiling below the top of the scale. It suits a student who needs a secure pass and a solid grounding rather than a route into higher-level mathematics. The graphics calculator requirement still applies, and so does the investigation component, so neither can be skipped on the grounds of tier.
programmes.countryNote: Core entries in Dubai are commonest where a student joined an international school late and is covering two years of content in one, or where mathematics is not part of the intended sixth-form plan. The decision is reversible for longer than families assume, and the time to review it is after the autumn assessment rather than after the January mock.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics, Extended tier
programmes.description: The full content list, including functions and their transformations, with access to the top grades. The calculator paper is substantially more demanding than its Core counterpart, and the investigation component becomes investigation and modelling, adding the task of building a model for a situation and commenting on its limitations.
programmes.countryNote: This is the default in Dubai's IB-continuum schools for anyone intending to take either Diploma maths course. A student entered for Core and then aiming at Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level will have a gap to close in Year 12, which is why the tier decision is worth taking seriously in Year 10 rather than treating it as an administrative detail.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
programmes.description: The modelling-and-technology route through Diploma maths, available at Standard and Higher Level, with heavy and explicit use of a graphics display calculator and an internal exploration written by the student. Statistics, modelling and interpretation carry more weight here than algebraic proof, and the calculator is expected to be used fluently in the examinations themselves.
programmes.countryNote: The overlap with 0607 Extended is the closest of any pair on this page. A Dubai student who has sat 0607 Extended arrives in Applications and Interpretation already able to use the calculator as a mathematical instrument and already used to being asked to model something and comment on it. That is a real advantage in the first term, and it is the clearest practical argument for the Extended tier.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-international-math.subjectsIntro: The grid below is the 0607 content list rather than a subject menu, since this page covers one syllabus. Each entry names what the strand assesses and where Dubai candidates reliably lose marks on it, so a first session can start somewhere useful instead of at page one of the textbook.

subjects.name: Number
subjects.description: Standard form, upper and lower bounds, ratio and proportion, percentage change and compound growth, and accuracy. The accuracy requirement is the quiet killer: answers given to the wrong degree of precision lose marks on questions that were solved correctly, and the convention has to be learned rather than guessed.

subjects.name: Algebra and graphs
subjects.description: Manipulation, equations, inequalities, sequences, and the graphs of linear, quadratic, exponential and reciprocal functions. In 0607 the graph work is done on the calculator as well as on paper, and marks are lost by sketching from the screen without labelling intercepts, asymptotes or turning points.

subjects.name: Functions
subjects.description: Function notation, domain and range, composite and inverse functions, and transformations of a given graph. This strand is the clearest single difference between the tiers and the one that most prepares a student for Diploma maths. Transformations are examined by asking for the effect of a change rather than for a memorised rule.

subjects.name: Coordinate geometry
subjects.description: Gradients, midpoints, lengths, parallel and perpendicular lines and the equation of a straight line in several forms. Students lose marks by giving a gradient as a decimal when an exact fraction is wanted, and by answering with a value where the question asked for the equation of the line.

subjects.name: Geometry
subjects.description: Angle properties, polygons, circle theorems, congruence and similarity, and constructions. The reliable loss here is reasoning: Cambridge awards marks for naming the property used, and an answer with the correct angle and no stated reason leaves marks on the paper in nearly every circle-theorem question.

subjects.name: Mensuration
subjects.description: Perimeter, area, surface area and volume of standard and compound solids, arcs and sectors. Marks are lost on units more than on method, especially where a volume is asked for in litres or a surface area in square metres after the working has been done in centimetres.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.description: Right-angled trigonometry, the sine and cosine rules, area of a triangle, bearings and three-dimensional problems. The non-calculator paper means exact values for the standard angles have to be known, and the calculator paper means a student must notice when the required angle is obtuse rather than accepting the first value the device returns.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vectors, magnitude, addition and scalar multiples, and the four transformations with their full descriptions. Describing a transformation is where marks go: a rotation needs the angle, direction and centre, and giving two of the three scores partially at best.

subjects.name: Probability
subjects.description: Single and combined events, tree and Venn diagrams, relative frequency and conditional situations. The commonest error is treating events as independent when the question describes selection without replacement, which changes every subsequent denominator and loses the whole chain of marks.

subjects.name: Statistics
subjects.description: Data display, averages from grouped data, cumulative frequency, box plots, scatter diagrams and lines of best fit. This strand is where the graphics calculator earns its place: statistical summaries and regression can be produced from the device, and the marks then depend on interpreting the output rather than computing it.

subjects.name: Sets
subjects.description: Set notation, Venn diagrams with two and three sets, unions, intersections and complements. Notation is the whole of the difficulty, and it is a half-hour fix: students who can shade a diagram correctly often cannot write the same region in symbols, which is what the question asks for.

sections.heading: What the three components ask for, tier by tier
paragraphs: A 0607 candidate sits three components, and the set depends on the tier. Core candidates take a non-calculator paper, a calculator paper and an investigation paper. Extended candidates take the harder versions of all three, with the final component becoming investigation and modelling. The practical point is that there is no component in which the calculator is irrelevant and no component in which it is sufficient, so a student needs both the arithmetic and the device.

The non-calculator component is short and catches out students who have never been made to work without one. Exact values, fraction arithmetic, standard-form manipulation and mental estimation are all assessed there, and Dubai students coming from an international background are frequently fluent on the device and rusty by hand. Fixing that is drill rather than teaching, and it is best started a year out rather than in the final term.

The investigation component is different in kind. The student is handed an unfamiliar situation, asked to generate cases, look for a pattern, state it in general terms and test it, and in the Extended version to build a model and comment on its limitations. It rewards method and communication rather than recall.

Because all three components are sat in the same series, there is no banked element and no coursework to soften a difficult paper, and a weak component cannot be avoided by preparation elsewhere. That changes how a year should be planned: the sensible pattern is to keep all three in view from the start rather than teaching content for two terms and discovering the investigation paper in April. sections.heading: The graphics display calculator is part of the mathematics
paragraphs: In most IGCSE maths syllabuses the calculator removes arithmetic. In 0607 it does something else: it is a mathematical instrument the candidate is expected to reason with. A question may give an equation with no algebraic route to a solution and expect the student to graph both sides, find the intersection and write the root to three significant figures. Another may hand over a data set and expect a regression line from the device, with the marks sitting in the interpretation.

Most Dubai students own the right device and use perhaps a fifth of it. The skills that matter are a short list: setting a sensible viewing window, graphing a function and reading intercepts and turning points, finding intersections, building a table of values, solving numerically, and producing one-variable and two-variable statistics. Each is a keystroke sequence. Written down and practised for twenty minutes, each becomes permanent, which is why a two-session calculator sprint is such an efficient purchase.

There is one habit worth drilling above all others. The device gives a long decimal and the paper wants a stated accuracy, and the mark for the question depends on the second. Students lose a steady trickle of marks across both calculator components by copying the screen verbatim or rounding too early in a multi-step calculation. Working to full precision and rounding only at the end is the rule, and the only way it sticks is by losing the mark on a marked script and seeing why.

sections.heading: How to practise an investigation when there is no formula to learn
paragraphs: Parents often ask how a student revises for the investigation paper, and the honest answer is that revision is the wrong word. The component tests a process, so it is practised the way a sport is practised: repeatedly, with feedback, on different situations. A student who has worked through ten investigation tasks with someone pointing out where the reasoning jumped is in a completely different position from one who has read about the paper.

The process itself is teachable and has a reliable shape. Generate small cases systematically rather than randomly. Record them in a table. Look for a relationship and state it in words before stating it in symbols. Test the statement on a case not yet used. Then, for the Extended version, build the model, use it to answer the question asked, and say where it would stop being reasonable. Students who write the general statement first and the cases afterwards lose marks even when the statement is right.

What a tutor adds here is the thing a textbook cannot: a reader. The component assesses communication as well as mathematics, and a student cannot tell whether their own explanation is clear. Having an unfamiliar question attempted cold, then read back line by line with the gaps named, is the single most useful session type on this syllabus, and it is the one that most Dubai Year 11 schemes of work have no room for.

There is a secondary benefit that matters for anyone heading into the Diploma. The internal exploration in both IB maths courses asks for the same habits at greater length: choose something, investigate it properly, write it so a reader can follow, and be honest about the limits. A student who has spent a year being made to explain their reasoning on 0607 investigations starts that piece of work from a much better place than one who has only ever answered structured questions.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the decision and its consequences
paragraphs: The tier decision is made by the school, usually in Year 10 or early Year 11, and it is usually presented to families as a judgement about current attainment. It is also a decision about the next two years, because the grade ceiling in Core is below the top of the scale and because Extended carries the functions content that Diploma maths assumes. Those two facts are what a family should be weighing, and neither of them is about how hard the current term feels.

There are good reasons to accept a Core entry. A student who joined an international school recently and is covering content at speed may be better served by securing a solid Core grade than by a thin Extended one. A student with no intention of taking mathematics beyond sixteen loses little. And a Core candidate still sits a calculator paper and an investigation paper, so the transferable skills are not lost, only the depth.

The reasons to resist a Core entry are narrower but sharper. If the intended route is Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, or A Level Mathematics, the functions and algebra in Extended are the foundation, and the gap has to be closed in Year 12 instead, during a course that is already demanding.

One practical note on how to raise it. Schools make tier decisions from their own assessment evidence, and they are generally willing to review one when a parent brings evidence rather than an opinion. A marked paper from outside the school, sorted by cause, is evidence; a conviction that a child is capable of more is not. That is a reason to get a diagnostic done in the autumn term rather than in February, by which point the internal deadline is close and the content gap is real. sections.heading: 0607, 0580 and the IB Diploma routes
paragraphs: A Dubai family with children in two different schools can easily end up with one child on 0580 and the other on 0607, and conclude that the second is simply a harder version of the first. It is not. The content overlaps substantially, but 0607 adds the investigation component and the graphics calculator and arranges the material with the Diploma in mind, while 0580 is a broader general qualification taken by far more candidates worldwide.

The practical consequence shows up in Year 12. A student from 0607 Extended walking into Applications and Interpretation finds the calculator already familiar and the modelling vocabulary already met. A student from 0580 Extended walking into Analysis and Approaches finds the algebra familiar and the technology unfamiliar. Neither is better placed overall; they are differently placed, and knowing which gap exists is worth more than a general sense that the Diploma will be hard.

Dubai's IB sector is large and growing, which is why this matters locally. The emirate's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, three of them International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, and IB programmes accounted for 7% of Dubai's private-school enrolment in 2024-25 against 37% for the UK curriculum. A family choosing between two schools is often also choosing, without being told, between two maths routes.

It also matters when a family moves house or school inside the emirate, which happens here more than in most markets. A student transferring from a British-curriculum school into an IB-continuum one in Year 10 can find their maths entry changed from 0580 to 0607 with a term gone, and the gap they carry is the investigation component and the calculator rather than the content. Identifying that early turns a frightening transfer into a short piece of work. The table maps the common transitions and what each one leaves to close.

sections.heading: What 0607 support costs in Dubai, and what to compare
paragraphs: Published rates in this market fall into bands rather than onto a single figure, and most providers publish nothing at all. Budget online tutors advertise from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour. Qualified online subject tutors sit around AED 150 to 300. In-home visits run about AED 180 to 500 once travel is priced in, specialists AED 200 to 450, and premium named tutors have been quoted as high as AED 650. Those come from providers' own pages and from Bestimate's 2026 Dubai cost survey; they are the market and not an IB Gram price list.

For 0607 specifically there is a scarcity effect worth naming. Fewer tutors teach this syllabus than teach 0580, and fewer again are fluent with the graphics calculator and the investigation component, so a parent filtering by both syllabus and location in Dubai is working from a very short list. That is the mechanism behind a quote that looks high: it is scarcity rather than quality, and it is reduced by removing the location filter rather than by negotiating.

The more useful comparison is not rate against rate but what each hour includes. An hour of teaching with nothing marked between sessions is a different product from an hour that follows marked homework and precedes a written note. For this syllabus add a third question: does the tutor set and read investigation tasks? A 0607 arrangement that never touches the investigation paper is leaving a whole component untouched, whatever it costs.

sections.heading: Where 0607 candidates in Dubai actually lose marks
paragraphs: Marked 0607 scripts cluster in a few places, and they are not the places families expect. Accuracy is first. The syllabus has conventions about how answers should be given, the calculator produces long decimals, and a steady stream of marks disappears into answers rounded too early or stated to the wrong precision. This is not a mathematics problem and it is fixed by habit, which makes it the cheapest available improvement.

Reasoning marks are second. Geometry and circle-theorem questions award marks for naming the property used, and transformation questions award them for a complete description. Students who produce the right number and no justification lose a third of the available marks across those strands without ever getting an answer wrong. A marked script makes this visible in a way no amount of explanation does.

Third is the investigation paper, where the loss is structural rather than careless: a general rule stated without the supporting cases, or a model produced with no comment on where it breaks. Fourth is the non-calculator paper, where students raised on the device are simply out of practice by hand. All four are diagnosable from one marked paper, and all four respond to different work, which is why the first session should be a diagnostic rather than a lesson.

What is usually not the cause, despite being the thing families worry about, is the mathematics itself. A student sitting in a 0607 Extended class has generally been judged capable of the content by people who see their work every week. Treating the problem as a lack of ability leads to more hours of re-teaching material that was understood the first time, which is both expensive and demoralising. Sorting the errors by cause first is what prevents that, and it takes one paper and about twenty minutes.

sections.heading: Regulators, equivalency and the limits of what we claim
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall to ADEK, Sharjah to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah to its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah to the federal Ministry of Education. Those five bodies are the whole regulator map, and a school's inspection report is published by its own regulator rather than by a tutoring company.

Equivalency is a separate process and a common source of confusion. For the British track, the Ministry of Education requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among the five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. A 0607 grade is one of the subjects that can count. No IB points threshold is published in that source, so we publish none, and families should verify their own case on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority. IB Gram does not perform equivalency and does not act in the process.

Our own position, stated plainly: IB Gram is a tutor-matching platform. We hold no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or IB endorsement of any kind, we are not a licensed school or training institute in the UAE, and we have no premises in the country. Private tutors here need a MoHRE private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, and you are entitled to ask any tutor to show theirs. Lessons are one-to-one over live video; IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai, because in-home tuition is a service we run only in India.

faqs.question: Does my child need a graphics display calculator for 0607?
faqs.answer: Yes. The syllabus is written on the assumption that a graphics display calculator is available, and questions on the calculator-permitted components can require graphing a function, finding an intersection, solving numerically or producing a statistical summary from the device. This is the main structural difference between 0607 and most other IGCSE maths syllabuses, where a scientific calculator is sufficient. The model should be one your child's school confirms is permitted, and it should be the same device used in every lesson and every piece of homework for a year.

faqs.question: Which graphics calculator models are allowed in a Cambridge exam?
faqs.answer: Cambridge publishes the rules on permitted calculators and the school's exams officer applies them, so those two sources are the ones to use rather than a recommendation from a tutoring site. In practice Dubai schools tend to standardise on one or two models from the common families and tell parents which to buy, partly so that classroom teaching matches the device in the student's hand. Devices with symbolic algebra capability are treated differently from ordinary graphing models, which is exactly why the school's own guidance is the answer here.

faqs.question: What is the 0607 investigation paper actually asking for?
faqs.answer: It hands the student an unfamiliar situation and asks them to explore it: generate small cases systematically, record them, notice a relationship, state it in general terms, and test it on a case not already used. The Extended version adds building a model, using it to answer the question posed, and commenting on where it would stop being reasonable. Marks sit in the process and the communication as much as in the final result, which is why a general rule stated with no supporting cases scores poorly even when it is correct.

faqs.question: Should my child take 0607 Core or Extended?
faqs.answer: Decide it from where they are going rather than from how this term feels. Core caps the available grades and omits the functions content; Extended covers the full list and is what both IB Diploma maths courses assume, particularly Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. A recently arrived student covering two years in one may be better served by a secure Core grade. A student intending to take mathematics past sixteen will otherwise be closing the functions gap during Year 12. The school decides, and the time to raise it is after the autumn assessment.

faqs.question: Does 0607 prepare a student better for IB maths than 0580?
faqs.answer: For Applications and Interpretation, clearly yes: the calculator fluency and the modelling vocabulary transfer directly. For Analysis and Approaches the picture is mixed, because 0607 Extended brings functions, transformations and graph reasoning while 0580 Extended brings slightly heavier routine algebra. Neither student is better placed overall and both have a gap. The useful thing is knowing which gap you have, because a 0607 student usually needs algebraic drill and a 0580 student usually needs technology and investigation practice.

faqs.question: Does a 0607 grade count towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: For the British track the Ministry requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. A mathematics IGCSE, whether 0580 or 0607, is ordinarily one of the five. One competitor page in this market publishes a six-subject requirement, which does not match the published rule. Verify your own case on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority rather than relying on any tutoring page.

faqs.question: Why does 0607 have a paper where calculators are not allowed?
faqs.answer: Because fluency by hand is part of being numerate, and a student who can only operate through a device cannot estimate, cannot check a result for plausibility and cannot work with exact values. The non-calculator component assesses fraction and surd arithmetic, standard form, exact trigonometric values and mental estimation. It is short, and it is where internationally educated students most often underperform, because they have been using a calculator since Year 7. It responds to drill rather than teaching, and the drill should start a year out.

faqs.question: Can a tutor who teaches 0580 handle 0607 as well?
faqs.answer: For the overlapping content, usually yes, and that is most of the syllabus. The risk is the rest. A tutor unfamiliar with the graphics calculator workflow will teach around it rather than through it, and a tutor who has never read an investigation script will set content practice instead. Both gaps are invisible to a parent until the results arrive, because the lessons themselves will look perfectly competent. Ask directly whether they have taught the investigation component and which calculator model they use.

faqs.question: How long does it take to get fluent on the graphics calculator?
faqs.answer: Less time than families expect. The skills that earn marks are a short list: setting a viewing window, graphing and reading intercepts and turning points, finding intersections, building tables, solving numerically, and one and two-variable statistics. Each is a keystroke sequence that can be written down and practised in twenty minutes. Two or three focused sessions, followed by using the device for all homework, generally installs the lot. The habit that takes longer is keeping full precision in intermediate steps and rounding only at the end.

faqs.question: How do we practise investigations without access to the mark scheme?
faqs.answer: By using the published assessment emphases and an experienced reader rather than by hunting for answers. Cambridge's own syllabus and specimen material set out what the component rewards, and past material is available through the school. The part that cannot be substituted is someone reading the student's written explanation and saying where the reasoning jumped, because a student cannot judge the clarity of their own argument. Published papers and mark schemes belong to Cambridge, so the right practice is to work from the official source and link to it rather than circulate copies.

faqs.question: My daughter is strong at maths but keeps losing accuracy marks. What now?
faqs.answer: That is the most common 0607 profile and it is a conventions problem rather than a mathematics problem. The calculator produces long decimals, the syllabus expects answers stated to a particular precision, and rounding part-way through a multi-step calculation shifts the final figure out of tolerance. The fix is mechanical: keep full precision in every intermediate step, round only at the end, and check what accuracy the question asks for before writing anything. It takes one marked paper to see the pattern and about three weeks of corrected homework to break the habit.

faqs.question: What does a 0607 tutor send us after each fortnight?
faqs.answer: Marked homework with the scheme reference alongside it, an error log grouped by cause rather than by topic, and a short written note naming what moved and what did not. Where an investigation task was set, the feedback on it goes in the same place, since the reasoning is the point and the score is not. None of this includes a predicted grade, which is the school's job and depends on assessments across the whole syllabus that a tutor does not set.

faqs.question: We are moving to Dubai mid-year into a 0607 class. Where do we start?
faqs.answer: With a diagnostic that covers both content and one investigation task, because the content gap after a move is usually smaller than the gap in calculator fluency, investigation technique and Cambridge command vocabulary. A four to six week transition block is the normal shape: calculator workflow in the first two sessions, a command-term glossary built from the student's own marked work, and a written list of strands the new school has already covered that your child has not. That list is also what you take to the new head of maths.

faqs.question: Is a group class a sensible way to cover 0607 in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It can work for content and it works poorly for the investigation component, which needs one reader for one student's written reasoning. The practical obstacle in Dubai is also the cohort: 0607 candidates in any one community are fewer than 0580 candidates and are spread across schools at different points in the syllabus, so a group of four at the same stage is hard to assemble. Where a group does exist, the per-student cost is genuinely lower, so the trade is real rather than imaginary.

faqs.question: How quickly can 0607 lessons start, and what if nobody is free?
faqs.answer: Usually within a week for evening slots on Gulf Standard Time, with the free trial often available sooner. The constraint is the size of the specialist pool for this syllabus, which tightens between January and May as mock results land. If no 0607 specialist is free at your preferred time we will say so and set out the options, which may be a different evening, a short wait, or starting with a strong general maths tutor on the overlapping content while being clear that is what it is.

intro.heading: The price of an hour, and the eight things that decide it
paragraphs: Start with the spread, because it is wider than any other service a Dubai family buys. The published hourly rates for mathematics support in this emirate run from roughly AED 33 at the cheapest online tier to AED 650 for a premium named tutor. That is a factor of twenty for something advertised in almost identical language. Three of the six most visible pages in this market publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote US dollars, which is not the currency any of this is actually paid in. So the first job of this page is to put the dirham figures in one place, each one attributed to whoever published it.

The second job is to explain the spread, because almost all of it is explicable and none of it is random. Eight things move a 0580 quote in Dubai: whether anybody travels, whether the tutor has actually taught the specification rather than mathematics in general, whether written work comes back marked, the tier, how close the exam series is, the session length, the group size, and whether you are paying weekly or in a block. Each of those is something you can ask about before any money moves, and each has an answer that either arrives in a sentence or does not.

The third job is the awkward one. This page is indexed against a phrase that contains the word home, because that is what Dubai parents type. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and that is true on every one of the country pages on this site. What we run for UAE families is one-to-one teaching on live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, with the same tutor each week. Rather than hide that behind a form, this page sets the two models side by side with the costs that do not appear on an invoice, and lets the comparison stand.

The honest summary of that comparison is that the in-home model wins on physical presence and loses on almost everything financial. A tutor who drives to Mudon for a 5pm lesson commits ninety minutes of their working day to deliver sixty minutes of teaching, and that ratio sits inside the AED 180 to AED 500 published band whether or not anybody itemises it. A visiting tutor will also usually insist on a longer minimum session for the same reason, so the real monthly commitment is larger than the hourly figure suggests. Remove travel and the same qualified teacher is available in a band that starts at AED 150.

There is one piece of genuinely good news for Dubai households this year. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under the second of Dubai's economic incentives packages, valued at AED 1.5 billion. For a family that had budgeted for a fee rise, that is unallocated money rather than a reason to spend it, and the section on where the dirhams do the most work is written for exactly that situation.

Everything here is specific to Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 and to Dubai. The permit position under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and what it costs, which is nothing. What a cheap hour contains and what an expensive one contains. Which subjects on a Year 11 timetable carry a premium and why. And what to buy first if the budget is fixed at a thousand dirhams a month.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-maths-0580-home-tu.programmesIntro: Rates in this market are set by level as much as by tutor, and the same person charges differently at each one. These are the levels a Dubai maths enquiry covers and what families typically end up spending at each.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
programmes.description: The level most Dubai maths enquiries concern, and the cheapest of the examined levels to support. Published agency rates for IGCSE online start around AED 150, with specialist bands running to AED 300 and beyond close to the series. Most families buy either a weekly hour across Year 11 or a block of six to ten sessions after a disappointing mock, and the second pattern is the more common one in this emirate.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's Year 11 cohort is large, which works in a family's favour on price: there are more people who can teach this level than any other, so the market is genuinely competitive. It works against you on timing, because every family in the emirate wants the same 5pm weeknight slots in the spring term, and the good tutors fill them by February.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics 0606
programmes.description: A scarcer level and therefore a dearer one. 0606 introduces differentiation, integration, kinematics and binomial series, so the pool of people who can teach it well is much smaller than the pool who can teach 0580, and rates sit nearer the specialist band. Families supporting both subjects usually find that the 0606 hour costs more than the 0580 hour from the same provider, which is scarcity rather than difficulty pricing.
programmes.countryNote: Not every Dubai school offers 0606, and where it is offered it is often restricted to a set within the top group. That scarcity is also why a family who needs it late in the year sometimes cannot find anybody locally at any price, which is worth knowing in September rather than in March.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level Mathematics
programmes.description: Roughly a band above IGCSE in this market. Published specialist and examiner-tier rates of AED 270 to AED 650 are quoted mainly against this level and the Diploma. Hours bought also tend to rise, because the content volume is larger and students are working to university offers, so a family that spent AED 800 a month in Year 11 commonly spends double that in Year 12.
programmes.countryNote: The practical Dubai consideration is that sixth-form maths assumes Extended-level fluency and teaches very little of it. The cheapest intervention available to a Year 11 family planning A Level mathematics is algebra work in the summer before Year 12, at the IGCSE rate, rather than catch-up at the sixth-form rate in October.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Mathematics
programmes.description: The dearest level in the Dubai market, with agency rates for IB starting around AED 200 and specialist bands reaching AED 450 and above. Part of that is content, part is the internally assessed exploration, which needs supervision rather than teaching and takes judgement a cheaper hour does not include. Families moving from 0580 into the Diploma should expect the hourly figure to rise even with the same provider.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, three of them International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. More Diploma places means more Diploma demand for tutors, and in a market where supply at that level is already the tightest, that is a reason to book early rather than a reason to expect prices to fall.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-maths-0580-home-tu.subjectsIntro: Not every hour on a Year 11 timetable costs the same, and the reason is almost always supply rather than difficulty. This is what a Dubai family can expect to pay a premium for and what they cannot.

subjects.name: Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: The most competitively supplied subject at this level in Dubai, which keeps rates near the published agency floor of about AED 150 online. A large pool of capable teachers means you can afford to be selective about whether they have actually taught the specification rather than mathematics generally.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics 0606
subjects.description: Scarce and therefore dearer, typically a band above 0580 from the same provider. Calculus at this level narrows the pool sharply, and in a bad week a family may find nobody available locally at any rate. Book in the autumn rather than the spring if the subject is on the timetable.

subjects.name: Physics 0625
subjects.description: Carries a premium over maths in this market, partly because fewer people teach it and partly because the practical paper and the mathematical content together narrow the field. Families supporting both maths and physics usually pay more per hour for the physics.

subjects.name: Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Similar supply position to physics. The organic chemistry and mole calculations are the two areas families most often buy support for, and a tutor who can teach both the calculation and the mechanism is priced accordingly rather than generously.

subjects.name: Biology 0610
subjects.description: Better supplied than physics or chemistry, so closer to the maths rate. The common enquiry is extended-response writing rather than content, which is cheaper to fix than it looks and often needs fewer sessions than a family has budgeted for.

subjects.name: Coordinated Sciences 0654
subjects.description: One qualification covering all three sciences, which means a tutor has to be competent across all three or a family has to buy three partial hours. Where one person can genuinely cover it, that hour is worth more than a single-science hour and is usually priced as such.

subjects.name: English First Language 0500
subjects.description: Well supplied in Dubai and close to the maths rate. The spend here tends to be short and targeted: a handful of sessions on directed writing and on analysing an unseen passage, rather than a year-long commitment.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language 0510 and 0511
subjects.description: Heavily demanded across the emirate's mixed-language intake, and well supplied, so rates stay moderate. The premium, where it exists, is for a tutor who can run the speaking component properly rather than only the written papers.

subjects.name: Economics 0455 and Business Studies 0450
subjects.description: Moderately supplied, with rates close to maths. These are exam-technique subjects more than content subjects at IGCSE, so the value is concentrated in marked written answers, which is exactly the thing a cheap hour leaves out.

subjects.name: Computer Science 0478
subjects.description: The clearest scarcity premium on a Dubai Year 11 timetable. Few people teach the specification, the pseudocode conventions are specific, and families routinely report paying noticeably more per hour here than for mathematics from the same provider.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First or Foreign Language
subjects.description: A separate market with its own supply constraints. Worth noting that Dubai schools must ensure teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a school requirement rather than a private-tutoring one, and a useful question to ask about anyway.

subjects.name: Examination Technique Across Subjects
subjects.description: The cheapest marks on any timetable and the hardest thing to buy, because it does not look like teaching. Showing method, respecting accuracy conventions, reading the command word and finishing the paper are worth a grade in several subjects at once, and an hour spent on them is not priced differently from an hour spent on content.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-maths-0580-home-tu.regionsTitle: Where in Dubai the travel maths changes the price most
dubai/cambridge-igcse-maths-0580-home-tu.regionsIntro: The further you live from the dense tutoring supply along the Sheikh Zayed Road corridor, the more a visiting tutor costs and the fewer of them will come. These are the communities where that gap bites hardest and what families there usually do about it.

regions.name: Town Square and Dubailand
regions.note: A long drive from almost everywhere, which prices a visiting tutor at the upper end of the in-home band and limits the choice to whoever is willing. Families here usually end up booking either a weekend double session or moving to video, because a weeknight visit rarely survives the term.

regions.name: International City and Warsan
regions.note: A price-sensitive cluster with a long commute into the main supply corridor. Group classes are more common here than elsewhere in the emirate, and the honest trade-off is cheaper hours against far weaker diagnosis for an individual student.

regions.name: Discovery Gardens and The Gardens
regions.note: Mid-rise apartment living with a reasonable run along the main road, so in-home supply exists but at full band. The bigger practical constraint is a quiet room, which is why a headset and a cleared table change the value of a session more than the rate does.

regions.name: Al Qusais, Al Nahda and Al Twar
regions.note: Dense, well connected and close to a large school population, so freelance in-home supply is better here than in the outer communities and rates sit lower in the band. The question worth asking is whether the tutor has taught the specification, because supply at this price point is mixed.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Triangle and Al Furjan
regions.note: Fast-growing, with large Year 11 cohorts nearby and heavy competition for weeknight slots in the spring term. Families who leave booking until February here are frequently choosing from whoever is left rather than from whoever is best.

regions.name: Mudon, Remraam and Serena
regions.note: Outer villa communities where a visiting tutor's travel is the dominant cost and a 5pm slot is barely feasible. These are the households where moving to video produces the largest financial difference, often two extra sessions a month for the same spend.

regions.name: Dubai Sports City and Motor City
regions.note: Well served and centrally placed, with several schools close by, so in-home rates sit mid-band. Sports commitments are the scheduling constraint rather than traffic, which argues for a fixed weekend slot that survives a fixture list.

regions.name: Deira, Bur Dubai and Karama
regions.note: Older, denser districts with the widest range of advertised rates in the emirate, from community-advertised hourly figures well below the agency floor up to full band. The permit question matters most here, because supply is largely informal and nobody is asked.

schoolClusters.city: Jebel Ali, Al Furjan and the Discovery Gardens corridor
schoolClusters.note: A large British-curriculum population spread across a long stretch of road, which makes visiting tutors expensive to schedule and video unusually attractive. Enquiries here cluster in January, straight after the first mock, and the useful first document is the marked script rather than a conversation about confidence.

schoolClusters.city: Mirdif, Al Qusais and Al Warqa
schoolClusters.note: Denser, better supplied with freelance tutors and more price-sensitive than the western communities. The advertised range here is the widest in Dubai, which makes the permit question and the has-this-person-taught-the-specification question more important than the rate itself.

sections.heading: What the search phrase means, and what IB Gram actually sells
paragraphs: A Cambridge IGCSE Maths 0580 home tutor in Dubai, as the phrase is used in this market, means a person who comes to your villa or apartment and teaches your child at the kitchen table. Published rates for that service in Dubai run from AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel inside the figure. It is a real service, plenty of providers in the emirate sell it, and this page is not going to pretend it does not work.

IB Gram does not sell it. We do not send a tutor to a UAE address, and home visits are a service we run only in India. What we run for Dubai families is one-to-one teaching on live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, with the same tutor each week, working from your child's statement of entry and their marked scripts. That is stated here in plain words rather than discovered after a form has been filled in, because the alternative is wasting your time and ours.

The reason this page exists under that phrase is that the money question behind it is the same either way. A parent typing it wants to know what the market charges, what makes one hour worth three times another, and what they should buy with a fixed monthly figure. Those answers do not depend on whether anybody drives anywhere, and nobody else in this market publishes them: three of the six most visible pages in this cluster quote no price at all, and the two that do quote dollars.

So this page is built as a pricing page. The provider models with their published dirham rates and their sources. The true cost of a home visit once the items that never appear on an invoice are counted. The eight things that move a quote, each with the question that tests it. A cost-in-context table anchored on the KHDA fee freeze. The permit position, which costs nothing and which almost nobody asks about. And a straight answer to the question a budget-constrained family is actually asking: with a thousand dirhams a month, what do we buy first?

sections.heading: The Dubai market in dirhams, by provider model
paragraphs: Every rate in the table below was published by the provider named in the last column, read in October 2026. None of them is an IB Gram price. We quote after a free trial lesson, because the honest figure depends on the tier, the number of weeks and how far the exam series is, and inventing a single number would be less useful to you than the attributed range.

The pattern across the table is that the model explains the price far better than the quality does. A budget online platform and a specialist agency can supply tutors with similar paper qualifications at a fourfold difference in rate, because one is selling volume and the other is selling matching and replacement. An in-home service and an online agency can field the same person at different prices, because one of them is paying for a car. An international marketplace prices in sterling or dollars and converts, which adds an exchange spread nobody mentions.

The column that matters most for a UAE parent is the fourth one. Private tutoring here is regulated by permit, and the question of who your tutor is and where they are physically based is one almost no provider volunteers. A UAE-resident individual giving private lessons needs a MoHRE private tuition work permit; a tutor teaching from outside the UAE is in a different position entirely, because that permit is a UAE work permit. Both can be legitimate. What is not legitimate is a provider routing a UAE family to an overseas number while implying a local service, which two of the competitor pages in this market do.

One more honest note about the top of the table. A rate of AED 650 an hour is not a fraud and it is also rarely the right purchase for 0580. At this level the specification is widely taught and the pool of competent teachers is large, so paying examiner-tier rates buys seniority the qualification does not demand. Save the premium band for a scarce level, such as Additional Mathematics 0606 or a Diploma internally assessed exploration, where the pool genuinely is small.

sections.heading: What a home visit costs once you count what is not on the invoice
paragraphs: The published in-home band already contains the travel, but it does not contain everything a household spends. Several real costs sit outside the invoice entirely, and they are the reason families who switch models often report the change felt bigger than the rate difference suggested.

The largest is the minimum session. A tutor driving across Dubai for a single hour has committed around ninety minutes of their day to earn sixty minutes of fee, so most in-home providers set a ninety- or one-hundred-and-twenty-minute minimum. That is sensible for them and expensive for you, and for a fifteen-year-old working on algebra it is also pedagogically worse: two hours of mathematics on a weeknight after a full school day produces diminishing returns somewhere around minute fifty. The monthly commitment is therefore larger than the hourly comparison implies, for teaching that is not better.

The second is the cost of a bad match. Tutoring matches fail for ordinary reasons: personality, pace, the tutor turning out to have taught a different specification. In an in-home arrangement the replacement has to be someone else who will also drive to your community at that hour, which in the outer villa communities may be nobody. On video the replacement can be anywhere, which makes switching cheap and therefore makes it actually happen rather than being endured until June.

The third is the cancellation. A visiting tutor whose session is cancelled at four hours' notice has usually already structured their afternoon around the drive, so in-home terms typically charge for it. A video session cancelled at the same notice is normally rescheduled inside the same week. Over a Dubai school year containing fixtures, assemblies, travel and the occasional sandstorm day, that difference is several sessions, which is real money rather than a convenience.

sections.heading: Eight things that move a 0580 quote in Dubai, and the question that tests each
paragraphs: Each row below is something you can ask about on a ten-minute call before any money moves, and each has an answer that either lands immediately or does not. A provider who cannot say whether written work comes back marked, or whether their tutor has taught the specification as opposed to mathematics generally, has not priced the work they are quoting for.

The item families most often fail to ask about is marking. There is a genuine difference between an hour of conversation about mathematics and an hour that produces annotated written work in the student's own hand showing where a method mark was available and where an accuracy mark went. The second takes the tutor unpaid time outside the session, so it is either inside the rate or it is not happening. Ask directly, and ask to see an example of what comes back.

The item families most often overestimate is the exam-proximity premium. Rates do firm up in the spring term, because demand for the 5pm weeknight slots across the emirate peaks at once and the better tutors are full. But the premium is modest compared with the cost of what late booking does to the work itself: six weeks out, nothing new can be taught and the plan narrows to converting partial knowledge into whole marks. Booking in October costs less and buys a different, better service, which is the clearest piece of financial advice on this page.

One row deserves particular attention in this emirate. Group size is the only lever that genuinely halves a price, and it is also the one that most changes what you receive. Four students working through timed questions with a competent teacher is good value in the final term. The same four students in November, one of whom cannot rearrange a formula, produces one child being taught and three being supervised. If the honest diagnosis is a specific gap, the group is not a cheaper version of the right thing; it is a cheaper version of a different thing.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context: fees, entries and a realistic monthly figure
paragraphs: Tutoring is bought out of the same household budget as school fees, so the figure that matters is the monthly one rather than the hourly one. The useful anchor this year is that KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. For a family who had planned a fee increase into their budget, that is unallocated money.

The monthly estimates in the table come from Bestimate's Dubai rate work and are given as ranges for a weekly one-hour session at three tiers, plus the exam-year figure where families step up to two sessions a week. Read them as the market rather than as a quote. The notable thing is how wide the budget-to-specialist spread is for the same nominal service, and how quickly a second weekly session changes the monthly total: most of the jump between the mid and the exam-year row is frequency, not rate.

Two items that catch Dubai families out are worth naming. The first is that examination entry fees are a school and centre matter, not a tutoring matter, and nothing a tutor charges includes them. They only become a household line at all if a student is entered as a private candidate rather than through their school, in which case the centre sets the fee and the deadline. The second is value added tax: how tuition is treated for VAT is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority and not something a tutoring page should assert, so the only question worth asking a provider is whether the figure they have quoted you is the figure you will pay.

The last row in the table is the one most families should look at hardest. A two-year plan sounds prudent and is usually the wrong shape for 0580. The subject is examined once at the end, almost all the recoverable marks sit in algebra and examination convention, and both of those respond to concentrated work rather than to a long thin drip. A defined block after a marked mock, repeated once, costs considerably less than twenty-four months of weekly sessions and in most cases achieves more.
