sections.heading: Is the person teaching your child legally permitted to do it?
paragraphs: This is the question with the clearest answer in the whole market and the one least often asked. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, and the application is made through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Two consequences follow for a parent comparing prices. First, nobody can justify a higher rate on the basis of permit costs, because there are none. Second, anybody offering private lessons in the UAE without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any figure quoted at you is unverified; a well-circulated number could not be confirmed against an official source and should not be repeated.

There is a second rule that matters in Abu Dhabi and is worth knowing wherever you live, because the principle behind it recurs. Press reporting indicates that the emirate's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and that the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the permit holder's own school. Treat that as press-reported rather than as the regulator's exact wording, and verify against the current policy document. The practical version is simple: your child's own classroom teacher, privately, is not the arrangement to look for.

A final distinction almost no provider volunteers. The MoHRE permit is a UAE work permit, so it applies to a person providing private lessons in the UAE. A tutor teaching a Dubai student from outside the UAE is in a different position. Both can be entirely legitimate. The question that cuts through it is the one in the table: where is this person physically based? A provider that will not answer that plainly is telling you something.

sections.heading: If the budget is fixed, where the dirhams do the most work
paragraphs: Suppose a Dubai family has decided on a thousand dirhams a month for a Year 11 sitting Extended 0580. At the mid band that is roughly one session a week with a qualified teacher, or two sessions a week at the budget tier, or a block of about six specialist sessions spread over two months. Those are genuinely different purchases, and the right one depends on a single piece of evidence: the marked mock paper.

If the losses on that script are mostly conventions and technique, buy the block at the higher band. Invisible working, premature rounding, bearings measured from the wrong reference, an angle given without a named theorem, frequency plotted instead of frequency density: those cost a grade between them and are fixable in six well-marked sessions. They are also the losses a cheaper hour is least likely to find, because finding them requires reading the script line by line rather than teaching the topic again.

If the losses are a genuine content gap in algebra, buy frequency at a lower band and buy it early. Rearranging with the subject appearing twice, indices, surds, non-linear simultaneous equations: these need repetition over weeks rather than intensity over days, and they pay back across every other topic on the paper because an algebraic step sits at the end of most multi-mark questions. In that situation two cheaper sessions a week beats one dearer one, as long as written work comes back marked.

If the student simply does not work between sessions, neither purchase will help and the money is better spent elsewhere. This is the uncomfortable third diagnosis and it is more common than either of the others. A fixed weekly slot with somebody who will ask what was done since last time has real value as structure rather than teaching, and it should be bought at the cheapest band that delivers it, not the most expensive. A provider who tells you that is worth more than one who sells you a specialist.
bullets: Technique and convention losses: buy a short block at the higher band
Algebra content gaps: buy frequency at a lower band, starting early
No work between sessions: buy structure at the cheapest band that provides it
In all three cases, the marked mock script is what tells you which one you have

sections.heading: What a cheap hour contains, and what an expensive one contains
paragraphs: Because the spread in this market is twentyfold, it is worth describing both ends concretely rather than implying that the dear one is simply better. At the bottom, an AED 50 to AED 80 hour in Dubai typically means a capable graduate, often a strong mathematician, working without the specification in front of them. The session is reactive: your child brings homework, the tutor helps with it, the homework gets finished. There is no marking outside the session, no diagnosis of why a question was wrong rather than that it was wrong, and no plan beyond next week. For a student who is simply not doing the work, that hour has genuine value as structure. For a student with a specific gap, it will not find it.

At the top, an AED 500 to AED 650 hour buys seniority: someone with long experience of the examination, often with assessment background, whose judgement about what will and will not appear is better than almost anybody's. That is worth real money on a Diploma exploration or a scarce syllabus. On 0580 it is usually the wrong purchase, because the specification is widely taught and the marks available to a Year 11 sit in algebra and technique rather than in anything exotic. Paying the premium band at this level is buying insurance against a risk that is not present.

The middle, which in Dubai means the AED 150 to AED 300 published range, is where the useful work happens for this qualification. What that band should contain is specific and you should ask for it: a tutor who has taught the specification and the tier, a first session that starts from the marked script rather than a conversation, exam-style work set between sessions and returned annotated, and a plan with the series date on it. If a provider in that band cannot describe those four things, they are charging mid-band for a bottom-band service, which is the commonest overpayment in this market.

One phrase to be sceptical about at every price point. Any provider describing someone as an examiner should be able to say what status is actually evidenced and when, and nobody can offer access to marking, boundaries or unreleased papers on the back of it. Cambridge's syllabuses, past papers and mark schemes are its copyright material: a tutor references and links them and works from what your school has legitimately provided. A provider offering a bundle of papers as a download is advertising a copyright problem rather than a resource.

sections.heading: Group classes, packages and the things that look cheaper than they are
paragraphs: Three formats in this market advertise a lower number and frequently deliver a higher cost per unit of progress. Worth naming each, because all three are reasonable purchases in the right circumstance and poor ones in the wrong.

Group classes halve or quarter the hourly figure and they are the only lever that genuinely does. In the final term, four Extended candidates working through timed questions with a teacher who marks them is good value. Earlier in the year, or with students at different stages, the group becomes supervision for most of the room. The question to ask is how the group was matched and on what evidence; an answer about year group and school is not an answer about mathematics.

Monthly packages look like a discount and sometimes are. The arithmetic is the whole story: divide by hours rather than by sessions, because a package of eight forty-five-minute sessions is six hours, not eight. In this market an advertised AED 799 monthly online package lands near the lower qualified-teacher band if the sessions are full hours and well above it if they are not, and an advertised AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 in-home monthly package for four two-hour sessions divides out above the online band while also delivering sessions longer than a weeknight can absorb.

Long upfront commitments are the third. A discounted two-year plan for a subject examined once at the end is usually the provider managing their revenue rather than your child's need, and it removes the one piece of leverage you have, which is the ability to stop. If a block is right, take a block with a stated endpoint, ask whether unused sessions expire, and renew deliberately. The pattern that works for most Dubai 0580 families is a defined block after a marked mock, reviewed against the next marked mock, repeated if the evidence says to repeat it.
bullets: Group classes: the only format that genuinely halves cost, and the weakest at diagnosis
Packages: divide by hours, not sessions, and check the session length first
Long plans: a subject examined once at the end rarely needs a two-year commitment
Review against the next marked assessment rather than against a renewal date

process.title: Tell us the tier and send the marked mock
process.description: The enquiry asks for the syllabus code, the tier and your child's most recent marked script. Those three turn a first session into a diagnosis, and the marked script is what determines whether the right purchase is a short block at a higher band or more frequency at a lower one.

process.title: A free trial lesson, with no card taken
process.description: One free session per family, with no card details required to book it. It is used on the marked script, sorting lost marks into causes: not known, known but misapplied, arithmetic, rounding, misread command word, out of time. You get the counts rather than an impression.

process.title: A written diagnosis and a number of sessions
process.description: After the trial you receive the loss breakdown, the two topic areas carrying the most marks, and an estimate of how many sessions the work needs. If the honest answer is fewer sessions than you expected, or that the problem is work habits rather than mathematics, the note says that.

process.title: You are quoted once, against that plan
process.description: We quote after the trial rather than publishing a list, and the quote is against a stated number of sessions with an endpoint. You will be told the session length, what comes back marked and what happens to a session cancelled at short notice, before anything is paid.

process.title: Marked work between every session
process.description: Exam-style work is set between sessions and comes back annotated in your child's own hand: where a method mark was available, where an accuracy mark went, what the command word asked for. The marking is the part you can check, which is why it is inside the rate rather than an extra.

process.title: Review against the next school assessment
process.description: The plan is reviewed when the next mock or class assessment is marked, by comparing the new loss breakdown with the old one. That document is produced by the school rather than by us, which makes it the only honest measure of whether the money is working.

whyPoints.title: Every figure is attributed and dated
whyPoints.description: The AED rates on this page belong to the providers named beside them, read in October 2026. We publish no invented price list for 0580 and we quote only after a trial lesson has established what the work actually is. A page that shows its sources can be checked, and one that does not cannot.

whyPoints.title: The permit position is stated, including the awkward part
whyPoints.description: The MoHRE private tuition work permit is free of charge for two years, so no rate can be justified by permit costs. We also state plainly that the permit is a UAE work permit and does not apply to a tutor teaching from outside the UAE, and we tell you to ask where your tutor is based.

whyPoints.title: No fine amounts, because none are published
whyPoints.description: Tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts has been published. A widely circulated figure could not be verified against an official source, so it does not appear here. Scare numbers are not information.

whyPoints.title: Marking is inside the rate, not an upsell
whyPoints.description: Written work comes back annotated in your child's own hand showing where method and accuracy marks went. That takes unpaid time outside the session, which is precisely why it is the first thing a cheaper hour quietly drops. You can ask to see an example before you book.

whyPoints.title: We will tell you to buy less
whyPoints.description: A subject examined once at the end rarely needs a two-year weekly commitment, and most 0580 problems are a defined block after a marked mock. Where the honest answer is fewer sessions, a cheaper band, or structure rather than teaching, that is what the written diagnosis says.

whyPoints.title: Delivery is stated before you enquire, not after
whyPoints.description: Lessons for UAE families are one-to-one on live video in Gulf Standard Time. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; that service exists only in India. Nothing on this page implies a tutor will arrive at a Dubai address, because none will.

faqs.question: What does an hour of Cambridge 0580 maths support actually cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published rates in October 2026 span a wide range. Budget online platforms advertise from AED 33 to AED 65. Specialist agencies list IGCSE from about AED 150, running to AED 300. In-home services in Dubai sit at AED 180 to AED 500 with travel inside the figure. International marketplaces quote from around AED 270, often in another currency first. Premium named tutors publish up to AED 650. Those are other providers' figures, attributed in the rate table on this page. IB Gram quotes after a free trial lesson rather than publishing a list, because the honest number depends on the tier and the number of weeks.

faqs.question: Why is the in-home band higher than the online band for what might be the same teacher?
faqs.answer: Because somebody is paying for a car. A tutor driving across Dubai for a one-hour lesson commits about ninety minutes of their day to earn sixty minutes of fee, and that ratio sits inside the published AED 180 to AED 500 band whether or not anybody itemises it. The same economics also pushes in-home providers to set a ninety- or one-hundred-and-twenty-minute minimum session, so the monthly commitment rises too. Remove the travel and the same qualified teacher is available in a band that starts at AED 150, which is most of the financial argument for video.

faqs.question: Is a monthly package better value than paying by the hour for Year 11 maths?
faqs.answer: Only after you do the arithmetic, and the arithmetic is the whole story. Divide by hours rather than by sessions: a package of eight forty-five-minute sessions is six hours, not eight. An advertised AED 799 monthly online package in this market lands near the lower qualified-teacher band if the sessions are full hours and well above it if they are not. An advertised AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 in-home monthly package for four two-hour sessions divides out above the online band, and two hours on a weeknight is longer than a fifteen-year-old can usefully absorb.

faqs.question: We have fixed AED 1,000 a month for maths. What should we buy with it?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on one document: the marked mock script. If the losses are conventions and technique, which means invisible working, premature rounding, bearings from the wrong reference, angles without a named theorem, buy a short block at the higher band, because finding those needs line-by-line reading rather than reteaching. If the losses are genuine algebra gaps, buy frequency at a lower band and start early, because rearranging and indices need repetition over weeks. If the student is not working between sessions, buy structure at the cheapest band that provides it.

faqs.question: Does the hourly rate change between Core and Extended entries?
faqs.answer: Modestly, usually AED 20 to AED 50 in this market. The extended tier covers additional content rather than the same content made harder, mostly in algebra, functions and trigonometry, so the preparation is wider and the pool of tutors comfortable across all of it is slightly smaller. The rate difference is not the important part of the tier question though. A Core entry caps the grade at C, which closes most sixth-form mathematics routes in Dubai, so that conversation with the department matters far more than the hourly figure attached to it.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a Year 11 on Extended usually need before the June series?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families buy and more concentrated. The pattern that works is a defined block of six to ten sessions after a marked mock, addressing the two causes carrying the most lost marks, then a review against the next mock and a decision to repeat or stop. In the final six weeks the useful work narrows to converting partial knowledge into whole marks, so nothing new should be starting then. A two-year weekly commitment for a subject examined once at the end is usually the provider's revenue plan rather than your child's need.

faqs.question: Is a group of four cheaper than one-to-one for 0580 revision?
faqs.answer: Considerably, and it is the only lever that genuinely halves the figure. In the final term, four Extended candidates working through timed questions with a teacher who marks them is good value per head. Earlier in the year, or with students at different stages, the group becomes supervision for most of the room, because the whole value of a session is one student's specific errors being found. Ask how the group was matched and on what evidence. An answer about year group and school is not an answer about mathematics.

faqs.question: What does the UAE tutor permit cost, and can we ask to see our tutor's?
faqs.answer: Nothing. The MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. So no rate can be defended on permit costs. You can and should ask a UAE-based tutor to confirm their permit. There is one further question almost nobody asks: the permit is a UAE work permit, so a tutor teaching your child from outside the UAE is in a different position entirely. Ask where the person is physically based.

faqs.question: Are examination entry fees included in anything a tutor charges?
faqs.answer: No, and they should not be. Entries are made by your child's school through its exams officer, within the board's published deadline, and the cost sits inside the school's fee arrangements rather than a tutoring invoice. Entry fees only become a separate household line if a student sits as a private candidate rather than through their school, in which case the examination centre sets both the fee and the deadline. That is a conversation with a centre, well before the entry date, and no tutoring provider arranges it on your behalf.

faqs.question: Does the Dubai fee freeze for 2026-27 actually free up money for tutoring?
faqs.answer: For some households, yes, and it is worth being deliberate about it. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. A family that had budgeted for a rise now has unallocated money. The sensible use of it for a 0580 candidate is a defined diagnostic block after the next marked mock rather than an open-ended weekly booking, because the spend that moves marks in this subject is concentrated rather than continuous.

faqs.question: What does an AED 60 hour actually contain in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Usually a capable graduate, often a genuinely strong mathematician, working without the specification in front of them. The session is reactive: your child brings homework, it gets finished, nothing is marked outside the session, and there is no diagnosis of why a question was wrong rather than that it was. For a student who simply is not working between lessons, that structure has real value and is correctly priced. For a student with a specific algebraic gap or a technique problem, it will not find it, and six months of it is more expensive than six well-marked sessions.

faqs.question: Do we pay more for a tutor who marks past-paper work properly?
faqs.answer: Usually AED 20 to AED 60 an hour more, and it is the single item most worth paying for at this level. There is a real difference between an hour of conversation about mathematics and an hour that produces annotated written work in your child's own hand showing where a method mark was available and where an accuracy mark went. Marking is unpaid time outside the session, so it is either inside the rate or it is not happening. Ask directly what comes back after each session, and ask to see an example before you commit.

faqs.question: Should we pay for sessions through the long summer break, or stop?
faqs.answer: It depends which summer. Between Year 10 and Year 11, a short block on algebra is among the best-value spending available, because rearranging, indices and surds pay back across every topic in the examination year and nothing is urgent yet, so rates and availability are both better. Between Year 11 and sixth form, the same logic applies even more strongly, since A Level and Diploma mathematics assume Extended fluency and teach very little of it. Paying for full weekly sessions through ten weeks with no target is the version that wastes money.

faqs.question: If we stop after two sessions, what happens to the money?
faqs.answer: That depends on how you bought, which is why the buying model matters as much as the rate. Pay-as-you-go carries the highest hourly figure precisely because the provider carries the risk of you leaving, and nothing is owed beyond the session taken. A block is discounted because you carried that risk instead, so ask before paying whether unused sessions expire, whether they can roll into the next term and what notice a cancellation needs. A provider who cannot answer those three questions clearly before payment is not a provider to pay in advance.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to put two siblings into the same 0580 session?
faqs.answer: Only if they are genuinely at the same point, which siblings in different year groups never are. Where two students are both on Extended and both losing marks in the same place, a shared session is reasonable value and roughly halves the per-child figure. Where they are not, you are buying one child teaching and one child supervision at a discount, which is more expensive than it looks. Many providers offer a modest household rate instead, usually ten to twenty per cent, which reflects shared booking administration rather than shared teaching.

intro.heading: What should be on your kitchen table after four weeks
paragraphs: Most tutoring is bought and judged on impression. The child seems happier about maths. The tutor is pleasant and arrives on time. The hour passes productively. Four months later a mock comes back and nothing has moved, and nobody can say why, because nothing was ever written down that could be compared with anything else. That is not a failure of the tutor's ability; it is a failure to generate evidence, and in a subject examined once at the end of two years it is expensive.

So this page starts from the opposite end. Here is what should physically exist after four weeks of 0580 support. Your child's most recent marked school script. A written breakdown of the marks lost on it, sorted into six causes rather than into topics. Two or three pieces of exam-style work in your child's own handwriting, annotated by the tutor to show where a method mark was available and where an accuracy mark went. Three or four short session notes saying what was taught, what your child could do unaided by the end, and what was still wrong. And a plan with dates, including the date of the next school assessment it will be judged against.

The reason to sort losses by cause rather than by topic is that the causes need completely different responses, and the topic tells you almost nothing. A student who lost eleven marks across mensuration, trigonometry and statistics has not got three problems. They may have one: they round halfway through and their final answers fall outside the accepted range. That is one or two sessions of work. The same eleven marks lost because the content was never understood is three to eight sessions per topic area. Identical topic lists, wildly different plans, and the only document that distinguishes them is the script.

Online delivery turns out to help with exactly this, which is not the usual argument made for it. A video session is a session where everything is already on a screen, so annotation is native, the marked work exists as a file rather than a photograph in a bag, and the record accumulates automatically. A parent who wants to read what happened in week two can read it in week nine. That is harder to produce when a tutor writes on loose paper at the kitchen table and takes the paper away.

This page covers what online actually changes about teaching 0580, the evidence pack in detail, how to read a marked script yourself, what a term looks like week by week, what mark movement honestly looks like and why nobody can promise a grade, how to audit a tutor in three weeks, the technology that matters and the kit that does not, and where online genuinely loses. Lessons for UAE families are one-to-one on live video in Gulf Standard Time; we do not offer home visits in the UAE, as that is a service we run only in India.
bullets: Sort lost marks by cause, not by topic; the causes need different plans
Expect annotated work in your child's own handwriting, not a verbal summary
Expect a three-line note after every session and a review date with a school assessment on it
Online delivery makes the record accumulate automatically rather than disappearing into a bag
No tutor can promise a grade; mark movement on marked scripts is what can honestly be shown
Audit in week three using the questions in this page's audit table

dubai/cambridge-igcse-maths-0580-online-.programmesIntro: What counts as evidence of progress changes with the level, because what is assessed changes. These are the levels a Dubai maths enquiry spans and the measurable that matters at each.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
programmes.description: Two written papers at the end of the course, nothing internally assessed, so the only honest measure of progress is performance on exam-style questions under time. That makes the measurable unusually clean: marks on a marked script, sorted by cause, compared with the same count a term earlier. Topic coverage is not a measure, because a student can cover every topic and still lose the same eleven marks to rounding.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools typically run mocks in November and again in February or March, which gives a family two independently produced measurement points inside Year 11. Those two documents, placed side by side, are worth more than any tutor's own assessment, because the school produced them and had no interest in the answer.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics 0606
programmes.description: Measured the same way and harder to fake, because the content reaches into differentiation, integration, kinematics and series. A student who can produce a correct derivative under time has demonstrated something specific; a student who nods along to a worked example has not. The evidence that matters here is unaided work on unseen questions rather than annotated examples.
programmes.countryNote: Because 0606 is offered by only some Dubai schools and usually only to a set, a student taking it is often the only one in their friendship group doing so. That isolation is itself a reason to generate written evidence: there is nobody to compare against informally, so the marked script is the only reference point available.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level Mathematics
programmes.description: The measurable shifts towards algebraic fluency, because the new content assumes it rather than teaching it. Progress at this level shows up as speed and accuracy on routine manipulation, not as understanding of new topics. A student who understands differentiation and takes four minutes to rearrange a formula will not cope with the paper, and that is visible on a timed script long before it is visible on a report.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the first-term collapse in sixth-form mathematics is common enough to be predictable, and it almost always traces back to Extended-level algebra that was never automatic. Families who keep their Year 11 marked scripts have the diagnostic already in hand when it happens.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation
programmes.description: Adds an internally assessed exploration, which is the one place at this level where progress is visible as a draft rather than as a mark. The honest evidence is the student's own successive drafts with the tutor's questions in the margin, never edits. Written papers are measured as at every other level: timed scripts, marked, with losses sorted by cause.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, three of them International Baccalaureate, so more Year 11 students in the emirate will face the Diploma route decision. The algebra evidence from a 0580 script is the single most useful input into whether Analysis and Approaches is realistic.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-maths-0580-online-.subjectsIntro: There are at least eleven maths routes running in Dubai Year 11 and sixth-form classrooms, and advice does not transfer between them. This is the grid, with what counts as evidence of progress on each.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 Core
subjects.levels: Papers 1 and 3, grades C to G
subjects.description: Progress shows as completed papers rather than as harder questions answered. A Core candidate loses most marks by leaving things blank or running out of time, so the measurable is the proportion of the paper attempted with visible method, tracked across three timed scripts.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 Extended
subjects.levels: Papers 2 and 4, grades A* to E
subjects.description: The measurable is multi-step questions carried to completion, because the longer paper is built from questions that chain three topics. A student who scores well on single-topic practice and poorly on a full paper has a chaining problem, which is visible only on a timed script.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0980
subjects.description: Identical teaching and identical evidence; only the grade labels differ. Worth knowing because a sixth form may state its entry requirement in one scale while the certificate arrives in the other, which causes avoidable confusion in a Dubai application cycle.

subjects.name: Cambridge International Mathematics 0607
subjects.description: A different syllabus with its own structure, a graphics calculator expectation and an investigative element, often chosen by schools running the IB continuum. Evidence of progress includes calculator fluency, which does not appear at all in 0580 preparation. A student revising 0580 papers for an 0607 entry is measuring the wrong thing.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics 0606
subjects.description: The only IGCSE-level course that teaches calculus, alongside logarithms, series, kinematics and vectors. Evidence here is unaided work on unseen questions: following a worked example proves nothing about whether a derivative can be produced under time pressure.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1, Foundation
subjects.description: A different board with a different paper structure and different tier labels. Progress is measured the same way but against Pearson's own past material, and the command vocabulary differs enough that cross-board practice teaches slightly wrong habits.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1, Higher
subjects.description: The Pearson equivalent of Extended, widely used across Dubai schools. The evidence discipline is identical: timed scripts, losses sorted by cause, compared term to term. Match every past paper and revision guide to the board on the statement of entry.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1
subjects.description: Pearson's calculus-bearing option at this level, the counterpart to Cambridge's Additional Mathematics. Scarce teaching supply in Dubai, so a family needing it should start looking early rather than assuming availability in the spring.

subjects.name: Cambridge International AS Level Mathematics
subjects.description: Progress is measured in algebraic speed as much as in content. A timed script where the manipulation is slow but correct predicts a difficult A2 year, and that is actionable in October rather than in June.

subjects.name: IB Diploma Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Assumes Extended-level fluency and extends into proof and calculus. The internally assessed exploration is evidenced by the student's own successive drafts with questions in the margin. A tutor's edits in the document are not evidence of progress; they are a problem.

subjects.name: IB Diploma Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling-led and statistics-heavy, with technology use assumed throughout. Progress evidence includes interpreting output and justifying a model choice in writing, which is a different skill from computing an answer and needs separately marked work.

subjects.name: Examination Technique as a Measurable
subjects.description: Not a route, and the most measurable thing on the list. Count the marks lost to invisible working, rounding, misread command words and running out of time on one script, then count them again on the next. That number moving is the cleanest evidence of progress available anywhere in mathematics.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-maths-0580-online-.regionsTitle: Where Dubai families take online sessions from, and what the room is like
dubai/cambridge-igcse-maths-0580-online-.regionsIntro: For video sessions the relevant local detail is not the commute but the room: whether a fifteen-year-old can close a door, where the paper goes, and whether the household's schedule is in one timezone. These are the communities most online enquiries come from and what they usually need to solve.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai and City Walk
regions.note: Apartment living with shared study space at a premium, so the practical fix is usually a headset and an agreed hour when the room is actually free. Families here often choose a later slot, around 6.30pm, once the household has settled rather than straight after the school run.

regions.name: DIFC and Business Bay
regions.note: A high proportion of households where both parents work late and the student is alone at 5pm, which makes the session note after each lesson the main channel of information. Written notes matter more here than anywhere else, because nobody is in the room to see how the hour went.

regions.name: JBR and Bluewaters Island
regions.note: Smaller apartments, considerable background noise and frequently a sibling in the same room. A second device propped as a document camera is usually the difference between a session that can see the working and one that cannot, and it costs nothing if an old phone exists.

regions.name: Dubai Creek Harbour
regions.note: Newer towers with reliable connectivity and few schools immediately nearby, so most students here commute and arrive home late. A 6pm or weekend slot holds better than a weeknight 4.30pm, and a weekend morning is the only realistic window for a full two-hour Extended paper.

regions.name: The Lakes, The Views and Jumeirah Golf Estates
regions.note: Villa households where a dedicated desk usually exists, which removes the commonest practical obstacle entirely. The constraint here is activity schedules, so families tend to fix one weeknight teaching slot and one weekend slot for timed papers.

regions.name: Tilal Al Ghaf and Dubai South
regions.note: Outer communities with long school runs, where the financial and scheduling case for video is strongest. These households are also the most likely to have moved into the emirate recently, which means a student adjusting to a new specification mid-course.

regions.name: Palm Jumeirah
regions.note: A high proportion of families who travel for several weeks at a time, so the useful arrangement is a schedule that follows the student rather than the address. Sessions continuing from another timezone are routine, and the written record is what keeps the plan intact across a trip.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: A mixed-curriculum cluster where a Year 11 friendship group may contain students on Cambridge, Pearson and CBSE mathematics at once. Comparing revision across those routes actively misleads, which is a conversation worth having in the first session rather than the fifth.

schoolClusters.city: The central districts: Downtown, DIFC, Business Bay and the Creek
schoolClusters.note: Families who live centrally and commute outward to school, so students arrive home late and sessions sit in the evening. The strongest reason these households choose video is that it survives a 6.30pm start, which a visiting arrangement rarely does on a weeknight.

schoolClusters.city: The western beachfront and Jumeirah corridor
schoolClusters.note: Long-established British schools within a short radius, and a resident population that travels frequently for work. The requirement most often stated here is continuity: the same tutor and the same plan while the family is out of the country for a fortnight.

sections.heading: What online actually changes about teaching 0580, and what it does not
paragraphs: A Cambridge IGCSE Maths 0580 online tutor in Dubai teaches on live video, one-to-one, in Gulf Standard Time. The honest description of what that changes is narrower than either the advocates or the sceptics claim, and it is worth being specific because the generalities are useless.

What genuinely changes for the better is the record. In a video session the working appears on a shared surface, so annotation is native rather than something a tutor has to remember to photograph. A script your child wrote on paper can be captured with a phone and marked on screen in front of them, with the marks saved rather than carried away in a bag. Over a term that accumulates into a file you can actually read, which is the difference between knowing progress happened and believing it did. Every claim on this page about evidence depends on that property.

What also changes is who is available. The pool of people who can teach the 0580 specification well and are willing to drive to a given Dubai community at 5pm on a Tuesday is small and arbitrary. The pool who can teach it on video is the whole pool, and matching can be done on what matters, which is whether they have taught this specification and this tier. For a scarce requirement, such as Additional Mathematics or a student who needs a particular approach, that difference is decisive rather than marginal.

What does not change is the mathematics, the amount of work a student has to do between sessions, or the fact that a fifteen-year-old who will not engage with the subject cannot be made to by any delivery method. Video is a channel. It makes a good session easier to evidence and a bad session easier to drift through, because nobody is physically present to notice a student scrolling. That risk is real and the countermeasure is the same as the evidence discipline: written work in the student's own hand, every week, marked. A student who is not working cannot produce it, and that shows up in week two rather than in March.

sections.heading: The evidence pack: what should exist by week four
paragraphs: This is the table to hold a provider against, including us. Each row is an artefact rather than an impression, and the final column is what its absence tells you. If three or more of these do not exist after a month of paid sessions, the hours may still have been pleasant and you have no way to know whether they worked.

The first row is not produced by the tutor at all, and that is the point. Your child's school marks mocks and class assessments with no interest in whether tutoring is working, which makes those documents the only genuinely independent measurement in the whole arrangement. A provider who proposes to measure progress exclusively against their own assessments is grading their own homework. Ask instead which school assessment the plan will be judged against, and put the date in your calendar.

The second row is the one almost nobody produces, and it is the highest-value document in the pack. A loss breakdown takes the marked script and sorts every lost mark into one of six causes: not known, known but misapplied, arithmetic slip, rounding or accuracy, misread command word, ran out of time. The counts matter more than the total. Eleven marks lost to rounding is one or two sessions of work. Eleven marks lost because three topics were never understood is most of a term. A plan built without that distinction is a guess dressed as a schedule.

The fifth row is the one families skip and then regret. Timed practice under correct conditions is the only way to test timing, and running out of time is consistently among the largest causes of lost marks for Extended candidates, because Paper 4 is built from multi-step questions that reward persistence and punish hesitation. A student who has never sat a full paper at correct duration will discover their pace in the examination hall, which is the worst available place to discover it.

sections.heading: Reading a marked script yourself: the six causes of a lost mark
paragraphs: You do not need to be a mathematician to read a marked 0580 script usefully. You need to be able to sort the losses, and the sorting is a judgement about the page rather than about the mathematics. Half an hour with the script and the table below will tell you more about what your child needs than any conversation with any provider.

Work through the paper question by question and put each lost mark into one box. Blank or an attempt unrelated to the topic is not known. Correct method applied to the wrong kind of question is known but misapplied, which is a selection problem rather than a knowledge problem. Right method with a wrong number is an arithmetic slip, and if most of them are on the paper where no calculator is permitted, that is the diagnosis right there. Correct working with a final answer just outside the accepted range is rounding. A calculation where words were asked for, or an angle given without a theorem named, is a misread command word. A strong first half with blank final questions is time.

Then count the boxes, and notice what the counts imply. The four middle causes together, known but misapplied, arithmetic, rounding and command words, are technique, and technique is fixable in weeks. Not known is content, and content is fixable in months. Time is fixable with timed papers and almost nothing else. Most Dubai Year 11 scripts that families bring in panic are dominated by the technique boxes, which is genuinely good news and the opposite of what the family has concluded.

There is a seventh pattern that sits outside the six and deserves its own row in the table: invisible working. A wrong final answer with nothing written between the question and the answer collects no method marks, where the same wrong answer with correct visible working collects most of them. Students who have come through systems that reward neat presentation are the worst affected, because they work on scrap and transcribe only the result. It takes about three sessions of enforced line-by-line working to retrain, and it is worth more marks than any topic on the syllabus.

sections.heading: A term of 0580 support, week by week, with the measurable at each stage
paragraphs: A plan that cannot be described week by week is not a plan. The table below is the shape a twelve-week engagement takes when it starts from a marked script, and the point of the fourth column is that each stage produces something checkable rather than a feeling of momentum.

Weeks one and two look like less teaching than families expect, and that is deliberate. The first session reads the script and produces the loss breakdown; the second attacks the largest technique cause, because technique is where the quick marks are and an early measurable win changes a student's willingness to do the work. Families who insist on starting with content teaching in week one usually do so because content feels like what they are paying for, and they lose the fastest marks available to them.

The middle weeks are ordinary: teach, set work, mark it, address what the marking showed. The discipline that makes them productive is that every session begins with the previous week's marked work rather than with a new topic. A session that starts with new content has quietly decided not to check whether last week worked, and a term of those is how four months pass with nothing to show.

The last third shifts to timed papers, because by then the useful question is no longer whether your child can do a question but whether they can do a paper. Two measurables matter there: the proportion of the paper attempted with visible working, and the count in the time box. Both are easy to read and both predict the real thing better than topic confidence does. At week twelve, the comparison between the first loss breakdown and the second is the whole report, and it either shows movement or it does not.

sections.heading: What mark movement honestly looks like, and why no grade can be promised
paragraphs: This is where most tutoring pages become vague, so here is the straight version. Nobody can promise a grade. Grade boundaries are set by the board after each series and vary between series, so the number of marks needed for a given grade in June 2027 is not knowable in advance by anybody, including a tutor who has taught the specification for twenty years. Anybody offering a guaranteed outcome is either misunderstanding the system or selling something they cannot deliver, and in this market both exist.

What can honestly be shown is mark movement on comparable scripts. If your child's November mock loses nineteen marks across the six causes and the February mock loses nine, that is real, independently produced and attributable. It may or may not be a grade, because that depends on boundaries nobody has set yet. What it is not is an opinion. A family holding two marked scripts and two loss breakdowns is in a far stronger position than one holding a reassuring conversation.

On realistic scale, the honest ranges are narrower than advertising implies and wider than pessimism suggests. Technique losses, which means rounding, command words, invisible working and accuracy, can usually be reduced substantially inside a term, because they are habits rather than knowledge and they respond quickly to marked work. Content gaps move more slowly and in proportion to the hours actually worked between sessions, not in the sessions themselves. Timing improves in proportion to the number of full papers sat under real conditions, which for most students is a small number because it is unpleasant.

One more honesty note, because the alternative is standard in this market. No provider can show you an unreleased paper or a grade boundary for a series that has not been graded, and anybody implying otherwise is describing a malpractice risk rather than an advantage. Cambridge's syllabuses, specimen papers, past papers and mark schemes are its own copyright material: the right behaviour is to cite them, link the official pages and work from what the school has legitimately provided. A provider circulating a bundle of papers as a download is advertising a problem.
bullets: Grade boundaries are set after each series, so no grade can be promised in advance
Mark movement across two school-marked scripts is independent evidence and can be shown

sections.heading: How to audit an online tutor in three weeks
paragraphs: Three weeks is enough. Not because progress will be visible by then, but because the presence or absence of an evidence habit is visible immediately, and the evidence habit is what predicts whether month four will have anything to show. The table below is five questions to ask in week three, with what a solid answer sounds like and what a weak one sounds like.

The pattern in the weak column is worth naming, because it is not incompetence. Weak answers are almost always about feelings and effort: your child is more confident, we are building strong foundations, there is a good rapport. Those statements may be true and they are not measurements, and a provider who offers them in week three will still be offering them in month five. The question to ask after each one is simply: how would I know that from a document?

Two of the five questions are specifically about your child doing work unaided, and that is deliberate. The commonest failure mode in online tutoring is a pleasant hour of guided work in which the tutor's prompts carry the student through, after which nobody knows what the student can do alone. It is a comfortable hour for everybody. The only cure is work attempted unaided between sessions and marked, which is why its absence is the single strongest signal in the audit.

If the audit goes badly, change tutor rather than model. This is the practical advantage of video that matters most and is least discussed: the replacement can be anybody who has taught the specification, rather than whoever else is prepared to drive to your community at that hour. Matches fail for ordinary reasons and the right response is to switch in week three, which is cheap, instead of enduring it until March, which is not.

sections.heading: The technology that matters, and the kit that does not
paragraphs: Families overthink this and providers encourage them to, so here is the short version. Three things materially affect whether an online maths session works, and none of them is expensive.

The first is a way for the tutor to see handwritten working as it happens. A second device propped to point at the page is the cheapest and often the best solution: an old phone on a stack of books, joined to the same call, pointed at the paper. The maths lives on paper, which is where the examination will also live, and the tutor sees the hand move rather than a finished answer. A graphics tablet is a reasonable alternative and is genuinely better for some students, and it is an upgrade rather than a requirement.

The second is audio. A headset with a microphone transforms a session in an apartment with a sibling in the room, and laptop speakers in a tiled Dubai living room produce echo that makes a sixty-minute session tiring for both people. It is the lowest-cost improvement available and the one families skip most often, because it is not obviously about mathematics.

The third is a fixed place and time. A student who takes the session at the dining table while the household moves around them is in a worse learning environment than the same student at a desk with a door, and this matters more at fifteen than at nine because the temptation to drift is larger. None of this requires a study. It requires a decision about where the laptop goes and a household agreement about the hour. What does not matter: a premium internet package, a second monitor, subscription software, or any platform feature beyond screen sharing, annotation and the ability to save what was written.
bullets: A second device pointed at the paper, so the tutor sees handwritten working as it happens

sections.heading: Where online loses, stated plainly
paragraphs: A page arguing for a model should say where it fails, otherwise the rest of it is advertising. There are four situations where a tutor in the room is better for a 0580 candidate, and a family in any of them should know it.

The first is a student who will not engage and has to be physically supervised. Video makes drifting easy, and a student who scrolls on a phone below the camera can waste an hour without anybody noticing until the marked work does not arrive. An adult in the room removes that option. The honest counter is that the marked work still reveals it within two weeks, so the failure is detected quickly rather than prevented, and some families would rather prevent it.

The second is severe mathematics anxiety, where the student needs a person beside them to attempt anything at all. This is real and it is more common at fifteen than parents expect, because it has usually been building since primary. In the acute phase, physical presence genuinely helps. The practical compromise some families use is a few sessions with somebody in the room to break the freeze, then video for the sustained work.

The third is a household where no quiet space exists at any hour and the session genuinely cannot happen. This is a real constraint in a shared apartment with multiple children, and a headset only solves part of it. The fourth is a student with specific access needs who requires physical materials or a particular kind of in-person support. In all four cases the right answer is not a better video platform. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, that service exists only in India, and where this page's model is the wrong one we would rather say so here than discover it in session three.

sections.heading: Running a timed paper at home so the result is worth something
paragraphs: A timed paper sat badly produces a number that misleads everybody, so the conditions matter as much as the paper. The rules are short and families break most of them the first time, usually out of kindness.

Correct duration, timed from a clock the student can see, with no pauses. Correct calculator rules, which means the calculator is physically out of the room for the paper that does not permit one, not merely unused. No phone. No access to notes, formula sheets beyond what the paper itself provides, or a parent to ask. One sitting. If the student stops early because they have finished, the remaining time is recorded, because finishing twenty minutes early with blanks is a different diagnosis from finishing exactly on time.

Afterwards, do not give the answers. The paper goes to the tutor unmarked and is marked line by line in the next session with the student present, which is where the learning actually is. A student who marks their own paper against an answer key learns which answers were wrong and nothing about why, and the why is the entire content of the exercise. This is also the moment when the method-mark lesson lands hardest: seeing marks available on a question you got wrong is more persuasive than being told about them.

Frequency matters less than most families assume. Two full papers properly sat and properly marked teach more than eight done loosely and self-marked, and in the final term a fortnightly rhythm is enough. In Dubai the practical obstacle is finding a two-hour uninterrupted window, which on a weeknight after a long school run rarely exists, so Saturday morning is usually the answer. Write the dates in a calendar at the start of the term rather than deciding each week, because the week will always have a reason.

whyPoints.description: Annotated work in your child's handwriting, dated timed scripts, three-line session notes and two loss breakdowns. whyPoints.title: Unaided work is the standard, not guided work
whyPoints.description: A pleasant hour in which the tutor's prompts carry a student through proves nothing about an examination hall. Work is set to be attempted without help and marked on that basis, because the gap between guided and unaided performance is where June disappointments come from.

whyPoints.title: No grade promises, and a reason
whyPoints.description: Grade boundaries are set by the board after each series, so the marks needed for a grade are not knowable in advance by anybody. What can be shown is mark movement across two school-marked scripts. Anyone promising an outcome is describing a system that does not work that way.

whyPoints.title: We say where this model is wrong
whyPoints.description: A student who needs physical supervision, acute mathematics anxiety, or a household with no quiet hour are all situations where somebody in the room is better. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; that service exists only in India, and where video is the wrong fit this page says so.

faqs.question: How will I know the online sessions are working before the next school report?
faqs.answer: By reading three things rather than waiting for one. First, the loss breakdown produced from your child's marked script in week one, with counts against six causes. Second, the annotated work your child attempted unaided each week, which shows whether the same error recurs on fresh questions. Third, a dated timed script from around week ten that is directly comparable to the one from week one. Reports arrive late and say little. Those three documents exist inside a month and answer the question directly, and you can read them without being a mathematician.

faqs.question: How does a tutor see my daughter's working if the lesson is on a screen?
faqs.answer: The simplest arrangement is a second device pointed at the page: an old phone propped on a stack of books, joined to the same call, aimed at the paper. The maths stays on paper, which is where the examination will be, and the tutor watches the hand move rather than seeing a finished answer. A graphics tablet works too and suits some students better, and a written script can also be photographed and marked on screen with your daughter watching. None of it needs a purchase if there is a spare phone in the house.

faqs.question: What should come back after each session, and in what form?
faqs.answer: Two things. A three-line note to you saying what was taught, what your child could do unaided by the end, and what was still wrong, short enough to read on a phone. And exam-style work set for the week, which comes back annotated in your child's own handwriting with the method and accuracy marks identified rather than ticked. If what comes back is a general message that the session went well, there is no record of what your child can do alone, which is the only thing the examination will test.

faqs.question: My son's mock went from forty-two to fifty-one marks. Is that a grade?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and nobody can tell you for certain in advance, because grade boundaries are set by the board after each series and vary between series. What the movement is, definitely, is nine marks of independently measured improvement on a script the school marked. The more useful question is where those nine came from. If they came out of the rounding, command-word and invisible-working boxes, the same work should keep paying. If they came from one topic that happened to appear, the next paper may not be as kind.

faqs.question: Can we record the sessions and go back over them?
faqs.answer: Ask the tutor and agree it in advance rather than assuming either way, because it involves a child and a recording and should be a deliberate decision with a stated purpose. Where it is agreed, recordings are genuinely useful for a worked example a student wants to revisit, and much less useful than people expect for revision, because nobody rewatches an hour. The higher-value record is the annotated written work, which takes thirty seconds to review and shows what your child could do rather than what the tutor explained.

faqs.question: Do we need a second screen, a tablet or a graphics tablet?
faqs.answer: No. Three things matter and none is expensive: a way for the tutor to see handwritten working as it happens, which a spare phone on a stack of books does well; a headset with a microphone, which is the single cheapest real improvement and the one families skip; and a fixed place with a door. A graphics tablet is a genuine upgrade for some students and not a requirement. Premium bandwidth, second monitors and subscription software make no measurable difference to a maths session.

faqs.question: How do we run a timed paper at home so the result actually means something?
faqs.answer: Correct duration, a clock the student can see, no pauses, one sitting, no phone, no notes beyond what the paper itself provides, and no parent to ask. For the paper that does not permit a calculator, the calculator leaves the room rather than sitting unused. If your child finishes early, record how much time was left, because finishing twenty minutes early with blanks is a different diagnosis from finishing on time. Then send it unmarked. It should be marked line by line in the next session with your child watching.

faqs.question: What happens if the internet drops in the middle of a session?
faqs.answer: Agree the fallback before it happens, which takes one message. The usual arrangement is that both sides try to rejoin for a few minutes, and if that fails the session is rescheduled rather than charged, because nobody travelled. The practical advantage of video shows up here: a rescheduled session can usually happen inside the same week, whereas a visit that collapses has already committed somebody's afternoon. Ask any provider what their policy is in writing before you book, alongside their late-cancellation terms.

faqs.question: Three weeks in, what should I be asking the tutor?
faqs.answer: Five questions. Which of the six causes is costing the most marks and what is the count? What has my child done unaided since we started, and can I see it marked? Which school assessment will we judge this against, and when is it? What will you not be able to fix by June, and why? And has my child sat a full paper at correct duration yet? Answers made of counts, documents and dates are solid. Answers about confidence, foundations and rapport are not measurements, however true they are.

faqs.question: Is online worse for a student with real maths anxiety?
faqs.answer: In the acute phase, often yes, and it is worth saying rather than arguing. A student who cannot attempt anything without a person beside them benefits from physical presence, and that anxiety has usually been building since primary school rather than appearing in Year 11. The compromise some families use is a short period with somebody in the room to break the freeze, then video for the sustained work. We do not offer home visits in the UAE, so where that is the right first step we will say so rather than sell around it.

faqs.question: Can a tutor mark a paper my daughter wrote by hand on paper?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the normal arrangement rather than a workaround. She photographs each page and sends it before the session, and it is marked on screen while she watches, with the method marks ringed and each lost mark named. Marking with the student present is the point: seeing that four marks were available on a question she got wrong teaches the method-mark lesson far better than being told about it. The marked file is then saved, so in March you can still read what November looked like.

faqs.question: How many marks is it realistic to move in a term?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on which boxes the losses sit in, which is why the sorting matters more than the total. Technique losses, meaning rounding, command words, accuracy and invisible working, usually reduce substantially inside a term because they are habits and they respond fast to marked work. Content gaps move in proportion to the hours your child actually works between sessions, not to the hours bought. Timing improves in proportion to the number of full papers genuinely sat under correct conditions, which for most students is a small number because it is unpleasant.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring work for a student who simply will not do the work?
faqs.answer: Not well, and no delivery method solves it. Video makes drifting easier, because a student scrolling below the camera can pass an hour without anybody noticing. The honest counter is that the evidence discipline detects it quickly: work set to be attempted unaided either arrives or does not, and that is visible in week two rather than in March. Detection is not prevention though. Where a family needs physical supervision rather than teaching, they should buy supervision, at the cheapest band that provides it, and not a specialist hour.

faqs.question: Our family is out of Dubai for several weeks at a time. Can the sessions follow us?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the genuine advantages of this model rather than a concession. Session times are adjusted to wherever your child is, the same tutor continues, and the plan and the marked work stay in one place rather than restarting on your return. A fortnight away in the middle of Year 11 stops being a fortnight lost. Agree the timezone shift in advance rather than session by session, and no cancellation charge applies to a change arranged ahead of time.

faqs.question: If we decide to stop, what evidence should we be left holding?
faqs.answer: Everything that was produced, and you should ask for it rather than assume. That means the loss breakdowns, the annotated work in your child's handwriting, the dated timed scripts and the session notes. Those documents are about your child and they are useful to the next tutor, to the school and to you. A provider who cannot hand over a file of marked work at the end of an engagement was never producing one, which is the thing this whole page is written to help you notice in week three instead of month five.

intro.heading: What the code 0580 tells you before anybody teaches anything
paragraphs: The number is not decoration. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics carries the syllabus code 0580, and that code decides which papers your child sits, how long they are, whether a calculator is allowed, which content is examinable and what the top available grade is. A tutor who says they teach IGCSE maths without asking for the code is about to guess. There are at least four different maths qualifications running in Dubai Year 11 classrooms, and the teaching for each one differs in ways that cost marks: 0580 is Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics, 0607 is Cambridge International Mathematics with its own investigation and graphics-calculator requirements, 0980 is the same content as 0580 reported on a 9 to 1 grade scale, and 4MA1 is Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A with a different paper structure entirely.

So the first useful thing a Dubai parent can do costs nothing. Find the statement of entry, or ask the exams officer, and write down the code and the tier. Those two facts determine everything that follows. A child entered for 0580 Core is sitting Papers 1 and 3 and cannot be awarded above a C. A child entered for 0580 Extended is sitting Papers 2 and 4 and the full A* to E range is open. Families discover this in April more often than anybody would like, which is the single most avoidable disappointment in the Dubai IGCSE year.

0580 is assessed entirely by written examination. There is no coursework, no internally assessed component and nothing to hand in, which makes it unusual among the subjects on a Dubai timetable and changes what tutoring is for. With a science or a language there is a piece of work to improve. With 0580 there is only performance under timed conditions on a paper nobody has seen, so every session has to be converted into something that survives a sealed room in June. That is a different skill from understanding the maths, and it is where most of the marks in this subject are won and lost.

The syllabus content divides into nine topic areas: number; algebra and graphs; coordinate geometry; geometry; mensuration; trigonometry; transformations and vectors; probability; and statistics. The Extended tier covers the core content plus additional material, most of it in algebra, functions and trigonometry. Nothing in that list is conceptually hard for a capable fifteen-year-old. What is hard is the quantity, the precision and the fact that a single question routinely pulls from three of the nine areas at once, so a student with one weak area loses marks in questions that look like they are about something else.

This page is written to be useful before you book anything. It sets out the paper structure, the Core and Extended decision with its consequences for sixth form, the topic-by-topic map of where marks actually go, what the non-calculator paper demands, how Cambridge's command words behave, and the entry calendar counted backwards using Cambridge's own published March 2027 dates. Lessons for Dubai families run one-to-one on live video in Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, as that is a service we run only in India.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-maths-0580-tutor.programmesIntro: 0580 is a decision point rather than an endpoint. What your child does in the two years after it determines which tier and which grade actually matter, so the routes are worth seeing side by side now.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
programmes.description: A two-year course examined by two written papers in a single series, tiered as Core or Extended, with no coursework. Core caps at grade C and covers the core subject content. Extended covers that plus additional content and opens the full A* to E range. The subject content runs across nine topic areas, and questions routinely combine several of them, which is why a narrow revision plan built topic by topic underperforms a mixed one.
programmes.countryNote: British-curriculum schools account for the largest single share of Dubai's private-school enrolment, so 0580 or its Pearson equivalent is the maths qualification most Year 11 students in the emirate are working towards. Tier decisions are usually taken by the school late in Year 10 or early in Year 11, and in Dubai that conversation often happens at the same time as a sixth-form application, which is why it is worth raising with the department early rather than waiting.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics 0606
programmes.description: A separate qualification sat alongside 0580 by students who have already covered the Extended content. It introduces differentiation, integration, kinematics, binomial series, logarithms and vectors, which makes it the only IGCSE-level course that teaches calculus. Two written papers, no coursework, grades A* to E. It is demanding and it is optional, and it only makes sense for a student who is already secure at Extended level rather than one who is being stretched into it.
programmes.countryNote: Not every Dubai school offers 0606, and some offer it only to a set within the top maths group. Where a school does not run it, families occasionally look for external entry, which depends on finding a centre in the emirate that accepts private candidates for the subject and series. That is a question for the centre, and availability changes, so it should be checked rather than assumed.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level Mathematics
programmes.description: The most common sixth-form destination for an Extended 0580 student in a Cambridge school. The jump is real: algebraic fluency has to be automatic, because the new content assumes it rather than teaching it. Students who arrived at an A Level maths classroom with a grade 6 equivalent and shaky rearranging spend the first term fighting Year 10 algebra while new material accumulates on top of it.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the practical constraint is often the sixth-form entry requirement rather than the content. Many schools in the emirate set a specific grade in Extended mathematics as the gate for A Level Mathematics, and a Core entry closes that door before the exam is sat. If A Level maths is the plan, the tier conversation is the important one and the grade conversation comes second.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation
programmes.description: For students moving from a British-curriculum Year 11 into an IB Diploma, which is a common move in Dubai given how many schools offer both. Analysis and Approaches is the algebra-and-proof route and assumes Extended-level fluency; Applications and Interpretation is modelling-led and statistics-heavy. Both carry an internally assessed exploration, which is the first piece of extended independent mathematics most students ever write.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, three of them International Baccalaureate, so the number of local Diploma places is rising. For a Year 11 student finishing 0580, the useful preparation over the summer is not Diploma content but the algebra the Diploma assumes: rearranging, indices, functions and surds, all of which are already on the Extended syllabus.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-maths-0580-tutor.subjectsIntro: The 0580 subject content is organised into nine topic areas. These are them, with what each one is actually examined on and the specific place marks go missing in a Dubai Year 11 cohort.

subjects.name: Number
subjects.description: Integers, fractions, decimals, percentages, ratio, standard form, bounds, indices and surds at Extended. The highest-frequency loss on the whole syllabus is reverse percentage: students multiply by 0.8 to undo a 20% increase. Upper and lower bounds are the second, because a question asking for the maximum of a quotient needs the largest numerator with the smallest denominator, and most students take both maxima.

subjects.name: Algebra and Graphs
subjects.description: Manipulation, expansion, factorising, linear and quadratic equations, simultaneous equations, inequalities, sequences, functions and graph sketching, with more function work at Extended. This is the topic that silently costs marks everywhere else, because a geometry or mensuration question that ends in an equation is lost at the rearranging step rather than at the geometry.

subjects.name: Coordinate Geometry
subjects.description: Gradient, midpoint, length of a line segment, the equation of a straight line and parallel and perpendicular conditions. Short and well-rewarded if the formulae are automatic. The recurring error is the perpendicular gradient: students take the reciprocal and forget the negative, which turns a two-mark answer into zero with no partial credit available.

subjects.name: Geometry
subjects.description: Angle properties, polygons, congruence, similarity, circle theorems and constructions. Circle theorems are learnable in a fortnight and are among the most predictable marks on the paper. The loss is almost always the reason, not the answer: a correct angle with no named theorem beside it does not earn the method mark in a question asking for a reason.

subjects.name: Mensuration
subjects.description: Perimeter, area, surface area and volume of standard and compound solids, arcs and sectors, and similar shapes with area and volume scale factors. The scale-factor rule is the classic: students apply a linear factor to a volume. Compound solids lose marks to premature rounding, because an intermediate value rounded to two decimal places propagates into a final answer outside the accepted range.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.description: Right-angled trigonometry, Pythagoras, bearings, and at Extended the sine and cosine rules, area of a triangle and trigonometry in three dimensions. Bearings are the single most reliable source of lost marks in Dubai cohorts, because a three-figure bearing measured clockwise from north is a convention that has to be practised rather than understood. Three-dimensional questions fail at the diagram, not the calculation.

subjects.name: Transformations and Vectors
subjects.description: Reflections, rotations, translations, enlargements including negative and fractional scale factors, and vector arithmetic and magnitude at Extended. Describing a transformation fully is the whole skill: a rotation needs angle, direction and centre, and a student who writes 'rotation 90 degrees' has given one of three required pieces of information and will be marked accordingly.

subjects.name: Probability
subjects.description: Single and combined events, tree diagrams, Venn diagrams and relative frequency, with conditional and without-replacement cases at Extended. Without replacement is the recurring error: the denominator has to change on the second branch, and a surprising number of otherwise strong students keep it fixed. Tree diagrams are worth drawing even when the question does not ask for one, because they generate method marks.

subjects.name: Statistics
subjects.description: Averages from lists and tables, grouped data, bar charts, pie charts, scatter diagrams and lines of best fit, with cumulative frequency, box plots and histograms with unequal intervals at Extended. Histograms with unequal class widths are the examiner's favourite discriminator, because frequency density has to be calculated rather than read, and students plot frequency instead.

subjects.name: Examination Technique for 0580
subjects.description: Not a topic area, and arguably the highest-yield thing to teach. Showing method so partial credit is available, respecting three-significant-figure accuracy unless told otherwise, keeping unrounded values in the calculator between steps, and reading the command word before starting. A student can gain a grade on technique alone without learning a single new piece of mathematics.
