sections.heading: The four papers, and which two your child actually sits
paragraphs: 0580 has four question papers and every candidate sits exactly two of them, decided by the tier the school enters. Core candidates sit Papers 1 and 3. Extended candidates sit Papers 2 and 4. Each paper carries half the grade, and there is no coursework or internally assessed component anywhere in the qualification. That structure is simple and it is routinely misunderstood, usually because a family has read about a different syllabus.

The important feature of the structure, and the one that changed for recent cohorts, is the calculator split. Within each tier, one paper is sat without a calculator and the other with one. For a student who has grown up with a calculator in reach since Year 7, the non-calculator paper is a genuine shock, and it is the paper where the gap between understanding mathematics and being able to execute it shows most clearly. Preparation for it is a separate activity from revision, and it has to start months before the series rather than weeks.

The two papers also reward different behaviours. The shorter, more structured questions are a test of breadth: a student needs something from almost every topic area and cannot afford a blank. The longer multi-step questions reward persistence and method-writing, because a student who cannot complete a part can still collect method marks for a correct approach, and one who writes nothing down collects nothing. The single most common avoidable loss in the whole subject is a student doing correct work in their head or on a calculator and leaving no trace of it on the page.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the decision that sets the ceiling before anybody revises
paragraphs: This is the most consequential conversation of the Dubai IGCSE maths year and it is often had late, quietly and by the school alone. Core and Extended are not difficulty settings on the same exam. They are different papers with different content, different durations and different grade ranges, and the entry fixes which one your child sits. A Core entry means the highest grade available is a C, whatever happens in the room.

That ceiling has a downstream consequence Dubai families care about more than the grade itself. Sixth-form mathematics, whether Cambridge A Level or IB Analysis and Approaches, assumes the Extended content as its starting point, and schools in the emirate commonly set an Extended grade as the entry requirement for A Level Mathematics. A Core entry therefore closes a sixth-form door in Year 10 or early Year 11, before any revision has happened and often before the family has realised a decision was taken.

None of which means Extended is automatically right. A student who is genuinely insecure with core algebra after a full year of teaching will do worse on Extended papers than on Core ones, and a confident C is a better outcome than a scattered E. The honest test is specific rather than general: by the end of Year 10, can the student rearrange a formula with the subject appearing twice, handle negative and fractional indices, solve a pair of simultaneous equations including one non-linear case, and factorise a quadratic without being told which method to use? Those four are the gate. If three of the four are secure, Extended is the right entry and the fourth is a term's work.

If you disagree with the school's tier recommendation, the productive approach is evidence rather than argument. Bring a marked mock, ask which specific questions drove the decision, and ask what performance between now and the entry deadline would change it. Entries have a deadline, and Cambridge publishes it for every series; once the entry is submitted, changing it is an administrative process with its own cut-off, so the conversation has to happen before that date rather than after the next mock.

sections.heading: Where 0580 marks are actually lost, topic by topic
paragraphs: Marks in this subject do not disappear randomly. The same handful of errors recur across cohorts and across years, and most of them are conventions rather than mathematics: a bearing measured from the wrong reference, a transformation described incompletely, a rounding carried out one step too early. That consistency is useful, because it means a tutor can predict where to look before seeing a single piece of your child's work, and it means a marked past paper tells you far more than a conversation does.

The table below maps the recurring loss in each of the nine topic areas. Read the third column as a checklist to run against your child's last mock. If three or more of those errors appear, the diagnosis is not that your child does not understand mathematics; it is that nobody has taught them the examination conventions 0580 operates under. That distinction changes the whole support plan, because convention errors are fixable in weeks and genuine content gaps are not.

Two patterns cut across every row. The first is premature rounding. Cambridge expects answers to three significant figures unless the question says otherwise, and the accepted range for a final answer assumes unrounded intermediate values. A student who writes down 4.47 halfway through a multi-step mensuration question and then uses it will produce a final answer outside the range and lose the accuracy mark while having done the mathematics correctly. The habit to build is keeping the full value in the calculator and rounding once, at the end.

The second is invisible method. On the longer paper, a student who reaches a wrong final answer with visible correct method keeps most of the marks, and a student who reaches the same wrong answer with nothing written down keeps none. Dubai students who have come through systems that reward neatness are frequently the worst offenders, because they do their working on a separate scrap and transcribe only the answer. Retraining that is unglamorous, takes about three sessions, and is worth more marks than any topic on the syllabus.

sections.heading: The paper with no calculator, and why it needs its own preparation
paragraphs: Of the two papers your child sits, one does not permit a calculator. For most Dubai students this is the harder of the two, not because the mathematics is more advanced but because fluency they have never needed is suddenly load-bearing. A student who reaches for a device to work out seven times twelve is not weak at mathematics; they are untrained in arithmetic, and that is a specific, closeable gap that nobody closes by revising topics.

What the non-calculator paper actually demands is a short list. Times tables to twelve, without hesitation. Fractions of all four operations, including mixed numbers. Converting between fractions, decimals and percentages in both directions. Squares to fifteen and the cubes and roots that recur. Multiplying and dividing by powers of ten. Simplifying surds at Extended. Long multiplication and division as written methods rather than as estimates. None of that is conceptually difficult, all of it is trainable, and in a Dubai Year 11 the fastest grade movement available is often here rather than in any topic area.

The training looks different from ordinary tutoring and parents sometimes resist it, because ten minutes of arithmetic at the start of a session feels like a waste of an expensive hour. It is the opposite. Arithmetic fluency is the thing standing between a student and the marks they already understand how to earn, and ten minutes a session for a term produces a different candidate. It also has a second effect worth knowing about: students who can compute reliably check their own work, and students who cannot do not, which is where the careless-error complaint actually comes from.

There is a mirror-image problem on the calculator paper that deserves naming. Students who rely on a calculator for everything often cannot tell when its answer is wrong, because they have no estimate to compare it against. A mistyped value produces an absurd answer, and the student writes it down. Teaching estimation before calculation, so that a rough answer exists before the exact one, catches that whole class of error. It costs nothing and it is almost never taught.

sections.heading: Command words, and the habits of a Cambridge mark scheme
paragraphs: 0580 questions are written in a controlled vocabulary, and each instruction carries an obligation. 'Work out' and 'calculate' ask for a value and expect visible working. 'Show that' is a different task entirely: the answer is already printed, so no credit exists for producing it, and the marks live wholly in the steps between the start and the stated result. A student who writes the given answer confidently and nothing else has scored zero on a question they could do. 'Explain' and 'give a reason' require words, and in geometry they require the name of a theorem. 'Write down' signals that no working is expected and that the marks are small. 'Sketch' permits a freehand shape with correct features; 'draw' expects accuracy.

Reading the command word before starting is the cheapest skill on this page and the least practised. In a marked mock it is usually visible immediately: the student has calculated beautifully on a question asking for an explanation, or written an essay on a question asking them to write down an answer. Both lose marks for reasons that have nothing to do with mathematical ability, which is why the first thing a diagnostic session does with a mock script is sort the losses by cause rather than by topic.

The mark scheme has habits worth understanding too. Method marks exist independently of the answer, so a correct approach with an arithmetic slip inside it keeps most of the credit. Answers are generally expected to three significant figures unless the question specifies otherwise, with exact forms accepted where the question asks for them. Follow-through credit means a wrong value carried correctly into a later part can still earn marks there, which is a strong argument for never abandoning a question after a mistake. And units matter: a question that specifies centimetres squared will not credit an answer in the wrong unit however correct the number.

A boundary worth stating plainly, because this market contains providers who cross it. Cambridge's syllabuses, specimen papers, past papers and mark schemes are its own copyright material. A tutor should reference them, cite the official URL and work from what a student's school has legitimately provided. A tutor should not distribute them as downloads, and nobody can show you an unreleased paper or a boundary for a series that has not been graded. If a provider offers either, that is not an advantage they have found; it is a reason to walk away.

sections.heading: The Cambridge calendar counted backwards, with a worked example
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Dubai schools overwhelmingly use the June series for Year 11. The thing almost nobody tells parents is how early the fixed dates sit relative to the exam, and how little flexibility exists once they pass.

The clearest published illustration is Cambridge's own key dates for the March series, which exists for schools in certain regions and is useful here purely as a worked example of the gap between entry and exam. For March 2027, Cambridge publishes an examination period of 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries due on 27 November 2026, forecast grades due on 27 February 2027, results released on Direct on 13 May and certificates issued in late June. Read that order again: the entry deadline falls more than two months before the first paper. Whatever tier your child is entered for is decided before the exam term has really begun.

There is a second administrative fact that costs families every year. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and it states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. A parent who downloads a timetable from a search result rather than from their school is taking a risk for no reason. Ask the exams officer which zone your centre sits in and get the timetable from them.

For completeness, Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November series, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so dates can be revised, which is why the practical rule for both boards is the same: link the live official timetable, do not rely on a date copied onto a page.

sections.heading: 0580, 0607, 0980 and 4MA1: four maths qualifications in one Dubai year group
paragraphs: A Dubai Year 11 friendship group can easily contain students sitting four different mathematics qualifications, and they compare revision with each other constantly. That is actively harmful, because the papers behave differently and advice does not transfer. Knowing which one your child is entered for is worth more than any revision resource.

0580 is Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics, tiered Core and Extended, reported on the A* to G scale. 0980 is the same subject content reported on the 9 to 1 scale, which schools choose for alignment with UK GCSE reporting; the teaching is identical and only the grade labels differ, which matters when a sixth form states its entry requirement in one scale and the certificate arrives in the other. 0607 is Cambridge International Mathematics, a different syllabus with its own structure, a graphics calculator expectation and an investigation element, often chosen by schools running the IB continuum because its style sits closer to Diploma mathematics. A student entered for 0607 who revises from 0580 past papers is preparing for the wrong examination.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, code 4MA1, is tiered Foundation and Higher rather than Core and Extended, and its paper structure differs from 0580's. Pearson also offers Further Pure Mathematics at this level, code 4PM1, which like Cambridge's Additional Mathematics reaches into calculus. Both boards are widely used across Dubai schools and a family moving between schools mid-course can genuinely change board, which is one of the more disruptive things that happens in a Year 11 maths classroom here.

The practical instruction is short. Find the statement of entry. Read the code and the tier. Match every past paper, revision guide and tutor to that exact code. If the code on the entry does not match what the class has been taught from, raise it with the department immediately and in writing, because entries have deadlines and the window to correct a mismatch is not open indefinitely.

sections.heading: After 0580: what the grade and the tier actually buy
paragraphs: The 0580 grade is used for three things in the UAE and it is worth knowing which of them your family is actually aiming at, because they have different thresholds. The first is sixth-form entry at your own school or another in the emirate, where the requirement is typically a specific grade in Extended mathematics for A Level Mathematics and a lower grade for other subjects. The second is the eventual Ministry of Education equivalency file, if your child will apply to a UAE university. The third is the algebraic foundation the next two years assume, which has no threshold at all and is the one that determines whether sixth form goes well.

On equivalency, the published British-track requirement is specific and worth getting right, because at least one ranking competitor publishes it incorrectly. Students on the British track must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among those five, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. That is the published rule as reported in July 2026. Equivalency is a Ministry process that families complete through the official channel; it is not something a tutoring provider performs, and no tutoring is required for it.

On the foundation question, the honest answer is that the grade matters less than which skills are secure underneath it. Two students can arrive at the same grade with completely different profiles: one with reliable algebra and weak statistics, another with the reverse. The first will cope with A Level or Analysis and Approaches and the second will struggle from the first fortnight, because sixth-form mathematics assumes algebraic fluency and teaches almost none of it. If sixth-form maths is the plan, the summer between Year 11 and Year 12 is better spent on rearranging, indices, surds and functions than on anything labelled as a head start.

One final thing worth saying out loud, because the alternative is implied everywhere in this market. No tutor can promise a grade, a tier change or an admission, and anybody who does is selling you something they cannot deliver. What support can honestly offer is a diagnosis you can check, work marked in your child's own hand, and a plan with dates on it. If the marks move, the marked papers will show it before any report does.

process.title: Send the code, the tier and the last marked paper
process.description: The enquiry asks for three things: the syllabus code from the statement of entry, the tier, and your child's most recent marked mock or class assessment. Those three make a first session diagnostic instead of exploratory, and the third is worth more than any description of the problem.

process.title: A free trial session spent on the script
process.description: The trial goes through the marked paper with your child, question by question, sorting the lost marks into causes: not known, known but misapplied, arithmetic, rounding, misread command word, out of time. No card details are taken and there is one trial per family.

process.title: You get the loss breakdown in writing
process.description: After the trial you receive a count of marks lost against each cause, the two topic areas carrying the most, and what the tutor would work on in the first four sessions. If most of the losses are conventions rather than content, the note says so, because that is a much shorter piece of work.

process.title: Pick the shape and fix the slot
process.description: Weekly through Year 10 and 11, a diagnostic block from a mock, timed-paper practice at the weekend, or a short pre-series intensive. The slot is fixed in Gulf Standard Time with the same tutor, and a full Extended paper needs a two-hour window, which usually means a weekend.

process.title: Work set, marked and returned in your child's own hand
process.description: Between sessions there is exam-style work, and it comes back annotated: where the method mark was available, where the accuracy mark went, what the command word asked for. The marking is the deliverable. A session that only talks about mathematics leaves nothing behind to check.

process.title: Review against the next mock, not against feeling
process.description: The plan is reviewed when the next school assessment is marked, by comparing the loss breakdown to the previous one. That is a measurable thing, it is produced by the school rather than by us, and it is the only honest way to tell whether the hours are working.

whyPoints.title: The syllabus code drives the match
whyPoints.description: Matching starts from 0580 and the tier rather than from the word maths. A tutor who has taught Extended Papers 2 and 4 knows which questions are built from three topics and how the non-calculator paper behaves, which a strong general mathematician may not.

whyPoints.title: Marked work is the evidence, not a progress feeling
whyPoints.description: Every fortnight there is exam-style work marked in your child's own hand with method marks identified. You can read it, challenge it and take it to the school. Nothing on this site asks you to take progress on trust when a marked script exists.

whyPoints.title: Cambridge material is cited, never redistributed
whyPoints.description: Syllabuses, specimen papers, past papers and mark schemes are Cambridge's copyright material. We link the official pages and work from what your school has legitimately provided. No provider can show you an unreleased paper or a grade boundary for an ungraded series.

whyPoints.title: No grade promises, in writing or in conversation
whyPoints.description: No tutor can promise a specific grade, a tier change or a university place, and nothing here implies otherwise. What is on offer is a diagnosis you can check against a marked script and a plan with dates attached to it.

whyPoints.title: Examination convention is taught as content
whyPoints.description: Three-significant-figure accuracy, rounding once at the end, naming a theorem in a reason, describing a transformation fully, showing method so partial credit exists. These are taught deliberately, because they are worth more marks than most topics on the syllabus.

whyPoints.title: Delivery is stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Sessions for UAE families are one-to-one on live video in Gulf Standard Time. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; that service exists only in India. No page here implies a tutor will arrive at a Dubai address, because none will.

faqs.question: Which two papers does my son sit if the school has entered him for Extended?
faqs.answer: Papers 2 and 4. Extended candidates sit those two and nothing else, each carrying half the grade, with no coursework anywhere in the qualification. One of the two does not permit a calculator and the other does, so the preparation for them is genuinely different rather than more of the same. Core candidates sit Papers 1 and 3 on the same calculator split. Check the statement of entry rather than assuming, and confirm durations and mark totals in the syllabus for his exam year on cambridgeinternational.org, since syllabuses are revised between cohorts.

faqs.question: Why is there a paper that does not allow a calculator, and how do we prepare for it?
faqs.answer: Because arithmetic fluency is part of what the qualification examines, and for most Dubai students it is the harder of the two papers. Preparation is a separate activity from topic revision and the list is short: times tables to twelve without hesitation, all four operations with fractions including mixed numbers, converting between fractions, decimals and percentages both ways, squares and the common roots, multiplying and dividing by powers of ten, and simplifying surds at Extended. Ten minutes at the start of each session for a term produces a noticeably different candidate, and it also teaches the student to notice when an answer is absurd.

faqs.question: Which 0580 topics cost a Dubai cohort the most marks?
faqs.answer: Bearings, histograms with unequal class widths, reverse percentages, upper and lower bounds in a quotient, and full descriptions of transformations. Those five are conventions rather than concepts, which is why they recur: nobody forgets how to do them, because nobody was taught them explicitly in the first place. Underneath all of them sits algebra, which costs marks in other topics rather than its own. A geometry question that ends in an equation is usually lost at the rearranging step, and a term spent on rearranging repairs marks across the whole paper.

faqs.question: My daughter understands the maths but keeps losing method marks. What is happening?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly invisible working. On the longer paper, a student who reaches a wrong answer with correct visible method keeps most of the marks, and one who reaches the same answer with nothing written down keeps none. Students who have come through systems that reward neat presentation are the worst affected, because they work on scrap paper and transcribe only the final answer. The fix takes about three sessions of enforced line-by-line working on the script itself. It is unglamorous and it is worth more marks than any single topic on the syllabus.

faqs.question: What does 'show that' require that 'work out' does not?
faqs.answer: On a 'show that' question the answer is already printed, so there is no credit available for producing it. Every mark lives in the steps between the starting point and the stated result, which means a student who writes the given answer confidently and nothing else scores zero on a question they could do. 'Work out' and 'calculate' ask for a value and expect visible working. 'Write down' signals that no working is needed and the marks are small. 'Explain' and 'give a reason' need words, and in geometry they need a theorem named rather than described.

faqs.question: When is the entry deadline, and can the tier be changed after the school submits it?
faqs.answer: Entry deadlines sit far earlier than families expect. Cambridge's published key dates for the March 2027 series show final entries due on 27 November 2026 against an examination period of 3 February to 4 March 2027, so the entry closes more than two months before the first paper. Changing an entry after submission is an administrative process with its own cut-off, handled by the school's exams officer with Cambridge, not something a family does directly. The practical consequence is that any disagreement about tier has to happen before the entry date, with a marked mock in hand.

faqs.question: What is a Cambridge administrative zone and why does the timetable version matter?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, and each zone has its own version of the timetable. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. That is a real risk a parent can create at home by downloading a timetable from a search result. Ask the exams officer which zone your centre is in and take the timetable from the school, then diarise from that document only.

faqs.question: How many past papers should a Year 11 get through before the June series?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families think, marked far better than most families manage. Three full papers sat under correct timing with the right calculator rules, each one marked line by line and then reworked, teaches more than a dozen papers done untimed and self-marked against an answer. The value is in the marking, because that is where the cause of each lost mark becomes visible. A sensible pattern in the final term is one timed paper a fortnight with a marking session attached, rather than a pile of scripts nobody has read properly.

faqs.question: The school has entered my son for Core and we think he should be on Extended. What can we do?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends on two things: whether the school agrees the student can cope with the extra content, and whether the entry deadline has passed. Entries carry the tier, so the window is set by Cambridge's published dates rather than by anybody's willingness. The test the department will apply is specific: can the student rearrange a formula where the subject appears twice, handle negative and fractional indices, solve non-linear simultaneous equations and factorise a quadratic unprompted? Bring a marked script, ask which questions drove the recommendation, and ask what evidence would change it.

faqs.question: Is there any advantage to sitting 0580 in the November series rather than June?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs IGCSE examinations in a June series and a November series, and Dubai schools overwhelmingly use June for Year 11 because it aligns with the school year and with sixth-form entry. November is mainly useful as a resit opportunity or for a student whose circumstances disrupted the June series. It is not a soft option: the same syllabus, the same standard, and a candidate sitting in November is revising through a term when their classmates have moved on. Any change of series is a conversation with the school's exams officer rather than a family decision.

faqs.question: My son has six weeks until the paper. What is the most useful thing to do now?
faqs.answer: Stop learning new content and start converting partial knowledge into whole marks. In six weeks the highest-yield work is the predictable material: circle theorems answered with a named theorem, histograms with unequal widths, bearings as three-figure values clockwise from north, reverse percentages, bounds, and full descriptions of transformations. Alongside that, one timed paper a week, marked properly, with the losses sorted by cause. Six weeks is genuinely enough to move a grade on technique alone, and it is not enough to teach a topic area that was never understood.

faqs.question: Does the exam give a list of formulas, or does my child memorise them all?
faqs.answer: Cambridge specifies in the syllabus which formulas are provided in the question paper and which candidates are expected to know, and that list differs by tier and has changed between syllabus versions. Do not rely on what an older sibling remembers. Download the syllabus for your child's examination year from cambridgeinternational.org, find the formula section and build the memorising list from it. Then test it cold rather than by recognition, because a formula a student can pick out of a list is not a formula they can produce in a sealed room.

faqs.question: Can my child sit Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics as a private candidate in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it has to be arranged with a centre rather than assumed. Some examination centres in the emirate accept private candidates for some subjects and series, and some do not; availability, deadlines and fees are set by the centre, and the entry still has to be submitted within Cambridge's published deadline for that series. The practical route is to contact centres directly, well before the entry date, and to ask specifically about the syllabus code and tier you need. It is not something a tutoring provider arranges on your behalf.

faqs.question: Does a Dubai school's inspection rating tell me anything about its maths teaching?
faqs.answer: A little, and less than parents hope. KHDA oversees the quality of private education in Dubai and inspects schools on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. An inspection report describes teaching and attainment across phases and subjects at the point of inspection, which is useful context about a department over a year group. It tells you nothing about your own child's position in their set, which teacher they have, or whether the tier recommendation they have been given is right. For that, the marked script is the only document that helps.

faqs.question: How does an IGCSE maths grade feed into the Ministry of Education equivalency file?
faqs.answer: On the British track, the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among those five, plus either one subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. That is the rule as published in July 2026. Equivalency is a Ministry process completed through the official channel; no tutoring provider performs it or guarantees it, and no tutoring is required for it. Verify the current requirement on the Ministry's own site before relying on it.

intro.heading: The hourly rate is the least useful number in this decision
paragraphs: A Cambridge IGCSE online tutor in Dubai will quote you somewhere inside a very wide band, and the band is real. Tutopiya lists online tuition from about AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. Unitors lists IGCSE tuition from AED 150. TutorChase lists AED 270. BartyED lists a premium tier at AED 650. Bestimate's Dubai rate table for 2026 puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and specialist exam-level support at AED 200 to 450 and above. Those were read from the providers' own pages in October 2026, they belong to those providers rather than to us, and not one of them tells you what you actually need to know.

What you need to know is which hours to buy. Two families can spend AED 7,200 across a Cambridge IGCSE year and get completely different results, not because one paid more per hour but because one spent the money on content revision in a subject where the loss was technique, and the other spent it on question-level marking of the two components that were actually bleeding marks. The hourly rate is a unit of selling. Marks recovered per hour paid is the unit that matters, and nobody in this market publishes anything about it.

Cambridge IGCSE is unusually well suited to being costed this way, because its assessment is modular in structure and public in detail. Each syllabus is a defined set of components with published mark schemes, and the losses on each behave differently. Practical and alternative-to-practical papers give marks back cheaply, because the failures are procedural and repeat. Extended-response marks are expensive, because they need a habit built rather than a fact learned. Multiple-choice papers sit in between and are frequently the most over-tutored thing in the whole course.

The series you sit is a money decision too, and almost nobody treats it as one. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with a March series as well. Entry deadlines sit months before the papers: for the March 2027 series, final entries were due 27 November 2026 and the exam period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027. A family deciding in January to prepare properly for March is working inside a decision somebody made in November, and a budget written without that knowledge is a budget written for the wrong window.

So this page is a set of priced decisions rather than a rate card. It prices the kinds of hour available to you. It ranks Cambridge component types by how cheaply their marks come back. It costs the series choice and the resit scenario. It compares a group of four against one-to-one at the same monthly spend. And it says what online delivery removes from the bill and the two things it adds, because pretending it adds nothing would be a sales claim rather than a number.

One structural fact, early, because it governs every table below. Tuition for UAE families is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Travel is the single largest hidden component inside an in-home hourly rate in this emirate, and removing it is why the online bands quoted on this page sit below the in-home ones rather than beside them.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-online-tutor.programmesIntro: Cambridge IGCSE sits inside a longer sequence of spending, and the per-hour rate changes at each boundary. The notes below describe what each stage costs a Dubai family and why, so a two-year Cambridge budget is not built by borrowing from the years where specialist rates are genuinely needed.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary (Years 7-9)
programmes.description: The cheap years. There is no external entry, no syllabus code and no mark scheme, so tutoring here is habit rather than specification: written stamina, showing working, reading a question properly. Cambridge runs Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, which gives a Dubai family an external reference point without an exam-year price tag attached to it.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai families who spend modestly in Year 9 on working-out discipline and question-reading tend to spend substantially less in Year 11, because the technique losses that cost a grade at IGCSE are the same losses, formed earlier and cheaper to fix. The usual mistake is to wait for a Year 10 report, by which point the same fix costs three times as many hours.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE (Years 10-11)
programmes.description: Two years, defined components, published mark schemes and grades reported A* to G. This is the stage where cost per mark can actually be calculated, because you can see which component lost what and what the mark scheme rewarded. It is also where tiering decisions carry a price: a late switch between Core and Extended wastes work that had already been paid for.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools enter Cambridge subjects alongside Pearson ones, sometimes inside the same school, so the first spend in Year 10 should confirm what is actually on the statement of entry. A term of tutoring aimed at the wrong board's paper format is the single most complete waste available in this market, and it happens most often to mid-year arrivals.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The expensive years, and the stage where the AED 200 to 450 specialist band starts to look like value rather than markup. Subject depth rises, hours per subject rise with it, and the number of subjects falls. Entry requirements are stated in IGCSE grades, so the Year 11 result is also an admissions document rather than only a report.
programmes.countryNote: Expect the per-hour rate to roughly double at the IGCSE-to-A-Level boundary in Dubai. That is the arithmetic reason to buy the qualified tier rather than the specialist tier through Years 10 and 11: the specialist budget has a job waiting for it, and spending it early does not make it available twice.

programmes.name: UAE Ministry of Education equivalency
programmes.description: On the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.
programmes.countryNote: This matters to a budget because a Dubai school may enter nine or ten Cambridge subjects while the equivalency count is five. A family with limited hours should know which subjects are carrying the equivalency load and which are carrying the sixth-form requirement, because those two sets are not identical and the overlap is where the money belongs. Verify your own case on moe.gov.ae; no provider performs equivalency on your behalf.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: Marks come back at different prices in different Cambridge subjects, because the components differ. The notes below say, per subject, where the recoverable marks usually sit for a Dubai student, which is the information a budget needs.

subjects.name: Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: The cheapest subject to improve per hour paid, because method marks are itemised and recoverable independently of understanding. A Dubai student who can do the maths and loses marks for unshown working is buying back marks at the lowest rate available in the whole course. Ask for marks separated into method and accuracy before buying anything.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics 0606
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by students aiming at A Level mathematics. Expensive per mark because the content genuinely has to be learned rather than tidied, and because the cohort is small enough that tutor supply is thinner. Worth buying only when the A Level target is already named by the school.

subjects.name: Physics 0625
subjects.description: Two cheap mark pools and one expensive one. Graph work, units and significant figures come back in two or three sessions. The practical or alternative-to-practical paper is similarly procedural. Six-mark extended responses are expensive and should be bought last, not first.

subjects.name: Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Moles calculations are the cheapest recoverable marks in the subject and the most commonly mis-taught; organic mechanisms are mid-priced; the qualitative analysis content on the practical paper is cheap and almost nobody revises it. A session plan that does not name which of the three it is targeting is not a plan.

subjects.name: Biology 0610
subjects.description: Command-term discipline is the whole economy of this subject. Describe, explain, compare and suggest earn different marks, and students who know the biology lose marks answering the wrong verb. That is a cheap fix with a fast return and it is where a limited biology budget should go first.

subjects.name: English First Language 0500
subjects.description: Assessed against objectives rather than right answers, so marks come back through redrafting rather than through content. Expensive in calendar time, cheap in hours: two sessions a month across a year beats a block, because each redraft needs a gap to be worth anything.

subjects.name: English Literature 0475
subjects.description: Where coursework exists, the hours are spent on planning and on feedback against the student's own drafts rather than on content delivery. Mid-priced per mark. Keep every draft dated; the sequence is both the record of teaching and the record of authorship.

subjects.name: Economics 0455
subjects.description: Definition and diagram marks are usually already held by Dubai students; the evaluation marks on extended responses are usually unclaimed entirely. That makes the subject look cheap and behave expensively, because evaluation is a habit. Budget a term, not a block.

subjects.name: Business Studies 0450
subjects.description: Case-study application is the subject, and generic answers are the standard loss. The fix is cheap and rarely taught: marking an answer with the stimulus detail that should have been used highlighted beside it. Two or three sessions move it; a term of content revision does not.

subjects.name: Computer Science 0478 and ICT 0417
subjects.description: Theory and practical components pull apart sharply, and a student can be secure in one and lost in the other. Confirm which component the marked work came from before agreeing any plan, because a folder of theory questions says nothing about practical performance.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-online-tutor.regionsIntro: Where a family lives in Dubai does not change the published rate card, but it changes the slot you can hold and therefore the price you end up paying for the same teaching. These notes are about that, not about geography.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Early school finishes make a 4pm start realistic, which is the cheapest hour in the Dubai week because almost nothing competes for it. Families here more often have a named sixth-form grade target, which makes the cost-per-mark calculation concrete rather than abstract.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and Jumeirah Lakes Towers
regions.note: Sessions land at 6.30pm or later, which is the expensive end of the evening for identical teaching. This cluster also has the widest gap between in-home and online rates in the emirate, because an in-home tutor crossing Sheikh Zayed Road at that hour prices the journey into the fee.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches, Dubai Hills and Mudon
regions.note: Long bus runs mean many Year 11 students are not at a desk before 4.45pm. Buying one sustainable weekly hour beats buying two that keep moving, because a cancelled session costs the full fee in opportunity and delivers nothing against the mark.

regions.name: Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Qusais
regions.note: Mixed boards within a short radius, so households often carry Cambridge and Pearson entries at once. The first money here should go on confirming syllabus codes from the statement of entry, because paper formats differ and a term aimed at the wrong one is a total loss.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Dubai Hills
regions.note: A dense cluster of British-curriculum schools, which means the same Cambridge mock papers recur. A tutor who has already marked that paper reaches a question-level diagnosis in session one rather than session three, and diagnostic hours are the ones families most resent paying for.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: University proximity keeps the AED 45 to 150 tier genuinely well supplied here, which is why this is the part of Dubai where the permit question matters most before money changes hands. Cheap and permitted are not mutually exclusive, but they should both be checked.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai and Business Bay
regions.note: Apartments, late finishes and frequent family travel. Blocks timed to a mock window tend to work better than year-round weekly slots here, because the weekly slot gets cancelled and the cancelled hour is the most expensive hour there is.

regions.name: The Springs, The Meadows and Jumeirah Park
regions.note: Settled communities where a fixed slot survives a whole term, which is the condition under which cost per mark actually improves. Consistency is a discount nobody prices: twelve sessions delivered beat eighteen booked and nine attended.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha, Dubai Hills and Umm Suqeim
schoolClusters.note: British-curriculum schools entering Cambridge syllabuses heavily, often alongside Pearson ones in different departments. Requests from this cluster usually arrive with a school-marked mock attached, which shortens diagnosis to one session and lowers the total hours a family needs to buy.

schoolClusters.city: Mirdif, Al Warqa and Dubai Silicon Oasis
schoolClusters.note: A mixed-board belt where Cambridge, Pearson and other curricula sit within a few kilometres. Households here frequently need the statement of entry checked first, because sibling assumptions carry across schools and paper formats do not.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai Marina, JLT and Al Sufouh
schoolClusters.note: Apartment communities with a high share of mid-year arrivals. The budget question that comes from here most often is whether to fund two subjects lightly or one properly, and the honest answer usually depends on which components are losing the marks rather than on which subject feels weakest.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-online-tutor.modesIntro: Three ways of buying Cambridge IGCSE support, each with a different cost shape. The right one depends on how many components are losing marks and how much calendar you have left before the series your child is actually entered for.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one across a term
modes.description: One fixed hour a week for twelve weeks, which is the shape that gives the lowest cost per mark recovered on technique losses. The feedback loop closes weekly, the same component can be re-tested, and the price per hour sits at whatever the qualified tier charges rather than at the premium an urgent block attracts. This is the default for Year 10 and the first half of Year 11.
bullets: Lowest cost per mark on method, units, graph work and command terms
The same component revisited after the fix, to show it held
A session note naming the paper, the component and the question numbers
Twelve weeks is nine or ten real sessions; budget against the real number

modes.title: Marked-paper blocks before a series
modes.description: Three to six sessions built around whole papers sat under timed conditions and marked question by question against the published mark scheme. Higher weekly spend, lower total, and it is the only format that reliably shows a parent what changed. It suits the weeks between a mock and the real series, and it stops when the series starts.
bullets: Whole timed papers rather than question sets
Marks recorded per question, not per paper
Targets the component the mock actually exposed
A defined end date; no rolling commitment

modes.title: Single-component repair
modes.description: The smallest useful purchase: two or three sessions aimed at one named component, usually a practical or alternative-to-practical paper, a graph-and-data weakness or a command-term problem. Cheap, fast, and frequently the only thing a family actually needs. It is also the honest answer when a parent is being sold a year.
bullets: One component named from the mock, nothing else
Two or three sessions, then stop and re-test
Often the best value purchase in the entire course
Scoped and priced in writing before the first session

sections.heading: What a Cambridge IGCSE online tutor in Dubai costs, by the kind of hour you are buying
paragraphs: Published market rates in Dubai run from about AED 33 an hour at the platform end to AED 650 at the premium end, with Cambridge IGCSE work mostly sitting between AED 150 and AED 300. Every figure here was read from the provider's own public page in October 2026 and belongs to that provider; none is an IB Gram price. We publish them because three of the six best-ranking pages for this search publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which no Dubai family pays tuition in.

The useful cut is not by tier but by what the hour does. A diagnostic hour, a teaching hour, a marking hour and a timed-paper hour produce completely different things and do not need the same person. A capable postgraduate at the lower band can supervise a timed paper perfectly well. Marking against a published Cambridge mark scheme at question level needs someone who knows the scheme. Teaching a six-mark extended response needs the most expensive hour in the list, and a term that spends every hour at that rate is a term that overpaid for supervision.

The table below sets out those four kinds of hour with the market band that can actually deliver each and roughly how many a term needs. Read it as a shopping list rather than a rate card. Our own quote depends on the subject, the components in play, the number of sessions and whether the work is weekly or a block, which is why there is no single number on this page. The trial lesson, one per family and requiring no card, exists so the first conversation is about which hours you need rather than about an invoice.

sections.heading: Cost per mark: which Cambridge components give the money back
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE marks are not uniformly priced. Some losses are procedural, repeat identically across papers, and close in two or three sessions; others are habits that take a term to build. A family with twelve hours to spend will get two or three grades more movement by starting at the cheap end of that list than by starting with the subject that feels most frightening. Almost every Dubai family does the opposite, because fear is a worse guide than a marked paper.

The cheap pools are consistent across subjects. Unshown working in mathematics. Units and significant figures in the sciences. Graph construction, axis labelling and reading values off a line. The practical or alternative-to-practical papers, where the failures are procedural and the content is narrow. Command-term mismatch, where a student who knows the biology answers 'describe' with an explanation and loses the mark for a reason nobody has ever told them. All of those close fast and stay closed.

The expensive pools are also consistent. Extended-response questions where marks depend on structure and on sustained reasoning. Evaluation marks in economics and business, which require a habit of weighing rather than a fact. Data-analysis questions that need interpretation rather than calculation. These are worth buying, and they are worth buying second. sections.heading: Choosing a series is a money decision, and the deadline came first
paragraphs: Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, and also offers a March series. Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests run in March, May and October. Which series your child sits determines how many weeks of tutoring the plan can contain, and because entry deadlines sit months before the papers, the window was effectively fixed before most families started thinking about it.

The March 2027 series is the clearest illustration available, and the dates are Cambridge's own. The exam period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027. Final entries were due 27 November 2026. Forecast grades are due 27 February 2027. Results reach centres on Direct on 13 May, with certificates in late June. Read backwards, that means a family wanting a properly planned March run needed the decision made in the autumn, and a family deciding in January is buying a compressed block at block prices rather than a term at term prices.

One administrative point has a genuine cost attached. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Get the timetable from your school's exams officer rather than from a search result, and check it against the statement of entry. This is the cheapest risk control in the whole process and it costs one email.

sections.heading: Resits priced honestly, including the ones that are not worth doing
paragraphs: A resit is the most emotionally driven purchase in this market and the one where families overspend most reliably. The question is never simply whether a grade can improve. It is whether the improvement arrives before the thing it was needed for, and whether the subject is one of the five that the equivalency count or the sixth-form offer actually depends on. Those two questions settle most resit decisions in about ten minutes and save a great deal of money.

The mechanics matter. A resit means a fresh entry in a later series, which means a fresh entry deadline sitting months before the paper. If results arrive in August and the sixth form has already made its offer conditional on a grade, a November attempt may land after the decision point and a following June attempt certainly will. Ask the school two things before buying any tutoring: what the deadline for the next series is, and whether the offer holder will wait. Both answers are free.

Where a resit is worth doing, the tutoring shape is different from a first attempt. The content was taught once already, so the money goes almost entirely into question-level marking and timed papers rather than into teaching. That is a cheaper mix than a first run, and a provider quoting you a full course for a resit is quoting the wrong product. sections.heading: Same monthly spend, different product: one-to-one against a group of four
paragraphs: Monthly packages are how this market actually sells, and the published examples are worth knowing. Packages seen in Dubai include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240 to 600 at the budget tier, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-tier and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. All read October 2026, all theirs rather than ours.

Set a fixed monthly figure against the options and the comparison becomes concrete. At roughly AED 800 a month a Dubai family can buy about four one-to-one hours at the qualified tier, about eight hours in a group of four, or around two hours at the specialist tier. Those are not three versions of the same thing. Four one-to-one hours can produce three marked papers and a measured movement on one component. Eight group hours can cover a lot of content and will produce almost no per-student marked work.

The rule that falls out of this is simple enough to apply without a spreadsheet. If the loss is content, groups are decent value. If the loss is technique, which for Cambridge IGCSE it usually is, groups are poor value at any price, because technique losses are individual and only visible on that student's own paper. Most Dubai families buy groups for a technique problem and then conclude that tutoring does not work.

sections.heading: What online removes from the bill, and the two things it adds
paragraphs: Online delivery removes travel, and in Dubai travel is not a small line. An in-home tutor crossing the city for a 6.30pm session is pricing forty to ninety minutes of unpaid movement into the hourly rate, which is most of the gap between Bestimate's in-home band of AED 180 to 350 and the online bands published by the platform-tier providers. It also removes the second journey: the one where a family drives a child to a tuition centre at exactly the hour Dubai traffic is at its worst.

It removes something less obvious too, which is the local supply constraint. A Cambridge Chemistry 0620 specialist does not have to live within a twenty-minute drive of your community to take a 5pm Gulf Standard Time booking. For thinly covered subjects such as Additional Mathematics or Computer Science, that is the difference between a specialist and whoever was available, and the cost of whoever was available is a wasted term rather than a lower rate.

It adds two things, and a page that pretended otherwise would be selling rather than costing. The first is equipment: a reliable connection, a device with a decent camera, headphones, and ideally a graphics tablet or a document camera for mathematics and the sciences, so working can be seen rather than described. That is a one-off household cost, not a per-session one. The second is supervision: somebody has to make sure the timed paper was actually timed and unaided. In an in-home arrangement the tutor does that; online, a parent does, and it takes about two minutes a week. Families who skip it lose the value of every timed-paper hour they paid for.

sections.heading: Nine subjects entered, five that count: budgeting by subject role
paragraphs: A Dubai school may enter a student for nine or ten Cambridge subjects. No family tutors nine subjects, and the ones that try spread the money so thinly that nothing moves. The allocation question therefore has to be answered before the rate question, and there is a defensible way to answer it that almost nobody uses: sort the subjects by what each one is actually for.

Three roles exist. Some subjects are carrying the UAE equivalency count, which on the British track requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not included among the five. Some are carrying a sixth-form entry requirement, published by the school and usually subject-specific. Some are carrying neither and are there for breadth. Those three sets overlap but are not the same, and the overlap is exactly where a constrained budget belongs.

Work it out on one sheet of paper. List the entered subjects. Mark which five are intended to carry equivalency. Mark which ones the Year 12 courses your child wants actually require, and at what grade, which the school publishes. The subjects marked twice get the money. The subjects marked once get attention if there is budget left. The subjects marked neither get none, and a parent who can say that out loud has already saved more than any discount in this market will give them. The whole exercise takes about fifteen minutes and needs no subject knowledge at all.

sections.heading: Package terms: the five questions that decide whether a cheap quote is cheap
paragraphs: Two providers quoting AED 200 an hour can be selling arrangements that differ in real cost by half. The difference is never in the headline. It is in the session length behind the hourly figure, the cancellation window, whether marking time is billed, whether the quote includes VAT, and what happens to unused sessions in a monthly package. Those five questions take one message to ask and they are the whole of the diligence most families need to do.

Two of them deserve expanding. On tax, limit the question to whether the figure quoted to you includes VAT; no page should be stating the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees as settled fact without a Federal Tax Authority citation, and anyone quoting you a ruling is going beyond what they can support. On anything described as free, ask what the condition is: how long the trial runs, who is eligible, whether a card is required, and whether it is one per family or one per subject. A condition stated up front is a term; a condition discovered later is a price increase.

There is a sixth question that is not about money and should be asked anyway. Lead forms for tutoring collect personal data about a minor, and the UAE has a personal data protection law, Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021. Ask what is collected, why, and how to have it deleted. Nobody needs your child's school, grades and photograph in a web form in order to arrange a trial lesson, and a provider who cannot answer that question has not thought about it.

sections.heading: What a Cambridge IGCSE quote should state before you pay it
paragraphs: Five things go in writing before the second session: the session length and the rate for it, the number of sessions being committed to, which components the work is targeting, the cancellation and rescheduling terms, and whether the quoted figure includes VAT. A quote that cannot survive being written down is not a quote. This is not an adversarial step; any competent provider will send it in one message, and the ones who will not have told you something useful.

Ask one more question that has nothing to do with price and everything to do with legality. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service, 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

Keep two distinctions straight while you are asking. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a document about premises and not a statement about teaching quality; an online provider does not hold one and should not imply it does. And in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, while the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat that as press-reported and check the current ADEK document; the practical reading is that hiring your child's own teacher is the wrong move regardless of what it costs.
