sections.heading: How these lessons run, and what this page will not claim
paragraphs: Sessions are one-to-one, live, over video, on a shared screen with a writing surface both people can use, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time against your child's own school calendar. The material is your child's own paper, the published Cambridge mark scheme for it, and the statement of entry that says which components actually apply. IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and the cost consequence of that is set out in the tables above rather than hidden behind a convenience argument.

We do not reproduce or supply Cambridge syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides. We reference them and point to cambridgeinternational.org, because reproducing them is a copyright matter and for unreleased material a malpractice one. We publish no IB exam or results date anywhere on this site, because the IB's own site blocks automated verification; confirm those with your school's coordinator. Cambridge and Pearson dates are quoted with the source's framing and should still be checked against the live official timetable your centre holds for its zone.

We hold no approval, accreditation, licensing or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and we operate no premises in the UAE. We make no promises about any grade, publish no satisfaction percentage and show no star rating, because none of those can be checked by the person reading them. A tutor here teaches, questions and gives feedback on the student's own work, and does not produce assessed work for any subject at any price. And if no suitable tutor is free for a Cambridge subject in the window you need, we will say so and say when that changes rather than filling the slot and billing for it.

process.title: Get the statement of entry
process.description: From your school's exams officer. It names the Cambridge syllabus codes, the components inside each and the tier where tiering applies. Spending money before you have it risks tutoring the wrong board's paper format, which is the most complete waste available in this market.

process.title: Send the most recent marked mock
process.description: Marked, ideally with marks recorded per question. A marked paper itemises the losses, which is what makes a cost-per-mark conversation possible. A description of the problem does not, and a first session spent discovering what a document would have shown is a session you paid for twice.

process.title: Take the trial lesson, then read the diagnosis
process.description: One lesson at no charge per family, no card required. Judge it on the written output: does it name components and question numbers, with the cheap losses separated from the expensive ones? That document is what you are deciding on, not the hour itself.

process.title: Buy the cheap marks first
process.description: Practicals, working-out discipline, units, graph technique and command terms, in that order. Two or three sessions each, re-tested afterwards. Expensive marks such as evaluation and extended response come second, when the easy ground has already been taken.

process.title: Put the five terms in writing
process.description: Session length, rate, session count, target components, cancellation terms and the VAT position, in one message before the second session. Ask separately about the MoHRE private tuition work permit. None of this is adversarial and all of it takes five minutes.

process.title: Re-test the component at six weeks
process.description: Sit the same component again under timed conditions and compare marks per question. If it moved, continue. If it did not and the sessions ran, change the target rather than the budget. If half the sessions were cancelled, change the slot instead.

whyPoints.title: Priced by component, not by a headline rate
whyPoints.description: Cambridge IGCSE is assessed through defined components with published mark schemes, which makes cost per mark calculable. We rank component types by how cheaply the marks come back, so a limited budget is spent in the order that actually moves a grade.

whyPoints.title: Every figure has an owner and a date
whyPoints.description: Each AED band on this page names the provider that published it and the month we read it. Three of the six best-ranking competitor pages for this search publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which no Dubai family pays tuition in.

whyPoints.title: The series calendar treated as a budget input
whyPoints.description: Cambridge entry deadlines sit months before the papers, and the March 2027 series shows the gap precisely. Knowing that changes whether you are buying a term at term prices or a compressed block at block prices, which is a larger difference than any hourly rate.

whyPoints.title: Delivery stated plainly, with the trade-off shown
whyPoints.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses; home visits are a service we run only in India. The tables say what that removes from a bill and the two things it adds, rather than only the flattering half.

whyPoints.title: Regulator and board facts cited, never worn as credentials
whyPoints.description: Cambridge timetable rules, MoHRE permit requirements, KHDA permissions and Ministry of Education equivalency are described with sources so you can verify them. We hold no approval or partnership from any of them and operate no premises in the UAE.

whyPoints.title: The authorship line is part of the service
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on the student's own work. Nobody here produces coursework or assessed work at any price, and keeping dated drafts is how a Dubai family can demonstrate that nobody did if the question is ever raised.

faqs.question: What does a Cambridge IGCSE online tutor in Dubai cost per hour?
faqs.answer: Published market rates in Dubai span roughly AED 33 to AED 650, with Cambridge IGCSE work mostly between AED 150 and AED 300. Tutopiya lists from AED 33-52 and EdFlik from AED 45-65 at the platform end; Unitors lists IGCSE tuition from AED 150; TutorChase lists AED 270; BartyED lists AED 650. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table puts specialist exam support at AED 200-450 and above. All read October 2026, all those providers' figures rather than ours. The more useful question is which kind of hour you need, because supervision, marking and teaching do not require the same tier.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge IGCSE paper gives me the most marks back per dirham?
faqs.answer: The practical or alternative-to-practical paper, almost every time. The content is narrow, the failures are procedural - apparatus naming, variable control, table headings, reading a scale - and students rarely revise it because it feels unexaminable. Two or three sessions typically close most of the available loss and it stays closed. After that, working-out discipline in mathematics, then units and graph technique in the sciences, then command-term accuracy. Extended-response and evaluation marks are worth having and should be bought last, because they need a habit built across a term rather than a procedure learned in a session.

faqs.question: Is the March series cheaper to prepare for than June?
faqs.answer: Only if the decision was made early. Cambridge's March 2027 series runs 3 February to 4 March 2027 with final entries due 27 November 2026, so a family that decides in the autumn can buy a term at term rates. A family deciding in January is buying a compressed block, which costs more per week even at the same hourly rate because the hours are concentrated and the slot is scarce. June gives the longest runway and usually the lowest total cost. Check which series your centre actually enters before planning anything; it is not a free choice for most Dubai students.

faqs.question: How much does it cost to resit one Cambridge IGCSE subject?
faqs.answer: Less than a first attempt, if it is bought correctly. The content was taught once already, so the tutoring mix shifts almost entirely to question-level marking and timed papers rather than teaching, which is typically a four to six session block rather than a term. A provider quoting a full course for a resit is quoting the wrong product. Before buying anything, ask two free questions: what the entry deadline for the next series is, and whether the sixth form holding the offer will wait for the result. If the answer to the second is no, the resit may not help.

faqs.question: At AED 800 a month, is a group of four better than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what is losing the marks. Around AED 800 buys roughly four one-to-one hours at the qualified tier or about eight to ten hours in a small group, using published market rates read in October 2026. If the problem is content coverage, the group is decent value. If the problem is technique, which for Cambridge IGCSE it usually is, the group is poor value at any price, because technique losses are individual and only visible on that student's own marked paper. Most families buy a group for a technique problem and then conclude tutoring does not work.

faqs.question: What does online tutoring save compared with a tutor who travels in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Mostly travel, which is a large hidden component of any in-home rate here. A tutor crossing the city for a 6.30pm session is pricing forty to ninety minutes of unpaid movement into the hour, and Bestimate's in-home band of AED 180-350 sits above the online bands largely for that reason. It also removes the family's own drive to a centre at the worst traffic hour, and it removes the local supply limit for thinly covered subjects. It adds a one-off equipment cost and about two minutes a week of parent supervision on timed work.

faqs.question: My child is entered for nine Cambridge subjects. How many should we tutor?
faqs.answer: Two, usually, and never nine. Sort the entry by role first. Five subjects are carrying the UAE equivalency count, which on the British track requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count. Some subjects are carrying a published sixth-form entry requirement. Some are carrying neither. The subjects in both the first two groups get the money; the rest get attention only if budget remains. A parent who can name the subjects that nothing downstream depends on has already saved more than any discount will give them.

faqs.question: Does a monthly tutoring package in Dubai work out cheaper than paying per hour?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the variable is expiry. Packages advertised in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. The arithmetic only works if the sessions are used, and a Dubai term reliably delivers nine or ten of twelve weeks once school events, travel and illness are counted. Ask what happens to unused sessions. A package of eight that expires monthly against a household that realistically runs six is a higher effective rate than paying per hour, dressed as a discount.

faqs.question: Should a Dubai tutoring quote include VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask whether the figure quoted to you includes it, and get the answer in writing. That is the correct scope of the question. Nobody should be stating the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees as settled fact without a Federal Tax Authority citation, and a provider offering you a confident ruling on the general position is going beyond what they can support. What matters commercially is narrow and answerable: is the number you were given the number that appears on the invoice. Put it in the same message as session length, session count, target components and cancellation terms.

faqs.question: What equipment do we need at home for Cambridge IGCSE online lessons?
faqs.answer: Less than families expect, and it is a one-off rather than a recurring cost. A reliable connection, a laptop or tablet with a usable camera, and headphones with a microphone, which matter more than the camera because mishearing a number wastes minutes. For mathematics and the sciences a cheap graphics tablet or a phone propped as a document camera is worth having, so working can be seen rather than described. A quiet room and a desk the student can write on complete it. No subscriptions, no software purchases and no specialist hardware are needed.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to start Cambridge IGCSE tutoring in Year 10 than in Year 11?
faqs.answer: Substantially, because Year 10 is where the cheap marks live and where there is time to test that a fix held. Procedural losses - unshown working, units, graph construction, command-term mismatch - cost the same to fix in either year, but in Year 10 the same component can be re-sat twice before it counts. Year 11 compresses everything into the weeks between the first mock and a series whose entry deadline has already passed, and compressed work is bought at block rates. If a Year 10 report shows the same grade across several subjects, that is technique, and it is the best-value purchase in the course.

faqs.question: Does a practical paper need separate tutoring, and what does it add?
faqs.answer: It needs separate attention and it adds very little to the bill, which is why it is the most underused purchase in this market. Whether a school enters the practical paper or the alternative-to-practical version, the assessed skills are procedural: naming apparatus, controlling variables, headings and units in a results table, reading a scale, identifying a source of error. Students almost never revise it. Two or three sessions typically recover most of the available marks and the gain holds across series. Confirm from the statement of entry which version your child actually sits before planning any of it.

faqs.question: How many hours does it take to move from a C to a B in Cambridge IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Nobody can answer that honestly as a number of hours, and anyone who does is guessing in front of you. What can be answered is which losses are available and how expensive each is to close. A C with secure content and procedural losses can move in a handful of sessions, because the marks are sitting in working-out, units and graph technique. A C with real content gaps takes a term, because the content has to be rebuilt in sequence first. Which of the two you have is a question for a marked paper, and it is the output the trial lesson is supposed to produce.

faqs.question: What happens to the cost if my child needs two subjects instead of one?
faqs.answer: It does not quite double if the subjects are sequenced rather than run in parallel. Two subjects taught simultaneously means two weekly slots, two sets of marked work and roughly twice the spend. Two subjects sequenced - single-component repair in the first, then the second - often costs around a third less in total, because each block is short and targeted and the student is not carrying two new habits at once. Sequencing works where both losses are procedural. Where both subjects have content gaps, parallel is unavoidable and the budget has to reflect that honestly.

faqs.question: Do I pay for the time a tutor spends marking my child's paper?
faqs.answer: Ask, because the answer varies and it changes the real rate. Three arrangements exist in this market. Marking is billed separately, which is transparent but raises the total. Marking is included outside the session, which is the best value if it genuinely happens. Or marking is done inside the session, which means you paid a teaching rate to watch someone read. The third is the common one and the most expensive. Put the question in the same written message as session length and cancellation terms, and ask to see one anonymised marked sample so you know what you are paying for.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-online-tutor.closingHeading: Decide which hours to buy before deciding what to pay for one
dubai/cambridge-igcse-online-tutor.closingBody: The useful order is documents, diagnosis, cheap marks, then expensive ones. Ask the school for the statement of entry and the correct zone timetable. Send the most recent marked mock. Take the trial lesson, which is one per family and needs no card, and judge it on the written diagnosis that follows: which components are losing marks, and which of those losses are cheap. Then buy the cheap ones first and re-test at six weeks. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and the rate, session count, target components, cancellation terms and VAT position go in writing before a second session is booked.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-physical-science-0.tutorsIntro: Tutors here teach chemistry and physics together, which is what a 0652 entry requires. Before anyone quotes you an hourly figure, the useful conversation is about how many hours the specific problem needs, because the hours matter more to your total than the rate does.

intro.heading: The rate is the small question. The hours are the big one
paragraphs: Parents comparing 0652 tutors in Dubai almost always compare hourly rates, because that is the number providers put in front of them. It is the wrong number to optimise. A tutor at AED 180 an hour who needs twenty-four sessions to fix a problem costs more than a tutor at AED 300 an hour who fixes it in eight, and the second one also returns your Year 11 evenings. The question that actually decides your total is how many hours the specific weakness needs, and that question can only be answered after somebody has looked at a marked script.

Here are the market numbers so the page is not coy about them. Read in October 2026 from published UAE rate cards and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table: budget online tutoring runs AED 45 to 150 an hour, a qualified subject tutor online runs AED 150 to 300, a tutor who travels to your community runs AED 180 to 500 once the drive is accounted for, an IGCSE and A Level specialist runs AED 200 to 450 and above, and premium named tutors reach AED 500 to 650 and above. Monthly packages advertised in Dubai cluster around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. None of those are IB Gram prices. They are the market you are shopping in.

0652 has a specific effect on where in those bands a quote lands. It is chemistry and physics in a single award, which means the tutor must hold both at IGCSE depth, and it is a smaller entry in Dubai than Coordinated Sciences 0654 or the separate sciences. Smaller entry means fewer tutors who have taught the exact paper structure recently, and scarcity prices upward. It also means something more useful: fewer sessions, in many cases, because there are two sciences to cover rather than three.

On the phrase in the URL. Home visits in Dubai are not something IB Gram sells, and no tutor will be sent to a UAE address; that is a service we run only in India. This page therefore does the honest thing with the home-tutoring question rather than ignoring it: what the in-home market charges, what the drive costs in time as well as money, and where the trade actually sits for a family in Dubai South or on the Palm. Our delivery across the Emirates is one-to-one teaching over live video, in Gulf Standard Time.

The rest of the page is arranged by cost rather than by syllabus. What AED 1,000 buys four different ways, the extras nobody budgets for, why the exam calendar moves the price, and what money cannot buy at any rate. If you want the syllabus content and the marking detail instead, that is on the pages for the online and the general 0652 searches.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-physical-science-0.programmesIntro: Cost per year is not flat across a British-curriculum pathway. These are the four stages where Dubai families spend on science support, and where the spending is and is not worth it.

programmes.name: Year 9: the cheapest intervention point
programmes.description: Short, targeted work on calculation fluency, graph work and practical write-ups. A handful of sessions here is the least expensive useful tutoring available in the whole pathway, because the habits being installed are the ones that later decide IGCSE marks and nothing has to be unlearned yet.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools generally fix science routes and tiers in the spring term of Year 9, so this is also the only point at which a modest spend can change which qualification a child sits. Families who spend nothing here and a great deal in Year 11 are the standard pattern in this city, and it is the expensive way round.

programmes.name: Year 10: maintenance, not rescue
programmes.description: Where most of the 0652 content is taught. Sensible spending is low and regular: a weekly or fortnightly session keeping pace with the school's sequence, with marked written work in between. Expensive Year 10 tutoring usually means either a content gap from Year 9 or a tier that was set optimistically.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai evenings in Year 10 are crowded, because Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run alongside the licensed curriculum as KHDA requires in every private school in the emirate. A short weekly marked task beats a long session nobody has time to prepare for, and it costs less.

programmes.name: Year 11: where the budget actually goes
programmes.description: Mocks, predicted grades and the exam series. Spending peaks here and is most often misallocated: general science tutoring where one block was weak, or an expensive spring intensive where an autumn practical block would have done more for less.
programmes.countryNote: Rates in this market rise with demand as the June series approaches, and the most contested slots in Dubai are weekday evenings between 5pm and 8pm. Families who book the same work in October rather than April pay less for it and get more use from it, because the skills carry through the mocks as well.

programmes.name: Resits and private candidates
programmes.description: A November or March series retake, sat through a school or as a private candidate at a registered exam centre. The tutoring is usually short and focused, but the surrounding costs — entry fees, centre administration, sometimes a different exam board timetable — are real and sit entirely outside any tutoring quote.
programmes.countryNote: Entry fees in the UAE are set by the exam centre rather than by Cambridge, and they vary by centre and by series, so the only reliable figure is the one your centre quotes you in writing. Ask about late-entry surcharges at the same time, because they are where resit budgets usually break.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-physical-science-0.subjectsIntro: Not every 0652 topic costs the same to fix. Below, each block is paired with the realistic size of the job, because that is what determines your total rather than the rate on the advert.

subjects.name: Units, prefixes and standard form
subjects.description: Usually two to three sessions and the best value on the whole syllabus. A student who is shaky here reads as weak in both chemistry and physics, and families regularly buy a term of science teaching when the actual problem was milli, kilo and powers of ten.

subjects.name: Balancing equations and writing formulae
subjects.description: Two to four sessions. Low glamour, high return: every quantitative chemistry mark downstream depends on a balanced equation appearing when the question does not ask for one. Skipping this and starting at stoichiometry is the commonest wasted spend in 0652 chemistry.

subjects.name: The mole, reacting masses and concentration
subjects.description: Four to six sessions, and the single largest line in most 0652 budgets. Charged twice because the content appears in both the multiple-choice and the theory paper. Worth paying for properly; not worth paying for before the units and equations work is done.

subjects.name: Electrolysis and electrode products
subjects.description: Two to three sessions if taught as a rule. Much longer if the student has memorised one worked example, because every variation the examiner introduces then has to be learned separately. Ask a prospective tutor which of those two approaches they use.

subjects.name: Rates, energetics and reversible change
subjects.description: Two to four sessions. Mostly graph reading and explanation structure rather than new content, so it overlaps with the data-technique work and is cheaper when bought alongside it than as a standalone block.

subjects.name: Acids, bases, salts and periodic trends
subjects.description: Two to three sessions. Salt-preparation questions are practical questions in disguise and reward a fixed sequence, so this block pairs efficiently with practical-component work rather than being bought separately.

subjects.name: Metals, fuels and air quality
subjects.description: One to two sessions. Cheap to fix because the marks go to naming specific substances rather than to understanding, and students usually see the pattern on their own marked script the first time it is pointed out.

subjects.name: Motion and graph interpretation
subjects.description: Three to four sessions. Gradient and area-under-graph work transfers directly into the practical component and into rate graphs in chemistry, so it is one of the few blocks that pays for itself twice within the same award.

subjects.name: Forces, moments and energy transfer
subjects.description: Two to four sessions. Diagram discipline is most of the job: distances measured from the pivot, forces labelled, energy transfers named rather than described loosely. Short sessions with marked practice suit this better than long ones.

subjects.name: Thermal physics, waves and sound
subjects.description: Two to three sessions. Ray diagrams with the normal drawn and particle-level explanations are the scoring behaviours, and both are quick to install. A common topic to drop from a plan when the budget is tight, and reasonable to drop if the marked script shows it secure.

subjects.name: Electricity, circuits and power
subjects.description: Four to six sessions and the biggest physics line in a 0652 budget. Systematic, repeatable question styles, so the money converts into marks reliably. Also the block most often left until the final weeks, when rates in this market are at their highest.

subjects.name: Magnetism and radioactivity
subjects.description: One to three sessions. Largely precision of language and systematic half-life working. Inexpensive, frequently overlooked, and a reliable source of marks on both papers for a student who has run out of budget for the larger blocks.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-physical-science-0.regionsIntro: What an in-home quote costs in Dubai depends heavily on where you live relative to the school belts and to where tutors actually live. These notes are about that geography, and about which communities pay the largest travel premium.

regions.name: Palm Jumeirah
regions.note: One access road and a single point of entry. A weekday evening visit means committing to the trunk in both directions, which is why in-home quotes for the Palm sit at the top of the AED 180 to 500 band regardless of the subject.

regions.name: Emirates Hills and Jumeirah Islands
regions.note: Low-density villa communities a long way from where most tutors live. The travel premium here is structural rather than negotiable, and families in this cluster are the most likely to find online delivery both cheaper and better matched.

regions.name: Dubai South and Expo City
regions.note: Furthest from the established school and tutoring belts. An in-home session can carry an hour of driving each way at the wrong time of day, and a tutor pricing honestly has to recover that somewhere.

regions.name: Al Khawaneej and Mushrif
regions.note: Villa areas with good school access but limited evening tutor supply nearby. Quotes here vary widely between providers, which usually reflects where the individual tutor lives rather than how good they are.

regions.name: Town Square and Mudon
regions.note: Large, newer family communities along the southern corridor. Session timing is dictated by the school run rather than by the student, and the realistic in-home start time is often later than parents want for an exam-year child.

regions.name: Jumeirah Golf Estates and Dubai Sports City
regions.note: Self-contained communities where a 60-minute visit routinely costs a tutor two hours door to door. Online removes that entirely, which is the clearest arithmetic in this comparison anywhere in the emirate.

regions.name: Nad Al Hamar and Ras Al Khor
regions.note: Well placed for several school belts and reasonable for travel, so in-home quotes here are closer to the middle of the band. Supply is still thinner for a chemistry-and-physics combination than for single-subject maths or English.

regions.name: Dubai Festival City and Al Jaddaf
regions.note: Central and well connected, with the shortest typical travel times of any cluster on this list. Even here, the premium exists: the drive is shorter, not absent, and the tutor pool is still limited to who can reach you.

The useful question in this cluster is not the rate but the number of sessions, because that is where the variation actually is.

sections.heading: What AED 1,000 buys four different ways
paragraphs: Hourly rates make options look comparable when they are not. A more useful exercise is to fix the spend and ask what each route delivers for it. Take AED 1,000, which is roughly a month of weekly support at the mid-market online band, and look at what four different routes produce for that money on a 0652 problem.

Spent on one-to-one online teaching at the qualified-tutor band, AED 1,000 buys something in the region of four to six hours of teaching plus the marked work in between. Spent on an in-home tutor at the published in-home band, it buys perhaps two to five hours, of which part of the value is the convenience of not organising anything. Spent on a tuition centre group class it buys considerably more contact time, shared with other students moving at one pace. Spent on past papers and a parent willing to mark honestly against the published mark scheme, it buys nothing at all, because the papers are free from the school and the mark scheme does the work.

That last row is not a joke and it belongs in any honest costing. A student with secure content, decent timing and no practical preparation does not need a tutor; they need four weeks of timed papers marked properly. Tutoring earns its money where something has to be diagnosed and taught, and the diagnosis is the part parents cannot do themselves because it requires knowing which lost mark belongs to which cause.

sections.heading: The three questions that should come before any quote
paragraphs: A provider who gives you an hourly rate before asking anything has told you nothing about your total. Three questions, asked in this order, turn a rate into a cost.

First: how many sessions, and against what target? A quote of AED 250 an hour means nothing until somebody commits to roughly how many hours the problem needs and what should look different afterwards. An honest answer sounds like four to six sessions on the mole with timed sets between, reviewed against the next school assessment. A dishonest answer sounds like we will see how it goes. Second: what is the session length and the per-hour effect of it? Ninety-minute sessions usually carry a lower effective hourly rate than sixty-minute ones because the setup is amortised, so the headline rate can be misleading in either direction.

Third: what comes back between sessions, and marked how? Marked written work against the published mark scheme is the part of a tutoring purchase that does the teaching when the tutor is not there, and it is also the only evidence you will have that the money is working. A provider charging a premium rate without returning marked work is charging for presence rather than progress. Ask what the marking looks like before the first paid session, and ask to see one marked piece after it.

A fourth, smaller one: VAT. This page does not state how UAE VAT applies to tuition fees, because that is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority's own guidance rather than for a tutoring site. What you should do is ask any provider whether a quoted AED figure is inclusive or exclusive, and have the answer in writing before you commit. Monthly package pricing is where this most often becomes a surprise.

sections.heading: The commute is a time cost before it is a money cost
paragraphs: The in-home premium gets discussed as a rate difference, which understates it. The real cost of a tutor driving to your community in Dubai is time, and most of that time is yours rather than theirs.

Consider a realistic weekday. School transport delivers your child home somewhere between 3.30pm and 4.30pm depending on the route. Activities, if any, run to 5pm or later. A tutor driving from where tutors tend to live to Dubai South, the Palm or Jumeirah Golf Estates between 5pm and 6pm is in the worst traffic of the week. The session therefore starts later than is ideal for an exam-year student, and it starts at whatever time the drive permits rather than at the time your child concentrates best. On a Year 11 evening with Arabic homework, Islamic Education and two other subjects also competing, that displacement matters more than the rate does.

There is a second-order cost that nobody quotes. A tutor committing two hours to deliver one can hold fewer slots, so the slots they do hold are the ones that fit their driving pattern. Families in outlying communities therefore get offered the leftover times. Online removes the whole structure: there is no travel on either side, a 90-minute booking is 90 minutes of teaching, and the slot is chosen for the student. During Ramadan, sessions move to post-Iftar timing without anybody renegotiating a drive.

Home visits in Dubai are not something IB Gram sells, so take the above as an argument rather than a neutral survey, and weigh it yourself. What should not be in dispute is the arithmetic: on a chemistry-and-physics combination, removing the drive-time constraint changes the pool of tutors you are choosing from. For a 0652 entry, which is smaller in this emirate than coordinated or separate sciences, that pool difference is the whole game.

sections.heading: The costs nobody budgets for
paragraphs: A tutoring quote is not the cost of getting an IGCSE grade. Several other things sit around it, and families planning a 0652 year are better off knowing about them in September than discovering them in February.

Exam entry is the first. Where a student sits through their school, the entry is handled in the school fees or billed separately depending on the school. Where a student sits as a private candidate — common for a resit — the entry goes through a registered exam centre, and the centre sets the fee rather than Cambridge. Those fees vary by centre and by series, which is why no honest page publishes a figure: the number that matters is the one your chosen centre quotes you in writing. Ask about late-entry surcharges in the same conversation, because missing a final entry deadline is the most expensive administrative error available in this process.

Then there are remarks and enquiries about results, requested through the school after results are issued and charged by the centre. Materials are usually modest but not zero: a scientific calculator the student is familiar with, a decent ruler and a protractor for graph and ray-diagram work, and printing if you want timed papers done on paper rather than on screen. Printing sounds trivial and is the one that actually recurs weekly.

Finally, the costs that are not invoiced. An expensive spring intensive bought because an autumn block was skipped. A term of general science tutoring bought because nobody read a marked script first. Sessions paid for in a week the student had three school assessments and no time to prepare. Those are the largest avoidable numbers in most Dubai tutoring budgets, and none of them appear on a rate card.

sections.heading: Why the calendar moves the price
paragraphs: Tutoring is a capacity business, and capacity in Dubai is not evenly spread across the year. A tutor with open slots in October is in a different position from the same tutor in April, when every Year 11 family in the emirate wants the same weekday evening. The content being taught has not changed. The price and the availability have.

Exam board deadlines explain most of the shape. Cambridge publishes key dates per series, and the pattern is instructive even when your child is sitting a different series. For the March 2027 series, Cambridge gives an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027, with final entries due 27 November 2026, forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results available on Direct from 13 May and certificates in late June. The entry deadline sits more than two months before the first paper. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE in May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

Two practical conclusions. First, decisions that cost money — a tier change, a resit entry, a move between codes — are governed by entry deadlines that fall long before the exams, so the planning window is autumn rather than spring. Second, Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Check the zone timetable through your school, every series, before building any revision plan around dates.

On IB dates, which come up because many Dubai families have children on both curricula: no IB exam or results date is published on this page, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and nothing in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. Ask your school's IB coordinator and use the date they give you.

sections.heading: Two sciences, not three: what that does to your total
paragraphs: 0652 covers chemistry and physics. Coordinated Sciences 0654 and Combined Science 0653 cover all three. The separate sciences cover one each, in more depth, across three entries. That difference has a direct effect on what a tutoring plan costs, and it cuts in two directions.

Upward, because the tutor has to hold both chemistry and physics at IGCSE depth and 0652 is a smaller entry in Dubai than the alternatives, so fewer tutors have taught the exact paper structure recently. Scarcity prices upward, and a provider who cannot find a genuine chemistry-and-physics tutor will offer a physics specialist who will cover the chemistry adequately and no better. That is the substitution to watch for, and the question that detects it is simple: which of the two sciences have you taught more recently at IGCSE, and to which tier?

Downward, because there is less content. A 0652 plan has two halves to diagnose rather than three, and in practice the quantitative work overlaps: unit handling, formula rearrangement, graph gradients and standard form all serve both halves. Fixing calculation discipline once improves marks in chemistry and physics simultaneously, which is why that block is consistently the best value on this syllabus. On a double award the same money has to stretch across a biology strand as well.

The net effect for most families is a plan of similar total cost to a 0654 plan but spent differently: a higher rate, fewer sessions, more of them concentrated on the quantitative spine. That is a better shape, because it front-loads the work that transfers across the award rather than spreading hours thinly across three sciences. It also makes the plan easier to check, since the quantitative gains show up on marked scripts within a few weeks.

sections.heading: Ramadan, summer and the rest of the Dubai year
paragraphs: The UAE academic calendar changes when tutoring is useful and when it is money spent for the look of it. A plan built without reference to it will book sessions in weeks where nothing can be absorbed.

During Ramadan, school hours shorten and the day reorganises around Iftar. Sessions move to post-Iftar timing, which works well and needs to be arranged rather than assumed; a tutor who cannot move the slot is a scheduling problem for the whole month. The weeks immediately before and after Eid are low-yield for new content and good for consolidation and timed practice. Summer, for a Dubai family, usually means travel across several time zones, which is workable online if the slot is agreed around the travel rather than against it. Summer is also the cheapest time to buy the units, equations and calculation-discipline work, because the content is not moving at school and nothing is urgent.

The term-time pattern matters too. Dubai schools run internal assessments at predictable points, and a week with three school assessments is a week where a tutoring session displaces revision the student actually needed to do. Pausing for that week costs nothing and preserves the value of the sessions around it. Any provider unwilling to pause for a school assessment week is optimising their calendar rather than your child's marks.

The one period that is genuinely worth paying a premium for is the run-up to the November mock, because that result feeds predicted grades and still leaves time to change the spring picture. If a budget only covers one concentrated block in the whole year, October and early November is where to spend it.

sections.heading: What money cannot buy on 0652
paragraphs: A page about cost should be clear about what is not for sale, because several things in this market are advertised as though they were.

A grade cannot be bought. No tutor can promise one on 0652 or on any other syllabus, and a provider offering a specific grade or a refund tied to a result is making a representation they cannot stand behind. What can be committed to is specific and checkable: which papers are being prepared for, what written work comes back marked, and a plain statement when a plan is not working.

Cambridge material cannot be bought from a tutor. Past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge; the legitimate route is cambridgeinternational.org and your child's school, which can supply what it is licensed to supply. A provider running a download library is distributing material it has no right to distribute, and that is a reason to be wary of everything else it tells you.

Assessed work cannot be bought. There is no coursework component on 0652, so the question arises less often here than on other qualifications, and the principle holds regardless: a tutor teaches, sets practice and marks the student's own work. Any offer to produce, draft or complete assessed work for a student is a malpractice exposure for the student, not a service.

And board or regulator standing cannot be bought. Nobody in private tutoring holds KHDA approval for tutoring, because a KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific instrument issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai — initial approval first, a maximum six-month window to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit and operates no UAE premises, which is exactly why this is an online service and why the page says so rather than letting you assume otherwise.

sections.heading: The cheaper routes, and when each is genuinely right
paragraphs: One-to-one tutoring is not always the correct purchase, and a page that pretended otherwise would be selling rather than advising. Four cheaper routes exist and each has a situation where it is the better answer.

School intervention sessions are already paid for. They come with laboratory access, which matters if your child sits the hands-on practical test, and with the teacher who sets the internal assessments. They are large, fixed in time, and not individually paced. For practical access and for catching up on recently taught material, they are the first thing to use and the most commonly under-used.

Group classes at a tuition centre are the cheapest contact hours available, sold as monthly packages. They work where a whole group shares the same gap, typically in general revision close to a series. They do not work for a 0652 student whose physics is solid and whose mole work is not, because a group moving at one pace cannot serve that. Self-study with past papers costs nothing beyond entry fees and is the right answer more often than the industry admits: a student with secure content and a timing problem needs timed papers marked properly, not teaching.

Finally, the sibling route. Most providers in this market price per student rather than per session, so two children on the same syllabus do not halve the cost, but a shared slot can still reduce the total where both are working on the same block. Worth asking about, worth being sceptical about if the two children are at different tiers, because a shared session at two different levels usually serves neither of them.

If one of those routes fits your situation, take it. The diagnostic session exists partly to establish which one you are in, and it is not unusual for the honest answer to be that no paid tutoring is needed this term.

process.title: Send the entry details and a marked script
process.description: The statement of entry gives the code, the tier and the practical paper number; the marked script shows where the marks are going. Between them they let a tutor estimate how many sessions a problem needs, which is the figure that decides your total rather than the hourly rate.

process.title: Diagnostic lesson at no charge
process.description: One per student, no card details taken. The session identifies which blocks are weak and why, and produces an estimate of sessions needed per block. Where the honest answer is school support plus marked past papers, that is what you are told, including when it means no purchase.

process.title: Get the plan and the number in writing
process.description: Sessions, target, session length, the rate at that length, whether the figure is VAT inclusive, what marked work returns each week, and the notice period if you stop. All of it before the first paid lesson rather than discovered along the way.

process.title: Teach, mark, review at the mock
process.description: Weekly or fortnightly teaching with a timed set in between, marked against the published Cambridge scheme. The plan is reviewed against the November mock rather than allowed to run, and continuing is a decision rather than a default.

process.title: Stop, change, or extend deliberately
process.description: Blocks end on a date. At the end, the marked scripts say whether the target was met, and the next decision is explicit: stop, change approach, or buy a new block with a new target. That is the single cheapest habit available to a tutoring budget.

whyPoints.title: Hours estimated before money is taken
whyPoints.description: You get an estimate of how many sessions a specific weakness needs, because that number drives your total far more than the hourly rate. An estimate can be wrong and will be revised in front of you; the absence of one is a warning sign.

whyPoints.title: Market figures with sources attached
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page is attributed to published UAE rate cards or Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table and dated October 2026. They describe the market you are shopping in, not an IB Gram price list, and they are there so you can argue with a quote.

whyPoints.title: No drive-time premium
whyPoints.description: Lessons run over live video, so there is no travel on either side and a 90-minute booking is 90 minutes of teaching. The slot is chosen for when your child concentrates, not for when a car can reach your community.

whyPoints.title: A tutor who holds both sciences
whyPoints.description: 0652 needs chemistry and physics at IGCSE depth in the same person. Matching online rather than by driving distance is what makes that possible, and we will tell you which of the two a tutor has taught more recently if you ask.

whyPoints.title: Blocks that end
whyPoints.description: Finite plans with a named target and a review date, rather than an open-ended weekly arrangement that renews quietly. Ending forces a judgement about whether the money worked, which is the point.

whyPoints.title: Clear about what is not for sale
whyPoints.description: No grade promises, no refund tied to a result, no Cambridge papers or mark schemes distributed by us, no assessed work produced for a student, and no claim to regulator or board approval. IB Gram holds no KHDA permit and has no UAE premises.

faqs.question: What is a fair hourly rate for 0652 tuition in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published UAE rate cards and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table, read in October 2026, put a qualified subject tutor working online at AED 150 to 300 an hour and an IGCSE or A Level specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above. A tutor travelling to your community sits in the AED 180 to 500 band. Because 0652 requires chemistry and physics in one tutor and is a smaller entry here than coordinated or separate sciences, quotes tend to sit in the upper half of the specialist band rather than the lower half.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper 0652 tutor actually cheaper overall?
faqs.answer: Often not, because your total is hours multiplied by rate and the hours vary far more than the rate does. A tutor at AED 180 who needs twenty-four sessions to fix a weakness costs more than one at AED 300 who fixes it in eight, and the second also returns two dozen Year 11 evenings. The useful comparison is not the rate but the estimate: ask each provider how many sessions, against what target, and treat an unwillingness to estimate as information about what you are buying.

faqs.question: Does a quoted AED rate for 0652 tuition include VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask, and get the answer in writing. This page does not state how UAE VAT applies to tuition fees, because that is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority's own guidance rather than for a tutoring site to interpret. What is reasonable to expect from any provider is a clear statement of whether a quoted figure is inclusive or exclusive, and a tax registration number if they hold one. Monthly package pricing is where the question most often becomes an unpleasant surprise rather than a detail.

faqs.question: Why is an in-home 0652 tutor in Dubai South quoted higher than one in Al Jaddaf?
faqs.answer: Distance from where tutors actually live, and the time of day you want. A weekday evening visit to Dubai South, the Palm or Jumeirah Golf Estates can mean an hour of driving each way in the worst traffic of the week, so a tutor committing two hours to deliver one has to recover that somewhere. Central communities like Al Jaddaf and Festival City carry shorter drives and quotes closer to the middle of the band. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses; lessons run over live video, which removes the premium entirely.

faqs.question: How many hours does it take to fix mole calculations for 0652?
faqs.answer: Four to six sessions with timed sets in between is the usual figure, provided two things are already in place: confident unit conversion and standard form, and reliable equation balancing. Where those are shaky, they come first and add two to five sessions, and skipping them is the commonest way a chemistry block produces no visible change. Because the mole appears in both the multiple-choice and the theory paper, this is the block where hours convert into marks most reliably on the Extended tier.

faqs.question: What should I spend first if the 0652 budget only covers six sessions?
faqs.answer: Calculation discipline and units, then whichever of the two sciences the marked script says is weaker. Units, prefixes and standard form are the cheapest fix on the syllabus and they lift chemistry and physics simultaneously, since both halves of 0652 rest on the same arithmetic. If the script shows method marks missing rather than wrong answers, that is a procedural fix worth more marks per session than any topic teaching. Six sessions spent that way outperform six spread across the whole award.

faqs.question: What does it cost to resit 0652 as a private candidate in the UAE?
faqs.answer: The entry fee is set by the registered exam centre rather than by Cambridge, and it varies by centre and by series, so the only reliable figure is the one your chosen centre gives you in writing. Ask at the same time about late-entry surcharges and about what the centre requires from a private candidate, particularly for the practical component. Tutoring for a resit is usually short and targeted, so the surrounding administrative costs can be a meaningful share of the total.

faqs.question: When is the cheapest time of year to book 0652 tutoring in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Summer and the early autumn term. Capacity is widest, rates sit at the lower end of each band, and the work that matters most — units, equation balancing, calculation discipline, the practical component — does not depend on where the school has reached. The most expensive window is February to May, when every Year 11 family in the emirate wants the same weekday evening slot. Identical work, bought six months apart, costs different amounts and delivers different value.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying more for a tutor who has taught the 0652 paper structure before?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the one premium on this syllabus that reliably earns itself back. 0652 is a smaller entry in Dubai than coordinated or separate sciences, so plenty of science tutors have never taught its exact paper structure and will substitute general chemistry and physics teaching instead. That costs you hours rather than quality. The question that detects it: which of the two sciences have you taught more recently at IGCSE, and to which tier? A tutor who answers specifically, and asks for the statement of entry, is worth a higher rate and fewer sessions.

faqs.question: Can two siblings share a 0652 session to halve the cost?
faqs.answer: Most providers in this market price per student rather than per session, so a shared slot reduces the total without halving it. It works where both children are on the same syllabus, at the same tier, and need the same block; it works badly where they are at Core and Extended respectively, because a session pitched between the two tiers serves neither. Ask what the per-student figure is for a shared slot, then compare it honestly against two shorter individual sessions.

faqs.question: Is a crash course before the exams worth the money for 0652?
faqs.answer: Only if the content is already broadly secure and the problem is timing, question order or technique. In that situation an intensive genuinely converts into marks. If whole topics are missing, an intensive is the most expensive way to discover that, because there is no time to teach them properly and the student spends the weeks before the papers feeling further behind. A diagnostic session before booking one is the cheapest insurance available against a four-figure mistake.

faqs.question: What costs sit outside the tutoring bill in a 0652 year?
faqs.answer: Exam entry, which the school bills or a registered centre charges for a private candidate; late-entry surcharges where a deadline is missed; remarks and enquiries about results, charged by the centre through the school; and small recurring material costs, mostly printing timed papers plus a calculator, ruler and protractor the student is familiar with. The largest uninvoiced cost is planning: a spring intensive bought because an autumn block was skipped, or a term of general tutoring bought because nobody read a marked script first.

faqs.question: Is online 0652 tutoring genuinely cheaper than a tutor who travels?
faqs.answer: On published market bands, yes: the online qualified-tutor band runs AED 150 to 300 an hour against AED 180 to 500 for a visit, and the gap is mostly the drive. The larger saving is not in dirhams. Removing the travel constraint means choosing a tutor who holds both chemistry and physics at IGCSE depth rather than whoever covers science within a weekday drive of your community, and on a smaller entry like 0652 that difference in matching is worth more than the rate difference.

faqs.question: Do I need to pay for a tutor at all if my child has school science support?
faqs.answer: Sometimes not, and a diagnostic session should tell you. School intervention sessions are already inside the fees you pay, come with laboratory access that matters for the hands-on practical paper, and are run by the teacher who sets the internal assessments. Where a student has secure content, reasonable timing and no practical preparation, the correct purchase is four weeks of timed papers marked properly, not a weekly tutor. Paid tutoring earns its money where something has to be diagnosed and taught.

faqs.question: What happens to the fee if we stop after two 0652 sessions?
faqs.answer: Ask before you start, because cancellation terms vary widely across this market and the differences are material. A reasonable arrangement has a stated notice period, no long tie-in, and no charge for sessions not yet taken. What to avoid is a package that commits several months at once without a clear exit, particularly where the sessions are being bought before a diagnostic has established what the plan should be. Get the terms in the same written message as the rate.

intro.heading: Taking the online rate apart
paragraphs: An online tutoring rate in Dubai is not a single thing. It is a teaching fee with several other charges stacked on top, and which charges apply depends entirely on how you booked. Book an independent tutor directly and you pay close to the teaching fee. Book the same person through an international marketplace and you pay their fee plus a platform margin, often in a currency you do not hold. Book through an agency and you pay the fee plus a matching and management margin. Book a monthly package from a centre and you pay a fee averaged across a group. The teaching in those four cases can be identical.

That is the useful way to think about cost for Cambridge IGCSE Physical Science 0652, because it is a single-award qualification covering chemistry and physics that needs one tutor holding both at IGCSE depth. The scarce thing is the person. Everything else in the price is distribution. A parent who understands which part of the number is distribution can ask better questions and usually pays less for the same hour.

The bands, for reference, read from published UAE rate cards and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table in October 2026: budget online tutoring AED 45 to 150 an hour, qualified subject tutor online AED 150 to 300, IGCSE and A Level specialist AED 200 to 450 and above, premium named tutors AED 500 to 650 and above. Those are market figures rather than IB Gram prices. What this page adds is the layer underneath them: what the spread is made of, and which parts of it you are choosing to buy.

Two things deserve naming early because they cost real money and rarely appear in a comparison. The first is currency. Several international platforms serving Gulf families quote in dollars, and a dirham household paying a dollar invoice absorbs a conversion and often a card charge on every session, which turns a quoted rate into an actual rate roughly two to four per cent higher. The second is mismatch. A tutor who turns out to be a physics teacher covering the chemistry adequately costs you three or four weeks before anybody admits it, and three or four weeks in Year 11 is worth more than any rate difference.

On delivery, plainly: lessons are one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. Home visits in the UAE are not a service IB Gram sells and no tutor is sent to a UAE address; in-home tutoring is something we offer only in India. For 0652 specifically the online format is also the better match, because the pool of tutors holding both sciences at IGCSE depth is a national pool rather than a drive-time one.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-physical-science-0.subjectsIntro: Online delivery suits some 0652 work better than others. Each block below is paired with how it is actually taught on screen and what, if anything, you need on your side of the camera.

subjects.name: Units, prefixes and standard form
subjects.description: Pure screen work. Conversion drills on a shared whiteboard with immediate correction, which is faster than paper because errors are caught in the moment. Nothing needed beyond the device. The cheapest block to buy and the one that lifts both halves of the award at once.

subjects.name: Mole and reacting-mass working
subjects.description: Taught as four written lines, which means the student writes on paper and shows it to the camera or photographs it afterwards. A cheap document stand or a phone propped on a book solves this entirely and is the only equipment this syllabus genuinely benefits from.

subjects.name: Balanced equations and formulae
subjects.description: Shared whiteboard work with the student typing or writing and the tutor annotating. Online has a real advantage here: every attempt stays visible on the board, so patterns in the errors are obvious to the student rather than only to the tutor.

subjects.name: Electrolysis and electrode reasoning
subjects.description: Diagram-led and well suited to a screen, with the cell drawn once and then varied repeatedly to test whether the rule has been learned rather than one example memorised. Varying a diagram live is quicker on a board than on paper.

subjects.name: Rate graphs and reaction conditions
subjects.description: Graph interpretation taught by annotating the figure on screen before any answer is written. The annotate-first habit is easier to enforce online, because the tutor can see exactly whether the student marked the plateau before writing.

subjects.name: Acids, salts and preparation methods
subjects.description: Sequence work: filtration, evaporation, crystallisation in the correct order. Taught as a written template and then tested on variations. No apparatus required, since the questions themselves are written rather than practical.

subjects.name: Motion graphs, gradients and areas
subjects.description: Best done on printed grids, so this is the block where printing earns its small cost. The student plots on paper, photographs it, and the tutor marks the plotting itself rather than only the answer, which is where the marks are.

subjects.name: Forces, moments and pivot diagrams
subjects.description: Diagram discipline taught by having the student draw first and the tutor annotate second. The distances-from-the-pivot error is visible immediately on a shared screen, which is harder to spot when looking across a table at an upside-down page.

subjects.name: Ray diagrams and the normal
subjects.description: Needs a ruler and a protractor on the student's side, and printed templates help. The scoring behaviour is drawing the normal and labelling angles to it, and online marking of a photographed diagram catches the omission reliably.

subjects.name: Circuits and electrical calculation
subjects.description: The highest-value physics block and well suited to screen teaching, because circuits can be redrawn and varied in seconds. The sketch-first rule is enforceable online: the tutor simply does not proceed until a circuit appears.

subjects.name: Thermal physics and particle explanations
subjects.description: Language precision work, taught conversationally and tested in writing. Explanations referring to particle spacing and energy score; explanations describing heat moving do not. No equipment needed at all.

subjects.name: Half-life and radiation types
subjects.description: Systematic halving on a shared board, plus comparison tables for alpha, beta and gamma properties. Short, cheap and frequently skipped, which makes it a reliable source of marks for a student whose budget has run out for larger blocks.

subjects.name: Practical method evaluation
subjects.description: Written work rather than bench work, so it transfers to a screen without loss. Taught as a three-slot template: name the uncontrolled variable or inadequate measurement, say why it matters, say what would improve it. Bench skills for the laboratory test stay with the school.

sections.heading: Why the same online tutor costs three different amounts
paragraphs: The teaching fee is the part of an online rate that pays the person doing the work. Everything else is distribution, and distribution is where the spread between AED 150 and AED 400 an hour mostly comes from on a 0652 booking. Understanding the channel you are buying through is more useful than comparing headline numbers, because two channels can deliver the same tutor at very different prices.

A freelance tutor booked directly carries no margin, which sounds ideal and comes with the fewest protections: no replacement if the fit is wrong, no cover for a cancelled week, and no second opinion if the plan is not working. An international marketplace carries a platform margin and frequently prices in dollars, which adds conversion and card costs to a dirham household on every invoice. An agency carries a matching and management margin and in exchange takes responsibility for the match, which is worth something precisely in the situation where the first tutor is wrong. A tuition centre spreads a fee across a group, which is cheapest per contact hour and least suited to a student with one specific weak block.

For 0652 the channel question has extra weight because the scarce input is a tutor holding both chemistry and physics at IGCSE depth. A channel with a large pool can match on that combination. A channel with a small pool substitutes a physics specialist who will cover chemistry adequately, and you will not discover this for three or four weeks. That substitution is the single most expensive thing that happens in online science tutoring, and no rate card shows it.

sections.heading: Currency is part of the price
paragraphs: A dirham household paying a dollar invoice does not pay the quoted rate. It pays the quoted rate plus a conversion spread and, usually, a foreign-currency card charge. Across a year of weekly sessions that is a few hundred dirhams nobody budgeted, and it is invisible in every comparison table except this one. The research behind these pages found international platforms serving Gulf families quoting USD tiers with no dirham figure anywhere on the page, which is a currency a UAE parent does not transact in.

There is a related signal worth reading. Some providers ranking for UAE searches route parents to non-UAE phone or messaging numbers, and at least one shows a Dubai footer address on a page targeting Abu Dhabi. Neither is illegal and both tell you something about who you are dealing with: the conversion path is the clearest available evidence of where a business actually operates. A UAE page with a dirham rate, a UAE contact route and an honest statement about where tutors are based is giving you more information than one with a dollar tier and a foreign number.

On VAT, this page states nothing about how UAE VAT applies to tuition fees, because that is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority's own guidance rather than something a tutoring site should interpret for you. The practical step is the same with every provider: ask whether a quoted AED figure is inclusive or exclusive, ask for a tax registration number if they hold one, and get both answers in writing before a package is paid for. Monthly packages are where this becomes a problem rather than a detail.

And on IB Gram's own position, stated rather than implied: there is no UAE office, centre or branch. Tuition is delivered online, the rate is quoted in dirhams, and where the right tutor for a niche combination is based outside the UAE you are told before you book rather than after. That disclosure is the thing several providers in this market avoid making, which is precisely why it belongs on the page.

sections.heading: What a mismatch costs, and what to ask about replacement
paragraphs: The most expensive event in a tutoring year is not an overpriced hour. It is four weeks with the wrong tutor. On 0652 the common version is a physics teacher covering the chemistry at a level that looks fine from outside the session and produces no movement in the chemistry marks. Nobody is behaving badly; the tutor is teaching what they know, and the parent has no way to see the gap because the sessions are calm and the student is agreeable.

Four weeks in Year 11 is worth more than any plausible rate saving. A weekly slot at the mid-market band is a four-figure sum, and the real cost is the term it occupied. This is why replacement terms belong in the first conversation rather than the complaint that follows. A channel that takes responsibility for the match is worth its margin exactly here, and a channel that offers a credit rather than a replacement is offering you your money back and not your term.

Three questions detect a likely mismatch before it happens. Which of the two sciences in 0652 have you taught more recently at IGCSE, and to which tier? What was the last practical paper you prepared a student for, Paper 5 or Paper 6? And what marked work will come back after the first session? A tutor who answers the first two specifically has taught the syllabus. A tutor who answers generally about science teaching has not, whatever their qualifications.

Two more questions worth asking of any online provider: who exactly is teaching, and will it be the same person each week? Rotating rosters are cheaper to staff and poor for a student who needs continuity across two sciences. And what happens if the tutor cancels? A plan with no cover arrangement loses a week each time, which over a term is a block of sessions you paid for in time rather than money.

sections.heading: What AED 45 an hour actually buys
paragraphs: The bottom of the published online band is real and it is not a scam. Rate cards in this market advertise online tutoring from around AED 45 to 65 an hour, and some platforms list from around AED 33. Understanding what sits at that price point is more useful than dismissing it, because for some situations it is the correct purchase.

At that rate you are generally buying a university student or a recent graduate, teaching from their own memory of the subject rather than from the current syllabus, with no marked written work and no diagnostic. For supervised homework, for keeping a Year 9 student moving, or for conversational reinforcement of content already taught properly at school, that can be perfectly adequate and the price is honest. What it will not do is diagnose why an Extended-tier candidate is losing method marks on mole calculations, because diagnosing that requires knowing the mark scheme rather than the chemistry.

The failure mode is predictable and expensive in a different way. A family buys twenty sessions at the low band through Year 11, sees no mark movement, and concludes tutoring does not work. The money spent is modest; the year is gone. Where a student has a specific diagnosed weakness in an exam year, six sessions at the specialist band will usually do more than twenty-four at the budget band, and the total is similar.

There is also a permit point that sits underneath the cheapest end of this market. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and university students and school students aged 15 to 18 are among those eligible to apply. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so no amount should be quoted to you. Because the permit costs nothing, not holding one is a choice rather than a hardship, and asking about it is a fair question at any price point.

sections.heading: The equipment budget, honestly
paragraphs: Online tutoring has a small setup cost that nobody mentions because it is unglamorous, and ignoring it is the reason some families get less from sessions than they should. For 0652 the list is short and specific.

A device with a working camera and a stable connection, which almost every household in Dubai already has. A way to show handwritten work: a phone propped on a book, a cheap document stand, or simply photographing the page and sending it. This is the one that matters most, because the marks on this syllabus live in written working — four-line mole calculations, plotted graphs, labelled diagrams — and a session where the tutor never sees the student's handwriting is a session spent on talking rather than on marks.

A printer, or access to one, for graph grids and ray-diagram templates. Plotting on screen is possible and worse: the examinable skill is plotting accurately on paper under time pressure, and it should be practised in that medium. Printing is also the recurring cost on this list, small per week and real across a year. Add a scientific calculator the student is genuinely familiar with, a ruler and a protractor. That is the whole list.

A headset is optional and helps in an apartment with siblings. What helps more than any hardware is a fixed place and a fixed time. The single best predictor of whether an online plan finishes is whether the student sits in the same room at the same hour each week, which costs nothing and is the thing most often not arranged.

sections.heading: Coverage and fallback, stated before you book
paragraphs: Availability is a cost, and it is the one no competitor in this market discloses. A 0652 entry needs a tutor holding chemistry and physics at IGCSE depth, in a weekday evening slot in Gulf Standard Time, which is the most contested hour of the week in Dubai. Sometimes that person is not free. What happens next is where providers differ most and say least.

The dishonest version is a quiet substitution: you are matched with whoever is available, the sessions begin, and the mismatch becomes your problem to notice. A variation found in the research behind these pages is concealment of delivery location, where a UAE family is routed to a tutor elsewhere through a foreign phone number with nothing stated on the page. Neither is illegal and both cost a family weeks.

The honest version is a disclosed fallback. Where no UAE-based specialist is free for the combination and time you need, the alternative offered is an experienced IGCSE science tutor working from India to Gulf Standard Time, stated before you book, with the rate and the tutor's background given at the same time. You may decline it. What you should not have to do is discover it.

sections.heading: Spending that stops being useful
paragraphs: Every tutoring budget has a point past which more money buys nothing, and knowing where it sits is the difference between a plan and a subscription. For 0652 the ceiling is set by what the grade is for.

If the next step is A Level or IB Diploma science, the threshold is the sixth form's entry requirement, usually expressed as a grade in a science qualification and sometimes as a preference for separate sciences. Spending to exceed that threshold comfortably is reasonable; spending to chase the top of the grade range when the requirement is already met is not, and the hours are usually better spent on another subject that is nearer the line.

If the next step is a UAE university, Ministry of Education equivalency becomes relevant and it changes the arithmetic, because equivalency counts subjects rather than ranking them. For the British track the requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at E or above or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. For the American track, English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics by at least 450 in SAT Math. No IB points threshold is published in the source used here, so none appears on this page; verify any figure on moe.gov.ae before relying on it.

Two cautions follow from that. Equivalency is handled by the Ministry and the relevant attestation authority, not by any tutoring provider, and nobody in this market performs or guarantees it. And tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, university admission or school progression; any provider implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency about a regulatory process.
