sections.heading: Who regulates what, and why it affects your quote
paragraphs: Regulation shows up in a tutoring price in two ways: through the permit a tutor must hold, and through the licensing a provider with premises must hold. Neither is decoration, and both are routinely misrepresented in this market.

On the tutor side, the MoHRE private tuition work permit applies to individuals giving private lessons. It is free of charge for two years, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system, and MoHRE's own service page lists a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Because it costs nothing, a tutor without one has made a choice, and the question is reasonable to ask at any rate.

On the provider side, a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum six-month window to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. That is an entirely different instrument from anything that applies to an online one-to-one service, and it is the source of the most dangerous phrase available to pages like this one. Nobody providing private tutoring holds regulator approval for tutoring; IB Gram holds no KHDA permit and operates no UAE premises.

The wider map matters because Dubai families move emirates. Dubai private schools are overseen by KHDA; Abu Dhabi and Al Ain by ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate; Sharjah by the Sharjah Private Education Authority; Ras Al Khaimah by its Department of Knowledge; and schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, which is a broader remit than inspection alone. A tutoring plan that follows a family across emirates should know which authority is now involved.

sections.heading: What a sensible online 0652 plan looks like on paper
paragraphs: Pulling the cost thinking together into something a parent can act on. A sensible plan for an online 0652 engagement in Dubai has five properties, and none of them concern the hourly rate.

It starts from a marked script, so the target is diagnosed rather than assumed. It names one or two blocks rather than the award, because the quantitative spine is where the hours convert into marks. It is finite, with a stated number of sessions and a review date tied to a real event such as the November mock. It produces one marked artefact a week against the published mark scheme, so progress is a comparison rather than an impression. And it states its limits in writing: who is teaching, where they are based, what happens if the fit is wrong, and whether the quoted figure is inclusive of VAT.

Cost-wise, that plan is usually cheaper than what families actually buy, which tends to be a standing weekly slot from September to June at a mid-market rate with no stated target. The standing slot is comfortable and it is where most of the avoidable spending in this market lives. A diagnostic session, a six-session block on calculation discipline, a four-session block on circuits and a short practical-skills block will cost less than half a year of weekly sessions and will usually move more marks, because each piece has a target and an end.

If the honest answer after a diagnostic is that no paid tutoring is needed this term, that is what you should hear. A student with secure content, reasonable timing and no practical preparation needs four weeks of timed papers marked properly, and the papers come from school. Saying so costs a provider a sale and is the only basis on which the rest of the page means anything.

faqs.question: Why do online 0652 quotes in Dubai vary so much for the same qualification?
faqs.answer: Because most of the spread is distribution rather than teaching. A freelance tutor booked directly carries no margin and no protections. An agency or platform carries a matching and management margin and takes responsibility for the match. An international marketplace carries a platform margin and often prices in dollars. A centre spreads a fee across a group. The same tutor can appear at very different prices through two of those channels, which is why asking what the margin buys is more useful than comparing headline numbers.

faqs.question: Does paying a tutoring invoice in dollars cost a Dubai family more?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it rarely appears in a comparison. A dirham household paying a dollar invoice absorbs a conversion spread and usually a foreign-currency card charge on every session, which turns a quoted rate into an actual rate a few per cent higher. Across a year of weekly sessions that is a few hundred dirhams nobody planned for. Several international platforms serving Gulf families quote USD tiers with no dirham figure anywhere, which is a currency UAE parents do not transact in.

faqs.question: What does an online science tutor at the bottom of the Dubai market provide?
faqs.answer: Advertised rates from around AED 45 to 65 an hour generally buy a university student or recent graduate teaching from their own memory of the subject, without a diagnostic and without marked written work. For supervised homework or for keeping a Year 9 student moving, that is adequate and honestly priced. It will not identify why an Extended-tier candidate is losing method marks on mole calculations, because that requires knowing the mark scheme rather than the chemistry.

faqs.question: How do I avoid being matched with a physics tutor for a 0652 entry?
faqs.answer: Ask two questions before booking. Which of chemistry and physics have you taught more recently at IGCSE, and to which tier? And for your last 0652 student, was it Paper 5 or Paper 6? A tutor who answers both specifically has taught the syllabus; a tutor who answers generally about science teaching has not, whatever the qualifications say. The substitution is not dishonest, it is just what happens when a channel's pool is too small, and it costs three or four weeks before anyone notices.

faqs.question: What should a provider do if the tutor is the wrong fit in week three?
faqs.answer: Replace the tutor and continue the plan, rather than issue a credit and start again. The distinction matters because the real loss in a mismatch is time, not money: four weeks in Year 11 is worth more than any rate saving. Agree the terms before the first session, including whether the same tutor teaches every week and what cover exists if they cancel. A plan with no cover arrangement quietly loses a week each time, which across a term is a block of sessions.

faqs.question: Do I need to buy equipment for online 0652 lessons?
faqs.answer: Very little, but one item matters. The student needs a way to show handwritten work: a phone propped on a book, a cheap document stand, or photographing the page and sending it. The marks on this syllabus live in written working, so a session where the tutor never sees the handwriting is spent on talking rather than on marks. Beyond that: printed graph grids, a familiar scientific calculator, a ruler and a protractor. A fixed room at a fixed hour helps more than any hardware.

faqs.question: Is screen-based graph work good enough for the 0652 practical questions?
faqs.answer: Plot on paper, not on screen. The examinable skill is accurate plotting on a printed grid under time pressure, with sensible scales and a best-fit line through the trend, so it should be practised in that medium. The pattern that works online is print, plot, photograph, submit, and the tutor marks the plotting itself rather than only the final answer. Printing is the one small recurring cost of online science tutoring and it is worth paying.

faqs.question: Which time slots are cheapest and easiest to book in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Anything that is not a weekday evening between 5pm and 8pm Gulf Standard Time, which is the most contested block in the week. Weekday afternoons before 5pm, Friday mornings and weekend slots are easier to fill and usually produce a better match, because you are shopping in a less crowded part of the market. Families who can move a session out of the evening peak routinely get a more experienced tutor for the same money, which is the simplest saving available on this page.

faqs.question: What happens if no UAE-based 0652 tutor is free when we need lessons?
faqs.answer: You are told before booking. 0652 needs chemistry and physics at IGCSE depth in one tutor, and the evening peak in Gulf Standard Time is the hardest slot to fill. Where no UAE-based specialist is available, the alternative offered is an experienced IGCSE science tutor working from India to your time zone, with the rate and background stated at the same time. You can decline it. Quiet substitution and concealed delivery location are practices this market has, and disclosure is the alternative.

faqs.question: Does an online 0652 tutor need the MoHRE private tuition permit?
faqs.answer: The permit applies to individuals giving private lessons and was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system, with MoHRE's own service page listing a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published.

faqs.question: Does KHDA licensing apply to an online tutoring provider?
faqs.answer: A KHDA Educational Services Permit is issued to training institutes with premises and staff in Dubai: initial approval first, a maximum six-month window to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. It is a different instrument from anything that applies to an online one-to-one service, and nobody providing private tutoring holds regulator approval for tutoring itself. IB Gram holds no such permit and operates no UAE premises, which is why delivery is online and why this page states it rather than implying otherwise.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does UAE Ministry of Education equivalency count?
faqs.answer: For the British track, five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not included among the five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject figure, which is wrong. Verify the current requirements on moe.gov.ae, and note that equivalency is handled by the Ministry rather than by any tutoring provider.

faqs.question: Is tutoring required for a UAE university application after 0652?
faqs.answer: No. Equivalency and admission are regulatory and institutional processes, and no tutoring is required for either. Any provider implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency about something it does not control. What tutoring can do is help a student reach the grade a particular sixth form or university programme asks for, and that threshold is the sensible ceiling on spending. Past the threshold, hours are usually better spent on whichever subject is nearest the line.

faqs.question: Which emirate authority oversees my child's school if we move from Dubai?
faqs.answer: Dubai private schools are overseen by KHDA. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, both of which also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. A tutoring plan following a family across emirates should know which authority now applies.

faqs.question: What would make you tell us not to buy 0652 tutoring at all?
faqs.answer: A marked script showing secure content, reasonable timing and no practical preparation. That student needs four weeks of timed papers marked properly against the published mark scheme, and the papers come from their school. Paid tutoring earns its money where something has to be diagnosed and taught, and a diagnostic session exists partly to establish which of those situations you are in. Hearing it costs a provider a sale, which is the only reason the rest of this page is worth anything.

Each one works from a marked script rather than a syllabus checklist, because a script shows what a student can do under timed conditions and a checklist shows what a scheme of work intended.

intro.heading: Evidence first: what should change, and how you would know
paragraphs: Most tutoring is sold on reassurance and reported on in adjectives. A parent hears that a child is engaging well, growing in confidence, and making progress, and three months later the mock comes back where it was. The alternative is not harder, it is just more specific: record a baseline in marks at the start, mark every piece of written work against the published scheme, categorise each lost mark by cause, and watch whether the categories shrink. That is what this page describes for Cambridge IGCSE Physical Science 0652, and it is the reason this page exists in the form it does.

0652 is a single award covering chemistry and physics. No biology. It produces one IGCSE grade and is entered at Core or Extended tier, with a multiple-choice paper, a structured theory paper, and a practical component sat either as a laboratory test or as its written alternative. The exact durations, mark totals and weightings are printed in the Cambridge syllabus document for the series your child is entered for, and that document — not a summary — is the thing to check at cambridgeinternational.org before planning anything.

There is a point about this code specifically that parents should hear early. 0652 is a smaller entry in Dubai than Coordinated Sciences 0654, Combined Science 0653 or the three separate sciences, and not every school in the emirate offers it. That matters because families searching for help with physical science sometimes discover, mid-conversation, that the statement of entry says 0654 or 0653 instead. The codes examine overlapping content through different paper structures, and preparing for the wrong structure wastes real money. Find the code before you buy anything.

What is useful about 0652 for a student who fits it: the two quantitative sciences, taught together, without the biology content load. The chemistry and physics in it carry the quantitative spine that A Level and IB Diploma science courses assume — the mole and concentration work, formula rearrangement, circuit reasoning, graph gradients. A student who takes 0652 and works properly on those blocks arrives at post-16 science with the right foundation, even though the award itself is a single grade rather than a double.

Lessons from IB Gram are one-to-one over live video, scheduled around Dubai school hours in Gulf Standard Time. Home visits are not a service we offer in the UAE; tutors are not sent to UAE addresses, and the reason this page recommends the online format is not convenience but matching. A tutor who holds both chemistry and physics at IGCSE depth is a specific person, and choosing by subject rather than by driving distance is how you get one. The practical consequence for a Dubai family is that the weekly slot is set by when your child concentrates best, not by when traffic on Al Khail Road allows a tutor to reach your community, and a 90-minute booking buys 90 minutes of teaching rather than 60 minutes plus a round trip somebody has to pay for.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-physical-science-0.programmesIntro: Evidence looks different at each stage of a British-curriculum pathway, because what counts as a meaningful measurement changes. These are the four stages around 0652 and what you should expect to be able to see at each one.

programmes.name: Year 9 and the tier decision
programmes.description: The year the school decides which science route and tier a student takes. Useful evidence at this stage is narrow: accuracy on calculation questions, quality of graph work, and whether practical write-ups score. Topic-test percentages are poor predictors because they are untimed and often open-book.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools generally set science routes in the spring term of Year 9, so a family wanting a particular route has one term in which evidence can change the decision. The evidence a head of science responds to is marked written work under timed conditions, which is precisely what a well-run tutoring block produces as a by-product.

programmes.name: 0652 Year 10: building the record
programmes.description: Content is delivered across chemistry and physics, and this is the cheapest year in which to build an evidence habit. Marked scripts from Year 10 give a tutor a loss-category profile long before it matters, and the fixes are procedural at this stage rather than remedial.
programmes.countryNote: Because Dubai schools run Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies alongside the licensed curriculum as KHDA requires, Year 10 evenings are more crowded here than in a UK comparison. A weekly marked task of twenty minutes beats a long session the student has no time to prepare for.

programmes.name: 0652 Year 11: moving the mock
programmes.description: The year the evidence becomes consequential, because mocks feed predicted grades. Progress shows up as loss categories changing shape: method marks appearing on calculations, data questions scoring fully, practical answers moving past one mark. The total often moves last, which is why categories are the better measure.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai mocks typically sit in November and again in February or March. A tutoring plan that does not name which mock it is aiming at has no deadline, and plans without deadlines drift. The November mock is the one worth targeting, because the result still has time to change the spring picture.

programmes.name: Where 0652 leads
programmes.description: A Level Chemistry or Physics, or IB Diploma sciences. Both assume the quantitative work 0652 contains: moles and concentration, formula rearrangement, circuit analysis, gradient and area from graphs. A single award at Extended tier with strong calculation evidence is a better foundation than a double award with weak calculation evidence.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai sixth forms set their own science entry requirements and some ask for separate sciences outright. The 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools and 16,846 places, three of them International Baccalaureate schools, so the local post-16 options are widening rather than narrowing.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-physical-science-0.subjectsIntro: Each content block below is paired with the evidence that shows whether it is secure. The point is to be able to answer the question a parent actually has — is this topic fixed? — with something other than an opinion.

subjects.name: Measurement, units and standard form
subjects.description: The quiet foundation of both halves of 0652. Evidence of security: unit conversions correct without prompting, standard form handled in multi-step calculations, and answers carrying units. Where this is weak, every calculation topic in the award reads as weak too.

subjects.name: Atomic structure, bonding and formulae
subjects.description: Electronic structure, ionic and covalent bonding, writing and balancing equations. Evidence: balanced equations produced unprompted in questions that do not ask for them explicitly, because the next step needs one. This is the gateway to all quantitative chemistry marks.

subjects.name: Stoichiometry and the mole
subjects.description: Relative formula mass, moles, reacting masses, concentration and volumes. Evidence: method marks appearing on scripts even when a final answer is wrong, and four written lines rather than a single number. The single most reliable predictor of an Extended-tier grade in 0652 chemistry.

subjects.name: Electrolysis and energy change
subjects.description: Electrode products, electrolytes, exothermic and endothermic reactions. Evidence: electrode products predicted correctly when the electrolyte is changed, which separates a student who learned a rule from one who memorised one example.

subjects.name: Rates of reaction and reversible reactions
subjects.description: Factors affecting rate, collision ideas, and where reversible reactions appear. Evidence: rate-graph questions answered from the gradient and the plateau rather than from a remembered sentence, and conclusions tied to the data shown.

subjects.name: Acids, bases, salts and the periodic table
subjects.description: Acid and base reactions, neutralisation, salt preparation methods and group trends. Evidence: salt-preparation answers giving filtration, evaporation and crystallisation in the right order, which is a practical question answered in a theory paper.

subjects.name: Metals, fuels and environmental chemistry
subjects.description: Reactivity, extraction, corrosion, air pollutants and fuels. Evidence: named substances in answers rather than general categories. Questions in this block reward specific chemical names and lose marks for vague descriptions of pollution.

subjects.name: Motion, forces and energy
subjects.description: Speed, acceleration, distance-time and speed-time graphs, forces, moments, energy transfer, work and power. Evidence: gradient and area-under-graph questions answered correctly, and moments questions with the distances measured from the pivot.

subjects.name: Thermal physics and the particle model
subjects.description: Particle behaviour, expansion, conduction, convection and radiation. Evidence: explanations referring to particle spacing and energy rather than to heat moving, which is the distinction the mark scheme is built on.

subjects.name: Waves, light and sound
subjects.description: Wave properties, reflection, refraction, the electromagnetic spectrum and sound. Evidence: ray diagrams with the normal drawn and angles labelled to it. Without the normal, a correct explanation still loses the diagram marks.

subjects.name: Electricity and circuits
subjects.description: Current, potential difference, resistance, series and parallel circuits, power and safety. Evidence: a sketched circuit appearing on the script before any calculation. Students who sketch first score reliably; students who calculate first do not.

subjects.name: Magnetism, electromagnetism and radioactivity
subjects.description: Magnetic fields, the motor effect, electromagnetic induction at Extended tier, radiation types and half-life. Evidence: field directions drawn consistently, and half-life questions worked by systematic halving rather than estimated.

sections.heading: Find the code before you buy anything
paragraphs: Physical Science 0652 sits alongside several other Cambridge science routes that cover overlapping content through different paper structures, and in Dubai the entry code on the statement of entry is the only reliable way to know which one a student is actually sitting. Families regularly arrive certain their child is on physical science and discover the school entered coordinated or combined science instead. The content overlaps enough for the confusion to be reasonable and the paper structures differ enough for the error to be expensive.

The practical differences are worth laying out. 0652 covers chemistry and physics and produces one IGCSE grade. Combined Science 0653 covers all three sciences and produces one grade. Coordinated Sciences 0654 covers all three and produces a double award, reported as two grades. Separate sciences — 0610 Biology, 0620 Chemistry, 0625 Physics — are three entries with three grades and more depth in each. All are tiered at Core and Extended except where a school's choice removes the option, and each has its own practical arrangement.

Which one suits a student is a school decision informed by timetable, set placement and post-16 intentions. Where a family has a view, the conversation to have is with the head of science, and the evidence that carries weight in it is marked timed work rather than classwork. A student wanting to move from combined to physical science, or from physical science to separate sciences, is asking the school to make a judgement about capacity, and the school will look at assessment data to make it.

The table below is the version of this comparison to take into that conversation. Verify the component detail for your child's series on cambridgeinternational.org, because Cambridge publishes a syllabus document per series and the one that matters is the one your child is entered for, not the one that was current when a page like this was written.

sections.heading: What gets measured in the first session
paragraphs: A baseline is not a test score. It is a profile of how marks are being lost, recorded in a form that can be compared six weeks later. Without one, a tutor is guessing and a parent is trusting, and neither of those produces a decision when the mock result arrives. The first session on 0652 therefore does something slightly unusual: it spends most of its time watching the student work rather than teaching.

Five things get recorded. Accuracy by topic block, so chemistry and physics are separated rather than averaged. Method marks on calculation questions, counted separately from correct answers, because a student losing method marks has a different problem from one getting wrong answers. Data-question performance, because answering from memory rather than from the figure is a distinct and common failure. Practical-component answers, which on 0652 are a fifth of the award and often untaught. And timing, measured by how far through a timed set the student gets rather than by how it felt.

Those five measures produce a profile rather than a grade, and the profile is what the plan is built from. A student scoring poorly overall but losing almost everything on method marks needs four sessions on calculation discipline, not a term of content. A student whose topic accuracy is fine and whose timing collapses needs paper practice, not teaching. A student weak across both halves of the award needs a content rebuild in syllabus order, and should be told that honestly rather than sold a six-week sprint.

The profile is written down and shared with the family, including the version that says tutoring is not the right purchase this term. That happens more often than the industry admits: a student with secure content, good timing and no practical preparation needs four sessions and better marked practice at school, not a weekly commitment through to June.

sections.heading: Twelve weeks of 0652 support, week by week
paragraphs: Plans that exist only as a description drift. A plan with a week number against each piece of work does not, because the absence of the work is visible. What follows is the shape a twelve-week block typically takes for a Year 11 student on 0652 with a mixed baseline: calculation discipline weak, physics content broadly present, chemistry quantitative work shaky, practical component untaught.

The front half targets procedure rather than content, because procedural gains show up fastest and they make the content work that follows measurable. Weeks one to three install the calculation method, the sketch-first rule for circuits, and the annotate-first rule for data questions. Weeks four to six take the weaker half of the award — usually chemistry — in syllabus order, with a timed set after each session. Weeks seven to nine do the practical component as a discrete block, because it is a fifth of the award and the rules are generic. Weeks ten to twelve are timed papers, reviewed against the scheme.

Each week produces one marked artefact. Not a report: a script, with the marks attributed and the misses explained. Those twelve scripts are the record, and they answer the question a term report cannot, which is whether a specific category of loss is shrinking. If the method marks are still absent in week eight after four weeks of drilling, the method drilling was the wrong intervention and something else is going on — frequently the underlying algebra, occasionally an attention or processing issue that needs a different conversation entirely.

The plan is also deliberately finite. Twelve weeks ends, and ending forces a judgement: continue with a new target, stop, or change approach. Open-ended weekly tutoring is comfortable for everyone involved and it is where families spend the most for the least visible return.

sections.heading: How to read a marked 0652 script
paragraphs: Most parents are handed a total and a grade, and a total hides everything useful. Reading a script properly takes about ten minutes and tells you what three term reports will not. The question is always the same: of the marks that were not awarded, what kind of mark were they?

Start with calculation questions. If the final answers are right, the marks are there and nothing needs doing. If the final answers are wrong but working is laid out in steps, method marks will have been awarded and the problem is arithmetic or a single misremembered relationship — a narrow, quick fix. If answers are bare numbers with no working, method marks have been forfeited whether the thinking was right or not, and that is a procedural problem worth more marks than any topic.

Then look at the data and graph questions, the ones where a table or figure is printed. If the answer does not refer to the figure, the student answered from memory. This is the most common single failure among well-revised students and it is why a high-effort student can plateau. Next, the practical-style questions: an evaluation that says the student should have been more careful has scored nothing, and an evaluation naming an uncontrolled variable or an inadequate measurement resolution has scored. Those two answers look similarly long on the page and are worth completely different amounts.

Finally, look at where the script stops. An unfinished paper is a timing problem and it is diagnosed separately from everything else, because the fix is question order and time allocation rather than content. A student who scores well on everything they attempted and leaves the last page blank does not need more teaching; they need to be taught to leave a question rather than fight it. Four categories, ten minutes, and you know what the next six weeks should contain.
bullets: Bare answers on calculations: method marks forfeited, procedural fix
Answers ignoring a printed figure: memory instead of data
Evaluations criticising the student rather than the method: no marks
A blank final page: timing, not knowledge

sections.heading: Why a mock grade moves when a topic test does not
paragraphs: Families often see a confusing pattern: topic test scores stay flat while the mock moves, or the reverse. Both are explicable, and understanding why keeps a reasonable plan from being abandoned at the wrong moment.

Topic tests are usually untimed or generously timed, focused on one block, and sometimes sat with notes available. They measure recall of recently taught material. Mocks are timed, cover the whole award, mix question types, and include the practical component. A student whose problem is procedural — no working shown, data ignored, poor timing — can score reasonably on topic tests for months and still underperform on every mock. Fixing the procedure moves the mock and leaves topic tests exactly where they were, which looks like nothing changing if topic tests are the only data a parent sees.

The reverse pattern has a different cause. A student who starts scoring better on topic tests while the mock stays flat is usually learning content in the week it is taught and not retaining it across the award. That is a revision-structure problem, not a teaching problem, and the fix is cumulative marked practice rather than more teaching hours. It is also why marked work on older topics matters: a question set that only covers this week's material cannot detect the issue.

Tier interacts with all of this. A Core-tier candidate has a grade ceiling, so improvement eventually stops being visible in grade terms even as marks rise. An Extended-tier candidate placed there optimistically can work hard and see very little movement, because the papers assume a foundation that is not yet built. Neither situation is a tutoring failure, and both need saying out loud rather than discovering in June. Where tier looks wrong, the school decides, and marked timed work is the evidence it responds to.

sections.heading: The chemistry half of 0652, in evidence terms
paragraphs: Chemistry in 0652 is where the quantitative marks live, and it is where a marked script is most informative. Three evidence patterns recur in Dubai cohorts, and each implies a different intervention.

The first pattern is correct chemistry with absent arithmetic. Equations balanced, products identified, reasoning sound, and then a reacting-mass calculation producing a number that is out by a factor of ten or a unit. This is a standard-form and unit-conversion problem presented as a chemistry problem, and it resolves in a few weeks of deliberate practice on conversions rather than on chemistry. Ignoring it and teaching more chemistry is the commonest way a term of tutoring produces no visible change.

The second is memorised rules misapplied. Electrode products given correctly for the electrolyte the student met in class and wrongly for the one in the question. Reactivity-series answers that work until the question uses a metal in an unfamiliar position. Salt-preparation methods recited in the wrong order. All of these are the same underlying issue: content learned as instances rather than as a rule, and the examiner's variation exposes it. The fix is to teach the rule and then test it on deliberately unfamiliar cases, which is a four-to-six-session job.

The third is vagueness in the environmental and extraction content, where questions reward named substances and students write general descriptions. This is the quickest of the three to fix and the easiest to overlook, because the answers look complete. A marked script shows it immediately: long answers, few ticks. Once a student sees that pattern on their own paper, the correction tends to stick without much repetition.
bullets: Wrong by a factor of ten: a units problem, not a chemistry one
Right for the taught example, wrong for the question's variation: rule not learned
Long answers with few ticks: naming, not knowledge
Method marks missing: four-line calculation discipline

sections.heading: The physics half of 0652, in evidence terms
paragraphs: Physics in 0652 produces cleaner evidence than chemistry because the failures are more visibly procedural. On a marked script, four things show up repeatedly, and three of them are visible without reading a single answer.

The first is the absence of a sketch. A circuit question answered without a drawn circuit, a moments question without a labelled diagram, a refraction question without the normal drawn. These are visible at a glance and they correlate strongly with lost marks, because the diagram is both a thinking tool and in several cases a scoring component in its own right. Enforcing sketch-first on every question for a few weeks produces a measurable change in the next marked set.

The second is graph work: axes chosen so the points occupy a corner, best-fit lines drawn through the first and last point, gradients calculated from the plotted points rather than from the line. Graph marks appear in both the theory paper and the practical component, so this is paid twice. The third is unit and prefix handling, particularly milli and kilo in electrical questions, which is the physics version of the chemistry arithmetic problem and responds to the same drilling.

The fourth is less visible and more important: reasoning questions about what happens when something in a described setup changes. Add a resistor in parallel, move the pivot, increase the frequency. These questions separate grades at Extended tier because they cannot be answered from memory, and the only preparation that works is repeated practice on the question style with the student making the prediction before any calculation. That is a slow kind of session and the one that produces the most durable gains in this half of the award.

sections.heading: Predicted grades, school reports and what KHDA bands mean
paragraphs: Evidence has an audience beyond the family. Predicted grades affect sixth-form and university conversations, set placement affects what a student is taught, and both are decided by schools using their own data. Knowing what that data looks like helps a parent participate rather than react.

Predicted grades in Dubai schools are generally built from mock performance plus teacher judgement, which is why the November mock matters disproportionately. A student with marked timed work showing a clear upward trend in specific question types has something to contribute to that judgement; a student with good classwork and a weak mock does not. This is the most practical reason to keep marked scripts: they are the only form of evidence that resembles the evidence the school itself is using.

Dubai private schools are inspected annually by KHDA on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak, and the band tells a parent about the school rather than about their child. It is useful context — a school's published inspection report comments on teaching and on assessment practice — and it is not a proxy for an individual student's progress. Abu Dhabi schools are inspected by ADEK, Sharjah's by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, and schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods, which is a broader remit than inspection alone.

One piece of genuine good news for budgeting: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. A flat fee year makes a defined twelve-week tutoring block easier to commit to, which is the shape this page recommends over an open-ended weekly arrangement.

sections.heading: The honest limits of progress evidence
paragraphs: Evidence is better than reassurance and it is not a guarantee of anything. Four limits are worth stating plainly, because a page that promises measurement without stating its boundaries is doing the same thing as a page that promises outcomes.

First, marks measured in a tutoring session are not marks measured in an exam hall. A student who performs under one-to-one conditions and freezes in a hall has an exam-conditions problem that marked homework will not detect. Timed, unsupported, full-paper practice is the closest available approximation, and it should be part of any plan in the final weeks for exactly this reason. Second, no tutor can promise a grade on 0652 or on anything else, and no amount of evidence changes that. What evidence provides is an early, honest answer about whether the current plan is working.

Third, there is no coursework on 0652, which removes a temptation that exists on other qualifications but also removes a source of guaranteed marks. The nearest equivalent is the practical component, and a tutor's role there is to teach the skills and mark the student's own work. No tutor should be producing, drafting or completing any assessed work for a student, on this syllabus or any other; on IGCSE science the question rarely arises, and the principle holds anyway.

Fourth, availability. A 0652 tutor must hold both chemistry and physics at IGCSE depth, and Gulf Standard Time evening slots are the most contested in the week. Where no UAE-based specialist is free for the combination and time you need, you will be told, and the alternative offered is an experienced IGCSE science tutor working from India to your time zone, disclosed before you book. That is a real limit, and concealing it behind a promise of instant matching would be the dishonest option.
bullets: Session marks are not exam-hall marks; timed full papers close the gap
No grade promises, with or without evidence
No tutor produces assessed work; the practical component is taught, not done for the student
Coverage limits stated before booking, not after

faqs.question: What does Cambridge IGCSE Physical Science 0652 actually cover?
faqs.answer: 0652 is a single-award IGCSE covering chemistry and physics, with no biology content. It produces one IGCSE grade and is entered at Core or Extended tier, with a multiple-choice paper, a structured theory paper and a practical component sat either as a laboratory test or as its written alternative. The chemistry includes bonding, stoichiometry, electrolysis, rates, acids and bases and organic material; the physics includes motion, forces, energy, thermal physics, waves, electricity and radioactivity. Check the syllabus document for your child's series on cambridgeinternational.org for the exact components.

faqs.question: Is 0652 the same as Combined Science or Coordinated Sciences?
faqs.answer: No, and the difference matters when you buy tutoring. Combined Science 0653 covers all three sciences for one grade. Coordinated Sciences 0654 covers all three and gives a double award, reported as two grades. Physical Science 0652 covers chemistry and physics only, for one grade. Each has its own paper structure, so preparing for the wrong one wastes money. Dubai families regularly find the statement of entry says something different from what they assumed, so confirm the code before any sessions are booked.

faqs.question: Do many Dubai schools offer 0652?
faqs.answer: It is a smaller entry here than Coordinated Sciences 0654, Combined Science 0653 or the separate sciences, and not every Dubai school offers it. That is worth knowing because a search for physical science help often ends with the discovery that the school entered a different code. If your child's school does offer 0652, the head of science is the person who can confirm the tier and which practical paper is entered, both of which are printed on the statement of entry in any case.

faqs.question: What should a tutor measure in the first 0652 session?
faqs.answer: Five things, recorded in marks rather than impressions: topic accuracy with chemistry and physics counted separately, method marks lost on multi-step calculations, performance on questions where the answer is in a printed figure, practical-component answers, and how far through a timed set the student reaches. Those five produce a profile that tells you what the plan should contain. A first session that produces only a general sense of the student's level has not given you anything you can compare against in six weeks.

faqs.question: How do I read my child's marked science script myself?
faqs.answer: Look at four things. On calculation questions, are answers bare numbers or laid out in steps? Bare numbers forfeit method marks regardless of the thinking. On questions with a printed table or graph, does the answer refer to the figure or to memory? On practical-style questions, does the evaluation name a weakness in the method or say the student should have been more careful? The second scores nothing. And where does the script stop? A blank final page is a timing problem, diagnosed and fixed separately from content.

faqs.question: Why did my child's mock improve when their topic tests did not?
faqs.answer: Because the two measure different things. Topic tests are usually untimed, cover one block and sometimes allow notes, so they test recent recall. Mocks are timed, cover the whole award, mix question types and include the practical component. Fixing procedural habits — showing working, reading the figure, managing time — moves a mock substantially and leaves topic tests exactly where they were. If topic tests are the only data you see, genuine progress can look like nothing happening at all.

faqs.question: My child works hard on 0652 and the marks are not moving. What should I check?
faqs.answer: Three things in order. Whether calculation answers show working, because effort spent on content cannot recover forfeited method marks. Whether unit conversions and standard form are secure, since an arithmetic weakness presents convincingly as a chemistry or physics weakness. And whether the tier is right: an Extended-tier candidate placed optimistically can work hard against papers that assume a foundation not yet built, and see very little movement. All three are visible on a marked script within about ten minutes.

faqs.question: How long before tutoring shows up in a 0652 result?
faqs.answer: Procedural changes appear in marked homework within two or three weeks and in a mock at the next sitting. Content rebuilds take a term, because the material has to be taught and then retained across the whole award rather than for one test. Practical-component work shows up as soon as the next paper containing practical-style questions. What should never take three months to appear is evidence of direction: if no loss category has changed shape after six weeks, the intervention was wrong and the plan should change.

faqs.question: Should we target the November mock or the spring one?
faqs.answer: November, if there is a choice. Dubai schools generally run mocks in November and again in February or March, and predicted grades draw heavily on them. A November result still leaves time for the spring picture to change, and it gives both the school and the family real data at a point where decisions about tier and set are still open. Aiming a plan at the spring mock compresses everything into the same weeks when every Year 11 family in the emirate is competing for the same tutoring hours.

faqs.question: Does the practical component need separate preparation on 0652?
faqs.answer: Yes. It carries roughly a fifth of the award, is common to both tiers, and is frequently untaught beyond school laboratory time. The marks go to rules rather than talent: the results table drawn before readings are taken, graph scales filling the grid, a best-fit line through the trend, anomalies named explicitly, a conclusion answering the question asked, and an evaluation identifying a specific weakness in the method. Four to six sessions usually covers it, and the gain also shows up in theory-paper practical-style questions.

faqs.question: Can a 0652 tutor help if my child is in the Core tier?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the work is different from Extended-tier work rather than easier. Core-tier tutoring concentrates on completeness and precision: making sure every question receives a scoring answer, that command terms are answered in the right register, and that calculation questions show working. It also addresses the ceiling honestly, because a Core entry caps the achievable grade. If a tier change is the aim, the school decides on its own assessment evidence, and marked timed work is what that evidence looks like.

faqs.question: What evidence does a head of science respond to in a set or tier discussion?
faqs.answer: Marked timed work, because that is the same kind of evidence the school generates itself. Classwork, verbal feedback and parental impressions carry much less weight, and reasonably so. A folder of weekly scripts showing a specific question type moving from unscored to scored over six weeks is a concrete argument. A request based on effort is not. The conversation also has a deadline, since changing an entry after submission is an administrative process rather than a teaching one.

faqs.question: Do KHDA inspection bands tell me anything about my child's science progress?
faqs.answer: They tell you about the school, not the student. Dubai private schools are inspected annually by KHDA on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, and the published report comments on teaching quality and assessment practice across the school. That is useful context when choosing a school and close to useless as a measure of one child's progress in one subject. For that, the only reliable source is marked work from your own child under timed conditions.

faqs.question: What if no 0652 specialist is free when we need lessons?
faqs.answer: You will be told before booking rather than after. A 0652 tutor needs both chemistry and physics at IGCSE depth, and weekday evening slots in Gulf Standard Time are the most contested in the week. Where no UAE-based specialist is available for your combination and time, the alternative offered is an experienced IGCSE science tutor working from India to Gulf Standard Time, stated openly. Quietly routing a UAE family to a tutor elsewhere without disclosure is a practice this market has, and we do not.

faqs.question: Are lessons for 0652 delivered at our home in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. Home visits in the UAE are not a service IB Gram provides, and no tutor will be sent to a UAE address. Lessons run one-to-one over live video with a shared whiteboard and the paper on screen, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around school hours and activities, and they move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan. For this syllabus the online format is also the better match: a tutor who holds both chemistry and physics at IGCSE depth is a specific person, and you choose from everyone who does rather than from whoever is nearby.

The answer to that tells you more about a physics tutor than a list of degrees does.

intro.heading: Why a mock grade on its own tells you almost nothing
paragraphs: A Dubai physics mock arrives as a letter and a percentage. Neither of those tells you what to fix. A 54 per cent on 0625 Paper 4 can belong to a student who understands electricity and cannot rearrange an equation, or to a student who rearranges confidently and has never properly separated mass from weight. Those two children need completely different terms of work. The first needs twenty minutes of algebra and then volume practice. The second needs three definitions rebuilt from scratch before any question is attempted. A tutor who asks for the script before asking what grade your child is aiming at is working from evidence, and that single habit is the difference between a term that moves a grade and a term that fills a Tuesday evening.

So the first session on a 0625 case is a diagnostic rather than a lesson. Your child sits a recent Extended paper under exam timing, in their own handwriting, with no help. The tutor then marks it against the published Cambridge mark scheme and tags every lost mark into one of five causes: a definition not known, an equation not recalled, a substitution error, a unit or prefix slip, and a command term read as something else. The output is not a percentage. It is a ranked list that says, for example, that eleven marks went on prefixes and conversions, nine on recall of the density and pressure relationships, and four on misreading describe as explain.

That list is what the following weeks are built on, and it is also what you get to see. Parents in Dubai are rarely short of enthusiasm from tutors and almost always short of paperwork. A ranked cause list, a fortnightly marked script and a running tally of which of the six 0625 topic areas is still leaking marks is paperwork you can take into a parents' evening and put next to the school's own data. When the school says your daughter is a solid six and the scripts say she drops eleven marks a paper on unit conversions alone, the conversation changes from opinion to arithmetic.

The URL you clicked says home tutor, because that is the phrase Dubai families actually type into Google. Here is the plain position before you read any further: IB Gram does not send tutors to houses, villas or apartments anywhere in the UAE, and home visiting is a service we run only in India. Physics lessons for Dubai students are delivered live online, one to one, over video, with a shared screen for circuit diagrams and ray boxes. We would rather say that on the first screen than bury it. The argument for it is straightforward: a family in Mirdif or Arabian Ranches gets a specialist who has marked hundreds of 0625 scripts instead of whichever qualified person happens to live inside a drivable radius on a weekday evening.

What follows is the detail: how 0625 is assessed paper by paper, where its marks actually go missing, what Dubai's market charges for physics help in AED, what eight weeks of documented work looks like, and where the honest limits of tutoring sit. None of it requires you to book anything to be useful.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-physics-0625-home-.programmesIntro: Dubai's British-curriculum schools run a predictable ladder, and Cambridge Physics 0625 sits at the hinge of it. Knowing which rung your child is on changes what a term of tutoring should be doing, so each programme below is described by what it demands rather than by its brochure wording.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary
programmes.description: The three years before an IGCSE option choice, usually taught as general science rather than separate physics. Checkpoint tests sit at the end of Year 9 in March, May and October windows. Work here is descriptive: observe, record, explain in a sentence. Almost none of it asks a student to rearrange a formula or convert a prefix, which is precisely why the jump into 0625 surprises families.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai this is where the science groups split. A student placed in the lower set in Year 9 is often routed towards Core 0625 or Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 without the family realising a decision has been taken. A term of numerical confidence work in Year 9 is usually cheaper and easier than fighting a tier change in Year 11.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics (0625)
programmes.description: Two years, six topic areas, two tiers. Core candidates sit Papers 1 and 3 and are capped at grade C. Extended candidates sit Papers 2 and 4 and can reach A*. Both tiers add a practical component, either the laboratory Paper 5 or the written Paper 6. The syllabus covers motion, forces and energy; thermal physics; waves; electricity and magnetism; nuclear physics; and space physics.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai centres differ on whether they enter candidates for Paper 5 or Paper 6, and on when they run mocks. Both decisions sit with the school, not with you, so the practical question to ask your head of science is which practical paper the centre enters and in which series. Everything about revision sequencing follows from the answer.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS & A Level
programmes.description: The post-16 route most Dubai British schools offer alongside or instead of the IB Diploma. A Level Physics assumes fluency with everything 0625 treated as new: vectors, graph gradients, exponential decay, and algebraic rearrangement under time pressure. Students who reached grade A on 0625 by memorising worked examples rather than by understanding method are the ones who stall in the first term.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools require a grade A or B at Extended 0625 before admitting a student to AS Physics. If that threshold is the live question in your house, the tutoring brief is narrow and measurable: lift the specific paper that the entry requirement is read from, and get there before the school's internal deadline rather than after results day.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: The other post-16 fork, offered by a large share of Dubai's international schools. DP Physics at Standard or Higher Level rewards the experimental write-up and the data analysis far more heavily than 0625 does, and it expects uncertainty handling that IGCSE barely touches. The internal assessment is the student's own investigation, marked at school and moderated by the IB.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai families often choose between A Level and the Diploma during Year 11, while 0625 revision is in full flow. The useful 0625 work in that term is the practical paper, because the measurement, uncertainty and graph skills in Paper 5 or Paper 6 are the ones DP Physics picks up and extends immediately.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-physics-0625-home-.subjectsIntro: Physics 0625 is rarely the only pressure point in a Year 10 or Year 11 timetable in Dubai. These are the Cambridge codes most often requested alongside it, with the specific place each one tends to lose marks.

subjects.name: Physics (0625)
subjects.description: Six topic areas, two written papers plus a practical component. Marks concentrate in electricity and magnetism and in motion, forces and energy. The reliable leak is numerical: prefix conversion, significant figures and equation rearrangement under time pressure, not conceptual misunderstanding.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620)
subjects.description: Twelve topic areas running from states of matter to organic chemistry. Stoichiometry is the gatekeeper: a student who cannot move confidently between moles, mass and concentration will lose marks in six separate topics, which is why 0620 grades often sit a band below 0625 grades for the same student.

subjects.name: Biology (0610)
subjects.description: The widest recall load of the three sciences, with twenty-one topic areas. Marks go on precision of language rather than on calculation: diffusion described instead of defined, an enzyme answer that never mentions active site shape, a transport answer that leaves out the direction of movement.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (0654)
subjects.description: Biology, chemistry and physics in one double-award qualification, with each discipline covered to less depth than its separate syllabus. Students move onto it to protect option-block space. The physics content overlaps 0625 heavily but the paper structure differs, so past-paper choice matters.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: The subject that silently determines a physics grade. Rearranging v squared equals u squared plus two a s, handling standard form, reading a gradient from a non-linear axis: all of it is 0580 content being examined inside 0625. Fixing the maths usually lifts both grades.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Taken by stronger Dubai sets in Year 11 alongside 0580, and a strong predictor of comfort in AS Physics. Calculus and function work here makes the graph interpretation in Paper 4 feel routine. Students carrying both 0606 and 0625 need session timing planned around the heavier week.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Frequently paired with physics by Dubai students heading towards engineering. The logic-gate and binary content shares reasoning habits with the electronics parts of 0625, and both papers punish partial method: an answer with the right idea and no working attracts few marks.

subjects.name: Design and Technology (0445)
subjects.description: Carries coursework, unlike 0625, which means a Year 11 student holding both faces a coursework deadline during physics revision season. Worth mapping in September so the practical paper preparation does not collide with the design submission week.

subjects.name: First Language English (0500)
subjects.description: The command-term work that helps physics lives here. Students who read describe, explain, suggest and compare as interchangeable in an English paper read them the same way in Paper 4, and the mark scheme does not forgive it.

subjects.name: Geography (0460)
subjects.description: Shares the graph, scale and data-description skills that Paper 6 tests. A student who can describe a trend from a climate graph can usually describe one from a cooling curve, once someone shows them the two tasks are the same task.

sections.heading: What a 0625 home tutor search in Dubai actually turns up
paragraphs: Type cambridge IGCSE physics 0625 home tutor in Dubai into Google and three kinds of result come back: agencies that will send a qualified adult to your villa, marketplaces listing independent tutors by neighbourhood, and online platforms. Prices for the first group run from roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour once travel is inside the number, and the pool is whoever lives close enough to reach you by 17:00. The second group is cheaper and entirely unvetted. The third group is where we sit, and it is worth being exact about why.

Physics at Extended tier is a narrow specialism. The adult who can teach a Year 9 general science lesson well is not automatically the adult who can tell you that your son's Paper 4 marks are going on prefix conversion rather than on the physics. There are not many 0625 Extended specialists in any one Dubai community, and geography should not be the filter that decides which one your child gets. Removing the drive removes the radius, and the radius is the only reason an in-home search narrows your choice at all.

The honest trade-off is real and worth stating. An adult in the room can take a phone off a desk, notice a slumped shoulder, and keep a reluctant fifteen-year-old sitting down. A screen cannot do that as well. For a student who needs supervision more than they need physics, in-home has a genuine advantage, and we will say so on a call rather than sell past it. For a student who needs the specific marks on their specific script identified and repaired, the specialist matters more than the proximity, and that is the case this page is making.

Online qualified subject tutor: roughly AED 150-300 per hour across the market

sections.heading: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625: the papers, the minutes and the marks
paragraphs: Everything about sensible revision follows from knowing which three papers your child is actually entered for. Cambridge IGCSE Physics is tiered. A Core candidate sits Paper 1 and Paper 3 and is capped at grade C. An Extended candidate sits Paper 2 and Paper 4 and can reach A*. Both then add one practical component: Paper 5, the laboratory test, or Paper 6, the written alternative to practical. The centre chooses which practical route it offers, and parents are frequently unaware a choice was made.

The weightings are the part worth memorising. The multiple-choice paper carries thirty per cent of the grade in forty questions, which means each question is worth a little under one per cent and a careless minute is expensive. The theory paper carries half the grade over eighty marks in seventy-five minutes, so the working rate is just over a mark a minute with no slack for a long detour. The practical component carries the remaining fifth. Students who treat Paper 6 as an afterthought are discarding a fifth of the grade in the component with the most predictable mark scheme in the whole syllabus.

The topic structure is six areas: motion, forces and energy; thermal physics; waves; electricity and magnetism; nuclear physics; and space physics. Those are not equally weighted in practice. Across recent Extended papers, motion and energy together with electricity and magnetism take the largest share of marks, while space physics and nuclear physics are smaller but highly predictable, which makes them the most efficient topics to secure first. Confirm the content and the paper arrangement for your child's series on the syllabus document at cambridgeinternational.org, because Cambridge revises syllabuses on a cycle and the version your school teaches is the one that counts.

sections.heading: The five causes of lost marks, and how each one shows on a script
paragraphs: Marking a few hundred 0625 scripts makes the pattern hard to miss. Lost marks almost never come from a student who has no idea what is happening. They come from five repeatable causes, and each leaves a different fingerprint on the page. The point of naming them is that each one has a different and much shorter repair than reteaching a topic.

The first is a definition not known. The answer gestures at the right idea in the student's own words and the mark scheme wanted a specific phrase, so a two-mark definition scores one or zero. The second is an equation not recalled, which shows as a blank space or a half-remembered symbol string followed by a correct-looking number that cannot be arrived at. The third is a substitution error: the right equation, the right rearrangement, and a value put in from the wrong line of the question. The fourth is a unit or prefix slip, which is the biggest single leak in this syllabus and shows as answers out by factors of a thousand, kilojoules treated as joules, centimetres never converted to metres.

The fifth is the command term. Describe wants what happens; explain wants why; suggest invites a reasoned possibility; compare requires both sides named in the same sentence. A student who reads all four as write what you know will produce a page of accurate physics and collect a fraction of the marks. That one is fixable in about two sessions, and it is usually worth more marks than any topic revision you could do in the same time. Which is why the cause list, and not the topic list, is what drives the plan.
bullets: Definition not known: specific mark-scheme wording missing from a correct idea
Equation not recalled: blank working with a plausible final number
Substitution error: correct method, value taken from the wrong line
Unit or prefix slip: answers out by factors of a thousand
Command term misread: accurate physics that answers a different question

sections.heading: Home tutor or online tutor for Dubai physics: what actually changes
paragraphs: The comparison most Dubai families are making is not online versus in-home in the abstract. It is this tutor who can reach my community versus that tutor who cannot. Once the question is put that way, the variables worth comparing are cost, the size of the pool you choose from, what happens to a diagram during the lesson, and what survives the lesson afterwards.

Travel is the hidden cost. An in-home rate quoted at AED 250 for sixty minutes includes a drive that may run forty minutes each way on a weekday evening, which is time you are paying for inside the hourly number. The same AED 250 paid for an online hour buys sixty minutes of a specialist's attention and no driving. That is before the second effect, which is availability: a tutor who is not driving can offer the 19:30 slot to a Marina family and the 20:30 slot to an Al Qusais family on the same evening, so the hard-to-fill times are easier to get.

Then there is the artefact. Physics is taught on a diagram, and a diagram drawn on a kitchen pad belongs to whoever picks the pad up. On a shared screen the circuit, the ray trace and the velocity-time graph are annotated in colour, saved, and sent with the session notes. A student revising in April can reopen the exact diagram from October. That matters more in this subject than in most, because the marks in waves and electricity are very often diagram marks.

The table below is the market, assembled from rates those providers publish themselves and from Bestimate's Dubai tutoring cost table. None of these figures is an IB Gram price list. They are here so you can recognise an outlier when you are quoted one.

Read the bands as what you are buying rather than as a quality ladder. The budget band is generally a university student or a recent graduate working from the textbook, which can be entirely adequate for a Year 9 student consolidating general science and is rarely enough for Extended Paper 4 under timing. The middle band buys a qualified subject teacher. The specialist band buys someone who knows the 0625 mark scheme well enough to tell you which specific wording scored and which did not. The premium band at the top is named individuals and examiner-marketed tutors, and that is also the band where claims need the most scrutiny.

Two pieces of local context make the numbers mean something. Dubai's private school fees were frozen for the 2026-27 academic year, confirmed by KHDA in May 2026 under the emirate's economic incentives package, so a tutoring budget set last year has not been squeezed by a fee rise this year. And Dubai has 227 private schools serving 387,441 students across seventeen curricula, with the UK curriculum taking the largest share of enrolment, which is why physics tutoring demand in this city clusters hard around Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE rather than around any single school's internal scheme. For our own pricing, the next step is the free trial lesson and a short consultation rather than a published table, because the right session length and frequency for a Core Year 10 student and an Extended Year 11 student eight weeks from a series are not the same product.

sections.heading: Eight weeks of 0625 on paper: the evidence file
paragraphs: Progress in physics is not smooth and does not announce itself in a report card. A student can spend three weeks fixing prefix conversion and show no grade change at all, because the mark gain is hidden behind an untouched second problem. The only way to see it is to write it down. The sequence below is how a typical eight-week block runs, and what lands in your inbox at each stage.

The first fortnight produces the ranked cause list, built from one timed paper sat under exam conditions. Weeks three to six attack the top two causes only, which is the hardest discipline in the whole process: a parent watching a tutor spend four weeks on units and command terms while the school teaches nuclear physics will reasonably ask why. The answer is arithmetic. Repairing an eleven-mark leak is worth more than adding a four-mark topic, and it transfers to every paper afterwards.

Week seven is a full paper under timing, marked the same way as the first one, with the two cause lists side by side. That document is the point of the exercise. It shows whether the marks moved, where they moved from, and what the next block should attack. If the top cause has not moved by week seven, something in the approach is wrong, and we would rather find that in week seven than in a results envelope. No tutor can promise a grade; what can be promised is that you will know, every fortnight, exactly where the marks stand.

sections.heading: Paper 6: the cheapest fifth of the grade to recover
paragraphs: The alternative to practical carries a fifth of the IGCSE Physics grade and is, by a wide margin, the most predictable paper in the syllabus. It asks a student to read a scale, tabulate results, plot points, draw a line, identify a source of error and suggest an improvement. The same half-dozen tasks recur series after series. Despite that, it is the paper most Dubai students revise last, usually because the school teaches practical skills inside lessons rather than as a revision topic with its own past papers.

The marks lost on it are mechanical and fixable in a handful of sessions. Scales read to the wrong precision. A results table with inconsistent decimal places, which costs a mark before any physics is done. Axes chosen so the plotted points occupy a third of the grid, which costs the scale mark. A line of best fit drawn through the first and last points instead of through the trend. An improvement suggested as be more careful, which earns nothing because it is not a change to the method.

The error-and-improvement questions have their own grammar, and that is learnable. An acceptable source of error names a specific measurement and why it was imprecise. An acceptable improvement names a specific change that would reduce that imprecision: repeat and average, use a larger distance, insulate the beaker, view the scale at eye level to avoid parallax. Four to six sessions spent purely on this component is a smaller investment than any topic rescue, and it operates on a full fifth of the grade. For a student sitting Paper 5 in the school laboratory instead, the written preparation is similar but the timing work differs, so confirm the entry with the head of science before planning the block.
bullets: Tabulate with consistent decimal places before plotting anything
Choose a scale that fills more than half the grid in both directions
Name the specific measurement when asked for a source of error
An improvement must change the method, not the student's attitude

sections.heading: Counting backwards from a Cambridge series
paragraphs: Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October windows. The decisions that shape your child's result sit months before the exam, and almost all of them belong to the school rather than to you. The useful habit is to work backwards from the series date and ask the centre a specific question at each milestone.

Cambridge's published key dates for its March 2027 series show how far ahead the chain runs: the examination period is 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries are due on 27 November 2026, forecast grades are due on 27 February 2027, results reach centres on Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June. The March series is not the series UAE centres use, but it is the clearest worked example available of a deadline sitting more than two months before a paper is sat. Apply the same arithmetic to a June entry and the conversation with your head of science about tier and practical route needs to happen in the autumn term, not in the spring.

One administrative detail is worth knowing because it has consequences. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable for each. Its own guidance states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after the wrong zone timetable was used. Ask the exams officer which zone your child's school sits in and work from that timetable alone, not from a PDF a friend forwarded from another country. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, which several Dubai schools use instead, runs in May or June and in November, publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, and issued its June 2026 results to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026.
bullets: Confirm your child's zone timetable with the exams officer, not from a forwarded file
Ask in the autumn term which tier and which practical paper the centre will enter
Final entries close months before the paper; tier changes close with them
Work the revision plan backwards from the series, not forwards from today

sections.heading: What a 0625 tutor may and may not do
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE Physics has no coursework component, which removes the sharpest academic-honesty question from this subject. The marks all come from examinations sat under supervision at the centre. That does not leave the question of boundaries empty, and it is worth knowing where the lines sit before you hire anyone, because the market around these queries contains providers who cross them.

A tutor teaches, questions, marks and explains. A tutor does not sit a paper, does not supply material a centre has not released, and does not produce work that a student will submit as their own. For subjects that do carry an internal assessment or coursework, including the sciences at IB Diploma level, the same rule holds in a sharper form: a tutor may teach the method, discuss the plan and give feedback on a student's own draft, and may never write, complete or redraft it to submission. Any provider offering to produce an internal assessment is offering a malpractice route, and the student carries the consequence.

Two practical points round this out. First, syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are Cambridge's copyright material; a tutor should reference them and point to the official source rather than hand over a folder of redistributed PDFs. Second, private tutoring in the UAE is permitted but regulated. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years, with eligibility extending to registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals offering private tutoring in the UAE without that permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any page quoting a specific figure with caution. The application route is MoHRE's own service page for private tutor licensing.

sections.heading: KHDA, the school report and what an inspection band means for physics
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects schools and publishes a banded judgement, from Outstanding down to Very Weak, which families read as a league table. For a physics parent, the band is less useful than the detail underneath it, because an Outstanding school can still have a Year 11 physics set taught by a non-specialist in a year when recruitment went badly.

The more useful question for a 0625 family is what the school's own data says about this subject and this cohort. Ask for the physics set's internal assessment pattern, who is teaching it this year, and how mock grades have mapped onto final grades in the last two series at that centre. A school with a consistent pattern of mocks sitting a grade below finals is marking harshly on purpose, and a panic over a mock result in that context is wasted energy. A school where mocks have historically overstated the final grade is the one where a November mock at grade six deserves immediate attention.

Two further pieces of Dubai context shape the market your family is shopping in. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate will not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. And the sector keeps expanding: the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four following a UK curriculum and three offering the International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose six per cent. More UK-curriculum places means more 0625 candidates each year, which is exactly why specialist availability in the weeks before a series tightens, and why an early booking is worth more than a late one.
