process.title: Send the last marked script
process.description: Not the report card, the actual paper. A photograph of each page is enough. The script tells a physics specialist in ten minutes what a conversation takes an hour to approximate, and it means the first session can start from evidence rather than from introductions.

process.title: A short call about the paper, not the price
process.description: Twenty minutes to establish tier, centre, practical route, series and what the school has said. We will tell you on this call if the problem looks like supervision rather than physics, because in that case an online specialist is the wrong purchase and you should hear that before paying.

process.title: A free trial lesson with a diagnostic set
process.description: One full session at no cost and with no card details taken. Your child works through a short set of Extended questions chosen to separate recall problems from method problems, and you receive the marked set afterwards whether or not you continue with us.

process.title: Fix the slot around the school timetable
process.description: Sessions run on Gulf Standard Time at a fixed weekday or weekend hour, chosen around the school run, activities and the school's own assessment calendar. Mock weeks are planned around in advance rather than rescheduled in a hurry when they arrive.

process.title: A marked return every fortnight
process.description: A timed section sat, marked against the mark scheme, tagged by cause, and returned with a running topic tally. At week seven the full paper and the two cause lists go side by side, which is the document that decides what the next block does.

whyPoints.title: Marking comes before teaching
whyPoints.description: The first thing that happens is a paper sat under timing and marked against the published scheme. Everything after that is chosen from the cause list it produces. It is slower to start and considerably faster to move marks than beginning with chapter one.

whyPoints.title: Matched by syllabus code, not by subject label
whyPoints.description: Physics 0625 Extended, Physics 0625 Core, Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 and Pearson 4PH1 are different papers with different mark schemes. The match is made on the code your child's centre has entered them for, which is the question we ask before anything else.

whyPoints.title: The work stays the student's own
whyPoints.description: A tutor explains, questions, marks and models method. A tutor never produces work a student will hand in. In this subject that mostly means practice papers are your child's handwriting and nobody else's, which is also the only way the marked diagnosis means anything.

whyPoints.title: A written record you can use elsewhere
whyPoints.description: Marked scripts, cause lists and topic tallies accumulate into something you can take to a parents' evening and set beside the school's data. Families use it most often to open a conversation about tier entry or set placement with specific numbers attached.

whyPoints.title: Honest about delivery and about availability
whyPoints.description: Lessons are live online over video; we do not place tutors in UAE homes. When no Extended 0625 specialist is free in the slot you need, you will be told that and offered the alternatives rather than matched with whoever is available that evening.

faqs.question: My son's 0625 mock came back at 48 per cent. What should I send a tutor first?
faqs.answer: Send the script itself, page by page, rather than the grade. A percentage tells a physics specialist almost nothing: 48 per cent on Extended Paper 4 could be a student who lost eleven marks to prefix conversion and otherwise understands the syllabus, or one who has not secured a single definition in electricity. Those need different terms of work. With the marked paper in hand, a tutor can tag the lost marks by cause within about ten minutes and tell you on the first call whether this is a content problem, a method problem or an exam-technique problem. Photographs of each page are perfectly adequate.

faqs.question: Which mark scheme do you mark my child's 0625 practice papers against?
faqs.answer: Against the published Cambridge mark scheme for the paper your child sat, with the relevant wording quoted back in the margin so you can see exactly which phrase earned the mark and which one did not. That matters more than a total. A student who writes the current gets bigger instead of the current increases has produced the right idea and the wrong answer, and seeing the two side by side fixes it in one session. We reference and point to official Cambridge sources rather than redistributing syllabus or paper documents, which are Cambridge copyright material.

faqs.question: Does an in-home physics tutor in Dubai really cost more than an online one?
faqs.answer: In this market, yes, and the difference is mostly travel. Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180 to 350 an hour, and independent home tutors commonly quote AED 200 to 500, with the drive built into the number. Online rates for a qualified subject tutor run around AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150. Those are the market's published figures, not an IB Gram price list. The practical effect of the gap is roughly one extra session a month for the same monthly spend.

faqs.question: Can my daughter move from Core to Extended 0625 during Year 11?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the deadline is administrative rather than academic. Tier is part of the entry the centre submits to Cambridge, and final entries close months before the examination period. Once that window shuts, the tier is fixed for that series. So the conversation to have with the head of science is in the autumn term, not after a spring mock. Bring evidence: a marked Extended paper section showing she can access the grades above C is a far stronger case than a request. If the window has closed, the realistic options are the next series or a different route post-16.

faqs.question: Is Paper 5 or Paper 6 better for my child, and do we get to choose?
faqs.answer: The centre chooses, not the family. Paper 5 is the practical test sat in the school laboratory over seventy-five minutes; Paper 6 is the written alternative to practical over sixty minutes. Both carry a fifth of the grade and both examine the same skills: reading instruments, tabulating, plotting, identifying error, suggesting improvement. Students who are confident with apparatus often prefer Paper 5; students who freeze with equipment in front of them usually score better on the written route. Ask your head of science which one the centre enters, because the revision work differs in timing even though the content overlaps heavily.

faqs.question: How many marks does a unit or prefix slip actually cost across a 0625 paper?
faqs.answer: On the scripts we mark it is routinely the largest single leak, and it compounds because the same habit recurs in every numerical topic. Centimetres left unconverted in a density calculation, kilojoules treated as joules in a thermal question, milliamps entered as amps in a circuit question: each is one or two marks, and a paper can hold half a dozen of them. The repair is mechanical rather than conceptual, usually two sessions plus short drills, and it transfers to every paper your child sits afterwards. Which is why it generally gets attacked before any topic revision.

faqs.question: What does calculate want in 0625 that determine does not?
faqs.answer: Calculate expects a numerical answer reached by working you can see, with the unit attached. Determine often expects you to extract a value from supplied data or a graph first, then use it, so the reading step itself carries marks. Describe asks what happens; explain asks why, and an answer with no causal link scores nothing even when every fact in it is correct. Suggest invites a reasoned possibility rather than a remembered fact. A student who treats these as interchangeable writes accurate physics and collects a fraction of the marks available, and two focused sessions usually corrects it.

faqs.question: My child understands physics in class but freezes in the exam. Is that a 0625 content problem?
faqs.answer: Usually not. Freezing shows up as a specific pattern on a script: strong early questions, blank or abandoned working in the second half, and marks lost on long structured items rather than on multiple choice. That is a timing and sequencing problem. The theory paper runs at just over a mark a minute across eighty marks in seventy-five minutes, so a four-minute detour on one part costs the last question entirely. The work is timed sections rather than more content: question triage, a rule for abandoning a stuck part, and practice at the real rate rather than untimed at the kitchen table.

faqs.question: How soon after starting should I expect to see the grade move?
faqs.answer: Expect to see the marks move before the grade does, and expect to see it in writing at week seven. A fortnight of repair work on unit conversion can lift a paper total by eight or nine marks without crossing a grade boundary, which looks like nothing on a report and is substantial progress. That is exactly why the week-seven document puts the first and second cause lists side by side. No tutor can promise a grade in a given series, and anyone who does is selling something they cannot deliver. What is reliable is that you will know where the marks stand every fortnight.

faqs.question: Do your physics tutors hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit?
faqs.answer: Ask, and check, for any tutor you consider anywhere in this market. The UAE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE, granted free of charge for two years, with eligibility covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Where a tutor is resident in the UAE and giving private lessons here, that is the relevant document. Individuals tutoring in the UAE without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published.

faqs.question: We live in Mirdif and weekday evenings are tight. What time can a 0625 session start?
faqs.answer: From around 18:30 on a weekday is the realistic answer for most Mirdif and Al Warqa families, because two school runs and an activity slot usually occupy the window before that. Saturday morning is the single most requested slot of the week among Year 11 families in that part of Dubai, so it books out earliest. Because lessons are delivered online, the start time is set by your household rather than by a tutor's route across the city, which is the main scheduling advantage: a 19:30 slot is as easy to staff as a 16:30 one.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor take 0625 Physics and 0580 Maths for one child?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and in this particular pairing it is frequently the better arrangement. A large share of lost physics marks are really maths marks: rearranging an equation, handling standard form, reading a gradient off an awkward axis. A tutor who sees both papers can fix the algebra inside the physics question rather than treating them as separate projects. The limit is time, not capability. Two subjects at Extended tier in Year 11 need two slots a week, and a single session split between them tends to do neither properly in the weeks before a series.

faqs.question: What happens if no Extended 0625 specialist is free in the slot we need?
faqs.answer: You get told. The honest position is that physics at Extended tier is a narrow specialism and the weeks before a June or November series are when availability tightens, because every centre's candidates want the same evenings. If the slot you need is unavailable, the options are a different time with the right specialist, a waiting position for the slot you want, or a referral elsewhere. What will not happen is a match with a generalist presented as a physics specialist, which is the quiet failure mode across this market.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start 0625 work in February before a June series?
faqs.answer: No, but the work changes shape. February is too late to reteach six topic areas and early enough to repair exam technique, secure the predictable topics and recover the practical paper. In that window the sensible plan is a diagnostic paper in the first week, then the top two mark-loss causes, then Paper 6 as a self-contained block because it is a fifth of the grade with the most predictable mark scheme in the syllabus. What February cannot absorb is a tier change, since final entries close months before the examination period.

faqs.question: Should we wait for the November series instead of entering in June?
faqs.answer: That decision belongs to the school, and it is driven by entry deadlines rather than by readiness. Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and the entry window for each closes well in advance, so a deferral is a conversation to have with the exams officer early rather than a choice to make after a disappointing mock. Weigh it against the post-16 timetable too: a November result arrives after most Dubai sixth-form and Diploma places have been offered, which can matter more than the extra months of preparation.

A useful question to put to any of them: which part of the electricity topic do Dubai students most often get almost right, and what does the mark scheme want instead? The specificity of the answer is the signal.

intro.heading: Six topic areas, and only two of them usually need the work
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE Physics is organised into six areas: motion, forces and energy; thermal physics; waves; electricity and magnetism; nuclear physics; and space physics. A student struggling with the subject is almost never struggling with all six. In the scripts that come to us from Dubai schools, the marks cluster: electricity and magnetism and the graph work inside motion take the bulk of the losses, waves takes a steady smaller share, and thermal, nuclear and space physics are usually lost through non-revision rather than non-understanding. That distribution is the reason a topic-by-topic page is more useful than a general one.

It also changes what a term of tutoring should look like. Reteaching a syllabus from the start is the default instinct and almost always the wrong purchase, because it spends the same number of hours on the areas that are already secure as on the ones that are not. A better sequence is: establish which two areas are leaking, fix those to the standard the mark scheme asks for, then sweep the predictable small areas for easy marks, then spend the remaining weeks on timing. The order matters because the first two steps transfer and the last one does not.

The other half of the problem is tier. Core and Extended share a syllabus structure and differ in content depth and in grade ceiling. A Core candidate sits Paper 1 and Paper 3 and cannot be awarded above a grade C. An Extended candidate sits Paper 2 and Paper 4 and reaches A* at the top. Revising Extended content for a Core paper wastes weeks; revising Core content for an Extended paper leaves marks on the table in exactly the sections that separate a six from an eight. Before any plan is made, the tier your child's centre has entered needs confirming, and that answer sits with the head of science.

Delivery is worth being direct about on a page with online in the URL. Physics lessons for Dubai students run live over video, one tutor and one student, with a shared screen carrying the circuit diagrams, the ray traces and the graph paper. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; visiting tuition is something we run only in India. For this subject the online format has a specific advantage that goes beyond logistics: a circuit drawn on a shared screen can be redrawn, recoloured, labelled and saved in seconds, and your child can reopen the exact diagram in April that was built in October.

What follows is the syllabus in the order a tutor would tackle it, a Core-versus-Extended comparison, a table of what one session fixes for each common presenting problem, and the board distinction between Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1 that decides which past papers are worth your child's time.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-physics-0625-onlin.programmesIntro: Four routes a Dubai science student may be sitting on, described by what each one assesses rather than by how it is marketed. The physics content overlaps between them; the papers do not, and that is what decides revision material.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics
programmes.description: Separate-science physics across six topic areas, examined entirely by written and practical papers with no coursework. Two tiers, Core and Extended, sitting different question papers from the same syllabus. Extended adds depth rather than new topics in most areas: more algebra, more multi-step calculation, more questions that require two ideas combined in one answer.
programmes.countryNote: The default science route in Dubai's selective British schools and the upper sets of larger ones. If your child is taking three separate sciences in Year 10 at a Dubai school, 0625 is almost certainly one of them, and the physics grade is usually the one most sensitive to maths fluency.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Co-ordinated Sciences
programmes.description: A double award covering biology, chemistry and physics in the space of two IGCSEs. The physics content is a reduced version of 0625 with the same conceptual spine. Students sit combined papers, so a question sequence can move from respiration to circuits within a few pages, which tests recall switching in a way the separate papers do not.
programmes.countryNote: Chosen in Dubai mainly to free an option block for a language, a creative subject or Additional Mathematics. The practical consequence for revision is that 0625 past papers contain material your child will not be examined on, so paper selection has to be deliberate rather than whatever comes up in a search.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics
programmes.description: The other board several Dubai schools use. Same subject, different paper architecture, different formula provision and different mark-scheme habits. Students sit two written papers rather than the Cambridge three-component pattern, and the practical skills are assessed within the written papers rather than through a separate component.
programmes.countryNote: The single most common revision error we see in Dubai is a student working through the other board's past papers because a search result or a sibling's folder offered them. Confirm the board and the specification code with the school, then revise from that board alone.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS Level Physics
programmes.description: Where 0625 leads for most Dubai British-school students who continue the subject. AS Physics assumes the IGCSE equations as background rather than as content, and introduces vectors resolved properly, uncertainty propagation and the practical paper as a formal skills assessment. The gap is largest for students who reached a high 0625 grade by pattern-matching worked examples.
programmes.countryNote: Entry to AS Physics at several Dubai schools is set at a grade A or B at Extended 0625. Where that threshold is the live issue, the tutoring brief is narrow and dated: lift the specific paper the requirement is read from, before the school's internal deadline.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-physics-0625-onlin.subjectsIntro: The codes most often requested alongside Physics 0625 by Dubai families, with what each one actually assesses. The pairing matters: several of these share skills with physics closely enough that work in one lifts the other.

subjects.name: Physics (0625)
subjects.description: Six topic areas examined over three components. Assesses recall of defined quantities, equation selection and rearrangement, graph interpretation and experimental reasoning. Extended questions commonly require two ideas combined, such as using a graph gradient to find acceleration and then applying a force relationship to it.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: Assesses number, algebra, geometry and statistics. The algebra and graph sections are examined again inside physics questions without being labelled as maths, which is why a student who is secure here rarely fails physics on method and a student who is not usually does.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620)
subjects.description: Twelve topic areas from states of matter to organic chemistry. Assesses calculation through stoichiometry, pattern reasoning through the Periodic Table, and precise mechanism description. Shares the practical-paper skills with physics almost exactly, so Paper 6 work in one board subject transfers.

subjects.name: Biology (0610)
subjects.description: Twenty-one topic areas with the heaviest recall load of the three sciences. Assesses definitional precision far more than calculation. Students who score well in physics by reasoning often underperform here until they accept that a biology answer needs the exact term, not an equivalent one.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Assesses functions, calculus, trigonometry and series at a level above 0580. Dubai students holding both 0606 and 0625 generally find the Extended graph and rate-of-change questions straightforward, and need session planning around whichever subject has the heavier week.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Assesses algorithmic reasoning, data representation and logic gates. The logic and binary content shares its habits of thought with the electronics sections of physics, and both subjects reward method shown over answers asserted.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (0654)
subjects.description: Assesses all three sciences to reduced depth across combined papers. The physics sections examine the same core relationships as 0625 with fewer multi-step calculations, and the paper layout means a revision plan built from separate-science papers will overshoot.

subjects.name: Mathematics for the IB MYP
subjects.description: Assessed against criteria rather than by paper weighting, with investigation and real-life application tasks. Dubai students moving from MYP into a Cambridge IGCSE physics set mid-ladder often need explicit work on timed written technique, which MYP assesses differently.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510)
subjects.description: Assesses reading, writing, listening and speaking for students for whom English is additional. Relevant to physics because command terms and multi-clause question stems are a language problem before they are a physics one, and that is a fixable one.

subjects.name: Geography (0460)
subjects.description: Assesses data response, graph and map interpretation and extended reasoning. The skills in its data questions map directly onto the practical paper in physics: describe the trend, quote figures with units, identify an anomaly, suggest a cause.

sections.heading: What an online 0625 tutor does in a sixty-minute session
paragraphs: A cambridge IGCSE physics 0625 online tutor in Dubai is being hired to do four things in an hour, and a session that does all four is doing too much. The four are: establish what is actually wrong, teach the piece that is missing, make the student produce something against the mark scheme, and leave behind work that can be done without the tutor present. A good session does two of those properly.

In practice the shape is: ten minutes on the questions set last week, with the student talking through their own working rather than the tutor reading it; twenty-five minutes of teaching on the one thing the diagnosis says matters, built on the shared screen in diagrams rather than in sentences; fifteen minutes of the student writing an answer under something close to exam timing while the tutor watches the pen rather than the face; and ten minutes agreeing what happens before the next session. The watching part is where online delivery earns its place. A shared screen with the student's working visible shows a tutor the exact moment a rearrangement went wrong, which a finished answer never does.

What a session cannot do is cover a topic. Electricity and magnetism is weeks of content; an hour is one idea taken properly, such as why current is the same everywhere in a series circuit and what that forces to be true about the potential differences. A parent judging value by ground covered will always prefer the tutor who races, and the race is why the same marks keep going missing in March. One idea, properly secured, with a question answered to mark-scheme standard, is the correct output of sixty minutes.

One idea per session, taken to the tier's required depth

sections.heading: The six topic areas, and what each one is really assessing
paragraphs: Treating the syllabus as six equal blocks is the most common planning error. They differ in mark share, in how predictable the question style is, and in how much maths sits inside them. The table below sets out what each area assesses and the specific way marks go missing in it, which is the information that lets you put revision time where it pays.

Two patterns in that table are worth saying out loud. The first is that the heaviest areas, motion and electricity, are also the most mathematical, so a physics problem in those areas is very often a maths problem wearing physics clothing. The second is that the lightest areas, nuclear and space physics, have the narrowest range of question types in the whole syllabus. Decay equations, half-life reasoning, orbital relationships and the life cycle of a star come round in recognisable forms series after series. For a student short of time, those are the cheapest marks available anywhere on the paper.

Waves sits awkwardly between the two. It carries a moderate mark share and its questions are highly diagram-dependent: refraction at a boundary, ray construction through a lens, wavefront spacing. Students lose marks there not through misunderstanding but through drawing: a normal omitted, an angle measured from the surface instead of from the normal, arrows missing from a ray. Those are drawing conventions, learnable in a session, and they are exactly the kind of mark that a verbal explanation of the physics never recovers.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: what actually differs, and what it costs
paragraphs: Tier is the single decision with the largest effect on a 0625 result, and most Dubai families only discover it was made when a mock paper arrives with a different number on it. Core and Extended share the six topic areas and diverge on depth, on question architecture and on the grade available at the end. A Core candidate can be awarded grades C to G. An Extended candidate can be awarded A* to E. There is no route from a Core paper to a grade B, however well the paper is sat.

The content difference is not a longer list of topics. It is that Extended questions ask for more steps in one answer, more algebraic rearrangement, and more explanation in causal rather than descriptive terms. A Core question about a circuit may ask for a current given a voltage and a resistance. The Extended version of that question gives a combination of resistors, asks for the total, then the current, then the potential difference across one branch, and awards the final mark only to an answer with a unit. A student who can do the Core version is not automatically four steps from the Extended one.

The decision has a deadline, and it is administrative. Tier forms part of the entry a centre submits to Cambridge, and final entries close well before the examination period: for the March 2027 series, Cambridge's published key dates put final entries on 27 November 2026 against an examination period of 3 February to 4 March 2027. The same arithmetic applies to a June entry. If a tier change is the live question in your household, it belongs in an autumn-term conversation with the head of science, supported by a marked Extended paper section, not in a spring email after a disappointing mock.

sections.heading: Electricity and magnetism: the biggest block of marks
paragraphs: If a Dubai student is losing marks in 0625, the odds favour this topic. It carries a large share of the paper, it is the most calculation-dense area in the syllabus, and almost all of its difficulty is concentrated in two ideas that are easy to half-learn. The first is the behaviour of series and parallel arrangements. The second is electromagnetic induction, which students routinely explain in terms of magnets being near wires rather than in terms of a changing field.

The series and parallel problem has a precise shape. Students memorise that current stays the same in series and splits in parallel, and voltage splits in series and stays the same in parallel, as four facts rather than as two consequences. Under exam pressure the four facts swap. The repair is not more memorising, it is one session establishing why current must be identical at every point in a single loop, after which the rest follows and cannot be swapped. The resistance combination rules then stop being arbitrary, and the reciprocal formula for parallel resistors stops being a thing to be recalled and becomes something that can be reconstructed.

Induction is the other reliable leak, and it is a language problem as much as a physics one. The mark scheme wants a change: the field through the coil changes, so a voltage is induced; faster change gives a larger induced voltage; no relative movement gives nothing. Students write that the magnet is inside the coil and the coil makes electricity, which contains no change and earns nothing. One session on the word change, applied to the generator, the transformer and the moving-wire demonstration, usually converts several marks on every subsequent paper. Prefixes complete the picture: milliamps, kilovolts and megaohms appear constantly in this topic, and an unconverted prefix turns a correct method into a wrong answer.
bullets: Establish why current is identical around a single loop before any rule is memorised
Rebuild the resistance combinations as consequences rather than formulae
Induction answers must name a change in field, not a position
Convert every prefix before substituting, as a written habit

sections.heading: Motion and energy: graphs are where the marks actually are
paragraphs: The motion, forces and energy area carries the other large block of marks, and inside it the graph questions are the most reliable source of loss. A distance-time graph and a speed-time graph look similar and mean different things. On the first, the gradient is a speed and the area underneath means nothing. On the second, the gradient is an acceleration and the area underneath is a distance. Students who have learned gradient equals speed as a single rule apply it to both and lose a run of marks in one question.

Reading the gradient is itself a technique with marks attached. The examiner wants a large triangle drawn on the graph, values read from the axes with their units, and a division shown. An answer that states a gradient with no triangle and no working collects the answer mark if it is right and nothing if it is wrong, which is a poor trade on a question worth three. Teaching this takes one session and is worth marks in every subsequent series, including at AS Level, where the same skill reappears with uncertainty attached.

Moments and pressure supply the other recurring losses in this area, and both are arithmetic rather than conceptual. Moments questions are lost by taking the moment about a convenient point rather than the pivot, and by leaving a distance in centimetres. Pressure questions are lost on area: a rectangle given in centimetres squared converted by dividing by a hundred instead of ten thousand. Energy questions are generally better answered, with one exception: efficiency, where students divide the wrong way round and report a figure above one hundred per cent without noticing that it is impossible. A sanity check on the final line is a one-minute habit that protects two or three marks a paper.
bullets: Separate the two graph types before practising either one
Draw the triangle, read the axes, show the division
Take moments about the pivot and convert distances to metres first
Check efficiency answers against the impossible, above one hundred per cent

sections.heading: What one session fixes, by presenting problem
paragraphs: Families usually arrive with a description of a symptom rather than a diagnosis: he does not revise, she panics, the teacher says he is careless. Those map onto a small number of actual problems, each with a different session shape and a different realistic timescale. The table sets out the mapping we work from, including the cases where tutoring is not the right answer.

The honest column is the last one. Some of these are quick. Command-term confusion, graph-type confusion and prefix conversion are each a session or two of work, and all three transfer to every paper afterwards, which makes them the best value available. Others are not quick: a student who has not secured the content of two topic areas needs weeks, and no amount of technique work substitutes. Telling those apart before you commit to a term is the point of a diagnostic session.

And some presenting problems are not tutoring problems. A student who will not sit down for a parent will often not sit down for a tutor on a screen either, and for that case an adult physically in the room has a genuine advantage that we do not pretend to match. IB Gram does not place tutors in UAE homes, so if supervision rather than physics is the real issue we will say so on the call rather than take the booking. A page that only lists the cases where it wins is a page you cannot use.

sections.heading: Cambridge 0625 or Pearson 4PH1: do not revise from the wrong board
paragraphs: Dubai's British-curriculum schools are split between Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel, and a handful offer both across different subjects. The consequence for revision is immediate and underestimated: past papers from the wrong board teach the wrong question style, and in physics the difference includes whether equations are supplied, how the practical skills are assessed and how many papers are sat. A student who has spent February working through the other board's papers has been practising, but not for their examination.

The structural differences are the ones to check first. Cambridge examines through a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper and a separate practical component. Pearson examines International GCSE Physics through written papers that carry the practical skills inside them rather than in a separate component. Both boards tier or stream their content differently, and both publish their own command-term conventions. None of that makes one board harder; it makes them different, and only one of them is your child's.

The session calendars differ too, which matters for planning. Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May or June and in November, publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, and released June 2026 results to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, with November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026. Take both boards' dates from their own live timetable pages rather than from any page restating them, including this one, because provisional timetables are revised.

sections.heading: How a physics lesson works on a screen
paragraphs: The reasonable objection to online physics is apparatus. You cannot hand a student a ray box over a video call, and nobody should pretend otherwise. What a screen does instead is show the thing a ray box demonstrates with more control: the angle measured from the normal, drawn and redrawn, with the construction visible in colour and the mark-scheme convention enforced while the student watches. For the questions 0625 actually asks, which are drawn and written rather than performed, that is closer to the examination than a demonstration is.

The working arrangement that makes this effective is specific. The tutor shares an annotated board rather than slides. The student works on the board too, so their rearrangement appears in real time and a mistake is caught at the moment it is made rather than after a finished answer is submitted. Circuits are built up component by component. Graphs are plotted on a grid on screen, with scale and axis labels checked before any point goes down. Everything built in the session is saved and sent, so the April revision folder contains the October diagrams rather than a memory of them.

For the practical component the approach differs by route. A student entered for the written alternative to practical is preparing for a paper about experiments rather than for an experiment, and that paper is preparable entirely on screen: reading scales from images, tabulating with consistent precision, plotting, identifying a specific source of imprecision and proposing a method change. A student entered for the laboratory test needs the school's apparatus for the handling itself, and the online work supports it by securing the recording, plotting and evaluation marks that surround the practical skill. We do not run in-person lessons in Dubai, so the laboratory handling stays with the school where the apparatus and the supervision already are.
bullets: Annotated shared board rather than slides, with the student writing on it too
Circuits and ray diagrams built step by step and saved after the session

sections.heading: Where the tutoring line sits in a no-coursework subject
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE Physics carries no coursework, so the marks all come from supervised examinations at the centre. That removes the hardest academic-honesty question in tutoring, which is what a tutor may touch on work a student will submit. It leaves three boundaries that still matter and that families are entitled to ask about directly.

The first is material. Syllabuses, question papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge. A tutor should cite them, work from them in a session and point you to the official source, rather than hand over a folder of redistributed files. The second is the student's own hand. Diagnostic papers are only diagnostic if the student wrote them unaided; a script produced with help tells nobody anything, which is why the trial session has your child working rather than watching. The third is claims. No grade can be promised for a given series, no provider in this market holds a board or regulator status that would let them promise one, and any page offering a specific score should be read with scepticism.

On permits, the position in the UAE is clear and worth knowing regardless of who you hire. Private tutoring is permitted and regulated: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years, with eligibility covering school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals tutoring in the UAE without that permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule has been published, any specific amount you see quoted is unsourced. Abu Dhabi adds a further rule through ADEK's professional-ethics requirements, which press reporting describes as barring school staff from paid tutoring of students enrolled at their own school.
bullets: Official papers and mark schemes are cited and linked, never redistributed

process.title: Name the tier and the board
process.description: Two questions decide everything that follows: is your child entered for Core or Extended, and is the paper Cambridge 0625 or another board's specification. If you are not certain, the head of science is. Getting this wrong costs a term of practice on the wrong papers.

process.title: One diagnostic set, unaided
process.description: A short set of questions spread across the six topic areas, sat without help, so the topic distribution of lost marks is visible. This is also the trial session, which runs at no cost with no card details requested, and you keep the marked set either way.

process.title: Agree the two areas to repair first
process.description: The diagnosis almost always points at two areas rather than six. We agree those two, and the order, before any teaching starts, so you can see later whether the plan did what it said. Anything outside the two is parked, deliberately and visibly.

process.title: Weekly sessions on the agreed sequence
process.description: Live online, one to one, at a fixed hour on Gulf Standard Time, with diagrams built on the shared board and saved. One idea per session taken to the tier's depth, with questions set that your child can complete without the tutor present.

process.title: Recheck on paper before moving on
process.description: Each repaired area closes with past-paper questions filtered to that area alone, marked against the published scheme. If the marks have not moved, the sequence changes rather than continuing. Then the next area opens.

whyPoints.title: The syllabus is treated as six unequal areas
whyPoints.description: Mark share, question predictability and maths load differ sharply between the six 0625 topics. Planning that ignores this spends equal time on space physics and electricity, which is the most common way a term of tutoring produces no grade movement.

whyPoints.title: Tier and board are confirmed before a plan exists
whyPoints.description: Core and Extended sit different papers; Cambridge and Pearson examine the practical skills differently. Both facts change which past papers are useful, and both are checkable in a single question to the school. We ask them first rather than last.

whyPoints.title: One idea per session, taken properly
whyPoints.description: Covering ground is what makes a session feel productive and what leaves the same marks missing in March. A session that secures why current is identical around a loop has done more than one that toured four topics.

whyPoints.title: The practical component is treated as a real fifth
whyPoints.description: Paper 5 or Paper 6 carries a fifth of the grade with the most predictable mark scheme in the syllabus, and it is the component most students revise last. It gets its own block of sessions rather than whatever time is left in May.

whyPoints.title: Clear about the format and its limits
whyPoints.description: Lessons are live online over video; no tutor is placed in a UAE home. Where a student needs an adult in the room more than a physics specialist, we say that on the call, because the alternative is selling you a term that cannot work.

faqs.question: How does an online physics tutor show my child a circuit without the apparatus?
faqs.answer: On a shared annotated board, built component by component, with your child drawing on it too. For 0625 that is closer to the examination than a demonstration, because the paper asks students to interpret and draw circuits rather than to assemble them. A tutor can delete a component, redraw the loop, mark the current direction in colour and show immediately why a reading changes. The diagram is then saved and sent, so the version built in October is available in April. The school keeps the apparatus work, which is where the equipment and the supervision already are.

faqs.question: Which of the six 0625 topic areas carries the most marks?
faqs.answer: Across recent Extended papers the heaviest shares sit with electricity and magnetism and with motion, forces and energy, and those two are also the most calculation-dense. Waves takes a steady middle share and is heavily diagram-based. Thermal physics, nuclear physics and space physics are smaller, and their question styles are the most predictable in the syllabus. That distribution is why revision time should not be split evenly: the two heavy areas need understanding, while the three light ones mostly need a weekend of structured recall to stop being guessed.

faqs.question: What is the real content difference between Core and Extended 0625?
faqs.answer: Not a longer topic list. Extended asks for more steps inside one answer, more algebraic rearrangement before substitution, and explanation in causal rather than descriptive terms. A Core circuit question may want a current from a voltage and a resistance; the Extended version supplies a resistor combination and asks for the total, then the current, then the potential difference across one branch. The grade consequence is absolute: Core is awarded C to G, Extended A* to E. A student aiming above a C must be entered for Extended, and that entry closes months before the papers.

faqs.question: My daughter understands the physics but her graph questions lose marks. What is going wrong?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly the two graph types have merged into one rule. On a distance-time graph the gradient is a speed and the area underneath means nothing. On a speed-time graph the gradient is an acceleration and the area is a distance. A student holding gradient equals speed as a single fact applies it to both and loses a run of marks in one question. The second half of the fix is technique: draw a large triangle on the graph, read values off the axes with units, show the division. That is a mark-bearing method, not presentation.

faqs.question: Do you teach the Pearson specification too, and can we revise from both boards' papers?
faqs.answer: We teach both, and no, mixing the papers is a mistake. Cambridge 0625 examines through a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper and a separate practical component. The Pearson International GCSE assesses practical skills inside its written papers instead. Equation provision and command-term conventions also differ. Practising the wrong board builds habits the mark scheme will not reward. Confirm the specification code with the school, then revise from that board's materials alone. The only legitimate cross-board use is extra drilling on a topic, with the question style ignored.

faqs.question: Does my child have to remember the physics equations in the 0625 exam?
faqs.answer: Treat recall as the expectation and verify the detail for your child's series on the syllabus document at cambridgeinternational.org, because provision differs between boards and is revised on a cycle. Practically, the safe approach is the same either way: a student who can reconstruct the relationships, rather than recite a list, handles both situations. In sessions that means deriving where possible, grouping relationships by topic area, and practising selection rather than recitation. Choosing the right relationship under pressure is the skill the paper actually tests, and it is where marks are lost even when a sheet is available.

faqs.question: How do you prepare for the practical paper when my child is not in a laboratory?
faqs.answer: The written alternative to practical is a paper about experiments rather than an experiment, and it is fully preparable on screen: reading scales from images, tabulating with consistent decimal places, choosing a scale that fills the grid, plotting, drawing a trend, naming a specific source of imprecision and proposing a method change that would reduce it. For a student entered for the laboratory test instead, the handling stays with the school and online work secures the recording, plotting and evaluation marks that surround it. Ask your head of science which route the centre enters.

faqs.question: Is space physics worth revising, or should my son concentrate on the big topics?
faqs.answer: Revise it, and early. Space physics carries a smaller share of the marks than electricity or motion, but its question range is the narrowest in the syllabus: the solar system, orbital reasoning, stellar life cycles, the expanding universe. A weekend of structured recall usually secures most of what the paper will ask. Students skip it because it feels peripheral, then meet it under time pressure in the last twenty minutes of a paper and guess. Cheap, predictable marks taken early also buy time to spend on the areas that genuinely need understanding.

faqs.question: My son is in a Core set but wants to study engineering. Does the tier matter later?
faqs.answer: It can, through the sixth-form door rather than through the university one. Several Dubai schools set entry to AS or A Level Physics at a grade A or B at Extended IGCSE, and a Core entry caps the grade at C, which closes that route at the school rather than at the degree. So the question to put to the head of science this term is whether a tier change is still possible for the coming series and what evidence would support it. A marked Extended paper section showing access to the higher grades is the strongest form that evidence takes.

faqs.question: Can two of my children share one online physics session?
faqs.answer: Only where they are genuinely at the same point, which is rarer than it sounds. Two students in the same year group at the same tier working on the same topic can share productively, and the discussion between them is often useful. Two students a year apart, or on different tiers, end up with a session that is slightly wrong for both. The economics are tempting and the outcome usually is not. Where siblings both need physics, two shorter separate sessions generally produce more movement than one longer shared one.

faqs.question: How often should a Year 10 student have sessions compared with a Year 11?
faqs.answer: Year 10 usually runs best at one session a week or one a fortnight, following the school's teaching sequence and securing each topic as it is taught. The work there is prevention. Year 11 is different: through the autumn one session a week on current content plus marked questions, and in the eight to ten weeks before a series, two or three sessions a week with the emphasis shifting from content to timed papers and the practical component. The pattern should change across the year rather than stay fixed at whatever was booked in September.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring work for a student who is quiet and will not ask questions?
faqs.answer: Often better than a room does, and the mechanism is specific. On a shared board the tutor can see the working appear and intervene at the exact point a rearrangement goes wrong, without the student having to announce that they are stuck. Being asked to write rather than to speak suits a reticent student. What does not work is a session where the tutor talks and the student listens, which is easy to let happen on a screen, so the structure deliberately puts the student's pen on the board within the first ten minutes.

faqs.question: What internet and equipment do we need for a physics session in Dubai?
faqs.answer: A standard home broadband connection, a laptop or tablet rather than a phone, headphones, and a way for your child to write on screen: a graphics tablet is ideal, a touchscreen with a stylus works, and a trackpad is workable but slower. A mouse and paper combination is the fallback, with the student photographing working into the session. Physics needs more drawing than most subjects, so the writing method is worth getting right before the first lesson rather than discovering it mid-session.

faqs.question: How quickly can an Extended 0625 specialist start, and what if none is free?
faqs.answer: Usually within a few days outside peak season, and the honest qualification is that the weeks before a June or November series are peak season for exactly this specialism, because every centre's candidates want the same evenings. If the slot you need is not covered, you will be told that rather than matched with a generalist introduced as a physics specialist. The alternatives are a different hour with the right tutor, a waiting position, or a referral. Early booking in the autumn term is worth more than negotiating in April.

faqs.question: Which Dubai schools do your 0625 students come from?
faqs.answer: Across the Cambridge-pathway British schools and several dual-pathway and International Baccalaureate schools that enter IGCSE in Years 10 and 11, spread from Al Barsha and Tecom through Silicon Oasis to the newer communities along the creek. Named schools on this page are context for the Dubai curriculum landscape, not relationships: no partnership or endorsement is claimed with any of them. What matters more for a match than the school name is the tier, the board, the practical route and the mock calendar, because those four facts decide the plan.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-physics-0625-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors matched through this page teach Cambridge 0625 rather than science in general, which means they know what the alternative-to-practical paper actually asks, which equations the syllabus expects a candidate to recall, and how an explain question differs from a describe question in the mark scheme.

intro.heading: Three components, and why the entry decides the plan
paragraphs: Every Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 candidate sits three components, and the set depends on two decisions the school has already made. The first is the tier: Core candidates take the Core multiple-choice and Core theory papers, Extended candidates take the Extended versions, and the tier sets the range of grades available. The second is the practical route: the school enters its candidates either for the practical test or for the written alternative to practical, and that single choice changes what the final weeks of preparation should contain.

Most parents do not know which of those their child is on, and most tutoring enquiries start without it. That is why the first thing worth doing is finding the statement of entry and reading the component codes. A plan built on the wrong tier teaches content that will not be examined; a plan built on the wrong practical route prepares for apparatus handling when the examined skill is interpreting a written description of an experiment, or the reverse.

Once the components are known, the physics itself divides neatly. The current syllabus is organised into six topic areas: motion, forces and energy; thermal physics; waves; electricity and magnetism; nuclear physics; and space physics. Electricity and magnetism is the largest block of difficulty for most candidates, thermal physics is the most commonly under-taught, and space physics is usually the last thing covered and the first thing forgotten.

The reliable marks in 0625 are not in the hard physics. They are in equation recall, in units, in significant figures, and above all in the command-term vocabulary. A candidate who writes a correct, well-reasoned paragraph in answer to a question that said state loses marks for length; a candidate who describes a trend when the question said explain loses the marks entirely. These are learnable in weeks and they are worth more than another pass through the syllabus.

Dubai is a large market for this subject, which cuts both ways. KHDA counted 227 private schools in the emirate in 2024-25, with 387,441 students and the UK curriculum accounting for 37% of enrolment, so separate-science physics is entered in volume and general science tutors are easy to find. What is harder to find is someone who will start by asking which practical component is on the entry, and that question is the difference between a plan and a set of lessons.

Everything here is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; in-home tuition is a service we run only in India. For a physics candidate the practical consequence is specific and worth stating plainly: a tutor cannot supervise apparatus over a video link, and nobody should pretend otherwise. What a tutor can do is prepare the written practical component thoroughly, teach experimental reasoning from real past questions, and make sure the laboratory time the school does provide is not wasted.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-physics-0625-tutor.programmesIntro: Physics at sixteen is a gateway rather than an endpoint, and the decision that matters is usually not about this year. The four stages below are the ones a Dubai family is choosing between, and each reads a 0625 grade for a different reason.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics, Core tier
programmes.description: A reduced content list examined through the Core multiple-choice paper, the Core theory paper and one practical component, with a grade range that stops short of the top of the scale. It gives a genuine grounding in physics and it is not a route into A Level Physics, which is the fact a family most needs to know before accepting the entry.
programmes.countryNote: Core entries in Dubai are usually made for students carrying a heavy subject load or covering content at speed after a mid-course arrival. The decision is reversible for longer than families assume, and the time to review it is after the autumn assessment, since the tier is settled with the entry and the entry deadline sits months before the papers.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics, Extended tier
programmes.description: The full content list across all six topic areas, examined through the Extended multiple-choice paper, the Extended theory paper and one practical component, with access to the top grades. The Extended theory paper rewards multi-step quantitative work and precise written explanation in roughly equal measure, which is why strong mathematicians can still stall on it.
programmes.countryNote: This is the standard entry in Dubai British-curriculum schools for anyone who might take physics or engineering further. Sixth forms in the emirate publish their own entry requirements for A Level Physics and they generally expect the Extended tier, so the tier conversation is in practice a conversation about Year 12 options.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS & A Level Physics
programmes.description: A substantial step up in both mathematical demand and experimental rigour, with practical skills assessed formally and a heavy emphasis on algebraic manipulation and graph linearisation. Students who arrive able to recall equations, handle units confidently and write to command terms spend the first term learning physics rather than learning how to write physics.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai sixth forms frequently pair A Level Physics with A Level Mathematics, and the combination is where the mathematical gap becomes visible. A student who scraped through 0625 by memorising worked examples finds the first term hard in a way that has nothing to do with physics ability, which is an argument for fixing the algebra in Year 11 rather than in Year 12.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Physics
programmes.description: Standard and Higher Level, with examinations plus an internally assessed scientific investigation designed and written by the student. The investigation is the student's own work throughout: a tutor may teach method, discuss uncertainty and give feedback on a draft the student has written, and may not produce any part of it.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's IB sector is sizeable and expanding, with the 2026-27 intake adding seven new private schools, three of them International Baccalaureate, among 16,846 new places. Families in IB-continuum schools often sit IGCSE at sixteen before the Diploma, so a 0625 Extended grade is read as readiness for Diploma physics rather than as a qualification in its own right.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-physics-0625-tutor.subjectsIntro: Physics is rarely the only request, and the subjects below are the ones most often taken alongside Cambridge 0625 in Dubai. subjects.description: Theory papers plus a practical route mirroring physics. Students strong in physics often underrate how exactly a chemistry definition must be phrased.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: The most content-heavy of the three sciences and the most dependent on command terms. subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Co-ordinated Sciences 0654
subjects.description: All three sciences in one double-award qualification with a practical component, covering less depth per discipline than separate sciences. Students entered for it sometimes arrive expecting separate-science physics content, and establishing which one is on the entry is the first thing a tutor should do.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Combined Science 0653
subjects.description: A single-award science across the three disciplines at lighter depth, common where a timetable is full. The risk is a late discovery that a sixth-form science course expects the double award or separate sciences, which is an entry-deadline problem rather than a revision one.

subjects.description: The maths syllabus most Dubai physics candidates sit alongside 0625. Rearranging formulae, handling standard form, working with gradients and reading graphs are all assumed by the physics papers, so a weakness here presents as a physics problem and gets treated as one.

subjects.description: The stretch maths option, adding calculus, logarithms, series and radians. It is not required for 0625, but students sitting both find the algebraic fluency it builds removes most of the mathematical friction from Extended physics questions.

subjects.description: Edexcel's physics qualification, with a different paper structure and a different approach to practical assessment from Cambridge. Mixed-board entries are more common in Dubai than families expect, so the board on the statement of entry matters as much as the subject.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Computer Science 0478
subjects.description: Theory and problem-solving papers covering data representation, networks and algorithms. Pseudocode questions reward following syllabus conventions rather than writing working code, which is a frequent and expensive surprise for technically capable students.

subjects.description: Substantial coursework alongside written papers, with practical work consuming large blocks of the spring term. For a physics candidate the relevance is scheduling: this deadline will win any conflict and should be mapped before an eight-week physics plan is written.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Environmental Management 0680
subjects.description: Assessed through written papers on resources, energy and sustainability, drawing on data interpretation skills shared with the sciences. It pairs easily with physics and rewards accurate use of data from tables and graphs rather than extended recall.

sections.heading: Which 0625 components your child is sitting
paragraphs: A 0625 candidate sits a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper and one practical component. The tier decides which version of the first two, and the school decides which practical route. Those three codes appear on the statement of entry, and they are the most useful piece of information a parent can bring to a first conversation with a tutor, far more useful than a description of how the child is finding the subject.

The weighting is worth understanding because it changes priorities. The theory paper carries the largest single share of the grade, the multiple-choice paper a substantial share, and the practical component the remainder. Families tend to assume the practical route is a minor administrative detail. It is not: it is a fifth of the grade, and it is the component least often practised at home, which makes it the cheapest available improvement in many cases.

There is also no banked element in 0625 and no coursework, so all three components are decided in the same series. A weak morning on one cannot be offset by work submitted earlier in the year, which makes written practice across the whole year the only real lever a family has. It also means a candidate cannot avoid a disliked component by preparing harder elsewhere, which is a conversation worth having early with a student who has decided they are bad at practicals.

The table below sets out all six components with what each tests and where candidates lose marks. Treat the weightings as the published structure and confirm the current version against the syllabus for your child's exam year, since Cambridge revises assessment structures between syllabus cycles. The school's exams officer holds that document and will share it on request.

sections.heading: Paper 5 or Paper 6, and what a tutor can honestly do
paragraphs: The practical route is the one place where the delivery format of tutoring genuinely matters, so it deserves a straight answer rather than a reassurance. If your child is entered for the practical test, they will handle apparatus in an examination room, and no tutor working over a video link can supervise that. The laboratory time belongs to the school, and a provider claiming to replace it is overselling.

What can be done for the practical test is still substantial, and it is mostly the part students neglect. The marks in that component are heavily concentrated in recording readings to a consistent precision, tabulating properly, plotting a graph with sensible axes and scales, drawing a line of best fit, taking a gradient correctly, and writing a conclusion that answers the question asked. Every one of those is a paper skill, and every one is teachable without apparatus.

If your child is entered for the alternative to practical, the position is simpler: the component is written, so it can be prepared in full. It asks a student to read a described experiment and reason about it, identify what was measured and how, spot sources of error, suggest improvements and handle the resulting data. That format rewards practice on past questions more than almost any other component in the subject, and it is routinely left until the final fortnight.

Either way, the thing to protect is the laboratory time the school does provide. A student who arrives at a practical lesson having already met the apparatus in a question gets far more from the hour than one meeting both at once. That is a legitimate and useful role for tutoring, and it is the opposite of replacing the school: reading the described experiment beforehand, then handling it in the laboratory, is the sequence that makes a limited practical scheme go further.

sections.heading: The six topic areas and where the marks sit
paragraphs: The current syllabus organises physics into six topic areas, and they are not equally difficult or equally examined. Electricity and magnetism is where most candidates lose most marks, partly because circuit reasoning is genuinely hard and partly because it is usually taught in the middle of Year 11 when time has started to run short. Motion, forces and energy is the foundation and the one that most rewards early, thorough teaching.

Thermal physics is the quiet problem. It contains straightforward content, it is examined reliably, and it is frequently compressed into a fortnight because it sits between two larger topics. Waves rewards diagram accuracy more than recall. Nuclear physics is short, self-contained and among the most efficient topics to revise late. Space physics is usually covered last and forgotten first, which makes it the standard gap in a January mock.

Questions that cross topics are the other thing to plan for, and they are where Extended candidates separate. A question about a transformer in a heating circuit draws on electricity, thermal physics and energy transfer at once, and a student who has revised each topic in isolation can know all three and still not see the route through. Mixed past-paper questions in the last six weeks are what build that, and they cannot substitute for the topic work that comes first.

The table below gives each topic with the equations that carry it, the characteristic mark losses and the point in the year at which it is best addressed. It is written as a planning tool: a family with twelve weeks left should be working from something like this rather than from the first chapter of a revision guide, because the order matters more than the coverage when time is short.

sections.heading: Equations: what must be recalled, and what the paper gives you
paragraphs: One of the first questions to settle with any physics candidate is what they are expected to know by heart. The syllabus sets out the equations candidates are expected to recall, and it is a finite list rather than an open-ended burden. A student who has never been shown that list is carrying an unnecessary anxiety, and a student who assumes everything will be provided is heading for a bad morning.

Recall is also a different skill from use, and they should be drilled separately. Knowing that power is energy divided by time is recall; recognising that a question about a kettle is a power question, converting the time to seconds and rearranging correctly is use. Students who practise only mixed problem sets tend to be slow at both, because each question tests the two things at once and neither gets isolated.

The most efficient physics homework we set is therefore unglamorous: a short timed recall test on the equation list, every week, until it is automatic, and separate problem sets that assume the recall is there. It takes five minutes of a session and removes a category of error that otherwise appears on every component. It also makes the multiple-choice paper markedly faster, which is where many candidates run short of time.

Units belong in the same drill rather than in a separate one. Most of the equation errors that appear on marked scripts are not the wrong formula but the right formula fed with a time in minutes, a length in centimetres or a mass in grams. Writing the conversion as the first line of every answer is a habit worth more than any amount of additional content teaching, and it is one a parent can check without knowing any physics at all.

sections.heading: Describe, explain, calculate: the vocabulary that awards the marks
paragraphs: More marks are lost in 0625 to command terms than to physics. The examiner is reading for a specific kind of answer, and the command term is the instruction that says which kind. A student who writes a paragraph where one word was wanted loses time; a student who lists observations where a causal mechanism was wanted loses the marks. Neither error reflects a gap in understanding, which is why both are so frustrating and so fixable.

The practical fix is a glossary built from the student's own marked work rather than copied from a revision guide. Each time a mark is lost to a command term, the term goes on the list with the question, what was written and what the scheme wanted. After a few weeks the list is short and personal, and reading it before an attempt changes how the answer is planned. This is the single highest-yield intervention in the subject.

There is a related habit that costs nothing and saves time. The mark allocation printed beside each question is an instruction about length: a one-mark question wants one thing, and a three-mark explanation wants three linked statements. Students who write the same quantity for every question either run out of time or under-answer the long ones, and the correction is simply to read the number in brackets before starting rather than after finishing.

The table below sets out the terms that recur most in 0625 with what an answer must contain and what will score nothing. Mark allocations vary by question, so treat the figures as the usual pattern rather than a rule, and check the allocation printed beside each question in the paper itself, which is the clearest available guide to how much to write.

sections.heading: Core or Extended, and what the tier actually decides
paragraphs: The tier is settled with the entry, and the entry deadline sits months before the papers, so this is an autumn conversation rather than a spring one. Core candidates work through a reduced content list and are reported on a range that stops short of the top grades. Extended candidates cover everything, including the Extended-only material in each topic area, and can reach the full range.

The honest case for Core is real. A student carrying ten subjects, or one who joined a Dubai school in Year 11 and is covering two years of content in one, may well secure a better outcome and a less damaging year on the Core tier. Physics is not a requirement for most routes at eighteen, and a solid Core grade is a better result than a thin Extended one.

The case against Core is narrower and sharper: Dubai sixth forms publish their own entry requirements for A Level Physics and generally expect the Extended tier, so accepting Core closes a door that may matter in eighteen months. The way to raise it with a school is with evidence rather than opinion, which means a marked paper sorted by cause. If the errors are command terms and units rather than physics, that is a specific argument and schools respond to it.

It is also worth checking whether the tier is uniform across the sciences. A student can be entered Extended for physics and Core for biology, or the reverse, and families frequently assume one decision covers all three. Reading all the component codes on the statement of entry together takes two minutes and occasionally reveals a combination nobody intended, which is a far cheaper discovery in October than in May.

sections.heading: The maths inside physics, and why a good mathematician can still stall
paragraphs: Physics at this level assumes a set of mathematical skills that are rarely taught as part of the physics course: rearranging a formula with the unknown in the denominator, working in standard form, converting between units including prefixes, reading a gradient from a graph, and handling significant figures consistently. A student weak in any of those presents as weak at physics, and will often be given more physics teaching, which does not help.

The reverse case is just as common and less expected. A strong mathematician can stall on Extended physics because the subject will not accept an unexplained answer. A correct calculation with no formula stated and no units loses method and accuracy marks, and an explanation question answered with an equation scores nothing at all. Mathematical confidence can actually delay the realisation that physics is a writing subject as much as a calculating one.

A diagnostic that separates the two is therefore the first session rather than a lesson. Ten minutes of pure rearrangement and unit conversion, ten minutes of graph reading, and three written explanation questions will show immediately whether the problem is mathematical, linguistic or genuinely about physics. Those three problems need three different responses, and treating all of them as a content gap is how a term of tutoring produces nothing.

Graph work deserves a line of its own, because it is where the two failure modes meet. A gradient question requires choosing two widely separated points, showing the triangle, computing the change in each quantity and attaching the right units to the result. A student can understand the physics, perform the arithmetic correctly and still lose most of the marks by reading values off without construction. It is a drill rather than a concept, and it recurs in the practical component as well as the theory paper.

sections.heading: Revision order for a Dubai Year 11, and what to leave until last
paragraphs: With twelve weeks to go the question is no longer what to revise but in what order, and the order should follow the mark loss rather than the textbook. Electricity and magnetism first, because it is the biggest gap for most candidates and needs the most time to repair. Then the command-term glossary and the equation recall list, which are quick and pay back across every component. Then the practical component your child is actually entered for.

After that come the topics that are efficient to revise late precisely because they are self-contained: nuclear physics, waves, and space physics. Space physics in particular is usually taught last and forgotten first, and a deliberate pass over it a fortnight before the papers reliably recovers marks that a January mock showed as missing. Thermal physics sits in between and should be checked rather than retaught if it was covered properly.

Two Dubai-specific adjustments matter. The school's coursework and practical deadlines in other subjects will win any conflict with a physics plan, so get the published assessment calendar and build around it. And where the exam period overlaps Ramadan, sessions should be shorter and moved to after Iftar, with the content weighted towards recall, command terms and multiple-choice drilling rather than towards new multi-step problem solving.

The last fortnight should contain nothing new and one protected empty evening a week. An exhausted candidate makes exactly the careless unit and command-term errors the whole plan exists to remove, so adding hours at the end usually costs marks rather than gaining them. Sessions get shorter, not longer, and the final few are spent reading questions accurately and checking the school's issued timetable rather than covering material.
