sections.heading: Apparatus, academic honesty and the claims we will not make
paragraphs: Cambridge 0625 has no coursework, which removes the largest academic-honesty risk in international education before it arises. The boundary that does exist concerns materials and the student's own work. A tutor may teach a topic, set questions, mark them against the published mark scheme and explain why a mark was awarded or withheld. A tutor may not supply material a board has not released, redistribute syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes as downloads, or sit or submit anything on a student's behalf. The right practice is to work from the official source at cambridgeinternational.org and link to it.

For families whose children go on to IB Diploma Physics, the equivalent line falls around the internally assessed scientific investigation. It must be the student's own work from the question onwards. Teaching method, discussing uncertainty and giving feedback on a draft the student has written are legitimate; producing any part of it is not, and it would put the student at risk of malpractice proceedings rather than help them. This market contains providers selling finished assessed work, and nothing of that kind is on offer here in any subject.

Our own limits, plainly. IB Gram is a tutor-matching platform. We hold no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or IB endorsement, we are not a licensed school or training institute in the UAE, and we have no premises in the country. Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate; naming a regulator is not a claim of its approval. Private tutors here require a MoHRE private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, and you may ask any tutor to show theirs. We publish no ratings, no student counts and no statistics without a method, and we promise no grade. Lessons are one-to-one over live video; IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai, because in-home tuition is a service we run only in India.

process.title: Find the three component codes
process.description: The statement of entry lists them, and they settle the tier and the practical route in one step. A plan built without them risks teaching Extended-only content to a Core candidate, or preparing apparatus technique for a student entered for the written alternative. Ask the exams officer if you cannot find the document.

process.title: Diagnostic that separates maths from physics from writing
process.description: The free 45-minute trial covers rearrangement and unit conversion, graph reading and three written explanation questions, because those three failure modes look identical from the outside and need different responses. You keep the resulting notes and error log whether or not you continue, with no card required.

process.title: Set the topic order from the diagnostic
process.description: Not from the textbook. For most candidates that means electricity and magnetism early, the command-term glossary and equation list alongside it, and the self-contained topics left deliberately late. The written plan names the order and what will be re-tested, before the first paid session.

process.title: Weekly sessions with equation recall every week
process.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a fixed slot held for the term. Five minutes of each session is a timed recall test on the equation list, drilled separately from problem solving, because the two are different skills and mixed practice isolates neither.

process.title: Re-test, then review honestly at six weeks
process.description: Each topic is re-tested two to three weeks after teaching, so the plan can show whether anything stuck. At six weeks the marked work and the error log are enough to judge the arrangement, and if the same causes remain we will recommend a change rather than more hours. No grade is predicted at any point.

whyPoints.title: The plan starts from the entry, not from the subject
whyPoints.description: Tier and practical route are read off the statement of entry before anything is taught, because they decide which content is examined and what the final weeks should contain. A plan written without them is a guess, and it is the commonest reason a term of physics tutoring misses the component that was actually leaking marks.

whyPoints.title: Command terms treated as the subject they are
whyPoints.description: A personal glossary built from your child's own marked work, with the question, what was written and what the scheme wanted. It is unglamorous and it is the highest-yield intervention in 0625, because correct physics written against the wrong command term scores nothing at all.

whyPoints.title: Equation recall drilled separately from problem solving
whyPoints.description: Five minutes of timed recall every session until the list is automatic, with problem sets that assume it. Mixed practice tests both at once and isolates neither, which is why students who only do past questions stay slow at both and run out of time on the multiple-choice paper.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the practical component
whyPoints.description: Apparatus supervision belongs to the school and no video link replaces it. What we prepare is the written practical component in full, and for the practical test the paper skills that carry most of its marks: recording precision, tabulating, plotting, gradients and conclusions. Saying what cannot be done is part of the service.

whyPoints.title: Limits written down
whyPoints.description: No regulator endorsement, no premises in the UAE, no ratings, no statistics without a method, no grade promises, and no reproduction of Cambridge material. Weightings and structures on this page are to be confirmed against the syllabus for your child's exam year, and exam dates against the school's own issued timetable.

faqs.question: Is my child entered for Paper 5 or Paper 6 in Cambridge 0625?
faqs.answer: The statement of entry answers it, and the answer changes the preparation significantly. Paper 5 is the practical test, sat with apparatus in an examination room; Paper 6 is the written alternative, in which an experiment is described and the candidate reasons about it on paper. Schools choose the route for their candidates, usually on the basis of laboratory capacity and cohort size. If you cannot find the document, the exams officer will confirm it. It is the single most useful fact to establish before buying any physics support.

faqs.question: Which equations does the 0625 syllabus expect a candidate to recall?
faqs.answer: The syllabus itself sets out the equations candidates are expected to know, and it is a finite list rather than an open-ended burden. The useful thing is to get that list from the syllabus document for your child's exam year, which the school's exams officer holds, and then drill it as a weekly timed recall test separate from problem solving. Students who have never been shown the list carry an unnecessary anxiety about it, and students who assume everything is provided discover otherwise in the exam room.

faqs.question: Does the Core tier limit the grade my son can get in physics?
faqs.answer: Yes. Core candidates work through a reduced content list and are reported on a range that stops short of the top grades, while Extended candidates cover everything and can reach the full range. The tier is settled with the entry, and the final entry deadline falls months before the papers, so this is an autumn conversation. There are genuine reasons to accept Core, particularly for a student carrying a heavy load or covering two years of content in one. There is one strong reason to resist it, which is that Dubai sixth forms generally expect Extended for A Level Physics.

faqs.question: My daughter can do the calculations but loses marks on explain questions. Why?
faqs.answer: Because explain asks for a causal mechanism and she is probably restating the observation. The examiner wants a chain: this happens, because of that, therefore this follows. Describe asks for what happens in sequence and will not accept a reason instead; explain asks for the reason and will not accept a description. Mathematically confident students hit this wall often, because the subject will not take an unexplained answer. The fix is a personal glossary built from her own marked work, and it takes a few weeks rather than a term.

faqs.question: How much of 0625 is electricity, and should we front-load it?
faqs.answer: Electricity and magnetism is one of six topic areas and it is where most candidates lose most marks, for two reasons. Circuit reasoning is genuinely difficult, and the topic is often taught in the middle of Year 11 when the timetable has started to compress. Front-loading it is usually the right call: it needs more time than any other area to repair properly, and almost every later question that combines topics touches it. Leave the self-contained areas, such as nuclear physics and space physics, for the late weeks instead.

faqs.question: Does a 0625 candidate really need to learn space physics?
faqs.answer: Yes. Space physics is one of the six topic areas in the current syllabus, covering the solar system, orbits, stellar life cycles and the expanding universe, and it is examined. The problem is positional rather than conceptual: it is usually taught last, often in a hurry, and it is the first thing forgotten, which is why it turns up as a blank section in January mock scripts. A deliberate pass over it about a fortnight before the papers is one of the most reliable mark recoveries available in the subject.

faqs.question: What does the multiple-choice paper in 0625 actually test?
faqs.answer: Recall and single-step application, under time pressure, with distractors designed to catch specific errors. It carries a substantial share of the grade and it is the most under-practised component in the subject, which is why it is often the easiest to improve. The useful way to work on it is timed sets sat at home and then reviewed question by question, with every wrong answer classified as content, misreading or units. Most students find the majority of their losses are not content, which changes what the next session should do.

faqs.question: Should we move from separate physics to Co-ordinated Sciences in Year 11?
faqs.answer: That is an entry-deadline decision rather than a revision one, and it belongs to the school. The honest considerations are what the next step requires and how much time remains. Co-ordinated Sciences covers all three disciplines at less depth in a double award, which reduces volume, while separate sciences give more depth and are sometimes expected by sixth-form science courses. Check the published entry requirements of the course your child is aiming at, in writing, before raising it, and raise it well before the final entry deadline.

faqs.question: The school has entered my son for the practical test. What can a tutor do?
faqs.answer: Quite a lot, but not the apparatus part, and a provider claiming otherwise is overselling. The laboratory time belongs to the school. What is teachable without apparatus is where most of that component's marks actually sit: recording readings to a consistent precision, tabulating properly, choosing axes and scales, plotting accurately, drawing a line of best fit, taking a gradient correctly and writing a conclusion that answers the question asked. Those are paper skills, they are drilled from past questions, and they are routinely neglected until the final fortnight.

faqs.question: Why does my child's answer score nothing when the physics is right?
faqs.answer: Usually one of three reasons, all mechanical. The command term was ignored, so an explanation was given where a description was wanted or the reverse. The calculation was written as a bare answer, forfeiting the method marks that a multi-step question mostly consists of. Or the units were missing, wrong or inconsistent after a prefix conversion. None of those is a physics problem and all three are visible on a marked script within minutes, which is why a diagnostic paper is worth more than a diagnostic conversation.

faqs.question: Is 0625 harder than IGCSE Chemistry or Biology?
faqs.answer: Differently hard, and the distinction is useful when deciding where tutoring money goes. Physics has the lowest content volume of the three and the highest mathematical demand, so it punishes weak algebra and unit handling. Chemistry sits in between and punishes imprecise definitions and mole calculations. Biology has the largest content volume and punishes command-term errors most of all. A student struggling in all three usually has a single shared cause, most often command terms, and fixing that once helps in every subject.

faqs.question: Does 0625 Extended lead straight into A Level Physics?
faqs.answer: It is the usual route, and Dubai sixth forms generally expect the Extended tier, but it is not a smooth continuation. A Level Physics raises the mathematical demand considerably and assesses practical skills formally, with much heavier algebraic manipulation and graph linearisation. The students who settle fastest are the ones who arrive able to recall equations without thinking, handle units and prefixes confidently and write to command terms. Those three habits are built in Year 11 and are worth more going into Year 12 than extra content ever is.

faqs.question: What is a realistic weekly plan for 0625 starting in January?
faqs.answer: One fixed weekly session, an order set by a diagnostic rather than by the textbook, and a timed recall test on the equation list in every session. For most candidates that means electricity and magnetism in the early weeks, the command-term glossary built alongside it, then the practical component on the entry, then the self-contained topics late. Timed multiple-choice sets sat at home throughout, reviewed in session. No new content in the final fortnight, and shorter sessions rather than longer ones in the last week.

faqs.question: Do we need a separate tutor for the maths inside physics?
faqs.answer: Rarely, if the physics tutor is willing to teach it. The mathematics 0625 assumes is a narrow list: rearranging formulae including an unknown in the denominator, standard form, unit and prefix conversion, gradients from graphs, and significant figures. A physics specialist can teach all of that in the context where it is used, which is more effective than teaching it abstractly in a separate maths session. A separate maths tutor is worth it when the gap is broader than physics, which the diagnostic will show.

faqs.question: Which 0625 topics should a Dubai Year 11 revise last?
faqs.answer: The self-contained ones, because they hold up well over a short interval and do not underpin anything else. Nuclear physics is short, reliably examined and efficient to revise late. Waves rewards diagram accuracy, which responds quickly to practice. Space physics should be given a deliberate pass about a fortnight out, since it is almost always the topic taught last and forgotten first. What should not be left late is electricity and magnetism, which needs weeks rather than days, or the command-term work that improves every other answer.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-physics-0625-tutor.closingHeading: Find the three component codes first
dubai/cambridge-igcse-physics-0625-tutor.closingBody: Before anything else, find the statement of entry and read the three component codes. They tell you the tier, and therefore which content is examined, and they tell you whether your child sits the practical test or the written alternative, which decides what the last month should contain. With those in hand, book the free 45-minute trial and ask for a diagnostic that separates the mathematics from the physics from the writing, because those three look identical from the outside and need different work. The notes and error log are yours whether or not you continue, and if the right recommendation is a short block on one component rather than a term of lessons, that is what we will say.

Each keeps two running records for every student, a recall scorecard and a question-type scorecard, and both live in a folder the family can open at any time without asking for a report.

intro.heading: Reassurance is not evidence, and psychology makes the difference hard to see
paragraphs: Psychology is a subject where a parent can be reassured for a whole term and discover nothing in the summer. The reason is that the material is interesting enough to discuss. A student who has read about obedience can hold a conversation about it at dinner, sound entirely in command, and still be unable to produce the study's aim, method, findings and conclusion cold in an examination hall. Interest and availability are different properties, and only one of them is examined.

The second reason is that psychology marks are distributed across question types that fail independently. A student can be strong on identifying terms, competent at describing studies, and lose almost everything available on the apply and evaluate questions, which is where the difference between a middling and a strong grade actually sits. A single overall mark hides that entirely. Two scripts with the same total can need completely different work, and no report written in sentences will tell a family which one they have.

So this page is about records rather than about teaching philosophy. Two running documents do most of the work. A recall scorecard lists each study and strand, which of the five elements the student produced cold, which was missing, and when it was last checked. A question-type scorecard takes a marked paper and splits the marks by question type, so the loss has an address. Both are short, both are readable by someone who has never studied psychology, and both make a tutor's claims checkable.

On delivery: lessons are one-to-one over live video. Home visits are not part of what IB Gram sells anywhere in the UAE, including Dubai, and are offered only in India. The page below answers the home-tutoring question properly rather than deflecting it, because it is a reasonable question with a real market behind it. What it concludes is that for a small-entry option subject like 0266, the family who insists on a tutor within driving distance is choosing from a pool of a handful of people, and the one who accepts live video is choosing from everyone who has taken a cohort through the syllabus.

What follows: the honest comparison between the three formats a Dubai family is actually weighing; the recall scorecard and how to keep it; what moves at week two, week six and week twelve; the question-type scorecard as a worked format; why the specialist you want is probably not in your postcode; what a parent can check without knowing the subject; how to schedule evidence collection around mocks, Ramadan and the series; the authorship question that dated work settles; and what the record protects if a tutor, a school or a country changes mid-course. Nothing here predicts a grade, because nothing honestly can.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-psychology-0266-ho.programmesIntro: The record a family should keep changes with the stage, and so does the thing worth measuring. These are the four points at which a Dubai psychology student generates evidence somebody should be reading.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary
programmes.description: Psychology is not taught at this stage, but the option decision is made at the end of it. The useful evidence here is not about psychology at all: it is whether the student can write a paragraph that makes a claim and supports it, and whether they can read a simple data table. Both are better predictors of a psychology grade than curiosity about the subject.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools set IGCSE option blocks in Year 9 and the blocks differ between schools in the same neighbourhood. A family moving school between Year 9 and Year 10, which happens often in this city, can find that psychology is not timetabled at the new school. Ask for the current year's option blocks rather than the prospectus.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Psychology
programmes.description: The course this page is about. Assessment is by written examination, so the evidence that matters is written: timed answers, marked, with the marks split by question type. A student's school reports will summarise effort and attitude, which are real but are not the same as a mark breakdown. The scorecards exist to supply what the reports cannot.
programmes.countryNote: Confirm the board and syllabus code on the school entry form before buying anything, including revision guides. Dubai schools use Cambridge and Pearson across different subjects, sometimes within one student's timetable, and material written for the other board rehearses question formats that will not appear.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE alternative
programmes.description: Some Dubai schools use Pearson rather than Cambridge for social-science options. Paper structures, command wording and mark-scheme language all differ, which changes what a scorecard should track. The record-keeping method on this page transfers unchanged; the question-type column headings do not, and should be taken from the board's own published assessment material.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs International GCSE in May or June and in November each year. Its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those dates set the real planning horizon for a retake inside one school year.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS & A Level Psychology
programmes.description: Where a strong 0266 student usually goes next. The evidence changes character: studies are examined in procedural detail, and a candidate is expected to design and justify investigations rather than recognise and critique them. A recall scorecard at this level tracks procedure and justification, not just aim and findings, and the volume of material makes an interval-based check essential rather than optional.
programmes.countryNote: A Dubai school running IGCSE Psychology does not necessarily run it at A Level, because staffing a small Year 12 group is harder than filling a Year 10 option block. Ask the sixth form whether the group ran this year, and ask how many students were in it, because a group of three can be cancelled late.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-psychology-0266-ho.subjectsIntro: A scorecard is organised by topic, because that is the level at which recall fails. These are the areas a Dubai 0266 student usually carries. Confirm the exact content list in the syllabus document for your child's examination year.

subjects.name: Memory and forgetting
subjects.description: Models of memory and explanations of forgetting. The characteristic failure is a student who can draw the model and cannot say what evidence supports it. On a scorecard this shows up as findings present, evaluation missing, which is a precise and fixable entry.

subjects.name: Perception
subjects.description: How sensory information becomes experience, including illusions and depth cues. Students hold the examples and lose the explanation, so the scorecard entry to watch is whether the mechanism can be stated without the picture in front of them.

subjects.name: Obedience and conformity
subjects.description: The best-known material in the subject and therefore the most over-trusted. Students describe the studies vividly and skip the method, which is where the marks are. Method missing is the single most common scorecard entry across this strand.

subjects.name: Attachment and development
subjects.description: Early relationships, their measurement and their claimed long-term effects. The evaluation work here is unusually rich because the methods are contested, and a student who holds two methodological criticisms has material for several different questions.

subjects.name: Atypical behaviour
subjects.description: Definitions of abnormality, explanations and approaches to treatment. The risk on this strand is writing from general knowledge or from media portrayals rather than from the course, which reads plausibly and earns nothing. The scorecard check is whether a named explanation appears.

subjects.name: Research design
subjects.description: Experiments, observations, self-report and correlation, with variables, controls and sampling. Checked weekly rather than three-weekly because the vocabulary recurs in questions on every other strand, so decay here costs marks across the whole paper rather than in one place.

subjects.name: Data, tables and graphs
subjects.description: Reading and drawing simple charts, the mean, median, mode and range, and matching a measure of central tendency to a data set. Small, examinable, and the strand most often absent from a revision plan entirely until somebody looks at a marked data question.

subjects.name: Research ethics
subjects.description: Consent, deception, withdrawal, debriefing, confidentiality and protection from harm, each with its remedy. Scored as present or absent rather than by quality, because a candidate either names the principle or does not, and naming it is what the mark scheme can credit.

subjects.name: Evaluation and application writing
subjects.description: Not a topic but a skill, tracked on the question-type scorecard rather than the recall one. These two question types hold the marks that separate the middle of the range from the top, and they fail for reasons that have nothing to do with how much content has been learned.

sections.heading: The three formats a Dubai family is actually weighing
paragraphs: A home-tutor search is usually a search for three things at once: convenience, attention, and the sense that somebody is accountable. Those are reasonable wants and they are not all best served by the same format. The question worth asking is not which option is better in the abstract but which one leaves behind something a parent can read in April.

The in-home market in Dubai is real and priced accordingly. Bestimate's rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 an hour, with independent home tutors between AED 200 and 500, and that upper band reflects distance as much as expertise. Monthly in-home packages advertised in this market have run to AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. Those figures were read in October 2026 and belong to the providers that published them; none of them is an IB Gram price.

IB Gram's own answer is live video, one-to-one, with no home visits offered anywhere in the UAE. The table compares the three formats on what each produces rather than on how each is marketed. The second row is worth a moment too. An hour booked with a tutor who drives across Dubai is not an hour of teaching, and the shortfall lands at both ends of the session rather than being announced.

sections.heading: The recall scorecard, and how to keep one
paragraphs: A named study is usable in an examination only if the student can produce five things about it without a prompt: its name, its aim, its method stated accurately enough to be repeated, its findings, and its conclusion. Recognition on a revision card is a different skill and a much weaker one. The recall scorecard exists to measure the five, one study at a time, at a stated interval.

Keeping it takes four minutes at the start of a session. The tutor names a study, the student produces the five elements aloud, and whichever element was absent is written down. Nothing is scored out of ten and no judgement is offered. What accumulates is a pattern, and the patterns are remarkably consistent: method is the element students lose first, conclusion is the one they confuse with findings, and the strand a student enjoys most is usually the one they describe rather than evaluate.

The interval matters as much as the check. A study checked every week never decays and tells you nothing. A study checked once a term has already decayed by the time anybody looks. Two to three weeks is the useful window for most topics, with research design checked weekly because its vocabulary recurs across the whole paper. The table shows the format with an illustrative set of entries; it is a worked example of the layout, not data about any student. A family can keep this themselves, incidentally, with no tutor involved. A parent reading five study names off a revision list and asking for the five elements each is running the same instrument, and the information it returns is the same information.

sections.heading: What moves at week two, week six and week twelve
paragraphs: Families expect marks to move first and they move last. The sequence in psychology is consistent enough to plan around. By week two what has changed is the recall scorecard: the missing elements have names, and the student knows which ones they are, which is itself a change in behaviour. No mark has moved and none should be expected to.

By week six two things are usually visible. Cold recall holds on the strands that have been checked at interval, and the question-type scorecard shows movement on the describe and explain questions, which are the ones a rule can fix quickly. Evaluate and apply questions typically have not moved yet, because those require a habit rather than a rule, and a habit takes longer than three sessions to install under time pressure.

By week twelve a mark comparison becomes meaningful, because there is a timed whole paper to set beside the week-one baseline. This is also where a timing problem stops being arguable: a student who ran out of time on both papers has a timing problem, not a knowledge problem, however convincingly the revision has been done. Nobody can promise where a grade will land, and a provider who offers a specific outcome in a written-examination subject should be treated with real scepticism. What a family can reasonably expect is to know, at week six, whether the work is landing. If the answer at week six is no, that is useful rather than disastrous. Six weeks of marked evidence identifies the mismatch precisely enough to change tutor or change approach with months still available, which is the opposite of the usual pattern where a family discovers in April that a year of sessions produced goodwill and no movement.

sections.heading: The question-type scorecard: giving a loss an address
paragraphs: A total mark on a psychology paper is close to useless as a planning tool. Two students on the same total can need entirely different work, and a parent handed a percentage has no way of knowing which situation they are in. Splitting the paper by question type takes about ten minutes with a mark scheme and turns a number into a diagnosis.

The pattern that emerges is nearly always lopsided. Identify and describe questions come back well, because they reward what revision actually produces. Explain questions lose a predictable slice where the student stopped at a definition. Evaluate questions lose more, because the ground gets named and the consequence does not. Apply questions lose the most, often almost everything available, because the student wrote correctly about the concept and never mentioned the person in the scenario. Data questions lose a small amount reliably, since the strand is rarely revised.

The table shows the format with illustrative figures, again as a layout rather than as data about anybody. Its value is the final column. A scorecard that ends in a diagnosis and no booked action is a nicely formatted complaint. One rule per session, introduced and then tested on the next paper, is what converts the scorecard into a changed script. Two rules work for almost every student: on an apply question the last sentence names the person in the scenario, and on an evaluate question the last sentence states the consequence for the conclusion.

sections.heading: Why the 0266 specialist you want is probably not in your postcode
paragraphs: This is the honest core of the home-tutor question. Supply of tutors is not even across subjects. Mathematics and the sciences are taught in every school in the emirate, so a family looking for a Mathematics tutor within driving distance is choosing from a deep pool. Psychology at IGCSE is an option subject with a small entry, concentrated in a minority of schools, and the number of people in the region who have taken a cohort through 0266 to examination is correspondingly small.

Narrow that small group further by who can reach a particular Dubai address between the end of the school day and dinner, and the pool can collapse to nobody. What usually happens next is that a family accepts a capable general tutor who is reading the syllabus a week ahead of the student. The lessons feel productive. The question-type scorecard does not move, because the tutor cannot see where an answer stops short in a subject they have not examined.

The table sets out the availability position by subject rather than pretending it is uniform. The entries are qualitative on purpose: publishing a tutor headcount would be an unverifiable number, and this project does not publish those. What the table does commit to is the behaviour. Where no specialist is free, we say so and name the alternatives rather than substituting quietly. No competitor page researched for this project discloses a coverage limit at all, and several route UAE families to contact numbers outside the country without saying where the tutor sits.

sections.heading: What a parent can check without knowing any psychology
paragraphs: None of this requires a parent to understand the subject, which is the point of keeping records rather than requesting opinions. Four checks take about five minutes each and need no subject knowledge at all. They are also the four things a tutor who is not doing the work will find difficult to produce on request.

Check one: ask to see the last three dated entries on the recall scorecard, and look at whether the missing element changed. If the same element is still missing after three checks, the remedy is not working and that is a conversation to have in week five rather than in March. Check two: ask for the question-type split from the most recent marked paper, and ask which two types the next session will address. A tutor who cannot answer that has not split the paper.

Check three: open a marked script and look for marks in the margin. Not comments, marks. A script covered in encouraging remarks and carrying no mark allocation has been read, not marked, and the two are different services. Check four: ask what the student wrote during the last session. If the answer is nothing, the hour was a conversation. Conversations have their place in a long engagement, but a run of them is how a term disappears pleasantly. None of these four checks is adversarial, and a tutor who is doing the work will welcome them, because they convert a parent's anxiety into a specific question with a specific answer. The tutors who resist are the ones keeping nothing, and finding that out in week five costs a family one session rather than a year.

sections.heading: Collecting evidence around mocks, Ramadan and the series
paragraphs: Evidence collection has to fit the Dubai school year or it quietly stops. Three periods are routinely mishandled. The first is the opening weeks of the course, when families ask for a full past paper the student has no content for; the result is a demoralising mark that measures nothing. The second is the school mock fortnight, when a tutor sets additional timed work on top of school examinations and the student does neither properly. The third is Ramadan, when a long evening paper becomes unrealistic and the sensible move is shorter, more frequent recall checks instead.

The mock fortnight is the single best evidence-gathering opportunity in the school year and most families waste it. The school has already produced timed scripts under proper conditions and marked them against a scheme. Asking for the script back, rather than only the mark, gives a tutor a free diagnostic that is more realistic than anything produced at home. Some schools return scripts readily and some need asking twice; it is worth the second ask.

The table maps the year onto what to collect and what not to attempt. One entry deserves emphasis: in the final fortnight before a series, no new topic should be introduced. A student who meets unfamiliar content in the last two weeks loses confidence in material they already held, and the cost of that is larger than the marks the new topic might have delivered. The last two weeks are for two timed papers, the marking, and sleep.

sections.heading: Authorship, and the question dated work settles
paragraphs: Psychology support runs into an authorship question wherever a student has written work to hand in. A tutor may teach research design, press a weak hypothesis until the student sharpens it, explain why a sampling choice is vulnerable, model the reasoning on an entirely different investigation, and mark what the student has produced in as much detail as the student can absorb. A tutor may not supply text for submission, settle the design on the student's behalf, or provide analysis the student then presents as their own.

Dated, marked-after-the-fact work settles this without anybody having to argue about it. If every piece in the folder was written by the student at a known time and marked afterwards, authorship is a matter of record. The ambiguity arises with undated documents developed jointly across several sittings, where nobody can later say which sentences came from where. That is a reason to keep the records in the order described on this page, quite apart from any question of measurement.

One provider researched for this project advertises completed assessed work at a fixed price. For a student that is a malpractice exposure capable of ending a qualification, and it is not a service any reputable tutor should be near. IB Gram does not supply assessed work, does not sell model answers for submission, and does not reproduce or distribute syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes. Those are published by the awarding body and should be obtained from cambridgeinternational.org or through the school.

sections.heading: What the record protects when something changes
paragraphs: Dubai is a city where things change mid-course more often than in most places. A family relocates between emirates, a parent's job moves, a school place opens at a better-matched school in January, a tutor returns to their home country at short notice. Each of those events can cost a term of diagnostic work, and each of them costs nothing if the record is portable.

A replacement tutor who is handed a recall scorecard and two question-type splits starts by diagnosing rather than by rediscovering. The first session goes on the missing elements already identified instead of on three weeks of cautious assessment, and the family does not pay twice for the same information. The same applies to a school. A new teacher receiving a student in January with evidence of what has and has not stuck is in a far better position than one receiving a cheerful summary.

There is a forecast-grade dimension as well. Schools produce forecast grades from the evidence they hold, and for a student who joined late or has had an interrupted year the school may hold very little. A folder of dated, marked, timed work is not a substitute for school assessment and should never be presented as one, but it is reasonable material to put in front of a teacher who is making a judgement with thin information. Ask rather than assume, and accept the school's answer. The quieter benefit is to the student. A child who has watched their own missing elements get named, repaired and then checked again has a reason to believe the work is doing something, and that belief survives a bad mock in a way that general encouragement does not.

process.title: Start with the code, the series and a real mark
process.description: The syllabus code off the school entry form, the series the school is entering, and the last mark with the paper it came from. A percentage with no paper attached cannot be split by question type, which means it cannot be used to plan anything. These three facts take a minute to find and save a session.

process.title: Build the baseline before any teaching
process.description: The free trial lesson, one per subject with no payment details taken beforehand, produces a short answer of two question types plus a cold check on one study. That is the week-one row in both scorecards. Without it, every later script looks reasonable and nothing can be compared.

process.title: Set the recall intervals explicitly
process.description: Two to three weeks for topic strands, weekly for research design, monthly for data and ethics. Written down, not remembered. A check that happens when it feels due will drift towards the material the student likes, which is exactly the material that needed checking least.

process.title: Split every marked paper by question type
process.description: Ten minutes with a mark scheme turns a total into a diagnosis. The session that follows works on the two largest losses and introduces one rule, which is then tested on the next paper. More than one rule per session is a list, and lists do not survive examination conditions.

process.title: Audit, then revise, in the final six weeks
process.description: Two whole timed papers, marked, both scorecards brought up to date, and the remaining sessions directed by what the audit exposes rather than by a revision plan written in advance. No new topic in the last fortnight, under any circumstances.

whyPoints.title: Two records, both readable by a non-specialist
whyPoints.description: A recall scorecard and a question-type split are short enough to read in five minutes and specific enough to act on. Neither requires a parent to understand psychology, which is the whole point of measuring rather than asking for an opinion.

whyPoints.title: Marks split by question type, not reported as a total
whyPoints.description: Two students on the same total frequently need opposite work. Apply and evaluate questions hold the marks that separate the middle of the range from the top, and they fail for reasons unrelated to how much content has been revised.

whyPoints.title: The record is portable by design
whyPoints.description: Scorecards and marked scripts live in a folder the family controls. In a city where families relocate between emirates and tutors leave at short notice, a portable record is the difference between a handover and a restart.

whyPoints.title: Rates are attributed, never presented as ours
whyPoints.description: In-home figures on this page belong to Bestimate and to independent providers, read in October 2026. They describe the market. IB Gram's own rate depends on level, length and format, and the trial lesson plus a short consultation is the honest route to it.

whyPoints.title: The availability position is qualitative and stated
whyPoints.description: 0266 is a small entry in this region and we say so rather than publishing a tutor headcount nobody could verify. Where no specialist who has examined the syllabus is free, the alternatives are named before any money is taken.

faqs.question: Do 0266 tutors in Dubai travel to the student's home?
faqs.answer: Some providers in the Dubai market do offer in-home visits, and the published rates reflect the travel: Bestimate's table shows AED 180 to 350 an hour and independent home tutors AED 200 to 500, with monthly in-home packages advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. For 0266 the trade is favourable, because the subject is a small option entry and filtering an already thin pool of specialists by driving distance usually means losing the specialist.

faqs.question: What should the first 0266 progress record contain?
faqs.answer: Four things, all dated from week one. A short written answer for at least two question types, marked with the marks in the margin rather than only comments. A cold-recall check on one study, noting which of the five elements was missing. A question-type split of whatever recent marked work exists, even if it is a school test. And a stated interval for the next recall check. That is the baseline. Everything afterwards is a comparison against it, and without it every later script will look reasonable with nothing to measure it against.

faqs.question: How soon should a 0266 mark actually change?
faqs.answer: Later than most families expect, and in a predictable order. By week two the missing recall elements have names but no mark has moved. By week six cold recall holds on checked strands and the describe and explain questions improve, because a rule fixes them quickly. Evaluate and apply questions usually remain flat at six weeks, since those need a habit rather than a rule. By week twelve a timed whole paper is comparable to the week-one baseline. Anyone offering a particular grade from a fixed number of sessions is describing something they cannot control.

faqs.question: What is a cold-recall scorecard for 0266, and why keep one?
faqs.answer: It is a one-page table listing each study or strand, which of the five elements the student produced without a prompt, which was missing, when it was last checked and when the next check falls due. It takes four minutes at the start of a session. The value is the pattern rather than any single entry: method is the element students lose first, conclusion gets confused with findings, and the strand a student most enjoys is usually the one they describe rather than evaluate. None of that shows up in a report written in sentences.

faqs.question: My child's 0266 school report says good effort. Is that evidence?
faqs.answer: It is evidence of effort, which is real and worth knowing, but it is not evidence about marks. Effort and attitude are what a subject teacher with a large class can observe reliably. What they rarely have time to produce is a per-question-type breakdown of a marked script, which is the thing that tells a family where marks are actually going. Ask the school for the marked script rather than the grade, particularly after mocks. A script with marks in the margin and a mark scheme beside it can be split by question type in about ten minutes.

faqs.question: How do I check 0266 progress if I do not know the subject myself?
faqs.answer: Four checks, none of which need subject knowledge. Ask for the last three dated scorecard entries and see whether the missing element changed; if it is the same after three checks, the remedy is not working. Ask for the question-type split from the latest paper and which two types the next session targets. Open a marked script and look for marks in the margin rather than only encouraging comments. And ask what the student wrote during the last session. If the answer is nothing, the hour was a conversation.

faqs.question: Should we collect 0266 evidence during the school mock fortnight?
faqs.answer: Collect it, but do not create more of it. The mock period is the best evidence-gathering opportunity in the year because the school has already produced timed scripts under proper conditions and marked them against a scheme. Ask for the script back rather than only the mark, and ask twice if necessary. What should not happen is a tutor setting additional timed papers on top of school examinations, because the student then does neither properly and the resulting marks measure fatigue rather than attainment.

faqs.question: What happens to the 0266 records when we change tutor?
faqs.answer: They stay with the family, which is why they live in a shared folder rather than in a tutor's notebook. A replacement tutor reads the recall scorecard and the last two question-type splits and spends the first session diagnosing rather than rediscovering. Without that handover a new tutor typically spends two or three sessions assessing cautiously, and the family pays a second time for information it already owned. The same applies when a child changes school mid-year, moves to another emirate, or leaves the UAE part-way through Year 11.

faqs.question: Can I see a 0266 tutor's marking before I commit to a block?
faqs.answer: You should, and the trial lesson is where it happens. One free trial per subject, with no payment details taken beforehand, should end with a short piece of your child's own writing marked and returned with marks in the margin. That single page tells you more about the tutor than any introduction: whether they mark to a scheme or to a general impression, whether they can name the question type, and whether the feedback is specific enough to act on. A tutor unwilling to produce a marked page in an hour is telling you something useful.

faqs.question: How many marked 0266 papers should we have by February before the exam?
faqs.answer: Fewer complete papers than families imagine, and more marked individual answers. Two whole timed papers in the final six weeks is the usual target, because a full paper is expensive in time for both student and tutor and its main value is timing evidence. What should be plentiful by February is marked individual answers across all six question types, so the scorecard has enough entries per type to show a trend rather than a single data point. Quality of marking matters more than volume of paper.

faqs.question: Does the 0266 evidence file help with a school forecast grade?
faqs.answer: It can inform a conversation, and it is not a substitute for school assessment. Schools build forecast grades from evidence they hold themselves, and for a student who joined late or had an interrupted year that evidence can be thin. A folder of dated, timed, marked work is reasonable material to put in front of a teacher making a judgement with limited information. Present it as context rather than as a claim, ask rather than assume, and accept the school's decision; the forecast is theirs to make and no tutor has standing in it.

faqs.question: What does an in-home 0266 session cost in Dubai compared with online?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai figures read in October 2026 put in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 an hour on Bestimate's table, with independent home tutors between AED 200 and 500. Qualified online one-to-one sits lower, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. The gap is travel rather than teaching quality. A tutor crossing the city at five in the afternoon spends close to two hours on a sixty-minute lesson, and that time appears in the rate whether or not it is itemised. Those are other providers' published figures, not IB Gram prices.

faqs.question: Why is a 0266 specialist hard to find near our part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Because supply is not even across subjects. Mathematics and the sciences are taught in every school in the emirate, so the pool of experienced tutors is deep everywhere. IGCSE Psychology is an option subject with a small entry concentrated in a minority of schools, so the number of people in the region who have taken a cohort through 0266 to examination is limited. Filtering that small group by who can reach one particular address during Dubai rush hour frequently leaves nobody, and the usual consequence is a capable generalist reading ahead of the student.

faqs.question: Can 0266 sessions keep running if we relocate from Dubai to another emirate?
faqs.answer: Yes, with no change to the tutor or the records, because delivery is over live video rather than tied to an address. What does change is the regulator overseeing the new school: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under ADEK, Sharjah under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah under its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the federal Ministry of Education. Confirm with the new school which board and syllabus code it enters, since a move can change the examination board even when the subject stays the same.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-psychology-0266-on.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach Cambridge IGCSE Psychology over live video to Dubai students, working to a stated session structure rather than improvising. Each marks the student's writing on screen while the student watches, which is the part of online delivery that has no in-person equivalent.

intro.heading: Content is what school supplies; technique is what a session should buy
paragraphs: Most Dubai students who need psychology help do not need the course taught again. They have had the lessons, they own the notes, and they can discuss obedience or memory with some fluency. What they lack is a set of moves: how to turn knowledge of a study into a sentence that scores, how to attach a concept to a stranger described in a question, how to decide in four seconds how long an answer should be. Those are techniques, they are learnable, and almost nobody teaches them as a separate thing.

This changes what an hour should contain. A session that spends fifty minutes explaining content the student has already met, and ten minutes on a worksheet, has bought a repeat of school at a premium. A session built around the student writing, being marked on screen, and then rewriting the single weakest move has bought something school cannot provide at class size. The format is why this page is organised around the anatomy of the hour rather than around a topic list.

There is a second reason to be explicit about structure. Online tuition has a reputation problem in some families, usually earned by sessions where a tutor talked at a screen for an hour while a student nodded. That is a bad lesson, not a bad medium. Screen-shared annotation of a student's own script, live, with both parties typing on the same page, is genuinely better than two people sharing one piece of paper at a kitchen table, and a demonstration run on screen with reaction times recorded in a shared sheet is better than a description of one.

On delivery and on honesty: tuition for UAE families is one-to-one over live video. There are no home visits anywhere in the UAE, including Dubai, because that service is offered only in India. Market rates for in-home visits are published by other providers and quoted later on this page with their sources, so a family can see the comparison rather than take a claim on trust. What the comparison shows for a small-entry option subject is that the choice is rarely online against in-person; it is a syllabus specialist against whoever is nearby.

What follows: the session anatomy block by block; the five evaluation handles; the mark-per-minute arithmetic; how demonstrations are actually run over video; the three-step move for unseen scenarios; what changes between 0266 and the courses after it; scheduling around Gulf Standard Time, Ramadan, mocks and the summer; the recording and data-protection position; and what each price tier in this market can and cannot do. No grade is predicted anywhere on this page, and no figure quoted here is an IB Gram price. Both of those omissions are deliberate, and both are easy to check against the rest of the page.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-psychology-0266-on.programmesIntro: Technique requirements change sharply between the three Cambridge and IB stages, and online delivery adds something different at each. These are the stages a Dubai psychology student passes through.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Psychology
programmes.description: Assessed by written examination, with answers short enough that technique dominates. A 15-year-old who knows where an answer stops, how long it should be, and which five handles produce an evaluation point is operating at a different level from one with the same knowledge and no moves. Online delivery adds live marking, which at this stage is the single most useful thing a session can contain.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the practical constraint is time rather than ability. A Year 11 student carries nine or ten subjects plus the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies lessons that KHDA requires of all private schools in the emirate. Technique work is attractive precisely because it is cheap in hours relative to content teaching.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS Level Psychology
programmes.description: A standalone one-year qualification and the usual first half of the A Level. Studies are examined in procedural detail, so describing a method loosely stops being a minor loss and becomes the main one. The technique that transfers best from 0266 is precise method description; the technique that has to be rebuilt is answer length, because responses get considerably longer.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai sixth forms running IGCSE Psychology do not all continue it to AS, since a small Year 12 group is harder to staff than a Year 10 option block. Ask the school whether the group ran this year and roughly how many students were in it, because a group of three or four can be withdrawn after offers are made.

programmes.name: Cambridge International A Level Psychology
programmes.description: The full qualification, adding specified applied areas studied in depth and expecting candidates to design and justify investigations rather than critique somebody else's. Ethical justification stops being a recall exercise and becomes something written into the student's own proposed design, which is the skill 0266 ethics work is really preparing.
programmes.countryNote: Universities in the UAE and abroad rarely require psychology for a psychology degree, and several prefer a science or Mathematics alongside it. What they do assume is comfort with research design and statistics, which is the strand candidates most often skip. Check specific programme requirements with the admissions office rather than inferring them.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Psychology
programmes.description: The alternative sixth-form route, taken at Standard or Higher Level, assessed through extended written responses plus an internal investigation the student designs and reports. The writing conventions differ from the Cambridge route and critical thinking is credited explicitly, so a student moving across needs new habits rather than more facts.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai has a substantial International Baccalaureate sector, with the programme accounting for 7% of private-school enrolment and three new IB schools among the seven opening for 2026-27. A student weighing Cambridge against the Diploma should ask which subject combinations each sixth form actually timetabled last year.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-psychology-0266-on.subjectsIntro: This grid is not a topic list. These are the nine techniques a 0266 session works on, because technique is the part a class of twenty-eight rarely gets to and the part that moves a script fastest.

subjects.name: Evaluating a study
subjects.description: Producing a creditable criticism of any study using sample, method, ethics, ecological validity or usefulness, and then stating what the weakness does to the conclusion. Taught as five handles so the student is never dependent on remembering a study-specific criticism.

subjects.name: Applying to an unseen scenario
subjects.description: Naming the concept, defining it in one clause, attaching it to the person described in the question, and stating the consequence for that person. The largest single avoidable loss in the subject, and a technique rather than a knowledge gain.

subjects.name: Writing to the command word
subjects.description: Reading the verb and the mark allocation before writing, and letting those two things set the length and shape. Ten seconds per question, no knowledge required, and it corrects the over-writing that costs time later in the paper.

subjects.name: Mark-per-minute timing
subjects.description: Converting the total marks and total minutes on a paper into a rough rate, then checking an answer's length against the marks available. Students who do this stop giving four sentences to a two-word question and stop abandoning the final high-tariff item.

subjects.name: Describing a method precisely
subjects.description: Stating what was done to whom, in what order, with what measured, closely enough that a reader could repeat it. The commonest missing element on any recall check, and the one whose loss grows more expensive at AS and A Level.

subjects.name: Reading a data table
subjects.description: Identifying what the rows and columns represent, spotting the comparison the question wants, and resisting the urge to describe every number. Short, examinable and widely skipped in revision until a marked data question appears.

subjects.name: Drawing and labelling a graph
subjects.description: Choosing an appropriate chart, labelling both axes with units, and plotting accurately. Marks here are procedural rather than conceptual, which makes them the most reliably recoverable marks on the paper for any student willing to practise twice.

subjects.name: Justifying an ethical judgement
subjects.description: Naming the principle, stating whether it was breached, satisfied or genuinely unclear, and saying what the researcher should have done instead. A moral complaint scores nothing; a named principle with a remedy scores twice.

subjects.name: Designing a simple investigation
subjects.description: Writing a testable hypothesis, identifying variables, choosing a sampling method and anticipating confounds. Lightly examined at 0266 and central at AS Level, so the work done here is an investment rather than a requirement.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-psychology-0266-on.regionsIntro: Over live video the question stops being which tutors are nearby and becomes when the student can reliably sit down. These are the patterns that shape a Dubai timetable.

regions.name: Al Safa
regions.note: Short runs to the Jumeirah school belt, so after-school starts are realistic. The usual complication is a second child at a school with a later finish, which tends to set the slot for the whole household rather than for one student.

regions.name: Al Wasl
regions.note: Central location with quick access to several schools and dense afternoon traffic between them. A session over video sidesteps the traffic entirely, which in this part of the city is worth more than it sounds on paper.

regions.name: Zabeel
regions.note: Mixed housing close to the city centre with reliable connectivity. Study space is the constraint rather than bandwidth, and the household agreeing a quiet hour matters more than the equipment used.

regions.name: Oud Metha
regions.note: Close to a long-established school cluster with large cohorts. Students here often finish early and arrive home with energy left, which makes an earlier evening slot genuinely productive rather than merely available.

regions.name: Al Karama
regions.note: High-density housing with students travelling to several different school districts. Journey times vary day to day, so a fixed weekend session holds across a term better than a weekday one that depends on a bus.

regions.name: Al Nahda
regions.note: Apartment district on the Sharjah side of the city with long commutes in both directions. Evening sessions after the journey has been absorbed work better than anything attempted immediately on arrival home.

regions.name: Bur Dubai
regions.note: Established district with a wide spread of curricula in nearby schools. Confirm the examination board before the first session, because two students in the same building frequently sit different qualifications in the same subject.

regions.name: Al Satwa
regions.note: Central and well connected to several school bus routes, so arrival times are predictable. A short recall opener suits students here, who tend to get home earlier than those in the outer communities.

schoolClusters.city: Indian and mixed-board schools across central Dubai
schoolClusters.note: Large cohorts and strong academic cultures, with option blocks that frequently prioritise the sciences and commerce. Where a social-science option such as psychology runs, the group can be small and taught by a teacher carrying another subject as their main load.

schoolClusters.city: The Al Barsha and Mirdif belt
schoolClusters.note: A mix of international and British-curriculum schools serving families spread across the eastern and central districts. Students here frequently travel a considerable distance to school, which is the practical reason an evening video slot outperforms an after-school one.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-psychology-0266-on.modesIntro: Three formats, distinguished by how much of the hour the student spends writing. That proportion is the honest measure of what a session is for.

modes.title: Standard technique session
modes.description: Sixty minutes to the published anatomy: recall opener, marking of the last task, teaching of the diagnosed gap, the student writing to the clock, live annotation of what was just written, then one rule and the next task. Roughly a third of the hour is the student writing, which is the point.

At least fifteen minutes of the student writing, timed
Annotation on screen immediately after writing, not days later
Exactly one rule introduced per session

modes.title: Demonstration session
modes.description: An occasional session built around running a psychological task live rather than reading about one. Reaction-time tasks, word-list recall, interference tasks and simple perception demonstrations all work over screen share, with results typed straight into a shared sheet and then discussed as data.

modes.title: Timed-paper session
modes.description: Ninety minutes in the final stretch: a whole paper written to the clock with the camera on, then an immediate read-through of where time went. The timing data is the product. Marking follows afterwards, so the session itself is about pace and abandonment rather than about content.
bullets: A full paper under proper timed conditions

sections.heading: The sixty-minute session, block by block
paragraphs: Publishing the structure of a session is unusual and it is the fastest way for a family to judge whether they are buying teaching or company. The shape below is what a 0266 technique session runs to, in the same order every week, because predictability lets a 15-year-old arrive knowing what is about to happen and reduces the warm-up to nothing.

Two blocks do most of the work and both involve the student producing rather than receiving. The writing block is fifteen minutes at the clock on a real past question, chosen for the question type with the largest current loss. The annotation block immediately follows it, with the tutor marking on screen while the student watches each sentence being credited or passed over. That sequence, write then watch it marked, is the mechanism. Reversing it, or separating the two by several days, removes most of the effect.

The opening and closing blocks are short and administrative in the best sense. Four minutes of cold recall at the start supplies the measurement. One rule and one task at the end supplies the continuity. What is deliberately absent is a long explanation block: content teaching occupies the middle and only where the marking has shown a genuine hole, because a student who already owns the notes does not need them read aloud. The structure also makes a session auditable from the outside. A parent who knows the hour runs in six blocks can ask what happened in each one, and the answer either matches or it does not. That is a very different conversation from asking how the lesson went.

sections.heading: Five handles that produce an evaluation sentence on any study
paragraphs: Evaluation is where psychology grades are decided and where students feel least equipped, usually because they have been taught criticisms study by study. That approach fails under pressure: faced with a study they half remember, a candidate has no criticism available and writes that it was old or small. Teaching five general handles instead gives them a tool that works on anything, including a study described in the question that they have never seen.

The handles are sample, method, ethics, ecological validity and usefulness. Each answers a different question and each produces a sentence with a predictable shape. The essential discipline is the second half of the sentence. Naming a weakness earns the opening mark; saying what the weakness does to the conclusion earns the one above it. A candidate who writes that the sample was all male and stops has done half the job and will usually be surprised by the mark.

The last column of the table matters as much as the others. A handle applied where it does not fit reads as a template, and examiners notice. Ecological validity is not a meaningful criticism of a naturalistic observation. Ethics is not a live criticism of a study that obtained consent and debriefed properly, except to note that it was handled well. Teaching students when to leave a handle alone is what separates a usable technique from a formula. The handles are drilled in a fixed order at first and then unordered. A student asked for three criticisms of a described study should be able to run down the list silently, discard the two that do not fit, and write the three that do, inside about a minute. That is the standard the block is working towards.

Where the claim is explicitly limited to that group

Where the design matches the claim closely

Where consent and debriefing were handled properly
Ecological validity

Naturalistic observations and field studies

sections.heading: Mark-per-minute: the arithmetic nobody teaches
paragraphs: Timing problems masquerade as knowledge problems and are much cheaper to fix. A student who abandons the final high-tariff question has not failed to learn that topic; they have spent the available minutes somewhere less profitable. The repair is arithmetic done once, before any revision, and then applied as a habit.

Divide the total marks on the paper by the total minutes available, allowing a few minutes for reading and checking. That gives a rough rate, and the rate converts into a length expectation for every question on the paper. A two-mark question gets a fraction of a minute and two words. A ten-mark question gets several minutes and a structured answer. Students who do this stop writing paragraphs for identify questions, which is where most of the lost time originates.

The habit that makes it stick is mechanical: underline the command word and circle the mark allocation before writing anything. It takes about ten seconds a question, requires no subject knowledge whatsoever, and in a timed-paper session shows up immediately in the time log. A student who ran out of time on two consecutive papers and then does not, after one session on this, has had the cheapest grade improvement available in the subject. It also removes the most common source of panic in the hall, which is realising at the forty-minute mark that a third of the paper remains. The log is what makes this measurable rather than anecdotal. In a timed-paper session the time spent on each question is written down as the student works, so the conversation afterwards is about two specific questions rather than about working faster in general.

sections.heading: Running psychology demonstrations over live video
paragraphs: Psychology is a practical subject taught almost entirely on paper, which is a loss, and online delivery recovers some of it more easily than a classroom does. Several classic tasks run perfectly well over screen share. A word list can be presented on screen for a controlled interval and recall tested immediately, which produces a serial-position pattern a student can see in their own data. A colour-word interference task can be shown and timed. Simple reaction-time tasks and perceptual illusions work equally well.

The teaching value is not the demonstration itself but the shift in role afterwards. The student participates, then is asked to be the researcher: what was the independent variable, what was measured, what was held constant, what confounds were present, what would a second trial need to control. Answering those questions about an experience they just had is a different cognitive act from answering them about a study in a textbook, and the vocabulary sticks noticeably better.

Two cautions apply. First, a demonstration is a teaching device, not research, and nothing from it should be presented as a finding; students should be told that explicitly so the distinction between a classroom exercise and published evidence stays clear. Second, nothing should be run that involves distress, deception of the student, or the collection of personal information about anybody else. A reaction-time task is fine. Anything involving a family member as an unwitting participant is not, and the ethics discussion that follows is more useful than the data would have been.

sections.heading: The unseen scenario: a three-step move
paragraphs: Apply questions give a short description of a person or situation the student has never seen and ask them to use course concepts on it. They are the largest single source of avoidable loss in 0266, and the reason is almost comic: students write a correct, well-organised account of the relevant concept and never mention the person in the question. The content is right, the answer is wrong, and the mark reflects the answer.

The fix is a three-step move executed in a fixed order. Name the concept. Define it in one clause, not a paragraph. Attach it to the person by name, using the details the question supplied. Then state the consequence for that person specifically. The attachment step is the one that gets skipped under pressure, which is why the rule given to students is blunt: the person in the question must appear in your answer by name, at least twice.

Practising this does not need new content, which makes it fast. A tutor takes five short scenarios in one session, and the student writes four sentences on each rather than a full answer, because the move is what is being rehearsed rather than the stamina. The table sets out the steps with wording that reliably works and the failure each step prevents. Within two sessions most students stop producing scenario-free answers, and the question type that was the worst on their scorecard is usually no longer in the bottom two.

2. Define
One clause, not a paragraph
[Concept] means that...
Spending half the answer on a definition
3. Attach

The scenario-free answer, the biggest single loss
4. Consequence

Stopping before the top mark is reachable

sections.heading: What changes after 0266, and how long each gap takes to close
paragraphs: Families often ask whether 0266 prepares a student for what comes next. It prepares them unevenly, and knowing which gaps are real prevents both complacency and panic. Some skills transfer wholesale: evaluation handles, ethical reasoning, the command-word habit. Others change in kind, and a student who assumes they transfer has an uncomfortable first term in Year 12.

The largest change is the level of procedural detail expected about studies. At 0266 a method stated roughly right is often enough; at AS Level a loose method is the main loss on a question. The second largest is answer length, which grows considerably and requires planning rather than fluency. The third is statistics, which at Cambridge AS and A Level and in the IB Diploma internal investigation stops being optional reading and becomes a working requirement.

The table puts weeks against each gap, which should be read as a planning estimate rather than a promise, because it depends entirely on the student. The useful point is the ordering. Closing the method-detail gap is quick and should be done first, because it also improves 0266 marks. Statistics is slower and can wait until the summer between the courses. Independent reading is the slowest and the one no tutor can do on a student's behalf, which is worth saying to a Year 11 student before they choose a sixth-form subject on the strength of enjoying it at 16. None of this is an argument against continuing. It is an argument for spending the summer between the courses on two specific things, method detail and statistics, instead of arriving in September and discovering both at once alongside new content.

sections.heading: Scheduling an online session in the Gulf calendar
paragraphs: The practical failure mode of online tuition is not technology. It is a slot that stops working in week five and nobody renegotiates it. Six constraints account for nearly all of it, and each has an adjustment that keeps the engagement alive rather than quietly ending it.

The most common is a tutor in another time zone whose convenient hours are a Dubai family's inconvenient ones, or the reverse. Sessions are therefore agreed in Gulf Standard Time explicitly, in writing, with the tutor's local time noted alongside so neither side is guessing after a clock change elsewhere. The second is the school run and the bus, which varies by community: a student who gets home at 4.15pm and one who gets home at 5.40pm cannot share a slot pattern, and the outer communities are consistently the later.

Ramadan, the mock fortnight and the summer break each need a stated plan rather than an improvised one. During Ramadan most families shift to post-Iftar timing and shorten the session slightly, keeping frequency intact because the writing habit is what frequency protects. During mocks the right move is to reduce what is set rather than add to it. Over the summer, families travelling between countries can usually keep a reduced pattern running, which matters more before a November series than before a June one. The sixth constraint is the final six weeks, when every demand arrives together. The adjustment there is subtraction rather than addition: two timed papers, no new topics, and protected sleep. Families who add sessions in that window usually find the extra hours displace the independent revision that was doing the real work.
