sections.heading: Recordings, privacy and a minor's data
paragraphs: An online lesson generates data about a child: a video feed, possibly a recording, written work, marks, notes about weaknesses, and sometimes the name of their school. That is personal data about a minor and it deserves an explicit position rather than a reassuring sentence. The UAE's Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection governs personal data here, and a family is entitled to ask how a provider handles it.

Recording should be a decision the family makes, not a default a platform applies. Before the first paid session, a parent should establish four things in writing: whether sessions are recorded at all, who holds any recording and where, how long it is kept, and how to have it deleted. Recordings can be genuinely useful, since a student can rewatch the annotation of their own script, but the usefulness does not make the question optional.

The same discipline applies to lead forms and to what a tutor is told. A form that collects a child's school, grades, and difficulties without stating why it needs them and how long it keeps them is collecting more than it should. Our position is that written work, marks and session notes live in a folder the family controls, that nothing about a child is collected without a stated purpose, and that a privacy policy link sits on every page. Those are commitments about process, not claims about outcomes, which is the kind of claim a page like this should be making.

sections.heading: What each price tier can and cannot do
paragraphs: Dubai's tutoring market spans roughly fourteenfold from the cheapest advertised hour to the most expensive, and the advertising for all of it uses similar language. Rather than ranking the tiers, the honest framing is what each one reliably delivers and where it stops. A budget tier that explains content well is good value for a Year 10 student with a content gap and poor value for a Year 11 student with a technique problem, because marking to a published scheme is not what that price buys.

The figures below were read in October 2026 and belong to the providers named. Bestimate's Dubai rate table and the published pages of EdFlik, Tutopiya, Unitors, TutorChase and BartyED supply the bands. None of these is an IB Gram rate: ours depends on level, session length and format, and the trial lesson plus a short consultation establishes it. Any page that quotes a single number for an entire market is simplifying something a parent needs to see in detail.

Read the fourth column first. The question that matters is not what a tier costs but what it cannot do, because that is where families get caught. No tier, at any price, can produce the student's writing for them, promise a particular grade, or substitute for the hours a student puts in alone. A provider who implies otherwise is selling something that does not exist, and in a market where several ranking pages publish no price at all, scepticism about the ones making the largest claims is well placed.

process.title: Agree the slot in Gulf Standard Time, in writing
process.description: With the tutor's own local time noted beside it. Clock changes elsewhere in the world are the single most common cause of a missed online session, and a slot recorded in two time zones survives them. Set it by the latest school finisher in the household rather than the earliest.

process.title: Settle the recording question before the first paid hour
process.description: Whether sessions are recorded, who holds the file, where it is stored, how long it is kept and how to have it deleted. Four questions, answered in writing. Recordings can be genuinely useful for rewatching annotation of a script, and that does not make the questions optional.

process.title: Diagnose the question type, then book technique work
process.description: The trial lesson, one free per subject with no payment details taken beforehand, produces a short timed answer marked on screen. That identifies which question type is losing most, which determines whether the first block is evaluation handles, the scenario move, or timing arithmetic.

process.title: Hold the session anatomy for at least a month
process.description: Same six blocks, same order, every week. Predictability removes the warm-up and lets a student arrive already knowing what is about to happen. Changing the structure weekly is how a technique engagement quietly reverts to a conversation about content.

process.title: Add timed whole papers only at the end
process.description: Two complete papers under proper conditions in the final six weeks, with time per question logged as the student works. The timing data is the point. Running whole papers early produces demoralising marks on content that has not been taught yet.

whyPoints.title: The session structure is published, not improvised
whyPoints.description: Six blocks with stated purposes, roughly a third of the hour spent with the student writing. A family can check that structure against what actually happened, which is harder to do with a session described only as personalised support.

whyPoints.title: Evaluation is taught as five reusable handles
whyPoints.description: Study-by-study criticisms collapse under pressure when a student half remembers the study. Sample, method, ethics, ecological validity and usefulness work on anything, including a study described in the question that they have never seen before.

whyPoints.title: Demonstrations are run, not described
whyPoints.description: Word-list recall, interference tasks and reaction-time tasks all run over screen share with results typed into a shared sheet. A student who identifies the variables in a task they just performed retains the vocabulary noticeably better than one reading about it.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling constraints are planned for by name
whyPoints.description: Gulf Standard Time agreed in writing, the slot set by the latest school finisher, post-Iftar timing during Ramadan, less work rather than more during mocks, and a reduced pattern agreed before summer travel starts.

whyPoints.title: The data position is stated as process, not reassurance
whyPoints.description: Recording, storage, retention and deletion answered in writing before the first paid hour, with the UAE's personal data protection law named. Written work and notes live in a folder the family controls.

faqs.question: How does an online 0266 lesson actually run from start to finish?
faqs.answer: To a fixed six-block hour. Four minutes of cold recall on two studies with no prompts, which is measurement rather than warm-up. Eight minutes reviewing the marked task from last week. Around eighteen minutes of teaching, but only where the marking exposed a genuine hole. Fifteen minutes of the student writing to the clock on a real past question. Ten minutes of the tutor annotating that answer on screen while the student watches. Five minutes to state one rule and set one task. Roughly a third of the hour is the student producing, which is the design.

faqs.question: Can psychology experiments be demonstrated in an online 0266 lesson?
faqs.answer: Several classic tasks run well over screen share. A word list can be shown for a controlled interval and recall tested at once, producing a serial-position pattern in the student's own data. Colour-word interference tasks, simple reaction-time tasks and perceptual illusions all work. The value comes afterwards, when the student switches from participant to researcher and identifies the variables, controls and confounds in something they just experienced. Nothing is run that involves distress, deception of the student, or collecting information about anyone else, and nothing from a demonstration is presented as research evidence.

faqs.question: What are the five ways to evaluate a study in 0266?
faqs.answer: Sample, method, ethics, ecological validity and usefulness. Each answers a different question and produces a sentence with a predictable shape, which means a student is never stranded by half remembering a study-specific criticism. The discipline is the second half of the sentence: naming the weakness earns the opening mark, and saying what it does to the conclusion earns the one above. Knowing when a handle does not apply matters equally. Ecological validity is not a real criticism of a naturalistic observation, and applying it there reads as a template.

faqs.question: How do I work out how long my child should spend on a 0266 question?
faqs.answer: Divide the total marks on the paper by the usable minutes, allowing a few minutes for reading and checking, which gives a working rate. That rate converts into a length expectation per question: a two-mark item gets a fraction of a minute and about two words, a ten-mark item gets several minutes and a plan. The habit that makes it stick is underlining the command word and circling the mark allocation before writing. Ten seconds a question, no subject knowledge needed, and it is often the cheapest grade improvement available.

faqs.question: What changes between 0266 and AS Level Psychology?
faqs.answer: Three things, in order of size. Procedural detail about studies: a loosely stated method is a minor loss at 0266 and the main loss at AS Level. Answer length, which grows enough that responses need planning rather than fluency. And statistics, which stops being optional reading and becomes a working requirement. Evaluation handles, ethical reasoning and the command-word habit transfer unchanged. Closing the method-detail gap first makes sense because it also improves 0266 marks, while statistics is better handled in the summer between the two courses.

faqs.question: Is the cheapest online 0266 tutoring tier ever the right choice?
faqs.answer: Yes, for a specific situation. Budget online tutoring, advertised in Dubai from around AED 33 to 52 by Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 by EdFlik when read in October 2026, explains content and supports homework perfectly adequately. That is good value for a Year 10 student with a content gap. It is poor value for a Year 11 student whose problem is technique, because marking to a published scheme and splitting a paper by question type is not what the price buys. Match the tier to the diagnosis rather than to the budget alone.

faqs.question: Do online 0266 lessons work for a student who says they learn better in person?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, once the session is built properly, because the objection is almost always to a particular bad experience rather than to the medium. A tutor talking at a screen for an hour is a poor lesson in any format. A student writing for fifteen minutes and then watching their own sentences annotated live on the shared screen is doing something that has no in-person equivalent at a kitchen table. What genuinely helps is a decent microphone, an agreed quiet hour, and a session structure the student can predict before it starts.

faqs.question: What time of day suits an online 0266 lesson in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It depends on the household rather than on the subject. Families in the central districts often finish school early enough for a 4.30pm or 5pm start to be productive. Those in the outer communities, where bus journeys can run well over an hour, generally do better at 6.30pm or 7pm, after the day has been absorbed. The rule that holds across the city is to set the slot by the latest finisher in the household rather than the earliest, because a session interrupted by a second school arrival loses the writing block first.

faqs.question: Will our 0266 sessions pause during the summer holidays?
faqs.answer: That is a decision worth making deliberately rather than by default. For a student entering a November series, the summer is the most valuable block available and pausing it is costly. For a June-series candidate, a reduced pattern of one session a fortnight keeps recall from decaying without consuming the holiday. Families travelling between countries can usually keep sessions running over video, which is one of the clearer practical advantages of the format. What rarely works is an unspoken assumption that sessions will resume on their own in September.

faqs.question: Can an online 0266 tutor follow my child's own school deadlines?
faqs.answer: They should, and a tutor who teaches to a generic sequence instead is adding a second syllabus to a student's week. Send the school scheme of work if the school publishes one, the dates of internal assessments and mocks, and any deadline the school has set. The practical effect is that teaching follows the school's order rather than a textbook order, and that a mock fortnight becomes a week of reduced work rather than a week of double work. Tutors who insist on their own sequence are usually working around not knowing the school's.

faqs.question: How does an online 0266 tutor handle the data and graph questions?
faqs.answer: Better than a classroom can, because a shared sheet is a live tool. Data generated in a demonstration goes straight into a sheet both sides can see, and the student plots it, labels the axes with units, and then answers the question types that attach to it. Marks on this strand are procedural rather than conceptual, which makes them the most reliably recoverable marks on the paper for any student prepared to practise twice. It is also the strand most commonly missing from a revision plan entirely until a marked data question appears.

faqs.question: Is a group online 0266 class cheaper and still useful?
faqs.answer: Cheaper per student, and useful for a particular purpose. A group works for shared explanation, worked examples and keeping a motivated student to a structure. What it cannot deliver is per-student marking, an individual question-type split, or a cold-recall check that pauses on one student's missing element. For a 0266 candidate whose problem is technique rather than content, the thing a group removes is precisely the thing worth paying for. For content catch-up early in Year 10, a group is a reasonable economy.

faqs.question: What internet speed do online 0266 lessons need in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Far less than most families assume, and the limiting factor is almost never bandwidth. A standard home fibre connection anywhere in the emirate carries video and screen sharing comfortably. The two things that genuinely degrade a session are the microphone and the room. A built-in laptop microphone in an open-plan apartment collects the whole household, and a tutor who cannot hear a hesitant half-answer cannot diagnose it. Headphones with a boom microphone cost very little and solve it. A second screen or tablet helps but is not necessary.

faqs.question: Can one online tutor take my child from 0266 through to A Level psychology?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking the question explicitly rather than assuming continuity. Ask whether the tutor has taught Cambridge AS and A Level Psychology to examination as well as the IGCSE, because the procedural detail, answer length and statistics expected at the later stage are genuinely different demands. Continuity has real value: a tutor who already holds a student's recall history and question-type history starts Year 12 with information nobody else has. It is not worth keeping a tutor who has only taught the earlier course, though.

intro.heading: Psychology at 16 is a precise subject that reads like a general one
paragraphs: Students choose psychology because it sounds like it will explain people. The course does explain people, but it does so through named studies, stated assumptions, controlled variables and a vocabulary of research design that has to be used exactly. The distance between an interesting opinion about memory and a creditable answer about a memory study is the whole of the subject, and a student who has not been shown where that line sits will write fluently and score in the middle.

Cambridge IGCSE Psychology 0266 asks for three things that can be separated and taught separately. First, knowledge: approaches, the assumptions behind them, named studies with method and findings attached. Second, application: taking a concept and using it on a scenario the student has not seen before. Third, evaluation: judging a study or an explanation on stated grounds such as sample, method, ethics or ecological validity. Most lost marks sit in the third category, and most revision time is spent in the first.

There is also a maths problem nobody warns families about. Psychology at this level handles data: tables, graphs, measures of central tendency, the difference between quantitative and qualitative evidence. A student who dislikes numbers can be ambushed by a question asking which measure of central tendency suits a data set and why. It is a small part of the course and a reliable source of dropped marks, and it is fixed in roughly two sessions once somebody notices.

Delivery is online. IB Gram matches Dubai families with specialist tutors who teach one-to-one over live video, screen-sharing the student's own written work. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or elsewhere in the UAE, because home visits are a service offered only in India. For 0266 that constraint works in a family's favour. Psychology is a small entry at IGCSE across the Gulf, the pool of tutors who have taken a cohort through it is correspondingly thin, and selecting from that pool by driving distance rather than by syllabus experience is how a family ends up with a general science tutor reading ahead each week.

The rest of this page covers what 0266 is and how it differs from the A Level and the Diploma course, the four approaches set against each other, the core topics a candidate carries, the research-methods terms that must be exact, the ethics vocabulary, a mark-band map from identify to discuss, who may legally take money for private tuition in the UAE, and how to start. Sources are named where a fact is sourced, and flagged where it must be verified against the syllabus for your child's examination year. One thing is not covered here, deliberately. No grade outcome is predicted anywhere on this page, because no tutor can honestly predict one. A provider who promises a particular grade in a subject examined by written paper is selling something nobody can deliver, and that promise should be read as a warning sign rather than as confidence.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-psychology-0266-tu.programmesIntro: Psychology appears at three school stages and in a fourth at university, and the expectations change sharply between them. Families often buy support pitched at the wrong one, which is why the comparison comes first on this page.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Psychology
programmes.description: The two-year Cambridge Upper Secondary course and the focus of this page. It introduces the main approaches to explaining behaviour, a set of named studies, the basics of research design, and the ethical framework psychological research operates inside. Assessment is by written examination, which concentrates the grade into a short window and makes timed written practice during the course the most valuable thing a tutor can run.
programmes.countryNote: Confirm with the school whether 0266 is actually timetabled before planning around it. Psychology is an option-block subject in Dubai and smaller cohorts are sometimes cut when numbers fall below a school's threshold, which is how families discover in Year 10 that the subject their child chose in Year 9 is no longer running at that school.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS & A Level Psychology
programmes.description: The sixth-form continuation, and a significant step rather than an extension. Content deepens into specified applied areas, studies are examined in far more detail, and research-methods questions expect a student to design and critique investigations rather than recognise them. Students arriving from 0266 with secure methods vocabulary find the transition manageable; students arriving with topic knowledge alone generally do not.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai sixth forms do not all offer Psychology at A Level even where the school runs IGCSE Psychology, because staffing a small Year 12 group is harder than staffing a Year 10 option. Ask the sixth form directly, and ask whether the group ran in the current year rather than whether it is listed in the prospectus.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Psychology
programmes.description: The other common sixth-form route in Dubai, offered at Standard and Higher Level. Diploma Psychology is assessed through written papers plus an internal assessment built around a simple experimental investigation, and it expects extended essay-style responses with explicit critical thinking. It is a different qualification from the Cambridge route rather than a harder version of it, and the writing conventions differ.
programmes.countryNote: The International Baccalaureate accounts for 7% of Dubai private-school enrolment, and the emirate's 2026-27 intake adds three new IB schools among seven new openings creating 16,846 places. A student weighing the Cambridge and Diploma routes in Dubai now has more choice of school than in previous years, but a specific subject at a specific level still depends on one timetable.

programmes.name: Psychology at degree level
programmes.description: Universities in the UAE and abroad rarely require school psychology for a psychology degree, and some prefer Biology or Mathematics alongside it. What they do expect is comfort with research design and statistics, which is precisely the strand IGCSE candidates most often avoid. A student who takes the methods work seriously at 16 arrives at a degree with the part most first-year students struggle with already familiar.
programmes.countryNote: Attestation and equivalency for a UAE university application sit with the Ministry of Education and the emirate authority, not with a school or a tutor. On the British track the published requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE passes at no less than grade E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, alongside one Advanced Level pass at grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary passes.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-psychology-0266-tu.subjectsIntro: A 0266 course divides into strands that fail independently of one another. These are the strands a tutor works through, with what each actually demands. Confirm the exact content list against the syllabus document for your child's examination year.

subjects.name: The biological approach
subjects.description: Behaviour explained through the brain, the nervous system, hormones and genetics. Strong on measurable evidence and on cases where physiology clearly drives behaviour; weak where culture or meaning is doing the work. Students over-apply it, because it feels the most scientific of the four.

subjects.name: The cognitive approach
subjects.description: Behaviour explained through internal mental processing: memory, attention, perception, schemas. The models are the examinable content, and students must be able to describe a model and then say what evidence supports or undermines it rather than simply reciting the diagram.

subjects.name: The learning approach
subjects.description: Behaviour as acquired, through classical and operant conditioning and through observation and imitation. The commonest error is mixing up the two forms of conditioning. A student who can state what is being paired and what is being reinforced will not make that error again.

subjects.name: The social approach
subjects.description: Behaviour explained by the presence and influence of other people: obedience, conformity, group effects, situational pressure. This strand carries the best-known studies in psychology, which makes it the one students feel most confident about and the one where they most often describe instead of evaluating.

subjects.name: Research methods and study design
subjects.description: Experiments, observations, self-report, case studies and correlation, with hypotheses, variables, controls, sampling and reliability attached. Marks here go to precision rather than fluency, and the vocabulary recurs in questions across every other strand on the paper.

subjects.name: Named core studies
subjects.description: Each study needs a name, an aim, a method stated accurately, the findings and a conclusion, plus two or three evaluation points. Recognition is not recall. A study the student can discuss when prompted but cannot produce cold under timed conditions will not be available in the examination hall.

subjects.name: Research ethics
subjects.description: Informed consent, deception, the right to withdraw, debriefing, confidentiality and protection from harm. These are not general good manners; they are the terms an examiner looks for. A student who writes that a study was unfair scores nothing where naming the breached principle scores.

subjects.name: Data handling and simple analysis
subjects.description: Tables, bar charts and graphs, mean, median and mode, range, and the distinction between quantitative and qualitative data. Short, examinable and widely skipped in revision. Knowing which measure of central tendency suits a skewed data set is a two-session fix that pays every series.

subjects.name: Application and evaluation
subjects.description: Taking a concept to an unseen scenario, and judging a study on stated grounds: sample, method, ethics, ecological validity, usefulness. This is where the difference between a middling and a strong grade is decided, and it is the strand least likely to be taught as a separate skill.

sections.heading: What 0266 is, and how it differs from A Level and Diploma psychology
paragraphs: Families searching for psychology support in Dubai are often reading material written for a different qualification. The three school routes share a vocabulary and almost nothing else. Cambridge IGCSE Psychology 0266 introduces the approaches and a set of named studies at a level a 15-year-old can hold. Cambridge AS and A Level Psychology 9990 examines specified applied areas in depth and expects a candidate to design and critique investigations. IB Diploma Psychology is assessed through extended written responses plus an internal investigation, with explicit credit for critical thinking.

This matters practically. A tutor whose experience is entirely Diploma will teach a Year 10 student to write Diploma-length essays, which wastes a year of session time on a skill the 0266 paper does not ask for. A tutor whose experience is entirely IGCSE will under-prepare a Year 12 student. Asking which syllabus code the tutor has taken a cohort through, and in which series, resolves this in one question and is worth more than a conversation about teaching philosophy.

The table compares the three routes across the things that change what tutoring should do. Treat the content-depth and assessment rows as orientation rather than specification: confirm current structures in the Cambridge syllabus document for your child's examination year on cambridgeinternational.org, or with the Diploma coordinator for the IB route, because both organisations revise their documents on a cycle and outdated versions circulate freely online. The row worth reading twice is the last one. It says what tutoring should target on each route, and those targets barely overlap. Buying Diploma-style essay coaching for a 0266 candidate is not a cautious overspend; it is time spent on a skill the paper will not reward.

sections.heading: Four approaches, set against each other
paragraphs: Approaches are the backbone of 0266 and are almost always taught as a sequence of topics, which is why students can name four and use none. An approach is not a chapter. It is a claim about where behaviour comes from, and its value in an examination is that it generates an explanation for any behaviour a question puts in front of a candidate. The useful drill is therefore not what is the cognitive approach but what would each approach say about this same piece of behaviour.

Run that drill with one scenario, a child who becomes anxious before tests, and ask for four one-sentence explanations. The biological answer reaches for physiological arousal. The cognitive answer reaches for how the child is interpreting the situation. The learning answer reaches for what previous experience has reinforced. The social answer reaches for the influence of peers, parents and classroom expectations. Four genuinely different sentences means the approaches are usable. Four versions of the same sentence means the student has labels.

The table sets the approaches against each other with the cell that matters most in the final column: how each one is actually used in an answer. Note the explains-badly column. Evaluation marks in psychology frequently come from identifying what an approach cannot account for, so a student who knows the weakness of an explanation has an evaluation point ready before they have read the question. That is the cheapest preparation available in this subject.

sections.heading: The core topics a candidate carries, and how to hold a study
paragraphs: Beyond the approaches sits a body of topic content: memory and forgetting, perception, attachment and development, obedience and conformity, and the psychology of atypical behaviour among them. Confirm the precise list in the syllabus for your child's examination year, because the published content changes between syllabus versions and revision material written for an older one is widely available and widely mistaken for current.

What does not change is how a study has to be held. Five elements make a study usable: its name, its aim, its method stated accurately enough that somebody could repeat it, its findings, and its conclusion. Two or three evaluation points attach to each. A student who can produce those five elements cold, without a prompt, owns the study. A student who recognises it on a revision card does not, and the difference only becomes visible in a timed paper when the card is not there.

The practical method is a cold recall check at the start of every session, which takes four minutes and does more for retention than any amount of rereading. Name a study, the student produces the five elements aloud, the tutor notes which element was missing. Over a term that produces a short list of studies with a consistently missing element, usually the method, and the remedy is targeted rather than general. This is also the most honest progress evidence available in psychology, because it cannot be faked by familiarity with a tutor.

sections.heading: The research-methods terms that have to be exact
paragraphs: Psychology is a subject where loose vocabulary costs marks in a way loose thinking sometimes does not. Reliability and validity are different properties. Ecological validity is not a synonym for validity in general. A random sample is one in which every member of the population has an equal chance of selection, which is not the same as a sample the researcher did not plan carefully. Demand characteristics describe participants working out and responding to the study's purpose, not a researcher's expectations leaking out.

These distinctions recur across the paper rather than appearing in one methods question, which is why the methods block pays back more than any single topic. A student who can define the terms and attach a standard strength and limitation to each design has material available for evaluation questions on every strand. The drill is definition first, tested cold, then application to a described study, then critique.

The table lists the terms a 0266 candidate needs with the definition that scores, the sloppy version students actually write, and where it shows up. Parents can use the middle two columns as a test at home: ask for a definition, and if what comes back resembles the third column rather than the second, the methods block is the first thing to buy. It is also the cheapest thing to buy, because the content is small and fixed. Two further pairs deserve the same treatment. Quantitative and qualitative data are distinguished by the form of the evidence, not by how rigorous the study was. And a correlation describes a relationship between two measured variables without establishing that one caused the other, which is a sentence a candidate should be able to write without hesitating in any series.

sections.heading: Ethics: six words an examiner is looking for
paragraphs: Ethics questions are among the most reliably available marks in 0266 and among the most reliably missed. The reason is that students answer them morally rather than technically. Asked what is ethically wrong with a study, a candidate writes that it was unfair on the participants, or that it would not be allowed today. Both statements may be true and neither names a principle, so neither can be credited in the band that requires one.

Six terms do almost all the work: informed consent, deception, the right to withdraw, debriefing, confidentiality, and protection from harm. Each has a precise meaning and each has a standard remedy attached. Deception, for instance, is sometimes defensible if a debrief follows and the deception was necessary to the design; a student who can say that has an evaluation point rather than a complaint. A student who can also say what the researcher should have done instead has two.

A useful exercise, and one that works well over video because both parties can annotate the same text, is to take a described study and annotate it for all six principles in turn, marking each as satisfied, breached, or unclear. Unclear is an allowed answer and often the correct one, which surprises students who expect ethics to be a matter of right and wrong. The habit transfers directly to the A Level and Diploma routes, where ethical justification has to be written into a student's own investigation rather than applied to somebody else's.

sections.heading: A mark-band map: where candidates stop writing
paragraphs: Most psychology underperformance is not a knowledge failure. It is a stopping failure. A student answers the question as far as describing, and the marks beyond that point go uncollected because nobody told them a further move existed. Mapping that explicitly, question type by question type, is a fast intervention: the student is not learning new content, only learning where the end of an answer actually sits.

The pattern is consistent. On identify questions candidates over-write, spending four sentences where two words score, and lose the time later. On describe questions they explain, which is a different instruction. On evaluate questions they offer a general comment about the study being old or small rather than naming the ground and stating the consequence. On apply questions they describe the concept and then stop before touching the scenario at all, which is the single largest avoidable loss in the subject.

The table maps each question type against what earns the opening marks, what earns the top marks, and where the student typically stops. Used as a self-check, it converts a vague instruction to write more into a specific one: on an apply question, the last sentence must mention the person in the scenario by name. On an evaluate question, the last sentence must say what the weakness means for the conclusion. Those two rules alone move scripts. There is a reading habit behind this as well. Students who underline the command word and the number of marks before writing allocate their effort correctly roughly from the first attempt, and students who begin writing immediately usually do not. It costs ten seconds a question and is the only revision technique on this page that requires no knowledge at all.

sections.heading: Who may legally take money for private tuition in the UAE
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is a permitted activity with a permit attached, and families are entitled to ask about it. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, which removes the most common excuse for not holding one. Eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18.

The official route is the MoHRE service page for private tutor licensing, which lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, and a figure circulating online could not be verified during research for this page, so no amount is quoted here and any provider quoting one should be asked for a source.

A separate rule deserves a Dubai family's attention. A tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal entity from an individual tutor and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, a rule reported in the press that should be checked against the current ADEK policy document. Never engage your child's own class teacher privately without establishing the position first.

sections.heading: A twelve-session plan for a 0266 student who is stuck in the middle
paragraphs: The commonest 0266 request from a Dubai parent is about a student who revises, understands the material in conversation, and keeps scoring in the middle of the range. That pattern has a standard shape and a standard sequence of repairs, and twelve sessions is usually enough to work through it provided the diagnosis happens first rather than last.

Sessions one and two are diagnostic: a short written answer of each question type, marked, plus a cold recall check on three studies and a methods vocabulary test. That produces a specific list rather than a general worry. Sessions three to five run the methods and data clinic, because methods marks recur across the paper and the content is small. Sessions six to eight attack the stopping problem on evaluate and apply questions, using the mark-band map as an explicit checklist. Sessions nine and ten build cold recall on the studies that keep losing an element.

Sessions eleven and twelve are whole papers under timed conditions, marked, held beside the week-one answers. That is the first comparison that means anything, and it is also where timing problems become undeniable. Nobody can promise a grade from twelve sessions, and a provider who does should be treated with real scepticism. What can be said is that the stopping problem and the methods problem are both fast to fix, and that a marked baseline in week one tells you within a session which of them you are dealing with.

Sessions 3-5: methods and data clinic, definitions tested cold
Sessions 6-8: the stopping problem on evaluate and apply questions
Sessions 9-10: cold recall rebuilt on the studies losing an element
Sessions 11-12: whole papers, timed and marked against the week-one baseline

sections.heading: Getting started, and the honest position on availability
paragraphs: Starting takes three facts and one hour. The three facts are the board and syllabus code from the school entry form, the series the school is entering, and the most recent real mark with the paper it came from. The hour is a free trial lesson, one per subject, with no payment details taken beforehand, which ends with a short written answer marked on screen and a note on which of the standard problems is dominant.

The disclosure concerns supply. IGCSE Psychology is a small entry across the UAE, far smaller than Mathematics or the sciences, and the number of tutors in the region who have taken a cohort through 0266 to examination is limited. On a week when none of them has a slot, we will say so rather than place a general science or humanities tutor and hope the difference does not show. The alternatives we would put to a Dubai family are a specialist in another time zone whose availability suits a Dubai evening, a start date a few weeks out, or a short diagnostic engagement now with the main block starting when a specialist frees up.

What we will not do is describe a willing generalist as a specialist. In a subject where marks turn on exact methods vocabulary and on knowing where an answer stops, a capable teacher reading the syllabus a week ahead of the student produces lessons that feel productive and scripts that do not move. A marked paper makes that visible inside a month, which is an expensive way for a family to find out something that could have been said at the start.

process.title: Send the code, the series and the last real mark
process.description: Take the board and syllabus code from the school entry form rather than from memory, and send the most recent mark with the paper it came from. A mark without a paper is not information. These three facts determine the level a tutor should pitch at and when the work has to start.

process.title: Diagnose before any teaching
process.description: The trial lesson, free, one per subject, with no payment details taken beforehand, produces a short written answer and a cold recall check on one study. Whether the dominant problem is content, methods vocabulary or the stopping habit decides what the next six sessions do, and guessing wastes them.

process.title: Fix the methods vocabulary early
process.description: Reliability, validity, ecological validity, sampling and demand characteristics recur in questions across every strand of the paper. The content is small and fixed, which makes it the highest return per session available in 0266 and the strand most often left until the final term.

process.title: Make cold recall the routine
process.description: Four minutes at the start of each session: name a study, the student produces aim, method, findings and conclusion without a prompt. The missing element gets logged by name. Over a term this builds the only progress record in psychology that familiarity with a tutor cannot fake.

process.title: Finish with timed whole papers
process.description: Two complete papers under examination conditions in the final fortnight, marked, kept beside the first diagnostic answers. This is the point at which a comparison carries meaning, and the point at which a timing problem stops being a suspicion.

whyPoints.title: Matched by syllabus code, not by subject name
whyPoints.description: A tutor is matched on having taught 0266 to examination, not on having studied psychology. The three school psychology routes differ enough that a Diploma specialist will teach a Year 10 student to write answers the Cambridge paper does not ask for, which costs a year of sessions.

whyPoints.title: Approaches taught as competing explanations
whyPoints.description: Four labels recited in order score nothing. Four different one-sentence explanations of the same behaviour score a great deal, and the weakness of each approach supplies an evaluation point before the question has even been read. That drill takes one session.

whyPoints.title: The data element is not skipped
whyPoints.description: Tables, graphs and the measures of central tendency are a small, examinable part of psychology that most revision material glosses over. Knowing which measure suits a skewed data set is two sessions of work and shows up in every series.

whyPoints.title: The permit position is stated with its source
whyPoints.description: The private tuition permit, its legal basis, its two-year validity and the fact that it carries no fee are set out with the official application route named. No fine amount is published anywhere official, so none is quoted here, and any provider quoting one should be asked where it came from.

whyPoints.title: Availability limits are disclosed first
whyPoints.description: 0266 is a small entry in this region. If no tutor who has taught it to examination is free, we say so and set out the alternatives rather than placing a generalist and letting a marked paper reveal it in February.

faqs.question: What is Cambridge IGCSE Psychology 0266, and is it the same as A Level Psychology?
faqs.answer: It is the Cambridge Upper Secondary psychology course, usually taken in Years 10 and 11, introducing the main approaches to explaining behaviour, a set of named studies, the basics of research design and the ethical framework research operates inside. It is not a lighter version of Cambridge AS and A Level Psychology 9990. The A Level examines specified applied areas in far greater depth and expects candidates to design and justify investigations rather than recognise and critique them. A tutor should be asked which code they have taught to examination, because the two courses reward different writing.

faqs.question: Which approaches does my child need by name for 0266?
faqs.answer: The biological, cognitive, learning and social approaches do most of the work, with individual differences useful as a limit on any universal claim. Confirm the content for your child's examination year in the syllabus document, since published content changes between versions. The test of whether they are usable is not definition but application: given one scenario, such as a child who becomes anxious before tests, can your child produce four genuinely different one-sentence explanations? Four versions of the same sentence means labels rather than positions, and that gap closes in about two sessions of focused work.

faqs.question: How many core studies does a 0266 candidate have to know?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most students try to learn, held far better than most students hold them. A usable study has five elements the candidate can produce cold: its name, its aim, its method stated accurately, its findings and its conclusion, with two or three evaluation points attached. Recognition on a revision card is not recall. The practical routine is a four-minute cold check at the start of each session, with the missing element logged by name. Over a term that produces a short, specific list rather than a general sense that revision is not sticking.

faqs.question: What ethics terms is a 0266 answer expected to use?
faqs.answer: Informed consent, deception, the right to withdraw, debriefing, confidentiality and protection from harm. Ethics questions are among the most reliably available marks in the subject and among the most reliably missed, because students answer them morally rather than technically. Writing that a study was unfair on its participants cannot be credited where naming the breached principle can. A stronger answer names the principle, says whether it was breached, satisfied or unclear, and then states what the researcher should have done instead, which turns a complaint into two creditable points.

faqs.question: Does 0266 involve maths, and how much?
faqs.answer: A small but genuinely examinable amount. Candidates handle tables, bar charts and graphs, the mean, median and mode, the range, and the distinction between quantitative and qualitative data. A question asking which measure of central tendency suits a particular data set and why is entirely fair and catches students who chose psychology to avoid numbers. The quantity of content is small enough to cover properly in about two sessions, which makes it one of the cheapest grade improvements available in the course and one of the most commonly postponed until the final term.

faqs.question: Where do 0266 candidates in Dubai most often lose marks?
faqs.answer: By stopping too early rather than by not knowing enough. On describe questions they explain, which is a different instruction. On evaluate questions they say a study was old or small without saying what that means for the conclusion. On apply questions they define the concept correctly and never mention the person in the scenario, which is the single largest avoidable loss in the subject. Two rules fix most of it: on an apply question the last sentence must name the person in the scenario, and on an evaluate question the last sentence must state the consequence.

faqs.question: Is a 0266 tutor legally allowed to teach privately in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Private tuition in the UAE operates under a permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories include school and government teachers, public and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The official application route is the MoHRE private tutor licensing service, which lists a two-working-day completion time. Those tutoring without a permit face fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted to you.

faqs.question: Can my child take 0266 if their school does not timetable it?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, through private-candidate entry at an examination centre that accepts external candidates for that syllabus, but the practical barriers are real. The centre controls the entry and its deadline sits months before the papers, so the decision has to be made early. Start by asking the current school whether it will enter the student even if it does not teach the course, because that is far simpler than approaching centres independently. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone.

faqs.question: Does 0266 help with applying to study psychology at a UAE university?
faqs.answer: It helps as preparation more than as a requirement. Most psychology degrees in the UAE and abroad do not demand school psychology, and some prefer Biology or Mathematics alongside it. What they do assume is comfort with research design and basic statistics, which is exactly the strand school candidates tend to avoid. A 0266 pass can count among the five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3 that the British-track equivalency requirement names, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count. Verify current requirements with the Ministry.

faqs.question: How is 0266 different from IB Diploma Psychology in Dubai schools?
faqs.answer: They are separate qualifications rather than levels of one. Diploma Psychology, offered at Standard and Higher Level, is assessed through extended written responses plus an internal investigation the student designs and reports on, with explicit credit for critical thinking. 0266 is pitched at Years 10 and 11 and assessed by written examination, with shorter responses and a lighter research-design demand. A student moving from one to the other needs new writing conventions rather than more content, and a tutor who has only taught one route will pitch the other wrongly.

faqs.question: How many 0266 sessions a week does a Dubai student need?
faqs.answer: One weekly session of sixty minutes suits most students through Years 10 and 11, provided something is written between sessions. Psychology improves through producing answers and through cold recall, not through contact time, so a second weekly session with no work in between generally adds cost rather than marks. Families usually move to two sessions in the eight to twelve weeks before a series, with one spent writing under timed conditions and the other on the marking. A twelve-session block is the usual shape for a student stuck in the middle of the range.

faqs.question: Will a 0266 tutor come to our home in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Psychology 0266 sessions run one-to-one over live video, with work screen-shared so both sides annotate the same page. For this subject the trade is favourable. IGCSE Psychology is a small entry across the Gulf, so the number of tutors who have taken a cohort through 0266 is limited, and narrowing that further to whoever can reach your address in Dubai traffic usually means accepting a generalist over a specialist.

faqs.question: Can a 0266 tutor support a school psychology investigation without breaking the rules?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach research design, question a weak hypothesis until the student improves it, explain why a sampling choice is vulnerable, model the reasoning on a different investigation, and give detailed feedback on what the student has produced. A tutor cannot supply text for submission, decide the design on the student's behalf, or hand over analysis the student then presents as their own. The boundary is easiest to hold when the student's work is dated and marked after it is written rather than developed jointly, because authorship then is not a matter of anybody's recollection.

faqs.question: Is Year 10 or Year 11 the better time to start 0266 tutoring?
faqs.answer: Year 10, if the choice is free. A session running alongside the school scheme of work consolidates each strand as it is taught and keeps the methods vocabulary accurate from the start, which prevents the Year 11 problem of meeting three terms of accumulated gaps at once. Starting in Year 11 still works and is what most families do, but the sequence has to be compressed and diagnosis matters more because there is no time to discover the real problem slowly. Either way, a marked baseline in week one is what makes the plan rational.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-psychology-0266-tu.closingHeading: Ask for a definition and a study
dubai/cambridge-igcse-psychology-0266-tu.closingBody: Two questions will tell you whether your child needs a Cambridge IGCSE Psychology 0266 tutor. Ask them to define reliability and validity without looking anything up. Then name one study from the course and ask for its aim, method, findings and conclusion, cold. If both answers come back clean, the course is in hand. If either wobbles, you have found the first six sessions. Send the board, code and series, take the free trial lesson, one per subject with no payment details taken beforehand, and you will have a marked answer and a specific starting point within the hour.

intro.heading: What an evidence file for Cambridge IGCSE Sociology looks like
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE Sociology 0495 is a two-year course that most Dubai schools begin in Year 10 and examine at the end of Year 11. It is not a soft option. Students arrive expecting opinion and discussion and find a subject with a technical vocabulary, several substantive topic areas, a research-methods strand that behaves more like a science paper than an essay subject, and extended-response questions that reward evaluation over recall. A child who talks fluently about family life in Dubai can still score poorly, because the paper does not ask what they think.

That gap between articulate and assessed is why parents start looking for a tutor. It is also why asking how it is going produces nothing useful. Sociology sets no spelling test and no sums you can check over dinner. Progress shows up only in the shape of a written answer: whether the student defined the term, whether a named perspective or named study appeared, whether a counter-argument arrived before the conclusion. None of that is visible to a parent unless somebody writes it down and keeps it.

So this page is built around the paperwork. A session on 0495 should leave behind something dated that you can open: a timed answer carrying marks and margin notes, a plan reworked after feedback, a running list of command words the student has now handled correctly and the ones still going wrong, and a short note saying what changed and what comes next. Over ten or twelve weeks that becomes a file. A file is the only honest way to separate real improvement from growing familiarity with a tutor, and it is the thing a family can take to a school parents evening instead of a feeling.

Delivery is online. IB Gram matches Dubai families with one-to-one tutors who teach over live video and screen-share the student's own script so both sides annotate the same page. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. That is a deliberate trade rather than a limitation. A small-entry subject like 0495 has very few specialist teachers in any single emirate, and narrowing the search to people who can drive to Jumeirah by five on a Tuesday means choosing geography over subject knowledge.

What follows sets out what the Dubai market charges in AED and who charges it, the command words that decide marks, the topics where candidates here lose them, a twelve-week reading of the evidence file, the Cambridge series calendar counted backwards from the exam, the academic-honesty line a sociology tutor may not cross, and the KHDA context your child's school works inside. Every figure is attributed and dated, because an unsourced number helps nobody making a decision about their child.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-sociology-0495-hom.programmesIntro: Sociology sits inside a wider Cambridge pathway, and the decision a Dubai family makes at 16 changes what the 0495 year needs to deliver. These are the programmes most often in play around a 0495 candidate in this emirate.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: The two-year Cambridge Upper Secondary qualification sat by the largest curriculum group in Dubai's private schools. Sociology 0495 is usually an option block choice taken alongside a humanities subject and a language. Assessment is by written examination at the end of the course, which places the whole grade on a short window and makes timed-answer practice during the year the single highest-value activity a tutor can run.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools enter candidates in either the June or the November series, and a few run both for different cohorts. Because 0495 is a smaller entry than Mathematics or Biology, a school may have one teacher covering it, and that teacher may also carry Geography or History. Independent one-to-one support is often the only route to a second expert reading of a student's written answers.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The other British-track option used by Dubai schools. Pearson codes differ from Cambridge codes, the paper structures differ, and the mark scheme language differs. A student revising from the wrong board's past papers will practise questions that are never asked. Confirming the board and the exact code on the school entry form before any revision begins prevents the most expensive mistake available in a Year 11 year.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs International GCSE in May or June and November each year. Its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those dates matter to a Dubai family planning a retake inside one academic year.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS & A Level
programmes.description: The usual destination for a Dubai student who enjoys 0495. A Level Sociology asks for sustained argument across longer essays, more theory by name, and a genuine grasp of methodological debate rather than a list of strengths and limitations. The habits that earn a strong IGCSE grade, define, apply, evaluate, conclude, are the same habits scaled up, which is why building them properly at 16 pays twice.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, a student must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or above, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among those five. Verify current wording with the Ministry before relying on it.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Dubai has a substantial IB sector, and some 0495 students move into the Diploma rather than A Level. There is no direct IB equivalent of IGCSE Sociology; the nearest routes are Global Politics, Psychology, or Social and Cultural Anthropology where a school offers it. The research-methods work in 0495 transfers directly into the Diploma internal assessment culture, where method choice has to be defended rather than asserted.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. Six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. A family choosing between an A Level and a Diploma route in Dubai now has more supply than in previous years, and the subject a child enjoys at 16 is worth weighing against what each sixth form actually timetables.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-sociology-0495-hom.subjectsIntro: A 0495 evidence file is organised by topic area, because that is how the syllabus is organised and how marks are reported back. These are the strands a Dubai tutor works through, and what each one tends to need.

subjects.name: Theory and methods
subjects.description: The perspectives, functionalism, Marxism, feminism and interactionism among them, plus the structure and action debate. Students who learn these as labels write unusable answers. Students who learn them as positions that predict what a sociologist would say about a family, a school or a newspaper can apply them anywhere on the paper.

subjects.name: Research methods and evidence
subjects.levels: Technical strand, heavily weighted in practice
subjects.description: Questionnaires, structured and unstructured interviews, observation, experiments, official statistics and documents, with sampling, reliability, validity, representativeness and ethics attached to each. This strand behaves like a science paper: terms have fixed meanings and marks go to precision, not to fluency.

subjects.name: Culture, identity and socialisation
subjects.description: Primary and secondary socialisation, agencies of socialisation, norms, values, roles and status, nature against nurture. Dubai students have unusually rich material here because many live across two or three cultural settings, and the examiner rewards a specific example far above a general observation.

subjects.name: Social inequality and stratification
subjects.description: Class, gender, ethnicity and age as sources of inequality, social mobility, poverty and life chances. The trap is description. A question on inequality rarely wants a list of differences; it wants a sociological explanation of why the difference persists and a judgement about which explanation holds up.

subjects.name: Family and household change
subjects.description: Family types, changing patterns of marriage, divorce and child-rearing, functions of the family, and critiques of each. Candidates lose marks by writing about their own household as though it were evidence. The fix is to name the pattern, name who argues about it, and then use the personal example as illustration.

subjects.name: Education
subjects.description: The functions of education, in-school and out-of-school factors in achievement, the hidden curriculum, labelling and setting, and the relationship between education and work. A Dubai candidate can use a private-school system with 17 curricula as a live case, provided the claim stays sociological rather than anecdotal.

subjects.name: Crime, deviance and social control
subjects.description: Definitions of crime and deviance, formal and informal social control, explanations of offending, and the problems of measuring crime. Measurement is where most marks sit: a student who can explain why official statistics under-record offences has a point to make in several different questions.

subjects.name: Media
subjects.description: Ownership and control, representation, audience effect debates and new media. The common error is to argue effects as though they were proven. The mark goes to the student who sets out a position, supplies the counter-position, and then says which is better supported and why.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-sociology-0495-hom.regionsIntro: Online delivery means the area a Dubai family lives in no longer limits the tutor pool, but it still shapes when a session can realistically start. These are the patterns that matter for scheduling a 0495 slot.

Market rates in Dubai as published in October 2026 run from roughly AED 45 an hour at the budget end to AED 650 for a premium named tutor, which is a fourteenfold spread for something described identically in the advertising. Knowing which category a quote belongs to is most of the work.

The in-home option carries a travel cost that is real whether or not it appears on the invoice. Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500, with the upper end reflecting distance as much as expertise. A tutor crossing from Al Barsha to Arabian Ranches at five in the afternoon is spending close to two hours on a sixty-minute lesson, and that time is priced in somewhere.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; lessons run one-to-one over live video and home visits are a service offered only in India. sections.heading: The evidence file: artefacts, dates and who keeps them
paragraphs: An evidence file is not a report card. It is the raw material: the student's own writing, marked, with dates on it. Four artefact types do almost all the work. The first is a timed answer, written to the clock on a past question, marked against the published assessment wording with the marks shown rather than summarised. The second is a plan, written before an answer and reworked after feedback, which shows whether the student can now structure an argument without being walked through it.

The third is a command-word log. Sociology marks are released by the verb at the front of the question, and a student who can describe but cannot evaluate will plateau at a predictable grade regardless of how much content they learn. Logging each command word by name, with the date it was last handled correctly, turns a vague worry into a short list of things to practise. The fourth is a one-paragraph session note: what was taught, what the student produced, what changed, what comes next.

The file lives in a shared folder the family can open, not in the tutor's notebook. That matters for a practical reason. Tutors change, schools change, and a student who moves from Dubai to another emirate or another country mid-course should not lose two terms of diagnostic work. It also removes the awkward conversation about value, because a parent can see for themselves whether the October script and the February script are different pieces of writing.

sections.heading: Command words in Cambridge social-science papers and the marks they release
paragraphs: The verb at the start of a sociology question is an instruction about how many marks are available and what kind of writing earns them. Students who treat every question as an invitation to write what they know will score heavily on short definition questions and poorly on everything else, which produces the characteristic middling grade that frustrates families who can see their child understands the material.

The repair is mechanical and fast. For each command word, the student learns the shape of the answer rather than the content: how many points, whether a counter-argument is required, whether a judgement must be stated, whether an example is expected. Two or three sessions on shape typically move a script further than two or three sessions on content, which is why a tutor should diagnose before teaching. The definitive list of command words for the current syllabus sits in the 0495 syllabus document on cambridgeinternational.org, and a tutor should be working from the version that matches the student's exam year rather than an older one.

The table below sets out the pattern a Dubai tutor sees most often across Cambridge social-science papers, the error attached to each command word, and what a session actually does about it. Note that the fixes are different in kind: some are vocabulary, some are structural, and one is simply a timing problem disguised as a knowledge problem. A parent can use the same table without a tutor present. Ask your child to read a recent answer aloud and say which command word the question used, then say what that word required. A student who cannot name the instruction has found the problem, and it is a cheaper problem to hold than a missing topic.

sections.heading: Where 0495 marks are actually lost
paragraphs: Marks in sociology leak from a small number of recurring places, and almost none of them are gaps in knowledge. The largest is the description and explanation confusion described above. The second is the unsupported assertion: a student writes that the media causes violence, or that the family is in decline, with no named position and no counter-position, and the examiner has nothing to credit. Sociology awards marks for handling a debate, not for arriving at the right answer, and a student who does not realise that will write confidently into empty space.

The third is misuse of personal experience. Dubai candidates have genuinely interesting material to draw on, with households spanning several cultures and schools running under more than a dozen curricula in one city. Used as illustration after a sociological point, that material is a strength. Used instead of a sociological point, it is anecdote and scores nothing. The discipline is to name the concept first, attribute the argument, and only then reach for the example.

The fourth is research methods, where precision is everything. Reliability and validity are not synonyms, a representative sample is not simply a large one, and an ethical objection is not the same as a practical one. A student who blurs these loses marks in a strand that recurs throughout the paper. The fifth is timing: a long first answer that leaves ten minutes for a question worth three times as much. That one shows up clearly in a marked timed script and nowhere else, which is the argument for producing them regularly.

sections.heading: Twelve weeks, read week by week
paragraphs: The question behind every tutoring decision is whether the money is doing anything. Sociology makes that hard to see, because the first six weeks of competent teaching often produce no visible grade change at all. What changes first is the shape of an answer, then the handling of command words, then the mark. A family that expects the mark to move in week three will conclude the tutoring has failed just as it starts working.

A twelve-week reading of an evidence file solves that by naming what should be visible at each stage. Week one produces a baseline: an unaided timed answer on a topic the student has already been taught at school, marked honestly. Weeks two to four produce plans rather than full answers, because structure is cheaper to fix than content. Weeks five to eight produce full answers with the scaffold progressively removed. Weeks nine to twelve produce whole papers under timed conditions, and this is the first point at which a mark comparison means anything.

The table sets this out with what each stage can and cannot tell you, which matters as much as the artefact itself. A plan improving in week three is real evidence of progress. It is not evidence that the grade has moved, and a tutor who presents it that way is overselling. The honest version is that early artefacts predict and late artefacts measure. The twelve-week shape also fits the Dubai school calendar reasonably well. A block started in late September reaches whole-paper work before the winter break, and a block started after the break reaches it before the spring mock window, which is when most schools collect the evidence they later use for forecast grades.

sections.heading: Counting backwards from a Cambridge series
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Most Dubai schools enter the June series, and some use November for retakes or for cohorts on a different calendar. The decisive dates are not the exam dates. They are the entry deadlines, which sit months earlier and are set by the school rather than the family.

The published March 2027 series is the clearest worked example of that gap. Its examination period runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries are due on 27 November 2026, forecast grades are due on 27 February 2027, results reach centres on Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June. The entry deadline therefore falls more than two months before the first paper, and a student who decides in January to sit a subject has already missed it. The same structural lag applies to June and November.

One further detail is worth a parent's attention. Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after working from the wrong zone timetable. A Dubai family should take the paper dates from the school's own exams officer, not from a timetable found online, and should check the current session dates on cambridgeinternational.org rather than relying on any date restated here.

sections.heading: Academic honesty in sociology: methods, data and whose words these are
paragraphs: Sociology invites a particular kind of boundary problem, because so much of the subject looks like discussion. A tutor can legitimately teach a student how an evaluation question is structured, question a weak argument until the student improves it, model an answer on a different question, and mark the student's own writing in detail. A tutor cannot supply sentences for the student to submit, improve a piece of assessed work to the point where the words are no longer the student's, or hand over a bank of prepared answers to be reproduced under examination conditions.

The line is easiest to hold when the artefacts are dated. If every answer in the file was written by the student at a known time and marked afterwards, there is nothing ambiguous about authorship. Problems arise with undated, co-written documents where nobody can later say which parts came from where. This is a practical argument for the evidence file as much as an ethical one, and it is the reason the marking happens after the writing rather than alongside it.

Some providers in this market sell completed assessed work outright. One researched competitor advertises finished Internal Assessments at a fixed price. For a student that is a malpractice exposure that can end a qualification, and no reputable tutor should go near it. IB Gram does not supply assessed work, does not sell model answers for submission, and does not reproduce syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes; those are published by Cambridge and should be obtained from cambridgeinternational.org or from the school.

sections.heading: KHDA, the Dubai school market and the subjects sitting alongside 0495
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. The scale is unusual: 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with the UK curriculum the largest group at 37% of enrolment and the International Baccalaureate at 7%. A 0495 candidate is therefore inside a crowded British-curriculum system where option blocks are set by timetable rather than by demand.

Fees are part of the planning picture. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. For a family budgeting tuition alongside school fees, that is a known quantity for one year, which is more than can be said for most inputs.

Alongside the licensed international curriculum, Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools, with KHDA requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and any different or additional content needs prior Ministry of Education permission. A 0495 student is carrying these subjects as well, and a realistic weekly plan has to account for them.
