sections.heading: Getting started, and what happens when no 0495 specialist is free
paragraphs: The honest version of getting started has four steps and one disclosure. The four steps are: tell us the board and the code from the school entry form, the series the school is entering, and the last mark the student actually received; take a free trial lesson, one per subject, with no payment details taken beforehand, which ends with a marked piece of the student's writing; agree a twelve-week plan naming the artefacts it will produce; and then read the weekly note. If the note is empty, the tutoring is not working and the conversation should happen in week three rather than week ten.

The disclosure is about availability. Sociology 0495 is a small entry compared with Mathematics or the sciences, and the number of tutors in the UAE who have taught it to examination is correspondingly small. On a week when no UAE-based 0495 specialist has a slot, we will say so rather than substitute a general humanities tutor and hope. The alternatives we would put to you are a specialist in another time zone whose availability fits a Dubai evening, a start date two or three weeks out, or a shorter diagnostic engagement now with the full plan beginning when a specialist frees up.

What we will not do is place a tutor who has never taught the syllabus, because in a subject where marks turn on command-word handling and methodological precision, a strong generalist produces confident answers that score in the middle. The evidence file makes that visible within four weeks, which is uncomfortable for everyone involved. Saying no at the start is cheaper for the family than discovering it in February.

process.title: Send the three facts that matter
process.description: The board and syllabus code from the school entry form, the series the school is entering, and the most recent real mark with the paper it came from. Those three facts settle more than a long conversation about learning styles, and they stop a tutor revising from the wrong board's past papers.

process.title: Take a trial that produces something
process.description: One free trial lesson per subject, with no payment details taken beforehand. It ends with a short piece of the student's own writing, marked, with the marks visible. That marked page is the baseline for everything afterwards and tells you more about the tutor than any introduction.

process.title: Agree a plan with artefacts named in it
process.description: A twelve-week plan that says which weeks produce plans, which produce full answers, and which produce whole timed papers. A plan that promises improvement without naming what will be written down is not a plan, and it cannot be checked by anyone in week six.

process.title: Read the weekly note, not the mood
process.description: One paragraph after each session: what was taught, what the student produced, what changed, what comes next. Two minutes of reading a week. If three consecutive notes say the same thing, raise it with the tutor rather than waiting for a report.

whyPoints.title: Rates are quoted with their source and month
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is attributed to the provider that published it and the month it was read. Those are market rates, not an IB Gram price list. For our own pricing, the consultation and the trial lesson are the honest route, because the number depends on level, format and session length.

whyPoints.title: A specialist beats a short drive
whyPoints.description: Restricting a 0495 search to tutors who can reach a Dubai address in rush hour selects for postcode rather than subject knowledge. Live video widens the pool to people who have taught the syllabus to examination, which for a small-entry subject is the difference between a specialist and a generalist.

whyPoints.title: The record belongs to the family
whyPoints.description: Marked scripts, plans, the command-word log and the session notes live in a folder you can open. Tutors change and families relocate between emirates; two terms of diagnostic work should not sit in somebody else's notebook.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line is stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions and marks. A tutor does not supply sentences for submission or sell prepared answers to reproduce in an examination. We say that in writing because at least one provider in this market sells finished assessed work, and a student who buys it risks the qualification.

whyPoints.title: Availability is disclosed before you pay
whyPoints.description: If no UAE-based 0495 specialist has a slot this week, we say so and set out the alternatives. No competitor page researched for this project discloses a coverage limit, and several route UAE parents to numbers outside the country without saying where the tutor sits.

faqs.question: How much does a Cambridge IGCSE Sociology 0495 home tutor cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market rates read in October 2026 put online one-to-one subject tutoring at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. In-home one-to-one sits higher because travel is priced in: Bestimate's Dubai table shows AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors AED 200 to 500. Budget freelance work starts far lower, from AED 45 to 65 with EdFlik. Premium named tutors reach AED 650, as BartyED publishes. Those are other providers' figures, not an IB Gram price list. Our own rate depends on level, session length and format, and the trial lesson is the sensible way to establish it.

faqs.question: Will a 0495 tutor actually visit our villa in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Sociology 0495 sessions run one-to-one over live video, with the tutor and student screen-sharing the same marked script. For this subject that is the stronger option rather than a compromise. The entry for 0495 across the UAE is small, so the pool of tutors who have taught it to examination is small, and filtering that pool further by who can reach your address during Dubai rush hour usually means accepting a generalist instead of a sociology specialist.

faqs.question: What evidence will I see after the first four 0495 sessions?
faqs.answer: Four things, all dated. An unaided timed answer from week one, marked with the marks shown rather than summarised, which is the real baseline. Two or three answer plans produced before writing and reworked after feedback, kept in both versions so the change is visible. A command-word log naming which verbs the student now handles correctly and when each was last checked. And four short session notes, one paragraph each. You should be able to read the lot in under ten minutes. What you will not see at four weeks is a moved grade, because structure improves before marks do.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether my child's 0495 grade is moving or just their confidence?
faqs.answer: Compare two timed answers on the same topic, written under the same conditions, several weeks apart, both marked against published assessment wording. Confidence rises early and means little on its own. A grade has moved when the later script shows structural change: the command word handled by name, a counter-argument present before the conclusion, a named example rather than a general observation, and the time distributed across questions in proportion to their marks. That is why the week-one baseline matters. Without it, every later script looks reasonable and there is nothing to measure against except memory.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge 0495 topics cause Dubai students the most trouble?
faqs.answer: Research methods first, because the vocabulary is technical and marks go to precision rather than fluency. Students routinely treat reliability and validity as synonyms and assume a representative sample simply means a large one. Social inequality is second: questions there want an explanation of why a difference persists, and candidates supply a description of the difference instead. Media is third, where students argue effects as settled rather than contested. Family and education feel easiest and are therefore where personal anecdote most often replaces sociological argument, which scores nothing however well written.

faqs.question: Does Cambridge IGCSE Sociology 0495 include a coursework component?
faqs.answer: Check the current syllabus document for your child's examination year on cambridgeinternational.org, and confirm the entry option with the school's exams officer, because Cambridge revises syllabuses on a cycle and components can change between versions. What does not change is the planning consequence. If the assessment is entirely by written examination, the whole grade rests on a short window and timed-answer practice through the year is the highest-value activity available. If a non-examined component applies to your cohort, its internal deadlines will sit well before the exam period and need to be in the plan from the start.

faqs.question: My child's school enters 0495 in the November series. Does that change the plan?
faqs.answer: It changes the calendar rather than the method. Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and entry deadlines sit months before the papers in both. For a November entry the work that matters happens across the Dubai autumn term, which collides with the busiest part of the school year, so the twelve-week block has to start earlier than families expect. Take the exact dates from the school's exams officer. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone.

faqs.question: Can a 0495 tutor work specifically on the research-methods questions?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for many students that is the highest-return request they could make. Research methods is the strand where marks are decided by exact use of terms: questionnaires against structured interviews, reliability against validity, representativeness against sample size, ethical objections against practical ones. It behaves like a science paper inside an essay subject. A focused block usually runs as definition drills, then short application questions, then evaluation of a named method in context, with each stage producing a marked script so the improvement can be read rather than assumed.

faqs.question: Is my child's 0495 tutor legally permitted to teach privately in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The official route is the MoHRE service page for private tutor licensing, which lists a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

faqs.question: Does 0495 count towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: On the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. A sociology pass can form part of that count where it is among the accredited subjects submitted. Alongside the five, the requirement includes one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or above, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Confirm current requirements with the Ministry or the emirate attestation authority directly; IB Gram describes the process and does not perform or guarantee it.

faqs.question: How many 0495 sessions a week do Dubai families usually begin with?
faqs.answer: One weekly sixty or ninety minute session is the usual start, with written work produced between sessions. Sociology improves through writing rather than through contact hours, so a second weekly session without homework between them tends to add cost rather than marks. Families move to two sessions in the eight to twelve weeks before a series, with one spent writing under timed conditions and one spent on the marking. During a holiday block, three to five consecutive sessions in a week on a single weak topic area work better than the same hours spread thinly across a term.

faqs.question: Can 0495 sessions move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most families ask for it. School days shorten during Ramadan and evening energy shifts late, so a 4.30pm slot that worked in January is often unusable. The practical pattern is to move sessions to after Iftar, shorten them slightly, and reduce the written work set between them while keeping the frequency intact. Losing the rhythm entirely for a month costs more than a shorter session does. Because delivery is over live video, the change is a calendar adjustment rather than a renegotiation of travel time, which is one of the quieter advantages of online scheduling.

faqs.question: What happens to the 0495 evidence file if we change tutor?
faqs.answer: It stays with you, which is the point of keeping it in a shared folder rather than a tutor's notebook. A replacement tutor starts by reading the marked scripts, the command-word log and the session notes, which means the first session diagnoses rather than repeats. Without that file a new tutor spends two or three sessions rediscovering what was already known, and a family pays twice for the same information. The same applies if your child changes school, moves to another emirate, or leaves the UAE part-way through Year 11.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start 0495 support ten weeks before the exam?
faqs.answer: Ten weeks is enough to change how a paper is answered, which is usually where the available marks are. It is not enough to rebuild a topic that was never learned. The sensible shape is a hard baseline in week one, then command-word and timing work through the middle weeks, then whole papers under timed conditions in the final fortnight. Nobody can promise a grade from that, and a provider who does should be treated with real scepticism. What can be said is that structural errors are faster to fix than content gaps, and a marked baseline tells you within a week which problem you have.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-sociology-0495-hom.closingBody: The quickest way to find out whether Cambridge IGCSE Sociology 0495 support will help your child is to produce a single marked page. Send the board and code from the school entry form, the series the school is entering, and the last real mark. The trial lesson, one free per subject with no payment details taken beforehand, ends with a short piece of your child's own writing marked against published assessment wording. If that page tells you something you did not already know, the tutoring has a basis. If it does not, you have lost an hour and learned where the gap is not.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-sociology-0495-onl.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed here teach Cambridge IGCSE Sociology over live video to students in Dubai. Each works from the current 0495 syllabus and the student's own school scheme of work, and each spends session time on written answers rather than on recapping notes the student already owns.

intro.heading: The paper rewards a kind of writing nobody is taught directly
paragraphs: Sociology is the subject where bright students most often underperform, and the reason is structural rather than intellectual. A Cambridge IGCSE Sociology paper does not ask a candidate what they believe about families, schools, crime or the media. It asks them to set out a position, attribute it, produce the strongest argument against it, and then reach a judgement that commits to one side with a reason. That is a skill, it is learnable in weeks, and it is rarely taught explicitly in a crowded Year 10 timetable.

The second structural problem is vocabulary. Roughly a third of the questions a 0495 candidate meets turn on the precise meaning of a technical term: reliability, validity, representativeness, primary and secondary data, covert and overt observation, sampling frame, verstehen. These are not loose descriptive words. Each has a fixed definition, each has a standard strength and a standard limitation attached to it, and a student who uses two of them interchangeably will lose marks in a strand that recurs across the whole paper rather than in one question.

The third is the named example. Candidates in Dubai write about society with real intelligence and almost no evidence, because nobody told them that an answer needs specific content they can name. Six well-chosen examples, held properly and mapped to topics, will serve a student across every question on the paper. Students who have none fall back on their own household, which reads as anecdote and earns nothing however fluently it is written. Building the bank takes about two sessions, and it is the single clearest instance of a sociology problem that looks like talent and is actually admin.

An online 0495 tutor is useful because all three problems are visible in writing and fixable in writing. The format matters here. A tutor who screen-shares the student's own script, marks it live with both parties looking at the same paragraph, and then asks the student to rewrite the weak move on the spot is doing something that cannot be done by sitting beside somebody with a pen. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. Lessons here are one-to-one over live video, and for a writing subject that is the format with the advantage.

What follows is organised as the subject is organised. The syllabus strands and what each one demands. The research-methods strand in full, method by method. The four perspectives, set against each other rather than listed. The anatomy of a long evaluation answer. What a sixty-minute session actually repairs. Then the practical layer: delivery mechanics in Dubai, what the market charges and who published the figure, where 0495 leads afterwards, and the questions worth asking a tutor before any money changes hands.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-sociology-0495-onl.programmesIntro: Sociology appears at three points in a Dubai student's school career, and the work needed at each is different in kind rather than in quantity. Knowing where your child sits prevents a tutor teaching to the wrong level.

programmes.name: Year 9 option choice
programmes.description: Most Dubai British-curriculum schools set IGCSE option blocks in Year 9, and sociology is usually a humanities block choice competing with Geography, History and Business Studies. The decision is made with almost no information, because the subject is rarely taught before it is chosen. A single session reading two past questions aloud tells a 13-year-old more about whether they will enjoy the course than any options evening.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai licenses 17 different curricula across its private schools, so option blocks vary considerably between schools in the same neighbourhood. A family moving school mid-year can find that sociology is simply not timetabled at the new one. Checking the option blocks before accepting a place saves a difficult conversation in Year 10.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Sociology
programmes.description: The two-year course and the focus of this page. Content is organised into substantive topic areas, each underpinned by theory and by research methods. The examined skills divide between recall of terms and studies, application of a concept to a situation, and analysis with evaluation. That last band carries the marks that separate a middling grade from a strong one, and it is the band least likely to be taught as a separate skill.
programmes.countryNote: Confirm the board and code on the school entry form before buying any revision material. Dubai schools use Cambridge and Pearson in roughly equal measure across different subjects, sometimes within the same student's timetable, and a candidate practising from the wrong board's past papers is rehearsing questions that will never be asked.

programmes.name: Cambridge International A Level Sociology
programmes.description: The natural continuation. A Level work asks for sustained argument across longer essays, theory handled by name and in detail, and a real position on whether sociology can be a science. The IGCSE habits transfer wholesale: define, attribute, counter, judge. Students who built those habits properly at 16 find the step up to be about stamina and reading rather than about a new skill.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE equivalency on the British track a student needs one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or above, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside five accredited GCSE or IGCSE passes at no less than grade E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education sit outside that count of five. Check current wording with the Ministry before relying on it.

programmes.name: IB Diploma social sciences
programmes.description: Dubai's International Baccalaureate sector is sizeable and some 0495 students move into the Diploma instead. There is no direct IB counterpart to IGCSE Sociology; the closest are Global Politics, Psychology, and Social and Cultural Anthropology where a school offers them. All three expect a defended method rather than an asserted one, which is exactly what the 0495 methods strand trains.
programmes.countryNote: The International Baccalaureate accounts for 7% of Dubai private-school enrolment, and the emirate's 2026-27 intake adds three new IB schools among seven new openings. Supply is rising, but a specific Diploma subject combination still depends on what one school timetables, so ask the sixth form directly rather than assuming.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-sociology-0495-onl.subjectsIntro: Sociology rarely travels alone. These are the Cambridge IGCSE subjects most often sitting in the same timetable as 0495 in Dubai, with the overlap that makes one tutor viable across two of them.

subjects.name: Sociology (0495)
subjects.description: Theory and methods, culture and socialisation, social inequality, family, education, crime and deviance, and media. Assessment turns on applying a named concept to a situation and then evaluating the explanation rather than describing the situation.

subjects.name: Psychology (0266)
subjects.description: Shares the research-methods vocabulary almost exactly, including sampling, reliability, validity and ethics, but applies it to studies of individual behaviour rather than social structures. A student taking both can learn the methods strand once and use it twice.

subjects.name: Global Perspectives (0457)
subjects.description: Skills-led rather than content-led, with research, argument and perspective-taking assessed directly. The evaluation discipline transfers straight into sociology answers, and students who do well in one are usually capable of doing well in the other.

subjects.name: Geography (0460)
subjects.description: Human geography overlaps heavily with sociology on urbanisation, migration and inequality. The difference is that geography wants data and location specificity, where sociology wants an attributed explanation. Students sometimes write a geography answer in a sociology exam.

subjects.name: History (0470)
subjects.description: Source evaluation in history is the same reasoning sociology applies to secondary data: who produced this, for what purpose, and what does that do to its reliability. Historians entering sociology usually arrive strong on evidence handling and weak on theory by name.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Shares the evaluation structure and the demand for a justified judgement rather than a balanced shrug. Economics candidates tend to write tighter conclusions than pure humanities students, which is an advantage they can carry directly into a 0495 evaluation question.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: The common option-block alternative to sociology in Dubai schools. Case-study technique in business, reading a scenario and applying a concept to it, is the same move a sociology application question asks for under a different name.

subjects.name: First Language English (0500)
subjects.description: The writing engine behind every essay subject. A student with strong 0500 control of paragraphing and discourse markers will structure a sociology evaluation more cleanly, though fluency alone never substitutes for a named position.

subjects.name: Travel and Tourism (0471)
subjects.description: Another applied social-science option that Dubai schools run, drawing on the emirate's own visitor economy. Its case-study discipline and its demand for specific data rather than general comment mirror what a sociology examiner wants from a named example.

sections.heading: The six strands of 0495 and the failure mode attached to each
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE Sociology is organised into substantive topic areas sitting on top of a theory and methods foundation. The topic areas cover culture, identity and socialisation; social inequality and stratification; the family; education; crime, deviance and social control; and the media. A student can know all six well and still write a weak paper, because each strand has a characteristic way of going wrong and the repairs are not interchangeable.

On socialisation the failure is anecdote. On inequality it is description where explanation was asked for. On the family it is treating one's own household as evidence. On education the trap is writing school policy rather than sociology. On crime and deviance it is forgetting that the measurement of crime is itself a topic. On media it is asserting effects as settled fact rather than as a contested debate with identifiable sides.

The table below pairs each strand with its failure mode and with the revision artefact that fixes it. The artefact column matters because sociology revision has a tendency to become rereading. Rereading notes produces familiarity and no marks. Producing a named-example card, a definition tested cold, or a judgement paragraph written to the clock produces something a tutor can mark and a student can measure. Check the exact topic list for your child's examination year on cambridgeinternational.org, since Cambridge revises syllabuses on a cycle and older versions circulate widely online. A parent can also use the strand column as a conversation prompt. Ask which of the six your child would least like to be asked about, and then ask why. The answer is usually the failure mode rather than the content, and it points straight at the first two sessions.

sections.heading: Research methods, method by method
paragraphs: The methods strand is where a 0495 grade is usually won or lost, and it is also the part a general humanities tutor is least likely to teach precisely. Marks here go to exactness. A questionnaire is reliable because it can be repeated identically, not because it is accurate. An unstructured interview has high validity because the respondent sets the terms, not because the researcher is sympathetic. A representative sample reflects the population's characteristics; size helps but does not by itself deliver it.

Each method carries a standard strength and a standard limitation that a student should be able to produce without thinking, plus an ethical dimension that must be kept separate from the practical one. Covert observation raises an ethical problem about consent and a practical problem about record-keeping, and a candidate who merges those into one point scores once where they could have scored twice. This is why the methods block is run as drills rather than as discussion.

The table sets out the methods a 0495 candidate needs to hold, what each one actually collects, its mark-scheme strength, its standard limitation, and the kind of question it tends to appear inside. A student who can reproduce this grid from memory has covered a recurring share of the paper before they have revised a single topic area. Two further distinctions belong in the same block. Primary data is collected by the researcher for the purpose at hand; secondary data was gathered by somebody else for their own reasons, which is why its categories can be unhelpful. And a pilot study is not a small version of the research; it is a test of the instrument, run to find out whether the questions work before the real sample is spent on them.

sections.heading: Four perspectives, set against each other
paragraphs: Perspectives are taught as a list and examined as a comparison, which is why students can recite four labels and still fail to use them. The useful question is never what functionalism is. It is what a functionalist would say about this family, this school, this newspaper, and what a Marxist or a feminist would say instead. Held that way, a perspective becomes a tool that generates an argument on any topic in the syllabus.

The practical test a tutor applies is simple. Give the student one scenario, a school setting a top set, and ask for four sentences, one per perspective, each making a different claim about the same facts. A student who produces four genuinely different sentences has the perspectives. A student who produces four restatements of the same observation has four labels and no positions, and that is a two-session fix rather than a term of content teaching.

The table compares the four on the same two topics, family and education, so the differences are visible rather than asserted. The final column names the misuse that costs marks most often. Students should also keep the structure and action debate in view: the first two perspectives in the table explain behaviour from the top down, the fourth builds it from interaction upwards, and a question asking which approach is more useful is asking about exactly that split. The same logic explains why perspectives and methods are taught together rather than in separate blocks. A writer who sees society as a structure tends to reach for large-scale quantitative data, and a writer who builds it from interaction reaches for observation and unstructured interviews. A student who can say why a perspective prefers a method has a ready-made evaluation point for almost any methods question on the paper.

sections.heading: The long evaluation answer, dissected
paragraphs: The highest-tariff question on a sociology paper is some version of to what extent, and it is answered by a repeatable four-move sequence. Move one establishes the claim in sociological language and attributes it to a position. Move two supports it with a named example or study. Move three produces the strongest available counter-position, not a weak one set up to be knocked down. Move four reaches a judgement that commits, with a stated reason for the weighting.

Almost every lost mark on these questions is a missing move. Students skip move one and start with the example. They skip move three and write a one-sided argument confidently. Most commonly they skip move four and conclude that both sides have merit, which answers a different question. An examiner reading a balanced non-conclusion has nothing to credit in the band that pays best, and the student walks away believing a thorough answer was undervalued.

A tutor teaches the sequence as scaffolding and then removes it. Week one, the student writes with the four moves labelled in the margin. Week three, the labels go but the order holds. Week six, the order flexes because the student can feel where a counter-argument is owed. That progression is visible in the scripts, which is why the sequence is taught through writing rather than explained in conversation. Students who only hear the sequence described can usually recite it and still not use it under time pressure.

sections.heading: What a sixty-minute online session actually fixes
paragraphs: Parents reasonably want to know what one hour buys. The answer depends on which of five common problems the student has, and the five have different costs. A command-word problem is the cheapest to fix and often moves a grade within three sessions. A missing bank of named examples takes longer but is entirely mechanical. A genuine content gap, a topic area never properly taught, is the most expensive and the one no amount of technique work will cover.

Diagnosis therefore comes before teaching. A tutor who starts delivering content in session one, without having seen the student write anything, is guessing. The first session should produce a short written answer and a judgement about which of the five problems is dominant. That judgement can be wrong and can be revised, but it has to be made, because the five repairs use session time in completely different ways.

The table maps the problem a parent usually reports onto the cause that shows up in the script, what the session does about it, and the artefact that comes out. The artefact column is there so a family can check that something happened. An hour that produces no writing, no glossary line and no marked page has produced a conversation, and conversations are pleasant but hard to measure against a paper. The sixth possibility is worth naming even though it is not in the table. Some students are not short of technique or content but of sleep, and a Year 11 timetable in Dubai carrying mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education alongside nine option subjects is genuinely full. A tutor who recognises that and reduces the written work set between sessions, rather than adding to it, is reading the situation correctly.

sections.heading: Delivery mechanics for a Dubai 0495 student
paragraphs: Online tuition fails for boring reasons far more often than for pedagogical ones. The three that matter are the microphone, the second screen and the file. A laptop's built-in microphone in an open-plan Dubai apartment picks up the whole room, and a tutor who cannot hear a hesitant answer cannot diagnose it. Headphones with a boom microphone cost very little and remove the problem entirely. Where a second screen or a tablet is available, the student can write on one surface while the tutor annotates on the other.

The file matters because sociology is a writing subject. Work should live in a shared folder both sides can open, with dates in the filenames, rather than arriving as photographs of a notebook in a messaging app. Photographs cannot be annotated, cannot be searched, and cannot be compared against a script from two months earlier. A typed or scanned script can be marked on screen while the student watches, which is where live video earns its advantage over a tutor sitting alongside.

Scheduling is the last piece. Sessions are agreed in Gulf Standard Time, which matters because many specialist tutors sit in other time zones and a Dubai evening is a convenient slot for several of them. During Ramadan most families move to post-Iftar timing and shorten sessions slightly rather than pausing, because frequency is what holds the writing habit together. A tutor should also know the school's mock window, since two weeks of school examinations will swallow any homework set across them.

sections.heading: What the Dubai market charges, by session shape
paragraphs: Rates in this market are quoted per hour, which obscures the real variable. A sixty-minute teaching session and a ninety-minute marking review cost roughly the same per hour and do completely different jobs. A monthly package converts an hourly rate into a predictable budget line and usually assumes a fixed number of sessions, which suits families planning around school fees. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion, so for one year the larger number in a family's education budget is at least stable.

The figures in the table are other providers' published rates, read in October 2026, with the provider named. They are the market, not an IB Gram price list, and nothing on this page should be read as our quotation. For our own rate the sensible route is the trial lesson and a short consultation, because the number genuinely depends on level, session length and format rather than on a headline band.

One pricing habit in this market deserves a flag. Several researched competitor pages publish no figure at all, and one asks the price question in its own list of frequently asked questions and then declines to answer it. Two more quote in US dollars on pages aimed at UAE families. A provider unwilling to put a currency and a number on a page is asking a parent to make a decision without the one input that makes comparison possible.

sections.heading: Where 0495 leads, and what UAE equivalency asks for
paragraphs: Sociology at 16 is not a narrowing choice. It feeds A Level Sociology, Psychology, Law, Politics, Criminology and a range of social-science degrees, and the writing discipline it trains, attribute a claim, counter it, judge it, is the core skill of every essay subject a student will later meet. For students in Dubai there is a second argument: the subject gives them a vocabulary for a city where several curricula, several nationalities and several household structures sit within one street.

The administrative layer is worth understanding early. Attestation and equivalency sit with the UAE Ministry of Education and the emirate authorities, not with a school and certainly not with a tutor. On the British track, the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at grade E or above or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. One ranking competitor page states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced figure is five.

For the International Baccalaureate route, no points threshold is published here, because none was read on the Ministry's own pages during research for this project. A family relying on a number for an IB equivalency decision should read it on moe.gov.ae or confirm it with the emirate attestation authority rather than taking it from any tutoring website, including this one. IB Gram describes the process and does not perform, expedite or guarantee any part of it, and tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, university admission or school progression.

sections.heading: Six questions to put to an online 0495 tutor before you pay
paragraphs: The market makes it hard to tell a sociology specialist from a capable generalist, because both interview well. Six questions separate them quickly. Which board and code has the tutor taught to examination, and in which series. What is the difference between reliability and validity, asked cold. How would a functionalist and an interactionist differ on the same school scenario. What does the tutor do in a session when a student has written a balanced non-conclusion. Where will the marked scripts live. And what happens if the tutor is unavailable for three weeks before the series.

The second question is the one that discriminates. A tutor who answers it crisply, with the standard strength and limitation attached, has taught the methods strand. A tutor who talks around it in general terms has not, and methods marks recur across the whole paper. The fourth question matters nearly as much, because the response reveals whether the tutor teaches writing moves or simply tells a student to add a conclusion.

One disclosure belongs on our side of that exchange. Sociology 0495 is a small entry across the UAE, so the number of tutors here who have taught it to examination is limited. On a week when no UAE-based 0495 specialist has a slot, we will say so and set out the alternatives: a specialist in another time zone whose availability suits a Dubai evening, a later start date, or a short diagnostic engagement now with the full plan beginning when a specialist frees up. Placing a willing generalist on a syllabus they have never examined produces confident answers that land in the middle of the mark range, and a marked script makes that visible inside a month.

process.title: Confirm the board, code and series
process.description: Read them off the school entry form rather than assuming. Dubai schools use Cambridge and Pearson across different subjects, sometimes for the same student, and revision from the wrong board's papers rehearses questions that will never be set. The series also fixes when the twelve-week block has to begin.

process.title: Produce one written answer before any teaching
process.description: The trial lesson, one free per subject with no payment details taken beforehand, ends with a short answer written by the student and marked on screen. That page decides which of the five common problems is dominant, and therefore what the next six sessions are actually for.

process.title: Run the methods block early, not late
process.description: Research-methods marks recur across the whole paper, so the terminology drill pays back for the rest of the course. Students resist it because it feels like vocabulary homework rather than sociology. Doing it in October rather than in April is the difference between a tool and a cram.

process.title: Build the example bank before the mocks
process.description: Six named examples, one per strand, written on cards and tested cold. Students without them default to their own household and score nothing for it. The bank takes two sessions to build and serves every question on the paper for the rest of the course.

process.title: Move to whole papers in the final fortnight
process.description: Two complete papers under timed conditions, marked, with the scripts kept beside the baseline from week one. This is the first point where a mark comparison means anything, and it is also where a timing problem becomes undeniable rather than suspected.

whyPoints.title: The methods strand is taught as drills
whyPoints.description: Reliability, validity, representativeness and the ethics of covert work are drilled to exam precision rather than discussed. That strand recurs across the paper, so the return on an unglamorous block of definition work is higher than on any single topic area.

whyPoints.title: Marking happens on screen while the student watches
whyPoints.description: Screen-shared annotation on the student's own script lets them see a sentence credited or ignored as it is read. Written feedback collected two days later is weaker, which is one of the few places where live video genuinely beats sitting beside somebody.

whyPoints.title: Perspectives are compared, never listed
whyPoints.description: Four labels recited in order are worth nothing in an examination. Four different sentences about the same school scenario are worth a great deal. Sessions test the second, which is a fast fix for a problem most students do not know they have.

whyPoints.title: Every figure carries its source and month
whyPoints.description: AED ranges on this page are other providers' published rates read in October 2026, attributed by name. Three of six researched competitor pages publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars to UAE families, which makes comparison impossible.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits are stated before you pay
whyPoints.description: Sociology 0495 is a small entry in the UAE. If no specialist who has taught it to examination is free, we say so and offer alternatives rather than placing a generalist and leaving the marked scripts to reveal it in February.

faqs.question: What does the Cambridge IGCSE Sociology 0495 syllabus actually cover?
faqs.answer: A theory and methods foundation, plus substantive topic areas covering culture, identity and socialisation; social inequality and stratification; the family; education; crime, deviance and social control; and the media. Theory means the perspectives, functionalism, Marxism, feminism and interactionism among them, and the structure against action debate. Methods means questionnaires, interviews, observation, experiments, official statistics and documents, each with sampling, reliability, validity and ethics attached. Read the topic list for your child's examination year on cambridgeinternational.org, because Cambridge revises syllabuses on a cycle and older versions circulate widely online.

faqs.question: Is online 0495 tutoring as effective as sitting beside a tutor?
faqs.answer: For a writing subject it has a specific advantage. Screen sharing puts the tutor and the student on the same paragraph of the same script, both able to annotate, which a shared paper page on a kitchen table does not do as well. The student also watches a sentence being credited or passed over in real time. What online needs is a decent microphone, a quiet hour and files in a shared folder rather than photographs of a notebook. Given those three things, the format is not a compromise for sociology; it is the better fit.

faqs.question: Which sociological perspectives does my child need by name for 0495?
faqs.answer: Functionalism, Marxism, feminism and interactionism are the four a candidate should be able to apply to any topic on the paper, with New Right arguments worth holding separately rather than folded into functionalism. The test is not whether a student can define them. It is whether, given one scenario such as a school setting a top set, they can write four sentences that make four genuinely different claims about the same facts. Students who produce four restatements of one observation have labels rather than positions, and that gap closes in about two sessions.

faqs.question: How do I know if my child is writing real evaluation for 0495?
faqs.answer: Read the last paragraph of a recent answer. Real evaluation commits: it says which argument is better supported and gives the reason for the weighting. A balanced non-conclusion, both sides have merit, answers a different question and leaves the top mark band unreachable. Then check whether the counter-argument earlier in the answer was the strongest available one or a weak position set up to be dismissed. Those two checks take a minute each and tell you more than any progress report. The fix is a four-move sequence practised in writing rather than explained in conversation.

faqs.question: What does an online 0495 session cost per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market rates read in October 2026 put qualified online subject tutoring between roughly AED 150 and 300 an hour, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. Budget freelance work runs lower, EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Premium named tutors reach the top of the market, with BartyED publishing AED 650. Monthly online packages advertised in Dubai sit around AED 799 for eight sessions. Those are other providers' figures with their own framing, not an IB Gram price list; ours depends on level, length and format.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover 0495 sociology and a second social science?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and the overlap is real rather than convenient. Cambridge IGCSE Psychology 0266 uses almost the same research-methods vocabulary, including sampling, reliability, validity and research ethics, applied to individual behaviour instead of social structures. Global Perspectives 0457 shares the evaluation discipline. Economics 0455 and Business Studies 0450 share the apply-a-concept-to-a-scenario move. What a tutor cannot credibly do is cover two subjects they have not taught to examination, so ask about each syllabus code separately rather than accepting a general humanities claim.

faqs.question: How long should a 0495 online session be for a Year 10 student?
faqs.answer: Sixty minutes is the working default, with the student writing inside the session for part of it. Ninety minutes works for a fortnightly marking review where a full answer or paper has been written at home beforehand, because the extra time goes on diagnosis rather than on attention. Below forty-five minutes there is rarely room to write anything and mark it, which reduces the session to conversation. In Year 10 frequency matters more than length: one hour a week with written work between sessions outperforms a longer session with nothing in between.

faqs.question: Does my child need to memorise named studies for 0495?
faqs.answer: They need a small number of specific, usable examples rather than a long list of half-remembered ones. Six is a workable target, one per strand, each specific enough to be checked and short enough to deploy in a sentence. The purpose is to replace general observation with named content: an examiner can credit a specific case applied to a claim and cannot credit a feeling about society. Students build the bank on cards and are tested cold, because an example recognised on a page is not the same as one retrievable under time pressure in an examination hall.

faqs.question: What equipment does a Dubai family need for online 0495 lessons?
faqs.answer: Less than most people expect. A laptop or tablet with a camera, headphones with a boom microphone rather than a built-in one, a quiet hour where a door closes, and a shared folder for files. The microphone is the item that actually matters: in an open-plan apartment a built-in microphone collects the whole room, and a tutor who cannot hear a hesitant half-answer cannot diagnose it. A second screen or tablet helps, letting the student write on one surface while the tutor annotates on the other, but it is useful rather than necessary.

faqs.question: Are 0495 lessons recorded, and what happens to a minor's data?
faqs.answer: Recording should always be a decision the family makes explicitly, not a default, and the answer should be in writing before the first paid session. Ask who holds any recording, for how long, on what storage, and how to have it deleted. The UAE's Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection governs personal data here, and a student's school, grades and written work are personal data about a minor. Our own position is that marked scripts and session notes live in a folder the family controls, and that nothing about a child is collected without a stated purpose.

faqs.question: Can my child sit 0495 as a private candidate in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Private-candidate entry depends on finding an examination centre in the emirate that accepts external candidates for that syllabus, and on meeting its entry deadline, which sits months before the papers. The centre handles the entry; a tutor cannot. Start by asking the child's current school whether it will enter them, because that is the simplest route, and only then approach centres. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone, so take paper dates from the centre rather than from any website.

faqs.question: Does 0495 lead anywhere useful for a UAE university application?
faqs.answer: It counts as one of the accredited subjects in the British-track equivalency requirement, which asks for five GCSE or IGCSE passes at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from those five, alongside one Advanced Level pass at grade E or above or two Advanced Subsidiary passes. Beyond the paperwork, it feeds A Level Sociology, Psychology, Law, Politics and social-science degrees. Attestation and equivalency sit with the Ministry of Education and the emirate authority, so verify current requirements there rather than with any tutoring provider.

faqs.question: How many named examples should a 0495 student actually have ready?
faqs.answer: Six, mapped one to each strand, is enough to answer every question on the paper. More than that and students stop rehearsing any of them properly; fewer and a question in an unlucky topic area leaves them writing generalities. Each example needs three things: a name, a claim it supports, and a sentence that applies it rather than describing it. They are built in about two sessions and then tested cold at intervals, which is also how a tutor can show a family that recall is holding rather than fading between terms.

faqs.question: What should I ask an online 0495 tutor before the first paid session?
faqs.answer: Six things. Which board and code have you taught to examination, and in which series. What is the difference between reliability and validity. How would a functionalist and an interactionist differ on the same school scenario. What do you do when a student writes a balanced non-conclusion. Where will the marked scripts live. And what happens if you are unavailable for three weeks before the series. The second question discriminates fastest: a specialist answers it crisply with the standard strength and limitation attached, and a generalist talks around it.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-sociology-0495-onl.closingBody: If you do one thing after reading this page, ask your child to define reliability, validity and representativeness without looking anything up, and then to say what is wrong with official crime statistics. Those four answers tell you more about a 0495 grade than a term's worth of reassurance. Send us the board, the code and the series, take the free trial lesson, one per subject with no payment details taken beforehand, and you will have a marked page and a glossary line by the end of the hour. From there the plan is arithmetic rather than guesswork.

intro.heading: In 0495 you can see the problem, which means you can see the progress
paragraphs: Sociology is the subject where parents most often cannot tell whether tutoring is working. The student enjoys the sessions. They talk fluently about family structures and labelling theory. They come home saying it makes sense now. And then a mock paper returns at a grade 5, because fluency in conversation is not what the mark scheme pays for. The gap between understanding a concept and scoring on an extended question is wider in 0495 than in almost any other IGCSE, and it is invisible unless somebody is marking the student's actual writing.

That is the whole premise of this page. A Cambridge IGCSE Sociology 0495 tutor in Dubai should be producing evidence, not reassurance. Every session should end with something you could put in front of the subject teacher: a script with annotations, an answer rewritten to show what the criteria wanted, a list of the three errors this particular student keeps making, dated so you can see when each one stopped appearing. If a family cannot see that record, they are buying a feeling.

The faults in 0495 are unusually diagnosable, which is what makes the record possible. Students lose marks for naming a study without using it, for describing two views instead of weighing them, for answering a question about one topic section with material from another, for treating a research-methods question as a general discussion rather than as an evaluation of a specific method in a specific context, and for writing a conclusion that announces a position the body of the answer never built. Each of those shows up on a marked script in under a minute. Each is fixable in a small number of sessions.

There is a Dubai-specific pressure worth naming too. Sociology is an option subject in a timetable that already carries mandatory requirements: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are compulsory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. A student carrying those alongside three sciences and an option block has less reading time than the syllabus assumes, so the efficiency of each hour of revision matters more here than in a lighter timetable. Marked practice is the most efficient hour available.

On delivery: sessions are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, with the student's own script shared on screen and annotated by both people as they work through it. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For a subject whose core activity is reading a piece of a student's writing and marking it against a criterion, the shared screen is the better surface, and it means the tutor is chosen for having taught 0495 rather than for living nearby.

subjects.description: Multiple choice and structured questions on markets, the macroeconomy and development. Progress shows in whether an evaluation names who gains, who loses and over what period. Students holding both subjects write the tightest cost-benefit paragraphs in either.

subjects.description: Case-study application across marketing, finance, operations and people. Progress appears as answers that use the case rather than the textbook. subjects.description: Two written papers including one built on a resource booklet. Progress is visible in data extraction with units and in evaluation that uses the resource. The same thin-supply market as 0495 in Dubai, and the same evaluation habit under assessment.

subjects.name: Development Studies (0453)
subjects.description: Development theory, inequality and change, assessed by written papers. Very close to 0495's social-inequality material, and progress in one is usually legible in the other because both reward a judgement built on evidence rather than on sentiment.

subjects.description: Two written papers with no coursework. Relevant because 0495 research-methods answers involve sample sizes, representativeness and simple statistics, and a student who misreads a percentage or a sample base loses sociology marks for a numerical reason.

sections.heading: What progress in 0495 looks like when you can actually see it
paragraphs: A Cambridge IGCSE Sociology 0495 tutor in Dubai should be able to show you four things after six weeks: a set of marked scripts, a dated list of the faults that were named, evidence that each of those faults has stopped appearing, and one extended answer rewritten from the criteria so you can compare it with the first attempt. If all four exist, the tutoring is working. If none do, the fact that your child finds the sessions enjoyable is not evidence of anything.

This matters more in sociology than in subjects with a right answer. In Maths a parent can see a correct solution. In 0495 the output is prose, and prose that reads well can score poorly for reasons invisible to anyone who is not marking against the criteria. A student can write three fluent paragraphs on the functions of the family, name two studies, reach a tidy conclusion, and land in the middle band because nothing in the answer weighed one position against another. The script shows this immediately; a conversation about the session does not.

The practical version of the evidence loop is simple and cheap to run. The student writes one extended answer to time between sessions. The session is spent marking it with the script on screen, both people annotating, with the criteria quoted rather than paraphrased. The fault is named in one sentence and written down with the date. The next answer is written with that fault as its single target. Over eight weeks the list has three items crossed off and two new ones, and the long-answer score has moved.

What this structure also does is make it obvious when tutoring should stop. When the fault list clears and the timed answers hold their standard across two different topic sections, the work is done and a family should stop paying. We write a handover note for the school's subject teacher and end the block. A plan with no finish condition is not a plan, and in a subject where improvement is this legible there is no excuse for leaving the end point vague.

sections.heading: The two 0495 papers and where the marks sit
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE Sociology is assessed by two written papers with no coursework, which means every mark in the qualification is earned in timed writing. On the current syllabus, one paper centres on sociological theory and research methods, and the other is built from the topic sections - family, education, crime and deviance and social control, and the media - with candidates answering on the sections their school has taught. Confirm the current paper structure, durations and weightings on cambridgeinternational.org for your child's exam series, because Cambridge revises specifications on a cycle and the arrangement has changed between versions.

Within each paper, the mark distribution is lopsided in a way students systematically misjudge. Short definition and description items are worth a mark or two each and are the easiest marks on the paper; most Dubai candidates collect them reliably. The extended evaluation items carry the largest single tariff, commonly in the region of 15 marks, and they are where a grade is decided. A student scoring well on the short items and poorly on the long ones has a technique problem, not a knowledge problem, and that pattern is visible on any marked script within thirty seconds.

The structural trap in Paper 2 is topic matching. A question in the education section invites education material, and an answer that imports a family study because the student knows it better earns little. Because schools teach a subset of sections, candidates sometimes revise broadly and then answer with whatever comes to mind under pressure. Drilling the habit of identifying the section before writing a word is a single-session fix with a real mark value.

The table below sets out what each component asks for and the fault that most reliably costs marks. Treat the tariffs as typical rather than fixed; the current specification is the authority on how any individual paper is built, and your child's teacher will know which topic sections the school has prepared.

sections.heading: The extended evaluation question, and the four things that move it
paragraphs: If a 0495 grade is going to move, this is almost always where it moves. The extended item is the largest tariff on the paper and the one students prepare for least deliberately, because they believe it rewards knowing more. It rewards doing something specific with what you already know, and the four behaviours that distinguish a top-band answer from a middle-band one can be named, practised and checked off a list.

The first is that the counter-position arrives early and is taken seriously. A middle-band answer spends three paragraphs on one side and then concedes something in paragraph four. A top-band answer raises the strongest objection to its own claim in the second paragraph and answers it. The second is that evidence is deployed rather than displayed: a study is introduced because it supports a specific claim, and the claim is stated before the study is named. The third is that the limits of the evidence are acknowledged - a small sample, an old study, a different society - which demonstrates exactly the scepticism the syllabus is teaching.

The fourth is that the conclusion follows. A conclusion that announces a position the body of the answer did not build reads as a preference, and it is marked as one. The simplest diagnostic a parent can apply, without knowing any sociology, is to read the last paragraph and ask whether its claim appeared anywhere earlier. If not, that is the fault, and it is usually fixable in two sessions because it is a structural habit rather than a gap in understanding.

The table sets out what each band of answer typically looks like on the page and what has to be added to move up. It is written so a parent can use it on their own child's script. That is deliberate: a family who can read the fault themselves is in a much better position to judge whether tutoring is delivering anything, with us or with anyone else.

sections.heading: Marking the student's own script: how the weekly loop runs
paragraphs: The mechanics of the evidence loop matter, because a loop that is described but not run produces nothing. Between sessions the student writes one extended answer to time - not an essay at leisure, a timed answer under something close to exam conditions, because the fault being diagnosed only appears under time pressure. The answer is sent before the session so the tutor has read it first and the hour is not spent reading.

In the session the script sits on screen and both people annotate it. The tutor marks against the criteria in Cambridge's own language rather than in a paraphrase, because a student who learns the actual wording can apply it to their next answer without a tutor present. Sections that score are marked as such, which matters: a student who only sees crosses stops writing the thing that was working. Then one fault is named, in a single sentence, and written down with the date.

One fault, not five. This is the discipline that makes the record useful. A script with eleven problems identified produces no change, because nobody can hold eleven corrections while writing to time. A script with one named target produces a measurably different next answer. The list grows over a term as earlier faults clear, and the dates on it are what let a parent see whether the sessions are doing anything.

The student keeps every annotated script as a file. By the final fortnight that folder is the revision resource: not a textbook, not a set of notes, but six marked answers in their own handwriting with the faults visible and the corrections beside them. Dubai students carrying a heavy mandatory-subject timetable alongside their options have limited revision hours, and rereading their own marked work is the highest-yield use of those hours available.

sections.heading: Research methods: the half Dubai students underrate
paragraphs: Research methods is where 0495 candidates most reliably lose marks they could have had, and the reason is a category error. Students revise methods as a list of definitions - questionnaire, interview, observation, official statistics - and the paper does not ask for definitions. It asks what a particular method can and cannot show about a particular question in a particular context, which is a judgement rather than a recall task.

The difference is visible in a single example. Asked about using questionnaires to study family roles, a middle-band answer explains what a questionnaire is, notes that it can reach many people, and adds that respondents may not tell the truth. A top-band answer asks who in the household fills it in, what that does to the data about the other members, whether the questions assume a family structure that the respondents do not have, and whether a method that can reach a thousand households is worth the shallowness that follows. Same knowledge, different operation.

Representativeness and sampling are the technical core, and they have a numerical component that trips students who are otherwise strong. A sample of thirty is not small or large in itself; it is small or large relative to the claim being made from it. A student who cannot reason about a percentage or a sample base loses sociology marks for an arithmetic reason, which is worth diagnosing rather than treating as a sociology gap. The practical and ethical limits of a method also need separating: that a method is difficult is not the same as that it is wrong, and candidates blur the two constantly.

This is also the part of the syllabus that transfers furthest. The scepticism 0495 teaches about where a number came from, who produced it and what it leaves out is the same scepticism that Global Perspectives assesses in its written paper and that the IB Diploma assesses in Theory of Knowledge. A student who gets research methods right at sixteen is being trained in something considerably more durable than an IGCSE grade.

sections.heading: Family, education, crime and the media in a Dubai context
paragraphs: The topic sections are where students have the most to say and the least discipline about saying it. Each section rewards the same structure, and each has a characteristic failure. The family section fails when candidates describe household types rather than evaluating a claim about them. Education fails when answers become opinion about schools. Crime and deviance fails when labelling and structural explanations are named without being applied. The media section fails when candidates generalise from their own habits to a population.

Local examples are useful here, and they need handling carefully. A Dubai student lives in a society with distinctive features worth thinking about sociologically - a large expatriate population, households structured around employment and residency, a schooling market with seventeen different curricula available, and a mandatory-subject requirement that applies across all of them. Those are legitimate things to reason about. What they are not is a licence to generalise: one student's observation of their own school is an anecdote, and presenting it as evidence costs marks rather than earning them.

The usable version is to treat local observation as a hypothesis and the syllabus material as the evidence base. A candidate can note that their own context raises a question about how far a theory developed in one society travels to another, and that is a genuinely sophisticated move that demonstrates the limits-of-evidence skill the top band wants. It is also the kind of answer an examiner reads rarely, which is reason enough to teach it.

On the mandatory-subject point, since families ask: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are compulsory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. These are facts about the timetable a student is working inside, and they explain why revision hours for an option subject are scarcer in Dubai than a syllabus designer might assume. They are not themselves 0495 content.

The point of publishing it is that a family can hold any provider, including us, to a record of this shape.

Notice that nothing in weeks one to three is content teaching. The first three sessions establish what the fault is and whether it is one fault or several, because a block that starts by teaching topic material to a student whose problem is structure wastes three hours and the money that bought them. Notice also that the evidence column contains objects, not adjectives: a marked script, a rewritten paragraph, a cleared list item. Progress you cannot put in a folder is not progress you can check.

Notice finally what happens at week ten. The block ends. There is a handover note for the subject teacher, the fault list is closed, and the family stops paying. If at week five the record showed nothing moving, the honest response would have been to change the approach or to say that we were not the right fit, and we would rather have that conversation at week five than complete ten weeks for the sake of tidiness.

Timings in Dubai shape this record in practical ways worth stating. Sessions move for the January mock fortnight rather than being charged through it. During Ramadan the slot shifts to post-Iftar hours, where a shorter later session works better than an exhausted afternoon one. And a student carrying three sciences plus mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education may write their timed answer at the weekend rather than midweek, which is fine as long as it is timed.

sections.heading: What a 0495 tutor will not do, and what no record can promise
paragraphs: A tutor working this way reads a great deal of a student's writing, so the boundary needs stating. A tutor may mark, annotate, quote the criteria, show what a stronger paragraph looks like on a different question, and say plainly that a paragraph is description where it needed to be evaluation. A tutor may not rewrite an answer on a student's behalf or supply sentences to be reproduced in an exam-style piece as the student's own thinking. There is no coursework in 0495, so no submission is at risk, but the habit matters: a student who has been handed prose has learned nothing they can use when the paper is in front of them alone.

Nor will we distribute exam material. Cambridge past papers, mark schemes and syllabus documents are copyright, and we do not reproduce or supply them. The official route is your child's school and its exams officer, and the current syllabus lives on cambridgeinternational.org. In sessions we work from the student's own answers and write equivalent questions when new material is needed, which is a better test in any case because the student has not seen them.

On outcomes, the record shows what changed; it cannot promise what will happen. No tutor can promise a grade, a number of marks or a point improvement, and a provider offering a certain 7, a promised grade jump or money back linked to a result is making a claim nobody can stand behind. We also publish no statistic about our students, because a figure without a sample, a date and a method is not evidence and we are not going to produce one for the sake of looking confident in a search result.

And on who we are: IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. We hold no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or the IB, and we run no centre or office in the UAE. Individuals providing private tutoring in this country need a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. We explain what these bodies do and link to them; we do not imply any of them endorse us.
